## ADR-0137: Body algorithm Path B-async (buffer-then-delayed-emit) — kbps-per-tick `throttleDuration` helper + `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` cumulative byte-equivalence + foot-gun `limit_kbps==0` 24h throttle + one-tick `fill_interval` floor + ZERO framework deltas

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-11
**Doctrine:** Phase-15 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl first-use convention (the `throttleDuration` helper is the algorithmic-core landing; ADR authored at this commit). Composes against phase-09 fault's `time.AfterFunc` + `cb.ContinueDecoding/Encoding` async-resume, phase-13 ADR-0128 (synthetic empty-terminal `RunDecodeData`), and phase-14 ADR-0131 (`EncoderFilterCallbacks.OverwriteBody`) — phase-15 is the FIRST §9 row to consume all three primitive sets simultaneously without amendment.
**Lands-in-task:** Task 3 (this commit; `bucket.go` + Group 3 unit tests verifying SPEC §6.6 empirical-verification matrix).

### Context

Phase 15's body algorithm shape decision is THE load-bearing structural choice for `envoy.filters.http.bandwidth_limit` — the choice of how envoy-go emulates Envoy's per-tick chunk-paced throttle behavior with envoy-go's coarser-grained `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` → buffer → `ContinueDecoding/Encoding` framework primitives. The BRAINSTORM (§§2-3) explored two algorithm shapes: Path A streaming (filter emits chunks at `fill_interval` cadence, mirroring Envoy's per-tick wire shape) vs. Path B-async (filter buffers the body, sleeps `throttleDuration`, then emits the full buffered body in one `ContinueDecoding/Encoding` call). Per SPEC §3 framework survey + §6.6 + §11.P8 + §11.P15: Path A is REJECTED (requires symmetric `EmitChunk` / `ConsumeChunk` framework primitives that envoy-go's HCM does not provide; would require new framework deltas which contradicts SPEC §1.7 ZERO-framework-deltas claim); Path B-async is the LANDED shape with the natural divergence-window: wire-shape DIVERGES (envoy-go's silent-then-blast vs. Envoy's rate-paced chunks at `fill_interval` cadence), but total-throttle wall-clock CONVERGES within ±70ms per §11.P9.

The kbps-per-tick `throttleDuration` arithmetic — `chunk_size = limit_kbps × 1024 × fill_interval_seconds` (KiB/s units NOT kilobits-per-second per §1.1 amendment 6; the BRAINSTORM steady-rate `body_size / limit_kbps` formula was REFUTED at §11.P15 empirical-pin) — is the pure-function algorithmic core. The function is allocation-free, has no per-stream state, and is unit-testable in isolation against SPEC §6.6's empirical-verification matrix (5 rows; covers one-tick floor, multi-tick scaling, fill_interval granularity, and the 79-tick large-body case). Plus the foot-gun branch (`limit_kbps == 0` at runtime → 24h arbitrarily-large throttle per §1.1 amendment 10 + §11 probeJ) matches Envoy's runtime-hang behavior on listener-level missing `limit_kbps` with active `enable_mode`. The one-tick `fill_interval` floor for sub-`chunk_size` bodies approximates Envoy's initial-burst capacity discharge within the same ±70ms tolerance.

The `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` cumulative byte-equivalence semantic (per SPEC §11.P3 + §6.7 + §1.1 amendment 7) is the structural bridge between envoy-go's Path B-async wire shape and Envoy's per-tick counter discipline: at timer-fire (when the body's `ContinueDecoding/Encoding` resumes), the caller increments `*_enforced` by `ticks` (NOT by 1) so the cumulative counter total matches Envoy's tick-by-tick accumulation exactly at stream completion. Wire-shape diverges; counter cardinality converges.

### Decision

**(i) Body algorithm shape: Path B-async (buffer-then-delayed-emit) with ZERO framework deltas.** Per SPEC §3 + §1.7. The decode-side filter buffers the body via `envoyhttp.FilterDataStatusDataStopIterationAndBuffer` (phase-13 ADR-0128's synthetic empty-terminal `RunDecodeData` ensures `DecodeData(endStream=true)` reaches the filter even on chunked-body EOF); arms `time.AfterFunc(throttleDuration, ...)` to fire `cb.ContinueDecoding()` at the elapsed throttle wall-clock; encode-side is symmetric with `ContinueEncoding`. The three framework primitives — phase-09 fault's `time.AfterFunc` + async-resume, phase-13 ADR-0128's decode-side body-buffering, and phase-14 ADR-0131's encode-side `OverwriteBody` (anticipated NOT invoked; see (vi)) — are consumed UNCHANGED. Phase-15 introduces no new HCM / chain / callback primitives.

**(ii) Throttle arithmetic: kbps-per-tick formula `chunk_size = limit_kbps × 1024 × fill_interval_seconds`.** Per SPEC §6.6 + §11.P15 + §1.1 amendment 6. The formula:

```
chunk_size_per_tick = limit_kbps × 1024 × fill_interval_seconds   (bytes/tick; KiB/s units NOT kbps)
ticks               = ceil(body_size / chunk_size_per_tick)
throttle_duration   = ticks × fill_interval
```

The KiB/s-per-second units (NOT kilobits-per-second) trace to the upstream `bandwidth_limit.pb.go:95` proto comment + §11.P15 empirical-pin which REFUTES the BRAINSTORM steady-rate formula `throttle = body_size / limit_kbps`. The empirical-verification matrix in `bucket.go` GoDoc (5 rows verbatim from SPEC §6.6) is the regression-anchor for the predicted-vs-observed wall-clock divergence; all 5 cases predict within ±70ms of empirical observation (the 100-byte / 5ms-observed outlier reflects Envoy's initial-burst capacity discharge, which envoy-go's one-tick floor approximates within the same tolerance).

**(iii) `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` at timer-fire — cumulative byte-equivalence with reference Envoy.** Per SPEC §11.P3 + §6.7 + §1.1 amendment 7. `throttleDuration` returns BOTH the wall-clock duration AND the tick count so the caller (Task 4 decode-side + Task 5 encode-side wiring) increments the `*_enforced` counter by `ticks` at timer-fire (NOT by 1 per stream). Envoy's per-tick counter discipline increments `*_enforced` once per `fill_interval` tick during the throttle window; envoy-go's Path B-async wire shape sees the timer-fire as a single event, but the counter increment-by-`ticks` reproduces the cumulative total exactly. Wire-shape diverges; counter cardinality at stream completion is byte-equivalent.

**(iv) One-tick `fill_interval` floor for sub-`chunk_size_per_tick` bodies; ±70ms tolerance per §11.P9.** Per SPEC §6.6 + §11.P9. When `body_size <= chunk_size_per_tick` (e.g. 100-byte body with 10 KiB/s + 50ms fill_interval → chunk_size=512), the formula yields `ticks=1` → `throttle_duration=fill_interval` (50ms). Envoy's initial-burst capacity discharges sub-chunk bodies without engaging the throttle window (observed 5ms wall-clock for the 100-byte case at §11.P9), so envoy-go's 50ms-vs-5ms divergence on this case lives WITHIN the ±70ms tolerance. The fast-passthrough threshold at 1ms hypothesis (BRAINSTORM §11.4) is REJECTED: the one-tick `fill_interval` floor is structurally honest with the kbps-per-tick model and matches Envoy's per-tick behavior within tolerance.

**(v) Foot-gun branch `limit_kbps == 0` → 24h arbitrarily-large throttle.** Per SPEC §1.1 amendment 10 + §11 probeJ. The listener-level `limit_kbps` is OPTIONAL at parse-time (PGV accepts unset wrapper; the runtime hang is the operational foot-gun). When the runtime sees `compiledConfig.limitKbps == 0` with active `enable_mode`, `throttleDuration` returns `(24 * time.Hour, 1)` — a wall-clock duration large enough that the stream effectively hangs on the first body chunk (matches Envoy's runtime-hang behavior). The `ticks=1` marker lets the caller still increment `*_enforced` by 1 at first tick (matching Envoy's first-tick increment). Mirrors Envoy verbatim; documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 forward-pointer notes (lands at Task 15).

**(vi) `cb.OverwriteBody` (phase-14 ADR-0131 primitive) anticipated NOT invoked; framework's buffered-return path emits bytes unchanged.** Per SPEC §3 + §11.P8 framework-survey. The buffered-then-resumed body emits via `FilterDataStatusDataStopIterationAndBuffer` (decode) / `FilterDataStatusDataStopIterationAndBuffer` (encode) + framework-internal buffer drain at `ContinueDecoding/Encoding` time; the filter does NOT mutate the buffered body, so the `OverwriteBody` primitive is NOT called on the throttle path. If Task 5 impl-time framework-survey reveals `OverwriteBody` IS required (e.g., if the encode-side buffered-return semantic requires an explicit body re-emission), phase-15 REUSES the existing phase-14 primitive — it does NOT introduce a new framework delta. The ZERO-framework-deltas claim per SPEC §1.7 stays unchanged either way: phase-15 either invokes ADR-0131 unchanged (no-delta REUSE) or does NOT invoke it (no-delta no-op).

**(vii) Wire-shape divergence-window: envoy-go silent-then-blast vs. Envoy Path A rate-paced chunks; total-throttle equivalent ±70ms; chunk-arrival divergent.** Per SPEC §11.P8 REFRAMED (BRAINSTORM hypothesized Path A but EMPIRICAL pin observed Path A in Envoy with envoy-go LANDING Path B-async by design); §11.P9 tolerance window. The two wire shapes:
- **Envoy (Path A rate-paced):** Body chunks arrive at the downstream client at `fill_interval` cadence (e.g., 50ms inter-chunk arrival times), each chunk sized at `chunk_size_per_tick`. The wall-clock total is `ticks × fill_interval`.
- **envoy-go (Path B-async):** Body is buffered server-side at the filter; downstream client sees ZERO bytes for `throttle_duration` wall-clock, then the full body arrives in one `ContinueDecoding/Encoding` blast. Total wall-clock is `ticks × fill_interval` (matches Envoy within ±70ms).

The divergence-window is allow-listed at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.5 (lands at Task 15); operator-facing documentation notes the wire-shape divergence at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes. A future trailer-emission framework phase (forward-pointer per §8.1) will land `EncoderFilterCallbacks.EmitTrailers` enabling per-chunk emission, at which point envoy-go can adopt Path A rate-paced wire shape (phase-15's divergence-window then closes; counters + wire-shape both byte-equivalent).

### Alternatives considered

(a) **Path A streaming** (filter emits chunks at `fill_interval` cadence; matches Envoy wire-shape) — REJECTED per SPEC §3 + §1.7 + §11.P8. Path A requires symmetric `EmitChunk` / `ConsumeChunk` framework primitives that envoy-go's existing HCM does not provide. Implementing Path A would require a new framework delta — `HTTPCallbacks.EmitData(slice, isLast)` or equivalent — which contradicts the SPEC §1.7 ZERO-framework-deltas claim. The Path B-async + ±70ms divergence-window trade-off lands the entire phase without framework surgery.

(b) **Steady-rate formula `throttle = body_size / limit_kbps`** (the BRAINSTORM hypothesis; assumes constant-rate emission) — REJECTED per SPEC §11.P15 empirical-pin. The §11.P15 measurement matrix observed Envoy emitting chunks at `fill_interval` cadence with chunk_size = `limit_kbps × 1024 × fill_interval_seconds`, NOT a continuous rate. The steady-rate formula yields incorrect predictions for the 4 multi-tick cases (off by 7-32% at the 4000-byte / 1-10 kbps cases); the kbps-per-tick formula predicts within ±70ms tolerance for all 5 rows.

(c) **Fast-passthrough threshold at 1ms** (`throttle_duration < 1ms` → skip timer-arm; emit synchronously) — REJECTED per SPEC §6.6 + the one-tick `fill_interval` floor. The minimum throttle is `fill_interval` (≥ 20ms per the PGV bound), so a 1ms threshold would never trigger in practice; adding the conditional branch + the special-case path complicates the algorithmic core without observable benefit. The one-tick floor is structurally honest with the kbps-per-tick model and matches Envoy's per-tick behavior within ±70ms.

### Consequences

- Phase-15 is the **FIRST §9 row since phase-12 csrf** to introduce ZERO framework deltas. The body algorithm Path B-async lands entirely by reuse of phase-09 fault's `time.AfterFunc` + async-resume + phase-13 ADR-0128's decode-side body-buffering + phase-14 ADR-0131's encode-side `OverwriteBody` (anticipated NOT invoked; see §Decision (vi)). Demonstrates phase-13 + phase-14's framework primitives as reusable infrastructure rather than single-use additions.
- The `throttleDuration` pure-function helper at `bucket.go` (~60 LoC code; ~50 LoC GoDoc + verification matrix) is the algorithmic-core landing. Future cross-filter use (e.g., a hypothetical `network.bandwidth_limit` L4 filter; the upstream Envoy filter exists at `envoy.filters.network.local_ratelimit` but envoy-go has not landed L4 filters in §9 family-rows) MAY reuse the helper unchanged.
- The `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` cumulative byte-equivalence discipline is the LOAD-BEARING bridge between envoy-go Path B-async wire shape and Envoy's per-tick counter discipline. Operators reading `*_enforced` counter totals at stream-completion see byte-equivalent values across reference + envoy-go (within the ±70ms wall-clock tolerance bracket). The differential fixture `0017-http-bandwidth-limit` (lands at Tasks 11-14) asserts counter-equivalence on all 6 scenarios.
- The wire-shape divergence-window (silent-then-blast vs. rate-paced chunks) is allow-listed at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.5; operators observing per-chunk timing (e.g., via custom downstream HTTP tracing) see structurally-different chunk-arrival patterns. The forward-pointer to the future trailer-emission framework phase notes the closing condition for this divergence-window (when `EmitTrailers` lands, Path A becomes structurally feasible).
- The foot-gun `limit_kbps == 0` → 24h throttle is the operational match for Envoy's runtime-hang behavior on listener-level missing `limit_kbps`. Operators porting Envoy configs to envoy-go see byte-equivalent failure modes (the boot config loads in both; the first body chunk hangs at wall-clock duration far exceeding typical request timeouts in both). The behavior is documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 forward-pointer notes (lands at Task 15).
- Group 3 unit tests (6 tests in `bandwidthlimit_test.go`; ~125 LoC) verify the formula against SPEC §6.6's empirical-verification matrix exactly. The kbps-per-tick matrix's 5 rows + the foot-gun + the empty-body + the one-tick floor + the fill_interval granularity + the large-body sanity all PASS on first land; no algorithmic surprises at the formula level.
- ADR-0125 amendment §(xi) (LANDED at SPEC commit `49e0361`) + phase-15's ADR-0136 (per-route `limit_kbps` CODE-LEVEL REQUIRED) + this ADR-0137 (algorithmic-core) jointly settle the phase-15 §9 row's structural shape. ADRs 0138 (14-stat filterStats) + 0139 (per-route INDEPENDENT-stats wiring) land at Tasks 7-8 and complete the §9 row's ADR set.

## ADR-0138: `bandwidth_limit` 14-active-stat `filterStats` surface (8 counters + 6 gauges) + namespace `<stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>` underscore-infix (NOT HCM-rooted) + Prometheus inline-prefix rendering (NO new SN10 rule; NO tag-extractor) + 2 histograms DEFERRED via twin-series-filter divergence-window

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-11
**Doctrine:** ADR-0061 (stats Registry / SN1–SN9 flattening rules); ADR-0118 (phase-11 local_ratelimit's `<stat_prefix>.http_local_rate_limit.<counter>` namespace shape + SN9 tag-extractor — structural precedent for phase-15's namespace shape; the inline-prefix discipline DIVERGES from SN9's tag-extractor); ADR-0117 (phase-11 per-route bucket isolation + INDEPENDENT-stats — cross-reference to ADR-0139); ADR-0085 (nil-Registry tolerance for test code paths); ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention; ADR lands at first-use impl-task); phase-06.1 baseline ("counters + gauges only — histograms deferred").
**Lands-in-task:** Task 8

### Context

Phase-15's `bandwidth_limit` filter surfaces stat-emission requirements ratified at SPEC §6.2 + §1.1 amendments 7 + 8 + 9 + §11.P3 + §11.P10 + §11.P11 + BRAINSTORM §2.6 + §2.7. BRAINSTORM §1.1 item 5 + §2.6 initially hypothesized **6 new counter+gauge stats** (`request_enabled`, `request_enforced`, `request_pending`, `response_enabled`, `response_enforced`, `response_pending`) plus 4 histograms deferred per phase-06.1 baseline (§8.2 deferral).

**SPEC §11.P3 + §11.P10 + §11.P11 empirically REFUTE on three axes:**

1. **Stat count.** Envoy v1.37.2's `bandwidth_limit` emits **16 stat names per active `stat_prefix`** — 8 counters + 6 gauges + 2 histograms (verbatim probeA verification at `/tmp/p15-pins/probeA.txt`). The 4 names BRAINSTORM hypothesized as histograms (`*_incoming_size`, `*_allowed_size` × {request, response}) are GAUGES, NOT histograms. The 2 actual histograms are `*_transfer_duration` × {request, response} — a duration-histogram axis BRAINSTORM did not anticipate. envoy-go MVP per phase-06.1 baseline emits 14 active stats (the 8 counters + 6 gauges); the 2 histograms are deferred under amendment 9's twin-series-filter divergence-window.
2. **Namespace shape.** Internal stat path is `<stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>` with single-segment `http_bandwidth_limit` underscore infix (NOT `http.bandwidth_limit.` dot infix; NOT HCM-rooted `http.<HCM>.<prefix>.bandwidth_limit.<counter>` as BRAINSTORM §2.7 hypothesized). Same shape as phase-11 local_ratelimit's `<stat_prefix>.http_local_rate_limit.<counter>` per ADR-0118.
3. **Prometheus rendering.** Envoy renders `envoy_<stat_prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<counter>{}` — stat_prefix INLINED into base name; NO labels; NO tag-extractor (refutes any HCM-rooted hypothesis AND refutes any SN9-analog tag-extractor hypothesis). NO new SN-numbered flattening rule is needed; the inline-prefix shape sits in `internal/stats/name.go`'s default-branch fallback alongside the SN9 detection but emits NO label.

The `*_enforced` counter has an additional semantic note (per §11.P3 + planner-time decision 15): reference Envoy increments `*_enforced` **per `fill_interval` TICK** during throttle (verbatim probeJ: `response_enforced: 99` for a hung 5-second stream ≈ 100 ticks at 50ms). envoy-go's Path B-async cannot observe per-tick events; the cumulative-byte-equivalence bridge is to bump `*_enforced += ticks` exactly once at timer-fire (where `ticks = ceil(body/chunk_size)`). The per-tick cumulative byte-equivalence claim is asserted at fixture 0017 (Tasks 11-14) on all 6 scenarios.

The `*_incoming_size` + `*_allowed_size` gauges are transient per-tick bytes-in-flight state. Envoy's Path A rate-paced chunk-emit updates them per-chunk; envoy-go's Path B-async approximates via single-blast emission — set `incoming_size = bodyLen` at endStream-arrival, set `allowed_size = bodyLen` at timer-fire (or immediately on the empty-body fast path), reset both to 0 at OnDestroy. The terminal-tick gauge values are byte-equivalent across both proxies; the intra-throttle per-tick dynamics observably diverge (the wire-shape divergence-window per ADR-0137).

### Decision

**(i) 14 active stats per `stat_prefix` (8 counters + 6 gauges) per SPEC §1.1 amendment 7.** The canonical name set:

```
8 counters (cumulative across all streams):
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_enabled
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_enforced
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_incoming_total_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_allowed_total_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_enabled
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_enforced
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_incoming_total_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_allowed_total_size

6 gauges (transient per-stream state):
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_pending
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_incoming_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.request_allowed_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_pending
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_incoming_size
  <stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.response_allowed_size
```

Registered at `newFilterStats(reg, statPrefix)` (listener-level boot-time path via `NewCounter` / `NewGauge` — panic-on-duplicate) AND `newFilterStatsIfAbsent(reg, statPrefix)` (per-route post-Freeze-idempotent path via `NewCounterIfAbsent` / `NewGaugeIfAbsent` per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139). The 14 names + the per-prefix `newFilterStats` registration helper are the canonical landing for SPEC §6.2 + amendment 7.

**(ii) Namespace shape: `<stat_prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>` underscore-infix (NOT HCM-rooted) per §11.P11.** Same structural shape as phase-11 local_ratelimit's `<stat_prefix>.http_local_rate_limit.<counter>` per ADR-0118 — single-segment `http_bandwidth_limit` underscore infix; filter-`stat_prefix`-rooted (NOT HCM-`stat_prefix`-rooted unlike phase-14 compressor's `http.<HCM>.compressor.<library>.<codec>.<counter>` shape per ADR-0132). Cross-filter precedent table:

| Phase | Filter | Namespace root | Infix shape |
|-------|--------|----------------|-------------|
| 11    | local_ratelimit | filter `stat_prefix` | `<prefix>.http_local_rate_limit.<counter>` |
| 14    | compressor | HCM `stat_prefix` | `http.<HCM>.compressor.<library>.<codec>.<counter>` |
| **15**    | **bandwidth_limit** | **filter `stat_prefix`** | **`<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>`** |

The choice of filter-`stat_prefix`-rooted vs HCM-`stat_prefix`-rooted follows upstream Envoy's filter-source verbatim per §11.P11 empirical pin; envoy-go mirrors without divergence. Future filters with stat-emission requirements adopt one of the two patterns per upstream Envoy's filter-source shape.

**(iii) Prometheus rendering: `envoy_<stat_prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<counter>{}` inline-prefix shape; NO new SN10 rule; NO tag-extractor per §11.P10 + amendment 8.** stat_prefix is INLINED into the Prometheus base name (NO label promotion; NO `envoy_<…>_prefix=<stat_prefix>` extracted tag). The full mapping for input `<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>` is:

```
internal:    "<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>"
                       │
                       ▼  (dot→underscore substitution + envoy_ prefix)
Prometheus:  "envoy_<prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<counter>{}"
```

The rendering lands as a filter-specific inline-prefix detection in `internal/stats/name.go`'s default-branch fallback (the same default branch that hosts the SN9 local_ratelimit detection — see ADR-0118). The bandwidth_limit detection differs from SN9 on the label-extraction axis: SN9 promotes the prefix to an `envoy_local_http_ratelimit_prefix=<prefix>` label; bandwidth_limit inlines the prefix into the base name AS-IS (after dot→underscore). The 14 canonical counter names below MUST stay in lockstep between `internal/stats/name.go`'s switch + `internal/filter/http/bandwidthlimit/bandwidthlimit.go`'s `newFilterStats` / `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` — the inline-detection enumerates the 14 expected suffixes to validate the path matches the filter's emitted set (defensive against typos + future widening). NO new SN-numbered rule is added; the detection is NOT given an SN number per §11.P10 "NO SN10 rule" + amendment 8 — it is a filter-specific inline-prefix detection slotted into the default-branch fallback alongside SN9 without semantic relation to the SN-numbered tag-extraction family.

The Group 8 `TestStatsNamespace_PromInlineFlatten_NoSN10` test exercises the full pipeline (Registry → WriteProm → Prometheus exposition text) + asserts the inline-prefix base name appears + asserts NO labeled form (`<base>{`) is emitted.

**(iv) Per-route stats INDEPENDENT (cross-reference ADR-0139).** Phase-15 per-route TPFC entries allocate their own `*filterStats` keyed by the per-route `stat_prefix` per ADR-0117 precedent — listener-level counters do NOT increment for per-route reqs. The 14-name surface lands under BOTH the listener-level `stat_prefix` AND each per-route `stat_prefix` (with the per-route post-Freeze idempotency guard via `NewCounterIfAbsent` + `NewGaugeIfAbsent`). The full INDEPENDENT-stats wiring discipline lands at ADR-0139; this ADR-0138 ratifies the 14-name surface used uniformly across listener-level + per-route allocations.

**(v) `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` cumulative-match per §11.P3 + planner-time decision 15.** Per the per-tick cumulative byte-equivalence bridge: reference Envoy bumps `*_enforced` per `fill_interval` TICK; envoy-go's Path B-async bumps `*_enforced += ticks` exactly once at timer-fire (where `ticks = ceil(body/chunk_size)` per ADR-0137's `throttleDuration` helper). The cumulative total at stream-completion is byte-equivalent across reference + envoy-go. Operators reading `*_enforced` counter totals see byte-equivalent values; intra-stream per-tick observations observably diverge. The differential fixture 0017 (Tasks 11-14) asserts counter-equivalence on all 6 scenarios within the ±70ms wall-clock tolerance bracket.

**(vi) 2 histograms DEFERRED per phase-06.1 baseline + amendment 9 twin-series-filter.** Reference Envoy v1.37.2 emits 2 UNCONDITIONAL transfer-duration histograms per active `stat_prefix` (`request_transfer_duration`, `response_transfer_duration`) — fire regardless of `enable_response_trailers` setting (refutes BRAINSTORM §8.2's implicit `enable_response_trailers`-gating assumption). envoy-go MVP per phase-06.1 baseline ("counters + gauges only — histograms deferred") emits NO histograms. The twin-series-filter divergence-window per amendment 9 + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §242 extension allow-lists the 2 histogram families:

```
envoy_<stat_prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_request_transfer_duration_{bucket, sum, count}
envoy_<stat_prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_response_transfer_duration_{bucket, sum, count}
```

Differential fixture 0017's `expectations.yaml` (Tasks 13-14) allow-lists via the twin-series-filter discipline; the differential harness's per-counter delta comparison filters these out before computing byte-equivalence. Operator dashboards querying `envoy_<prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<dir>_transfer_duration_*` see Envoy emit but envoy-go absent — documented at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes. Future re-activation: a histogram-emit-infra phase lands `*stats.Registry.Histogram` + Prometheus `histogram_*` extractor; phase-15's `filterStats` extends with 2 histogram fields; the divergence-window closes.

**(vii) `*_incoming_size` / `*_allowed_size` gauges set at endStream-arrival / timer-fire then reset at OnDestroy.** Per SPEC §6.7 + §6.8 + §11.P3:

- `*_incoming_size`: set to `bodyLen` at endStream-arrival via `Set(int64(bodyLen))` (transient — reflects bytes-buffered-but-not-yet-forwarded).
- `*_allowed_size`: set to `bodyLen` at timer-fire (or immediately on the empty-body fast path where throttle == 0) — one-blast emission mirrors Envoy's terminal-tick state.
- Both gauges reset to 0 at OnDestroy (the transient nature mirrors Envoy's per-stream gauge lifecycle).

Reference Envoy's Path A rate-paced per-tick dynamics (each chunk updates the gauges to per-chunk values) are NOT mirrored by envoy-go's Path B-async — terminal-tick byte-equivalence holds; intra-throttle per-tick dynamics observably diverge per the wire-shape divergence-window (ADR-0137). The gauges' OnDestroy reset to 0 is handled inside the Stop-races-Fire OnDestroy discipline at SPEC §6.9 + ADR-0137 (currently the OnDestroy implementation in `bandwidthlimit.go` decrements `*_pending` under the Stop()-returns-true branch; the `*_incoming_size` / `*_allowed_size` reset MAY be added at a future ergonomics pass if operators report stale terminal-tick values; phase-15 MVP accepts the terminal-tick stale-value as byte-equivalent with reference Envoy whose own gauges retain terminal-tick values until the next stream).

### Alternatives considered

**(a) HCM-rooted namespace `http.<HCM>.bandwidth_limit.<counter>` (REJECTED per §11.P11 empirical refutation).** BRAINSTORM §2.7 hypothesized this shape mirroring phase-14 compressor's HCM-rooted namespace. SPEC §11.P11 empirically refuted via probeA `/stats?filter=bandwidth_limit` text scrape: reference Envoy emits `default.http_bandwidth_limit.request_enabled: 0` (filter-`stat_prefix`-rooted), NOT `http.<HCM>.bandwidth_limit.request_enabled` (HCM-rooted). The HCM-rooted shape would require a Rule SN2 reuse + the Prometheus rendering would carry an `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix=<HCM>` label — neither matches reference Envoy's verbatim output. REJECTED.

**(b) New SN-numbered tag-extractor rule with `envoy_local_http_bandwidth_limit_prefix=<stat_prefix>` label (REJECTED per §11.P10 empirical refutation).** A hypothetical "SN10 rule" analogous to phase-11 ADR-0118's SN9 (which extracts `envoy_local_http_ratelimit_prefix=<stat_prefix>`) would promote the bandwidth_limit `stat_prefix` to an extracted Prometheus label. SPEC §11.P10 empirically refuted via probeA `/stats/prometheus` scrape: reference Envoy emits `envoy_default_http_bandwidth_limit_response_enabled{} 3` with NO labels (the `{}` is empty). Adding a tag-extractor would diverge from reference Envoy. REJECTED. The inline-prefix detection in `internal/stats/name.go`'s default-branch fallback is NOT a new SN-numbered rule — it does not promote the prefix to a label; it inlines the prefix into the base name AS-IS (after dot→underscore substitution).

**(c) Histogram emission in MVP (REJECTED per phase-06.1 baseline + ADR-0060).** Phase-06.1 established "counters + gauges only — histograms deferred" as the stats Registry's primitive surface. Phase-15 MVP inherits the baseline; emitting the 2 unconditional `transfer_duration` histograms would require: (a) extending `stats.Registry` with a Histogram primitive (~150 LoC); (b) extending `internal/stats/prom.go` with `histogram_*` bucket/sum/count rendering (~100 LoC); (c) extending the namespace flattening machinery to handle the histogram-suffix family. Out of scope for phase-15's §9 row. The twin-series-filter divergence-window per amendment 9 is the correct discipline — phase-15 MVP emits 14 active stats; the 2 histograms are allow-listed at fixture 0017 + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §242. REJECTED for MVP; reactivated at a future histogram-emit-infra phase.

**(d) `*_enforced` increment-once-per-stream instead of increment-by-`ticks` (REJECTED per §11.P3 empirical refutation).** A simpler-sounding alternative would bump `*_enforced` exactly once per throttled stream regardless of body size. Reference Envoy bumps per-`fill_interval`-tick (e.g., 99 increments for a 5-second stream at 50ms fill_interval). Increment-once would diverge cumulatively (the differential `*_enforced` counter delta would be off by a factor of `ticks` per stream). The increment-by-`ticks` bridge per planner-time decision 15 maintains cumulative byte-equivalence. REJECTED. The bridge is the LOAD-BEARING discipline for the per-counter delta byte-equivalence claim across the 6 fixture-0017 scenarios.

### Consequences

- **Phase-15 adds 14 names to BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.2 stat-table (46 → 60 names total).** The 14 names are listed verbatim at SPEC §13.2 (Tasks 15 bundle); the 2 deferred histograms are documented at the twin-series subsection + §13.4 forward-pointer notes (DO NOT count in the 60-name table). Phase-15 is the second §9 row after phase-14 compressor to grow the stat-table by a double-digit count (compressor added 17; bandwidth_limit adds 14).
- **`internal/stats/name.go` gains an inline-prefix detection for `.http_bandwidth_limit.` in its default-branch fallback** — slotted alongside the SN9 local_ratelimit detection but emitting NO label. The detection enumerates the 14 canonical counter+gauge suffixes per amendment 7 (must stay in lockstep with `bandwidthlimit.go`'s `newFilterStats` / `newFilterStatsIfAbsent`). The default-branch error return for truly unrecognized names is preserved — only names matching the `.http_bandwidth_limit.` segment with a valid suffix flatten via the inline-prefix path; all other unmatched names continue to return the existing "no recognized top-level segment" error. ADR-0061's SN1–SN9 rule set is UNCHANGED (no new SN number assigned per §11.P10); the detection is implementation-detail in the default-branch fallback.
- **The 2 histograms `*_transfer_duration` are DEFERRED via amendment 9 twin-series-filter divergence-window.** Operator divergence-window documented at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes; differential fixture 0017's `expectations.yaml` allow-lists; BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §242 twin-series subsection extends with a phase-15 entry. Future re-activation: a histogram-emit-infra phase lands `*stats.Registry.Histogram` + Prometheus `histogram_*` extractor; phase-15's `filterStats` extends with 2 histogram fields; the divergence-window closes.
- **The per-route INDEPENDENT-stats discipline lands at ADR-0139** (NOT this ADR; cross-reference). This ADR-0138 ratifies the 14-name surface used uniformly across listener-level + per-route allocations; ADR-0139 ratifies the lazy-cache wiring + per-route INDEPENDENT-stats vs SHARED-stats discrimination. The two ADRs jointly settle the phase-15 stat-emission shape.
- **Group 8 unit tests (4 tests; ~280 LoC) verify the 14-stat namespace surface + Prometheus inline-prefix rendering + post-Freeze idempotency** per SPEC §14.1 Group 8 extension (NOT in SPEC §14.1's original 7-group enumeration; the Group 8 stats-integration tests land at Task 8 per PLAN's file-structure table). The 4 tests: (1) `TestStatsNamespace_AllFourteenActiveStatsRegistered` — exactly 14 stats registered (8c + 6g) under the per-prefix namespace; (2) `TestStatsNamespace_UnderscoreInfix_NotHCMRooted` — internal path is `<prefix>.http_bandwidth_limit.<counter>` underscore-infix (NOT HCM-rooted); (3) `TestStatsNamespace_PromInlineFlatten_NoSN10` — Prometheus rendering produces `envoy_<prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<counter>` inline-prefix shape with NO labels; (4) `TestStatsNamespace_NewFilterStatsIfAbsent_Idempotent` — multi-call returns pointer-equivalent *Counter + *Gauge instances per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 post-Freeze idempotency. All 4 PASS under `go test -race -count=1`.
- **The `*_enforced` increment-by-`ticks` cumulative byte-equivalence discipline** is asserted at fixture 0017 (Tasks 11-14) on all 6 scenarios within the ±70ms wall-clock tolerance bracket. Per-counter delta byte-equivalence per scenario is the LOAD-BEARING differential claim; the discipline is mirrored in BOTH `DecodeData`'s timer-fire callback AND `EncodeData`'s timer-fire callback per SPEC §6.7 + §6.8.
- **ADR-0125 amendment §(xi) (LANDED at SPEC commit `49e0361`) + phase-15's ADR-0136 (per-route `limit_kbps` CODE-LEVEL REQUIRED) + ADR-0137 (algorithmic-core) + this ADR-0138 (stat surface + namespace) + ADR-0139 (per-route wiring) jointly settle the phase-15 §9 row's structural + stat-emission shape.** The 5-ADR set (ADR-0135..ADR-0139) + the ADR-0125 §(xi) amendment paragraph completes the §9 row's ADR ratification per SPEC §1.7 + planner-time decision 13.

## ADR-0139: Per-route INDEPENDENT-stats wiring for `bandwidth_limit` — `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute` + `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` (counters + gauges) + `sync.Map` lazy-cache keyed by `*BandwidthLimit` pointer-identity + `enable_mode: DISABLED` as the disable mechanism

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-11
**Doctrine:** ADR-0117 (phase-11 per-route bucket isolation; the canonical machinery phase-15 inherits VERBATIM); ADR-0061 stats Registry LBP-1 invariant + AMENDMENT (NewGaugeIfAbsent post-Freeze idempotent registration — gauge counterpart to phase-11's NewCounterIfAbsent); ADR-0073 typed_per_filter_config 3-tier merge (most-specific override) + AMENDMENT carryover; ADR-0125 §(xi) amendment (NEW 6th canonical bare-message-via-TPFC + code-level-required-`limit_kbps` pattern); ADR-0072 boot-fail-fast (applies at New only; request-time per-route TPFC parse failures fall back to listener inherit per phase-11 precedent).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 7

### Context

Phase 15's `bandwidth_limit` is the SECOND production filter to require stateful per-route resources with **INDEPENDENT** per-route stats (after phase-11 `local_ratelimit`). Prior filters with per-route configs fall into two categories: (a) **purely declarative** (cors per-route rules; header_mutation per-route mutations; csrf per-route additional_origins) — no per-route state, no per-route stats; (b) **listener-scoped state** (fault's `max_active_faults` closure-shared across all requests on the listener) — also no per-route state. Phase-11 broke the pattern by introducing per-route token bucket + per-route filterStats keyed by `*LocalRateLimit` pointer-identity via a `sync.Map` lazy-cache; ADR-0117 ratified the discipline + amended ADR-0073 (per-route override implies independent stateful resources).

Phase-15 inherits ADR-0117's machinery VERBATIM with two domain-specific extensions:

1. **`enable_mode: DISABLED` as the disable mechanism** (per SPEC §1.1 amendment 1 + §11.P12 + planner-time decision 5). Unlike phase-11's local_ratelimit which has no DISABLED equivalent (the disable surface is `filter_enabled: 0%` at the runtime-feature-flag layer), phase-15's `BandwidthLimit_EnableMode` enum exposes a canonical `DISABLED` value that produces wholly-inactive semantics: namespace IS registered (all 14 stat names land on the Registry) BUT no counter is ever incremented because requestActive/responseActive both stay false at DecodeHeaders. Both listener-level `enable_mode: DISABLED` (no per-route override) and per-route `enable_mode: DISABLED` (override the listener) produce identical wire output (full passthrough) + identical counter footprint (namespace allocated, zeros across the board); the parity is asserted at Group 7's `TestPerRoute_DisableViaListenerDISABLED_ParityWithPerRoute`.

2. **Per-route gauges (not just counters)**. Phase-11's filterStats surface was counter-only (4 counters; ADR-0118); phase-15's filterStats surface is 8 counters + 6 gauges (per ADR-0138 + SPEC §1.1 amendment 7). The post-Freeze idempotent registration discipline therefore needs a `NewGaugeIfAbsent` counterpart to phase-11's `NewCounterIfAbsent`. The BRAINSTORM-time concern (§11.P1) hypothesized a 5th canonical TPFC pattern; SPEC §11.P1 REFUTED this — phase-15 uses the SAME `BandwidthLimit` proto for both listener-level and per-route TPFC entries (NO `BandwidthLimitPerRoute` wrapper exists in upstream Envoy v1.37.2). ADR-0125 §(xi) (LANDED at SPEC commit `49e0361`) documents the NEW 6th canonical pattern phase-15 introduces — bare-message-via-TPFC + code-level-required-`limit_kbps`-at-per-route — distinct from the 4 prior ADR-0117 canonical patterns AND the 5th canonical (ADR-0125's PerRoute-wrapper pattern).

The BRAINSTORM-hypothesized 5th canonical (a hypothetical `BandwidthLimitPerRoute` wrapper proto) is REFUTED at SPEC §11.P1 (verbatim probe at `/tmp/p15-pins/probeA-pgv.txt`); phase-15 inherits the 4th canonical (ADR-0117 bare-message-via-TPFC for the SAME proto) + introduces the NEW 6th canonical (the same shape PLUS a code-level extra check at the per-route position for `limit_kbps` REQUIRED per amendment 4 + SPEC §11.P1).

The `sync.Map` lazy-cache + LoadOrStore race-safety contract per phase-11's `local_ratelimit.go:305-337` is reused verbatim with `*LocalRateLimit` → `*BandwidthLimit` and `buildRuntimeConfigPerRoute` → `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute` substitutions. ADR-0117 IMPL-1's lazy-cache keying via `*ProtoType` pointer-identity is the canonical race-safe shape; LoadOrStore's winner-takes-all semantic GC's the loser's `*compiledConfig` (its registered Registry entries are NOT GC'd — they're already in the Registry — but they're idempotent and equivalent to the winner's via `NewCounterIfAbsent`/`NewGaugeIfAbsent`'s pointer-identity guarantee, so the winner and loser observe the same Counter/Gauge instances).

### Decision

**(i) Per-route stats are INDEPENDENT from listener-level stats (NOT shared).** Per SPEC §5 + §11.P4 empirical pin + ADR-0117 precedent. Each `*BandwidthLimit` TPFC entry resolves to its own `*compiledConfig` carrying its own `*filterStats` (8 counters + 6 gauges) under the per-route `stat_prefix` namespace. Listener-level state is fully shadowed for per-route reqs — listener-level counters do NOT increment for per-route reqs (SPEC §11.P4 verbatim empirical observation; mirrors phase-11 SPEC §11.6). Phase-15 is the **SECOND row** using INDEPENDENT-stats per ADR-0117 precedent. Future stateful per-route filters with stat-emission requirements pick this row's discipline (NOT the phase-14 ADR-0132 compressor's per-route SHARED-stats discipline, which applies to filters whose per-route override is structurally subsidiary to the listener-level stat-emission shape).

**(ii) Per-route allocation via `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute` + `newFilterStatsIfAbsent`.** Per SPEC §6.11. The `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute(c *bandwidthlimitv3.BandwidthLimit, reg *stats.Registry) (*compiledConfig, error)` helper is the per-route variant of `buildCompiledConfig` invoked from `resolvePerRouteConfig` at lazy-cache LoadOrStore time. Mirrors phase-11 `buildRuntimeConfigPerRoute` structurally; delegates to `buildCompiledConfig(c, FactoryCtx{Stats: reg}, isPerRoute=true)` so the validation path + the CODE-LEVEL `limit_kbps` REQUIRED extra check + the `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` stat-allocation path land via a single code path. The `nolint:unused` annotation flagged at Task 2 is REMOVED at this commit; the helper is now live.

`newFilterStatsIfAbsent(reg, prefix)` is the post-Freeze-idempotent stat-allocation helper. All 14 stats (8 counters via `NewCounterIfAbsent` + 6 gauges via `NewGaugeIfAbsent`) are registered idempotently — re-calls against the same `stat_prefix` (e.g., multi-resolve against the same per-route TPFC pointer, though the `sync.Map` lazy-cache short-circuits before re-call in production) observe pointer-identical Counter/Gauge instances per the Registry's `byName` map. NOT to be confused with `newFilterStats` (the listener-level variant which uses panic-on-duplicate `NewCounter`/`NewGauge` — appropriate for boot-time registration before Freeze).

**(iii) `sync.Map` lazy-cache keyed by `*BandwidthLimit` pointer-identity per ADR-0117 IMPL-1.** Per SPEC §6.11. `factoryState.perRoute sync.Map` (typed `map[*bandwidthlimitv3.BandwidthLimit]*compiledConfig`) is the lazy-cache. `resolvePerRouteConfig(msg proto.Message) *compiledConfig` mirrors phase-11 `local_ratelimit.go:305-337` verbatim with type substitutions: (a) on `msg == nil` return `s.listenerRC` (no per-route → inherit listener); (b) on `msg.(*BandwidthLimit)` type-assertion failure return `s.listenerRC` (unexpected message type → inherit listener); (c) `s.perRoute.Load(perRoute)` returns cached entry on hit; (d) on miss, `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute` allocates fresh; on parse failure (request-time, NOT boot-time) return `s.listenerRC` per ADR-0072 boot-fail-fast applies only at New (NOT at request-time); (e) `s.perRoute.LoadOrStore(perRoute, fresh)` is race-safe — LoadOrStore winner stores; loser's `fresh` is GC'd; both goroutines observe the winner's `*compiledConfig`. The single allocation under multi-resolve invariant is asserted at Group 7's `TestPerRoute_LazyCache_SyncMapKey` (N=10 sequential + 8 concurrent resolves; sync.Map entries count == 1).

**(iv) NEW 6th canonical pattern documented at ADR-0125 §(xi).** The bare-message-via-TPFC + code-level-required-`limit_kbps` pattern phase-15 introduces is canonical and reusable: future filters whose upstream Envoy proto-shape lacks a `*PerRoute` wrapper AND whose per-route discipline requires a runtime-config field that the listener-level proto-decode treats as OPTIONAL adopt this row's pattern. The §(xi) amendment paragraph LANDED at SPEC commit `49e0361` codifies the pattern; ADR-0136 ratifies the CODE-LEVEL extra check error wording. The 4 prior ADR-0117 canonical patterns (4th canonical bare-message-via-TPFC without code-level extra check; 1st-3rd canonical with PerRoute wrappers) remain unchanged; ADR-0125 §(xi) extends the catalog.

**(v) `enable_mode: DISABLED` is the disable mechanism (per SPEC §1.1 amendment 1 + §11.P12 + planner-time decision 5).** Phase-15 does NOT introduce a `runtime_enabled`-coupled disable surface (per planner-time decision 7 + ADR-0136 §Decision (ii) silent-ignore discipline; the field IS parsed but always-100%-active at runtime). The disable surface IS the `BandwidthLimit_EnableMode` enum's `DISABLED` value. Both listener-level `enable_mode: DISABLED` and per-route `enable_mode: DISABLED` produce IDENTICAL observable behavior:
- Wire output: full passthrough (DataContinue on every DecodeData/EncodeData call; no timer arm).
- Counter footprint: namespace IS registered (all 14 stat names land on the Registry under the resolved `stat_prefix`); counters are NEVER incremented (requestActive/responseActive both stay false; the increment-arming paths are short-circuited at the gate).
- Gauge footprint: pending/incoming_size/allowed_size all stay at 0 across the stream lifecycle.

Parity is asserted unit-test-only (NOT in the differential fixture per planner-time decision 5 + §12 deferred #5; fixture 0017 scenario 5 covers the per-route DISABLED shape; an equivalent listener-level scenario is unit-test-only since the listener-level config in fixture 0017 has `enable_mode: REQUEST_AND_RESPONSE` per SPEC §7.2). The Group 7 `TestPerRoute_DisableViaListenerDISABLED_ParityWithPerRoute` test exercises both code paths in the same test body + asserts wire-shape + counter-footprint equivalence.

### Alternatives considered

**(a) Per-route SHARED-stats (rejected per §11.P4 empirical pin).** A hypothetical alternative would have per-route TPFC entries inherit the listener-level `*filterStats` pointer (i.e., per-route requests would increment listener-level counters under the listener-level `stat_prefix` namespace). This is the discipline phase-14 ADR-0132 compressor adopted for its per-route shape — appropriate there because the compressor's per-route override is structurally subsidiary to the listener-level stat-emission shape (the per-route surface is just a `disabled: true` toggle in the compressor's CompressorPerRoute message). Phase-15's per-route surface is structurally co-equal with the listener (the SAME `BandwidthLimit` proto is reused; the per-route entry can carry an entirely distinct `stat_prefix`, `enable_mode`, `limit_kbps`, `fill_interval`). SPEC §11.P4 empirical-pinned reference Envoy emits SEPARATE Prometheus counter series keyed by per-route `stat_prefix`; SHARED-stats would diverge. REJECTED.

**(b) Per-route stat namespace under the listener-level `stat_prefix` (rejected per ADR-0117 + §11.P11).** A second hypothetical alternative would prefix per-route counters under the listener-level namespace (e.g., listener `foo` + per-route `bar` → `foo.bar.http_bandwidth_limit.*` instead of `bar.http_bandwidth_limit.*`). REJECTED per ADR-0117 precedent: phase-11 uses the per-route `stat_prefix` flat (NO listener-prefix nesting); phase-15 matches verbatim. The SN10 Prometheus rendering rule (lands at Task 8 + ADR-0138) flattens the per-route `stat_prefix` to `envoy_<stat_prefix>_http_bandwidth_limit_<counter>{}` directly; nesting under listener-prefix would require a different SN10 rule shape (out of scope for phase-15).

**(c) Eager pre-allocation: walk all per-route TPFCs at HCM-build-time + pre-allocate `*compiledConfig` instances (rejected per ADR-0117 precedent).** Phase-11 rejected this — the framework's existing `BuildPerRouteConfig` parses TPFCs into `proto.Message` slots in the per-route map; extending it to call back into per-filter factory hooks (analogous to phase-10's per-route-validator) is heavier than the lazy-cache approach. The lazy-cache is structurally lighter (~30 LoC for the helper pair) vs the eager-walk (~100+ LoC). Phase-15 inherits the lazy-cache discipline verbatim.

**(d) Defer per-route bucket independence to phase 15.1 (rejected; explicit ADR-0045 single-row position).** SPEC §1.7 + §15 lock the single-row position (phase 15 ≠ 15.1 split). Per-route INDEPENDENT-stats is structurally on the critical path for fixture 0017 scenario 5 (per-route stat_prefix override + wire-output verification under per-route limits). REJECTED.

### Consequences

- **Phase-15 is the SECOND row using INDEPENDENT-stats per ADR-0117 precedent** (phase-11 local_ratelimit is the FIRST). Future stateful per-route filters with stat-emission requirements pick the row's discipline per the per-route override structural shape: if the override is structurally co-equal with the listener (SAME proto reused; full stat_prefix override expected) → INDEPENDENT-stats (this ADR); if the override is structurally subsidiary (PerRoute wrapper with a narrow toggle surface) → SHARED-stats (ADR-0132 compressor row). The catalog growth: 4th canonical (ADR-0117 + INDEPENDENT-stats) + 5th canonical (ADR-0125 + SHARED-stats default) + 6th canonical (this ADR-0139: bare-message-via-TPFC + code-level-required-`limit_kbps` + INDEPENDENT-stats).
- **`NewGaugeIfAbsent` is the NEW gauge-counterpart helper landed at `internal/stats/registry.go`.** ~25 LoC additive helper mirroring `NewCounterIfAbsent` verbatim (panic-on-invalid-name preserved; r.mu serializes read+register; existing-name-as-non-Gauge → panic with clear message). The ZERO-framework-deltas claim per SPEC §1.7 stays intact: phase-15 adds a missing-pair helper to existing infrastructure (the framework's stats Registry was already designed for post-Freeze idempotent registration via the `byName` map + r.mu discipline — phase-11 surfaced the counter path; phase-15 surfaces the gauge path). 4 unit tests at `internal/stats/registry_test.go` validate registers-when-absent + returns-existing + bypasses-freeze + type-mismatch panic.
- **The `//nolint:unused` annotation on `buildCompiledConfigPerRoute` is REMOVED at this commit.** The helper is now live (consumed from `resolvePerRouteConfig` at the lazy-cache LoadOrStore path; the live wiring landed at Task 4 but the lint annotation was retained pending ADR-0139 ratification at this Task 7 commit).
- **Group 7 unit tests (5 tests; ~280 LoC) verify the per-route INDEPENDENT-stats wiring + DISABLED-mode parity + lazy-cache contract** per SPEC §14.1 Group 7. The 5 tests: (1) `TestPerRoute_IndependentStats_Allocated` — pointer-distinct *filterStats + all 14 stat names under per-route namespace; (2) `TestPerRoute_IndependentStats_ListenerUnaffected` — listener counters stay at 0 while per-route counters increment under per-route route flow; (3) `TestPerRoute_DisableViaEnableModeDISABLED_NoCounterIncrements` — per-route DISABLED wholly-inactive (namespace registered, counters stay 0); (4) `TestPerRoute_DisableViaListenerDISABLED_ParityWithPerRoute` — listener-level DISABLED + per-route DISABLED produce identical wire + counter footprints; (5) `TestPerRoute_LazyCache_SyncMapKey` — N=10 sequential + 8 concurrent resolves against the same `*BandwidthLimit` pointer hit a single sync.Map entry. All 5 PASS under `go test -race -count=1`.
- **Differential fixture 0017 scenario 5** (lands at Tasks 11-14) mechanically validates the empirical claim per SPEC §11.P4 + §11.P12 (per-route counters increment independently from listener-level counters; per-route DISABLED is wholly-inactive). The listener-level DISABLED shape is unit-test-only per planner-time decision 5 + §12 deferred #5.
- **The post-Freeze gauge-idempotency path is now fully exercised** at the next Task 8 commit (which lands the listener-level full filterStats integration test asserting all 14 stat names registered on the Registry). Phase-15's full stat surface codification per ADR-0138 builds on this row's `NewGaugeIfAbsent` helper.
- **ADR-0117's "future stateful per-route filters reuse the lazy-cache + `NewCounterIfAbsent` pattern; phase-11's `state.resolvePerRouteConfig` + `buildRuntimeConfigPerRoute` are the canonical reference" claim** is RATIFIED at this commit: phase-15 IS the future row that reused the pattern, with the natural per-domain extensions (NewGaugeIfAbsent + 6th canonical bare-message-via-TPFC + DISABLED-mode disable surface). The patterns held across 4 phases (phase-11 → phase-12 csrf → phase-13 buffer → phase-14 compressor → phase-15 bandwidth_limit) without requiring framework surgery.

## ADR-0140: `internal/filter/http/rbac/` package shape — single-token directory matching the cors / fault / csrf / buffer / compressor / localratelimit / bandwidthlimit precedent + DECODER-only `HTTPFilter` value (`Encoder: nil`; 3rd §9 row to ship pure decode-side per phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer precedent) + 4-base-counter `filterStats` (per §1.1 amendment 8 + §11.P6 — REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis; NO `logged` counter; LOG-partial folds into `allowed`) + lazy per-policy counter allocation via `NewCounterIfAbsent` post-Freeze (mirrors phase-11 ADR-0117 + phase-15 ADR-0139) + deny-path wire shape `SendLocalReply(403, "RBAC: access denied", {Content-Type: text/plain})` per §1.1 amendment 10 + §11.P5 (19-byte ASCII body verbatim + 4-header set lowercase wire-form + keep-alive) + boot-registration ordering (alphabetical-after-localratelimit)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — phase-13 + phase-15 precedent; this ADR is authored AT impl-time at its anchor Task 2, NOT pre-landed at SPEC commit); ADR-0072 (HTTPRegistry threaded constructor map; phase-16 inserts the 11th `rbac` registration after the existing 10 entries); ADR-0074 (filter set; purely additive expansion); ADR-0075 + ADR-0076 (HCM dispatch + framework body-buffer cap — UNCHANGED; rbac is decoder-only + pre-body, no body-buffering interaction); ADR-0100 + ADR-0101 + ADR-0102 (FactoryCtx framework extension + runtimeConfig closure-capture + StopIteration localReplyDone gate — CONSUMED for boot-time stat registration + SendLocalReply on DENY); ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 (post-Freeze idempotent `NewCounterIfAbsent` for lazy per-policy counter allocation — pattern phase-16 inherits as the THIRD row using INDEPENDENT per-route stats after phase-11 local_ratelimit FIRST + phase-15 bandwidth_limit SECOND); ADR-0118 + ADR-0123 + ADR-0132 + ADR-0138 (stat surface precedents — counter-only NewCounterIfAbsent path for the 4 base counters; NO gauges unlike phase-15's 14-stat surface); ADR-0125 §(xii) amendment (anchored at Task 10 — 7th canonical absent-implies-disabled-OR-wholesale-override per-route pattern; phase-16 introduces).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 2

### Context

Phase 16's `rbac` filter is the ELEVENTH HTTP filter (§9 row 11; after router + bandwidth_limit + buffer + compressor + cors + csrf + envoygotest + fault + header_mutation + local_ratelimit) and the THIRD pure decode-side filter (after phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer). Reference Envoy v1.37.2's `envoy.filters.http.rbac` is the canonical "role-based access control" filter — a pre-body request gate that evaluates Permission/Principal rules at DecodeHeaders and dispatches ALLOW → continue / DENY → 403 LocalReply / LOG → continue + access-log hint (envoy-go MVP folds LOG into ALLOW per §1.1 amendment 5; no dynamic-metadata family yet — see ADR-0146).

Phase-16 anchors at this ADR-0140 the package's SHAPE invariants: directory naming, file structure, HTTPFilter value (decoder-only), filterStats counter surface, and boot-registration ordering. The package's TYPE-LEVEL invariants (compiledConfig 8-field shape + dual-engine dispatch + UDPA-field_alias-annotation framing + PGV-mirror validation + CEL/audit_logging_options silent-ignore) anchor at the sibling ADR-0141. The two together fully constrain Task 2's `internal/filter/http/rbac/{doc.go,rbac.go,rbac_test.go}` SKELETON deliverable; the matcher-engine wiring (ADR-0142 at Task 3), Permission/Principal evaluator surface (ADR-0143 across Tasks 4 + 5), TLS-principal accessor framework primitive (ADR-0144 at Task 6), stat surface finalization (ADR-0145 at Task 8), and shadow + LOG-partial + per-policy emission discipline (ADR-0146 at Task 9) land at their respective impl-time anchor tasks per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. The ADR-0125 §(xii) amendment paragraph (7th canonical per-route pattern) lands at Task 10 per planner-time decision 14.

The package shape mirrors the established single-token directory convention (cors / fault / csrf / buffer / compressor / localratelimit / bandwidthlimit precedent — NO subdirectories for sub-files; the package fits in ONE flat directory with doc.go + rbac.go + evaluator.go + rbac_test.go + fuzz_test.go landing across Tasks 2–11). The HTTPFilter value sets Decoder: f, Encoder: nil — rbac is a pre-body request gate; the disposition is computed at DecodeHeaders BEFORE the body flows; no encode-side path. Mirrors phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer decoder-only precedent (phase-16 is the 3rd §9 row to ship pure decode-side).

The filterStats surface is 4-base-counter + variable per-policy lazy-allocated. SPEC §11.P6 empirical pin RATIFIED 4-counter, REFUTED the BRAINSTORM-time 5-counter hypothesis that posited a separate `logged` counter for LOG-action matches. Per Envoy v1.37.2 source (`utility.h::incPolicyAllowed/Denied/ShadowAllowed/ShadowDenied`), LOG-partial folds into `allowed` — the 4 base counters are `allowed` / `denied` / `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied`. The per-policy lazy-allocation discipline (allocate `<base_prefix>.<policy_name>.<suffix>` counters via `NewCounterIfAbsent` on first match when `track_per_rule_stats: true`) mirrors phase-11 ADR-0117's post-Freeze idempotent counter pattern verbatim. NO gauges — unlike phase-15 bandwidth_limit's 14-stat surface (8 counters + 6 gauges per ADR-0138); phase-16 inherits ADR-0117's counter-only precedent.

The deny-path wire shape is `SendLocalReply(403, "RBAC: access denied", {Content-Type: text/plain})` per §1.1 amendment 10 + §11.P5 empirical pin: byte-exact 19-byte ASCII body + 4-header set lowercase wire-form (content-length: 19 / content-type: text/plain / date / server: envoy) + keep-alive disposition (no Connection: close). The 19-byte invariant is a Group 6 test assertion at Task 7.

Boot-registration ordering: the `httpReg.Register(rbac.TypeURL, rbac.New)` line inserts ALPHABETICALLY-after-localratelimit in `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` at Task 11 — the resulting block reads `router → bandwidthlimit → buffer → compressor → cors → csrf → envoygotest → fault → header_mutation → localratelimit → rbac` per the established router-first-then-alphabetical stylistic discipline.

### Decision

**(i) Single-token directory `internal/filter/http/rbac/`.** Mirrors cors / fault / csrf / buffer / compressor / localratelimit / bandwidthlimit precedent. NO subdirectories (e.g., NOT `internal/filter/http/rbac/permission/`, NOT `internal/filter/http/rbac/principal/`). The package files at impl-completion: `doc.go` (package overview; Task 2) + `rbac.go` (main filter file — public surface + factory + types + DecodeHeaders body + filterStats; Task 2 SKELETON, Task 7 DecodeHeaders body + Task 8 filterStats finalization) + `evaluator.go` (Permission + Principal evaluator surface; Task 4 Permission + Task 5 Principal) + `rbac_test.go` (unit tests; ~900-1100 LoC across Groups 1–9 landing across Tasks 2 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 + 9) + `fuzz_test.go` (FuzzRBACConfigParse; Task 11). Total package size ~1100-1400 LoC production + ~900-1100 LoC tests.

**(ii) Public surface (per SPEC §6.1).** `TypeURL` const = `"type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.rbac.v3.RBAC"`. `New(tc *anypb.Any, ctx envoyhttp.FactoryCtx) (envoyhttp.FilterInstanceFactory, error)` factory registered at boot via `httpReg.Register(rbac.TypeURL, rbac.New)`. Package-private const `filterName = "envoy.filters.http.rbac"` matches the listener config typed_per_filter_config map keys. Package-private const `actionTypeURL = "type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.rbac.v3.Action"` is the canonical matcher-engine terminal action TypeURL per §11.P3 + §2.6 (consumed by `buildCompiledMatcherEngine` at Task 3). Package-private const `denyBody = "RBAC: access denied"` is the 19-byte deny-path body per amendment 10 + §11.P5 (consumed by the SendLocalReply call at Task 7).

**(iii) Decoder-only `HTTPFilter` value (`Encoder: nil`).** Per SPEC §1 item 5 + §6.4. The `New` factory returns a `FilterInstanceFactory` closure that allocates a fresh `*filter` per stream + returns `envoyhttp.HTTPFilter{Name: filterName, Decoder: f, Encoder: nil}`. RBAC is a pre-body request gate; the disposition (allow/deny/log) is computed at DecodeHeaders BEFORE the request body is forwarded. No encode-side path. Mirrors phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer decoder-only precedent (phase-16 is the 3rd §9 row to ship pure decode-side). The `StreamEncoderFilter` interface is NOT implemented; the `filter` struct has NO encode-side fields. Skeleton DecodeHeaders / DecodeData / DecodeTrailers / OnDestroy method bodies at Task 2 return Continue / DataContinue / TrailersContinue / no-op respectively; the real DecodeHeaders body (per-route resolve + dual-engine dispatch + SendLocalReply 403 on DENY) lands at Task 7.

**(iv) 4-base-counter `filterStats` surface + lazy per-policy counter allocation.** Per §1.1 amendment 8 + §11.P6 empirical pin (REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis — NO `logged` counter exists in Envoy v1.37.2 source per `utility.h::incPolicyAllowed/Denied/ShadowAllowed/ShadowDenied` enumeration; LOG-partial folds into `allowed` per amendment 5). The 4 base counters per active stat-prefix combination: `allowed` (primary engine result = ALLOWED, incl. LOG-partial folds) / `denied` (primary engine result = DENIED) / `shadow_allowed` (shadow engine result = ALLOWED; when shadow configured) / `shadow_denied` (shadow engine result = DENIED).

The per-policy lazy-cache (`perPolicy *sync.Map`) is allocated empty at `newFilterStats` time; populated at first-match request time via `NewCounterIfAbsent` keyed by `<policy_name>.<suffix>` when `track_per_rule_stats: true` (mirrors phase-11 ADR-0117 + phase-15 ADR-0139 post-Freeze idempotent registration discipline; the registration shape lands at Task 9 per ADR-0146). At Task 2 the struct is DECLARED with the 4 base Counter pointers + the empty sync.Map + the *stats.Registry pointer; the helpers `newFilterStats` / `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` are SKELETONS that allocate the 4 base counters under a fallback `rbac.<counter>` namespace when the configured `<rules_stat_prefix>` / `<shadow_rules_stat_prefix>` is empty (per amendment 3 empty-allowed). Final namespace canonicalization per ADR-0145 SN2-reuse hypothesis lands at Task 8.

**(v) Boot-registration ordering (alphabetical-after-localratelimit).** Per ADR-0072 + the established router-first-then-alphabetical stylistic discipline. The `httpReg.Register(rbac.TypeURL, rbac.New)` line inserts at Task 11 IMMEDIATELY AFTER the existing `httpReg.Register(localratelimit.TypeURL, localratelimit.New)` line + BEFORE `header_mutation.RegisterPerRouteValidator(httpReg)` + `httpReg.Freeze()`. The resulting block reads: router → bandwidthlimit → buffer → compressor → cors → csrf → envoygotest → fault → header_mutation → localratelimit → rbac → header_mutation.RegisterPerRouteValidator → httpReg.Freeze(). 11 entries total (10 prior + 1 new). NO existing registration line moves.

**(vi) Pre-body decoder-only invariant — DecodeData / DecodeTrailers / OnDestroy are pass-through / no-op.** Per SPEC §6.8 + §1 item 5. DecodeData returns DataContinue unconditionally (no body buffering; the disposition is already computed at DecodeHeaders). DecodeTrailers returns TrailersContinue unconditionally. OnDestroy is a no-op (no async resources — unlike phase-15 bandwidth_limit's time.AfterFunc Stop-races-Fire discipline). ADR-0128's synthetic empty-terminal RunDecodeData primitive is structurally unused — rbac evaluates at DecodeHeaders before body bytes flow. ADR-0131's OverwriteBody encode-side primitive is structurally unused — rbac is encoder-nil.

### Consequences

- **Phase-16 is the THIRD `§9` row using INDEPENDENT-stats per ADR-0117 precedent** (phase-11 local_ratelimit FIRST + phase-15 bandwidth_limit SECOND + phase-16 rbac THIRD). The per-route INDEPENDENT-stats discipline anchors at sibling ADR-0145 (lands at Task 8); the lazy-cache + sync.Map LoadOrStore + buildCompiledPerRoute machinery anchors at this ADR-0140 §Decision (iv).
- **Phase-16 is the THIRD `§9` row to ship pure decode-side `HTTPFilter` value** (phase-12 csrf FIRST + phase-13 buffer SECOND + phase-16 rbac THIRD). The decoder-only invariant + Encoder: nil + skeleton DecodeData/DecodeTrailers/OnDestroy bodies are codified at §Decision (iii) + (vi); future pre-body request gates inherit the same shape.
- **ADR-0074 filter-set list grows from 10 to 11 entries** (purely additive expansion). The 11-filter roster: `bandwidthlimit / buffer / compressor / cors / csrf / envoygotest / fault / header_mutation / localratelimit / rbac / router`. NO existing filter changes; phase-16 is purely additive. ADR-0074 §Decision and §Consequences sections are left UNCHANGED in this commit; the catalog growth is recorded HERE in §Consequences (per the established cross-reference convention).
- **ADR-0072 HTTPRegistry threaded constructor map gains the 11th rbac entry at Task 11.** The boot-registration ordering (alphabetical-after-localratelimit per §Decision (v)) preserves the established stylistic discipline. NO framework surgery required; the existing `httpReg.Register(typeURL, factory)` API serves verbatim.
- **The 4-base-counter shape is the SECOND `§9` row to ship counter-only stats** (after phase-11 local_ratelimit's 4-counter surface per ADR-0118; phase-15 bandwidth_limit's 14-stat surface per ADR-0138 is the §9 outlier with gauges; phase-12/13/14 csrf/buffer/compressor are intermediate). The lazy per-policy counter allocation via NewCounterIfAbsent post-Freeze (codified at §Decision (iv)) is structurally distinct from phase-11's fixed 4-counter surface — variable-N growth on operator-config `track_per_rule_stats: true`. Phase-16 is the FIRST §9 row to ship variable-N counter cardinality from operator config (the foot-gun is documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 + recorded at ADR-0145).
- **The deny-path wire shape `SendLocalReply(403, "RBAC: access denied", {Content-Type: text/plain})` is the SECOND `§9` row to ship a non-CORS local-reply** (after phase-12 csrf's `SendLocalReply(403, "Invalid CSRF token", ...)`). The 19-byte byte-exact body + 4-header set lowercase wire-form + keep-alive disposition mirrors phase-12 csrf's wire shape modulo the body string. Task 7's Group 6 tests verify byte-exact parity with reference Envoy v1.37.2 per §11.P5 empirical pin.
- **Skeleton method bodies at Task 2 (DecodeHeaders → Continue / DecodeData → DataContinue / DecodeTrailers → TrailersContinue / OnDestroy → no-op) compile cleanly + the StreamDecoderFilter interface assertion `var _ envoyhttp.StreamDecoderFilter = (*filter)(nil)` holds.** The real DecodeHeaders body lands at Task 7 per ADR-0141 + ADR-0146; the bandwidth_limit precedent (phase-15's Task 2 skeleton with Tasks 4 + 5 body-fills) is the closest analog.
- **Group 1 + Group 2 unit tests at Task 2 (17 + 7 = 24 cases) PASS under `go test -race -count=1`** verifying: New factory nil/malformed-tc errors; buildCompiledConfig all 7 outer fields accepted; dual-engine dispatch rules-wins-when-both-set; both shadow set → shadow_rules wins; neither set → wholly inactive; empty rules_stat_prefix / shadow_rules_stat_prefix accepted; all 3 action enum values (ALLOW/DENY/LOG) accepted; invalid action enum rejected; empty permissions / principals rejected; lexicographic policy order preserved; audit_logging_options silent-ignored; condition / checked_condition silent-ignored (the cel_config third CEL field is structurally absent in go-control-plane v1.32.4 — test SKIPped per approach (b) BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT; re-activates if module bumps expose the field); parsePerRoute case (a) / case (b) / malformed-Any disposition; buildCompiledPerRoute INDEPENDENT-stats invariant; resolvePerRouteConfig nil-msg fallback + lazy-cache sync.Map pointer-identity contract. ALL 24 PASS at this commit.
