## ADR-0141: `compiledConfig` shape + 7-consumed proto-faithful field decomposition (per §1.1 amendment 1; outer envelope has NO silent-ignored set — the silent-ignore lives one level deeper inside `config.rbac.v3.RBAC`) + dual-engine dispatch table (`rules` xor `matcher`; rules-wins-when-both-set per §1.1 amendment 2 + `rbac.pb.go:38`; `shadow_rules` xor `shadow_matcher` analogous) + UDPA-`field_alias`-annotation framing (NOT a Go-level oneof; the .pb.go binding generates as two independent optional fields with FILTER-SOURCE-ENFORCED precedence) + envoy-go-side defensive PGV-mirror validation (per amendment 4 — action enum defined_only; policies.permissions/principals min_items=1; envoy-go-own error wording per phase-11 ADR-0115 + phase-15 ADR-0136 precedent) + ALLOW + DENY + LOG-partial action enum (per amendment 5 LOG-partial = always-allow + match-runs + matched-policy captured + `access_log_hint` metadata silent + `allowed` counter increments per amendment 8 — folds into `allowed` since LOG always-allows) + CEL three-field silent-ignore (per amendment 6 — `condition` + `checked_condition` + `cel_config`; refines BRAINSTORM §2.7 two-field claim) + `audit_logging_options` silent-ignore (per §2.1.1)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — phase-13 + phase-15 precedent; this ADR is authored AT impl-time at its anchor Task 2); ADR-0040 (out-of-scope deferrals format — silent-ignore discipline for audit_logging_options + 3 CEL fields); ADR-0073 (typed_per_filter_config 3-tier merge — most-specific override; phase-16's per-route discipline inherits ADR-0073's wholesale-not-merge semantic for case (b)); ADR-0085 (Registry nil-tolerance — `if ctx.Stats != nil` gate at buildCompiledConfig caller-side); ADR-0101 (closure-capture-at-New + read-only-shared-after-New discipline); ADR-0115 + ADR-0126 + ADR-0136 (envoy-go-own error wording discipline — phase-11 / phase-13 / phase-15 PGV-mirror clear-text-error precedent).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 2

### Context

ADR-0141 codifies the TYPE-LEVEL invariants of the rbac package: the `compiledConfig` 8-field shape + the dual-engine dispatch table (rules xor matcher with rules-wins precedence + shadow_rules xor shadow_matcher with shadow_rules-wins precedence) + the UDPA-field_alias-annotation framing rationale + the envoy-go-side defensive PGV-mirror validation discipline + the ALLOW/DENY/LOG-partial action enum semantic + the CEL three-field silent-ignore + the audit_logging_options silent-ignore. Sibling ADR-0140 anchors the SHAPE-LEVEL invariants (directory + HTTPFilter value + filterStats counter surface + boot-registration ordering); the two ADRs together fully constrain Task 2's deliverable.

The outer `envoy.extensions.filters.http.rbac.v3.RBAC` proto has 7 fields per §1.1 amendment 1 (proto-faithful): `rules` / `matcher` / `shadow_rules` / `shadow_matcher` / `rules_stat_prefix` / `shadow_rules_stat_prefix` / `track_per_rule_stats`. ALL 7 are consumed at parse time. The outer envelope has NO silent-ignored set — the silent-ignore (CEL three fields + audit_logging_options) lives one level deeper inside `config.rbac.v3.RBAC` per the proto tree's two-level wrap. This is structurally distinct from the SPEC §1.1 amendment 1 outer-envelope analysis SPEC § analogs at phase-13/14/15 (which had silent-ignored fields directly on the outer envelope).

The dual-engine dispatch (rules + matcher; shadow_rules + shadow_matcher) is annotated in upstream proto via the UDPA `field_alias` annotation pattern — but the `.pb.go` binding generates as two INDEPENDENT OPTIONAL fields, NOT as a Go-level `oneof`. SPEC §11.P1 RATIFIED this finding: the proto comment at `rbac.pb.go:38` "When both rules and matcher are configured, rules will be ignored" is FILTER-SOURCE-ENFORCED precedence — the parser sees both fields as set; the filter source code (Envoy's `Config::Config`) discriminates with `if (rules) { ... } else if (matcher) { ... }`. Phase-16 mirrors this discipline at `buildCompiledConfig`: the dispatch table is `case c.GetRules() != nil → rules` / `case c.GetMatcher() != nil → matcher` / `default → wholly inactive`. Analogous for shadow.

Envoy-go-side defensive PGV-mirror validation per amendment 4: although the proto-typed enum can hold only values in the .pb.go generated set after a successful Unmarshal, defensive checks guard against future enum extensions + make the invariant explicit at the envoy-go boundary. Phase-16 mirrors phase-11 ADR-0115 + phase-15 ADR-0136 envoy-go-own error wording discipline (clear-text error messages distinct from Envoy's exact phrasing). The 3 PGV-mirror checks at Task 2: (a) action enum defined_only (ALLOW=0 / DENY=1 / LOG=2); (b) per-policy permissions min_items=1; (c) per-policy principals min_items=1. The destination_port lte=65535 check is at the Permission evaluator surface (Task 4); the deprecated/extension-coupling PARSE-REJECT checks (Permission_Metadata + Permission_Matcher + Permission_UriTemplate + Principal_SourceIp + Principal_Metadata + Principal_Custom) land at Tasks 4 + 5 per ADR-0143.

The ALLOW/DENY/LOG action enum semantic per amendment 5: ALLOW match → ALLOWED; DENY match → DENIED; LOG match → ALLOWED + matched-policy captured + `access_log_hint` metadata SILENT in envoy-go MVP (Envoy emits per §8.6 — divergence-window documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4). LOG-partial means: the engine evaluates ALL policies (NOT short-circuit on first match); the matched-policy is captured for per-policy emission when `track_per_rule_stats: true`; the disposition is ALWAYS ALLOWED. NO separate `logged` counter — LOG folds into `allowed` per amendment 8 + §11.P6.

CEL three-field silent-ignore per amendment 6 (REFINES BRAINSTORM §2.7 two-field claim): `Policy.condition` (CEL `v1alpha1.Expr` AST) + `Policy.checked_condition` (typechecked AST) + `Policy.cel_config` (the THIRD CEL field introduced post-v1.32.x in newer go-control-plane versions; structurally absent in v1.32.4 binding — silent-ignore is doctrinal). All three are silent-ignored at parse + runtime; the evaluator treats condition as always-true (compiled policy struct has NO condition slot; `policyMatches` at Task 7 skips condition evaluation entirely).

`audit_logging_options` silent-ignore per §2.1.1: the inner `config.rbac.v3.RBAC.audit_logging_options` field carries `[#not-implemented-hide:]` in upstream Envoy per §11.P2. Phase-16 matches Envoy v1.37.2 disposition — silent-ignored at parse + runtime. The compiledRulesEngine struct has NO audit_logging_options slot.

### Decision

**(i) `compiledConfig` 8-field shape per SPEC §6.2.** The struct fields are: `rules *compiledRulesEngine` (primary; nil when matcher set or both unset) + `matcher *compiledMatcherEngine` (primary alt; nil when rules set or wholly inactive) + `shadowRules *compiledRulesEngine` (shadow; nil when shadow_matcher set or no shadow) + `shadowMatcher *compiledMatcherEngine` (shadow alt; nil when shadow_rules set or no shadow) + `rulesStatPrefix string` (proto: rules_stat_prefix; empty permitted per amendment 3) + `shadowRulesStatPrefix string` (proto: shadow_rules_stat_prefix; empty permitted) + `trackPerRuleStats bool` (proto: track_per_rule_stats) + `stats *filterStats` (4 base counters + per-policy lazy-cache; nil when ctx.Stats is nil per ADR-0085).

**(ii) Dual-engine dispatch table (rules-wins-when-both-set per amendment 2 + `rbac.pb.go:38`).** `buildCompiledConfig` selects the primary engine via switch:
```
switch {
case c.GetRules() != nil:
    cc.rules = buildCompiledRulesEngine(c.GetRules(), "primary")
case c.GetMatcher() != nil:
    cc.matcher = buildCompiledMatcherEngine(c.GetMatcher())
default:
    // Neither set: filter is wholly inactive per rbac.pb.go:33.
}
```
Analogous for shadow:
```
switch {
case c.GetShadowRules() != nil:
    cc.shadowRules = buildCompiledRulesEngine(c.GetShadowRules(), "shadow")
case c.GetShadowMatcher() != nil:
    cc.shadowMatcher = buildCompiledMatcherEngine(c.GetShadowMatcher())
}
```
Group 1 tests `TestBuildCompiledConfig_BothRulesAndMatcherSet_RulesWins` + `TestBuildCompiledConfig_BothShadowSet_ShadowRulesWins` + `TestBuildCompiledConfig_NeitherEngineSet_WhollyInactive` verify.

**(iii) UDPA `field_alias`-annotation framing (NOT a Go-level oneof).** Per SPEC §11.P1 empirical pin. The `.pb.go` binding generates `rules` + `matcher` as two INDEPENDENT optional fields (NOT a Go `oneof`). The precedence (rules wins) is FILTER-SOURCE-ENFORCED — the parser observes both fields as set; the dispatch table at §Decision (ii) discriminates. Mirrors Envoy's C++ `Config::Config` `if (rules) { ... } else if (matcher) { ... }` body. The UDPA annotation is metadata-only at the proto level; the precedence semantic lives entirely at the filter source code.

**(iv) Envoy-go-side defensive PGV-mirror validation (per amendment 4).** Three PGV-mirror checks at `buildCompiledRulesEngine` per Task 2:
- (a) Action enum defined_only: `case rbacconfigv3.RBAC_ALLOW, rbacconfigv3.RBAC_DENY, rbacconfigv3.RBAC_LOG` — default → `"rbac: invalid action %v (must be ALLOW/DENY/LOG)"`.
- (b) Per-policy permissions min_items=1: `if len(p.GetPermissions()) == 0` → `"rbac: policy %q must have at least one permission"`.
- (c) Per-policy principals min_items=1: `if len(p.GetPrincipals()) == 0` → `"rbac: policy %q must have at least one principal"`.

Envoy-go-own error wording per phase-11 ADR-0115 + phase-15 ADR-0136 precedent (clear-text error messages distinct from Envoy's exact phrasing). Group 1 tests `TestBuildCompiledConfig_InvalidActionEnum_Rejected` + `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_EmptyPermissions_Rejected` + `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_EmptyPrincipals_Rejected` verify.

**(v) ALLOW/DENY/LOG-partial action enum semantic (per amendment 5).** The 3-value `RBAC_Action` enum drives the engine result:
- ALLOW match → engine result ALLOWED (+ `allowed` counter increments).
- ALLOW no-match → engine result DENIED (+ `denied` counter increments).
- DENY match → engine result DENIED (+ `denied` counter increments).
- DENY no-match → engine result ALLOWED (+ `allowed` counter increments).
- LOG match → engine result ALLOWED + matched-policy captured (+ `allowed` counter increments per amendment 8 folds-into).
- LOG no-match → engine result ALLOWED + no matched-policy (+ `allowed` counter increments).

NO separate `logged` counter — LOG folds into `allowed` per amendment 8 + §11.P6 (REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis). The `access_log_hint` dynamic-metadata emission for LOG-matches is SILENT in envoy-go MVP (divergence-window documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4; couples to a future dynamic-metadata family phase). Engine evaluation + counter emission land at Task 7 (DecodeHeaders body + evaluateRulesEngine + emitPrimaryCounters); ADR-0146 finalizes the LOG-partial discipline.

**(vi) CEL three-field silent-ignore (per amendment 6).** All three CEL fields silent-ignored at parse + runtime:
- `Policy.condition` (v1alpha1.Expr AST; CEL symbolic expression).
- `Policy.checked_condition` (v1alpha1.CheckedExpr; typechecked AST).
- `Policy.cel_config` (NEW per amendment 6; structurally absent in go-control-plane v1.32.4 — silent-ignore is doctrinal pending module bump).

The compiled `compiledPolicy` struct carries only `name` + `permissions` + `principals` — NO condition slot. The evaluator at Task 7's `policyMatches` does NOT consult any CEL field; the runtime treats condition as always-true. Operator divergence-window if any CEL field is set on the operator-supplied proto (Envoy v1.37.2 evaluates per Q7; envoy-go MVP silent-ignores); divergence-window documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4. Group 1 tests `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_ConditionField_SilentIgnored` + `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_CheckedConditionField_SilentIgnored` verify the silent-ignore is STRUCTURAL (the parser reads NO CEL fields; setting them on the proto does NOT alter parse outcomes). `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_CelConfigField_SilentIgnored` is SKIPped at Task 2 per approach (b) BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT (the cel_config field is not present in go-control-plane v1.32.4 proto binding; the silent-ignore disposition is structural — buildCompiledRulesEngine reads NO CEL fields; the test re-activates when the module bumps expose the field).

**(vii) `audit_logging_options` silent-ignore (per §2.1.1).** The inner `config.rbac.v3.RBAC.audit_logging_options` field is silent-ignored at parse + runtime. The compiledRulesEngine struct has NO audit_logging_options slot. Group 1 test `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_AuditLoggingOptions_SilentIgnored` verifies — setting the field on the proto does NOT produce an error; the compiled output has no slot to inspect (silent-ignore is structural). Matches Envoy v1.37.2's `[#not-implemented-hide:]` annotation per §11.P2.

### Consequences

- **The `compiledConfig` 8-field shape is the canonical reference for future filters consuming dual-engine dispatch + UDPA-field_alias-annotation framing.** Future filters that adopt the rules+matcher pattern (e.g., a hypothetical future ext_authz/ext_proc with a similar dual-engine pattern) inherit the §Decision (ii) dispatch table verbatim. The UDPA-field_alias-annotation framing (§Decision (iii)) is a proto-level metadata invariant — future filters that observe `field_alias` annotations on their proto schemas treat them as FILTER-SOURCE-ENFORCED precedence (NOT Go-level oneof).
- **The 3 PGV-mirror checks (action defined_only + permissions/principals min_items=1) anchor at this ADR-0141 §Decision (iv).** Future Permission/Principal-bearing filters that consume `config.rbac.v3.RBAC` (or sub-messages with similar PGV envelopes) inherit the defensive-mirror discipline. Envoy-go-own error wording continues phase-11 ADR-0115 + phase-15 ADR-0136 precedent (clear-text, NOT Envoy's exact phrasing).
- **The LOG-partial fold-into-allowed semantic (§Decision (v)) is structurally locked at this ADR-0141** — no separate `logged` counter; engine result ALLOWED for both LOG-match and LOG-no-match; matched-policy captured for per-policy emission per ADR-0146. BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis REFUTED at SPEC commit per §11.P6; the disposition holds at impl-time. Group 6 test `TestDecodeHeaders_LOGMatch_HeaderContinue_AllowedCounterIncremented` at Task 7 + Group 5 test `TestEvaluateRulesEngine_LogMatch_AllowedWithPolicyName` at Task 7 verify.
- **The CEL three-field silent-ignore (§Decision (vi)) is the THIRD §9 row to silent-ignore a non-trivial sub-message proto field** (after phase-15 bandwidth_limit's 3-field silent-ignore per ADR-0136 §Decision (ii); phase-13 buffer's pre-route runtime_enabled silent-ignore per ADR-0125 §(ix); phase-16 rbac's 3 CEL + audit_logging_options silent-ignore per this §Decision (vi) + (vii)). The silent-ignore discipline scales linearly with the proto surface; the divergence-window documentation at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 codifies the operator-facing impact.
- **The `audit_logging_options` silent-ignore (§Decision (vii)) matches Envoy v1.37.2's `[#not-implemented-hide:]` annotation** per §11.P2 — NO current divergence-window for this field (Envoy does NOT implement either; envoy-go matches the no-op disposition). Future re-activation couples to access-log + dynamic-metadata family phases.
- **Group 1 + Group 2 unit tests at Task 2 (24 cases total; 17 Group 1 + 7 Group 2) PASS under `go test -race -count=1`** verifying every claim in §Decision (i)–(vii). The 1 test SKIPped (`TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_CelConfigField_SilentIgnored`) is doctrinal — the cel_config field is structurally absent in go-control-plane v1.32.4 binding; the silent-ignore disposition is doctrinal per amendment 6. The SKIP is documented inline in the test body with a re-activation note for module bumps.
- **The compiledMatcherEngine type is a forward-declared placeholder at Task 2** — its `tree` field is typed `any` pending the matcher.Matcher type's introduction at Task 3 + ADR-0142. The `buildCompiledMatcherEngine` helper at Task 2 returns a sentinel error (`"rbac: matcher-engine evaluator not yet implemented at Task 2 (lands at Task 3 per ADR-0142)"`); the dual-engine dispatch path is structurally exercised by Group 1's rules-wins tests but the matcher-only path is unreached at Task 2 (no Group 1 test sets `matcher` alone; the matcher-only path tests land at Task 3 + Task 7 Group 5). Task 3 replaces the placeholder with the real `*matcher.Matcher` field + live `matcher.New(m, []string{actionTypeURL})` invocation.
- **The `buildPermissionEvaluators` + `buildPrincipalEvaluators` stubs at `internal/filter/http/rbac/evaluator.go` return empty slices with no error at Task 2** per BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT approach (a) — minimum-viable inputs exercise the dispatch path without hitting the stubs. The real switch (Permission Large 11 + 3 PARSE-REJECT; Principal Large 11 + 3 PARSE-REJECT) lands at Tasks 4 + 5 per ADR-0143. The empty-slice return preserves the dispatch-path semantic at Task 2: the compiled policy carries empty permissions/principals slices; downstream evaluateRulesEngine (Task 7) treats empty as "structurally cannot match" — but this code path is unreached at Task 2 since DecodeHeaders is a stub returning Continue without invoking the evaluator surface.

## ADR-0142: Matcher-engine evaluator framework primitive at NEW top-level package `internal/matcher/` (cross-phase reusable; future filters ext_authz / jwt_authn / oauth2 / ext_proc all consume the same `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` primitive for parts of their config surface — extending `supportedActionTypes` + widening `MatchContext` additively) — `Matcher` opaque type wrapping a parsed match-tree + `New(tree, supportedActionTypes []string) (*Matcher, error)` constructor (parse-time PARSE-REJECT for unknown terminal `Any.TypeUrl` per §11.P3 + §2.6; envoy-go-only error wording `"matcher: terminal action type %q unsupported by this caller"`) + `Evaluate(MatchContext) (*anypb.Any, error)` walker (no-match per `rbac.pb.go:43-46` proto comment returns `(nil, nil)`; caller interprets nil-result as filter-specific no-match disposition — RBAC interprets as DENY per `evaluateMatcherEngine`) + `MatchContext` interface (initial accessor subset scoped to RBAC's canonical surface per planner-time decision 17 — Header / Path / Method / SourceIP / DestinationIP / DestinationPort / RequestedServerName; widened additively by future filters per §Decision (iii))

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — phase-13 + phase-15 precedent; this ADR is authored AT impl-time at its anchor Task 3); ADR-0040 (out-of-scope deferrals format — the matcher-engine input + predicate-type set scoped to RBAC's canonical surface; additive-widening is the deferral disposition for future filters); ADR-0101 (closure-capture-at-New + read-only-shared-after-New discipline — the parsed Matcher tree is read-only post-`New`; concurrent `Evaluate` calls are safe); ADR-0115 + ADR-0126 + ADR-0136 (envoy-go-own error wording discipline — `"matcher: terminal action type %q unsupported by this caller"` follows the phase-11 / phase-13 / phase-15 PGV-mirror clear-text-error precedent).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 3

### Context

The `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` proto is the generic match-tree primitive used by multiple Envoy HTTP filters as an alternative to filter-specific config DSLs. Phase-16's `envoy.filters.http.rbac` is the FIRST envoy-go filter to consume this primitive: the outer `RBAC.matcher` field carries a `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` tree whose terminal on_match leaves dispatch a `*xds.core.v3.TypedExtensionConfig` wrapping (in the RBAC case) a `envoy.config.rbac.v3.Action` proto per §11.P3 + §2.6.

Future HTTP filters consume the same primitive: ext_authz uses `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` for its match-tree-driven action dispatch; jwt_authn for per-route provider selection; oauth2 for per-route override matching; ext_proc for processing-mode predicates. Each future consumer extends the terminal-action TypeURL allow-list with its own filter-specific terminal proto + adds new predicate accessors as needed. The cross-phase-reuse intent rules out a per-filter copy of the evaluator: a single shared primitive serving multiple filters preserves the framework-delta accretion shape per SPEC §1.7 + BRAINSTORM preference.

Location: NEW top-level `internal/matcher/` package — NOT `internal/filter/http/rbac/matcher/` (rbac-specific scope) NOR `internal/filter/http/matcher/` (HTTP-filter-scope). The package is a cross-phase reusable framework primitive that any filter (HTTP or otherwise) MAY consume; the top-level location avoids future relocation when ext_authz / jwt_authn / oauth2 / ext_proc land and would otherwise force a refactor. SPEC §11.2 carry-forward + §3.2 ratify the top-level location.

Terminal-action TypeURL discipline: the proto-level `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` permits an arbitrary `TypedExtensionConfig` at each on_match leaf. The matcher-engine evaluator itself does NOT know how to interpret a terminal action — that's the caller's responsibility. To prevent silent acceptance of arbitrary terminals (which a future caller-side dispatch would either ignore or panic on), the evaluator validates every terminal `Any.TypeUrl` at parse time against a caller-supplied `supportedActionTypes []string` allow-list. Unknown TypeURLs surface a PARSE-REJECT with verbatim envoy-go-only error `"matcher: terminal action type %q unsupported by this caller"` per §2.6 + §11.P3 + the phase-11 / phase-13 / phase-15 envoy-go-own error wording precedent.

`MatchContext` interface scope: the matcher's predicate evaluators need request-side accessors (header lookup, path, IP, etc.) to evaluate predicates against per-stream data. Filter-specific accessors (e.g., rbac's `DownstreamPrincipal()`, ext_authz's check-result, jwt_authn's decoded claims) belong on the consuming filter's per-stream state — NOT on the framework primitive's interface. The initial accessor set is scoped to RBAC's canonical predicate surface per planner-time decision 17: Header / Path / Method / SourceIP / DestinationIP / DestinationPort / RequestedServerName. Future filters widen the interface additively as new predicates land; existing implementations extend the new methods accordingly per ADR-0142 §Decision (iii). The interface is the cross-phase-reuse boundary — the matcher package imports NO filter-specific types.

### Decision

**(i) Cross-phase reusable framework primitive at NEW top-level `internal/matcher/` package.** The package exports:
- `Matcher` opaque type wrapping a parsed `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` tree (read-only post-construction).
- `New(tree *matchv3.Matcher, supportedActionTypes []string) (*Matcher, error)` constructor — parses the proto tree + validates every terminal action `Any.TypeUrl` against the caller-supplied allow-list at config-load time.
- `Evaluate(MatchContext) (*anypb.Any, error)` walker — walks the parsed tree at request time + returns the first matched terminal action `*anypb.Any` OR `(nil, nil)` per the proto comment at `rbac.pb.go:43-46` on no-match.
- `MatchContext` interface — request-side accessor abstraction implemented by each consuming filter on its per-stream `*filter` (or a thin adapter).

Phase 16's rbac filter is the FIRST consumer; future filters (ext_authz, jwt_authn, oauth2, ext_proc) consume the same primitive additively. The matcher package itself imports NO filter-specific types — the cross-phase-reuse rests on the clean `MatchContext` interface boundary.

**(ii) Parse-time PARSE-REJECT for unknown terminal `Any.TypeUrl` per §11.P3 + §2.6.** `New` walks the tree at config-load time + checks each on_match terminal leaf's `Any.TypeUrl` against the caller-supplied `supportedActionTypes` allow-list. Unknown TypeURLs surface verbatim envoy-go-only error wording `"matcher: terminal action type %q unsupported by this caller"` (printf-style with the offending TypeURL as %q-quoted). Phase-16's rbac caller supplies `[]string{"type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.rbac.v3.Action"}` (the canonical RBAC terminal per §11.P3); non-canonical terminals (e.g., a hypothetical future matcher-extension action type) PARSE-REJECT until rbac's caller-side allow-list is extended in a future phase.

Empty `supportedActionTypes` (nil or `[]string{}`) rejects every terminal — the consequence is a load-time-failure for any matcher tree carrying terminal actions, which is the correct conservative disposition for the boundary case.

**(iii) `MatchContext` additive-widening discipline (initial accessor set scoped to RBAC's canonical surface per planner-time decision 17).** Initial methods: `Header(name) (value string, present bool)` + `Path() string` + `Method() string` + `SourceIP() net.IP` + `DestinationIP() net.IP` + `DestinationPort() uint32` + `RequestedServerName() string`. The set is scoped to RBAC's canonical predicate surface — the predicates RBAC's matcher-engine actually evaluates against (per §3.2 + the empirical RBAC-config-shape surveys at §11).

Future filters widen the interface additively as new predicates land:
- ext_authz: MAY add `CheckResponseHeaders() http.Header` for matcher-driven post-check dispatch.
- jwt_authn: MAY add `DecodedClaims() map[string]any` for claim-driven matchers.
- oauth2: MAY add `OAuthToken() string` for token-presence predicates.

Each widening is structurally additive: existing implementations (rbac at phase 16) extend the new methods to return zero-value defaults (empty header set, nil claims, "") — no in-place ADR-0142 amendment is required. The cross-phase-reuse boundary preserves backward compatibility through the additive discipline.

The matcher package's internal predicate evaluators dispatch on the SinglePredicate input's `Any.TypeUrl`: header-input → `MatchContext.Header()`; future inputs route through the appropriate accessor. Adding a new input is a localised patch on the input-dispatch switch + (optionally) a new MatchContext accessor.

**(iv) Initial predicate evaluator subset (per PLAN.md line 69).** Phase-16 lands:
- SinglePredicate value-match with input `envoy.type.matcher.v3.HttpRequestHeaderMatchInput` (routes through `MatchContext.Header(name)`; HTTP/2 pseudo-headers `:path` and `:method` route via the implementer's choice — typically through `Path()` + `Method()` respectively).
- AND-predicate combinator over predicate children (short-circuit on first FALSE).
- OR-predicate combinator over predicate children (short-circuit on first TRUE).
- NOT-predicate combinator (logical negate of child).

StringMatcher subset (cncf xds variant): Exact / Prefix / Suffix / Contains / SafeRegex with `ignore_case` honored. Custom matcher extensions PARSE-REJECT in this build.

MatcherTree variant (exact/prefix-trie dispatch on input) is PARSE-REJECTED at `New`-time: RBAC's canonical config surface uses MatcherList exclusively. Adding MatcherTree support is an additive future extension per §Consequences below.

Additional inputs (DestinationIP / DestinationPort / SourceIP / ServerName via the network common-inputs package) land additively as future callers require them; the dispatch is a TypeURL-keyed switch such that adding a new input is a localised patch.

**(v) Read-only-post-`New` + concurrent-safe `Evaluate` per ADR-0101 closure-capture discipline.** The parsed tree is constructed once at `New`-time + read-only thereafter; `Evaluate` walks the cached structure without mutating shared state. Concurrent `Evaluate` invocations across goroutines are safe; the `TestMatcher_StatelessAcrossEvaluations` test verifies via 64 concurrent calls under `go test -race`.

### Consequences

- **`internal/matcher/` is the canonical home for the `xds.type.matcher.v3.Matcher` evaluator across all current + future envoy-go phases.** Future filters (ext_authz, jwt_authn, oauth2, ext_proc) consume the same package + extend `supportedActionTypes` + widen `MatchContext` additively. No relocation is anticipated — the top-level location is fixed at phase 16.
- **The `"matcher: terminal action type %q unsupported by this caller"` envoy-go-only error wording is structurally locked.** Future filters do NOT customise the wording — the matcher package owns the error string. Wrapping at the caller (rbac's `buildCompiledMatcherEngine` adds `"rbac: matcher: ..."` prefix; future ext_authz's analogous helper adds `"ext_authz: matcher: ..."` prefix) preserves the inner wording for fuzzer + operator-error-pattern matching. The Group 8 test `TestMatcherNew_UnknownTypeURL_PARSE_REJECT` at Task 3 verifies the verbatim wording; the rbac-side Group 5 test `TestEvaluateMatcherEngine_UnknownTerminalTypeURL_ParseRejected` at Task 7 verifies the wrapping.
- **MatchContext widening is the additive-extension surface.** Future ADRs that widen MatchContext (e.g., ext_authz adding `CheckResponseHeaders()`) do NOT amend ADR-0142 in-place — they author standalone ADRs that document the new accessor + the additive-extension discipline. The cross-phase-reuse boundary stays stable.
- **The MatcherList-only restriction (§Decision (iv)) is a structural deferral.** Future matcher-extension-family phases that need MatcherTree (exact/prefix-trie dispatch) land that variant additively. The current PARSE-REJECT disposition is conservative: the alternative (silent-accept MatcherTree as a no-op) would surface as a runtime no-match, which violates the parse-time-fail-fast discipline per ADR-0072.
- **Per-phase test coverage anchors at Task 3 + Task 7 (Group 8 + Group 5 subset).** Task 3's `matcher_test.go` covers the framework-primitive surface: `TestNew_CanonicalActionTerminal_Accepted`, `TestNew_UnknownTerminalTypeURL_PARSE_REJECT`, `TestNew_EmptyAllowList_AllTerminalsRejected`, `TestEvaluate_*` (header / path / AND / OR / nested-depth-3), `TestMatchContext_AdapterPattern`, `TestMatcher_StatelessAcrossEvaluations`. Task 7's Group 5 subset (`TestEvaluateMatcherEngine_CanonicalActionTerminal_Honored`, `TestEvaluateMatcherEngine_NoMatch_Denied`, `TestEvaluateMatcherEngine_UnknownTerminalTypeURL_ParseRejected`) covers the rbac integration through `buildCompiledMatcherEngine`.
- **rbac.go's `buildCompiledMatcherEngine` Task-2 sentinel-error STUB is REPLACED at Task 3 with the real `matcher.New(m, []string{actionTypeURL})` call.** The `compiledMatcherEngine.tree` field is RE-TYPED from `any` (Task-2 placeholder) to `*matcher.Matcher`. Both updates land in the same commit as this ADR. Task 7 wires the matcher-engine path into `evaluateEngine` dispatch via the `*matcher.Matcher.Evaluate` walker per ADR-0146.
- **`internal/matcher/` registers as the 40th go-test-race package** (phase-15 baseline 38 + phase-16's `internal/filter/http/rbac/` 39 + `internal/matcher/` 40) per SPEC §14.2. Phase-16's gate-B six-gate run includes both packages in the `go test -race -count=1 ./...` exit-0 acceptance.
- **The package boundary is the cross-phase-reuse contract.** The matcher package imports NO filter-specific types (no `internal/filter/...` imports; only stdlib + protobuf-deps + the cncf xds + envoy go-control-plane proto modules). Phase-16's rbac caller adapts its `evalContext` to `matcher.MatchContext` via a thin adapter at Task 7 (`matcherCtxAdapter` per PLAN.md line 64); future filters adapt analogously. Breaking the boundary would couple the framework primitive to a single consumer + force a refactor when subsequent consumers land.

## ADR-0143: Permission + Principal Large 11+11 evaluators + AND/OR/NOT recursive combinators + Permission/Principal evaluator interface design + deprecated-field PARSE-REJECT discipline (Permission_Metadata + Principal_SourceIp + Principal_Metadata per §11.P12; envoy-go-only divergence from Envoy v1.37.2 lenient-accept-with-deprecation-warning) + extension-coupling PARSE-REJECT (Permission_Matcher + Permission_UriTemplate + Principal_Custom — the LATTER is NEW per §1.1 amendment 7; Principal has 14 variants not 13 as BRAINSTORM hypothesized; the 14th `custom` TypedExtensionConfig couples to mTLS-extension family) + SourcedMetadata + FilterState always-no-match runtime semantic (per §2.5 + §8.10; parse-supported but evaluator returns FALSE; couples to dynamic-metadata + filter-state families) + Principal_Authenticated three-case algorithm (per §1.1 amendment 12 + §6.6 — case (a) nil principal_name + len(DownstreamPrincipal)>0 → TRUE; case (b) non-nil StringMatcher iteration over URI SAN/DNS SAN/Subject DN candidates; case (c) plaintext → FALSE) + shared-infrastructure adapter usage (PathMatcher/HeaderMatcher/StringMatcher/CidrRange evaluators local to rbac at Task 4 with tech-debt note for future extraction)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — phase-13 + phase-15 precedent; this ADR is authored AT impl-time at its anchor Tasks 4 + 5 — Task 4 lands the Permission section, Task 5 lands the Principal section + finalizes); ADR-0040 (out-of-scope deferrals format — the SourcedMetadata + FilterState parse-supported-runtime-FALSE disposition; the 6 PARSE-REJECT deferrals for deprecated + extension variants); ADR-0101 (closure-capture-at-New + read-only-shared-after-New discipline — every evaluator tree is constructed once at `New`-time via `buildPermissionEvaluators` / `buildPrincipalEvaluators`; concurrent per-stream `evaluatePermission` / `evaluatePrincipal` calls are race-safe); ADR-0115 + ADR-0126 + ADR-0136 (envoy-go-only-check + PGV-mirror clear-text-error precedent — the 6 PARSE-REJECT error strings follow the phase-11 / phase-13 / phase-15 envoy-go-own-error precedent verbatim).
**Lands-in-task:** Tasks 4 + 5

### Context

`envoy.config.rbac.v3.Policy` carries two parallel oneof-rich expression trees: `permissions` (the action-side rules — what the request asks to do) and `principals` (the actor-side rules — who is asking). Each tree is a recursive composition of evaluator variants over a Permission/Principal proto oneof. Per the v1.32.4 go-control-plane proto bindings + SPEC §6.5 + §1.1 amendments 7 + 12, the canonical surfaces are:

- **Permission Large 11** (per `rbac.pb.go:1500+`): `any`, `header`, `url_path`, `destination_ip`, `destination_port`, `destination_port_range`, `requested_server_name`, `and_rules`, `or_rules`, `not_rule`, `sourced_metadata`. Plus 3 DEFERRED variants (`metadata` deprecated; `matcher` + `uri_template` extension TypedExtensionConfig) PARSE-REJECTed per §2.3 + §8.8 + §11.P12.
- **Principal Large 11** (per `rbac.pb.go:1100+`; per §1.1 amendment 7 — Principal has **14 variants** not 13 as BRAINSTORM hypothesized; the 14th is `custom` TypedExtensionConfig at field 12): `any`, `authenticated`, `direct_remote_ip`, `remote_ip`, `header`, `url_path`, `and_ids`, `or_ids`, `not_id`, `sourced_metadata`, `filter_state`. Plus 3 DEFERRED variants (`source_ip` deprecated; `metadata` deprecated; `custom` extension TypedExtensionConfig per amendment 7 + §8.11 NEW) PARSE-REJECTed.

The two evaluator surfaces share a common shape: each implements a small interface (`permissionEvaluator { evaluatePermission(ctx evalContext) bool }`, `principalEvaluator { evaluatePrincipal(ctx evalContext) bool }`); each carries concrete per-variant evaluator types pre-compiled at parse time; AND/OR/NOT combinators recurse over the inner Permission/Principal lists. The `evalContext` interface is implemented by the per-stream `*filter` (or an analogous adapter) exposing the request-side accessors each evaluator variant needs (header lookup, path, IP, port, SNI, TLS principal candidates, sourced-metadata, filter-state).

`Principal_Authenticated` is the load-bearing TLS-principal evaluator (per §1.1 amendment 12 + SPEC §6.6 + ADR-0144). Three-case algorithm:
- **Case (a)** `nameMatcher == nil` (no `principal_name` field set) + `len(ctx.DownstreamPrincipal()) > 0` → TRUE (matches ANY authenticated user per amendment 12).
- **Case (b)** non-nil StringMatcher iterates over the candidate slice (URI SAN first, then DNS SAN, then Subject DN per ADR-0144 priority order) → TRUE on first match.
- **Case (c)** plaintext / no client cert (empty candidate slice) → FALSE.

The TLS-principal accessor (`DownstreamPrincipal() []string` on `DecoderFilterCallbacks`) is the cross-phase-reusable framework primitive authored at ADR-0144; the Principal_Authenticated evaluator at this ADR consumes it.

Deprecated-field disposition: Envoy v1.37.2 lenient-accepts the deprecated variants (`Permission_Metadata`, `Principal_SourceIp`, `Principal_Metadata`) with a deprecation warning logged at parse time; envoy-go diverges to PARSE-REJECT per §11.P12. The divergence is intentional + envoy-go-only (per ADR-0136 envoy-go-only-check discipline): the deprecated fields' upstream semantics are unstable + the migration paths (`sourced_metadata` for `metadata`; `direct_remote_ip` / `remote_ip` for `source_ip`) are well-defined. Operators carrying deprecated configs get a clear parse-time error pointing to the canonical replacement.

Extension-coupling disposition: `Permission_Matcher` + `Permission_UriTemplate` + `Principal_Custom` are all TypedExtensionConfig variants where the payload's `Any.TypeUrl` selects a per-extension impl. envoy-go MVP carries NO extension impls for these variants — PARSE-REJECT is the conservative disposition (silent-accept would surface as runtime no-match, violating parse-time-fail-fast per ADR-0072). Future codec-extension or mTLS-extension family phases re-activate one or more by extending the per-variant switch + amending this ADR in-place.

SourcedMetadata + FilterState always-no-match runtime semantic: `Permission_SourcedMetadata` + `Principal_SourcedMetadata` + `Principal_FilterState` are parse-supported (the SourcedMetadata / FilterStateMatcher proto payloads are accepted at parse time + carried on the compiledConfig) but the evaluator ALWAYS returns FALSE at runtime per §2.5 + §8.10. The dynamic-metadata + filter-state subsystems are not yet wired in envoy-go MVP. The disposition is structural: the parse path retains the proto for forward-compatibility (an operator config carrying these fields parses successfully + the future dynamic-metadata-family phase swaps the runtime impl in-place without re-parsing). The runtime no-match is a documented divergence-window — operator configs relying on SourcedMetadata / FilterState predicates for ALLOW-policies see "phantom denies" until the runtime subsystems land.

Shared-infrastructure adapter strategy: the 4 inner matcher types (StringMatcher, HeaderMatcher, PathMatcher, CidrRange) are widely consumed across filter packages (csrf uses StringMatcher for additional_origins; phase-04/05/06 routing primitives consume HeaderMatcher / PathMatcher; the matcher-engine framework primitive at ADR-0142 carries its own StringMatcher impl for the cncf/xds variant). At Task 4 the rbac evaluator implements the canonical envoy-variant adapters locally (`matchString`, `matchHeader`, `matchPath`, `matchCidr` in `evaluator.go`) — NOT extracted to a shared package. The local-impl disposition is intentional at phase 16: extracting an `internal/stringmatcher/` package crosses a boundary that needs cross-phase brainstorm (csrf's existing inline StringMatcher consumer would need refactoring; the cncf variant in `internal/matcher` would need reconciliation). TECH-DEBT noted at PROGRESS.md Task 4 entry per REVIEW.md M-5 forward-pointer convention: a future operator-ergonomics phase MAY extract these adapters once the cross-filter consumer set stabilizes.

### Decision

**(i) Permission + Principal evaluator interfaces are minimal + per-stream-stateless.** Each evaluator implements a single boolean accessor over the per-stream `evalContext`:
```go
type permissionEvaluator interface { evaluatePermission(ctx evalContext) bool }
type principalEvaluator  interface { evaluatePrincipal(ctx evalContext)  bool }
```
The evaluators carry parse-time-validated state (matcher protos, CIDR ranges, port numbers); the `evalContext` provides request-side accessors. No state mutates across `evaluatePermission` / `evaluatePrincipal` invocations — concurrent per-stream calls are race-safe per ADR-0101.

The `evalContext` interface widens additively across Tasks 4 + 5 + 6 + 7. At **Task 4** the interface carries Permission-relevant accessors: `Header(name)`, `URLPath()`, `DestinationIP()`, `DestinationPort()`, `RequestedServerName()`. At **Task 5** the interface widens with Principal-relevant accessors: `DirectRemoteIP()`, `RemoteIP()`, `DownstreamPrincipal()` (consumed by `prinAuthenticated`), plus SourcedMetadata + FilterState accessors (returning always-empty in MVP per §Decision (iv) below). At Task 7 the `*filter` body constructs the evalContext from request headers + connection state per SPEC §6.7.

**(ii) Permission Large 11 evaluator catalogue (lands at Task 4).** The 11 accepted variants per SPEC §6.5:
- `permAny{val bool}` — matches anything when val=true; PGV `const=true` enforced at parse-time (val=false → PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-own error `"rbac: permission.any must be true (PGV const=true mirror)"`).
- `permHeader{matcher *routev3.HeaderMatcher}` — wraps the route HeaderMatcher (note: Permission.header proto field is typed as the route variant per `rbac.pb.go` v1.32.4 binding); dispatches through local `matchHeader` adapter.
- `permURLPath{matcher *matcherv3.PathMatcher}` — wraps PathMatcher; dispatches through local `matchPath` adapter (inner StringMatcher on `Path` field).
- `permDestIP{cidr *corev3.CidrRange}` — CIDR-range match against `ctx.DestinationIP()` via local `matchCidr` adapter.
- `permDestPort{port uint32}` — exact-match against `ctx.DestinationPort()`; PGV `lte=65535` enforced at parse-time.
- `permDestPortRange{start, end int32}` — `start <= port < end` half-open semantic (matches `typev3.Int32Range`'s documented contract).
- `permSNI{matcher *matcherv3.StringMatcher}` — match against `ctx.RequestedServerName()` via local `matchString` adapter.
- `permAnd{children []permissionEvaluator}` — AND-semantic short-circuit (FALSE on first child returning FALSE; empty children → TRUE per conjunction-over-empty-set).
- `permOr{children []permissionEvaluator}` — OR-semantic short-circuit (TRUE on first child returning TRUE; empty children → FALSE per disjunction-over-empty-set).
- `permNot{child permissionEvaluator}` — logical negate of child.
- `permSourcedMetadata{matcher *rbacconfigv3.SourcedMetadata}` — parse-supported; ALWAYS returns FALSE at runtime per §2.5 + §8.10.

The `buildOnePermission(p *rbacconfigv3.Permission) (permissionEvaluator, error)` switch dispatches over 14 cases (the 11 accepted variants + 3 PARSE-REJECT + nil-rule defensive). `buildPermissionEvaluators` iterates wrapping errors with `permission[%d]:` prefix.

**(iii) Principal Large 11 evaluator catalogue (lands at Task 5).** The 11 accepted variants per SPEC §6.5 + §1.1 amendments 7 + 12:
- `prinAny{val bool}` — matches anything when val=true; PGV `const=true` mirror at parse-time (val=false → PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-own error `"rbac: principal.any must be true (PGV const=true mirror)"`); mirrors permAny's defensive discipline for symmetry across the two oneofs.
- `prinAuthenticated{nameMatcher *matcherv3.StringMatcher}` — implements the three-case algorithm per §Decision (vi) below (case (a) nil nameMatcher + len(DownstreamPrincipal)>0 → TRUE / case (b) non-nil StringMatcher iterates over URI SAN → DNS SAN → Subject DN CN candidates / case (c) empty principals → FALSE).
- `prinDirectRemoteIP{cidr *corev3.CidrRange}` — CIDR-range match against `ctx.DirectRemoteIP()` (peer connection source IP, pre-XFF) via the local matchCidr adapter per §11.P18.
- `prinRemoteIP{cidr *corev3.CidrRange}` — CIDR-range match against `ctx.RemoteIP()` (XFF-resolved client IP) per §11.P18. The production *filter's RemoteIP() consumes the framework's XFF resolver when one is exposed; phase-16 MVP may return the peer addr verbatim when the framework primitive is not yet surfaced to filters (Task 7 finalizes the wiring). The two variants are distinct per the proto comment at `rbac.pb.go:1059-1069`.
- `prinHeader{matcher *routev3.HeaderMatcher}` — wraps the route HeaderMatcher (Principal.header proto field uses the same routev3.HeaderMatcher typing as Permission.header per the v1.32.4 proto binding); dispatches through the local matchHeader adapter shared with permHeader.
- `prinURLPath{matcher *matcherv3.PathMatcher}` — wraps PathMatcher; dispatches through the local matchPath adapter shared with permURLPath.
- `prinAnd{children []principalEvaluator}` — AND-semantic short-circuit (FALSE on first child returning FALSE; empty children → TRUE per conjunction-over-empty-set); mirrors permAnd semantics.
- `prinOr{children []principalEvaluator}` — OR-semantic short-circuit (TRUE on first child returning TRUE; empty children → FALSE per disjunction-over-empty-set); mirrors permOr semantics.
- `prinNot{child principalEvaluator}` — logical negate of child; mirrors permNot semantics.
- `prinSourcedMetadata{matcher *rbacconfigv3.SourcedMetadata}` — parse-supported; ALWAYS returns FALSE at runtime per §2.5 + §8.10 (mirrors permSourcedMetadata; dynamic-metadata subsystem not yet wired in envoy-go MVP).
- `prinFilterState{matcher *matcherv3.FilterStateMatcher}` — parse-supported; ALWAYS returns FALSE at runtime per §2.5 + §8.10 (filter-state subsystem not yet wired in envoy-go MVP).

The `buildOnePrincipal(p *rbacconfigv3.Principal) (principalEvaluator, error)` switch dispatches over 14 cases (the 11 accepted variants + 3 PARSE-REJECT + nil-identifier defensive). `buildPrincipalEvaluators` iterates wrapping errors with `principal[%d]:` prefix per §6.5. Each AND/OR combinator recursive call goes back through `buildPrincipalEvaluators` (so the same error-wrapping discipline applies to deep AND/OR trees); the NOT combinator recurses through `buildOnePrincipal` directly.

**Module-version note on the 14th variant** — `Principal_Custom` (the NEW field discovered per §1.1 amendment 7) is structurally absent from the v1.32.4 go-control-plane proto binding pinned in envoy-go's `go.mod` (the field landed in Envoy post-v1.32.x; visible in v1.37.2 per `rbac.pb.go:1112` referenced by amendment 7). The PARSE-REJECT disposition is encoded in `buildOnePrincipal`'s `default:` arm via a Go-level type-name introspection (`strings.HasSuffix("%T", ".Principal_Custom")` selects the canonical wording from §Decision (iv) below) so an operator running a forward-compatible binding that DOES expose Principal_Custom still receives the locked envoy-go-only error. The explicit typed case + the Group 4 `TestPrinCustom_PARSE_REJECT` test re-activate (lifting the `t.Skip()` + adding the typed `case *rbacconfigv3.Principal_Custom:`) when the module bumps to a v1.37.x+ binding. Approach (b) per BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT structural-absence convention; same disposition as Group 1's `TestBuildCompiledRulesEngine_CelConfigField_SilentIgnored` for the `Policy.cel_config` third CEL field per amendment 6.

**(iv) Deferred PARSE-REJECT discipline (6 total — 3 Permission + 3 Principal).** Verbatim envoy-go-only error wording per §2.3 + §2.4 + §11.P12 + §8.8 + §8.11:

| Variant | Error wording (verbatim) | Lands |
|---|---|---|
| `Permission_Metadata` | `"rbac: permission.metadata deprecated; use sourced_metadata"` | Task 4 |
| `Permission_Matcher` | `"rbac: permission.matcher extension types unsupported in this build"` | Task 4 |
| `Permission_UriTemplate` | `"rbac: permission.uri_template extension types unsupported in this build"` | Task 4 |
| `Principal_SourceIp` | `"rbac: principal.source_ip deprecated; use direct_remote_ip or remote_ip"` | Task 5 |
| `Principal_Metadata` | `"rbac: principal.metadata deprecated; use sourced_metadata"` | Task 5 |
| `Principal_Custom` | `"rbac: principal.custom extension types unsupported in this build"` (per amendment 7; structurally absent from v1.32.4 binding — encoded in `default:` arm via type-name introspection) | Task 5 |

The 3 Permission rejections are envoy-go-only divergences from Envoy v1.37.2 (lenient-accept-with-warning per §11.P12); same disposition applies to the 3 Principal rejections. The 6 wordings are structurally locked at this ADR — future re-activation phases extend the per-variant switch + amend this ADR in-place per ADR-0044.

**(v) SourcedMetadata + FilterState parse-supported-runtime-FALSE semantic (per §2.5 + §8.10).** `Permission_SourcedMetadata`, `Principal_SourcedMetadata`, `Principal_FilterState` accept the proto payload at parse time (the SourcedMetadata / FilterStateMatcher field is carried on the evaluator's struct); the evaluator's `evaluatePermission` / `evaluatePrincipal` method ALWAYS returns FALSE at runtime. The disposition is forward-compatible: a future dynamic-metadata-family or filter-state-family phase replaces the runtime impl in-place WITHOUT re-parsing operator configs. Operator divergence-window documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 phase-16 forward-pointer notes (lands at Task 9 per ADR-0146).

**(vi) Principal_Authenticated three-case algorithm (per §1.1 amendment 12 + §6.6).** The `prinAuthenticated` evaluator carries a single field `nameMatcher *matcherv3.StringMatcher` (the parsed value of `Principal_Authenticated.principal_name`; MAY be nil per the proto comment at `rbac.pb.go:1432-1438`). At runtime, the evaluator dispatches over three cases:

```go
func (e *prinAuthenticated) evaluatePrincipal(ctx evalContext) bool {
    candidates := ctx.DownstreamPrincipal()
    if len(candidates) == 0 {
        return false  // case (c)
    }
    if e.nameMatcher == nil {
        return true   // case (a)
    }
    for _, candidate := range candidates {  // case (b)
        if matchString(e.nameMatcher, candidate) {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}
```

- **Case (a)** `nameMatcher == nil` (no `principal_name` field set; the absent-field-implies-match-any-authenticated-user semantic per amendment 12) + `len(ctx.DownstreamPrincipal()) > 0` → TRUE. Order matters: the empty-principals check runs FIRST (so a nil-matcher + plaintext connection correctly returns FALSE per case (c), not TRUE).
- **Case (b)** non-nil StringMatcher iterates over the candidate slice (URI SAN → DNS SAN → Subject DN Common Name priority order per ADR-0144) — TRUE on first match via the local matchString adapter; FALSE if no candidate matches. The iteration is order-preserving: when the StringMatcher pattern matches multiple candidates, the EARLIEST candidate (highest priority) wins. The matchString adapter honors all StringMatcher subset variants (Exact / Prefix / Suffix / Contains / SafeRegex with `ignore_case`).
- **Case (c)** plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert (empty candidate slice from `DownstreamPrincipal()` — either nil or zero-length) → FALSE (regardless of whether nameMatcher is set or nil). This is the "trust_chain_verification" caveat per the proto comment: when the downstream cert is absent, no principal name exists.

The `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` accessor is the framework primitive authored at ADR-0144 (lands at Task 6); this ADR consumes it. At Task 5 the production `*filter` provides a STUB `DownstreamPrincipal()` returning nil (the framework callback does not yet exist); Task 6 replaces the stub with `return f.dcb.DownstreamPrincipal()` after the framework primitive lands on `DecoderFilterCallbacks`. The test-side `stubEvalContext` lets tests pre-populate the principals slice for case (a) + case (b) coverage; the empty-slice default exercises case (c).

**(vii) Shared-infrastructure adapter strategy — local impl in `evaluator.go` at Task 4 (TECH-DEBT for future extraction).** The 4 inner matchers (StringMatcher, HeaderMatcher, PathMatcher, CidrRange) are implemented locally in `evaluator.go` as private helpers:
- `matchString(*matcherv3.StringMatcher, candidate string) bool` — Exact / Prefix / Suffix / Contains / SafeRegex with `ignore_case` for non-regex variants.
- `matchPath(*matcherv3.PathMatcher, candidate string) bool` — delegates to matchString on the inner Path StringMatcher.
- `matchHeader(*routev3.HeaderMatcher, evalContext) bool` — 8 HeaderMatchSpecifier variants (PresentMatch + canonical StringMatch + 5 deprecated direct specifiers + RangeMatch) honoring `treat_missing_header_as_empty` + `invert_match`.
- `matchCidr(*corev3.CidrRange, net.IP) bool` — IPv4/IPv6 CIDR containment with `prefix_len` defaulting to 0 when wrapperspb.UInt32Value unset.

The local-impl disposition is intentional: csrf + the matcher-engine framework primitive at ADR-0142 already have their own StringMatcher impls (csrf is narrow — only Exact + no-ignore-case; matcher.go's impl is for the cncf/xds StringMatcher variant which is type-incompatible with the envoy variant Permission.requested_server_name consumes). Extracting an `internal/stringmatcher/` package crosses a boundary that needs cross-phase brainstorm. TECH-DEBT noted at PROGRESS.md Task 4 entry per REVIEW.md M-5 forward-pointer convention; a future operator-ergonomics phase MAY extract these adapters once the cross-filter consumer set stabilizes.

### Consequences

- **The 11 Permission evaluator types + the buildOnePermission 14-case switch are the canonical phase-16 surface.** Future operator-ergonomics phases that need to add a new accepted variant (e.g., if upstream un-deprecates `metadata` or adds a 12th variant) extend the switch + amend this ADR in-place per ADR-0044. The 6 PARSE-REJECT variants stay locked at their verbatim error wording unless an explicit re-activation amendment lands.
- **Principal evaluator catalogue + prinAuthenticated three-case algorithm finalized at Task 5.** Per the split-anchor disposition, Task 4 landed the Permission section + Principal-related sections marked as placeholders (`<!-- TODO-at-impl-time-Task-5 -->` markers). Task 5's commit (this one) edits this ADR in-place to fill the placeholders verbatim per the locked wording. The Lands-in-task field is dual-anchored (`Tasks 4 + 5`); the §Status line flipped from `Accepted (Permission section; Principal section TODO-at-Task-5)` to `Accepted` post-finalization.
- **`evalContext` widens additively across Tasks 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 — no breaking changes.** Task 4 declares the Permission-relevant accessors (Header / URLPath / DestinationIP / DestinationPort / RequestedServerName). Task 5 adds Principal accessors (DirectRemoteIP / RemoteIP / DownstreamPrincipal + SourcedMetadata / FilterState always-empty stubs). Task 7 constructs the live evalContext from request headers + connection state. Each widening extends the interface; existing test-side stubs add the new accessor methods returning zero-value defaults.
- **The `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` accessor (ADR-0144) is the load-bearing dependency for `prinAuthenticated`.** Per the three-case algorithm at §Decision (vi), case (a) checks `len(ctx.DownstreamPrincipal()) > 0` and case (b) iterates the slice. ADR-0144's accessor primitive lands at Task 6 (framework callbacks.go interface + HCM-side TLS extraction + chain plumbing); the Principal_Authenticated evaluator at Task 5 consumes it.
- **The 6 PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-only divergences from Envoy v1.37.2 are documented operator-divergence-windows.** Operators migrating from upstream Envoy configs carrying deprecated `permission.metadata` / `principal.source_ip` / `principal.metadata` or extension `permission.matcher` / `permission.uri_template` / `principal.custom` get a clear parse-time error. The error wordings name the canonical replacement (where one exists) — `metadata` → `sourced_metadata`; `source_ip` → `direct_remote_ip` / `remote_ip`. Extension variants receive the `"unsupported in this build"` wording flagging the future codec-extension / mTLS-extension family phase as the re-activation path.
- **SourcedMetadata + FilterState always-no-match runtime FALSE is a structural divergence-window** (per §2.5 + §8.10 + planner-time decision 8). Operator configs relying on SourcedMetadata / FilterState predicates for ALLOW-policies see "phantom denies" until the dynamic-metadata + filter-state subsystems land. Documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 phase-16 forward-pointer notes (lands at Task 9 per ADR-0146). The parse-supported disposition preserves forward-compatibility — operator configs carrying these fields parse without modification when the runtime subsystems land.
- **Local matcher adapter impls (`matchString`, `matchHeader`, `matchPath`, `matchCidr`) are TECH-DEBT for future extraction.** Per §Decision (vii), the local-impl disposition is intentional at phase 16 — extracting an `internal/stringmatcher/` package crosses a cross-filter boundary that needs brainstorm (csrf's narrow inline impl; matcher.go's cncf/xds variant impl). REVIEW.md M-5 forward-pointer at end-of-phase REVIEW (Task 16) signals the extraction candidate to operators of subsequent phases.
- **Group 3 + Group 4 tests anchor at Tasks 4 + 5 (`internal/filter/http/rbac/rbac_test.go`).** Group 3 (15 tests) covers the Permission Large 11 + 3 PARSE-REJECT + const=true PGV mirror at Task 4. Group 4 (14 tests) covers the Principal Large 11 + 3 PARSE-REJECT + the prinAuthenticated three-case algorithm at Task 5 (the three-case is one test with three subtests for cases (a) / (b) / (c)). Per phase-16 acceptance: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/filter/http/rbac/ -run 'TestPerm' -v` (Group 3) + `go test ... -run 'TestPrin' -v` (Group 4) both exit 0.
- **The Permission evaluator surface's `evalContext` consumers stay phase-16-rbac-local at Task 4** — the evaluators' `evaluatePermission` accepts the rbac-private `evalContext` interface, NOT the cross-phase-reusable `matcher.MatchContext`. The two interfaces differ in scope: `matcher.MatchContext` is the matcher-engine framework primitive's request-side accessor (used by the matcher-engine PARSED-tree walker for non-rbac filters too); `evalContext` is rbac-specific (used by the rules-engine Permission/Principal walker). Task 7's `matcherCtxAdapter` bridges the two for the matcher-engine path. The separation preserves the cross-phase-reuse boundary on `matcher.MatchContext` (no rbac-specific accessors leak into it) while keeping the rbac-specific accessors (DownstreamPrincipal / SourcedMetadata / FilterState) on the rbac-private `evalContext`.

## ADR-0144: TLS-principal accessor on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` framework primitive — `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` returning priority-ordered candidates (URI SAN values from `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].URIs[]` first, DNS SAN values from `state.PeerCertificates[0].DNSNames` second, Subject DN Common Name from `state.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName` third per `rbac.pb.go:1432-1438` + §1.1 amendment 12 + §11.P14) + plumbing from connection-level TLS state through HCM dispatch to per-stream filter-callback (extract `*tls.Conn.ConnectionState()` at HCM dispatch time; thread into `chain.SetTLSPrincipals(principals)` before `RunDecodeHeaders`) + three-case algorithm for `Principal_Authenticated.principal_name` consumption (codified at ADR-0143 §Decision (vi); ADR-0144 codifies the accessor surface) + cross-phase reuse intent (future filters jwt_authn / ext_authz / oauth2 / ext_proc consume the same accessor for TLS-principal introspection) + list-returning vs matcher-applying API choice (LIST-returning per SPEC §3.1 + §11.3 carry-forward decision — flexibility for caller-side matching; future filters can extract names without re-rolling TLS-context plumbing) + plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert handling (returns nil slice; ADR-0143's case (c) defers to this nil-slice semantic) + canonical 3-cert-field scope (URI SAN + DNS SAN + Subject DN CN only per D11; Issuer DN + Serial + fingerprints DEFERRED to future TLS-context-extension phase)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — phase-13 + phase-15 precedent; this ADR is authored AT impl-time at its anchor Task 6); ADR-0071 (filter framework iteration protocol — DecoderFilterCallbacks is the framework-supplied surface threaded into every decode-side filter; per-stream-stateless after chain build per the single-dispatch-goroutine invariant); ADR-0072 (HTTP registry freeze-after-boot — the accessor's existence is a parse-time-stable framework surface; no per-request registry mutation); ADR-0040 (out-of-scope deferrals format — the Issuer DN + Serial + fingerprints fields are DEFERRED with forward-pointer to a future TLS-context-extension phase).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 6

### Context

`Principal_Authenticated` (per Envoy v1.37.2's `envoy.config.rbac.v3.Principal_Authenticated` proto at `rbac.pb.go:1432-1438`) requires access to the downstream client TLS certificate's principal name(s) for the three-case algorithm at ADR-0143 §Decision (vi) + SPEC §6.6: case (a) nil principal_name + len(candidates)>0 → TRUE; case (b) non-nil StringMatcher iterates over candidates in priority order; case (c) plaintext / no-client-cert → FALSE.

Per Envoy v1.37.2 semantics + §1.1 amendment 12 + §11.P14: the candidate list comprises URI SAN values (first priority — SPIFFE / service identity), then DNS SAN values (second priority — DNS identity), then the Subject DN Common Name as the third-priority fallback. The three canonical cert fields are the load-bearing input set; the proto comment at `rbac.pb.go:1432-1438` documents the three-field priority verbatim. Per D11 (PLAN.md §95-138): Issuer DN + Serial number + cert fingerprints are DEFERRED to a future TLS-context-extension phase — phase-16 MVP scope is the canonical 3 fields only.

**Current envoy-go state (pre-Task-6):** Phase 03 ships downstream TLS termination on `internal/listener/`. The TLS context (cert chain, principal info) is held by the listener/connection layer; the HCM dispatch path receives the resolved `net.Conn` (which is a `*tls.Conn` when the listener is TLS-enabled). This TLS state is NOT currently surfaced through `DecoderFilterCallbacks` — filters that want TLS principal info would otherwise need to roll their own connection-layer plumbing (couple to listener internals; break the framework boundary).

**Cross-phase reuse motivation:** Future filters (jwt_authn for cert-bound tokens, ext_authz for principal-pivoted decisions, oauth2 for cert-mtls flows, ext_proc for sidecar-style auth) all need TLS principal candidates. A framework-primitive accessor on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` is the appropriate boundary: each future filter consumes the same accessor; the connection-layer TLS plumbing lives in HCM dispatch once + flows through `chain.SetTLSPrincipals` to every per-stream callback.

### Decision

**(i) Accessor on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` is `DownstreamPrincipal() []string`.** A list-returning method (NOT matcher-applying):

```go
// internal/filter/http/callbacks.go — DecoderFilterCallbacks extension:
DownstreamPrincipal() []string
```

Returns the priority-ordered TLS principal-name candidates. Returns nil (or empty) for plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert connections.

Rationale for list-returning (vs matcher-applying): flexibility — the caller (e.g., Permission/Principal evaluator) does its own matching against the candidates; the framework primitive does NOT couple to the StringMatcher type. Future filters can extract names without re-rolling TLS-context plumbing. Mirrors the `internal/listener/match.go` precedent of phase-07.2 (multi-valued accessor over StringMatcher coupling). Per SPEC §3.1 + §11.3 carry-forward decision.

**(ii) Plumbing — connection-level TLS state threads through HCM dispatch to per-stream filter-callback via `chain.SetTLSPrincipals`.** Three layers:

1. **TLS extraction helper** at `internal/filter/hcm/connection.go`:
   ```go
   func extractTLSPrincipals(state *tls.ConnectionState) []string {
       if state == nil || !state.HandshakeComplete || len(state.PeerCertificates) == 0 {
           return nil
       }
       cert := state.PeerCertificates[0]
       var principals []string
       for _, u := range cert.URIs { principals = append(principals, u.String()) }
       principals = append(principals, cert.DNSNames...)
       if cn := cert.Subject.CommonName; cn != "" { principals = append(principals, cn) }
       return principals
   }
   ```
   Plus a wrapper `downstreamTLSPrincipals(downstream net.Conn) []string` that handles the `*tls.Conn` type assertion.

2. **Chain-side per-stream field + accessor** at `internal/filter/http/chain.go`:
   ```go
   type FilterChain struct {
       // ... existing fields ...
       tlsPrincipals []string
   }
   func (c *FilterChain) SetTLSPrincipals(p []string) { c.tlsPrincipals = p }
   func (d *decoderCB) DownstreamPrincipal() []string { return d.c.tlsPrincipals }
   ```
   Set once per request before filter iteration starts (single dispatch-goroutine invariant per ADR-0071); read-only thereafter.

3. **HCM dispatch wire-in** (symmetric H1 + H2):
   - H1 (`connection.go` `dispatchRequest`): `chain.SetTLSPrincipals(downstreamTLSPrincipals(downstream))` after `chain.SetRequestCtx` + before `RunDecodeHeaders`. The downstream `net.Conn` is threaded through `runConnection` → `serveOneRequest` → `dispatchRequest` (3 signature widenings).
   - H2 (`h2dispatch.go`): `runH2` extracts TLS principals once at connection build time + stores on `h2Dispatcher.tlsPrincipals`; the dispatcher copies to each `chainDispatchAction.tlsPrincipals` at `Match` time; `WriteH2` calls `chain.SetTLSPrincipals(c.tlsPrincipals)` after `SetRequestCtx` + before `RunDecodeHeaders`. The per-conn caching mirrors the H1 semantic (one TLS state per connection for the conn's lifetime).

**(iii) Priority ordering URI SAN → DNS SAN → Subject DN CN.** The candidate slice carries:
1. URI SANs from `state.PeerCertificates[0].URIs[]` (highest priority — SPIFFE / service identity per the proto comment).
2. DNS SANs from `state.PeerCertificates[0].DNSNames` (second priority — DNS identity).
3. Subject DN Common Name from `state.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName` (third priority — fallback). Empty CN is intentionally skipped (would otherwise pollute the slice with `""` candidates that match a `Prefix("")` matcher unexpectedly).

Per D11 + SPEC §12.11 + §8.9: canonical 3 cert fields ONLY. Issuer DN + Serial + fingerprints DEFERRED to a future TLS-context-extension phase — out-of-scope for phase-16 per ADR-0040 deferral format.

**(iv) List-returning vs matcher-applying API choice — LIST-returning per SPEC §3.1 + §11.3 carry-forward decision.** Rejected alternative: a matcher-applying API `MatchDownstreamPrincipal(m *matcherv3.StringMatcher) bool`. Rationale for the rejection:
- Couples the framework primitive to a single matcher type (StringMatcher), locking future filters into the same matching surface.
- Forces the framework to know the matcher's semantics (Exact / Prefix / Suffix / Contains / SafeRegex / ignore_case) — a cross-phase-stable surface should NOT know per-filter matcher subsetting.
- The list-returning API enables future filters to extract principal names for ANY purpose (logging, header injection, decision-tree dispatch) without re-rolling TLS-context plumbing.

LIST-returning is the cross-phase-stable choice. Each future filter applies its own matcher logic to the returned slice.

**(v) Plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert handling — returns nil slice.** Three failure modes all collapse to nil:
- `downstream` is not a `*tls.Conn` (plaintext listener; type assertion fails).
- `state.HandshakeComplete` is false (pre-handshake / aborted; defensive against callers reading state before the handshake completes).
- `len(state.PeerCertificates) == 0` (server-auth-only TLS — TLS without mTLS; client did NOT present a cert).

ADR-0143 §Decision (vi) case (c) defers to this nil-slice semantic: `len(ctx.DownstreamPrincipal()) == 0` → `prinAuthenticated.evaluatePrincipal` returns FALSE. The plaintext disposition is intentional + structural: an RBAC ALLOW policy requiring `Principal_Authenticated` MUST fail-closed on a plaintext connection (no principal can be authenticated without TLS).

### Consequences

- **The `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` accessor is the load-bearing dependency for `prinAuthenticated` (per ADR-0143 §Decision (vi)) AND the cross-phase-reusable surface for future filters.** Phase-16 Task 6 (this commit) lands the framework primitive + HCM-side TLS extraction + chain plumbing; future filters (jwt_authn / ext_authz / oauth2 / ext_proc) consume the same accessor surface without re-rolling TLS-context plumbing.
- **DecoderFilterCallbacks now has one additional method; every existing implementation adds a `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` body.** The production impl `decoderCB` in `chain.go` returns the chain's per-stream `tlsPrincipals` field. Test-side mock implementations (across 8 filter packages — callbacks_test, buffer_test, bandwidthlimit_test, compressor_test, csrf_test, fault_test, header_mutation_test, localratelimit_test) add a no-op `return nil` body to satisfy the interface. The addition is purely additive (no signature change to existing methods); no existing test logic breaks.
- **HCM dispatch is symmetric H1 + H2.** H1 extracts TLS principals per request (the downstream conn is threaded through `runConnection` → `serveOneRequest` → `dispatchRequest`); H2 extracts ONCE at connection build time + caches on `h2Dispatcher.tlsPrincipals` (then propagated to every per-stream `chainDispatchAction`). The per-conn caching for H2 mirrors the connection-pinned-TLS-state semantic (a single TLS handshake state covers all streams on the conn for the conn's lifetime).
- **The chain.tlsPrincipals field is per-stream stateless after set — single-dispatch-goroutine invariant per ADR-0071.** `SetTLSPrincipals` is called once at chain build time by HCM dispatch BEFORE `RunDecodeHeaders`; the field is read-only thereafter from any filter callback. No synchronization required (single dispatch goroutine drives both the set + the read).
- **Plaintext / non-mTLS / no-client-cert handling — nil slice → ADR-0143 case (c) FALSE.** An RBAC ALLOW policy requiring `Principal_Authenticated` on a plaintext listener fails-closed. The disposition is intentional: a `Principal_Authenticated` predicate semantically requires a TLS-authenticated principal; absent TLS, no principal exists. Operator-divergence-window documented at fixture 0018 scenario 6 (Tasks 12-14): mTLS scenario exercises the full extraction path end-to-end with a real client cert.
- **Canonical 3-cert-field scope is FINALIZED at phase-16; Issuer DN + Serial + fingerprints DEFERRED per D11.** Future TLS-context-extension phases extend the helper additively + amend this ADR in-place per ADR-0044. The DEFERRED set is documented at SPEC §12.11 + §8.9 + this ADR's §Decision (iii) — operators carrying RBAC policies that match against Issuer DN / Serial / fingerprints get a phase-16-MVP no-match (forward-pointer to the extension phase via the PROGRESS.md follow-up note at Task 6).
- **Test coverage anchors at Task 6.** Three test surfaces: (a) chain-side plumbing unit tests at `internal/filter/http/chain_test.go` (3 tests: NoSeed_NilSlice + SeededViaSetTLSPrincipals_ReturnsSeed + OrderingPreservedAcrossCalls); (b) `extractTLSPrincipals` helper unit tests at `internal/filter/hcm/tls_test.go` (11 tests: 9 extractTLSPrincipals cases — nil state / handshake-incomplete / no-peer-certs / URI-only / DNS-only / CN-only / all-three / multiple-of-each / empty-CN-skipped — plus 2 downstreamTLSPrincipals wrapper tests); (c) Group 7 rbac evaluator consumption tests at `internal/filter/http/rbac/rbac_test.go` (5 tests exercising `prinAuthenticated` three-case via seeded `stubEvalContext.DownstreamPrincipal()` — plaintext / URI-first / DNS-second / CN-third / full priority ordering). End-to-end mTLS path is fixture 0018 scenario 6 at Tasks 12-14.
- **Cross-phase reuse intent — additive interface widening, NOT in-place ADR amendments.** Future filters consume the same `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` accessor. If a future filter requires a different TLS field (Issuer DN / Serial / fingerprint), the framework adds a NEW accessor method to `DecoderFilterCallbacks` (NOT amending the existing one) — preserving the cross-phase-stable surface + the per-method ADR audit trail.
