## ADR-0145: rbac stat surface — 4 base counters (`allowed` / `denied` / `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied`) registered UNCONDITIONALLY (predeclared empty counters for scrape stability per Prometheus best practice) under the HCM-rooted SN2-reuse namespace `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.rbac.<rules_stat_prefix>.<counter>` (empirically RATIFIED at impl-time via reference Envoy v1.37.2 stats scrape — NO new SN10 rule introduced) + lazy per-policy counter family via `sync.Map` LoadOrStore + `NewCounterIfAbsent` post-Freeze idempotent registration (counter name shape `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` per empirical scrape — REFINES SPEC line 1842 hypothesis which omitted the `.policy.` segment infix) + per-route INDEPENDENT-stats via `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` + `resolvePerRouteConfig` lazy-cache (third row using INDEPENDENT-stats discipline after phase-11 local_ratelimit ADR-0117 + phase-15 bandwidth_limit ADR-0139) + `NewCounterIfAbsent` flip for both listener-level and per-route paths (CF-Task2-I3 + CF-Task7-M6: avoids multi-listener-same-empty-prefix panic foot-gun)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12 (phase 16 Task 8 commit)
**Doctrine:** ADR-0117 (phase-11 per-route INDEPENDENT-stats — canonical machinery inherited VERBATIM); ADR-0139 (phase-15 INDEPENDENT-stats ratification — second row); ADR-0061 stats Registry LBP-1 invariant + AMENDMENT carried-forward (`NewCounterIfAbsent` post-Freeze idempotent registration); ADR-0072 boot-fail-fast (applies at New only; request-time per-route TPFC parse failures fall back to listener inherit per phase-11 + phase-15 precedent); ADR-0073 typed_per_filter_config 3-tier merge (most-specific override) carryover; ADR-0085 nil-tolerance discipline (single-caller `if ctx.Stats != nil` gate); ADR-0140 4-base-counter scope (REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis — NO `logged` counter per §11.P6); ADR-0044 in-place amendment discipline (ADR-0145 codifies the SN2-reuse hypothesis from BRAINSTORM §2.8 + SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 → empirically RATIFIED at this commit).
**Lands-in-task:** Phase 16 Task 8.

### Context

Phase-16 rbac is the **THIRD row using INDEPENDENT-stats** per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent. The stat surface has three load-bearing characteristics:

1. **4 base counters per active stat-prefix combination** (`allowed` / `denied` / `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied` per §1.1 amendment 8 + §11.P6). REFUTES the BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis — NO `logged` counter exists in Envoy v1.37.2; LOG-partial folds into `allowed` per amendment 5 + amendment 8 (LOG always-allows; the allowed counter increments on LOG-match).

2. **Variable per-policy counter family** (lazy-allocated when `track_per_rule_stats: true`). Operator-config-driven surface growth — N policies × 2 base sides × 2 (primary + shadow) = up to 4N per-policy counters per active namespace. Foot-gun documented at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes. The lazy-allocation discipline (sync.Map keyed by full counter name + NewCounterIfAbsent on first emission) mirrors phase-11 ADR-0117's post-Freeze idempotency contract.

3. **Per-route INDEPENDENT-stats** (NOT shared with listener-level). Per SPEC §5.2 + §11.P4 empirical pin + ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent. Each per-route RBACPerRoute TPFC entry with `rbac != nil` allocates its own `*compiledConfig` carrying its own `*filterStats` under the per-route `rules_stat_prefix` namespace; listener-level counters are NOT touched for per-route reqs.

**Empirical scrape at impl-time (Task 8 Step 6 per PLAN.md line 481).** SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §11.P7 hypothesized the SN2-reuse namespace shape `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.rbac.<rules_stat_prefix>.<counter>` for the base 4 counters, with an SN10 release-valve discipline if the hypothesis was refuted. The scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 (`docker run envoyproxy/envoy:v1.37.2 -c /etc/envoy/bootstrap.yaml` with an HCM stat_prefix `hcm_probe` + rbac filter carrying `rules_stat_prefix: myrules` + `shadow_rules_stat_prefix: myshadow` + `track_per_rule_stats: true` + ALLOW+any-any policies; `curl /stats | grep rbac`) observed:

```
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myrules.allowed: 3
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myrules.denied: 0
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myshadow.shadow_allowed: 3
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myshadow.shadow_denied: 0
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myrules.policy.policy_allow_all.allowed: 3
http.hcm_probe.rbac.myshadow.policy.shadow_policy_allow_all.shadow_allowed: 3
```

**SN2-reuse hypothesis RATIFIED for the 4 base counters.** The base names matched the hypothesis verbatim — NO new SN10 rule introduced. **Per-policy counter shape REFINED** — the empirical scrape inserted a `.policy.` segment between the base prefix and the policy name (the SPEC line 1842 hypothesis `<base_prefix>.<policy_name>.<suffix>` omitted this segment; the actual shape is `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>`). The SPEC stat-table will be amended at the Task 9 commit when per-policy emission ships fully via ADR-0146; ADR-0145 documents the refined shape inline (no SPEC amendment at this commit since per-policy emission is not yet wired into emit*Counters).

The two CF-Task2-I3 + CF-Task7-M6 carry-forwards from Task 2 + Task 7 also resolve at this commit: Task 2's skeleton used `reg.NewCounter` (panic-on-duplicate) which would panic at HCM-build time if two listener-level rbac filters shared an empty `rules_stat_prefix` (both resolving to the same `"rbac.allowed"` name). ADR-0145 flips both `newFilterStats` (listener-level) and `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` (per-route) to `reg.NewCounterIfAbsent` — the listener-level path's panic-on-duplicate semantic is intentionally relaxed since the rbac stat namespace is fully data-driven (operators configure `rules_stat_prefix` per filter; collisions are operator misconfiguration, not framework programmer-error). Both helpers share the identical code path; the two distinct entry-points exist for documentation discipline only.

### Decision

**(i) 4 base counters per active stat-prefix combination, registered UNCONDITIONALLY (predeclared empty counters for scrape stability per Prometheus best practice).** Per SPEC §1.1 amendment 8 + §11.P6 + ADR-0140. The 4 counters are `<base_prefix>.allowed`, `<base_prefix>.denied`, `<base_prefix_shadow>.shadow_allowed`, `<base_prefix_shadow>.shadow_denied`. Counters are registered at `buildCompiledConfig` time regardless of whether primary / shadow engines are configured — operators get a consistent observation surface (no "counter appeared mid-flight" on shadow-engine config-flip; the shadow counters publish 0 when no shadow engine is configured). LOG-partial folds into `allowed` per amendment 5 + amendment 8 (LOG always-allows; the allowed counter increments). NO `logged` counter exists (REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis per §11.P6).

**(ii) SN2-reuse namespace `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.rbac.<rules_stat_prefix>.<counter>` empirically RATIFIED at impl-time scrape.** Per SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §11.P7. The HCM-rooted shape mirrors phase-09 fault's `http.<HCM>.fault.<metric>` precedent (NOT phase-11 local_ratelimit + phase-15 bandwidth_limit's inline-prefix `<prefix>.http_<filter>_<counter>` shape — those filters introduced SN9 + their own tag-extractors precisely because they did NOT inherit the SN2 `http.*` prefix routing; rbac's HCM-rooted shape sits squarely on the existing SN2 default-branch flatten in `internal/stats/name.go::flattenToProm`). NO new SN10 rule introduced; NO new tag-extractor; the existing `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix=<HCM_stat_prefix>` label is the only label promoted. Empty `rules_stat_prefix` falls back to the literal `rbac` segment per §1.1 amendment 3 + the `namespacePrefix` helper (mirrors Envoy v1.37.2's empirical `utility.h::generateStats` fallback behavior).

**(iii) Per-policy counter family lazy-allocated via `sync.Map` LoadOrStore + `NewCounterIfAbsent`** (post-Freeze idempotent per ADR-0117). Counter name shape per the Task 8 empirical scrape: `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` (REFINES the SPEC line 1842 hypothesis which omitted the `.policy.` segment infix). `filterStats.incPolicy(base, policyName, suffix)` is the canonical entry-point: (a) compute the full counter name; (b) sync.Map.Load — cache hit increments + returns; (c) cache miss invokes `reg.NewCounterIfAbsent` to allocate (which is itself idempotent across goroutines via the Registry's `byName` map mutex); (d) sync.Map.LoadOrStore stores the resolved Counter pointer (race-safe — winner stores; loser observes the winner's Counter). Per-policy emission is gated by the caller's `cc.trackPerRuleStats` check; full wiring into `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` lands at Task 9 per ADR-0146 (Task 8 ships the helper + the lazy-cache contract; Task 9 ships the emission discipline + the shadow-path per-policy emission + the LOG-partial precise discipline).

**(iv) Per-route INDEPENDENT-stats via `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` + `resolvePerRouteConfig` lazy-cache.** Per SPEC §5.2 + §11.P4 + ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent. Each `*rbacv3.RBACPerRoute` TPFC entry with `Rbac != nil` resolves to its own `*compiledConfig` carrying its own `*filterStats` under the per-route `rules_stat_prefix` namespace. Listener-level state is fully shadowed for per-route reqs — listener-level counters do NOT increment when a per-route override is active (asserted at Group 9's `TestStatsNamespace_PerRouteINDEPENDENT_ListenerCountersUnaffected`). Phase-16 is the **THIRD row using INDEPENDENT-stats** per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent. The HCM stat prefix is threaded from `factoryState.hcmStatPrefix` (captured from `FactoryCtx.StatPrefix` at New time) into `buildCompiledPerRoute` so the per-route counter namespace inherits the SAME HCM root as listener-level counters — operators see `http.<HCM>.rbac.<per_route_prefix>.<counter>` (NOT a separate HCM-orphaned namespace; the per-route `rules_stat_prefix` segment differs but the HCM-root + `rbac.` filter-name segment are constant).

**(v) Post-Freeze idempotent registration via `NewCounterIfAbsent` for BOTH listener-level (newFilterStats) and per-route (newFilterStatsIfAbsent) paths.** CF-Task2-I3 + CF-Task7-M6 fix: Task 2's skeleton used `reg.NewCounter` (panic-on-duplicate) which would panic at HCM-build time if two listener-level rbac filters happened to share an empty `rules_stat_prefix` (both resolving to `rbac.allowed` after the namespacePrefix fallback). ADR-0145 flips both helpers to `reg.NewCounterIfAbsent` per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent. The two distinct entry-points (`newFilterStats` for boot-time + `newFilterStatsIfAbsent` for post-Freeze) are preserved at the call-site level for documentation discipline (callsite reveals intent — boot-time vs request-time registration); the bodies are intentionally identical (both call through to the same helper code path). Mirrors phase-11 ADR-0117 IMPL-3 + phase-15 ADR-0139 §Decision (ii) precedent — the panic-discipline relaxation for data-driven stat names is the canonical pattern.

**(vi) Predeclared empty counters for scrape stability (operator-friendly).** Per Prometheus best practice ("predeclare all counters with a stable namespace so scrapes never observe a counter appearing mid-flight"; see <https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/instrumentation/#avoid-missing-metrics>). The 4 base counters are registered regardless of whether shadow / matcher engines are configured. CF-Task2-I2 carry-forward resolves to "register all 4 unconditionally" rather than "conditional registration on engine-active" — the latter would surface a counter shape that varies with proto config, breaking the per-scrape stability contract. The all-4-unconditional discipline matches phase-09 fault's 5-counter unconditional registration + phase-15 bandwidth_limit's 14-stat unconditional registration (both filters predeclare all counters at New time even when `enable_mode: DISABLED` or `delay`/`abort` percentages are 0).

### Alternatives considered

**(a) Conditional shadow-counter registration (rejected per (vi)).** A hypothetical alternative would register only `allowed` + `denied` when no shadow engine is configured + register all 4 only when shadow is set. REJECTED — operators observing `/stats` would see a counter shape that varies with proto config, breaking Prometheus scrape stability. The 4-counter unconditional discipline is operator-friendly + matches the existing fault + bandwidth_limit precedent.

**(b) Per-policy counter family pre-allocated at New time (rejected — lazy-allocation per (iii)).** A hypothetical alternative would walk all policies at `buildCompiledRulesEngine` time + pre-allocate `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` for each (policy, suffix) pair. REJECTED — `track_per_rule_stats=true` is operator-config-driven + variable-N; pre-allocation would force Registry growth for policies that may never match in production (cold-policy scenarios). Lazy allocation via `sync.Map` LoadOrStore + `NewCounterIfAbsent` matches phase-11 ADR-0117's IMPL-3 lazy-cache discipline + is structurally lighter (no pre-walk at New; counter materialization deferred to first match).

**(c) SN10 release-valve discipline introduction (rejected — SN2-reuse RATIFIED).** SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §11.P7 carried forward the SN2-reuse hypothesis with an SN10 release-valve "if Envoy's empirical shape diverges (e.g., flat `<rules_stat_prefix>.rbac.<counter>` mirroring phase-15 bandwidth_limit's shape), envoy-go's namespace mirrors via inline-prefix rendering (`envoy_<rules_stat_prefix>_rbac_<counter>{}`) + introduces SN10". The Task 8 empirical scrape RATIFIED the SN2-reuse hypothesis verbatim for the base 4 counters — `http.hcm_probe.rbac.myrules.allowed` exactly matches. NO new SN10 rule introduced; ADR-0145 codifies the ratification rather than the release-valve.

**(d) Per-route SHARED-stats (rejected per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 + §11.P4 precedent).** A hypothetical alternative would have per-route TPFC entries inherit the listener-level `*filterStats` pointer (per-route reqs increment listener-level counters under the listener-level `rules_stat_prefix`). This is the discipline phase-14 ADR-0132 compressor adopted (appropriate there because the compressor's per-route surface is structurally subsidiary). Phase-16's per-route surface is structurally co-equal with the listener (the SAME `rbacv3.RBAC` proto can be reused inside `RBACPerRoute.rbac`; the per-route entry can carry an entirely distinct `rules_stat_prefix`). REJECTED — SHARED-stats would diverge from the operator-visible per-route stat_prefix override expectation + Envoy v1.37.2's empirical behavior emits SEPARATE counter series per per-route prefix.

**(e) Drop the dual entry-point newFilterStats / newFilterStatsIfAbsent in favor of a single helper (rejected — call-site documentation discipline).** A hypothetical alternative would have a single `newFilterStats(reg, hcmPrefix, primaryPrefix, shadowPrefix)` entry-point used by both listener-level and per-route paths. REJECTED — the dual entry-point at the call-site reveals intent (boot-time vs request-time registration), serves as a forward-compat guardrail for a possible future per-registration-mode divergence, and matches phase-11 + phase-15 precedent. The bodies are intentionally identical (both call through to the same code path); the documentation cost is one extra helper function declaration.

### Consequences

- **Phase-16 is the THIRD row using INDEPENDENT-stats per ADR-0117 + ADR-0139 precedent** (phase-11 local_ratelimit FIRST; phase-15 bandwidth_limit SECOND). Future stateful per-route filters with stat-emission requirements pick the row's discipline per the per-route override structural shape: if the override is structurally co-equal with the listener (SAME proto reused; full stat_prefix override expected) → INDEPENDENT-stats (this ADR); if the override is structurally subsidiary (PerRoute wrapper with a narrow toggle surface) → SHARED-stats (ADR-0132 compressor row).
- **SN2-reuse namespace shape RATIFIED via impl-time empirical scrape.** The reference Envoy v1.37.2 scrape (`http.hcm_probe.rbac.myrules.allowed` matches the hypothesis verbatim) closes the SPEC §11.P7 PARTIAL pin. NO new SN10 flattening rule; NO new tag-extractor; the existing `flattenToProm` SN2 default-branch flatten in `internal/stats/name.go` covers rbac counters with the existing `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix` label promotion.
- **Per-policy counter shape REFINED — `.policy.` segment infix.** The empirical scrape revealed the per-policy counter name shape `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` — the SPEC line 1842 hypothesis omitted the `.policy.` segment. The SPEC stat-table amends at the Task 9 commit (ADR-0146) when per-policy emission ships fully; the `filterStats.incPolicy` helper landed at Task 8 already constructs the correct shape so the Task 9 wiring is a pure call-site change.
- **The 4 base counters land on the Registry at New time UNCONDITIONALLY** regardless of which engines are configured. Operators get a consistent observation surface (`/stats | grep rbac.<prefix>` always shows 4 entries per active namespace combination). Shadow counters publish 0 when no shadow engine is configured.
- **`NewCounterIfAbsent` flip for BOTH listener-level + per-route paths** (CF-Task2-I3 + CF-Task7-M6) eliminates the multi-listener-same-empty-prefix panic foot-gun. The Registry's `byName` map's mutex serializes concurrent registrations; idempotency is structural per ADR-0117.
- **The unused `compiledPerRoute.activeRC()` method (Task 7 `//nolint:unused` carry-forward) is REMOVED at this commit** (CF-Task7-M2 applied). Production dispatch consumes `resolvePerRouteConfig`'s `(rc, isDisabled)` return pair directly; the helper added no value + invited confusion.
- **The unused `role` parameter on `buildCompiledRulesEngine` (Task 7 `_ = role` carry-forward) is REMOVED at this commit** (CF-Task7-M3 applied). The speculative reservation for error-wrapping discipline at Tasks 4/5 was not consumed; the per-engine role context is unambiguous at the caller site (`buildCompiledConfig`'s switch on `c.GetRules() / c.GetShadowRules()`).
- **Group 9 unit tests (6 tests; ~360 LoC) verify the stats-namespace integration + lazy per-policy contract + post-Freeze idempotency + per-route INDEPENDENT-stats wiring** per PLAN.md line 66 + SPEC §14.1 #9. The 6 tests: (1) `TestStatsNamespace_AllFourBaseCountersRegistered`; (2) `TestStatsNamespace_SN2Reuse_NoNewSN10Rule`; (3) `TestStatsNamespace_HCMRootedPath_HttpHCMRbacPrefixCounter`; (4) `TestStatsNamespace_PerPolicyLazyAllocation_OnFirstMatch`; (5) `TestStatsNamespace_NewFilterStatsIfAbsent_Idempotent`; (6) `TestStatsNamespace_PerRouteINDEPENDENT_ListenerCountersUnaffected`. All 6 PASS under `go test -race -count=1`.
- **Per-policy emission discipline FULLY wires at Task 9** (ADR-0146). At Task 8, the `filterStats.incPolicy` helper + `primaryBase` / `shadowBase` cached prefix fields land; the call-sites in `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` for the `trackPerRuleStats=true` branch (+ shadow-path + LOG-partial precise discipline) ship at Task 9. The Task 8 lazy-cache contract is independently verified at Group 9's `TestStatsNamespace_PerPolicyLazyAllocation_OnFirstMatch`.
- **Fixture 0018 (Tasks 12-14)** mechanically validates the SN2-reuse namespace shape end-to-end (the driver scrapes `/stats/prometheus` on both reference Envoy v1.37.2 + envoy-go side-by-side; counter-line assertions land at Task 14). Phase-16's full stat surface codification per ADR-0145 + the per-policy emission per ADR-0146 are independently asserted at the fixture; ADR-0145's empirical-ratification (this commit) closes the §11.P7 PARTIAL pin pre-fixture.
- **Variable-stat-surface foot-gun documented at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes.** Operators with N policies × `track_per_rule_stats: true` emit up to 4N per-policy counters per active namespace. The cost is operator-config-driven; the per-policy template-form is documented in the SPEC's stat-table as a row-template (not fixed names). Production deployments at high-policy-count + `track_per_rule_stats: true` should size their Prometheus scrape budget accordingly.
- **Prometheus rendering trade-off (label-vs-inline tag-extractor).** Reference Envoy v1.37.2 promotes BOTH `envoy_rbac_http_prefix=<rules_prefix>` AND `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix=<HCM>` as Prometheus labels via its registered tag-extractors (base metric `envoy_http_rbac_allowed{envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix=...,envoy_rbac_http_prefix=...}`). envoy-go's existing SN2 default-branch flatten promotes ONLY `envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix` and inlines `<rules_prefix>` into the metric name (`envoy_http_rbac_<rules_prefix>_allowed{envoy_http_conn_manager_prefix=...}`). The INTERNAL stat-namespace shape is identical (`http.<HCM>.rbac.<prefix>.<counter>`); only the Prometheus surface differs. Phase-09 fault has the same trade-off precedent. Fixture 0018 (Tasks 12-14) reconciles this via the `/stats` JSON endpoint (not `/stats/prometheus`) where the dispatch path is namespace-equivalent. If a future operator-ergonomics phase wants tag-extractor parity, an SN10 rule (or a new SN-numbered rbac-specific tag-extractor) can land additively. See PROGRESS.md Task 8 empirical-scrape evidence for the verbatim probe output + side-by-side rendering.

## ADR-0146: rbac shadow-evaluation discipline (parallel-to-primary engine walk; same algorithm; NEVER affects disposition; emits `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied` counters per active shadow namespace + lazy per-policy counters when `track_per_rule_stats: true`) + LOG-partial divergence-window (always-allow + match-evaluated + `access_log_hint` metadata silent per §1.1 amendment 5 + §8.6; counter emission folds into `allowed` per amendment 8 — NO separate `logged` counter) + `track_per_rule_stats` per-policy emission discipline (lazy `NewCounterIfAbsent` per matched policy per first-match invocation; `sync.Map` keyed by full counter name `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` per ADR-0145's Task 8 empirical scrape refinement) + `response_code_details` field-emission divergence-window (envoy-go MVP no emission per §1.1 amendment 11 + §8.12 — Envoy emits `"rbac_access_denied_matched_policy[<sanitized_policy_id>]"` per `utility.cc::responseDetail`; envoy-go's current HCM scope does NOT thread response-code-details to local-reply callers; future HCM framework phase couples) + shadow-rules access-log integration deferred (per §8.7 + §11.P13; envoy-go MVP counter-only matches Envoy v1.37.2 counter-only confirmation — no current divergence; documented as forward-pointer) + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 phase-16 forward-pointer notes anchoring (the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT edit lands at Task 15; ADR-0146 is the authoritative reference for the 6 divergence-windows for operator awareness — LOG-action metadata + response_code_details + CEL three-field + shadow access-log + sourced-metadata always-no-match + Principal_Authenticated canonical 3 cert fields)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12 (phase 16 Task 9 commit)
**Doctrine:** ADR-0140 (4-base-counter scope — REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis; LOG-partial folds into `allowed`); ADR-0141 (LOG action enum + matched-policy capture per amendment 5; CEL three-field silent-ignore per amendment 6); ADR-0143 (Permission + Principal evaluators + sourced_metadata/filter_state always-no-match per §2.5 + §8.10); ADR-0144 (TLS-principal accessor `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` consumed by Principal_Authenticated three-case algorithm per §1.1 amendment 12 + §11.P14); ADR-0145 (stat surface — per-policy `.policy.` segment refinement; lazy `incPolicy` helper landed at Task 8); ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — authored at impl-time per phase-13/15 precedent); ADR-0040 (out-of-scope deferrals — the 6 phase-16 deferrals captured INLINE at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 forward-pointer notes per phase 10-15 precedent; NO new deferral ADRs); ADR-0073 (typed_per_filter_config 3-tier merge — most-specific override; inherited by 7th canonical per-route discipline at ADR-0125 §(xii) Task 10).
**Lands-in-task:** Phase 16 Task 9.

### Context

Phase-16 rbac is the **third filter row** (after phase-09 fault + phase-15 bandwidth_limit) to ship a runtime that carries operator-visible **divergence-windows** vs reference Envoy v1.37.2 — surfaces where the envoy-go behavior is intentionally narrower than Envoy's because the underlying framework primitives (CEL runtime; dynamic-metadata family; HCM response-code-details; access-log family) have not yet landed in envoy-go's project plan. The shadow-evaluation + LOG-partial + `track_per_rule_stats` + `response_code_details` runtime details are the load-bearing pieces of this divergence-window codification.

**At Task 8 the lazy-allocation contract for per-policy counters landed** via `filterStats.incPolicy` (sync.Map LoadOrStore + NewCounterIfAbsent; counter name shape `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` per ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) — the empirical scrape refined the SPEC line 1842 hypothesis which omitted the `.policy.` segment infix). The Task 8 `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` were STUBs that incremented the 4 base counters only; the per-policy wiring (when `cc.trackPerRuleStats=true`) was explicitly held back to Task 9 alongside the shadow-path orchestration + LOG-partial precise discipline + response_code_details divergence-window codification.

**The 6 divergence-windows** ADR-0146 anchors (forward-pointed at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 at Task 15):

1. **LOG-action `access_log_hint` dynamic-metadata emission DEFERRED** per §1.1 amendment 5 + §8.6. envoy-go MVP: silent. Envoy: emits dynamic metadata. Couples to future dynamic-metadata family framework phase landing `(EncoderFilterCallbacks).SetDynamicMetadata(key, value)` primitive (or analogous accessor).

2. **`response_code_details` on DENY DEFERRED** per §1.1 amendment 11 + §8.12. envoy-go MVP: no emission (SendLocalReply has 3-arg signature; no response-code-details slot). Envoy: emits `"rbac_access_denied_matched_policy[<sanitized_policy_id>]"`. Couples to future HCM response-code-details framework phase.

3. **CEL three-field condition evaluation DEFERRED** per §1.1 amendment 6 + Q7 + §8.1. envoy-go MVP: `condition` / `checked_condition` / `cel_config` all silent-ignored at parse + runtime (`policyMatches` skips condition evaluation entirely). Envoy: full CEL evaluation. Couples to future CEL runtime framework phase. Anchored at ADR-0141 §Decision; ADR-0146 cross-references.

4. **Shadow-rules access-log integration NO CURRENT DIVERGENCE** per §8.7 + §11.P13. envoy-go MVP: counter-only. Envoy v1.37.2: ALSO counter-only (the §11.P13 empirical confirmation closes the BRAINSTORM §6 hypothesis — no shadow-decision-annotated access-log entries in Envoy either). Documented as forward-pointer because future Envoy releases MAY introduce shadow access-log integration; envoy-go's deferral is preemptive.

5. **`sourced_metadata` + `filter_state` runtime always-no-match** per §2.5 + §8.10. envoy-go MVP: parse-supported but evaluator returns FALSE. Envoy: actual evaluation against dynamic-metadata + filter-state subsystems. In practice no operator-visible divergence under fixture-baseline default-empty conditions per §11.P15 (both Envoy + envoy-go return same disposition; the divergence-window is structural — couples to dynamic-metadata + filter-state families). Anchored at ADR-0143 §Decision; ADR-0146 cross-references.

6. **`Principal_Authenticated` canonical 3 cert fields only** per §1.1 amendment 12 + §8.9 + D11. envoy-go MVP: URI SAN + DNS SAN + Subject DN CN. Additional cert fields (Issuer DN, Serial Number, fingerprints) NOT exposed. Couples to future TLS-context-extension phase. Anchored at ADR-0144 §Decision (canonical 3-cert-field scope); ADR-0146 cross-references.

**Shadow-evaluation discipline** is structurally a parallel-to-primary engine walk per SPEC §6.7 + §6.9. The shadow rules / shadow matcher proto fields (`shadow_rules` / `shadow_matcher`; mutually exclusive per §1.1 amendment 2) configure a second engine instance whose evaluation NEVER affects the primary dispatch outcome (the SendLocalReply path is driven exclusively by the primary engine's `engineResultAllowed` / `engineResultDenied`). The shadow walk emits its own counters under the `shadow_rules_stat_prefix` namespace — `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied` base + lazy per-policy `<shadow_base>.policy.<policy_name>.shadow_allowed` / `<shadow_base>.policy.<policy_name>.shadow_denied` when `track_per_rule_stats: true`.

**LOG-partial precise discipline** per amendment 5 + amendment 8: LOG action → always `engineResultAllowed`; matched-policy captured for per-policy emission. The matched policy participates in the per-policy `.allowed` counter family (LOG folds into allowed; the matched policy is operator-visible). NO `logged` counter exists per §11.P6 (REFUTES BRAINSTORM 5-counter hypothesis). `access_log_hint` dynamic metadata is silent at envoy-go MVP (deferred per the divergence-window above).

### Decision

**(i) Shadow-evaluation discipline: parallel-to-primary engine walk; NEVER affects disposition; emits shadow counters.** Per SPEC §6.7 + §6.9. The shadow walk is invoked from `DecodeHeaders` only when `cc.shadowRules != nil || cc.shadowMatcher != nil`. Algorithm + walk-order are identical to the primary (lexicographic policy iteration for rules engine; matcher-tree dispatch for matcher engine). The shadow `engineResult` + matched-policy name are passed to `emitShadowCounters`, which increments `shadowAllowed` / `shadowDenied` base counters + (when `cc.trackPerRuleStats=true`) the per-policy counter under the SHADOW base prefix via `cc.stats.incPolicy(cc.stats.shadowBase, policyName, suffix)`. Shadow result NEVER flows into the dispatch switch — `engineResultDenied` on shadow does NOT trigger SendLocalReply.

**(ii) LOG-partial divergence-window codification.** Per amendment 5 + amendment 8 + §11.P6. LOG action → always `engineResultAllowed`; matched policy captured. `emitPrimaryCounters` increments `allowed` base + per-policy `.allowed` (when track-true + matched). NO `logged` counter exists. The `access_log_hint` dynamic-metadata emission is silent at envoy-go MVP (forward-pointer to dynamic-metadata family framework phase per §8.6). Operator-visible behavior: LOG-action requests pass through unchanged + tick the `allowed` counter (operator sees the request was evaluated + matched-policy ticks under per-policy emission for visibility). On reference Envoy v1.37.2 the same request additionally emits a dynamic-metadata key carrying the access-log hint; envoy-go MVP omits this metadata key (silent-emit).

**(iii) `track_per_rule_stats` per-policy emission discipline.** Per §1.1 amendment 8 + §11.P10 + ADR-0145 §Decision (iii). When `cc.trackPerRuleStats=true` AND a policy matched (matched-policy name non-empty), `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` call `cc.stats.incPolicy(<base>, policyName, <suffix>)` to lazily allocate + increment the per-policy counter. The counter name is `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` where:
- `<base_prefix>` = `cc.stats.primaryBase` (primary side) or `cc.stats.shadowBase` (shadow side); HCM-rooted `http.<HCM>.rbac.<rules_prefix>` shape per ADR-0145 §Decision (ii) + Task 8 empirical scrape.
- `<policy_name>` = the matched `compiledPolicy.name` (verbatim from the proto policies map key).
- `<suffix>` ∈ `{allowed, denied, shadow_allowed, shadow_denied}` per disposition × side.

Lazy allocation via `sync.Map.LoadOrStore` + `NewCounterIfAbsent` per ADR-0145 §Decision (iii); race-safe across concurrent first-emission. **Operator-config-driven surface growth foot-gun:** N policies × 2 base sides × 2 (primary + shadow) = up to 4N per-policy counters per active namespace. envoy-go MVP imposes NO parse-time N-cap (mirrors Envoy permissive disposition per D7); documented at SPEC §13.4 forward-pointer notes. Future operator-ergonomics phase MAY add an envoy-go-only N-cap.

**(iv) `response_code_details` divergence-window codification.** Per amendment 11 + §8.12. envoy-go MVP: no emission. The `SendLocalReply` framework primitive has a 3-arg signature (status, body, OrderedHeaders) — there is no response-code-details slot. Reference Envoy v1.37.2 emits `"rbac_access_denied_matched_policy[<sanitized_policy_id>]"` via the `utility.cc::responseDetail` path; that surface couples to the HCM response-code-details framework which envoy-go has not yet landed. Forward-pointer to future HCM response-code-details framework phase. Operator-visible at observation surfaces that consume the field — access logs with `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%` formatter; trace span tags; etc. Under fixture-baseline conditions (no access log; no trace; just `/stats` + wire bytes) NO operator-visible divergence per §11.P15 (the 403 + 19-byte body + 4-header set are byte-identical to Envoy).

**(v) Shadow-rules access-log integration deferred (forward-pointer; NO current divergence).** Per §8.7 + §11.P13. envoy-go MVP emits shadow counters only — no shadow-decision-annotated access-log entries. Reference Envoy v1.37.2 ALSO counter-only per §11.P13 empirical confirmation. Documented as forward-pointer since future Envoy releases MAY introduce shadow access-log integration (the BRAINSTORM §6 hypothesis anticipated possible Envoy-side shadow access-log emission; §11.P13 closed the hypothesis at counter-only). envoy-go's deferral is preemptive — the divergence-window is structurally documented even though no current divergence exists.

**(vi) BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 phase-16 forward-pointer notes anchoring.** Per planner-time decision 4 + 16. The 6 divergence-windows enumerated above are the authoritative content for the `### Phase 16 forward-pointer notes` subsection of BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 (the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT edit lands at Task 15 per PLAN.md task allocation; ADR-0146 is the in-place reference). The subsection codifies for operators: which Envoy-side observable surfaces are intentionally narrower in envoy-go MVP; which future framework primitive each surface couples to; the §11.P15 invariant that under fixture-baseline conditions the divergence-windows produce NO operator-visible behavior delta (both Envoy + envoy-go return same disposition; same wire bytes; same counter increments — the deltas only surface when an operator consumes dynamic metadata, access logs with response-code-details formatter, or CEL-evaluated conditions).

### Alternatives considered

**(a) Shadow disposition affects dispatch (rejected per (i)).** A hypothetical alternative would have the shadow engine's `engineResultDenied` participate in the dispatch decision (e.g., DENY-if-EITHER-engine-denies). REJECTED — REFUTES SPEC §6.7 + §11.P6 + the entire purpose of shadow rules (shadow = observe-only-without-enforcement; operators iterate policy designs against production traffic without risking false-positive denials). Envoy v1.37.2's shadow walk never affects dispatch per the `utility.cc::checkPolicyMatch(shadow=true)` calling convention. The chosen disposition (parallel-walk; counter-only emission) matches the reference behavior exactly.

**(b) Separate `logged` counter for LOG-action (rejected per amendment 8 + §11.P6).** A hypothetical alternative would emit a third base counter `logged` for LOG-matched requests (BRAINSTORM §2.6 5-counter hypothesis). REJECTED — REFUTES §11.P6 empirical confirmation that Envoy v1.37.2's `utility.h::ENFORCE_RBAC_FILTER_STATS` macro defines only `allowed` + `denied` (no `logged`). LOG-action engine output is `engineResultAllowed`; the `allowed` counter ticks. Per-policy `<policy_name>.allowed` ticks for matched-policy visibility. This is the canonical 4-base-counter shape per ADR-0140 + ADR-0145.

**(c) Per-policy counter emission unconditional (rejected per (iii) gating).** A hypothetical alternative would emit per-policy counters whenever a policy matches, regardless of `track_per_rule_stats`. REJECTED — operator-config-driven N-policy × 4-counter surface growth must be opt-in per Envoy v1.37.2's behavior (the `track_per_rule_stats` flag controls per-policy emission). envoy-go mirrors. The gating discipline at `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` is `cc.trackPerRuleStats && policyName != "" && suffix != ""`.

**(d) Per-policy counter naming without `.policy.` segment infix (rejected per ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) refinement).** A hypothetical alternative would use the SPEC line 1842 hypothesis `<base_prefix>.<policy_name>.<suffix>` (no `.policy.` segment). REJECTED — refuted by the Task 8 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 which inserts a literal `.policy.` segment between the base prefix and the policy name. The empirical shape is `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>`; ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) codifies the refined shape; ADR-0146 inherits it via `cc.stats.incPolicy(base, policyName, suffix)` which constructs `base + ".policy." + policyName + "." + suffix` internally.

**(e) Emit `response_code_details` via header-channel workaround (rejected per (iv)).** A hypothetical alternative would synthesize an `x-envoy-response-code-details` header on the SendLocalReply call to thread the matched-policy ID to operators consuming the wire-headers carrier. REJECTED — that is a non-standard header that operators do NOT expect on a deny response; Envoy emits the value via the HCM response-code-details framework (which exposes it to access-log formatters + trace span tags), NOT via a wire header. The workaround would diverge from Envoy in BOTH directions (envoy-go would emit a header Envoy doesn't; Envoy would emit the field via a channel envoy-go doesn't have). The chosen disposition (no emission; forward-pointer to future HCM response-code-details framework phase) preserves the byte-identical wire-bytes invariant on the SendLocalReply path AND keeps the divergence-window structural (operator-config-driven on whether the divergence is observable).

**(f) Shadow-rules access-log integration eagerly added (rejected per (v)).** A hypothetical alternative would proactively emit shadow-decision-annotated access-log entries (using the AccessLog framework primitive once it lands). REJECTED — §11.P13 confirmed Envoy v1.37.2 is ALSO counter-only on shadow; eagerly adding the integration would create a forward-divergence (envoy-go emits shadow access-log entries; Envoy doesn't). The chosen disposition matches Envoy v1.37.2's counter-only behavior + documents the forward-pointer for future Envoy releases that MAY introduce the integration.

### Consequences

- **The 4 base counters (`allowed` / `denied` / `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied`) tick unconditionally per disposition × side** per ADR-0145 §Decision (i) + ADR-0146 §Decision (i)+(ii). LOG-matched paths fold into `allowed` per amendment 8. Shadow disposition NEVER affects primary dispatch (parallel-walk discipline per §6.7).
- **Per-policy counters are lazy-allocated via `filterStats.incPolicy`** per ADR-0145 §Decision (iii); the emission discipline at `emitPrimaryCounters` / `emitShadowCounters` is gated on `cc.trackPerRuleStats && policyName != "" && suffix != ""`. Counter name shape `<base_prefix>.policy.<policy_name>.<suffix>` per the Task 8 empirical scrape refinement.
- **SPEC §13.2 stat-table line 1842-1845 templates** carry the per-policy counter rows. The empirical-scrape-refined `.policy.` segment is documented at ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) + ADR-0146 §Decision (iii). The SPEC stat-table rows themselves remain in their hypothesis form (`<rules_stat_prefix>.<policy_name>.<suffix>` per line 1842) per phase-15 SPEC-immutable-post-commit precedent; the ADR-trail (ADR-0145 + ADR-0146) is the authoritative reference for the impl-time-refined shape. Operators reading SPEC §13.2 are cross-referenced to ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) + ADR-0146 §Decision (iii) for the live counter shape. **SPEC §13.2 in-place amendment was considered + rejected** per phase-15 precedent (no in-place SPEC amendments at impl-time; the ADR-trail carries refinements); the §13.2 row-template form is operator-orienting (operators query per-policy by `grep policy` regardless of the exact intermediate segment), so the documentation cost of the deferral is low.
- **Shadow walk invocation gate** is `cc.shadowRules != nil || cc.shadowMatcher != nil` per the existing `DecodeHeaders` body (Task 7 landing). When shadow is unconfigured, the shadow walk is skipped entirely + the `shadow_allowed` / `shadow_denied` base counters publish 0 (predeclared empty counters for scrape stability per ADR-0145 §Decision (vi)).
- **Response-code-details divergence-window is operator-visible only at observation surfaces consuming the field** — access-log formatters with `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`; trace span tags; etc. Under fixture-baseline conditions (no access log; no trace; just wire bytes + `/stats`) NO operator-visible divergence per §11.P15. Fixture 0018 (Tasks 12-14) asserts wire-byte equivalence + stat equivalence; response-code-details divergence is non-asserted (the field is not threaded to either Envoy's or envoy-go's `/stats` endpoint).
- **The 6 divergence-windows enumerated at §Context** anchor the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT §13.4 phase-16 forward-pointer notes subsection (the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT edit lands at Task 15 per PLAN.md task allocation). ADR-0146 is the authoritative reference; the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT subsection is operator-facing prose that cross-references back to ADR-0146 §Decision (i)-(vi).
- **Group 5 + Group 9 unit tests extend the Task 7 + Task 8 baseline by 7 new test cases** verifying the emission discipline: (1) `TestDecodeHeaders_LOGMatch_TrackPerRuleStats_AllowedPerPolicyCounterIncremented`; (2) `TestDecodeHeaders_PerPolicyEmission_OnlyMatchedPolicyCounters_Increment`; (3) `TestDecodeHeaders_PerPolicyEmission_TrackPerRuleStatsFalse_NoPerPolicyCounters`; (4) `TestDecodeHeaders_ShadowEnabled_PrimaryDispositionWins_ShadowCountersIncrement`; (5) `TestDecodeHeaders_ShadowEnabled_TrackPerRuleStats_PerPolicyShadowCountersIncrement`; (6) `TestDecodeHeaders_ShadowDeniedWithTrackPerRuleStats_PerPolicyShadowDeniedCounter`; (7) `TestDecodeHeaders_DenyMatch_NoResponseCodeDetailsEmitted_DivergenceWindow`. All 7 PASS under `go test -race -count=1`. Total rbac test count rises from 93 PASS + 2 SKIP (Task 8) to 100 PASS + 2 SKIP (Task 9).
- **No framework-primitive surface changes at Task 9** — the changes are purely internal to `internal/filter/http/rbac/`. `emitPrimaryCounters` + `emitShadowCounters` gain per-policy emission gating (the function signatures already carried the `policyName` parameter from Task 7); no API edits to `DecoderFilterCallbacks` or `MatchContext`.
- **Fixture 0018 (Tasks 12-14) end-to-end validates** the 6 divergence-windows + the shadow-walk discipline + the LOG-partial counter emission + the `track_per_rule_stats` per-policy counter emission against reference Envoy v1.37.2 side-by-side. The 8-scenario matrix per BRAINSTORM §6.2 + SPEC §7.1 covers: scenario 1 (ALLOW + match → 200 + `allowed=1`); scenario 2 (ALLOW + no-match → 403 + `denied=1`); scenario 3 (DENY + match → 403 + `denied=1`); scenario 4 (DENY + no-match → 200 + `allowed=1`); scenario 5 (LOG + match → 200 + `allowed=1` + per-policy `.allowed=1`); scenario 6 (mTLS + Principal_Authenticated three-case); scenario 7 (shadow primary-ALLOW + shadow-DENY → 200 + `allowed=1` + `shadow_denied=1`); scenario 8 (matcher-engine + track_per_rule_stats per-policy emission). Counter-line assertions land at Task 14.
- **Cross-references:** ADR-0143 §Decision (vi) (Principal_Authenticated three-case algorithm consumed by divergence-window #6); ADR-0144 §Decision (canonical 3-cert-field scope — divergence-window #6's structural anchor); ADR-0145 §Decision (iii) (per-policy `.policy.` segment refinement — emission discipline inherits); ADR-0141 §Decision (CEL three-field silent-ignore — divergence-window #3); SPEC §1.1 amendments 5 + 8 + 11 + §6.7 + §6.9 + §8.6 + §8.7 + §8.10 + §8.12 + §11.P6 + §11.P10 + §11.P13 + §11.P14 + §11.P15.

## ADR-0147: Phase-03 TLS-layer `require_client_certificate=true` blanket-rejection lifted SCOPED to well-formed mTLS configurations (validation_context.trusted_ca PEM provided) — maps onto stdlib `crypto/tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert` mode + `ClientCAs` pool populated from the parsed trusted_ca

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Doctrine:** Phase-16 framework-delta. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention (impl-time-unanticipated escape valve; mirrors phase-14 ADR-0134 + phase-13 ADR-0127-v2 in-task-lift precedent). Phase-16 anticipated ADR roster: ADR-0140..ADR-0146 (7 ADRs per BRAINSTORM §7). ADR-0147 is the 8th — the unanticipated-but-required structural change to lift the phase-03 TLS-layer blanket rejection of `require_client_certificate=true` (ADR-0032 §Decision (7)) for fixture 0018's scenario 6 mTLS path.
**Lands-in-task:** Task 14 (fixture 0018 integration uncovered the missing functionality; ADR authored at Task 14 follow-up in-place per ADR-0044 §Decision (b) impl-time-anchoring).

### Context

Phase-03's `internal/tls/config.go.NewDownstreamConfig` blanket-rejected `require_client_certificate=true` with `"tls: downstream: require_client_certificate is not supported in phase 03"` per ADR-0032 §Decision (7). The rejection was structurally appropriate at phase-03 (TCP+TLS bootstrap; no listener-level filter required mTLS-server-verify), but blocks fixture 0018's scenario 6 — the listener `l_test_a_tls` MUST require a verified client cert to thread the cert URI SAN to the rbac filter's `authenticated_admin` policy via the ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` framework primitive.

Phase-16 SPEC §7.2 (line 1241) DOES specify the listener-level config as:
> *"transport_socket: DownstreamTlsContext{common_tls_context:{tls_certificates:[server cert/key], validation_context:{trusted_ca:fixture-CA, match_subject_alt_names:[<SPIFFE pattern>]}}, require_client_certificate: true}"*

This was authored at SPEC time per the BRAINSTORM-time mTLS-required hypothesis. The phase-03 TLS-layer restriction was NOT flagged at SPEC time (the SPEC §3 framework-survey enumerated rbac-filter primitives, not TLS-layer pre-existing restrictions). The restriction surfaced empirically at Task-14 dry-run.

Three resolution paths were considered:

- **(a) Skip scenario 6 from the fixture differential.** The ADR-0144 framework primitive is unit-tested at Task 6 (Group 7) for the three-case algorithm + case (c) plaintext-FALSE path. The fixture's mTLS scenario was the END-TO-END validation. Skipping loses the end-to-end claim but preserves all per-task acceptance gates.
- **(b) Lift the phase-03 restriction WHOLESALE (allow `require_client_certificate=true` unconditionally; do nothing about ClientCAs / verify configuration).** REJECTED — leaks no-verify semantics on production paths where operators set `require_client_certificate=true` without a trusted_ca; behavioral surprise vs Envoy (which also requires a trusted_ca chain for verification).
- **(c) Lift SCOPED — accept `require_client_certificate=true` only when `validation_context.trusted_ca` is also provided; load the trusted_ca into a ClientCAs pool + set `tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert`.** ACCEPTED.

### Decision

**(i) Lift the phase-03 ADR-0032 §Decision (7) blanket-rejection of `require_client_certificate=true` SCOPED to well-formed mTLS configurations.** `NewDownstreamConfig` accepts `require_client_certificate=true` when AND ONLY when:
- `common_tls_context.validation_context` is non-nil; AND
- `validation_context.trusted_ca` is set (DataSource resolves to a non-empty PEM that AppendCertsFromPEM accepts).

If either condition fails, error with `"tls: downstream: require_client_certificate=true requires validation_context.trusted_ca"`. The earlier `"is not supported in phase 03"` error is RETIRED.

**(ii) Map onto stdlib `crypto/tls` mTLS semantics.** When the lift fires, the constructed `*tls.Config` carries:
- `ClientCAs = <pool populated from trusted_ca PEM>` (via `x509.NewCertPool` + `AppendCertsFromPEM`).
- `ClientAuth = tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert` — the strictest stdlib mode; the server requires AND verifies the client cert against the ClientCAs pool. Matches Envoy's `require_client_certificate=true` semantics verbatim (Envoy verifies via `validation_context` whenever `require_client_certificate=true` is set).

**(iii) Preserve all other phase-03 TLS-layer restrictions UNCHANGED.** The SDS-bound secrets rejection (`tls_certificate_sds_secret_configs` + `validation_context_sds_secret_config` + `combined_validation_context`), the `custom_validator_config` rejection, the `match_typed_subject_alt_names` rejection, the `verify_certificate_hash` + `verify_certificate_spki` rejections — ALL remain rejected via the unchanged `commonTLSContextToConfig` pre-checks. The lift is NARROWLY SCOPED to `require_client_certificate=true` + the trusted_ca-required gate; future fixtures needing additional mTLS surface (SDS-bound mTLS secrets, custom validators, etc.) will require additional scoped lifts (each via its own ADR per ADR-0044).

**(iv) Test surface split.** `config_test.go`'s pre-existing `t.Run("require_client_certificate", ...)` test (which asserted the rejection error) is split into TWO tests:
- `require_client_certificate_without_trusted_ca` — asserts the rejection still fires when `validation_context.trusted_ca` is absent; error must contain BOTH `"require_client_certificate"` AND `"trusted_ca"`.
- `require_client_certificate_with_trusted_ca` — asserts the lift fires when `validation_context.trusted_ca` is provided; `cfg.TLSConfig.ClientAuth == tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert` + `cfg.TLSConfig.ClientCAs != nil`.

**(v) Listener-manager integration unchanged.** `internal/listener/manager_test.go`'s pre-existing `TestNewManager_MultiChain_RequireClientCert_Errors` still passes (the test's `mkDownstreamTSRequireClientCert` helper does NOT set a trusted_ca; the no-trusted_ca rejection branch fires; the error message still contains `"require_client_certificate"`).

### Alternatives considered

**(a) Skip fixture 0018 scenario 6 entirely (drop mTLS path from the differential matrix; rely on Task 6 Group 7 unit tests for ADR-0144 validation).** REJECTED — fixture 0018 is the END-TO-END validation of the ADR-0144 framework primitive (HCM dispatch → connection-state extraction → chain.SetTLSPrincipals → filter-callback observation → Principal_Authenticated three-case algorithm). Skipping the scenario leaves the plumbing untested at integration scale; the unit tests cover the surface but not the wiring. The SPEC §7.1 + §11.P14 specifically calls out scenario 6 as the ADR-0144 end-to-end integration anchor.

**(b) Lift WHOLESALE (allow `require_client_certificate=true` unconditionally).** REJECTED — see §Context. Leaks no-verify semantics on production paths where operators may set `require_client_certificate=true` without a trusted_ca (expecting Envoy's strict behavior); behavioral surprise. The SCOPED lift matches Envoy's behavior verbatim (Envoy errors if `require_client_certificate=true` without a verification context).

**(c) Implement an envoy-go-only `require_client_certificate_no_verify: true` extension.** REJECTED — non-standard surface; operators portably configuring `require_client_certificate=true + trusted_ca:<pem>` get the strict behavior they expect.

**(d) Defer fixture 0018 scenario 6 to a future phase that lifts SDS-bound mTLS secrets too (a "real mTLS phase").** REJECTED — the lift required for fixture 0018 is narrowly scoped (no SDS; no custom validators; just `require_client_certificate=true + trusted_ca:<pem>`); deferring the entire scenario blocks the ADR-0144 end-to-end validation for an open-ended duration. The SCOPED lift unblocks fixture 0018 without taking on the broader phase commitment.

### Consequences

- **`internal/tls/config.go.NewDownstreamConfig`** gains a 20-LoC code path that loads the trusted_ca DataSource (via the existing `loadDataSource` helper; supports `inline_bytes` / `inline_string` / `filename`) + appends to a ClientCAs pool + sets `ClientAuth = tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert`. The change is additive — the no-trusted_ca rejection branch still fires for misconfigured operators.
- **`internal/tls/config_test.go`** gains the `require_client_certificate_with_trusted_ca` test case asserting ClientCAs + ClientAuth fields; the pre-existing `require_client_certificate` test case is renamed `require_client_certificate_without_trusted_ca` with the assertion strengthened to require BOTH `"require_client_certificate"` AND `"trusted_ca"` in the error message.
- **`internal/listener/manager_test.go.TestNewManager_MultiChain_RequireClientCert_Errors`** continues to pass UNCHANGED — the test's helper builds a transport socket without a trusted_ca, hitting the rejection branch; the error message still contains `"require_client_certificate"` (with the additional `"trusted_ca"` substring, which the test does NOT assert on).
- **Fixture 0018's `envoy-go.yaml`** (Task 13 author) carries `require_client_certificate: true` on the `l_test_a_tls` listener's `DownstreamTlsContext`; with ADR-0147 the listener manager successfully constructs the chain TLS config + the listener accepts mTLS connections.
- **Fixture 0018 scenario 6 PASSES end-to-end** — the driver's `runTLSScenario6` builds an mTLS-capable http.Client carrying the fixture client cert; the listener verifies the client cert against the fixture-CA via the ClientCAs pool; the HCM dispatch's `connection.go.downstreamTLSPrincipals` extracts the cert URI SAN (`spiffe://example.com/admin`); the chain plumbs it to the rbac filter's `evalContext.DownstreamPrincipal()`; the `authenticated_admin` policy's `Principal_Authenticated.principal_name.StringMatcher` matches → ALLOW → 200.
- **Phase-03 TLS-layer scope preserved.** ADR-0147 is a TARGETED lift — only `require_client_certificate=true` + `trusted_ca`-required gate. The broader phase-03 restrictions (SDS, custom validators, match_typed_san, verify_certificate_*) remain rejected. Future fixtures needing those surfaces will require additional scoped lifts.
- **No SPEC §1.1 amendment.** ADR-0147 codifies a TLS-layer pre-existing restriction lift (not a phase-16 rbac-filter surface change). The phase-16 SPEC §7.2 listener config is already authored with `require_client_certificate=true` (line 1241) anticipating the lift; the lift simply unblocks that authored config. No SPEC line modifications needed.
- **Cross-references:** ADR-0032 §Decision (7) (phase-03 TLS-layer scope discipline — the lifted clause); ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention — impl-time-unanticipated escape valve); ADR-0134 (phase-14 framework-delta precedent — impl-time-unanticipated ADR lands at impl-task follow-up); ADR-0127-v2 (phase-13 in-task-lift precedent); ADR-0144 (TLS-principal accessor framework primitive — the dependency this lift unblocks for fixture 0018 scenario 6); SPEC §7.2 (line 1241 — the authored listener config requiring the lift); SPEC §11.P14 (the ADR-0144 end-to-end integration anchor scenario 6).

## ADR-0148: `internal/filter/http/jwtauthn/` package shape — single-token directory matching cors/fault/csrf/buffer/compressor/localratelimit/bandwidthlimit/rbac precedent (underscore-stripped per ADR-0114) + DECODER-only `HTTPFilter` value (`Encoder: nil`; 4th §9 row to ship pure decode-side per phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer + phase-16 rbac precedent) + 7-base-counter `filterStats` (per SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §11.P6 — REFUTES BRAINSTORM 8-per-provider-scaling hypothesis; NO gauges; NO histograms; canonical names `allowed` + `cors_preflight_bypassed` + `denied` + `jwks_fetch_success` + `jwks_fetch_failed` + `jwt_cache_hit` + `jwt_cache_miss` per `ALL_JWT_AUTHN_FILTER_STATS` macro) + unconditional counter allocation at New() time (NO lazy-allocation; mirrors phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer SHARED-stats discipline) + deny-path wire shape `SendLocalReply(401-or-403, getStatusString(reason), {www-authenticate: Bearer realm="<original_uri>"<, error="invalid_token">})` per SPEC §1.1 amendments 8 + 12 + §11.P1 + §11.P2 + boot-registration ordering (alphabetical-after-header_mutation)

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-13
**Doctrine:** Phase 17 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. Co-anchors with ADR-0149 (compiledConfig shape) + ADR-0150 (HTTP-outbound primitive) + ADR-0151 (JWT verifier primitive) + ADR-0152 (token extraction) + ADR-0153 (8th canonical per-route) + ADR-0154 (stat surface) + ADR-0155 (deny-path wire shape).
**Lands-in-task:** Task 2 of phase-17 PLAN.

### Context

Phase 17 lands `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn` as the 10th §9 production HTTP filter (after cors @ 07.1, fault @ 09, header_mutation @ 10, local_ratelimit @ 11, csrf @ 12, buffer @ 13, compressor @ 14, bandwidth_limit @ 15, rbac @ 16). The package shape decision (directory naming + file split + filter-struct + factory signature + filterStats shape + boot-registration ordering + deny-path wire shape) builds on the cors / fault / header_mutation / localratelimit / csrf / buffer / compressor / bandwidthlimit / rbac precedents.

The package directory + Go-package identifier are both `jwtauthn` — single token underscore-stripped per ADR-0114 (which codified the single-token discipline for compound proto type-names; matches `localratelimit/` + `bandwidthlimit/` precedent). The proto type-URL preserves the underscore as `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn` (per Envoy upstream convention), but the Go-package identifier strips it for Go-language naming hygiene.

Files mirror the phase-14 + phase-15 + phase-16 multi-file split (the precedent for larger filters with multi-subsurface logic): `jwtauthn.go` (filter type + factory + decode methods + filterStats struct + compiledConfig + per-route helper), `evaluator.go` (6-variant JwtRequirement evaluator + extraction-source iteration + RequirementRule dispatch), `provider.go` (JwtProvider compiled-state + algorithm allow-list + JWKS reference + extraction-source set + side-effect set), `jwtauthn_test.go` (unit tests; anticipated 1500-2500 LoC given the evaluator + provider + extraction-source + verification subsurface), `fuzz_test.go` (the 21st fuzzer in the repo — `FuzzJwtAuthnConfigParse`), `doc.go` (package overview).

The DECODER-only HTTPFilter value (`Encoder: nil`) makes phase 17 the 4th §9 row to ship pure decode-side (after phase-12 csrf, phase-13 buffer, phase-16 rbac). jwt_authn is a request-gate filter — validation happens at `DecodeHeaders` before any body, and side-effects (header strip + forward_payload_header + claim_to_headers + clear_route_cache) all operate on the request headers. No encode-side surface is structurally needed.

The 7-base-counter `filterStats` shape is empirically RATIFIED-via-REFUTATION-of-BRAINSTORM-hypothesis at SPEC §11.P6 via verbatim scrape of Envoy v1.37.2 `source/extensions/filters/http/jwt_authn/stats.h`. The BRAINSTORM hypothesis of "8 base counters with per-provider scaling: 2 per-provider counters (jwt_authn_success/failed) + 5 per-provider JWKS counters + 1 filter-wide bypass" was REFUTED — Envoy emits 7 filter-wide counters (`allowed`, `cors_preflight_bypassed`, `denied`, `jwks_fetch_success`, `jwks_fetch_failed`, `jwt_cache_hit`, `jwt_cache_miss`) at the HCM stat_prefix scope; NO per-provider scaling; NO gauges; NO histograms. The `jwt_cache_hit` + `jwt_cache_miss` pair is gated on `jwt_cache_config` (deferred per §8 deferral 8); structurally unreachable under phase-17 MVP.

The deny-path wire shape is empirically RATIFIED-AND-EXTENDED at SPEC §11.P1 + §11.P2 + §11.P3 via verbatim scrape of Envoy v1.37.2 `source/extensions/filters/http/jwt_authn/filter.cc`. The status mapping is 401 for most failure-reasons + 403 specifically for `JwtAudienceNotAllowed` (RFC 6750 semantic: 401 = unauthenticated; 403 = authenticated-but-not-authorized-for-this-audience). The body is `getStatusString(status)` from jwt_verify_lib's ~70-entry canonical mapping. The WWW-Authenticate header is `Bearer realm="<original_uri>"` with conditional `, error="invalid_token"` appended for non-`JwtMissed` statuses (RFC 6750 §3 challenge syntax). The `strip_failure_response: true` proto field strips BOTH body AND WWW-Authenticate header. The phase-04 HCM-scope limitation around `response_code_details` field emission is documented as a divergence-window per SPEC §1.1 amendment 11 + §8 deferral 13 (envoy-go MVP defers; Envoy emits `jwt_authn_access_denied{<reason>}`).

The boot-registration ordering follows ADR-0072 + ADR-0100 §2.2 alphabetical-after-router convention: `router → bandwidthlimit → buffer → compressor → cors → csrf → envoygotest → fault → header_mutation → jwtauthn → localratelimit → rbac → Freeze`. The `jwtauthn` entry inserts between `header_mutation` and `localratelimit` to maintain alphabetical ordering. Per ADR-0072, registration order does NOT affect runtime behavior; this is a stylistic discipline only.

The factoryState shape is SIMPLIFIED relative to phase-11/15/16 (which carried per-route lazy-cache `sync.Map` for INDEPENDENT-stats). Phase-17 SHARED-stats discipline (per ADR-0153 + §5.2) eliminates the need for per-route filterStats allocation; the listener-level filterStats is shared across all routes. The factoryState carries one `sync.Map` for `compiledPerRoute` lazy-build (keyed by per-route TPFC proto pointer; mirrors phase-16 pattern minus the per-route stats branch).

The §1.1 amendments 8 + 12 + §11.P1 + §11.P2 RATIFICATIONS materially refine the deny-path wire shape from BRAINSTORM hypothesis:
- BRAINSTORM §4 hypothesized "401 + WWW-Authenticate Bearer realm=\"<issuer>\"" — REFINED to "401 default + 403 for JwtAudienceNotAllowed + WWW-Authenticate Bearer realm=\"<original_uri>\" + conditional error=invalid_token append".
- BRAINSTORM §10 §17.P2 hypothesized realm=\"<issuer>\" — REFUTED; Envoy uses request URI captured at DecodeHeaders.

The 12 §1.1 amendments authored in phase-17 SPEC (matching phase-16 rbac's 12-amendment volume) document the empirical refinements. The structural design (DECODER-only filter, 7-counter filterStats, deny-path wire shape, boot-registration ordering) survives intact despite the refinements.

### Decision

**(i) Single-token package directory `internal/filter/http/jwtauthn/`.** Per ADR-0114. The directory name + Go-package identifier are both `jwtauthn` (no underscore); the proto type-URL preserves the underscore as `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn`. Matches `localratelimit/` + `bandwidthlimit/` precedent. The TypeURL const at `internal/filter/http/jwtauthn/jwtauthn.go` is `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.jwt_authn.v3.JwtAuthentication`; the `filterName` package-private const is `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn`.

**(ii) DECODER-only `HTTPFilter` value.** The factory's `FilterInstanceFactory` closure returns `envoyhttp.HTTPFilter{Name: filterName, Decoder: f, Encoder: nil}`. jwt_authn is a pre-body request gate — validation + side-effects (strip / forward_payload_header / claim_to_headers / clear_route_cache) all operate at `DecodeHeaders` time; no encode-side surface is structurally needed. 4th §9 row to ship decode-only (phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer + phase-16 rbac precedent). The compile-time assertion `var _ envoyhttp.StreamDecoderFilter = (*filter)(nil)` at `jwtauthn.go` documents the discipline.

**(iii) 7-base-counter `filterStats` (proto-faithful per SPEC §1.1 amendment 9 + §11.P6).** The seven counters — `allowed`, `denied`, `cors_preflight_bypassed`, `jwks_fetch_success`, `jwks_fetch_failed`, `jwt_cache_hit`, `jwt_cache_miss` — register unconditionally at `New()` time via `newFilterStats(reg, ctx.StatPrefix)`. The pair `jwt_cache_hit` + `jwt_cache_miss` is STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE under phase-17 MVP per §8 deferral 8 (jwt_cache_config silent-ignored); the counters publish 0 for the listener's lifetime but are registered for scrape-stability per Prometheus best practice. The `cors_preflight_bypassed` canonical naming REFUTES the BRAINSTORM `bypassed_cors_preflight` hypothesis per §1.1 amendment 10. NO gauges. NO histograms. NO per-provider counter scaling — REFUTES BRAINSTORM "8 per-provider counters" hypothesis (multiple providers contribute to the same `allowed` / `denied` / `jwks_fetch_*` counters at filter-wide scope).

**(iv) Unconditional counter allocation (NO lazy-allocation).** All 7 counters allocate at `New()` time via `reg.NewCounter` calls inside `newFilterStats`. Mirrors phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer SHARED-stats discipline (DIVERGES from phase-11 / phase-15 / phase-16 INDEPENDENT-stats + lazy per-policy allocation). Operators see a consistent scrape surface from listener-load onward; the seven counters are predeclared regardless of provider configuration. Per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance: `buildCompiledConfig` guards via `if ctx.Stats != nil` before calling `newFilterStats` — test code paths with nil `ctx.Stats` proceed without counter registration; `cc.stats` is nil; counter-emission helpers nil-tolerate.

**(v) Deny-path wire shape per ADR-0155 §Decision (anchored at Task 9).** SendLocalReply emits status 401 for most failure-reasons + 403 specifically for `JwtAudienceNotAllowed` (mirrors Envoy filter.cc `code = (status == Status::JwtAudienceNotAllowed) ? Http::Code::Forbidden : Http::Code::Unauthorized`); body is `getStatusString(status)` from jwt_verify_lib's ~70-entry canonical table; WWW-Authenticate header is `Bearer realm="<original_uri>"` with conditional `, error="invalid_token"` append for non-`JwtMissed` statuses (RFC 6750 §3 challenge syntax); `strip_failure_response: true` strips both body AND WWW-Authenticate; per-route runtime-resolve dangling-name error emits 403 + plain body `"Failed JWT authentication: Wrong requirement_name: <name>"` + NO WWW-Authenticate. ADR-0148 anchors the design intent; the body shape ships in full at Task 9 per ADR-0155.

**(vi) Boot-registration ordering — alphabetical-after-`header_mutation`.** Per ADR-0072 + ADR-0100 §2.2. The `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot wiring inserts `httpReg.Register(jwtauthn.TypeURL, jwtauthn.New)` between `header_mutation` (line 127) and `localratelimit` (line 128) at Task 10 landing. Registration order does NOT affect runtime behavior per ADR-0072; this is a stylistic discipline only. The Task 1 PROGRESS preamble captures the 11-Register baseline (router + 10 filters) at master tip `d225bb7`; Task 10 brings the count to 12.

**(vii) factoryState simplification (single sync.Map for per-route only; SHARED-stats discipline).** Per ADR-0153 + §5.2. The `factoryState` struct carries `listenerRC *compiledConfig` + `perRoute sync.Map`. UNLIKE phase-11 + phase-15 + phase-16 (which carried per-route INDEPENDENT-stats via per-route `*filterStats` allocation paths), phase-17 SHARED-stats discipline means the listener-level `cc.stats` is the SOLE counter surface; per-route TPFC entries materialize as lightweight `*compiledPerRoute` values (disabled + requirementName) without spawning fresh `*filterStats`. The sync.Map is keyed by `*jwt_authnv3.PerRouteConfig` proto pointer-identity per ADR-0117 + ADR-0125 §(xiii); race-safe via LoadOrStore.

### Consequences

- **The package `internal/filter/http/jwtauthn/` lands at Task 2** with `doc.go` + `jwtauthn.go` (filter type + factory + DecodeHeaders body STUB + filterStats + helpers) + `jwtauthn_test.go` (Group 1 + Group 7 + Group 11 tests; Groups 2/3/4/5/6/8/9/10/12 stubbed with `t.Skip` for downstream task visibility). The `evaluator.go` + `provider.go` files anticipated at SPEC time DEFERRED into `jwtauthn.go` at Task 2 for cohesion (Task 5/6/7 may split them out as the surfaces grow). LoC at Task 2: doc.go ~150, jwtauthn.go ~480, jwtauthn_test.go ~870 (35-test Group 1 + 11 Group 7 + 3 Group 11 + 9 stubbed downstream). Task 2 commit lands the §Decision + §Consequences bodies for ADR-0148 + ADR-0149 per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
- **The 7 base counters publish under the SN2-reuse namespace** `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.jwt_authn.<counter>` per ADR-0154 + §11.P7 (RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME-EMPIRICAL-SCRAPE at Task 8). When HCM stat_prefix is empty (test code paths), the namespace folds to `jwt_authn.<counter>` to satisfy the Registry's name regex. The `baseStatPrefix(hcmStatPrefix)` helper at `jwtauthn.go` implements the namespacing; Task 8 closes the RATIFIED-PENDING pin by running the empirical scrape against fixture 0019's reference Envoy listener config.
- **The STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE counters publish 0 indefinitely under MVP** (`jwt_cache_hit` + `jwt_cache_miss`). Operators consuming `/stats` see these counters with value `0`; documented divergence-window vs reference Envoy v1.37.2 which exercises the cache path when `jwt_cache_config` is set. Future caching-family framework phase wires these counters into the cache lookup path; the structural registration today anticipates that wiring.
- **The deny-path wire shape divergence-window for `response_code_details`** per §1.1 amendment 11 + §8 deferral 13. envoy-go MVP: no emission (SendLocalReply 3-arg signature has no response-code-details slot). Envoy: emits `jwt_authn_access_denied{<reason_with_spaces_as_underscores>}`. Joint with phase-16 ADR-0146 §Decision (iv) forward-pointer; future HCM response-code-details framework phase closes both divergences simultaneously. Operator-visible only at observation surfaces consuming the field (access logs with `%RESPONSE_CODE_DETAILS%`; trace span tags); under fixture-baseline conditions (wire-bytes + `/stats` only) NO operator-visible divergence.
- **Boot-registration site at `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` lands at Task 10** between `header_mutation` (line 127) and `localratelimit` (line 128). The PROGRESS Task 1 preamble notes the 11-Register baseline; Task 10 brings the count to 12 (alphabetical-after-`header_mutation` per ADR-0100 §2.2).
- **The decoder-only HTTPFilter value is verified at Task 2 via the compile-time assertion** `var _ envoyhttp.StreamDecoderFilter = (*filter)(nil)`. The `DecodeHeaders` + `DecodeData` + `DecodeTrailers` + `OnDestroy` + `SetDecoderCallbacks` methods are all implemented at Task 2 (DecodeHeaders is a STUB returning `envoyhttp.Continue`; the others are no-ops / passthrough). Task 9 fills the DecodeHeaders body per ADR-0155.
- **Task 2 acceptance**: Group 1 (19 cases — outer-envelope parse, filter_state_rules silent-ignore, 7-counter registration, canonical naming, RemoteJwks/LocalJwks Task-3/Task-4 stub error, no-JWKS-source PARSE-REJECT, clock_skew default, JwtRequirement 6-variant parse, RequirementRule match-required + dangling-name PARSE-REJECT) + Group 7 (11 cases — parsePerRoute PGV-mirror + 3 disposition cases + dangling-name Task-7-stubbed) + Group 11 (3 cases — pointer-identity lazy-cache + concurrent LoadOrStore race-safe) all PASS under `go test -race -count=1`. Total 33 PASS + 10 SKIP (downstream groups + dangling-name).
- **Cross-references:** ADR-0149 (compiledConfig shape — paired Task 2 ADR); ADR-0150 (jwks framework primitive — Task 3); ADR-0151 (jwt framework primitive — Task 4); ADR-0152 (token extraction — Task 5); ADR-0153 (8th canonical per-route — Task 7); ADR-0154 (stat surface — Task 8); ADR-0155 (deny-path wire shape — Task 9); ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance pattern); ADR-0100 §2.2 (boot-registration ordering); ADR-0114 (single-token directory discipline); ADR-0072 (boot-time fail-fast); ADR-0125 §(xiii) (8th canonical per-route).
