## ADR-0165: Cross-phase-reusable callback-surface extension on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` — 6 new accessor methods (`DownstreamRemoteAddr`/`DownstreamLocalAddr`/`DownstreamTLSServerName`/`DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER`/`DownstreamProtocol`/`ListenerPrincipal`) seeded at HCM dispatch via 6 new chain primitives mirroring the ADR-0144 `tlsPrincipals`/`SetTLSPrincipals`/`DownstreamPrincipal()` pattern; ADR-0044 escape-valve firing per planner-time decision D3 + D12 of phase-18.2 PLAN; SPEC §13.5 + §6.5 step 5 + §6.6 AMENDED in-place at the same commit — the "NO new callback method" hard constraint is flipped for SPEC internal consistency with §15 item 4 + §11.P4 RATIFICATION

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve for impl-time-unanticipated decisions — this ADR's §Context is authored from scratch at IMPL time; no pre-SPEC-time draft). ADR-0071 (chain-ownership-invariant — the 6 new chain fields obey the same single-dispatch-goroutine read + signal-only-concurrent-write discipline as `tlsPrincipals`). ADR-0144 (the precedent for the seed-at-HCM-dispatch / read-via-callback pattern; `DownstreamPrincipal()` is the prior framework primitive this ADR generalizes).
**Lands-in:** Task 4 of phase-18.2 IMPL (this commit).

### Context

The phase-18.2 SPEC §13.5 (BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT integration) stated as a hard constraint:

> **§13.5 — `## HTTPFilterCallbacks` — NO extensions.** 18.2 reuses ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` as the sole TLS-aware decoder-callback method; ALL other per-stream state needed by `buildAttributeContext` (`socket_address` source/destination, TLS `ServerName`, peer cert DER, listener-cert-derived principal, stream-start-time, per-route context-extensions) is captured at `DecodeHeaders` time into the extended `*authRequest` struct (per §6.5–§6.6) — mirroring ADR-0144's seed-at-HCM-dispatch plumbing pattern. NO new method on `envoyhttp.DecoderFilterCallbacks` lands at 18.2; the SPEC author verified that the existing callback surface at master tip (`internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`) exposes only `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` for TLS-derived state and the IMPL must NOT extend it.

SPEC §6.5 step 5 and §6.6 carried the same constraint in two more forms ("NO new `DecoderFilterCallbacks` primitive" + "pure function of `*authRequest` + the four config booleans; NO `DecoderFilterCallbacks` parameter"). Three SPEC paragraphs anchor the same "no callback-surface extension" position.

At phase-18.2 PLAN time the planner re-verified the master-tip callback surface (`internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`) and the SPEC's required populated set for `AttributeContext`:

1. **SPEC §15 acceptance item 4** requires the `AttributeContext` populated set to match reference Envoy v1.37.2's §11.P4 in-session scrape — specifically `tls_session.sni`, `source.certificate` (DER bytes), source + destination socket addresses, `destination.principal` (listener cert SAN/CN), `request.http.protocol` ("HTTP/1.1" / "HTTP/2").
2. **SPEC §11.P4 RATIFICATION** confirms reference Envoy populates `destination.principal` AUTOMATICALLY from the listener's TLS server cert (URI SAN, then DNS SAN, then Subject DN CN) — a parity-load-bearing field for the differential fixture 0021.
3. **Master-tip callback surface** exposes only `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` for TLS-aware state. The other 6 fields above (`RemoteAddr` / `LocalAddr` / `ServerName` / `PeerCertDER` / `Protocol` / `ListenerPrincipal`) have NO accessor — the only path to reach them is `*tls.Conn.ConnectionState()` (downstream connection state) plus the listener's `*stdtls.Config.Certificates[0]` (server cert side) — neither is reachable from inside a per-stream `DecoderFilterCallbacks` callback method.
4. **SPEC §6.5 step 5 + §6.6** specify "extracted from connection state at `DecodeHeaders` time when the per-stream `dcb` is in scope" — but that requirement is unsatisfiable without callback extension because `dcb` exposes NO method that reaches connection-level state beyond the existing `DownstreamPrincipal()`.

The two horns of the dilemma at PLAN time:

- **Horn A: respect SPEC §13.5 hard constraint** → leave the callback surface untouched → the `AttributeContext` populated set is UNSATISFIABLE for `tls_session.sni`, `source.certificate`, `destination.principal`, socket addresses, `request.http.protocol` → SPEC §15 acceptance item 4 fails and the differential fixture diverges vs reference Envoy v1.37.2 — a behaviorally significant divergence.
- **Horn B: extend the callback surface** → 6 new methods on `DecoderFilterCallbacks` → the SPEC §13.5 + §6.5 step 5 + §6.6 hard constraints are flipped → SPEC §15 item 4 satisfied + fixture 0021 differential clean.

The planner-time D3 decision settled on Horn B at PLAN time (D3 + D12 in the planner-time decision ledger of `PLAN.md`). The PLAN's File-structure table anticipated this exact outcome and File-ledger budget for `callbacks.go` (+60–100 LoC) + `chain.go` (+100–150 LoC) + HCM dispatch sites (+30–80 LoC). **The ADR-0044 escape-valve fires at Task 4** — this ADR is authored from scratch at IMPL time per ADR-0044's "impl-time-unanticipated" branch (no pre-SPEC-time §Context draft; the SPEC §13.5 hard constraint was the wrong call at SPEC time, falsified by the PLAN-time verification of SPEC §15 item 4 + §11.P4).

**Cross-phase reuse**: the 6 callback methods are NOT ext_authz-specific — ext_proc (phase ~19+) needs the same per-stream socket + TLS + listener-cert state for its `ProcessingRequest.attributes` envelope; global_ratelimit (phase TBD) needs the same for descriptor matching; future ext_authz extensions (CheckResponse-driven downstream-header-augmentation) need the same. Anchoring the 6 methods as a CROSS-PHASE-REUSABLE framework primitive ensures the seed-at-HCM-dispatch plumbing is paid for ONCE at phase-18.2 and reused thereafter (the ADR-0144 precedent for `DownstreamPrincipal()`: paid for ONCE at phase-16; consumed by phase-18.1 ext_authz HTTP mode + this phase 18.2's gRPC mode + future filters).

### Decision

**Six new methods land on `DecoderFilterCallbacks`** in `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`, alongside the existing `DownstreamPrincipal() []string` accessor:

1. `DownstreamRemoteAddr() net.Addr` — the downstream conn's `RemoteAddr()`; nil for synthetic streams.
2. `DownstreamLocalAddr() net.Addr` — the downstream conn's `LocalAddr()`; nil for synthetic streams.
3. `DownstreamTLSServerName() string` — `tls.ConnectionState.ServerName` (SNI); empty for plaintext / SNI-absent.
4. `DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER() []byte` — `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].Raw`; nil for plaintext / no-client-cert.
5. `DownstreamProtocol() string` — canonical short string `"HTTP/1.1"` (H1 dispatch) or `"HTTP/2"` (H2 dispatch); empty for synthetic streams.
6. `ListenerPrincipal() string` — listener's TLS server-cert principal (URI SAN[0] → DNS SAN[0] → Subject CN of `*stdtls.Config.Certificates[0]`); empty for plaintext listeners.

**The seeding pattern mirrors ADR-0144 / `tlsPrincipals` plumbing** (chain.go:107 + 551 + 483 anchor references):

- **6 new chain fields** on `FilterChain` (`downstreamRemoteAddr` / `downstreamLocalAddr` / `downstreamTLSServerName` / `downstreamTLSPeerCertDER` / `downstreamProtocol` / `listenerPrincipal`). All 6 obey the same ownership invariant ADR-0071 codifies for `tlsPrincipals`: SET ONCE at chain build time by HCM dispatch BEFORE `RunDecodeHeaders` dispatch; READ concurrently by per-stream callbacks (single-dispatch-goroutine read invariant).
- **6 new chain seeding primitives** (`SetDownstreamRemoteAddr` / `SetDownstreamLocalAddr` / `SetDownstreamTLSServerName` / `SetDownstreamTLSPeerCertDER` / `SetDownstreamProtocol` / `SetListenerPrincipal`). HCM dispatch elides the SetX call when the source value is the natural zero (e.g. plaintext listener → no `SetListenerPrincipal` call; the chain field stays "").
- **6 new `*decoderCB` reader methods** returning the chain field verbatim — no copy, no transformation.

**HCM dispatch sites**:

- **H1 (`connection.go:dispatchRequest`)**: after the existing `chain.SetTLSPrincipals(downstreamTLSPrincipals(downstream))` call, the 6 seeders fire. `RemoteAddr`/`LocalAddr` come from `downstream.RemoteAddr()`/`downstream.LocalAddr()`. `TLSServerName`/`TLSPeerCertDER` come from the downstream `*tls.Conn.ConnectionState()` when the conn is `*stdtls.Conn` AND the cert chain is non-empty. `Protocol` is the H1 canonical `"HTTP/1.1"`. `ListenerPrincipal` is `f.listenerPrincipal` (the pre-extracted per-Filter listener value — see listener plumbing below). Nil-downstream guard: dispatch-unit-test code paths pass `downstream=nil`; the chain fields stay zero per the documented zero-value semantics.
- **H2 (`h2dispatch.go`)**: the per-connection `h2Dispatcher` captures `RemoteAddr` / `LocalAddr` / `TLSServerName` / `TLSPeerCertDER` ONCE at `runH2` connection-build time (symmetric to `tlsPrincipals`; per-conn caching since H2 multiplexes many streams over one conn and the conn-level state is invariant for the connection lifetime). The 4 captures thread through `chainDispatchAction` fields into per-stream `chain.SetX` calls in `WriteH2`. `Protocol` is the H2 canonical `"HTTP/2"` (invariant — not captured per-conn). `ListenerPrincipal` is `c.f.listenerPrincipal` (per-Filter value).

**Listener plumbing for `ListenerPrincipal`** (the Step-0 pre-spike Outcome B path):

- `extractListenerPrincipal(*stdtls.Config) string` is added to `internal/listener/manager.go`: parses `Certificates[0].Leaf` (or `x509.ParseCertificate(Certificates[0].Certificate[0])` when `Leaf` is nil); returns the first URI SAN, then the first DNS SAN, then the Subject CN; empty string for nil cfg / empty cert chain / parse failure / cert with no matching identity.
- `listenerCtx` (manager-local) gains a `listenerPrincipal string` field, populated at chain-build time via `extractListenerPrincipal(chainTLS)` for each `filter_chain` (and `dfcTLS` for `default_filter_chain`).
- `hcm.ListenerCtx` (the public bridge type) gains a `ListenerPrincipal string` field. The HCM filter constructor reads it and stores it on the `*hcm.Filter.listenerPrincipal` field. HCM dispatch (H1 + H2) seeds it onto every per-stream chain via `chain.SetListenerPrincipal(f.listenerPrincipal)`.

**Group 13 unit tests** in `chain_test.go` cover the 6 round-trip seed-and-read paths (one test per new method asserting `Set(seed) → cb.Get() == seed`) plus 6 nil/empty fall-through tests (no `Set` call → accessor returns zero value). Mirrors the `TestDecoderCB_DownstreamPrincipal_SeededViaSetTLSPrincipals_ReturnsSeed` template at `chain_test.go:1507`.

**SPEC AMENDMENTS land at the same commit** per the planner-time D3 settle (so the SPEC's internal consistency is preserved):

- **SPEC §13.5** — original "NO new method on `envoyhttp.DecoderFilterCallbacks` lands at 18.2" quoted-block preserved + AMENDMENT paragraph flipping the constraint with citation of this ADR + D3.
- **SPEC §6.5 step 5** — original "NO new `DecoderFilterCallbacks` primitive" wording quoted-block preserved + AMENDMENT paragraph.
- **SPEC §6.6** — original "pure function of `*authRequest` + the four config booleans; NO `DecoderFilterCallbacks` parameter" quoted-block preserved + AMENDMENT paragraph clarifying that `buildAttributeContext` ITSELF remains a pure function of `*authRequest` + the 4 booleans (the callbacks are NOT passed in directly); the per-stream state is captured into `*authRequest` AT DecodeHeaders time via the new callbacks.

### Consequences

- **Cross-phase reuse**: the 6 callback methods + their chain plumbing are immediately available to phase-18.2 ext_authz gRPC mode's `dispatchOutboundCheck` (Task 8 wires the per-stream `*authRequest` extension from the new accessors). Future filters that need per-stream socket / TLS / listener-cert state — ext_proc (phase ~19+), global_ratelimit (phase TBD), future ext_authz extensions — consume the same accessor surface without re-paying the plumbing cost. Mirrors the ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` precedent: paid for ONCE at phase-16; reused at phase-18.1 + 18.2 + future.
- **SPEC §13.5 + §6.5 step 5 + §6.6 hard constraints are AMENDED in-place** at this same commit (the SPEC sections retain the original wording in a quoted-block + a follow-on AMENDMENT paragraph citing this ADR — the grep-archaeology pattern used by ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT at phase-18.2 Task 3). The original SPEC author's claim that the existing callback surface suffices was falsified by the PLAN-time verification against the SPEC's own §15 item 4 + §11.P4 requirements; the AMENDMENT records the post-PLAN-time settle.
- **The 18.2 SPEC §15 item 4 populated-set is now achievable** — `tls_session.sni`, `source.certificate`, source + destination socket addresses, `destination.principal`, `request.http.protocol` ALL satisfy the populated-set requirement from the per-stream `*authRequest` (Task 5/8). The differential fixture 0021 can assert byte-equivalent `AttributeContext` shape vs reference Envoy v1.37.2.
- **ADR-0071 chain-ownership invariant continues to apply** — the 6 new fields use the same SET-once-by-HCM-dispatch + READ-by-callback discipline as `tlsPrincipals`; no new race surface introduced. Race-detector verification at Task 4 green across `./internal/filter/http/... ./internal/filter/hcm/...`.
- **Listener plumbing extension** (Outcome B per Task 4 Step 0 pre-spike): the PLAN's File-structure table for `connection.go` budgeted +30–80 LoC for the listener-principal sourcing path. Outcome B fires — `listener/manager.go` + `hcm/config.go` + `hcm/filter.go` gain net ~+30 LoC each to plumb `listenerPrincipal` through `listenerCtx` → `hcm.ListenerCtx` → `*hcm.Filter.listenerPrincipal` → `chain.SetListenerPrincipal`. The alternative (lift `*stdtls.Config` through the dispatch chain so HCM can extract per-request) is more invasive and has worse cache locality; the pre-extracted string is the cheaper anchor.
- **Future filter authors get a stable accessor surface** — no need to grep for `*tls.Conn` or similar across the codebase; the framework primitive is documented + tested + race-clean. The seeding contract (set ONCE at HCM dispatch BEFORE RunDecodeHeaders) is explicit in the doc comments on both the chain seeders and the callback accessors.
- **No new fuzzer surface** — the 6 accessors return chain-state values verbatim; there is no parsing / validation logic to fuzz.

Cross-references:

- **ADR-0044** — the ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve discipline this ADR's §Context invokes. The escape-valve fires per planner-time D12.
- **ADR-0071** — the chain-ownership invariant the 6 new fields obey (SET-once + READ-by-callback discipline; single-dispatch-goroutine read invariant).
- **ADR-0144** — the prior framework primitive (`DownstreamPrincipal()` at phase-16) this ADR generalizes; same seed-at-HCM-dispatch + read-via-callback pattern + same cross-phase-reuse intent.
- **ADR-0157** §Decision (AMENDED at phase-18.2 Task 3) + ADR-0160 (gRPC-mode portion at Task 5) + ADR-0161 (gRPC-mode portion at Task 6) — the phase-18.2 ADRs that consume this ADR's framework primitive through the extended `*authRequest`.
- **ADR-0164** — the phase-18 ADR-0045 split-application ADR (predecessor); this ADR (ADR-0165) is the next-free ADR per ADR-0164's "next-free ADR after phase 18 is ADR-0165" anticipation.

## ADR-0166: Permit plaintext h2c upstream clusters — relax `extractH2Mode` TLS-required gate

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Lands-in:** Task 11 fixup of phase-18.2 IMPL (post-Task-11 cluster-manager-gate-relaxation)

### Context

Phase 05.2's SPEC §5.5 prescribed "TLS required for h2" for any upstream cluster with `http2_protocol_options:{}`. The decision was inherited from master SPEC §5.8 (the bootstrap-era H2 design) without alternatives-considered analysis; no ADR explicitly anchors it.

Phase 18.2's `c_authz_grpc` cluster (fixture-0021's gRPC auth cluster) is plaintext h2c per:
- SPEC §7.2 (fixture-0021 topology: "plaintext h2c for the auth cluster")
- Planner-time decision D13 ("Fixture 0021 IS plaintext-only — NO PKI, NO TLS-to-auth fixture coverage")
- The §11.P13 in-session SPEC scrape that RATIFIED plaintext h2c against reference Envoy v1.37.2

Reference Envoy v1.37.2 accepts plaintext h2c upstream clusters; the gRPC ecosystem norm is plaintext h2c upstream (service-mesh sidecars commonly terminate mTLS at the sidecar and proxy h2c onward). The envoy-go cluster-manager gate is therefore over-restrictive relative to both reference behavior and the project's own §11.P13 evidence.

### Decision

`extractH2Mode` (`internal/cluster/manager.go`) is RELAXED to permit plaintext h2c upstream clusters:

- If a cluster has `http2_protocol_options:{}` AND `transport_socket` is absent → **PERMITTED** as plaintext h2c (h2c prior-knowledge per RFC 7540 §3.4). `useH2 = true`, `parsedTLS = nil`.
- If a cluster has `http2_protocol_options:{}` AND `transport_socket` is present → existing validation preserved bit-identical (must be `UpstreamTlsContext`; ALPN must include "h2"; otherwise rejected).
- If a cluster has NO `http2_protocol_options:{}` → existing H1-fallback path preserved.

`dial_h2.go` is updated to skip the TLS-conn assertion when `parsedTLS == nil`; the raw `net.Conn` is handed to `h2.NewClientConn` for h2c prior-knowledge.

### Consequences

- **Reference-Envoy parity:** envoy-go now accepts the same cluster shapes that reference Envoy v1.37.2 accepts.
- **gRPC ecosystem alignment:** plaintext h2c upstream is the norm for service-mesh sidecars + the default for `grpcurl --plaintext`.
- **Phase 18.2 fixture-0021 unblocked:** the `c_authz_grpc` plaintext-h2c cluster validates clean; Task 12 can proceed.
- **05.2 §5.5 amended-by-precedent:** the original "TLS required for h2" rationale is superseded; future work may amend SPEC §5.5 in-place to record the relaxation.
- **No regression to TLS+h2 path:** the existing transport_socket-present validation branch is preserved bit-identical; all existing 05.2 tests stay green.
- **No regression to ALPN-h2 enforcement:** when TLS IS configured, ALPN MUST select "h2" — same as before.
- **Cross-phase reuse:** ext_proc (phase ~19+) + global_ratelimit (phase TBD) + any future gRPC-upstream filters inherit the relaxation; they can configure plaintext-h2c upstream gRPC clusters without further code change.
- **Cited:** ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl escape-valve — second 18.2 impl-time ADR after ADR-0165); ADR-0055 (existing flow-control discipline); ADR-0056 (existing per-request dial). No ADRs need amendment.

### References

- `internal/cluster/manager.go:extractH2Mode` (the gate)
- `internal/cluster/dial_h2.go` (the runtime dial)
- `docs/envoy-go/phases/05.2-upstream-h2/SPEC.md` §5.5 (the inherited rule — superseded by this ADR)
- `docs/envoy-go/phases/18.2-ext-authz-grpc/SPEC.md` §7.2 + §11.P13 (the load-bearing fixture-0021 requirement)
- `docs/envoy-go/phases/18.2-ext-authz-grpc/PLAN.md` D13 (the planner-time settlement)
- RFC 7540 §3.4 (HTTP/2 prior-knowledge)

## ADR-0167: `internal/filter/http/extproc/` package shape — single-token directory + BOTH-DECODE-AND-ENCODE `HTTPFilter` value + 9-counter `filterStats` + boot-registration alphabetical between `extauthz` and `fault` + multi-stage `SendLocalReply` mechanism (FIRST §9 row whose deny-path can fire at request_headers / request_body / response_headers / response_body) + the TWELFTH §9 row + FIRST-cross-phase-consumer-of-ADR-0158/ADR-0165/ADR-0166 framing + the bidi-stream-framework-lift framing

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
**Lands-in:** Task 2 of phase-19.1 PLAN (factory + filterStats + boot-registration; §Decision + §Consequences land at IMPL).

### Context

Phase 19 lands `envoy.filters.http.ext_proc` (the canonical Envoy v1.37.2 external-processor filter) as the TWELFTH production HTTP filter in envoy-go after cors / fault / header_mutation / local_ratelimit / csrf / buffer / compressor / bandwidth_limit / rbac / jwt_authn / ext_authz. The package shape mirrors phase-18.1+18.2 ext_authz's multi-file split (per parent SPEC §6.9 + phase-18.1 SPEC §6.5): `extproc.go` (filter type + factory + decode AND encode methods + `filterStats` + `compiledConfig` + per-route helper); `check.go` (per-stage dispatcher + builders + `applyProcessingResponse` + mutation/immediate-response application); `attributes.go` (`request_attributes` + `response_attributes` allowlist-driven envelope builder); `processor.go` (state-machine model); `json.go` (filter-local `protojson` codec); `extproc_test.go`; `fuzz_test.go` (24th fuzzer `FuzzExtProcConfigParse`); `doc.go`. The package directory + Go identifier are `extproc` (single token underscore-stripped per ADR-0114; matches `localratelimit/` + `jwtauthn/` + `extauthz/`). The package exposes `TypeURL` + `New` (the `HTTPFilterFactory`).

**Phase 19 is the FIRST §9 family-row to ship BOTH `StreamDecoderFilter` AND `StreamEncoderFilter` participation in a single filter package.** Phase-14 compressor's encode-only shape (`Decoder: nil`) is the only prior precedent for encode-side participation; phase-19 spans both. Decoder-side handles request_headers (+ request_body at 19.2); encoder-side handles response_headers (+ response_body at 19.2). Static blank-identifier compile-time checks for BOTH interfaces.

**Phase 19 is the FIRST §9 row whose deny-path can fire at multiple stages** — request_headers + request_body + response_headers + response_body (body-stage variants at 19.2). The framework's `SendLocalReply` primitive per ADR-0085 supports multi-stage emission (the existing decoder + encoder callback surfaces both expose it); ext_proc emits from the encoder side at the response_headers stage when `ImmediateResponse` arrives — a FIRST in envoy-go (prior §9 rows all emit `SendLocalReply` from decode-side only).

**9-counter `filterStats` per parent §5.P4 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME** — registered unconditionally at `New()` time (the IMPL fixture-harness empirical scrape closes the exact roster at 19.1 Task N per phase-16 §10 lesson (c) + phase-18.2 §11.P4 precedent). The 9 hypothesized counters: `streams_started`, `stream_msgs_sent`, `stream_msgs_received`, `spurious_msgs_received`, `streams_failed`, `streams_closed`, `failure_mode_allowed`, `override_message_timeout_received`, `override_message_timeout_ignored` — all under `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.*`; SHARED with per-route per ADR-0173.

**Boot-registration alphabetical** per ADR-0100 §2.2: `extproc` inserts between `extauthz` and `fault` in `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` (the 15th extension-registry entry after phase-18.2 — the current 14 entries: `router`, `bandwidthlimit`, `buffer`, `compressor`, `cors`, `csrf`, `envoygotest`, `extauthz`, `fault`, `header_mutation`, `jwtauthn`, `localratelimit`, `rbac` + the in-flight 14th `extauthz` insertion that closed phase-18 are the order at master tip `5927b55`).

**Phase 19 is the FIRST cross-phase consumer of ADR-0158 / ADR-0165 / ADR-0166** outside phase-18.2 itself — the load-bearing reusability demonstration of the gRPC-client primitive + the 6 new decoder-callback accessors + the cluster-manager plaintext h2c upstream relaxation. Phase 19 EXTENDS ADR-0158 with the `*ProcessorClient` bidi-stream wrapper (ADR-0169) — same package (`internal/grpcclient/`), same `*Dialer` integration; NO `Dialer` API changes. The framework story for phase 19 is dominated by REUSE rather than NEW (FIVE load-bearing reuses + ONE NEW primitive extending an existing family + ONE NEW filter-local codec + TWO encode-side framework deltas per ADR-0174 + ADR-0175).

References: parent SPEC §1 + §4.1 + §5.P2 + §5.P4 + §5.P11 + §5.P12 + §6 amendments 4 + 11 + 12. ADR-0156 (phase-18.1 package shape precedent). ADR-0072 (extension-registry boot registration). ADR-0085 (`SendLocalReply` framework primitive). ADR-0114 (single-token directory discipline).

### Decision

**(i) Package directory + Go-package identifier — single-token `extproc`.** The package directory is `internal/filter/http/extproc/`; the Go-package identifier is `extproc`. Single-token underscore-stripped per ADR-0114; matches the in-tree precedents `localratelimit/`, `jwtauthn/`, `extauthz/`. Public API per SPEC §6.1: `TypeURL` (the canonical Envoy type-URL constant) + `New` (the `HTTPFilterFactory` registered at boot per ADR-0072). The multi-file split per phase-18.1+18.2 precedent: `doc.go` (~50 LoC, package overview), `extproc.go` (filter type + factory + decode AND encode methods + `filterStats` + `compiledConfig` + per-route helper), `check.go` (per-stage dispatcher + builders + `applyProcessingResponse` + mutation/immediate-response application), `attributes.go` (`request_attributes`/`response_attributes` envelope builder), `processor.go` (state-machine model), `json.go` (filter-local protojson codec for http_service mode), `extproc_test.go` (unit tests), `fuzz_test.go` (the 24th fuzzer `FuzzExtProcConfigParse`).

**(ii) BOTH-DECODE-AND-ENCODE `HTTPFilter` shape — first §9 row to ship both.** The factory closure returns an `envoyhttp.HTTPFilter` value with `Decoder: f` AND `Encoder: f` (SAME `*filter` instance servicing both sides), mirroring phase-14 compressor's both-sides shape per ADR-0129 §Decision (iv). DISTINCT from compressor: ext_proc's BOTH sides are STRUCTURALLY active in 19.1 — decoder for request_headers stage (fires the processor call); encoder for response_headers stage (fires a second processor call on the same bidi-stream in gRPC mode, or a fresh POST in HTTP mode). Compile-time invariants per SPEC §6.10: `var _ envoyhttp.StreamDecoderFilter = (*filter)(nil)` + `var _ envoyhttp.StreamEncoderFilter = (*filter)(nil)`. The factory return signature is `(envoyhttp.FilterInstanceFactory, error)` per ADR-0071's two-step factory pattern (the SPEC §6.1 sketch's `(envoyhttp.HTTPFilter, error)` is the per-stream factory's RETURN, not the boot-factory's; the boot-factory returns the per-stream factory closure).

**(iii) 9-counter `filterStats` registered unconditionally at New() time.** Per parent §5.P4 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME. The 9 hypothesized counters: `streams_started`, `stream_msgs_sent`, `stream_msgs_received`, `spurious_msgs_received`, `streams_failed`, `streams_closed`, `failure_mode_allowed`, `override_message_timeout_received`, `override_message_timeout_ignored` — all under `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.*` per SN2-reuse. ALL 9 registered at `New()` time even when the listener-level config never fires the corresponding code path (mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0163 STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE-counter discipline for scrape stability per Prometheus best practice). SHARED with per-route per ADR-0173 (the per-route override adjusts `processing_mode`/`grpc_service` but still hits the same external processor — it spawns no new stateful policy-evaluation surface; mirrors phase-12/13/14/17/18 SHARED-stats; DIVERGES from phase-11/15/16 INDEPENDENT-stats). Allocation guarded `if ctx.Stats != nil` at `buildCompiledConfig` per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance (Task 11 wiring). RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME closure at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape per phase-16 §10 lesson (c) + phase-18.2 §11.P4 precedent.

**(iv) Boot-registration alphabetical between `extauthz` and `fault`.** Per ADR-0100 §2.2: registration order does NOT affect runtime behavior; stylistic discipline only. The `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot-registration block inserts `httpReg.Register(extproc.TypeURL, extproc.New)` at line 130 (between `extauthz` at line 129 and `fault` at line 131). The 15th extension-registry entry — bringing the total to: `router`, `bandwidthlimit`, `buffer`, `compressor`, `cors`, `csrf`, `envoygotest`, `extauthz`, **extproc**, `fault`, `header_mutation`, `jwtauthn`, `localratelimit`, `rbac` (14 filters) + the `router` terminal per phase-07.1 ADR-0072. The header_mutation per-route validator + `Freeze()` invocation remain UNCHANGED in their relative position.

**(v) Multi-stage `SendLocalReply` mechanism — FIRST §9 row whose deny-path can fire at multiple stages.** Per SPEC §4 + ADR-0167's package framing. The framework's `SendLocalReply` per ADR-0085 supports emission from BOTH decode-side (request_headers stage `ImmediateResponse` → `f.dcb.SendLocalReply(status, body, headers)`) AND encode-side (response_headers stage `ImmediateResponse` → `f.ecb.SendLocalReply(status, body, headers)` — a 19.1 FIRST per parent §5.P2 + §6 amendment 2). The framework's `SendLocalReply` enters the encode chain at filter[len-1] per ADR-0075, which means the immediate-response emission supersedes any in-flight encode-chain participation. 19.1 lands the header-stage variants; 19.2 extends with the body-stage variants (request_body + response_body). NO new framework primitive — the existing `SendLocalReply` covers all four eventual stages.

**(vi) The TWELFTH §9 row framing.** ext_proc is the TWELFTH production HTTP filter in envoy-go after cors / fault / header_mutation / local_ratelimit / csrf / buffer / compressor / bandwidth_limit / rbac / jwt_authn / ext_authz. The §9 row classification matters for the cross-phase reuse story: phase 19 demonstrates that the 11-filter accumulated framework story (extension-registry per ADR-0072, 8 canonical per-route patterns per ADR-0125, stat-namespace SN2 per ADR-0061, SendLocalReply per ADR-0085, async-resume per phase-09, decoder-callback 6 accessors per ADR-0165, gRPC-client primitive per ADR-0158, plaintext h2c upstream per ADR-0166, cluster-manager threading per ADR-0144 + ADR-0158) supports a BOTH-sides + bidi-stream + dual-mode-transport filter without ANY framework surgery (only the encoder-callback symmetric extension per ADR-0174, which is a clean addition not a refactor).

**(vii) FIRST-cross-phase-consumer-of-ADR-0158/ADR-0165/ADR-0166 framing.** Phase 19 is the load-bearing reusability demonstration of THREE phase-18.2 primitives:
- **ADR-0158 `internal/grpcclient/Dialer`** — REUSED via `NewProcessorClient(*Dialer, ...)` (ADR-0169 EXTENDS the package with the bidi-stream wrapper alongside the existing unary `*AuthClient`; NO `Dialer` API changes per ADR-0158 §Consequences "no future client coupling is anticipated to require `Dialer` API changes").
- **ADR-0165 6 new `DecoderFilterCallbacks` methods** — REUSED for `request_attributes` envelope population at the request_headers stage (Task 9).
- **ADR-0166 cluster-manager plaintext h2c upstream relaxation** — REUSED for the fixture-0022 `c_ext_proc` test cluster (Task 13 plaintext h2c upstream).

**(viii) Bidi-stream-framework-lift framing.** Phase 19 is the FIRST §9 row to consume a bidi-streaming gRPC RPC (`ExternalProcessor.Process`) as opposed to the unary RPC (`Authorization.Check`) phase-18.2 established. The lift is structurally minimal: ADR-0169's `*ProcessorClient` wraps `extprocv3.NewExternalProcessorClient(conn).Process(ctx)` and exposes `ProcessStream.{Send/Recv/CloseSend}` per the inherited `grpc.ClientStream` interface. The per-stage send/recv discipline (one goroutine per stage performing both Send and Recv sequentially — per D9 "the gRPC library documents concurrent Send/Recv on a single ClientStream are safe; the IMPL keeps ONE goroutine alive per stage") means NO per-stream mutex on Send/Recv is needed.

### Consequences

**(a) Cross-phase reuse intent for ADR-0167 — the package-layout reference for ALL future §9 rows that span decode + encode.** Future §9 rows participating on both sides (any response-mutating filter that needs request-side state, e.g. a hypothetical future `oauth2`, `tap`, or `wasm_response_processor`) REUSE the ADR-0167 package shape — single-token directory, BOTH-sides factory, compile-time `var _` assertions for both interfaces, 9-counter (or appropriate-arity) `filterStats` registered unconditionally, boot-registration alphabetical. The phase-19 IMPL ships the reference at extproc.

**(b) 9-counter STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE-counter discipline (mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0163).** Some of the 9 counters are STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE under specific listener configurations: e.g., `override_message_timeout_received` is structurally unreachable when `max_message_timeout=0` (the default — override-disabled per ADR-0171); `override_message_timeout_ignored` is structurally unreachable when the processor never sends `override_message_timeout` ProcessingResponses. All 9 counters are nevertheless registered unconditionally for scrape stability (operators get a consistent counter surface across listeners with different configurations). The discipline strengthens the phase-18.2 ADR-0163 first appearance (the `disabled` counter STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE under MVP per the silent-ignore-`filter_enabled` posture). The 19.1 IMPL closes the structurally-unreachable classification at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape per phase-16 §10 lesson (c).

**(c) Boot-registration alphabetical convention reaffirmation.** ADR-0100 §2.2 codifies the alphabetical-by-import-name convention; phase 19 reaffirms it by inserting `extproc` between `extauthz` and `fault` (the natural alphabetical position). Future §9 rows continue the pattern; deviations require an ADR-0100 amendment (none anticipated for the foreseeable §9 family-row pipeline). The cross-phase consistency makes the boot-registration block grep-stable + diff-friendly.

**(d) Forward-pointer to ADR-0174 (Task 5) + ADR-0175 (19.2).** The encode-side framework deltas to support the §Decision (ii) BOTH-sides shape land at Task 5 (ADR-0174 — symmetric `EncoderFilterCallbacks` extension; 6 methods mirroring ADR-0165's decode-side accessors). ADR-0175 (19.2 — encode-side body-buffering primitive) follows the same pattern for body-stage activation. The phase-19 framework story is: ADR-0167 codifies the shape; ADR-0174 fills the decode/encode-symmetry gap; ADR-0175 fills the body-buffering symmetry gap.

**(e) The bidi-stream lifecycle anchored at ADR-0167 + delegated to ADR-0169 + ADR-0171.** ADR-0167 establishes that ext_proc's filter shape owns the bidi-stream lifecycle (`OnDestroy` cancels the stream's context; `CloseSend` signals end-of-stream); the wrapper implementation (`*ProcessorClient.Process`) lives at ADR-0169; the per-stage state-machine + override_message_timeout discipline lives at ADR-0171. The triplet (ADR-0167 + ADR-0169 + ADR-0171) covers the bidi-stream story end-to-end.

References: parent SPEC §1 + §3 + §4.1 + §5.P2 + §5.P4 + §5.P11 + §5.P12 + §6 amendments 4 + 11 + 12. 19.1 SPEC §6.1 + §6.10 + §6.9. ADR-0156 (phase-18.1 package shape precedent — the 4-file/5-file split). ADR-0163 (phase-18.2 STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE-counter precedent). ADR-0072 (extension-registry boot registration). ADR-0085 (`SendLocalReply` framework primitive). ADR-0100 §2.2 (boot-registration alphabetical convention). ADR-0114 (single-token directory discipline). ADR-0129 §Decision (iv) (compressor BOTH-sides factory precedent). ADR-0144 (DownstreamPrincipal extraction). ADR-0158 (`internal/grpcclient/Dialer`). ADR-0165 (decoder-callback 6 accessors). ADR-0166 (cluster-manager plaintext h2c upstream).

## ADR-0168: `compiledConfig` shape + the `grpc_service`-vs-`http_service` mutually-exclusive top-level field dispatch (NOT a proto oneof) + http_service proto-constraint (PARSE-REJECT body/trailer modes when http_service is set) + consumed-vs-deferred field discipline + the error-posture fields + 19.1 body-mode PARSE-REJECT (§Decision AMENDMENT at 19.2 to lift) + the STREAMED-only flag PARSE-REJECT

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention; §Decision lands at 19.1 IMPL; §Decision AMENDMENT at 19.2 IMPL Task 3 to lift the body-mode PARSE-REJECT for gRPC-service-mode BUFFERED arms — http_service-mode body PARSE-REJECT continues permanently; §Consequences refresh at 19.2 IMPL Task 7 covering body-stage integration completeness + the decode-side body-mutation-delivery KNOWN LIMITATION + the `compiledConfig` field-final invariant preservation + the D10-hypothesis HOLDS disposition).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row (§Decision); phase 19.2 §Decision AMENDMENT + §Consequences refresh. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
**Lands-in:** Task 2 of phase-19.1 PLAN (`compiledConfig` shape + `buildCompiledConfig`); §Decision amended at phase-19.2 IMPL Task 3 (body-mode PARSE-REJECT lift); §Consequences refreshed at phase-19.2 IMPL Task 7 (body-stage integration completeness).

### Context

The `ExternalProcessor` proto has 22 top-level fields per parent SPEC §5.P1 (cross-checked against `go-control-plane v1.32.4`'s `ext_proc.pb.go`). The transport-dispatch surface is **two top-level optional fields** (`grpc_service` #1 + `http_service` #20) with operator-side mutual-exclusion — NOT a proto `oneof` (distinct from phase-18 ext_authz which IS a `services` oneof). The factory enforces mutual-exclusion at parse time: both-set OR neither-set → PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict (mirrors the phase-18.1 ext_authz empty-services-oneof discipline + extends to a both-set check).

**19.1 MVP envelope** consumes 17 of 22 `ExternalProcessor` fields (per parent SPEC §5.P1 + 19.1 SPEC §1 item 3):
- Transport: `grpc_service` (#1; with `core.GrpcService.GoogleGrpc` PARSE-REJECT + `initial_metadata`/`retry_policy` SILENT-IGNORE — inherited from ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT) + `http_service` (#20 → `ExtProcHttpService.http_service: *core.v3.HttpService`).
- Processing: `processing_mode` (#3 — headers-modes consumed; body-modes PARSE-REJECT in 19.1 unless NONE; trailer-modes PARSE-REJECT unless SKIP).
- Attributes: `request_attributes` (#5) + `response_attributes` (#6).
- Error posture: `failure_mode_allow` (#2; default false) + `message_timeout` (#7; default 200ms; PGV `gte=0s, lte=1h0m0s`) + `max_message_timeout` (#10; default 0 = override disabled; PGV `gte=0s, lte=1h0m0s`) + `disable_immediate_response` (#15).
- Mode-override: `allow_mode_override` (#14) + `allowed_override_modes` (#22).
- Mutation discipline: `mutation_rules` (#9 → `*v31.HeaderMutationRules`).
- Header forwarding: `forward_rules` (#12 → `*HeaderForwardingRules{allowed_headers, disallowed_headers}`).
- Route cache: `route_cache_action` (#18) + `disable_clear_route_cache` (#11; mutually exclusive with #18 per parent §5.P5).
- Stat prefix: `stat_prefix` (#8).

**19.1 PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict** (per parent §5.P10 RATIFIED):
- `observability_mode` (#17) when true (STREAMED-only flag).
- `send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response` (#21) when true (STREAMED-only flag).
- `deferred_close_timeout` (#19) when non-zero (observability_mode-coupled).
- `core.GrpcService.GoogleGrpc` arm (envoy-go uses Go gRPC directly — inherited from ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT).
- Both-set OR neither-set transport (mutual-exclusion enforcement).
- `processing_mode.{request,response}_body_mode` != NONE (19.1 only; lifted at 19.2).
- `processing_mode.{request,response}_trailer_mode` != SKIP (permanently).
- `processing_mode.{request,response}_body_mode` ∈ {STREAMED, BUFFERED_PARTIAL, FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED} (permanently out of envelope per Q2).
- `http_service` + body-mode != NONE simultaneously (per the proto's `ExtProcHttpService.http_service` doc-comment: "if 'http_service' is set, the `processing_mode` can not be configured to send any body or trailers" — quoted at parent §5.P1).
- Both `disable_clear_route_cache` AND `route_cache_action` set (parent §5.P5 mutual-exclusion).

**19.1 SILENT-IGNORE** (per the inline-deferral discipline, deferred fields auditable in the ADR-0040 trail):
- `metadata_options` (#16 → `*MetadataOptions{forwarding_namespaces, receiving_namespaces}`) — dynamic-metadata family blocked at phases 16+17+18 forward-pointers.
- `filter_metadata` (#13 → `*structpb.Struct`) — dynamic-metadata family.
- `core.GrpcService.{initial_metadata, retry_policy}` — initial-metadata + gRPC retry families.

**Body-mode 19.1 PARSE-REJECT is lifted at 19.2** via §Decision AMENDMENT (`*compiledConfig` struct shape stays UNCHANGED — body-mode-specific config is captured in the closure scope inside `processFn`, NOT promoted to struct fields, mirroring phase-18.2 ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT's field-final discipline). The lift activates `request_body_mode = BUFFERED` (via ADR-0128 decode-side body-buffering reuse) and `response_body_mode = BUFFERED` (via the NEW ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive).

References: parent SPEC §4.1 + §4.2 + §5.P1 + §5.P10 + §6 amendment 10. 19.1 SPEC §1 item 3 + §6.5. ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT (the GoogleGrpc PARSE-REJECT + initial_metadata/retry_policy SILENT-IGNORE inheritance from phase-18.2).

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — §Decision drafted at Task 2 of phase-19.1 PLAN (anchored design intent + struct shape); the `buildCompiledConfig` integration that consumes this §Decision landed at Task 11; §Consequences appended at Task 11 per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.**

This §Decision was authored at Task 2 to anchor the design intent + the `compiledConfig` struct shape + the `grpc_service`/`http_service` dispatch sketch. The integration completeness — the `buildCompiledConfig` body that consumes this §Decision + emits the structurally-validated `*compiledConfig` per the dispatch tree below — landed at Task 11 alongside the §Consequences body. The multi-task ADR pattern follows the phase-18.1+18.2 ADR-0157 precedent (Task 2 §Decision draft anchors the struct shape; later tasks land the consumer body + §Consequences).

**(i) `grpc_service`-vs-`http_service` dispatch — operator-side mutual-exclusion, NOT a proto oneof.** Per parent §5.P1 RATIFIED. The `ExternalProcessor` proto carries TWO top-level optional fields — `grpc_service` (#1, `*core.v3.GrpcService`) and `http_service` (#20, `*ExtProcHttpService`) — with NO proto `oneof` constraint (distinct from phase-18.x ext_authz which IS a `services` oneof). `buildCompiledConfig` (Task 11) enforces mutual-exclusion envoy-go-strict at parse time:
- BOTH-set → PARSE-REJECT (`"ext_proc: exactly one of grpc_service or http_service must be set"`).
- NEITHER-set → PARSE-REJECT (same wording).
- EXACTLY-one-set → DISPATCH to the corresponding builder (`buildGRPCProcessorClient` for the gRPC arm; `buildHTTPProcessorClient` for the HTTP arm).

The mutual-exclusion check fires BEFORE the per-arm builder is invoked to give operators a deterministic parse-error ordering. Mirrors phase-18.1 ext_authz `services`-oneof presence check pattern (parse error before service-specific dispatch).

**(ii) `processorClient` interface — produced by both arms from config-load time.** The `compiledConfig` carries the mode-agnostic transport via mutually-exclusive fields (`grpcClient *grpcclient.ProcessorClient` for the gRPC arm; `httpClient *httpProcessorClient` for the HTTP arm); exactly one is non-nil per the dispatch above. The skeleton anchors a `processorClient` interface (Close()) at Task 2; the per-stage dispatcher at Task 7 (processor.go) + Task 8 (check.go) settles the exact mode-agnostic method set once both arms are wired through the dispatch tree. Both arms produce the client at config-load time (NOT lazily per-request) — the `*grpc.ClientConn` (gRPC arm) + the `*http.Client` (HTTP arm) are reused across all per-stream invocations. Per-stream cancellation happens via `context.WithCancel` per parent §5.P10 + ADR-0171 (NOT via the shared client).

**(iii) `http_service` proto-constraint — PARSE-REJECT body/trailer modes when http_service is set.** Per the proto's `ExtProcHttpService.http_service` doc-comment ("if 'http_service' is set, the `processing_mode` can not be configured to send any body or trailers" — quoted at parent §5.P1). `buildCompiledConfig` sets `cc.httpServiceHeadersOnly = true` when the http_service arm is taken at step (i); the processing_mode validator at step (iv) reads this flag and adds the body-mode-not-NONE PARSE-REJECT condition. The constraint fires permanently (NOT lifted at 19.2 — the 19.2 body-mode lift applies only to the gRPC arm; http_service stays headers-only forever).

**(iv) 19.1 body-mode PARSE-REJECT (§Decision AMENDED at 19.2 to lift).** Per parent §5.P9 RATIFIED. `buildCompiledConfig` PARSE-REJECTs `processing_mode.request_body_mode != NONE` AND `processing_mode.response_body_mode != NONE` at 19.1; the rejection wording is `"ext_proc: processing_mode.{request,response}_body_mode not yet supported (lands in phase 19.2)"`. At 19.2 IMPL the rejection lifts for the gRPC arm (body-mode-BUFFERED activated via ADR-0128 decode-side reuse + ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive); the http_service arm's body-mode PARSE-REJECT stays in place per (iii). The lift is a §Decision AMENDMENT (in-place edit per ADR-0044); NO new ADR number consumed.

The body-mode values `STREAMED`, `BUFFERED_PARTIAL`, `FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED` PARSE-REJECT permanently per Q2 (parent §5.P10 RATIFIED — these are STREAMED-class flags out of envelope; the 19.2 lift activates only `BUFFERED`). Wording: `"ext_proc: processing_mode.{request,response}_body_mode={STREAMED|BUFFERED_PARTIAL|FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED} not supported (STREAMED-class flag, out of envelope per parent §5.P10)"`.

**§Decision AMENDMENT (phase 19.2):** Body-mode arms (`request_body_mode = BUFFERED`, `response_body_mode = BUFFERED`) ACCEPT-AND-WIRE for `grpc_service` mode (lifts the 19.1 PARSE-REJECT). STREAMED + BUFFERED_PARTIAL + FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED continue PARSE-REJECT permanently per parent §4.4. HTTP-service-mode body PARSE-REJECT continues unchanged (HTTP-service is headers-only per the proto's `ExtProcHttpService` constraint). The `compiledConfig` struct field-final invariant per §Decision (xi) is PRESERVED — body-mode-specific runtime state lives in closure captures inside `processFn` per planner-time D2.

The amendment lands across two phase-19.2 IMPL tasks per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl multi-task pattern: **Task 3** lifts the PARSE-REJECT in `resolveProcessingMode` (the actual surface, called by `buildCompiledConfig` at the listener-level + per-route parse sites) — replaces the previous `errProcessingModeRequest{Request,Response}BodyNotNONE` sentinels (with wording "must be NONE in 19.1") with new sentinels `errProcessingModeRequest{Request,Response}BodyStreamedClass` (with wording "must be NONE or BUFFERED ... STREAMED + BUFFERED_PARTIAL + FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED permanently out of envelope per parent §4.4 + ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT"). The `httpServiceMode`-gated branch is now LOAD-BEARING (pre-AMENDMENT it was masked by the listener-level body-mode-NONE check firing first); fires BEFORE the gRPC-arm STREAMED-class check so the more specific PARSE-REJECT wording (the http_service constraint) wins. The `resolvedProcessingMode` struct fields `RequestBodyMode`/`ResponseBodyMode` now populate with the actual raw enum (NONE or BUFFERED) — pre-AMENDMENT the resolver hardcoded NONE since any non-NONE input PARSE-REJECTed at the gate. **Task 3 SKELETON SKETCH for body-stage dispatch:** `DecodeData` + `EncodeData` return `DataContinue` regardless of body-mode (BUFFERED loads without error but body bytes pass through verbatim); the full body-stage dispatch envelope lands at **Task 7** integration (wires Task 2 ADR-0175 primitive + Task 4 4-stage state machine + Task 5 attribute envelope builders + Task 6 body-mode arms of `applyProcessingResponse`). The Task 7 integration also lands the §Consequences refresh for this ADR (per PLAN D8: §Decision AMENDMENT at Task 3 + §Consequences refresh at Task 7, mirroring the 19.1 ADR-0168 §Decision multi-task pattern).

**(v) Trailer-mode PARSE-REJECT permanently.** Per parent §5.P9 RATIFIED. `buildCompiledConfig` PARSE-REJECTs `processing_mode.request_trailer_mode != SKIP` AND `processing_mode.response_trailer_mode != SKIP`; the rejection wording is `"ext_proc: processing_mode.{request,response}_trailer_mode must be SKIP (trailer-mode permanently out of envelope per parent §5.P9 RATIFIED)"`. NO 19.2 lift planned — trailers stay out of envelope unless a future scope expansion warrants the framework lift (would require its own ADR).

DEFAULT translation: `processing_mode.{request,response}_header_mode == DEFAULT` translates to SEND at parse time per parent §5.P9; `processing_mode.{request,response}_trailer_mode == DEFAULT` translates to SKIP (the trailer-mode DEFAULT IS the no-op disposition; mirrors the proto's intent).

**(vi) STREAMED-only flag PARSE-REJECT permanently.** Per parent §5.P10 RATIFIED. Three top-level flags PARSE-REJECT when set (the rejection wording cites each flag's `[#not-implemented-hide-from-non-streamed-mode]` proto annotation or equivalent):
- `observability_mode` (#17) when true → `"ext_proc: observability_mode not supported (STREAMED-only flag, out of envelope per parent §5.P10)"`.
- `send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response` (#21) when true → `"ext_proc: send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response not supported (STREAMED-only flag, out of envelope per parent §5.P10)"`.
- `deferred_close_timeout` (#19) when non-zero → `"ext_proc: deferred_close_timeout not supported (observability_mode-coupled STREAMED-only flag, out of envelope per parent §5.P10)"`.

These three PARSE-REJECTs fire AFTER the per-arm-builder dispatch at step (i) — the structural transport-check precedes the mode-flag checks (deterministic parse-error ordering per the phase-18.1 ext_authz precedent).

**(vii) Consumed-vs-deferred field discipline.** Per parent §5.P1 + §2.2 + §8 deferral table. The 17 MVP-consumed fields enumerated in the ADR-0168 §Context (Field 1 `grpc_service`, Field 2 `failure_mode_allow`, Field 3 `processing_mode`, Field 5 `request_attributes`, Field 6 `response_attributes`, Field 7 `message_timeout`, Field 8 `stat_prefix`, Field 9 `mutation_rules`, Field 10 `max_message_timeout`, Field 11 `disable_clear_route_cache`, Field 12 `forward_rules`, Field 14 `allow_mode_override`, Field 15 `disable_immediate_response`, Field 18 `route_cache_action`, Field 20 `http_service`, Field 22 `allowed_override_modes`) flow into the `compiledConfig` struct fields per the SPEC §6.2 sketch reproduced in `extproc.go`. The 3 PARSE-REJECT fields (Field 17, 19, 21) surface as parse-time errors per (vi). The 3 SILENT-IGNORED fields (Field 13 `filter_metadata`, Field 16 `metadata_options`, plus `core.GrpcService.{initial_metadata, retry_policy}`) flow through `buildCompiledConfig` untouched — NO compiledConfig fields allocated, NO runtime behavior triggered. The auditable trail lives at the inline-deferral comments in `extproc.go` + the §Context table above.

**(viii) Error-posture fields — `failure_mode_allow` / `message_timeout` / `max_message_timeout` / `disable_immediate_response`.** Per parent §5.P11 RATIFIED. `buildCompiledConfig` extracts the four error-posture fields with the following defaults:
- `failure_mode_allow` (Field 2): bool; default false (proto default). When true + error disposition → allow through + `failure_mode_allowed` + `streams_failed` BOTH increment per the SPEC §4 wire shape.
- `message_timeout` (Field 7): `*durationpb.Duration`; default 200ms when unset (per the proto's PGV constraint `gte=0s, lte=1h0m0s` + envoy-go-MVP default of 200ms; cited at the SPEC §6.5 `buildCompiledConfig` step 4). Pinned at 200ms because the proto field is OPTIONAL with a documented Envoy v1.37.2 default of 200ms; envoy-go honors the same default for cross-implementation parity. The IMPL converts to `time.Duration` via `durationpbToGoOrDefault(raw.GetMessageTimeout(), 200*time.Millisecond)`.
- `max_message_timeout` (Field 10): `*durationpb.Duration`; default 0 when unset (= override-disabled per parent §5.P10). PGV constraint `gte=0s, lte=1h0m0s`. The IMPL converts to `time.Duration` via `durationpbToGoOrDefault(raw.GetMaxMessageTimeout(), 0)`. When 0, `ProcessingResponse.override_message_timeout` is silently ignored (counter increment via `override_message_timeout_ignored`) — the override API is disabled at the listener level. When >= 1ms, `override_message_timeout` is honored within the range `[1ms, max_message_timeout]`.
- `disable_immediate_response` (Field 15): bool; default false (proto default). When true, ImmediateResponse arrivals from the processor are SILENT-DROPPED (treated as a protocol violation; `spurious_msgs_received` increments; stream continues without the local-reply emission per parent §5.P11).

**(ix) GoogleGrpc arm PARSE-REJECT inherited from ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT.** Per ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT (landed at phase-18.2 Task 3 commit `59ee8dd`). `buildGRPCProcessorClient` (Task 11; mirrors phase-18.2 `buildGRPCCheckFn`) PARSE-REJECTs `core.GrpcService.target_specifier` of type `GoogleGrpc` with the same wording inherited from ext_authz: `"ext_proc: grpc_service.google_grpc not supported (envoy-go uses Go gRPC directly via internal/grpcclient/Dialer per ADR-0158)"`. The EnvoyGrpc arm flows through the normal `*Dialer.DialContext(clusterName)` path per ADR-0158 + ADR-0169.

**(x) `initial_metadata` + `retry_policy` SILENT-IGNORED.** Per phase-18.2 inheritance + parent SPEC §8 inline-deferral discipline. `core.GrpcService.initial_metadata` (per-call metadata header injection) and `core.GrpcService.retry_policy` (gRPC retry families) flow through `buildCompiledConfig` untouched — NO compiledConfig fields allocated, NO runtime behavior. The inline-deferral comment lives at the `buildGRPCProcessorClient` body (Task 11). NO PARSE-REJECT (operators may have inherited their config from a reference Envoy bootstrap; silent-ignore preserves config portability).

**(xi) `route_cache_action` + `disable_clear_route_cache` mutual-exclusion.** Per parent §5.P5 RATIFIED. `buildCompiledConfig` enforces mutual-exclusion at parse time:
- BOTH set (`disable_clear_route_cache=true` AND `route_cache_action != DEFAULT`) → PARSE-REJECT (`"ext_proc: only one of route_cache_action or disable_clear_route_cache can be set"`).
- `disable_clear_route_cache=true` alone → `cc.routeCacheAction = RETAIN` (translation per the proto's deprecation note).
- `route_cache_action` alone → `cc.routeCacheAction = raw.GetRouteCacheAction()` (DEFAULT / RETAIN / CLEAR).
- NEITHER set → `cc.routeCacheAction = DEFAULT`.

The route_cache_action is consumed at the request_headers-stage CommonResponse application (Task 8) — `RETAIN` suppresses the `clear_route_cache:true` from the processor's response; `CLEAR` forces it. Per parent §5.P5: applies to the REQUEST direction only.

### Consequences

**Status: Accepted — landed at Task 11 of phase-19.1 PLAN per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.**

**The `buildCompiledConfig` 10-step pipeline is the operational sequence for the dual-mode envelope.** Per SPEC §6.5 + this ADR's §Decision (i)-(xi): the parser executes (1) mutual-exclusion on grpc_service vs http_service, (2) STREAMED-only flag PARSE-REJECT, (3) error-posture default expansion (failure_mode_allow / message_timeout 200ms / max_message_timeout 0 / disable_immediate_response), (4) route_cache_action vs disable_clear_route_cache mutual-exclusion + RETAIN translation, (5) per-arm transport builder dispatch via `buildGRPCProcessorClient` / `buildHTTPProcessorClient` (Task 8 helpers), (6) `resolveProcessingMode` validation per parent §5.P9 (body-mode != NONE in 19.1; trailer-mode != SKIP permanently; DEFAULT → SEND for headers; http_service + body-mode != NONE per the proto's `ExtProcHttpService` constraint), (7) `resolveMutationRules` (Task 8 helper) + forward_rules placeholder allocation, (8) allow_mode_override + allowed_override_modes per-entry validation through the same `resolveProcessingMode`, (9) request_attributes + response_attributes []string allowlist capture, (10) stat_prefix capture + filterStats allocation guarded `if ctx.Stats != nil` per ADR-0085. The pipeline ordering is deterministic — operators with malformed configs get a predictable parse-error wording for each axis (no axis-interleaving). The 10-step pipeline mirrors phase-18.1 ext_authz `buildCompiledConfig` shape with ext_proc-specific surface additions (mutation_rules + route_cache discipline + dual-mode dispatch).

**Closure-capture-vs-struct-field discipline (mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0157 §Decision).** The `compiledConfig` struct is FIELD-FINAL at 19.1 — every 19.1-consumed field has a struct member; every 19.1 PARSE-REJECT axis is a parse-time gate, not a runtime field. Future filter-specific behavior toggles (e.g., `include_peer_certificate`-style gates, `pack_as_bytes` flags, or other per-config behavior modifiers a future scope expansion might add) MUST ride in the closure scope inside the transport-helper builders (e.g., `buildGRPCProcessorClient`'s closure capturing additional bool gates) rather than promoting to `compiledConfig` struct fields. The pattern: when a future fixture pins a need for a new gate, the gate lands as a closure-captured parameter on the helper builder, NOT a `compiledConfig` field expansion. This keeps `compiledConfig` minimal + future-extension-friendly without struct-field churn at every consumer addition. The 19.2 body-mode AMENDMENT (lift the body-mode PARSE-REJECT for the gRPC arm via `request_body_mode = BUFFERED`) adds NO new `compiledConfig` fields — the body-mode-specific buffering primitive (ADR-0175 at 19.2) is consumed via the dispatcher's closure scope inside `processFn` (Task 11 of 19.2 IMPL). The struct shape stays UNCHANGED across the body-mode lift — only the parse-time gate flips at step 6 of the pipeline.

**The `compiledConfig` immutability + read-only-shared discipline per ADR-0101.** Once `buildCompiledConfig` returns, the `*compiledConfig` is shared across ALL per-stream filter goroutines for the listener's lifetime. Per ADR-0101: NO field mutations after construction. Per-stream state (`f.activeProcessingMode`, `f.requestContentType`, `f.streamStartTime`, etc.) lives on the per-stream `*filter` instance; `compiledConfig` is the read-only listener-level surface. Per-route resolution (Task 10) reads `cc.processingMode` to derive `effectiveProcessingMode` overrides but DOES NOT mutate `cc` itself. The `*resolvedMutationRules` / `*resolvedForwardRules` / `*resolvedProcessingMode` pointer-typed fields are immutable post-construction (their substantive bodies were finalized in their respective resolver helpers + the carrier struct is read-only); shared safely across the per-stream goroutines without mutex protection.

**Operator-error-message UX discipline — every PARSE-REJECT axis carries a consistent `ext_proc:` prefix + a descriptive suffix.** The 11 PARSE-REJECT axes (mutual-exclusion neither/both, observability_mode, send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response, deferred_close_timeout, GoogleGrpc, EnvoyGrpc empty cluster_name, unknown cluster, UseH2 false, nil cluster manager, body-mode != NONE, trailer-mode != SKIP, http_service body-mode, route_cache_action mutual-exclusion, allowed_override_modes[i] validation) all share the `"ext_proc: <axis>: <reason>"` shape. This lets operators grep parse-error logs by filter family + by axis (`grep "ext_proc: processing_mode"` etc.). The shape mirrors phase-18.1 ext_authz error wording for cross-filter UX consistency. Future ext_proc PARSE-REJECT additions (e.g., the 19.2 body-mode-not-BUFFERED axis) MUST follow the same shape.

**Cross-listener `*grpc.ClientConn` reuse discipline per ADR-0158 §Decision (v) + ADR-0169.** The gRPC arm of `buildCompiledConfig` calls `buildGRPCProcessorClient` (Task 8 helper) which calls `grpcclient.NewProcessorClient(dialer, clusterName, messageTimeout)` — and the underlying `*grpc.ClientConn` is allocated ONCE per (cluster_name, `*compiledConfig`) pair. Multiple listeners pointing at the SAME upstream processor cluster will get DISTINCT `*grpc.ClientConn` instances (one per `*compiledConfig`); within a single listener, ALL per-stream `(*ProcessorClient).Process(ctx)` invocations multiplex over the SAME `*grpc.ClientConn` via gRPC's transport-level HTTP/2 stream multiplexing. The leaks-on-exit MVP per ADR-0158 §Decision (vi) applies — envoy-go has no xDS-CDS hot-reload yet; the connection is reclaimed at process exit.

**SILENT-IGNORE auditable-trail discipline.** The 3 silent-ignored top-level fields (filter_metadata #13, metadata_options #16, plus `core.GrpcService.{initial_metadata, retry_policy}`) flow through `buildCompiledConfig` UNTOUCHED — NO struct field allocation, NO runtime behavior, NO PARSE-REJECT. The auditable trail lives at: (a) the inline doc-comment comments in `extproc.go` (the field-roster comment block) + `buildGRPCProcessorClient`'s "step 5: initial_metadata + retry_policy SILENT-IGNORED" comment; (b) the §Context section of this ADR (the SILENT-IGNORE list); (c) the parent SPEC §8 deferred-items list (items 7-9 + 14). A future maintainer adding consumption of any of these fields MUST update all three sites + add a corresponding `compiledConfig` field + the per-field parse-path. The 5 silent-ignored per-route fields (async_mode + request_attributes + response_attributes + metadata_options + grpc_initial_metadata) parallel this discipline at the per-route layer per ADR-0173.

**Forward-pointer to 19.2's body-mode lift mechanism.** Phase 19.2 IMPL replaces the step-6 body-mode PARSE-REJECT (for the gRPC arm only — http_service stays headers-only per §Decision (iii)) with a body-mode DISPATCH: `request_body_mode = BUFFERED` activates the ADR-0128 decode-side body-buffering primitive (REUSED from phase-13); `response_body_mode = BUFFERED` activates the NEW ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive (phase-19.2 only). The §Decision (iv) is the AMENDMENT site — in-place edit per ADR-0044 (no new ADR number consumed). The lift activates the body-mode arms of `processFn` (the per-stage dispatcher) via the closure-capture discipline above — NO `compiledConfig` field additions, NO `resolvedProcessingMode` field additions, NO new ADR for the struct-shape impact. Concurrently, ADR-0172 §Decision AMENDMENT (body-mode portion at 19.2) extends the CommonResponse dispatcher to consume `body_mutation` + `body_response` stages; ADR-0171 §Decision AMENDMENT (body-mode portion at 19.2) extends the state-machine stage enum from 2 (request_headers + response_headers) to 6 (adds request_body + response_body + request_trailers + response_trailers; trailer arms stay PARSE-REJECT permanently per §Decision (v), so the trailer indices stay reserved-but-inactive). The cross-ADR AMENDMENT bundle at 19.2 is structurally isolated from the §Decision body — no rewrites of the existing §Decision (i)-(xi), only additions to the lift mechanism + dispatcher.

**No new fuzzer surface at Task 11.** The 24th fuzzer `FuzzExtProcConfigParse` lands at Task 14 of 19.1 PLAN per the SPEC §7.3 contract — it exercises `buildCompiledConfig` parse paths with the 8-12 seed encoding corpus. Task 11's wire-up of the production `New` factory completes the call-site `FuzzExtProcConfigParse` will exercise; the fuzzer itself is a Task 14 deliverable. The fuzzer's seed corpus MUST cover the 11 PARSE-REJECT axes enumerated in the operator-error-message UX discipline above + the happy-path gRPC + HTTP arms.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at Task 11.** The D12 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.1 IMPL beyond the 8 anticipated) UNCHANGED. ADR-0177 stays unconsumed. The Task 11 IMPL settled entirely within the existing ADR-0168 framing — the 11-clause §Decision body covers all surfaces the integration completeness exposed; no new decisions surfaced that warrant their own ADR. The carryforward F (drop `peerCertDERFn` YAGNI parameter) + G (per-route grpc_service consumption — at the Task 11 rework follow-up, `(*factoryState).resolvePerRouteConfig` constructs per-route `*grpcclient.ProcessorClient` via `buildGRPCProcessorClient` with the listener-level FactoryCtx + messageTimeout; the `*ProcessorClient` is cached on the factoryState by raw `*corev3.GrpcService` pointer-identity per ADR-0117 in a sync.Map alongside the existing `s.perRoute`; `(*filter).resolvePerRoute` selects the per-route `*ProcessorClient` over `cc.grpcClient` and caches it on `f.activeProcessorClient` which `openProcessorStream` reads at per-stream bidi-stream open time) + H (cross-mode PARSE-REJECT — at the Task 11 rework follow-up, `parseExtProcPerRoute(raw, httpServiceMode)` accepts a listener-arm flag passed by `resolvePerRouteConfig` from `listenerRC.httpServiceHeadersOnly`; HTTP-mode listener + per-route `grpc_service` override → PARSE-REJECT with operator-grep-able `"ext_proc: per-route: overrides.grpc_service incompatible with http_service listener"` wording; HTTP-mode listener + per-route `processing_mode` body-mode != NONE → PARSE-REJECT via `resolveProcessingMode`'s existing httpServiceMode-gated check (lifted from the initial Task 11 commit's hard-coded `false`); the opposite cross-mode direction is structurally not possible per the proto — there is no per-route `http_service` override field) + I (per-filter cache isolation test) + J (ADR-0117 cite comment) + E (errSentinel cleanup) all resolved IN-PLACE without ADR consumption. The initial Task 11 commit (`ebfd35b`) deferred G + H based on a fabricated "reserved for future per-stream construction" framing that contradicted SPEC §5 line 216 ("MVP-CONSUMED" classification for per-route grpc_service) and PLAN Task 10 line 602 acceptance gate ("grpc_service consumed"); the spec compliance review flagged the deferral as incomplete-implementation REWORK; the rework follow-up closes both Carryforwards in a separate commit on top of `ebfd35b` with 4 new Group 8 tests landing the per-route routing + cross-mode PARSE-REJECT assertions.

**§Consequences refresh (phase 19.2 Task 7 — body-stage integration completeness).** The 19.2 §Decision AMENDMENT body-mode lift (clause (iv)) is wired END-TO-END at phase-19.2 IMPL Task 7. The integration consumes the Tasks 2-6 primitive set: Task 2 ADR-0175 `BufferEncodedBody` encode-side primitive (structurally available; the chain-side accumulation path is exercised by Task 8 race tests); Task 4 4-stage state machine (`stageRequestBody` + `stageResponseBody` enum values; `dispatchStage` extended unchanged); Task 5 body-stage attribute envelope builders (`buildRequestBodyProcessingRequest` + `buildResponseBodyProcessingRequest`); Task 6 body-mode arms of `applyProcessingResponse` (`body_mutation` dispatch + `skipBodyStageDispatch[direction]` per-direction skip-flag consumer). The Task 7 wiring lands at `(*filter).DecodeData` + `(*filter).EncodeData` per the SPEC §6.3 pseudocode — body-mode-active gate + mid-stream accumulate-and-continue + endStream stash-dispatch-park. Per planner-time D2 closure-capture pattern: the body-buffer pointers (`f.decodeBodyBuf` + `f.encodeBodyBuf`) are captured by pointer in the dispatch-goroutine closure; the body-stage `processFn` envelope reads + writes them via the `*filter` receiver. The body-stage outbound action enum collapses onto the SAME 5-value enum the header-stage dispatch uses (`actContinue` / `actStop` / `actError` / `actImmediate` / `actContinueButStillWaiting`) — the 4-stage state machine extension preserves the structural symmetry between header + body stages per ADR-0171 §Decision AMENDMENT clause-extension.

**Decode-side body-mutation-delivery KNOWN LIMITATION at 19.2 — closure deferred to a future phase.** The encode-side body-mutation arm WORKS end-to-end via ADR-0131 `EncoderFilterCallbacks.OverwriteBody` reuse: the dispatch goroutine's `completeStage` path invokes `(*filter).deliverEncodeBodyMutation` (which calls `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(f.encodeBodyBuf)`) BEFORE the resume signal fires; HCM at `connection.go` H1 line 595 + `h2dispatch.go` H2 line 406 reads `chain.EncodeBodyOverride()` post-RunEncodeData + substitutes `resp.Body` with the (possibly-mutated) bytes. The decode side has NO equivalent — envoy-go's HCM reads upstream-bound body bytes from its own `bodyBuf` (H1 `connection.go` line 483-514) / `h2req.Body` (H2 `h2dispatch.go` line 361), both captured BEFORE the filter-chain mutation lands. The body_mutation arm at the decode side STILL runs (Task 6 wiring): the processor SEES the body bytes + can request mutation; the `applyProcessingResponse` arm writes new bytes to `f.decodeBodyBuf` + reconciles Content-Length on `f.decodeHeaders`. The HEADER reconciliation DOES propagate to upstream (the HCM's `req.Header` is the same map as `f.decodeHeaders`); only the BODY bytes are not delivered. The structural skip-flag path (`f.skipBodyStageDispatch[directionRequest]`) is honored at the body-stage entry per SPEC §4.3 row 2 — the body-stage outbound dispatch SKIPS as required; only the upstream-delivery of the mutated bytes is the gap. Closure deferred to a future phase that adds the decode-side body-mutation-delivery framework primitive (likely a future ADR analogous to ADR-0131 for the decode side; speculative ADR-0178 or later). This limitation is documented in the `(*filter).DecodeData` doc-comment + this §Consequences refresh; the 19.2 differential fixture (Task 9) scopes its mutation scenarios to the encode side where delivery works fully.

**`compiledConfig` struct field-final invariant PRESERVED through Task 7 wiring.** Per clause (xi) the struct shape stays UNCHANGED across the body-mode lift. Task 7 adds NO new `compiledConfig` fields — the body-mode-specific runtime state lives on the per-stream `*filter` (`decodeBodyBuf` / `encodeBodyBuf` / `skipBodyStageDispatch` — all introduced at Tasks 2-6) + the closure scope inside `dispatchStage` (the per-message-timer + per-stage context). The grep verifies field count parity: `grep -A30 'type compiledConfig struct' internal/filter/http/extproc/extproc.go | grep -c '	' = N` is identical pre- and post-Task-7. The closure-capture-vs-struct-field discipline (the second clause of this §Consequences body, anchored at the phase-18.2 ADR-0157 §Decision precedent) HOLDS through the 19.2 body-mode wire-up — Task 7 lands no new struct-field shape evolution.

**D10 hypothesis HOLDS through Task 7 — ADR-0177 stays unconsumed.** Per planner-time D10 + ADR-0044 escape-valve discipline: NO additional ADR fires at 19.2 IMPL beyond ADR-0175 (Task 2) + the three §Decision AMENDMENTs (ADR-0168 / ADR-0171 / ADR-0172). Task 7 settles entirely within the existing framework primitive set — the encode-side delivery reuses ADR-0131 `OverwriteBody`; the body-stage dispatch reuses the Task 4 state machine + the Task 5 envelope builders + the Task 6 mutation arms; the decode-side delivery is documented as a KNOWN LIMITATION rather than consuming a new framework primitive (the alternative would have been a decode-side `OverwriteBody` analog landing as a new ADR, but the 19.2 scope reduction defers that to a future phase). The next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0177` (unconsumed at the post-Task-7 commit).
