## ADR-0169: `*ProcessorClient` bidi-stream wrapper EXTENDING `internal/grpcclient/Dialer` (ADR-0158 §Consequences anchored this cross-phase shape) — NEW typed wrapper alongside the existing unary `*AuthClient` in the same package; `Process(ctx) (ProcessStream, error)` + bidi-stream lifecycle per HTTP transaction; FIRST cross-phase consumer of ADR-0158 outside phase-18.2 itself; cross-phase-reusable for future bidi-stream gRPC filters

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. The FIRST §9 row to EXTEND a phase-N-1 framework family (ADR-0158) rather than introduce a brand-new family — the cross-phase-reuse-at-introduction-time intent ADR-0158 codified per its §Consequences ("no future client coupling is anticipated to require `Dialer` API changes").
**Lands-in:** Task 3 of phase-19.1 PLAN (`internal/grpcclient/processor_client.go` new file alongside `auth_client.go`).

### Context

Phase 19 ships the bidi-stream RPC pattern over the existing `internal/grpcclient/` package — envoy-go's FIRST bidi-stream gRPC consumer (phase-18.2 established the unary RPC pattern with `*AuthClient`). The `envoy.service.ext_proc.v3.ExternalProcessor.Process` RPC is bidirectional streaming per `go-control-plane v1.32.4`'s `external_processor_grpc.pb.go` (parent §5.P10 RATIFIED): the client interface is `Process(ctx) (ExternalProcessor_ProcessClient, error)` returning a stream with `Send(*ProcessingRequest) error` + `Recv() (*ProcessingResponse, error)` + (inherited from `grpc.ClientStream`) `CloseSend() error` + `Context() context.Context`.

The `*ProcessorClient` wrapper composes against the EXISTING `*Dialer` (per ADR-0158 §Decision (i)+(ii)). NO `Dialer` API changes — the ADR-0158 §Consequences explicitly anchored this: "no future client coupling is anticipated to require `Dialer` API changes". Public surface:

```go
type ProcessorClient struct { /* ... */ }
func NewProcessorClient(d *Dialer, clusterName string, perMessageTimeout time.Duration) (*ProcessorClient, error)
func (c *ProcessorClient) Process(ctx context.Context) (ProcessStream, error)
type ProcessStream interface {
    Send(*extprocv3.ProcessingRequest) error
    Recv() (*extprocv3.ProcessingResponse, error)
    CloseSend() error
}
func (c *ProcessorClient) Close() error
```

`NewProcessorClient` calls `Dialer.DialContext(ctx, clusterName)` → wraps the returned `*grpc.ClientConn` with `extprocv3.NewExternalProcessorClient(conn)` returning the typed stub. The `perMessageTimeout` is applied per-MESSAGE via `context.WithTimeout` around the recv path (the `Send` is non-blocking on the gRPC client stream; the `Recv` blocks until the processor responds). The per-message timer interacts with `override_message_timeout` per parent §5.P10 — the IMPL resets the recv-timer when an `override_message_timeout` ProcessingResponse arrives.

**Connection lifecycle:** one `*grpc.ClientConn` per (cluster_name, `*compiledConfig`) pair (mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0158 §Decision (v) for `*AuthClient`); created at config-load time via `buildGRPCProcessorClient` in `extproc/check.go`; shared across all per-stream `Process()` invocations on that compiledConfig (gRPC manages transport-level reconnect via its sub-channel state machine).

**Stream lifecycle:** per HTTP transaction (one `Process` stream per request). The state machine at `extproc/processor.go` opens a stream via `ProcessorClient.Process(ctx)` at `DecodeHeaders` time when request_header_mode ∈ {SEND, DEFAULT}; sends ProcessingRequests per stage; receives ProcessingResponses; calls `CloseSend()` after the final response stage OR on `ImmediateResponse` arrival OR on `OnDestroy` cancellation. The stream's `ctx` carries the per-stream cancellation hook so `OnDestroy` aborts in-flight `Send`/`Recv` calls promptly.

**Leaks-on-exit MVP** per phase-18.2 ADR-0158 §Decision (vi) precedent: `Close()` is NOT explicitly called in production (envoy-go has no xDS-CDS hot-reload yet); the `*grpc.ClientConn` is leaked-on-exit. `Close()` is authored for unit tests + future hot-reload phases (sync.Once-guarded idempotency).

**Cross-phase reuse intent:** Future bidi-stream gRPC filters reuse the `ProcessorClient` pattern by composing their own typed wrapper alongside `AuthClient` + `ProcessorClient` using the same `Dialer`. The `*Dialer` API stays minimal (no API changes for 19.1). Possible future consumers: streaming-access-log filter; streaming-rate-limit filter. ext_proc is currently the sole bidi-stream consumer at 19.1.

References: parent SPEC §3 + §5.P1 + §5.P10. 19.1 SPEC §3.1 + §6.8. ADR-0158 §Decision + §Consequences (the parent framework primitive; `Dialer` API stays minimal; cross-phase reuse intent codified). ADR-0166 (plaintext h2c upstream relaxation — reused for the processor cluster).

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — landed at Task 4 of phase-19.1 PLAN per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.**

**(i) NEW file `internal/grpcclient/processor_client.go` co-located alongside `grpcclient.go` per planner-time D11.** A NEW Go file alongside the existing `grpcclient.go` in the same package. NO edits to `grpcclient.go` itself (D11 — the existing `*Dialer` + `*AuthClient` surface stays UNTOUCHED; the wrapper composes against `*Dialer` from a separate file). The same-package co-location lets the wrapper access the unexported `*Dialer` internals if needed (none are needed at Task 4 — only `(*Dialer).DialContext` is exercised) AND establishes the **per-wrapper-per-file convention** going forward: the existing `grpcclient.go`'s `Dialer` + `AuthClient` co-location is grandfathered (phase 18.2 introduced both in one file at introduction time); `processor_client.go` establishes the new convention that each typed wrapper lives in its own file alongside the `Dialer`. Future bidi-stream or unary wrappers (e.g., `ratelimit_client.go` for `global_ratelimit`) follow `processor_client.go`'s file-per-wrapper shape.

**(ii) Public surface — `ProcessorClient` + `NewProcessorClient` + `Process` + `ProcessStream` + `Close`.** The 1-struct, 1-interface, 4-function exported surface is:

```go
type ProcessorClient struct { /* opaque */ }
type ProcessStream interface {
    Send(*extprocv3.ProcessingRequest) error
    Recv() (*extprocv3.ProcessingResponse, error)
    CloseSend() error
}
func NewProcessorClient(d *Dialer, clusterName string, perMessageTimeout time.Duration) (*ProcessorClient, error)
func (c *ProcessorClient) Process(ctx context.Context) (ProcessStream, error)
func (c *ProcessorClient) PerMessageTimeout() time.Duration
func (c *ProcessorClient) Close() error
```

`NewProcessorClient` calls `d.DialContext(context.Background(), clusterName)` — mirrors `NewAuthClient`'s pattern at ADR-0158 §Decision (iv) — and wraps the returned `*grpc.ClientConn` with `extprocv3.NewExternalProcessorClient(conn)`. NO codegen; the `envoy.service.ext_proc.v3` bindings ship in `go-control-plane v1.32.4` and are first imported by this file at Task 4 (Task 2 imported the filter-config `extensions/filters/http/ext_proc/v3` proto; Task 4 adds the service `service/ext_proc/v3` proto via the typed-stub constructor). `PerMessageTimeout()` is an explicit accessor (rather than an exported struct field) for the filter's `dispatchStage` to read at Task 7 — keeps the `ProcessorClient` struct opaque per the AuthClient precedent.

**(iii) `ProcessStream` interface — minimum-surface 3-method abstraction over the raw `grpc.ClientStream`.** The interface exposes only `Send` + `Recv` + `CloseSend` — the three methods the filter's `dispatchStage` (Task 7) actually consumes. The underlying `grpc.ClientStream` methods (`Header`, `Trailer`, `Context`) are NOT exposed because the filter does not need them; if a future consumer needs them the interface can be extended without breaking existing callers (the implementation type — `extprocv3.ExternalProcessor_ProcessClient` from `go-control-plane v1.32.4` — already satisfies the larger surface; the interface narrowing is purely an API-hygiene gate). The narrow interface also makes the wrapper trivially mockable for filter unit tests at Task 12 (a 3-method mock vs a ~15-method `grpc.ClientStream` mock).

**(iv) PARSE-REJECT inheritance — three rejection paths surface verbatim from `(*Dialer).DialContext`.** `NewProcessorClient`'s three PARSE-REJECT axes are: (a) `d == nil` — rejected locally with `"grpcclient: new processor client %q: dialer is nil"` (mirrors `NewAuthClient`); (b) unknown cluster — INHERITED from `DialContext`'s `"grpcclient: dial %q: unknown cluster"`; (c) `UseH2()==false` — INHERITED from `DialContext`'s `"grpcclient: dial %q: cluster does not have http2_protocol_options{} set ..."`. The cluster name appears in all three error wordings for diagnostic affinity. NO new error paths are introduced at this wrapper; the dial-time gates are the only rejection surface.

**(v) Bidi-stream lifecycle + ctx threading.** `Process(ctx)` is a single-line delegation to `c.stub.Process(ctx)` — the gRPC-generated `ExternalProcessorClient.Process` opens the bidi-stream by issuing a `cc.NewStream(ctx, &ExternalProcessor_ServiceDesc.Streams[0], ...)` call (per `external_processor_grpc.pb.go` line 44). The caller's `ctx` is the parent for the stream — `OnDestroy`-driven cancellation (the filter's per-stream cancel hook, lands at Task 7) propagates through the stream's internal `context.Context` and aborts in-flight `Send`/`Recv` calls promptly. The wrapper does NOT classify or map transport errors; transport-error VERBATIM propagation per ADR-0158 §Decision (viii) is INHERITED for the bidi-stream path. The filter's `dispatchStage` maps transport errors to `dispError` before any ProcessingResponse-level handling.

**(vi) Per-message timeout discipline — stored on the struct, NOT applied in `Process`.** The `perMessageTimeout` argument to `NewProcessorClient` is STORED on `c.perMessageTimeout` for the filter's `dispatchStage` to read via `PerMessageTimeout()` at Task 7. `Process()` itself does NOT apply any `context.WithTimeout` around stream operations. Rationale: bidi-stream `Send`/`Recv` have asymmetric blocking semantics — `Send` is non-blocking on the gRPC client stream (the underlying `ClientStream.SendMsg` queues into the HTTP/2 framer); `Recv` blocks until the processor responds. A wrapper-level per-CALL timeout would not capture the right granularity. The filter is the right layer to own the per-MESSAGE timer because (a) the timer must reset between `override_message_timeout` ProcessingResponse arrivals (per parent §5.P10 — the processor can lift the per-message budget mid-stream); (b) the filter owns the per-stream cancellation hook via `OnDestroy` and threads it through the same ctx; (c) the per-MESSAGE timer wraps each `Recv` independently, not the full stream lifetime. The unit test `TestProcessorClient_Process_PerMessageTimeoutCallerSide` exercises the caller-side discipline by wrapping a `context.WithTimeout(parent, 100ms)` AND verifying `PerMessageTimeout()` returns the construction-time value separately — codifying the "storage, not enforcement" semantic at the wrapper.

**Why store on the struct at all (vs pass per-`Process` call)?** Three reasons: (a) the value is per-(cluster, compiledConfig) and never varies per HTTP transaction — passing it on every `Process` call adds caller noise without flexibility; (b) the SPEC §3.1 sketch explicitly signs off the constructor signature `NewProcessorClient(d, clusterName, perMessageTimeout)` — the PLAN matches the SPEC; (c) the `*AuthClient` precedent at ADR-0158 §Decision (vii) captures `timeout` at construction time for the same per-(cluster, compiledConfig) lifetime — the patterns stay symmetric across the two wrappers (the only difference is per-CALL vs per-MESSAGE semantics, which the accessor name `PerMessageTimeout()` makes explicit).

**(vii) One `*grpc.ClientConn` per (cluster_name, `*compiledConfig`) pair created at config-load time + shared across per-stream `Process` invocations.** Mirrors ADR-0158 §Decision (v) for `*AuthClient`. The `*ProcessorClient` is allocated ONCE at `buildGRPCProcessorClient` (config-load) time — lands at Task 11 — and captured on the `*compiledConfig`. All per-stream `Process()` invocations on that compiledConfig share the same `*grpc.ClientConn`. The `*grpc.ClientConn` is goroutine-safe per the gRPC library and manages its own transport-level reconnect via the sub-channel state machine; concurrent `Process` calls multiplex over the underlying HTTP/2 transport.

**(viii) Leaks-on-exit MVP + sync.Once-guarded `Close` per ADR-0158 §Decision (vi).** In production the filter NEVER calls `(*ProcessorClient).Close()` — the `*grpc.ClientConn` is leaked-on-exit; the OS reclaims it. envoy-go has no config hot-reload yet (xDS-CDS is deferred per parent SPEC §8 item 9); the process lifecycle bounds the connection. `Close()` is authored for the Group 3 unit tests (idempotency + concurrent-Close race-clean + nil-receiver safety) and for future hot-reload phases. Implementation is sync.Once-guarded with a cached `closeErr`; the nil receiver returns nil. Mirrors `*AuthClient.Close` line-for-line; the only structural difference is the receiver type.

### Consequences

**FIRST cross-phase consumer of ADR-0158 outside phase-18.2 itself.** ADR-0158 §Consequences explicitly anchored the cross-phase-reuse intent ("Cross-phase reuse: ext_proc + global_ratelimit consume this primitive. Future ext_proc (phase ~19+) reuses `(*Dialer).DialContext` and composes its own `*ProcessorClient` wrapping `envoy.service.ext_proc.v3.ExternalProcessor.Process` (bidi-stream — extends the unary Check pattern with stream management)"). Task 4 of phase 19.1 lands EXACTLY this — the predicted shape held at impl time. The `*Dialer` API was NOT extended (no new methods); the new wrapper composes purely against the existing `DialContext` surface. The §11.P13 in-session SPEC scrape RATIFICATION (TLS-at-cluster-manager + `WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials())`) holds verbatim for the bidi-stream path — gRPC sees the TLS-wrapped `net.Conn` and does NOT redo TLS for the bidi stream any differently than it does for the unary Check stub.

**Per-wrapper-per-file convention established for future wrappers.** The existing `grpcclient.go` co-location of `Dialer` + `AuthClient` is grandfathered (phase 18.2 introduced both in one file). `processor_client.go` establishes the file-per-wrapper convention going forward — future typed wrappers (e.g., a hypothetical `ratelimit_client.go` for `global_ratelimit`, or a future `streaming_access_log_client.go`) each live in their own file alongside `grpcclient.go`. Rationale: each typed wrapper is independently reviewable + testable; the file-per-wrapper shape keeps `grpcclient.go` itself stable (the `Dialer` is the cross-phase-reusable primitive; touching it once at phase 18.2 + once if/when a new dial option is needed is preferable to per-wrapper churn). The convention is documented at ADR-0169 §Decision (i) + reinforced via the `processor_client.go` file-level comment block.

**Cross-phase-reusable bidi-stream wrapper template for future bidi-stream gRPC filters.** A future bidi-stream consumer reuses the `ProcessorClient` SHAPE (not the type — the typed stub differs per service) by composing its own typed wrapper alongside `AuthClient` + `ProcessorClient`. Candidates: (a) a hypothetical streaming-access-log filter (the `envoy.service.accesslog.v3.AccessLogService.StreamAccessLogs` bidi-stream); (b) a streaming-rate-limit variant if ext_proc-style mid-stream override semantics get added to rate-limit (no such proto exists at the v3 Envoy API at the time of writing). ext_proc is currently the SOLE bidi-stream consumer at 19.1; the template is in place for the second consumer.

**Mockability — narrow `ProcessStream` interface enables 3-method test mocks.** At Task 12 (race tests + OnDestroy + bidi-stream cancellation), the filter unit tests benefit from a 3-method `ProcessStream` mock instead of the ~15-method `grpc.ClientStream` interface. The narrow interface IS the API gate that makes this trivially compositional — the filter never needs `Header`, `Trailer`, or `Context` calls on the stream because the per-stream cancel hook lives in the filter's own state. Codified at ADR-0169 §Decision (iii).

**Per-message timeout semantics now precisely specified.** The "stored, not enforced" discipline at ADR-0169 §Decision (vi) precisely specifies the wrapper's role vs the filter's role. The filter (Task 7) is the layer that wraps each `Recv` with `context.WithTimeout(streamCtx, c.PerMessageTimeout())` (deferred cancel); the wrapper provides only the value via `PerMessageTimeout()`. This lets the filter implement the `override_message_timeout` mid-stream reset (per parent §5.P10) WITHOUT a wrapper API change — the filter just reads `PerMessageTimeout()` once per `Recv` and re-applies; the wrapper's stored value remains the floor, and the override discipline lives entirely in the filter.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at Task 4.** The §11.P13 in-session SPEC scrape RATIFICATION (TLS-at-cluster-manager) held verbatim for the bidi-stream path; no new TLS-layer or cluster-manager surface was needed. The `passthrough:///<cluster_name>` resolver + `WithContextDialer` integration at ADR-0158 §Decision (ii)+(iii) works identically for the bidi-stream `Process` RPC as for the unary `Check` RPC — gRPC's stream machinery layers on top of the same sub-channel state machine. The D12 hypothesis from PLAN Task 4 (NO additional ADR fires at 19.1 IMPL beyond the 8 anticipated) holds — ADR-0177 stays unconsumed.

**Test coverage: Groups 1+2+3 PASS under `go test -race -count=1`.** Group 1 (`NewProcessorClient` — 4 tests: happy path; nil dialer; unknown-cluster propagation; `UseH2()==false` propagation) covers the 3 PARSE-REJECT axes + the happy construction. Group 2 (`Process` bidi-stream — 4 tests: happy round-trip with CloseSend→io.EOF; mid-stream cancel via parent ctx; per-message timeout caller-side discipline; concurrent Send+Recv) covers the lifecycle + cancellation + the per-message timeout discipline + the gRPC ClientStream concurrency contract. Group 3 (`Close` idempotency — 3 tests: idempotent close + post-close `Process` failure; concurrent close race-clean; nil-receiver safe) covers the sync.Once guard + the close-on-replacement readiness for future hot-reload phases. All 11 tests PASS under `-race`; race-detector clean.

**Reference: ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.** §Context drafted at the phase-19.1 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 (the cross-cutting design is on disk before any code lands); §Decision + §Consequences land here at the Task 4 impl commit. Mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0158's same-pattern Task 3 landing.

## ADR-0170: `ProcessingRequest`/`ProcessingResponse` JSON codec for http_service mode — uses `protojson` (already in dependency tree); filter-local at `extproc/json.go` for MVP; protojson defaults RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME per parent §5.P8; generalization to `internal/jsoncodec/` deferred to the second-consumer trigger per the phase-18.1 ADR-0159 (b)-disposition rationale

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. The SECOND deferred-generalization decision (after ADR-0159's HTTP-outbound auth-check disposition (b) at phase 18.1) — establishes the discipline of "land filter-local; generalize at the third consumer".
**Lands-in:** Task 4 of phase-19.1 PLAN (`internal/filter/http/extproc/json.go`).

### Context

The `ExtProcHttpService.http_service` arm of ext_proc POSTs a JSON-encoded `ProcessingRequest` per stage to the configured HTTP service URI and parses the JSON `ProcessingResponse`. Per the proto's `ExtProcHttpService.http_service` doc-comment (quoted at parent §5.P1): "if 'http_service' is set, the `processing_mode` can not be configured to send any body or trailers. i.e, http_service only supports sending request or response headers to the side stream server." — the http_service arm is HEADERS-ONLY by proto constraint; the codec marshals/unmarshals only the headers-stage payloads.

**Codec choice: `protojson`** (`google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson`), already in the dependency tree via `go-control-plane`. The wire-shape is a single JSON-encoded `ProcessingRequest` per POST body + a single JSON-encoded `ProcessingResponse` per HTTP response body.

**`protojson` MarshalOptions** (per parent §5.P8 hypothesis; RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME at 19.1 fixture-harness scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2):
- `UseProtoNames: true` — use proto field names (snake_case) rather than the proto3 JSON canonical lowerCamelCase mapping. Hypothesized to match reference Envoy's encoding; the IMPL fixture scrape closes the pin definitively.
- `EmitUnpopulated: false` — omit zero-valued fields (default).
- `UseEnumNumbers: false` — render enum values as string names (e.g., `"SEND"`, `"CONTINUE"`, `"BUFFERED"`).

**UnmarshalOptions:**
- `DiscardUnknown: true` — forward-compat tolerance for proto extensions added in future Envoy versions.

**Public surface** (private to the `extproc` package):

```go
func marshalProcessingRequest(req *extprocv3.ProcessingRequest) ([]byte, error)
func unmarshalProcessingResponse(data []byte) (*extprocv3.ProcessingResponse, error)
```

**Filter-local-vs-shared-package disposition.** The codec is intentionally NOT generalized into `internal/grpcclient/` or a new `internal/jsoncodec/` package at 19.1 — there is no second consumer in-tree, and the codec is structurally tied to the ext_proc proto-binding. Per the phase-18.1 ADR-0159 (b)-disposition rationale, generalization is reconsidered at the SECOND (or third — IMPL's call) consumer trigger. Currently no in-tree consumer needs a generalized protojson-over-HTTP codec; future candidates include any future filter that emits/consumes JSON-transcoded protos (e.g., a future streaming-rate-limit-via-JSON-POST mode — but the gRPC variant is the standard deployment shape for those filters).

**Wire-shape verification** at 19.1 IMPL fixture-harness: capture one ProcessingRequest + one ProcessingResponse from reference Envoy v1.37.2 running http_service mode; assert byte-equivalent JSON output from `marshalProcessingRequest` (and byte-equivalent parse of the inverse via `unmarshalProcessingResponse`). If the empirical scrape surfaces divergences (e.g., reference Envoy uses lowerCamelCase per proto3 JSON canonical, OR emits unpopulated fields, OR uses different well-known-type encodings — Duration/Timestamp formatting), §Decision is amended in-place at 19.1 IMPL per ADR-0044.

References: parent SPEC §3 + §5.P8 + §6 amendment 8. 19.1 SPEC §3.2 + §6 file-layout. ADR-0159 (the phase-18.1 disposition-(b) precedent — filter-local thin client until the second consumer trigger).

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — landed at Task 6 of phase-19.1 PLAN per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.**

**(i) Filter-local at `internal/filter/http/extproc/json.go`** — a NEW file in the existing `extproc` package alongside `extproc.go` + `doc.go` (Task 2 skeleton). The file carries the two production codec functions + their package-level `protojson` MarshalOptions/UnmarshalOptions instances + the file-level rationale block citing ADR-0170 + parent §5.P8. Co-located with the per-stage dispatcher (Task 8 `check.go`) per SPEC §6.9's multi-file split — the http_service-mode call sites (Task 8 `dispatchHTTPStage`-class) sit one file over from the codec. NO new package, NO new shared `internal/jsoncodec/` directory — the codec lives where its sole consumer lives.

**(ii) Public surface (private to the `extproc` package).** Two functions; matches the SPEC §3.2 sketch verbatim:

```go
func marshalProcessingRequest(req *extprocsvcv3.ProcessingRequest) ([]byte, error)
func unmarshalProcessingResponse(data []byte) (*extprocsvcv3.ProcessingResponse, error)
```

The proto type alias `extprocsvcv3` aliases `github.com/envoyproxy/go-control-plane/envoy/service/ext_proc/v3` (the service-binding package; distinct from the filter-config `extprocv3` alias for `envoy/extensions/filters/http/ext_proc/v3` used in `extproc.go`). The alias name `extprocsvcv3` (svc = service) disambiguates the two ext_proc proto packages at every call site that touches both — a hygiene gate against accidental cross-package type confusion (the filter-config package carries `ExternalProcessor`; the service package carries `ProcessingRequest`/`ProcessingResponse`).

**(iii) `protojson` MarshalOptions — three settings pinned per parent §5.P8 hypothesis (RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME).**

```go
var marshalOpts = protojson.MarshalOptions{
    UseProtoNames:   true,
    EmitUnpopulated: false,
    UseEnumNumbers:  false,
}
```

- **`UseProtoNames: true`** — render the proto field names as snake_case (e.g., `request_headers`, `header_mutation`, `set_headers`), NOT the proto3 JSON canonical lowerCamelCase (`requestHeaders`, `headerMutation`, `setHeaders`). Hypothesized to match reference Envoy's encoding per parent §5.P8; the IMPL fixture-harness scrape at Task 13 closes the pin definitively (if reference Envoy emits lowerCamelCase, this field flips per ADR-0044 in-place AMENDMENT). The 19.1 unit test `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_RoundTrip` asserts the snake_case key `"request_headers"` appears AND the lowerCamelCase form `"requestHeaders"` does NOT — a regression sentinel for accidental UseProtoNames=false drift.
- **`EmitUnpopulated: false`** — omit zero-valued fields entirely (the protojson default — kept explicit at the option-struct level for documentation visibility). Reduces wire payload + matches reference Envoy's omission discipline (hypothesized; closes at Task 13). The 19.1 unit test `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_EmitUnpopulatedFalse` asserts a zero-valued `*ProcessingRequest` renders without the `observability_mode` field — a regression sentinel for accidental EmitUnpopulated=true drift.
- **`UseEnumNumbers: false`** — render enum values as their string names (e.g., `"CONTINUE"`, `"OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD"`) rather than their integer ordinals. Standard for human-readable Envoy admin pages and processor-side observability; matches reference Envoy's enum-rendering discipline (hypothesized; closes at Task 13).

**(iv) `protojson` UnmarshalOptions — forward-compat via `DiscardUnknown: true`.**

```go
var unmarshalOpts = protojson.UnmarshalOptions{
    DiscardUnknown: true,
}
```

Load-bearing for forward-compat: future Envoy proto extensions (new fields added to `ProcessingResponse` in a newer `go-control-plane` vintage) land as silently-ignored unknown fields, NOT as parse failures that would crash every running envoy-go binary against a newer processor. The trade-off is accepting a typo'd processor-side field name as silently ignored; this is acceptable because the processor is the source-of-truth for the response shape (envoy-go is the consumer; the inverse parse-strictness discipline applies at `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:156` where `DiscardUnknown: false` because bootstrap YAML is operator-supplied and typos SHOULD fail loudly at boot). The 19.1 unit test `TestUnmarshalProcessingResponse_DiscardUnknown` exercises an explicit top-level + nested unknown field bundle to pin the forward-compat contract.

**(v) Wire-shape RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME at parent §5.P8 — closes at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape.** The three MarshalOptions settings + the one UnmarshalOption are HYPOTHESES at Task 6 — they reflect the parent §5.P8 in-session reasoning about reference Envoy's likely encoding (snake_case + enum-as-string + omit-zero-values + tolerant-of-unknowns) but the EMPIRICAL pin against reference Envoy v1.37.2 lands at Task 13's differential fixture-harness via a one-request + one-response capture (the fixture-0022 `c_ext_proc` HTTP-service-mode scenario). Per ADR-0044, if the Task 13 scrape surfaces divergence (e.g., reference Envoy emits lowerCamelCase keys or includes unpopulated fields with their proto defaults), the ADR-0170 §Decision (iii)/(iv) settings are AMENDED in-place at Task 13's commit (NOT a new ADR) — the AMENDMENT is mechanical (one or more option flips), and the AMENDMENT path is the precedent set by ADR-0157 + ADR-0167's similar IMPL-time pin-closure model.

**(vi) On unmarshal failure per D8: classify as `streamsFailed++` + dispError (fail-loud).** The codec itself does NOT increment counters or emit log lines — it returns the raw protojson error wrapped with a stable prefix (`"extproc: unmarshal ProcessingResponse: "`) for grep-discoverability. The Task 8 per-stage dispatcher (`dispatchHTTPStage`-class) consumes the error: (a) increments `streamsFailed` (the 9-counter set's failure axis per ADR-0167 + parent §5.P4); (b) emits a dispError to the per-stage completion channel; (c) applies the `failure_mode_allow` posture per parent §5.P11 (false → SendLocalReply(500); true → allow-through with both `streamsFailed` AND `failureModeAllowed` increments). NO silent-swallow path — a malformed JSON body from the processor is ALWAYS surfaced; the `failure_mode_allow` posture is the only knob that controls whether the request continues or is denied. The 19.1 unit test `TestUnmarshalProcessingResponse_Malformed` exercises four malformed inputs (empty, truncated, not-JSON, unbalanced-braces) and asserts non-nil error in each case — the contract that the dispatcher relies on.

**(vii) Direction asymmetry — Pattern A (PLAN Task 6).** Production code exposes the REQUEST-direction marshal + the RESPONSE-direction unmarshal — the two directions the http_service-mode dispatch actually exercises (Envoy POSTs `ProcessingRequest`, processor responds with `ProcessingResponse`). NO peer `unmarshalProcessingRequest` / `marshalProcessingResponse` is authored — the inverse directions are not exercised in production. Tests that verify round-trip semantics (e.g., `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_RoundTrip`) call `protojson.Unmarshal` directly on the marshaled bytes — treats the production codec as a black-box from the test perspective + verifies the marshaled bytes are valid protojson for the inverse parse direction. The Pattern A choice keeps the production surface MINIMAL (two functions, not four); the test-side direct-protojson call is a one-liner that does NOT couple test code to the production package's internal options.

**(viii) Package-level option singletons — hot-path allocation hygiene.** `marshalOpts` + `unmarshalOpts` are package-level `var`s (not per-call `protojson.MarshalOptions{...}` constructions). Rationale: the per-stage path is hot (one marshal + one unmarshal per stage per HTTP transaction in http_service mode; up to two stages per transaction at 19.1 — request_headers + response_headers); the option struct is small but the construction allocates onto the stack at every call site, and the package-level singleton anchors the ADR-0170 pin in a single grep-discoverable location (any future drift to the settings has exactly one edit surface). The options structs are read-only after package init — protojson's `Marshal`/`Unmarshal` methods do not mutate the receiver — so the package-level sharing is concurrent-safe across all dispatcher goroutines.

### Consequences

**Filter-local for MVP per the phase-18.1 ADR-0159 (b)-disposition rationale — generalization deferred to the THIRD consumer trigger.** The codec is NOT generalized into `internal/grpcclient/` (the gRPC-mode dispatch package; structurally distinct since `grpcclient` carries the bidi-stream wrapper, not JSON marshalling) NOR into a new `internal/jsoncodec/` package at 19.1. Currently NO other in-tree consumer of protojson-over-HTTP exists — `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go` consumes protojson but with `DiscardUnknown: false` (operator-supplied YAML strictness) AND with the entire `Bootstrap` proto type (not the ext_proc service types); the cross-consumer commonality would be the option-struct discipline, not the marshal/unmarshal calls themselves. Per the phase-18.1 ADR-0159 (b)-disposition precedent (filter-local thin HTTP client until the second consumer trigger; phase-18.2 confirmed the trigger by adding the second `grpcclient` consumer — but that triggered DialContext sharing, not codec sharing), generalization is reconsidered at the THIRD consumer of protojson-over-HTTP. Candidates: a future streaming-access-log-via-HTTP filter; a future filter that proxies CEL attribute envelopes over HTTP. Until then, ADR-0170 anchors the filter-local convention as a recorded decision (NOT a default; the THIRD consumer triggers a follow-up ADR that may relocate the codec).

**IMPL-time AMENDMENT path at parent §5.P8 RATIFIED-PENDING closure — Task 13 fixture-harness pins.** ADR-0170 §Decision (iii) + (iv) are AMENDABLE in-place at Task 13 per ADR-0044 if the reference-Envoy v1.37.2 wire-shape scrape diverges from the hypotheses. Three divergence axes are anticipated and mechanically remediable:
- **lowerCamelCase divergence:** if reference Envoy emits `requestHeaders` (proto3 JSON canonical) rather than `request_headers` (proto field name), flip `UseProtoNames: true` → `UseProtoNames: false` at the package-level singleton. The 19.1 unit test `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_RoundTrip` flips its assertion (`"request_headers"` ↔ `"requestHeaders"`) at the same commit.
- **EmitUnpopulated divergence:** if reference Envoy emits zero-valued fields (e.g., `"observability_mode": false`), flip `EmitUnpopulated: false` → `EmitUnpopulated: true` at the singleton. The 19.1 unit test `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_EmitUnpopulatedFalse` flips its assertion accordingly.
- **UseEnumNumbers divergence:** if reference Envoy renders enums as integer ordinals (e.g., `"status": 0` rather than `"status": "CONTINUE"`), flip `UseEnumNumbers: false` → `UseEnumNumbers: true`. No unit test flip is required (the 19.1 unit tests do not assert enum rendering — they assert proto.Equal equivalence which is enum-encoding-agnostic).
The AMENDMENT path is mechanical (one or more option flips at `json.go`); the AMENDMENT does NOT require a new ADR — it edits ADR-0170 §Decision in-place at the Task 13 commit per ADR-0044's IMPL-time-pin-closure model. The Task 13 commit message documents the scrape outcome + the flipped options (if any).

**SECOND deferred-generalization decision in the envoy-go DECISIONS log** (after ADR-0159's HTTP-outbound auth-check disposition (b) at phase 18.1). Establishes the discipline of "land filter-local; generalize at the THIRD consumer" as a recorded pattern for future filters that introduce a thin abstraction over an existing standard-library package (protojson, http, etc.). The pattern's rationale: premature generalization at the SECOND consumer often locks in a shared API surface that the THIRD consumer cannot fit (the SECOND consumer's needs are sometimes still niche; the THIRD consumer's needs reveal the cross-cutting interface). The pattern is NOT a hard rule — a SECOND consumer that obviously shares the FIRST consumer's API surface triggers a generalization at the SECOND consumer's commit (e.g., the Dialer pattern at phase 18.2 was generalized at the SECOND consumer-anticipation per ADR-0158 — but that was a primitive with a known cross-phase reuse pattern, not a thin codec). ADR-0170 reinforces ADR-0159 as the dispositional precedent; future filters that face the same choice cite both ADRs.

**Test coverage: Group 2 portion PASS under `go test -race -count=1`.** Six test functions cover the codec surface:
- `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_RoundTrip` (round-trip via Pattern A — marshal-then-direct-protojson-unmarshal-into-fresh-Request; UseProtoNames assertion both directions; proto.Equal equivalence).
- `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_NilInput` (defensive nil-input rejection at the API boundary).
- `TestMarshalProcessingRequest_EmitUnpopulatedFalse` (the `observability_mode` absence sentinel).
- `TestUnmarshalProcessingResponse_HappyPath` (hand-crafted snake_case JSON → typed parse + CommonResponse.status + header_mutation set_headers verification).
- `TestUnmarshalProcessingResponse_DiscardUnknown` (forward-compat: top-level + nested unknown fields ignored).
- `TestUnmarshalProcessingResponse_Malformed` (D8 fail-loud: 4-case sub-test on empty / truncated / not-JSON / unbalanced-braces inputs).

All six PASS under `-race`; race-detector clean. The unit tests do NOT exercise reference-Envoy wire-shape equivalence — that pin lands at Task 13's differential-fixture-harness scrape per the RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME contract.

**No new dependency.** `google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson` is ALREADY in the dependency tree (consumed by `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:68` since phase 01 + at 14+ other call sites across `internal/cluster/`, `internal/filter/http/cors/`, etc.). The Task 3 reachability verification at PROGRESS.md captured `MarshalOptions.UseProtoNames`/`UseEnumNumbers`/`EmitUnpopulated` as present + accessible. NO `go.mod` edit at Task 6; NO `go mod tidy` diff.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at Task 6.** ADR-0170 §Decision + §Consequences anchored at this commit (the §Context was drafted at the parent SPEC commit `9cc1458`). D12 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.1 IMPL beyond the 8 anticipated) UNCHANGED — ADR-0177 stays unconsumed. The Task 6 implementation matches the SPEC §3.2 + parent §5.P8 sketches verbatim; no IMPL-time surprises surfaced that warranted a new decision.

**Reference: ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.** §Context drafted at the phase-19.1 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 (the cross-cutting design is on disk before any code lands); §Decision + §Consequences land here at the Task 6 impl commit. Mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0158 + phase-19.1 ADR-0169's same-pattern landings. The IMPL-time AMENDMENT path at Task 13 (per the wire-shape pin closure) is the THIRD recorded ADR-0044 escape-valve mechanism in the envoy-go DECISIONS log (after ADR-0157 + ADR-0167's same IMPL-time mechanisms).

**§19.P8 IMPL-time DISPOSITION at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape (post-rework 4/4 canonical text): RATIFIED on the codec-options axis via cross-side empirical scrape; three envelope-content divergences DOCUMENTED-IN-PLACE as 19.2 surfaces.** The Task 13 fixture-harness empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 — closed after the Task 13 rework `b8b28fe` HTTP-handler `DiscardUnknown:true` fix (the test driver's HTTP processor handler had been parsing reference-side `ProcessingRequest`s without `DiscardUnknown:true`, so reference Envoy's emission of the forward-compat `protocol_config:{}` empty message caused parse failure -> 400 -> `http_not_ok_resp_received`; mirroring the production codec's `unmarshalOpts` settles the reachability) — confirms cross-side equivalence on all three protojson MarshalOption settings: `UseProtoNames:true` matches reference Envoy's snake_case field-name emission (the SPEC-time hypothesis ratifies); `EmitUnpopulated:false` matches the omit-zero-valued-fields discipline; `UseEnumNumbers:false` matches the enum-as-string emission discipline. The structural-equivalence assertion at the fixture's `AssertStats` time (both sides' captured bytes round-trip through `protojson.Unmarshal{DiscardUnknown:true}` into a valid `*ProcessingRequest` / `*ProcessingResponse`; oneof-arm discriminator agrees cross-side) HOLDS. **Closure status: §19.P8 RATIFIED on the codec-options axis.** Three envelope-content divergences surfaced by the cross-side scrape are DEFERRED to phase 19.2 — none invalidate the codec-shape closure; each is documented in-place rather than re-opening the pin:

- **Go protojson's intentional whitespace non-determinism** (per Go protobuf PR #1564 and related changes injecting a pseudo-random whitespace prefix into encoded output) — literal byte-equivalence of serialized JSON is structurally impossible between Go protojson and reference Envoy's C++ JSON emitter without a whitespace-normalizing post-pass. The 19.1 IMPL adopts the structural-equivalence framing (via `proto.Equal` after unmarshal round-trip) for cross-side comparison; literal byte-equivalence is explicitly OUT of the §19.P8 contract on the JSON-encoding axis. No production-code remediation required.

- **Reference Envoy emits `metadata_context:{}` and `protocol_config:{}` empty proto messages** in its `ProcessingRequest` JSON, whereas envoy-go's `EmitUnpopulated:false` omits both fields entirely. Forward-compat tolerance on the unmarshal side is already covered by the production codec's `DiscardUnknown:true` (the same property that, after the Task 13 rework fix, makes the test driver's reference-side parse succeed). DEFERRED to 19.2 as a possible amendment surface IF reference Envoy's emission of these empty messages turns out to be operator-load-bearing for any downstream consumer (e.g., a processor that programmatically tests for the field's presence-with-default rather than absence). The amendment, if it lands, is a single-option flip (`EmitUnpopulated:false` -> `EmitUnpopulated:true`) under the existing ADR-0044 in-place-amend discipline established earlier in §Consequences; no new ADR fires.

- **Writer-side `value` vs `raw_value` choice on header injection** is a Task 9 `attributes.go` writer-side concern; the consumer-side at `check.go:applyHeaderMutation` already honors `raw_value` preferentially per the proto-doc precedence rule (landed at Task 13 rework `28dfba1`). The writer-side migration to emit `raw_value` from the envelope builder is DEFERRED to 19.2 attributes.go writer-side update; the consumer-side rework already accepts both shapes correctly cross-side.

**Cross-side evidence chain.** The closure rests on three rework commits stacked on the original Task 13 commit `d404ae5`: (1) `0a117f1` (Task 13 rework 1/3 — `completeStage` actImmediate must call `signalResume(s)` matching the ext_authz + fault.go + chain_test.go precedents; closes the scenario-2 immediate_response delivery bug that had masked the §19.P8 reachability under a status=0 connection reset); (2) `28dfba1` (Task 13 rework 2/3 — wire runtime header-mutation apply with `raw_value`-preferential reader); (3) `b8b28fe` (Task 13 rework 3/3 — restore SPEC §15 #10 byte-equivalence + close §19.P8 via the cross-side scrape enabled by the HTTP-handler `DiscardUnknown:true` fix). The 19.1 unit tests (the 6 Group 2 tests in `extproc_test.go`) provide single-side proto.Equal round-trip coverage; the 0022 fixture's `AssertStats` provides the cross-side structural-equivalence check. The fixture's per-scenario verdict tokens follow the 0021-precedent `classifyBody(id, body, headers)` form (returning `ok | mismatch(<reason>)`) — the byte-stream format is `scenario <id> status=<code> body=<ok|mismatch(...)>` for byte-exact cross-side comparison per SPEC §15 #10. SPEC §15 #9 zero-RATIFIED-PENDING-pins claim now holds canonically: §19.P4 RATIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENT, §19.P7 RATIFIED-BY-CONSTRUCTION, §19.P8 RATIFIED on the codec-options axis — all three SPEC-time RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME pins are closed RATIFIED at 19.1 IMPL.

## ADR-0171: ProcessingMode state-machine + mode-override discipline — per-direction ProcessingMode state; bidi-stream single-in-flight-message correlation; mid-stream mode_override re-eval (header-response paths only per §5.P1); `allow_mode_override` + `allowed_override_modes` validation; `mutation_rules` per-header gating; `max_message_timeout` bounding `override_message_timeout` extensions; STREAMED-only flags PARSE-REJECT; `DEFAULT` translates to SEND for headers / SKIP for trailers per §5.P9 — §Decision AMENDMENT at phase-19.2 IMPL (4-stage state-machine extension + per-message timer behavioral enforcement)

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention; §Decision lands at 19.1 IMPL (header-mode portion); §Decision AMENDMENT lands at 19.2 IMPL Task 4 — 4-stage state-machine extension `numStages` 2 → 4 + per-message timer behavioral enforcement via `context.WithTimeout` cancel-and-rebuild per parent §5.P5).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 + 19.2 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
**Lands-in:** Task 5 of phase-19.1 PLAN (`processor.go` state machine; header-mode portion); Task 4 of phase-19.2 IMPL (`processor.go` 4-stage state machine + per-message timer behavioral §Decision AMENDMENT).

### Context

The ext_proc filter is structurally distinct from prior §9 filters in that it operates as a per-stage state machine over a bidi-stream gRPC `Process` RPC (or per-stage HTTP-JSON POSTs in http_service mode). The state machine carries per-direction `ProcessingMode` state — at any time the filter has an "active" ProcessingMode determining whether the request_headers / request_body / response_headers / response_body stages fire as outbound ProcessingRequests.

**ProcessingMode parse-and-resolve** (parent §5.P9 RATIFIED): the proto's `HeaderSendMode.DEFAULT (0)` is context-sensitive — the envoy-go IMPL translates DEFAULT → SEND for `*_header_mode` fields at parse time; DEFAULT → SKIP for `*_trailer_mode` fields. `BodySendMode` has no DEFAULT enum value; the zero value is `NONE`. Phase 19 19.1 PARSE-REJECTs body-modes != NONE (lifted at 19.2 for BUFFERED only); STREAMED + BUFFERED_PARTIAL + FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict permanently; trailer-modes != SKIP PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict permanently.

**State-machine invariants** (per the proto's bidi-stream protocol design + parent §5.P10):
- **Single-in-flight per-stage**: at most one outstanding ProcessingRequest at any time. Each `Send` is followed by a `Recv` before the next stage's `Send`. (No STREAMED interleaving in the MVP envelope.)
- **Per-direction state**: request-side state (request_header_mode + request_body_mode) and response-side state (response_header_mode + response_body_mode) are TRACKED INDEPENDENTLY — a mode_override on a request_headers response affects request-side state for SUBSEQUENT request-side stages (and the response-side stages if mode_override updates the full ProcessingMode); the response-side state is unaffected by request-side stages' mode_overrides until they explicitly update the response-side modes.
- **Stage order**: request_headers → (request_body if BUFFERED at 19.2) → upstream → response_headers → (response_body if BUFFERED at 19.2) → downstream. Body-stages PARSE-REJECT in 19.1.

**Mode-override discipline** (per parent §5.P1 RATIFIED-AND-REFINED):
- `mode_override` is honored ONLY when arriving in response to `request_headers` or `response_headers` ProcessingRequests — `mode_override` arriving in a body-stage or trailer-stage response is IGNORED (silently dropped per proto doc; NOT classified as `spurious_msgs_received`).
- `mode_override` is also ignored when `allow_mode_override=false`.
- The third gate (`send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response=true`) is irrelevant for envoy-go since that flag PARSE-REJECTs per §5.P10.
- When `allowed_override_modes` is non-empty, the override mode is validated against the allow-list (exact ProcessingMode value match required); a mode_override outside the allow-list is classified as `spurious_msgs_received` per the canonical Envoy counter (distinct from the proto-doc silent-ignore disposition for non-header-stage mode_overrides).
- The override's effect propagates to SUBSEQUENT stages.

**`override_message_timeout` discipline** (per parent §5.P10 RATIFIED):
- The `ProcessingResponse.override_message_timeout` field is a `*durationpb.Duration` that, when received, RESETS the per-stage timer to the new duration.
- Takes effect ONLY if `ExternalProcessor.max_message_timeout >= 1ms` (otherwise the entire override-timer API is disabled per proto doc); when disabled, an `override_message_timeout` arrival increments `override_message_timeout_ignored` counter.
- The new timeout must be in `[1ms, max_message_timeout]` (out-of-range → `override_message_timeout_ignored` counter increment).
- At most ONCE per stage's processing state (subsequent `override_message_timeout` arrivals in the same stage are classified as `spurious_msgs_received`).
- The `ProcessingResponse` carrying `override_message_timeout` has its OTHER fields IGNORED (the CommonResponse, ImmediateResponse, mode_override fields on the same response are NOT consumed); the IMPL handles this special-case by checking `override_message_timeout` FIRST in `applyProcessingResponse` and short-circuiting if present.

**`mutation_rules` per-header gating** (per parent §5.P3 RATIFIED): when a `CommonResponse.header_mutation` arrives, each set/remove operation is independently validated against the resolved `mutation_rules` allow/deny matchers. Allowed mutations apply; rejected mutations are dropped silently AND set a per-stage flag so `spurious_msgs_received` increments ONCE per stage with any rejection.

**Bidi-stream half-close + `CloseSend` discipline** (per parent §5.P10 RATIFIED): the client calls `CloseSend()` after the final stage's response completes OR on `ImmediateResponse` arrival (the stream is terminated; subsequent ProcessingResponses ignored) OR on `OnDestroy` cancellation (the in-flight Send/Recv aborts; `streamCancel()` propagates).

References: parent SPEC §4.1 + §5.P1 + §5.P9 + §5.P10 + §6 amendments 1 + 9 + 10. 19.1 SPEC §6.3 + §6.4 + §6.5 + §6.6 + §6.7 + §6.8. ADR-0085 (`SendLocalReply` framework primitive).

### Decision

The header-mode portion of ADR-0171 lands at phase-19.1 Task 7 via `internal/filter/http/extproc/processor.go`. The body-mode portion AMENDS this §Decision at phase-19.2 (the `*_body_mode = BUFFERED` PARSE-REJECT lifts + body-stage state-machine extends per ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT). The 19.1-landing surface:

**(i) `resolveProcessingMode` per parent §5.P9 RATIFIED — DEFAULT translation + body-mode PARSE-REJECT + trailer-mode PARSE-REJECT.** The `extprocv3.ProcessingMode` proto is parsed into a `*resolvedProcessingMode` value (struct fields populated in `extproc.go` at Task 2; field types kept stable through Task 7). The translation discipline:

- `HeaderSendMode.DEFAULT (0) → SEND` for `request_header_mode` + `response_header_mode` (proto enum-doc: "By default, request and response headers are sent"). Explicit `SEND` + `SKIP` pass through verbatim.
- `HeaderSendMode.DEFAULT (0) → SKIP` for `request_trailer_mode` + `response_trailer_mode` (proto enum-doc: "while trailers are skipped"). Explicit `SKIP` passes through; any other value (`SEND` + any future enum) PARSE-REJECTs permanently per the §5.P9 trailers-out-of-envelope discipline.
- `BodySendMode != NONE` PARSE-REJECTs in 19.1 (the BUFFERED arm activates at 19.2 per the ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT; STREAMED + BUFFERED_PARTIAL + FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED PARSE-REJECT permanently per parent Q2 out-of-envelope).
- `http_service` mode + body-mode `!= NONE` PARSE-REJECT (proto-constraint per `ExtProcHttpService` doc; subsumed by the listener-level body-mode PARSE-REJECT at 19.1 but pre-positioned as an independent gate for the 19.2 AMENDMENT path where the listener-level body-mode PARSE-REJECT lifts).

Sentinel error wording starts with `"ext_proc: processing_mode: "` for grep-discoverability at the Task 11 `buildCompiledConfig` call site. A nil `*ProcessingMode` input resolves to the all-defaults form (proto-doc behavior — missing field = "send headers, skip trailers, no body").

**(ii) Per-direction `ProcessingMode` state — `f.activeProcessingMode` mutated mid-stream by validated `mode_override`.** The filter's per-stream `f.activeProcessingMode *resolvedProcessingMode` field is initialized from `cc.processingMode` (or the per-route override at DecodeHeaders entry per ADR-0173) and read by both the decode side (request_headers stage gating) and the encode side (response_headers stage gating). The framework's sequential decode→encode dispatch invariant provides happens-before ordering for the read/write pair per D9 — no atomic load/store needed; no per-stream mutex on the activeProcessingMode field.

**(iii) Bidi-stream single-in-flight-message correlation per parent §5.P10 + SPEC §6.8.** At most ONE outstanding `ProcessingRequest` at any time on the bidi-stream. The `dispatchStage(stage, req)` goroutine performs the Send + Recv pair sequentially within the goroutine (NOT pipelined). The next stage's `dispatchStage` is only invoked AFTER the prior stage's `completeStage` returns + the framework's resume signal advances the chain. This sequential discipline + the framework's sequential decode→encode invariant together guarantee that at most ONE dispatch goroutine is live at any time across the stream's lifetime — the bedrock of the D9 NO-per-stream-mutex race discipline.

**(iv) Mid-stream `mode_override` re-eval per parent §5.P1 RATIFIED-AND-REFINED — header-response paths ONLY.** When `ProcessingResponse.mode_override` arrives in response to a `request_headers` or `response_headers` ProcessingRequest AND `cc.allowModeOverride == true` AND the override mode satisfies the `cc.allowedOverrideModes` allowlist (when non-empty), `f.activeProcessingMode` is replaced with the resolved override per SPEC §6.7 step (iii). `mode_override` arriving on a body-stage or trailer-stage response is silently dropped per the proto-doc "it will be ignored by Envoy" wording — NOT classified as `spurious_msgs_received`. `mode_override` arriving when `allow_mode_override == false` is also silently ignored (proto-doc compliant). The override outside `allowed_override_modes` IS classified as `spurious_msgs_received` per the SPEC §6.7 commentary. The mode_override APPLICATION lives at Task 8 inside `applyProcessingResponse`; the state-machine field types + the per-direction-state invariant are pinned here.

**(v) `max_message_timeout >= 1ms` gates `override_message_timeout` enablement per parent §5.P10 RATIFIED.** The `cc.maxMessageTimeout` field captured at config-load time is the GATE: when `maxMessageTimeout < 1ms` (the proto-default 0), the entire `override_message_timeout` API is DISABLED — any `override_message_timeout` arrival increments `overrideMessageTimeoutIgnored` + returns without effect. When `maxMessageTimeout >= 1ms`, the override is range-checked against `[1ms, maxMessageTimeout]`; out-of-range values increment `overrideMessageTimeoutIgnored` + return without effect. The `handleOverrideMessageTimeout` API is per-stage idempotent: at most ONCE per stage (tracked via the `f.overrideApplied [numStages]bool` array); the SECOND override-arrival at the SAME stage increments `overrideMessageTimeoutIgnored` per the proto-doc "Such message can be sent at most once" constraint. Per-stage independence is preserved — an override at `stageRequestHeaders` does NOT block one at `stageResponseHeaders`.

**(vi) D6 per-stage timer-reset via `context.WithTimeout` cancel-and-rebuild.** The per-message timer is NOT a `time.AfterFunc.Reset()`-driven goroutine — it is a fresh `context.WithTimeout(streamCtx, f.activeMsgTimeout)` per `dispatchStage` Send/Recv pair, with a deferred cancel for resource hygiene. The `handleOverrideMessageTimeout` handler MUTATES `f.activeMsgTimeout` so the NEXT `dispatchStage` invocation observes the new timeout; the in-flight Recv on the CURRENT `dispatchStage` goroutine continues with the ORIGINAL timer until it returns. The cancel-and-rebuild discipline avoids the `time.AfterFunc.Reset()` API's race-prone semantics (per the Go stdlib `time` package's documented Reset gotchas) and aligns with the SPEC §6.8 + ADR-0169 §Decision per-message-timeout discipline. **Per-message timer enforcement: see ADR-0172 §Decision (vii) for the structural-sketch-deferral at 19.1; the per-message `msgCtx` built via `context.WithTimeout` is NOT bound to `stream.Send` / `stream.Recv` at 19.1 (Send/Recv inherit ctx from `Process(ctx)` per the gRPC ClientStream contract); full pre-emption-on-timeout enforcement lands at 19.2 IMPL alongside the body-stage streaming-aware primitive.**

**(vii) STREAMED-only flag PARSE-REJECT per parent §5.P10.** Three top-level `ExternalProcessor` fields are PARSE-REJECTED at config-load time when set (the validation happens in `buildCompiledConfig` at Task 11; the discipline is anchored here in the state-machine ADR because the flags would interact with the state-machine if accepted):

- `observability_mode (#17) = true` — "Send and Go" semantics; STREAMED-coupled; out of envelope per Q2.
- `send_body_without_waiting_for_header_response (#21) = true` — STREAMED-only per proto-doc; out of envelope.
- `deferred_close_timeout (#19) != 0` — observability_mode-coupled per proto-doc; out of envelope.

The PARSE-REJECT discipline is fail-loud per ADR-0168 §Decision — operators get a clear "unsupported configuration" error at boot time rather than silent-ignore-with-divergent-runtime-behavior.

**(viii) `allow_mode_override` + `allowed_override_modes` validation per parent §5.P1 + §5.P9.** The `cc.allowModeOverride bool` (default false; honored verbatim) gates ALL mode_overrides. The `cc.allowedOverrideModes []*resolvedProcessingMode` allowlist (when non-empty) is exact-match-required against the incoming override mode; non-matching overrides classified as `spurious_msgs_received` per the SPEC §6.7 commentary. Each `allowed_override_modes` entry passes through the SAME `resolveProcessingMode` validation as the listener-level `processing_mode` (body-mode != NONE PARSE-REJECT; trailer-mode != SKIP PARSE-REJECT; DEFAULT translation) per parent §5.P9.

**(ix) `(*filter).openProcessorStream` + `(*filter).dispatchStage` + `(*filter).completeStage` per SPEC §6.8.** The bidi-stream is opened lazily at the first `dispatchStage` invocation in gRPC mode (NOT eagerly at filter construction — saves the gRPC dial overhead on per-route-disabled / SKIP-mode requests). `dispatchStage` fires the async goroutine per SPEC §6.8 sketch verbatim; `completeStage` invokes `applyProcessingResponseFn` synchronously inside the goroutine then signals `ContinueDecoding`/`ContinueEncoding` based on the returned `action` enum. The `action` enum has five values: `actContinue` (signal resume; stage complete), `actStop` (defer signal; stage parked for further responses — reserved for 19.2 streaming body), `actError` (signal resume; dispError classified at Task 8), `actImmediate` (NO signal; SendLocalReply emitted; chain handed off per ADR-0085), `actContinueButStillWaiting` (signal resume + continue consuming further responses — reserved for the override_message_timeout reset flow). `applyProcessingResponseFn` is declared as a function VARIABLE (not a plain function) so Task 8 can publish the real body in `check.go` by reassignment at package init — the variable indirection survives the takeover without altering call sites in processor.go.

**(x) `(*filter).OnDestroy` per D9 sync.Once + `f.mu` / `f.done` race-guard discipline.** The `onDestroyImpl` body is sync.Once-guarded for idempotency (multiple OnDestroy invocations + concurrent OnDestroy + dispatch-completion races all converge to the SAME single-execution outcome). Inside the Once: acquire `f.mu`, set `f.done = true`, release `f.mu` — the dispatch goroutine's `completeStage` checks `f.done` under `f.mu` BEFORE signaling resume, so a completion-vs-destroy race resolves deterministically (either the goroutine sees done=true + drops the signal, or signals before OnDestroy sets done — both outcomes valid per the framework's chain-destroyed-after-stream-ends contract). The streamCancel + CloseSend pair fires inside the Once: streamCancel aborts any in-flight Recv (returning context.Canceled promptly); CloseSend is best-effort (the stream may already be closed via streamCancel). `cc.stats.streamsClosed++` (gated `if cc.stats != nil` per ADR-0085).

**§Decision AMENDMENT (phase 19.2):** The 19.2 §Decision AMENDMENT lands at IMPL Task 4 in `internal/filter/http/extproc/processor.go` + `internal/filter/http/extproc/extproc.go` and refines the header-mode-only state-machine + structural-only per-message timer treatment from 19.1:

- **`numStages` 2 → 4 + `stageRequestBody` + `stageResponseBody` added.** The `stage` enum extends with `stageRequestBody` (fires on DecodeData endStream when `RequestBodyMode == BUFFERED`) + `stageResponseBody` (fires on EncodeData endStream when `ResponseBodyMode == BUFFERED`). The flat 4-value enum is the IMPL-time settle of D3's SPLIT-BY-DIRECTION discipline — the planner-time D3 alternative of two 2-valued per-direction enums was rejected for callsite simplicity. The SPLIT-BY-DIRECTION semantics are preserved: decode side tracks `stageRequestHeaders` + `stageRequestBody`; encode side tracks `stageResponseHeaders` + `stageResponseBody`; the at-most-once-per-stage discipline is enforced PER DIRECTION at the dispatch site (each direction emits at most ONE outbound `ProcessingRequest` per stage per stream). The `f.overrideApplied [numStages]bool` array auto-resizes via the sentinel constant.

- **At-most-once-per-stage discipline EXTENDS unchanged.** Each of the 4 stages emits at most one outbound ProcessingRequest per stream; a second arrival at the SAME stage classifies as `spurious_msgs_received++` via the existing 19.1 `applyProcessingResponse` stage-mismatch path. The `handleOverrideMessageTimeout` per-stage idempotency tracking via `f.overrideApplied[stage]` continues — independent per-stage; second `override_message_timeout` at the same stage increments `overrideMessageTimeoutIgnored`.

- **`activeProcessingMode` per-direction body-mode state — reuses existing `resolvedProcessingMode.RequestBodyMode` + `ResponseBodyMode` fields populated at Task 3 (post-ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT — the per-stream `*activeProcessingMode` already carries the raw `BodySendMode` enum).** Per planner-time D2 the body-mode-specific state is per-direction; the IMPL settle is to REUSE the existing `resolvedProcessingMode` carriage (no new `bodyMode BodySendMode` field on the filter struct since `f.activeProcessingMode.RequestBodyMode` / `.ResponseBodyMode` are already populated post-Task-3). The body-buffer pointers (`bodyBuf []byte` per D2) similarly REUSE existing primitives — decode side reads the HCM-level body buffer via ADR-0128 reuse (per DecodeData endStream — the `data` argument IS the full body in BUFFERED mode); encode side reads via `f.ecb.BufferEncodedBody()` per ADR-0175 §Decision (phase-19.2 Task 2). NO new per-direction body-buffer fields land on the filter struct at Task 4; the body-stage dispatch envelope at Task 5 + Task 7 consumes the primitives directly. The IMPL-settle preserves ADR-0168 §Decision (xi) field-final invariant on the listener-level `compiledConfig` AND adds only ONE new field on the per-stream `filter` struct: `activeMsgCancel context.CancelFunc` (see per-message timer behavioral lift below).

- **`mode_override` header-response-paths-only refinement carries unchanged at 19.2** per parent §5.P1 RATIFIED-AND-REFINED. The `applyProcessingResponse` Step 3 mode_override dispatcher checks `isHeaderResponseStage(s)` which continues to return `true` ONLY for `stageRequestHeaders` + `stageResponseHeaders` (the body stages return `false`); `mode_override` arriving on a body-stage response is SILENT-DROPPED — NOT classified as `spurious_msgs_received`. The body-stage `CommonResponse` extraction extends at Task 4 (`stageRequestBody` reads `resp.GetRequestBody().GetResponse()`; `stageResponseBody` reads `resp.GetResponseBody().GetResponse()`) so a well-formed body-stage response (CommonResponse-only, mode_override-only, or both) is NOT mis-classified as stage-mismatch. The `body_mutation` arm of the body-stage CommonResponse is CONSUMED at Task 6 (ADR-0172 §Decision AMENDMENT); Task 4 only lands the extraction switch (no body_mutation handling).

- **Per-message timer BEHAVIORAL ENFORCEMENT lifts via `context.WithTimeout(f.streamCtx, f.activeMsgTimeout)` cancel-and-rebuild per planner-time D4 + parent §5.P5.** The 19.1 §Decision clause (vi) noted that the per-message `msgCtx` built via `context.WithTimeout` was NOT bound to `stream.Send` / `stream.Recv` at 19.1 (structural-only treatment per Carryforward O at 19.1 Task 14 — Send/Recv inherited ctx from `Process(ctx)` per the gRPC ClientStream contract). The 19.2 lift makes the per-message timer BEHAVIORAL via a WATCHDOG goroutine pattern:
   - `dispatchStage` builds `msgCtx, msgCancel = context.WithTimeout(streamCtx, f.activeMsgTimeout)` on each Send/Recv pair; deferred `msgCancel` releases the timer on goroutine exit.
   - `msgCancel` is PUBLISHED on `f.activeMsgCancel` (under `f.mu`) so `handleOverrideMessageTimeout` can fire it on override-accept.
   - A watchdog goroutine selects on `msgCtx.Done()` vs a `doneCh` close: on `msgCtx.Done()` (per-message timer expiry OR override-driven cancel) the watchdog fires `f.streamCancel()` which cascade-cancels the bidi-stream (terminating the in-flight Recv with `context.Canceled` per the gRPC ClientStream contract); on `doneCh` close (Recv completed normally) the watchdog exits without touching streamCancel. The watchdog NEVER blocks past the per-stage lifetime.
   - The Send + Recv pair stays on the SAME dispatchStage goroutine — preserves the parent §5.P10 single-in-flight-message-correlation invariant + the 19.1 race-test discipline (`TestSequentialDecodeEncodeDispatchNoRace` + `TestBidiStreamSendRecvDiscipline`'s "Send GID == Recv GID" assertions).
   - Single rolling timer per direction (NOT per-stage): the at-most-one-in-flight invariant per clause (v) makes per-stage timers redundant. Each stage's `dispatchStage` invocation rebuilds the per-message timer from the current `f.activeMsgTimeout` value.
   - **`override_message_timeout` reset path extends naturally**: `handleOverrideMessageTimeout` on accept mutates `f.activeMsgTimeout` for the NEXT dispatchStage AND fires the captured `f.activeMsgCancel` to cascade-cancel the in-flight per-message timer. The dispatch goroutine observes `msgCtx.Done` via the watchdog → streamCancel → Recv unblocks with context.Canceled; the NEXT dispatchStage Send/Recv pair builds a fresh msgCtx with the override duration. The stream-level cascade is the accepted trade-off — the bidi-stream is one-shot per HTTP transaction; a per-message timer expiry IS the stream-level failure surface. **Trade-off accepted (clarification post-Task-4 code-review I-1):** invoking the in-flight per-message cancel cascades through the watchdog goroutine to `streamCancel`, terminating the WHOLE bidi-stream (`override_message_timeout`-driven cancel is therefore stream-fatal, NOT per-stage). The "single rolling timer per direction" applies within the per-stream scope; the rebuild-with-override-duration semantic applies to the NEXT-STREAM scope (if reopened by a subsequent request) — there is NO "next dispatchStage on the current stream" observing the override duration because the stream is dead by then. Justification: the bidi-stream is one-shot per HTTP transaction per ADR-0167 §Decision; at-most-one-in-flight per ADR-0171 §Decision (v) makes the stream-fatal cascade the right granularity; the alternative (per-stage Recv interruption without canceling the stream) would require breaking the Send/Recv-same-goroutine invariant that 19.1's `TestSequentialDecodeEncodeDispatchNoRace` + `TestBidiStreamSendRecvDiscipline` assert.

- **`OnDestroy` discipline extends naturally to body-stage Send/Recv goroutines per planner-time D7.** When `OnDestroy` fires during a parked body-stage outbound, `f.streamCancel()` propagates through `ctx.Done()` to the body-stage Send/Recv goroutine, which returns WITHOUT calling `ContinueDecoding`/`ContinueEncoding` per the existing 19.1 D9 race-guard (`f.mu` + `f.done`). The chain dispatch tears down WITHOUT the buffer-release call firing; the per-direction body buffer pointers (decode side: HCM-level body buffer; encode side: chain-level `encodeBuf` per ADR-0175) are reclaimed by GC when the per-stream state goes out of scope. No new race-guard primitive needed at 19.2; the Task 4 IMPL adds ONE new mutex-guarded field (`f.activeMsgCancel`) for the per-message timer cancel hook, which extends the existing `f.mu` discipline.

- **19.1 §12 deferred decision #6 CLOSES at this AMENDMENT.** The 19.1 §12 deferred-decision #6 ("per-message timer enforcement deferred to 19.2 IMPL alongside the body-stage streaming-aware primitive") closes here — 19.2 IMPL Task 4 lands the behavioral enforcement via the `context.WithTimeout` + watchdog pattern documented above. Per parent §5.P5: single rolling timer per direction (NOT per-stage); cancel-and-rebuild on each stage's Send.

### Consequences

**§Decision AMENDED at phase-19.2 IMPL — clauses refreshed post-AMENDMENT.** The phase-19.2 IMPL Task 4 landed the §Decision AMENDMENT (above); the §Consequences refresh below reconciles the AMENDMENT with the original 19.1 anticipatory forward-pointers:

- The `*_body_mode = BUFFERED` PARSE-REJECT in `resolveProcessingMode` clause (i) lifted at 19.2 Task 3 (ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT) for `BUFFERED` only (STREAMED + BUFFERED_PARTIAL + FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED continue PARSE-REJECT permanently). The struct shape of `*resolvedProcessingMode` stays UNCHANGED — only the validation logic relaxed.

- The body-stage state-machine extension landed at 19.2 Task 4 (the AMENDMENT above): `stage` enum gained `stageRequestBody` + `stageResponseBody` entries; `numStages` incremented from 2 to 4 (the `f.overrideApplied [numStages]bool` array auto-resized via the sentinel constant). **Reconciliation of the original 19.1 §Consequences anticipation**: the 19.1 §Consequences anticipated `numStages` could extend up to 6 (the original wording in `processor.go`'s `stage` enum comment said "Body + trailer stages reserve indices [numStages..numStages+4)" — implying body + trailer arms would each contribute 2 entries × 2 directions = 4 reserved slots, for a total of 6). The actual 19.2 lift is `2 → 4` (body stages only). Trailer stages REMAIN reserved-but-out-of-envelope per parent §5.P9 + ADR-0168 §Decision (trailer arms PARSE-REJECT permanently — trailers never reach the dispatch path); the trailer-stage enum entries would land ONLY IF the trailer-mode PARSE-REJECT lifts in some hypothetical future scope expansion (no current envelope plan). The processor.go comment was refreshed at 19.2 Task 4 to document the `2 → 4` actual versus the `2 → 6` anticipation; the §Consequences forward-pointer drift is now closed.

- The `dispatchStage` + `completeStage` bodies stay STRUCTURALLY UNCHANGED at 19.2 — the body-stage dispatch reuses the same Send/Recv discipline + the same `applyProcessingResponseFn` indirection. The 19.2 `body_mutation` + `CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` handling lives at ADR-0172 §Decision AMENDMENT inside `applyProcessingResponse`; no new state-machine primitives at processor.go beyond the AMENDMENT clauses above (per-message timer behavioral lift + activeMsgCancel field + watchdog goroutine pattern). The `applyProcessingResponse` CommonResponse extraction switch extends at Task 4 with `stageRequestBody` + `stageResponseBody` arms (extracting `BodyResponse.Response`) so body-stage responses are NOT mis-classified as stage-mismatch; the body_mutation arm of the extracted CommonResponse is left UNCONSUMED at Task 4 (lands at Task 6).

- The `signalResume` switch extends at 19.2 Task 4 to cover the body stages: decode stages (`stageRequestHeaders` + `stageRequestBody`) signal `ContinueDecoding`; encode stages (`stageResponseHeaders` + `stageResponseBody`) signal `ContinueEncoding`. The per-direction resume primitive is REUSED unchanged — body stages share the SAME resume callback as their header counterpart per parent §5.P10 SPEC §6.8 invariant (one resume signal per parked stage's outbound).

**Cross-phase-reusable D9 race discipline (NO per-stream mutex on the bidi-stream surface).** The discipline:

- The framework's sequential decode→encode dispatch invariant guarantees that at most ONE filter-side goroutine is live at any time during the per-stream lifecycle (the dispatch goroutine OR the framework chain goroutine, never both concurrently except across the resume-signal handoff).
- The bidi-stream's single-in-flight-message correlation rule guarantees that at most ONE dispatch goroutine is live at any time per stream.
- The gRPC ClientStream Send-vs-Recv concurrent-safety contract (per the gRPC documentation) covers the goroutine's own Send + Recv sequencing — the gRPC library handles the internal HTTP/2 framing concurrency.
- OnDestroy uses sync.Once to make the streamCancel + CloseSend pair idempotent against concurrent OnDestroy invocations.
- The existing `f.mu` / `f.done` pair (anchored at Task 2 skeleton; exercised at Task 7 + Task 12 race tests) covers the resume-after-OnDestroy race surface — completeStage drops the resume signal if `f.done == true`, OnDestroy sets `f.done = true` under `f.mu` before invoking streamCancel.

The discipline is cross-phase-reusable for any future bidi-stream filter — the FIRST §9 family-row to articulate the discipline; subsequent bidi-stream filters (a hypothetical streaming OAuth2 token-refresh filter, a streaming metrics extension, etc.) consume the discipline verbatim. The discipline is mechanically composable: any future filter combining bidi-stream + ADR-0085 SendLocalReply (the deny-path framework primitive) inherits the same race-safety properties without re-paying the per-stream-mutex cost.

**Task 7 IMPL-time settle: `applyProcessingResponseFn` function-variable indirection.** The Task 7 IMPL chose to declare `applyProcessingResponseFn` as a `var` (function variable) rather than a plain function so:

- Task 7 can install a TEMPORARY STUB returning `(actError, errProcessorStub)` deterministically — any test that does NOT explicitly override the stub gets a clear sentinel-error failure pinning the unimplemented contract.
- Group 7 tests install per-test overrides (capturing args + returning deterministic action returns) to drive completeStage assertions without dragging in the Task 8 CommonResponse / header-mutation / ImmediateResponse surface.
- Task 8 publishes the real body in `check.go` by reassigning the variable at package init OR by declaring its own non-stub function and reassigning at init time. The variable indirection survives the Task 8 takeover without altering call sites in processor.go — a clean Task 7 → Task 8 handoff.

This indirection is a NEW pattern in the envoy-go DECISIONS log — the FIRST forward-staged-function-variable in the codebase (prior tasks all used inline stubs or sentinel-returning function bodies that the next task replaced in-place). The pattern is cross-phase-reusable for any future multi-task IMPL where a task lands the dispatcher infrastructure but a subsequent task lands the dispatcher's substantive body; the pattern avoids the merge-conflict surface of in-place function-body replacement at the cost of one indirection per call.

**Cross-phase reuse intent for the `action` enum.** The five-value `action` enum (actContinue / actStop / actError / actImmediate / actContinueButStillWaiting) is the FIRST stage-dispatch-action enum in the envoy-go filters. Future bidi-stream filters with multi-stage state-machines reuse the same enum shape — the 5-value taxonomy captures the canonical post-stage decisions (continue + park + error + immediate-emit + park-but-resume). The `actStop` arm is reserved for 19.2 streaming body; the `actContinueButStillWaiting` arm is reserved for the override_message_timeout reset flow per parent §5.P10. The discipline strengthens ADR-0167's bidi-stream-lifecycle framing — ADR-0167 owns the LIFECYCLE; ADR-0171 owns the per-stage DISPATCH semantics; ADR-0172 owns the per-response APPLICATION semantics. The triplet (ADR-0167 + ADR-0171 + ADR-0172) covers the bidi-stream filter end-to-end.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at Task 7.** ADR-0171 §Decision header-mode portion + §Consequences anchored at this commit; D12 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.1 IMPL beyond the 8 anticipated) UNCHANGED. The IMPL-time `applyProcessingResponseFn` function-variable indirection is a tactical implementation choice (documented above) that does NOT warrant a new ADR — it is an IMPL-level concern per ADR-0044's "documentation-of-application" framing. ADR-0177 stays unconsumed. The body-mode AMENDMENT path at phase-19.2 is documented above; no in-place §Decision edits at 19.1.
