## ADR-0172: CommonResponse mutation + ImmediateResponse multi-stage deny discipline — `header_mutation` set/remove per direction per stage (HEADER-MODE PORTION); `body_mutation` body/clear via ADR-0128 decode-side + NEW ADR-0175 encode-side at 19.2 (BODY-MODE PORTION); `status` CONTINUE/CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE (CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE at 19.2); `clear_route_cache` + `route_cache_action` precedence (request-headers stage only per §5.P5); `ImmediateResponse{status, headers, body, grpc_status, details}` multi-stage deny via `SendLocalReply` + grpc_status content-type sniff per §5.P2; `mutation_rules` per-header gating per §5.P3; records `CommonResponse.dynamic_metadata` + `CommonResponse.trailers` deferrals

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention; §Decision lands at 19.1 IMPL (header-mode portion); §Decision AMENDMENT lands at phase-19.2 Task 6 to add body-mode portion — see §Decision AMENDMENT below).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 + 19.2 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
**Lands-in:** Task 6 of phase-19.1 PLAN (header_mutation + ImmediateResponse-at-headers portion); Task 6 of phase-19.2 IMPL (body_mutation + CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE + body-stage ImmediateResponse §Decision AMENDMENT).

### Context

`ProcessingResponse` carries the processor's per-stage response. The `CommonResponse` substructure has 5 fields per parent SPEC §5.P1: `status` (CONTINUE / CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE enum), `header_mutation` (set_headers + remove_headers), `body_mutation` (oneof body bytes / clear_body bool / streamed_response — the last arm PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict permanently since STREAMED is out of envelope), `trailers` (HeaderMap — `[#not-implemented-hide:]` per the proto; DEFERRED), `clear_route_cache` (bool).

**`header_mutation` per-direction per-stage application** (HEADER-MODE PORTION in 19.1):
- request_headers stage's CommonResponse.header_mutation applies to the DECODE-side request headers via `f.dcb.RequestHeaders().Set/Add/Del` (or framework analog).
- response_headers stage's CommonResponse.header_mutation applies to the ENCODE-side response headers via `f.ecb.ResponseHeaders().Set/Add/Del`.
- `set_headers` is `[]*core.HeaderValueOption` carrying an `append_action` enum (`APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD`, `OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD`, `OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS`, `ADD_IF_ABSENT`) — the IMPL settles the 4-arm dispatch per the phase-18.2 ext_authz `OkHttpResponse.headers` precedent + the phase-10 header_mutation enum-handling.
- `remove_headers` is `[]string` — drop wholesale.
- `mutation_rules` per-header gating applies (parent §5.P3): each individual mutation is validated; rejected mutations dropped + `spurious_msgs_received` counter increment ONCE per stage with any rejection.

**`body_mutation` per-direction per-stage application** (BODY-MODE PORTION at 19.2):
- `body_mutation.body` (bytes): REPLACE the body wholesale (only valid when the corresponding body_mode is BUFFERED; combined with `status = CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` for full-message-replacement).
- `body_mutation.clear_body` (bool): CLEAR the body wholesale.
- `body_mutation.streamed_response`: PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict (STREAMED is out of envelope per Q2; the FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED arm of BodySendMode is also out of envelope; the proto doc explicitly couples this body_mutation arm to FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED).
- Decode-side body replacement uses the existing phase-13 ADR-0128 body-buffering primitive (already accumulates request body in `DataStopIterationAndBuffer`).
- Encode-side body replacement uses the NEW ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive (§5.P11 REFUTED at SPEC time — the framework gap is confirmed).

**`status` CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE handling** (at 19.2):
- `CONTINUE` (default): apply header_mutation + body_mutation in the standard way; the stream continues.
- `CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE`: full replacement — the processor has built a complete substitute message; header_mutation set_headers becomes the FULL header set (existing headers other than those preserved by allow-list are dropped); body_mutation.body becomes the FULL body. Effectively: turn a GET into a POST/PUT/PATCH, or build a synthetic response. Honored ONLY at the header stages (request_headers / response_headers); body-stage CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE is structurally invalid (the body has already been consumed; classified as `spurious_msgs_received`). 19.1 PARSE-REJECTs the CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE status (silent-classify as `spurious_msgs_received` + dispError) since body-mode is OUT in 19.1; 19.2 IMPL activates the proper handling.

**`clear_route_cache` + `route_cache_action` precedence** (per parent §5.P5 RATIFIED):
- The two top-level fields (`disable_clear_route_cache` + `route_cache_action`) are mutually exclusive at parse time → PARSE-REJECT.
- `route_cache_action` enum: `DEFAULT (0)` = clear-only-if-`CommonResponse.clear_route_cache`-set; `CLEAR (1)` = always-clear; `RETAIN (2)` = never-clear.
- `disable_clear_route_cache: true` is equivalent to `route_cache_action: RETAIN` (per proto enum doc); IMPL translates at parse time.
- **Applied ONLY at the request_headers stage** (per the `RouteCacheAction` enum doc + the proto-doc "This field is ignored in the response direction" on `CommonResponse.clear_route_cache`); body-stage and response-stage `CommonResponse.clear_route_cache` arrivals are silently dropped.
- The route-cache-clear emission goes through the existing `cb.ClearRouteCache()` HCM-side primitive (already used by phase-10 header_mutation + phase-17 jwt_authn).

**`ImmediateResponse` multi-stage deny discipline** (per parent §5.P2 RATIFIED):
- `ImmediateResponse` can arrive in response to ANY stage's ProcessingRequest — request_headers + (request_body at 19.2) + response_headers + (response_body at 19.2). FIRST §9 row whose deny-path is multi-stage.
- `status` (`*type.v3.HttpStatus`, PGV-required) — the response code (e.g., 403, 500).
- `headers` is `*HeaderMutation` (NOT a plain `[]HeaderValueOption` like phase-18.2 `DeniedHttpResponse.headers`) — the IMPL applies SET+REMOVE via `set_headers` + `remove_headers`. `mutation_rules` per-header gating applies.
- `body` (`[]byte`) — the response body. The proto doc states "sent using the text/plain content type, or encoded in the grpc-message header" — the IMPL applies content-type discipline based on a `content-type: application/grpc` request-header sniff (NOT via `DownstreamProtocol()` which returns HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2): non-gRPC downstream → body with `content-type: text/plain` (unless overridden); gRPC downstream → body encoded into the `grpc-message` response header.
- `grpc_status` (`*GrpcStatus{status uint32}`) — when non-nil AND the downstream is gRPC, add a `grpc-status: <status>` response trailer; when downstream is non-gRPC, IGNORED.
- `details` (`string`) — maps to `response_code_details` — DEFERRED (envoy-go HCM does not surface response_code_details; joint divergence-window with phase-16/17/18 forward-pointers).
- The local-reply emission goes through `SendLocalReply` per ADR-0085 + the per-direction callback surface (`f.dcb.SendLocalReply` for decode stages; `f.ecb.SendLocalReply` for encode stages). The framework's `SendLocalReply` enters the encode chain at `filter[len-1]` per ADR-0075, supporting multi-stage emission seamlessly.
- `disable_immediate_response: true` configuration silently drops ImmediateResponse messages (treated as protocol violation; `spurious_msgs_received` increments; stream continues without local reply emission).

**DEFERRED fields recorded:**
- `CommonResponse.trailers` (`[#not-implemented-hide:]` proto-flag) — silent-ignore per the not-implemented convention.
- `ProcessingResponse.dynamic_metadata` — dynamic-metadata family (blocked at phases 16+17+18 forward-pointers; ext_proc EXTENDS the cluster).

References: parent SPEC §4.1 + §5.P2 + §5.P3 + §5.P5 + §6 amendments 2 + 3 + 5. 19.1 SPEC §4 + §6.7. ADR-0085 (`SendLocalReply` framework primitive). ADR-0128 (decode-side body-buffering — reused for `request_body_mode = BUFFERED` at 19.2). ADR-0175 (encode-side body-buffering — fires at 19.2).

### Decision

The Task 8 IMPL settles the header-mode portion of the §Context-drafted ADR-0172 contract via the following sub-clauses (the body-mode portion lands at 19.2 IMPL per the ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl AMENDMENT path):

**(i) `applyProcessingResponse` per-stage dispatcher** lives in `internal/filter/http/extproc/check.go` and is installed onto the Task 7 function-variable `applyProcessingResponseFn` via an explicit `func init()` block per the Carryforward C wiring (race-safe per Go spec §"Package initialization" — package init runs in a single goroutine before any other goroutine can observe the variable). The dispatcher executes the 7-step sequence per SPEC §6.7 in the exact order: (1) ImmediateResponse short-circuit; (2) override_message_timeout delegation; (3) mode_override re-eval; (4) CommonResponse extraction; (5) applyHeaderMutation per direction; (6) clear_route_cache / route_cache_action precedence (request_headers stage ONLY); (7) CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE → spurious + dispError per D7. The dispatcher returns a 5-value action enum per ADR-0171: actContinue (happy path) / actImmediate (ImmediateResponse) / actError (stage-mismatch or CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE) / actStop (reserved 19.2) / actContinueButStillWaiting (override_message_timeout — see clause (vi) Carryforward B disposition).

**(ii) `applyHeaderMutation` per-direction apply with per-header `mutation_rules` gating** per parent §5.P3. The 4-arm `append_action` switch dispatches per the phase-10 header_mutation + phase-18.2 ext_authz precedent (APPEND_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD → headers.Add; OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD → headers.Set; OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS → headers.Set iff name exists; ADD_IF_ABSENT → headers.Add iff name absent). At 19.1 the substantive header-mutation application against the in-flight headers is **deferred to Task 11 buildCompiledConfig integration** when the `dcb.RequestHeaders()` / `ecb.ResponseHeaders()` framework analogs are wired — the Task 8 implementation performs the mutation_rules gating + the 4-arm switch dispatch + tracks the rejection count, but the actual `headers.Set/Add/Del` call site lands at Task 11. The gating-and-rejection-count discipline (the parent §5.P3 RATIFIED ONCE-per-stage spurious counter) is exercised + tested at Task 8; the chain-level injection is exercised at Task 11.

**(iii) `resolveMutationRules` compiles `*v31.HeaderMutationRules` into the protected-set boolean carrier** per parent §5.P3. The four boolean wrappers (`allow_all_routing` / `allow_envoy` / `disallow_system` / `disallow_all`) are pre-compiled onto the `*resolvedMutationRules` struct directly — Task 8 PROMOTES the Task 2 empty placeholder struct to carry the four boolean fields (the field promotion is race-safe because `compiledConfig` is immutable post-buildCompiledConfig per ADR-0101, so the rules struct is read-only + safe to share across all per-stream goroutines + per-stage dispatch invocations). The TestSkeletonReachability anchor at Task 2 only references the type (`_ resolvedMutationRules`), not specific fields, so the promotion does not break the anchor. The PGV regex-matcher fields (`allow_expression` / `disallow_expression`) are SILENT-IGNORED at 19.1 for IMPL-simplicity — the 19.1 fixture scope does not exercise regex-driven per-header overrides; the regex-matcher promotion is reserved for an IMPL-time AMENDMENT path if a fixture pins the gap. The proto's `disallow_is_error` wrapper is IGNORED at envoy-go-strict — parent §5.P3 RATIFIED classifies all rejected mutations as `spurious_msgs_received++` + drop regardless (envoy-go does NOT 500-on-rejected-mutation; the proto's per-rule discipline maps onto envoy-go's monotonic-counter-only convention).

**(iv) `emitImmediateResponse` translates `*ImmediateResponse` arrivals into `SendLocalReply`** per ADR-0167 + ADR-0085 + parent §5.P2. The decode-stage (stageRequestHeaders) emits via `f.dcb.SendLocalReply`; the encode-stage (stageResponseHeaders) ALSO routes via `f.dcb.SendLocalReply` since the framework's `SendLocalReply` enters the encode chain at `filter[len-1]` per ADR-0075 and the BOTH-decode-and-encode filter per ADR-0167 carries f.dcb non-nil throughout the per-stream lifetime. **This is the FIRST §9 row to emit `SendLocalReply` from the encode side at the response_headers stage** per ADR-0167 (phase-14 compressor is encode-only but does NOT emit local replies; all prior §9 rows are decode-only emitters). The gRPC-downstream-detection sniff per parent §5.P2 reads `f.requestContentType == "application/grpc"` (the field exists on `*filter` per Task 2 skeleton; the real capture-site lands at Task 11 DecodeHeaders body): on gRPC downstream, the ImmediateResponse body routes into the `grpc-message` response header + content-type → `application/grpc`; non-gRPC routes body verbatim with content-type → `text/plain` fallback.

**(v) `grpc_status` emission caveat (19.1 SPEC-divergence)**: the existing `SendLocalReply` primitive does NOT carry trailers across the OrderedHeaders surface (the framework's local-reply path is single-shot per ADR-0085; trailers are an HTTP/2-only wire feature). At 19.1 the grpc-status field is emitted as a HEADER instead of a trailer — a pragmatic 19.1 divergence from the parent SPEC §5.P2 wording. The 19.1 fixture asserts grpc-status in the response headers; the trailer-emission path is reserved for a future ADR / 19.2 IF the framework grows a `SendLocalReply`-with-trailers primitive (the divergence-window is itself a recorded decision — no ADR-0044 escape-valve fires at Task 8 since the 19.1 acceptance gate does not require trailers).

**(vi) Carryforward B disposition — `actContinueButStillWaiting` arm RETAINED**: the override_message_timeout response branch in `applyProcessingResponse` returns `actContinueButStillWaiting` (NOT actContinue) per the SPEC §6.7 sketch. The dispatcher's `completeStage` (processor.go) treats it equivalently to `actContinue` AT 19.1 (signaling resume on the parked stage) because the in-flight Recv on the dispatchStage goroutine cannot be reset mid-flight without canceling the stream (gRPC ClientStream Send/Recv don't accept per-call ctx; the streamCtx-rebuild approach would terminate the whole stream). The structural distinction is preserved for 19.2 streaming body re-dispatch — when the body stages activate, a streaming body response may legitimately carry override_message_timeout BEFORE the substantive CommonResponse, and the dispatcher will need to re-Recv on the same stream rather than signal resume. At 19.1 the structural distinction is a no-op at the dispatcher; at 19.2 it becomes load-bearing. The arm + its semantics are documented in the action enum doc-comment + the `applyProcessingResponse` doc-comment.

**(vii) Carryforward D disposition — per-message timer enforcement is STRUCTURAL ONLY at 19.1**: Task 7's `dispatchStage` builds a per-message `msgCtx` via `context.WithTimeout(f.streamCtx, perMessageTimeout)` but does NOT bind it to `stream.Send` / `stream.Recv` (which inherit ctx from `Process(ctx)` at stream-open per the gRPC ClientStream contract — Send/Recv do not accept per-call ctx). The Task 8 disposition picks option (b) from the BOOTSTRAP carryforward: **NO code change in processor.go**; this ADR §Consequences and the Task 8 PROGRESS entry note the per-message timer is a structural sketch at 19.1 — actual enforcement defers to a future ADR / 19.2 IMPL. The option (a) alternative (a `time.AfterFunc(perMessageTimeout, f.streamCancel)` started before Recv; reset/stopped on Recv-complete; on fire → `streamCancel()` aborts the stream + maps to dispError+streamsFailed++) is deferred because: (1) the 19.1 fixture scope does not exercise the per-message timeout enforcement directly (the SPEC's `message_timeout` discipline lives in the test-harness fixture's processor-server behavior, not in the dispatcher's pre-emption path); (2) the 19.2 IMPL has more comprehensive per-message timer surface (body-stage streaming changes the Recv pattern; a per-message AfterFunc may not be the right primitive once body streaming arrives — better to design the primitive ONCE for the 19.2 streaming-aware case than to ship a 19.1 stop-gap that 19.2 has to rewrite). The disposition is documented at the PROGRESS Task 8 entry + at the `dispatchStage` doc-comment in processor.go (no doc edit at Task 8 — the existing Task 7 doc-comment is structurally accurate; the gap is documented in the PROGRESS entry only per option (b)'s "doc-only amendment" framing).

**(viii) `buildGRPCProcessorClient` constructor per SPEC §6.5 + ADR-0157 §Decision AMENDMENT + ADR-0169** — mirrors phase-18.2 buildGRPCCheckFn: GoogleGrpc arm PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict (envoy-go uses google.golang.org/grpc directly); EnvoyGrpc.cluster_name PGV-mirror (non-empty); cluster-manager lookup + UseH2() gate; `grpcclient.NewProcessorClient(dialer, clusterName, messageTimeout)` construction. `initial_metadata` + `retry_policy` SILENT-IGNORED per ADR-0169 (processor-server designers may set them in their config files for forward-compat without envoy-go PARSE-REJECT).

**(ix) `buildHTTPProcessorClient` constructor per SPEC §6.5** — validates the `*ExtProcHttpService.HttpService.HttpUri.Uri` field is set + non-empty (PARSE-REJECT on empty); constructs `*http.Client{Timeout: http_uri.timeout}` (zero timeout = no timeout per the proto default); captures the base URL. **Proto-field-name correction**: the SPEC §6.5 sketch referenced `server_uri` (a drafting carry-over from auth-filter terminology); the actual `ExtProcHttpService` proto at `go-control-plane v1.32.4` exposes `http_service.http_uri` (NOT `server_uri`). The 19.1 IMPL captures only the base URL from `http_uri.uri`; the `path_prefix` field referenced in the SPEC §6.5 sketch does NOT exist on the proto in 19.1 (the SPEC's reference anticipated a richer proto shape). The per-stage POST URL is constructed at the dispatcher (Task 11 wires the call site) as the bare base URL with the per-stage path-suffix derived from the stage discriminator. `httpProcessorClient.Close()` invokes `Transport.CloseIdleConnections()` (best-effort; nil-tolerant per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance).

**(x) `mapTransportError` failure-mode dispatch per SPEC §4 + parent §5.P11 + D5** — the per-stage transport / unmarshal / per-message-timeout error classification. `failure_mode_allow=false` (proto default): emit `SendLocalReply(500, "", nil)` on the request_headers branch; `SendLocalReply(0, "", nil)` on the response_headers branch as the stream-reset signal per phase-04 + ADR-0085; `streamsFailed++` (already incremented at the dispatchStage Recv-error path in processor.go); return actImmediate so the dispatcher does NOT signal resume (the local-reply handoff supersedes the chain). `failure_mode_allow=true`: silent-continue + `failureModeAllowed++`; return actContinue so the resume path fires + the framework chain proceeds normally. The substantive consumer call site (the dispatchStage's completeStage's recvErr-bearing path) routes through `mapTransportError` at Task 11 buildCompiledConfig integration when the failure-mode dispatch enters the production code path; the Task 8 wiring is structural + tested via Group 9 fixtures.

### Decision AMENDMENT (phase 19.2)

The 19.1 §Decision body above ANCHORED the 7-step `applyProcessingResponse` dispatcher with the header-mode portion only — the `body_mutation` arm + the body-stage `ImmediateResponse` arm + the `CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` arm at body stages were all RESERVED for the 19.2 IMPL per the §Decision (i) "the body-mode portion lands at 19.2 IMPL per the ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl AMENDMENT path" forward-pointer + the §Consequences "§Decision AMENDED at 19.2 for body-mode portion" anchor. Phase 19.2 Task 6 lands the AMENDMENT in-place per ADR-0044's in-place §Decision edit convention. The AMENDMENT supplies four sub-clauses + retires one 19.1 sentinel:

**(xi) `body_mutation` oneof switch CONSUMED per SPEC §4.2** — the per-stage CommonResponse.body_mutation oneof is now dispatched via `applyBodyMutation(f, s, bm)` (new helper in check.go, ~30 LoC):

  - **`*BodyMutation_Body` arm** — replaces the per-direction body buffer (decode side: `f.decodeBodyBuf`; encode side: `f.encodeBodyBuf`) with the processor-supplied bytes via `writeBodyMutation(f, s, newBody)`. Content-Length reconciliation per ADR-0128 §Decision (decode side) + ADR-0175 §Decision (encode side): when `len(newBody)` differs from the prior buffered body length, `Content-Length` on the corresponding header set (`f.decodeHeaders` / `f.encodeHeaders`) is updated via `header.Set("content-length", strconv.Itoa(len(newBody)))`. nil-tolerant on the header carrier (synthetic / test paths that did not invoke DecodeHeaders / EncodeHeaders).
  - **`*BodyMutation_ClearBody` (true) arm** — empties the body buffer + Content-Length: 0 via the same `writeBodyMutation` path with `newBody = nil`. **`*BodyMutation_ClearBody` (false)** is a no-op per the proto's "treated as no-op" framing (the buffer + headers unchanged).
  - **`*BodyMutation_StreamedResponse` arm** — PARSE-REJECT per planner-time D6 + SPEC §4.2 row 3: increments `spurious_msgs_received` + returns `actError` + `errStreamedResponseBodyMutationUnsupported` sentinel with the verbatim D6 wording `"ext_proc: streamed_response body mutation not supported (STREAMED body modes out-of-envelope per parent §4.4)"`. STREAMED body modes are out-of-envelope permanently per parent §4.4 deferred-field discipline; the malformed-response classification follows ADR-0172 §Decision (iv) discipline.

  The body-buffer write is an in-place slice-header replacement on the per-direction filter field. **Body-buffer write strategy** (Task 6 planner-time choice): the alternative options were (a) introduce a new `OverwriteEncodedBuffer(b []byte)` framework primitive on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` (would consume `ADR-0177` + falsify D10) OR (b) defer body-write to Task 7 via a "pending body replacement" carrier field. Task 6 picks neither: the per-direction `decodeBodyBuf` / `encodeBodyBuf` `[]byte` fields on the *filter struct serve as both the pre-mutation stash (populated by Task 7's DecodeData / EncodeData endStream entry) AND the post-mutation carrier (read by Task 7's resume path before releasing the body downstream). The framework primitive for actually emitting the post-mutation buffer downstream is the EXISTING `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(b []byte)` per ADR-0131 (encode side) on the resume path — at Task 7's body-stage integration, the resume handler reads `f.encodeBodyBuf` + invokes `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(f.encodeBodyBuf)` inside the EncodeData callback. Decode side: the analogous per-chain decode-buffer mutation is reserved for Task 7 wire-up (the framework's decode-side buffer-then-release discipline per ADR-0128 already handles per-call replacement via similar mechanisms). **No new framework primitive lands at Task 6**; D10 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.2 IMPL beyond ADR-0175 + the three AMENDMENTS) HOLDS.

**(xii) `CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` stage-aware dispatch per SPEC §4.3 table** — replaces the 19.1 single-arm spurious-dispatch with the per-stage three-arm switch:

  - **Header stages + body-mode = NONE**: CONSUMED as no-op for body (header_mutation at Step 5 already applied; no body to replace). The 19.1 spurious-dispatch LIFTS — no counter increment + no error + `actContinue`. The 19.1 SPEC §12 deferred decision #7 (`CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` handling) CLOSED at 19.2 SPEC time per SPEC §4.3 + IMPL-confirmed here.
  - **Header stages + body-mode = BUFFERED**: CONSUMED as combined header+body replacement. header_mutation (at Step 5) + body_mutation (at Step 5.5) BOTH apply during the same dispatch turn; the body-stage outbound dispatch MUST be SKIPPED on the next DecodeData/EncodeData entry since the body is already in flight via the header-stage response. The dispatcher sets `f.skipBodyStageDispatch[direction]` (a new `[2]bool` field on *filter struct — index 0 = request, index 1 = response) and returns `actContinueButStillWaiting` per SPEC §4.3 row 2 transition note. **Task 7 contract**: the body-stage entry point (DecodeData / EncodeData endStream) checks `f.skipBodyStageDispatch[direction]` BEFORE invoking the body-stage dispatchStage; when set, the body-stage outbound call is skipped + the (pre-replaced) body buffer is released directly to the chain via `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(f.encodeBodyBuf)` (encode side) / decode-side analog. The `actContinueButStillWaiting` return signals the header-stage dispatcher that the stream "continues to the next stage but the next stage's outbound is suppressed" — completeStage already treats this equivalently to actContinue per Carryforward B (clause (vi)).
  - **Body stages (request_body / response_body)**: TREATED AS CONTINUE per the proto's "ignored at body stages" wording + the race-avoidance rationale at SPEC §1 item 4 (the body is already in flight; replacement would race with the buffered-body release path). No counter increment — the proto silently ignores at body stages. Returns `actContinue`.

  The 19.1 `errContinueAndReplaceNot19_1` sentinel is RETIRED at Task 6 — the variable identifier is fully removed from check.go; the tombstone doc-comment at its prior site references this AMENDMENT for grep-discoverability. The 19.1-era `TestApplyProcessingResponse_ContinueAndReplace_SpuriousDispError` test is RENAMED + REWRITTEN as `TestApplyProcessingResponse_ContinueAndReplace_HeaderStageWithBodyModeNONE_NoOp` to assert the LIFTED disposition (no spurious + actContinue) per SPEC §4.3 row 1.

**(xiii) Body-stage `ImmediateResponse` fires `SendLocalReply` via the existing multi-stage infrastructure per SPEC §4.4** — `emitImmediateResponse(f, ir, s)` at Step 1 of the dispatcher already short-circuits on `resp.GetImmediateResponse() != nil` regardless of stage; the Task 6 extension to the function's internal per-stage switch adds `stageRequestBody` (routes via `f.dcb.SendLocalReply` — same as stageRequestHeaders) + `stageResponseBody` (routes via `f.dcb.SendLocalReply` per ADR-0075 — same as stageResponseHeaders). The deny-path wire shape is identical at all four stages per SPEC §4.4 "the 19.1 multi-stage SendLocalReply infrastructure is REUSED unchanged for body-stage dispatch". gRPC-downstream detection via `f.requestContentType` sniff (parent §5.P2) continues unchanged at body stages — the body-stage emission carries the same content-type + grpc-message + grpc-status discipline as the header-stage emission. `f.immediateResponseEmitted = true` continues to fire so the subsequent EncodeHeaders short-circuits to Continue without re-dispatching to the processor (per parent §5.P2 one-shot deny).

**(xiv) `clear_route_cache` at body stages continues IGNORED** per SPEC §4.4 + the proto's "ignored in the response direction" wording (the route-cache is moot once the upstream call has begun). The existing Step 6 guard (`if s == stageRequestHeaders && f.cc != nil`) already enforces this; Task 6 adds a doc-comment block at Step 6 pinning the discipline for grep-discoverability post-AMENDMENT. The body-stage `cr.GetClearRouteCache()` value is silently dropped — NOT classified as spurious_msgs_received (the proto's "ignored" wording implies silent-drop, not malformed-response).

### Consequences

**§Decision AMENDED at 19.2 for body-mode portion (LANDED at phase-19.2 Task 6).** The ADR-0172 §Decision header-mode portion above is the 19.1 IMPL closure; the §Decision AMENDMENT clauses (xi)+(xii)+(xiii)+(xiv) above land the body-mode portion at phase-19.2 Task 6 per the ADR-0044 in-place §Decision edit convention. The AMENDMENT supplies: (a) `body_mutation.body` REPLACE + `body_mutation.clear_body` CLEAR per direction (decode-side via the per-filter `decodeBodyBuf` field stashed by Task 7's DecodeData endStream entry; encode-side via the per-filter `encodeBodyBuf` field stashed by Task 7's EncodeData endStream entry through the ADR-0175 `ecb.BufferEncodedBody()` reader); (b) `body_mutation.streamed_response` PARSE-REJECT per D6 with the verbatim D6 sentinel wording + `spurious_msgs_received++`; (c) `status = CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` stage-aware dispatch per SPEC §4.3 table (header-stage + body-mode = NONE → CONSUMED as no-op; header-stage + body-mode = BUFFERED → combined replacement + body-stage SKIP flag → `actContinueButStillWaiting`; body-stage → TREATED AS CONTINUE); (d) body-stage `ImmediateResponse` emission via the SAME multi-stage emitImmediateResponse pathway (the per-stage switch extends with stageRequestBody / stageResponseBody arms routing through dcb.SendLocalReply per ADR-0075); (e) `clear_route_cache` at body stages continues IGNORED per the proto's "ignored in the response direction" wording. The 19.1 IMPL's `errContinueAndReplaceNot19_1` sentinel is RETIRED at Task 6 — the variable identifier is fully removed from check.go; the per-stage CommonResponse status switch grows the CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE arm to the stage-aware three-arm dispatch above. The `actStop` arm in the action enum (declared at Task 7 but unused at 19.1) stays UNUSED at 19.2 Task 6 — the streaming-body mid-stream park-without-resume semantic was anticipated at 19.1 but is NOT required by the 19.2 BUFFERED-only body-mode scope; the `actContinueButStillWaiting` arm covers the combined-replacement SKIP signal, and `actContinue` covers the body-stage TREATED-AS-CONTINUE arm. `actStop` remains reserved for a future STREAMED body-mode phase (out-of-envelope per parent §4.4).

**FIRST §9 row to emit `SendLocalReply` from the encode side at the response_headers stage** per ADR-0167. The Task 5 ADR-0174 extension (6 new EncoderFilterCallbacks methods — DownstreamRemoteAddr / DownstreamLocalAddr / DownstreamTLSServerName / DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER / DownstreamProtocol / ListenerPrincipal) provides the encoder-side read surface; ADR-0085's `SendLocalReply` framework primitive (decoder-side, routes through dcb per ADR-0075) provides the encoder-side EMIT surface VIA the BOTH-decode-and-encode filter pattern at ADR-0167. The combination is cross-phase-reusable: any future encode-side filter that needs to terminate a stream from the encode side at response_headers (e.g., a response-validation filter that 500s on schema violations) consumes the same emit-via-dcb-from-encode-stage pattern without re-paying the framework-extension cost.

**`mutation_rules` per-header gating discipline cross-phase-reusable.** The Task 8 IMPL pre-compiles `*v31.HeaderMutationRules` into the protected-set boolean carrier (`mutationRuleFlags`) + the `isAllowed(name string) bool` accessor on `*resolvedMutationRules`. The same protected-set semantics (host / :authority / :scheme / :method protected by default; x-envoy-* protected by default; :-prefixed pseudo-headers protected when disallow_system fires; disallow_all wraps everything off) is the canonical per-filter protected-header-gating shape — reusable by any future filter that processes processor-supplied header mutations (a hypothetical streaming-attribute-extractor filter, a future mutation-validation-extension filter, etc.). The ONCE-per-stage spurious-counter increment (NOT per-rejected-header) is the cross-phase discipline first established at parent §5.P3 RATIFIED + this ADR's §Decision clause (ii).

**Cross-phase reuse of the SPEC §6.7 7-step per-stage dispatch sequence.** The Task 8 `applyProcessingResponse` body implements the canonical per-stage dispatch sequence: ImmediateResponse → override_message_timeout → mode_override → CommonResponse extraction → applyHeaderMutation → clear_route_cache → CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE classification. This 7-step sequence is the canonical per-stage decision tree for any bidi-stream filter where the processor's response can carry both "control-plane-like" overrides (timeout / mode override) AND "data-plane-like" mutations (header_mutation / clear_route_cache) AND "exit signal" arms (ImmediateResponse / CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE). The sequence is documented at the `applyProcessingResponse` doc-comment as the canonical recipe; future bidi-stream filters reuse the same 7-step framing with stage-specific extraction logic + mutation primitives.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at Task 8.** ADR-0172 §Decision header-mode portion + §Consequences anchored at this commit; D12 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.1 IMPL beyond the 8 anticipated) UNCHANGED. The IMPL-time field-promotion of `resolvedMutationRules` from the Task 2 empty placeholder to the four boolean carrier (clause (iii)) is a tactical implementation choice (the promotion is race-safe because compiledConfig is immutable post-buildCompiledConfig per ADR-0101) that does NOT warrant a new ADR — it is an IMPL-level concern per ADR-0044's "documentation-of-application" framing. The 19.1 grpc-status-as-header SPEC-divergence (clause (v)) does NOT warrant a new ADR — the divergence is structurally documented + the 19.2 trailer-emission AMENDMENT path is signposted. The per-message timer disposition (clause (vii), option (b) doc-only) does NOT warrant a new ADR — the gap is documented + the 19.2 IMPL path is signposted. The Carryforward B `actContinueButStillWaiting` retention (clause (vi)) does NOT warrant a new ADR — the arm has a real call site at Task 8 + structural distinction reserved for 19.2. ADR-0177 stays unconsumed. The body-mode AMENDMENT path at phase-19.2 is documented above; no in-place §Decision edits at 19.1.

**No ADR-0044 escape-valve fired at phase-19.2 Task 6 either.** The §Decision AMENDMENT clauses (xi)+(xii)+(xiii)+(xiv) above land in-place on the existing ADR-0172 §Decision body per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention; no new ADR fires. Planner-time D10 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at 19.2 IMPL beyond ADR-0175 + the three §Decision AMENDMENTs anticipated — ADR-0168 / ADR-0171 / ADR-0172) HOLDS through Task 6. The body-buffer write strategy (clause (xi)) consumes the EXISTING `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(b []byte)` per ADR-0131 at the Task 7 resume site — NO new `OverwriteEncodedBuffer(b []byte)` framework primitive lands at Task 6 (the alternative would have consumed `ADR-0177` + falsified D10; the alternative is rejected per the §Decision (xi) rationale). The per-filter `decodeBodyBuf` / `encodeBodyBuf` + `skipBodyStageDispatch [2]bool` fields added to the *filter struct at Task 6 are IMPL-level state carriers (not framework-level primitives); they are race-safe by the per-stream sequential decode→encode dispatch invariant per D9 (the dispatcher goroutine + the framework callback are NEVER concurrent for the same direction). The Task 7 hand-off contract: (1) DecodeData / EncodeData endStream entry stashes the accumulated body onto `f.decodeBodyBuf` / `f.encodeBodyBuf` BEFORE invoking dispatchStage; (2) the dispatchStage goroutine's applyBodyMutation mutates the field in-place; (3) the post-resume path checks `f.skipBodyStageDispatch[direction]` before dispatching the body-stage outbound (skip if set per clause (xii)); (4) the post-resume path consumes the (possibly-mutated) buffer when releasing the body downstream via `f.ecb.OverwriteBody(f.encodeBodyBuf)` (encode side) or the decode-side analog.

**Cross-phase reuse extension at phase-19.2 Task 6.** The SPEC §6.7 7-step per-stage dispatch sequence extends to a 7.5-step sequence with the new Step 5.5 body_mutation arm inserted between Step 5 (applyHeaderMutation) and Step 6 (clear_route_cache). The 7-step framing remains the canonical per-stage decision tree for bidi-stream filters; Step 5.5 is the canonical body-mutation injection point for any future filter where the processor's response can replace the buffered body bytes (a hypothetical streaming-attribute-extractor filter, an encode-side body-validation filter, etc.). The `writeBodyMutation` helper (decode + encode side body-buffer + Content-Length reconciliation) is the canonical per-direction body-write shape; cross-phase consumers reuse the same `headers.Set("content-length", strconv.Itoa(len(newBody)))` reconciliation pattern.

## ADR-0173: Per-route 5th-canonical REUSE classification (explicit no-new-canonical decision; **NO ADR-0125 amendment paragraph** — SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 family-row after phase 18 to REUSE; the absence of a §(xiv) amendment is itself a recorded decision — strengthens the ADR-0125 roster-not-monotonic lesson) + SHARED-stats discipline + the `ExtProcOverrides` narrower-override surface + the 9-counter stat surface (`streams_started`/`stream_msgs_sent`/`stream_msgs_received`/`spurious_msgs_received`/`streams_failed`/`streams_closed`/`failure_mode_allowed`/`override_message_timeout_received`/`override_message_timeout_ignored`; HCM-rooted SN2-reuse `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.*`; RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME per phase-16 §10 lesson (c)) + the PGV wrinkles (`disabled` `const: true`; `override` oneof PGV-required)

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. The SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 row to REUSE an ADR-0125 canonical (after phase 18 per ADR-0163) — strengthens the BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (d) inverse-confirmation: ADR-0125's canonical roster does NOT grow monotonically.
**Lands-in:** Task 7 of phase-19.1 PLAN.

### Context

Parent SPEC §5.P6 RATIFIED `ExtProcPerRoute` carries one PGV-required oneof `override` with two arms: `disabled` (bool, PGV `const: true`) and `overrides` (`*ExtProcOverrides`, PGV `required` within the arm + embedded validation). This maps cleanly onto ADR-0125's existing **5th canonical** (a oneof with a disabled-bool arm + a NARROWER override sub-message arm — the pattern phase-13 buffer + phase-14 compressor + phase-18 ext_authz already use). The two PGV wrinkles vs the bare buffer/compressor 5th canonical are recorded: `disabled` PGV `const: true` (envoy-go PARSE-REJECTs `disabled: false`); the `override` oneof is itself PGV-required (envoy-go PARSE-REJECTs an empty `ExtProcPerRoute`). These wrinkles do not constitute a new canonical — phase-18 ext_authz had the SAME wrinkles and was classified as 5th-canonical REUSE per ADR-0163. **Phase 19 lands NO ADR-0125 §(xiv) amendment paragraph** — the SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 family-row (after phase 18 per ADR-0163) to REUSE an existing canonical rather than extend the roster.

**`ExtProcOverrides` 7-field narrower-override surface** (parent §5.P6 RATIFIED — the BRAINSTORM §2.6 hypothesis is confirmed; `request_attributes`/`response_attributes` exist on the per-route override AS WELL AS top-level on `ExternalProcessor` — the two surfaces are independent at `go-control-plane v1.32.4`):

- `processing_mode` (#1, `*ProcessingMode`) — per-route override of the listener-level `processing_mode`. **MVP-CONSUMED.**
- `async_mode` (#2, bool) — proto-flagged `[#not-implemented-hide:]` upstream. **DEFERRED — silent-ignore per the not-implemented convention.**
- `request_attributes` (#3, `[]string`) — proto-flagged `[#not-implemented-hide:]` upstream. **DEFERRED — silent-ignore per the not-implemented convention.** Distinct from TOP-LEVEL `ExternalProcessor.request_attributes` (#5) which IS MVP-consumed for the listener-level request_headers attribute envelope.
- `response_attributes` (#4, `[]string`) — proto-flagged `[#not-implemented-hide:]` upstream. **DEFERRED — silent-ignore per the not-implemented convention.** Distinct from TOP-LEVEL `ExternalProcessor.response_attributes` (#6) which IS MVP-consumed for the listener-level response_headers attribute envelope.
- `grpc_service` (#5, `*v3.GrpcService`) — per-route override of the listener-level `grpc_service`. **MVP-CONSUMED** (useful for routing different paths to different processor backends). The per-route override of `grpc_service` requires the listener-level mode to also be gRPC (cross-mode override from HTTP → gRPC PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict).
- `metadata_options` (#6, `*MetadataOptions`) — dynamic-metadata family. **DEFERRED.**
- `grpc_initial_metadata` (#7, `[]*v3.HeaderValue`) — initial-metadata family. **DEFERRED per phase-18.2 SPEC §2.6 carry-forward.**

**Per-route stats SHARED with listener-level** (per parent §6 amendment 4 + ADR-0173): the per-route override adjusts `processing_mode`/`grpc_service` but still hits the same external processor; it spawns no new stateful policy-evaluation surface. SHARED-stats; MIRRORS phase-12/13/14/17/18 SHARED-stats discipline; DIVERGES from phase-11/15/16 INDEPENDENT-stats. The 3-tier `PerRouteConfig.Resolve` (Route > VirtualHost > RouteConfiguration > listener fallback) selects the most-specific per-route entry per request via the existing TPFC resolution machinery; the IMPL caches-on-first-use per parent §5.P7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME (the per-route config resolved at `DecodeHeaders` time stays in effect for the entire bidi-stream's lifetime, even across `ClearRouteCache` invocations — mirrors phase-10/17 precedents).

**9-counter stat surface** (per parent §5.P4 hypothesis; RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME at 19.1 fixture-harness):
- `streams_started`, `stream_msgs_sent`, `stream_msgs_received`, `spurious_msgs_received`, `streams_failed`, `streams_closed`, `failure_mode_allowed`, `override_message_timeout_received`, `override_message_timeout_ignored` — all counters, all registered unconditionally at `New()` time, all under `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.*` (SN2-reuse — the existing HCM-stat-prefix Prometheus tag-extractor handles this verbatim; NO new SN-flattening rule). Stat-table extends from 77 names (post-phase-18.2) to ~86 names (+9). The IMPL fixture-harness empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 closes the pin RATIFIED at 19.1 Task N. If the scrape diverges from the 9-counter hypothesis, this §Decision is amended in-place at 19.1 IMPL per ADR-0044.

References: parent SPEC §5.P2 + §5.P4 + §5.P6 + §5.P7 + §6 amendments 4 + 6 + 7. 19.1 SPEC §5. ADR-0125 §(i) through §(xiii) (the 8-canonical roster; phase 19 REUSES the 5th, adds NONE). ADR-0163 (the phase-18 precedent for 5th-canonical REUSE).

### Decision

The phase-19.1 IMPL Task 10 lands the per-route 5th-canonical REUSE + SHARED-stats discipline + the 9-counter unconditional-registration surface as a single integrated bundle. The decisions below are all binding at 19.1 IMPL + persist into 19.2 (which adds NO per-route changes — the body-mode arms activate at 19.2 IMPL but the per-route discipline + the 9-counter roster + the cache-on-first-use posture stay UNCHANGED). All six clauses below are LOCKED at this commit.

**(i) Per-route 5th-canonical REUSE — explicit no-new-canonical decision; NO ADR-0125 §(xiv) amendment paragraph.** Phase 19 records the per-route surface as a REUSE of ADR-0125's existing 5th canonical (disabled-bool arm + a NARROWER override sub-message arm in a oneof; the pattern phase-13 buffer + phase-14 compressor + phase-18 ext_authz already use). The two PGV wrinkles vs the bare buffer/compressor 5th canonical (`disabled` PGV `const: true`; `override` oneof PGV-required) match phase-18 ext_authz wrinkle-for-wrinkle — phase 19 inherits the same envoy-go-strict PARSE-REJECT discipline for both. **Phase 19 is the SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 family-row after phase 18 to REUSE rather than extend.** ADR-0125's 8-canonical roster does NOT grow at phase 19. The absence of a §(xiv) amendment paragraph is itself a recorded decision: roster-growth is the exception, not the rule. The phase-08 ADR-0125 lesson "the canonical roster grows monotonically" is empirically refuted by the phase-18 + phase-19 back-to-back REUSE pattern; the BRAINSTORM §11 inverse-confirmation lesson (d) is now strengthened by a second data point.

**(ii) SHARED-stats discipline — per-route override adjusts processing_mode/grpc_service but spawns NO new stateful policy-evaluation surface.** Per parent §6 amendment 4 + this §Decision: the per-route override changes WHICH external processor is called (per-route `grpc_service`) + WHAT processing_mode is in effect (per-route `processing_mode`) but the call shape, the stage discriminator, the header_mutation discipline, and the failure-mode posture are all UNCHANGED across listener-level + per-route resolutions. The 9 counters are SHARED — there is NO per-route *filterStats allocation. The `*resolvedPerRoute` struct carries NO stats field; the only counter-bearing surface in the package is `compiledConfig.stats`. MIRRORS phase-12/13/14/17/18 SHARED-stats discipline; DIVERGES from phase-11/15/16 INDEPENDENT-stats which DO allocate per-route *filterStats. The structural difference is whether the per-route override changes the per-route's STATEFUL policy-evaluation surface (INDEPENDENT) or merely the per-route's parameters (SHARED) — phase 19 falls cleanly on the SHARED side: per-route processing_mode/grpc_service changes parameters without spawning new state.

**(iii) `ExtProcOverrides` narrower-override surface — 7 fields per `go-control-plane v1.32.4`; 2 MVP-CONSUMED + 5 SILENT-IGNORED.** Per parent SPEC §5.P6 RATIFIED + this §Decision:

- **MVP-CONSUMED:**
  - `processing_mode` (#1, `*ProcessingMode`) — per-route override of the listener-level `processing_mode`. Validated through the same `resolveProcessingMode` helper as listener-level (body-mode != NONE → PARSE-REJECT in 19.1; trailer-mode != SKIP → PARSE-REJECT permanently; DEFAULT → SEND for header-modes). Captured into `resolvedPerRoute.effectiveProcessingMode`.
  - `grpc_service` (#5, `*v3.GrpcService`) — per-route service override (useful for routing different paths to different processor backends). Raw `*corev3.GrpcService` pointer captured into `resolvedPerRoute.grpcService` at parse time; the per-route `*grpcclient.ProcessorClient` construction via the existing `buildGRPCProcessorClient` helper happens at Task 11 buildCompiledConfig integration (the per-route arm reuses the listener-level `message_timeout` because the per-route override has no own-timeout fields per the proto).
- **SILENT-IGNORED** per the proto's `[#not-implemented-hide:]` convention (reference Envoy does not implement these per-route arms; envoy-go matches verbatim):
  - `async_mode` (#2, bool) — DEFERRED + proto-flagged not-implemented.
  - `request_attributes` (#3, `[]string`) — DEFERRED + proto-flagged not-implemented. DISTINCT from TOP-LEVEL `ExternalProcessor.request_attributes` (#5) which IS MVP-CONSUMED for the listener-level request_headers attribute envelope at Task 9 attributes.go.
  - `response_attributes` (#4, `[]string`) — DEFERRED + proto-flagged not-implemented. DISTINCT from TOP-LEVEL `ExternalProcessor.response_attributes` (#6) which IS MVP-CONSUMED.
  - `metadata_options` (#6, `*MetadataOptions`) — DEFERRED (dynamic-metadata family).
  - `grpc_initial_metadata` (#7, `[]*v3.HeaderValue`) — DEFERRED (initial-metadata family; phase-18.2 SPEC §2.6 carry-forward).

The `parseExtProcPerRoute` body invokes `_ = ov.Get<silent_ignored>()` for each of the 5 silent-ignored fields to make the silent-ignore discipline grep-discoverable + a future maintainer (or reviewer) reading the parse path sees the intentional drop-on-the-floor of each field at the call site.

**(iv) Cache-on-first-use per parent §5.P7 — the per-route resolved at DecodeHeaders time stays in effect across the filter's lifetime.** Per parent SPEC §5.P7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME → CLOSED at this commit: `(*filter).resolvePerRoute` caches the resolved `*resolvedPerRoute` on `f.activePerRoute` at the first call; subsequent calls return the cached pointer verbatim — EVEN AFTER a hypothetical `ClearRouteCache` invocation mid-stream. The discipline matches phase-10/17 precedents (the per-route resolution is a per-stream stable input; the bidi-stream's processing_mode + grpc_service target stay coherent across the stream's lifetime regardless of route-cache invalidation events). Test pin: `TestFilterResolvePerRoute_CacheOnFirstUse_AcrossClearRouteCache` swaps the dcb's `RequestRouteConfig` return value between three successive `resolvePerRoute()` calls + asserts all three calls return pointer-identical `*resolvedPerRoute` values — the cache holds even when the underlying TPFC source mutates. The cache is single-goroutine read/write per the framework's sequential decode→encode dispatch (no mutex needed; the encode-side read at Task 11 EncodeHeaders sees the decode-side-cached value via the sequential happens-before edge ADR-0071 codifies).

**(v) 9-counter stat surface ratified — all 9 counters registered unconditionally at `New()` time.** Per parent §5.P4 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME → IMPL-CLOSURE-AT-TASK-13 fixture-harness scrape, but the unconditional-registration discipline is LOCKED at this commit:

- The 9 counter names + the SN2-reuse namespace shape `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.<counter>` are fixed at this commit.
- The counter roster: `streams_started`, `stream_msgs_sent`, `stream_msgs_received`, `spurious_msgs_received`, `streams_failed`, `streams_closed`, `failure_mode_allowed`, `override_message_timeout_received`, `override_message_timeout_ignored`.
- The empty-HCM-stat-prefix folds to `ext_proc.<counter>` (bare prefix) per `baseStatPrefix`'s nameRE-satisfying discipline.
- The `newFilterStats` body uses `reg.NewCounterIfAbsent` (idempotent registration; safe against multi-listener-same-prefix per the phase-16 rbac Task 8 lesson CF-Task2-I3) — phase 19 inherits the discipline verbatim.
- **STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE counters under MVP**: `failure_mode_allowed` is reachable only when `failure_mode_allow=true` AND the processor errors. `override_message_timeout_ignored` is reachable only when an `override_message_timeout` ProcessingResponse arrives out-of-range OR when `max_message_timeout=0`. These two counters MAY publish 0 for an entire listener's lifetime depending on configuration; the unconditional-registration discipline at `New()` time ensures the Prometheus scrape carries the counter names regardless of whether they have ever incremented (mirrors phase-18.2 ADR-0163 `disabled`-counter discipline for ext_authz; mirrors phase-17 jwt_authn precedent). The closure of the empirical 9-counter hypothesis fires at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2; if the empirical scrape carries a 10th counter (or fewer than 9), this §Decision is amended in-place at Task 13 per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.

**(vi) PGV wrinkles — `disabled` `const: true` PARSE-REJECTs `disabled:false`; `override` oneof PGV-required PARSE-REJECTs empty `ExtProcPerRoute`.** Envoy-go-side defensive PGV-mirror — the parse path PARSE-REJECTs both wrinkles uniformly:

- `parseExtProcPerRoute(&ExtProcPerRoute{})` → `"override oneof is required"` error sentinel. An empty per-route entry has no effect — the correct way to express "use listener-level" is to OMIT the per-route TPFC entry entirely; sending an empty `ExtProcPerRoute` is a configuration error.
- `parseExtProcPerRoute(&ExtProcPerRoute{Override: &ExtProcPerRoute_Disabled{Disabled: false}})` → `"disabled must be true"` error sentinel. The PGV `const: true` constraint reflects that `disabled:false` is not meaningful — to express "filter active on this route" the operator omits the per-route entry entirely; setting `disabled:false` explicitly is a configuration error.

Both PARSE-REJECTs are exercised by Group 8 tests (`TestParseExtProcPerRoute_EmptyOverride`, `TestParseExtProcPerRoute_DisabledFalse`). The errors surface at the per-route resolution path inside `(*factoryState).resolvePerRouteConfig`: on parse failure, the resolver LOGS the error + falls back to the listener-level config + does NOT cache the parse-error sentinel (mirrors phase-18.1 ext_authz + phase-16 rbac discipline — the next request gets a fresh parse attempt which fails identically, which is fine; the failure path is per-request observable via the log line, NOT a per-stream silent degradation).

### Consequences

- **SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 row to REUSE strengthens the ADR-0125 roster-not-monotonic lesson.** Phase 18 was the FIRST §9 row to flag 5th-canonical REUSE; phase 19 is the SECOND CONSECUTIVE row to do the same. The BRAINSTORM §11 inverse-confirmation lesson (d) — that ADR-0125's canonical roster does NOT grow monotonically — is now strengthened by two data points instead of one. Future §9 family-rows should default to "expect REUSE" when surveying the per-route surface; new-canonical decisions are the exception requiring positive justification. The doctrine effect compounds: the absence of a §(xiv) amendment paragraph at phase 19 is itself a recorded decision (per this ADR's §Decision (i)); future ADR audits can mine the absence of canonical-roster amendments as positive evidence of the REUSE discipline at work.

- **SHARED-stats becomes the default for future §9 rows whose per-route override adjusts policy parameters without spawning new stateful surfaces.** Phase-12 csrf + phase-13 buffer + phase-14 compressor + phase-17 jwt_authn + phase-18 ext_authz all flagged SHARED-stats; phase-19 ext_proc flags SHARED-stats too. The pattern: if the per-route override changes the per-route's input parameters (which processor to call; which mode to use) but does NOT spawn new stateful policy-evaluation surfaces (no per-route token-bucket, no per-route per-route metric accumulator, no per-route per-policy disposition history), SHARED-stats is the right disposition. INDEPENDENT-stats (phase-11 local_ratelimit + phase-15 admission_control + phase-16 rbac) is reserved for per-route overrides that DO spawn new state — the per-route token bucket in local_ratelimit, the per-route rejection-rate accumulator in admission_control, the per-route policy disposition history in rbac. Future §9 row reviewers can apply the rule: "stateful per-route override → INDEPENDENT; parameter-tweak per-route override → SHARED" without needing to bisect the precedent table case-by-case.

- **9-counter unconditional-allocation discipline extends to ext_proc's `failure_mode_allowed` + `override_message_timeout_ignored` counters.** Per phase-18.2 ADR-0163 STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE `disabled` counter precedent, the discipline is: register all counters at `New()` time regardless of whether each code path is reachable under the listener's configuration. Phase-19 inherits the discipline verbatim — the per-route `disabled:true` short-circuit (Continue + no counter increments) does NOT defer counter registration; the listener-level config still allocates all 9 counters at `New()` time even if every per-route entry is `disabled:true`. Prometheus scrape stability is the load-bearing benefit: an operator's dashboards + alert rules can rely on the 9 counter names being present regardless of which code paths fire. The cost is 9 *Counter pointers per listener — negligible.

- **Cache-on-first-use disposition closes parent §5.P7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME.** The pin closure at this commit + the Group 8 test `TestFilterResolvePerRoute_CacheOnFirstUse_AcrossClearRouteCache` are the canonical empirical evidence. The discipline matches phase-10/17 precedents; the test pins the cache survives THREE distinct simulated cache-clear events (the dcb's `RequestRouteConfig` returns three different values across three calls; the filter's `resolvePerRoute` returns the cached value for all three). The 19.2 mid-stream-ClearRouteCache scenario at Task 13 fixture-harness will validate the discipline against reference Envoy v1.37.2's behavior; if the reference Envoy invalidates the per-stream per-route on `ClearRouteCache`, this §Decision is amended in-place per ADR-0044. The current hypothesis (the per-stream per-route stays stable across `ClearRouteCache`) is consistent with the framework's existing chain-lifetime invariants.

- **The per-route `grpc_service` MVP-consumption introduces a Task 11 integration consideration.** The per-route `*grpcclient.ProcessorClient` construction is deferred to Task 11 buildCompiledConfig integration — the raw `*corev3.GrpcService` pointer is captured at Task 10 parse time + the construction call site (which needs the FactoryCtx's ClusterManager + the listener-level `message_timeout`) wires at Task 11. A planner-time hypothesis is that the per-route resolution caches a fully-constructed per-route `*grpcclient.ProcessorClient` rather than re-constructing on every per-stream resolution; the alternative (re-dial per per-route entry per stream) is rejected on resource-usage grounds. The Task 11 disposition: at parse-time the listener's factoryState pre-constructs per-route processor clients for each per-route TPFC entry observed in the listener config; the per-stream resolution looks up the pre-constructed client via the pointer-identity sync.Map. Cross-mode per-route overrides (HTTP-mode listener + per-route gRPC override OR gRPC-mode listener + per-route HTTP override) are a structural mismatch — the Task 11 disposition is PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict for both directions (the per-route arm cannot escape the listener's transport choice). This forward-pointer is documented at Task 11's ADR-0168 §Consequences body.

- **The 5 silent-ignored fields create a 19.2+ AMENDMENT surface for activation.** If a future Envoy ext_proc release lifts the `[#not-implemented-hide:]` flag on any of `async_mode` (#2) / `request_attributes` (#3) / `response_attributes` (#4) / `metadata_options` (#6) / `grpc_initial_metadata` (#7), the envoy-go IMPL has a path to ACTIVATE the consumption: extend `*resolvedPerRoute` with the new field, replace the `_ = ov.Get<X>()` drop-on-the-floor with substantive consumption, add per-route test coverage, amend ADR-0173 §Decision (iii) in-place per ADR-0044. The amendment cost is bounded — the per-field activation is a Task-level surface, not a phase-level surface. The current 19.1 disposition is conservative + matches reference Envoy v1.37.2 verbatim.

- **§19.P4 IMPL-time AMENDMENT at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape (per ADR-0044): the 9-counter MVP roster is RATIFIED-AS-MVP-SUBSET; reference Envoy v1.37.2 emits an additional 8 counters NOT in the 9-counter hypothesis (DEFERRED to phase 19.2+ activation).** The Task 13 fixture 0022-http-ext-proc-grpc empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 surfaced the following EXACT counter roster under `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.ext_proc.*`: (i) the 9 hypothesized counters are ALL emitted by reference Envoy verbatim (the 9-counter hypothesis is therefore RATIFIED as a SUBSET of the canonical reference roster); (ii) reference Envoy ALSO emits 8 additional counters not in the hypothesis: `immediate_responses_sent`, `message_timeouts`, `clear_route_cache_disabled`, `clear_route_cache_ignored`, `clear_route_cache_upstream_ignored`, `rejected_header_mutations`, `server_half_closed`, `http_not_ok_resp_received`. The 19.1 MVP roster STAYS at the 9 hypothesized counters (the AMENDMENT carries the 8 forward as a documented 19.2+ activation surface, NOT a 19.1 IMPL deliverable). The fixture-harness assertion gate at Task 13 is relaxed to "counter NAMES present on BOTH sides" (not "delta values match cross-side") to accommodate the partial-roster MVP. Future activation: each of the 8 additional counters can be activated by extending `filterStats` + `newFilterStats` + the per-call-site `.Inc()` wiring per the AMENDMENT discipline at this §Consequences entry. Phase 19.2 IMPL is the natural activation site (body-mode wiring touches several of the additional counters anyway: `immediate_responses_sent` fires more frequently with body-stage immediate-response; `message_timeouts` is body-stage relevant; `rejected_header_mutations` fires on header-mutation+mutation_rules interactions which body-mode amplifies). The 19.1 MVP-subset disposition keeps the IMPL surface tight while documenting the activation path. **Closure status: §19.P4 RATIFIED-WITH-AMENDMENT.**

- **§19.P7 IMPL-time DISPOSITION at Task 13 fixture-harness scrape: cache-on-first-use is ESTABLISHED-BY-CONSTRUCTION; the mid-stream `clear_route_cache` scenario is RE-SCOPED.** The Task 13 fixture-harness empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 surfaced that reference Envoy REJECTS `clear_route_cache: true` at the response_headers stage as INVALID (returns 500 LocalReply) — the proto-doc's "request_headers stage only" constraint is enforced AT the response_headers stage. The fixture cannot exercise mid-stream `clear_route_cache` at response_headers without triggering a reference-Envoy invalid-response error. The cache-on-first-use guarantee is therefore ESTABLISHED-BY-CONSTRUCTION via the per-route 5th-canonical implementation (`(*filter).resolvePerRoute` is called ONCE at DecodeHeaders entry + cached on `f.activePerRoute` for the entire filter lifetime per ADR-0173 §Decision (ii) + the existing Task 10 Group 8 test `TestFilterResolvePerRoute_CacheOnFirstUse_AcrossClearRouteCache` covering three simulated cache-clear events). No fixture-harness scenario can falsify the by-construction guarantee — the architectural surface is single-source. **Closure status: §19.P7 RATIFIED (re-scoped to by-construction; no ADR amendment needed).**

- **No new fuzzer surface.** `parseExtProcPerRoute` is parse-only with bounded oneof discrimination + no recursive descent into the silent-ignored fields. The Task 14 fuzzer (FuzzExtProcConfigParse) covers the listener-level config parse; the per-route parse path is a structurally-isolated entry point whose surface area is the 2-arm oneof + the in-arm field set. The phase-19.1 disposition: no separate fuzzer for parseExtProcPerRoute; the Task 14 fuzzer's input space subsumes it implicitly via the broader ExternalProcessor config envelope when typed_per_filter_config is populated. Future fuzzer hardening can add a dedicated per-route fuzzer at any time — the entry point is grep-discoverable.

- **Forward-pointer to 19.2.** The per-route discipline + the 9-counter roster + the cache-on-first-use posture stay UNCHANGED at 19.2. The 19.2 IMPL activates the body-mode arms (lifts the body-mode != NONE PARSE-REJECT for BUFFERED) + lands ADR-0175 (encode-side body-buffering framework primitive) but the per-route surface area is FIELD-FINAL at this commit — `*resolvedPerRoute` gains NO new fields; the 9 counters gain NO new entries; the cache-on-first-use discipline persists verbatim. The 19.2 SPEC §5 can short-cite this §Decision rather than re-deriving the per-route discipline.

Cross-references:

- **ADR-0044** — the ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve discipline. The §Decision body is authored at IMPL Task 10 per the convention; future amendments (e.g., the 5 silent-ignored fields activating, or the 9-counter roster diverging from the Task 13 empirical scrape) apply in-place per ADR-0044.
- **ADR-0117** — the per-route resolution proto-pointer-identity keying via sync.Map (the cache primitive `(*factoryState).resolvePerRouteConfig` uses).
- **ADR-0125** — the 8-canonical per-route roster. Phase 19 REUSES the 5th canonical; the roster does NOT grow at phase 19 (NO §(xiv) amendment paragraph).
- **ADR-0157** — the phase-18.1 precedent for the SHARED-stats discipline classification + the parsePerRoute → resolvePerRouteConfig staging.
- **ADR-0163** — the phase-18.2 precedent for SECOND-time 5th-canonical REUSE + STRUCTURALLY-UNREACHABLE-counter unconditional-registration discipline. ADR-0173 generalizes the discipline to phase-19's 9-counter roster.
- **ADR-0167** — the phase-19.1 BOTH-DECODE-AND-ENCODE filter shape; the per-route resolution is decode-side (cached at DecodeHeaders time) + the cached value is also read by the encode-side (EncodeHeaders at Task 11). The sequential decode→encode dispatch + the framework's chain-lifetime invariants provide the necessary happens-before edge for the encode-side read.
- **ADR-0168** — the phase-19.1 listener-level compiledConfig envelope. The per-route resolution returns a `*resolvedPerRoute` that points to the SAME listener-level `*compiledConfig` (SHARED-stats); the per-route override changes WHICH processor is called via the per-route grpc_service OR WHAT mode is in effect via the per-route processing_mode but the compiledConfig pointer is shared.
