## ADR-0174: Cross-phase-reusable symmetric `EncoderFilterCallbacks` extension — 6 new accessor methods (`DownstreamRemoteAddr`/`DownstreamLocalAddr`/`DownstreamTLSServerName`/`DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER`/`DownstreamProtocol`/`ListenerPrincipal`) mirroring ADR-0165's `DecoderFilterCallbacks` additions; reuses ADR-0165's chain-field plumbing (SET-once at HCM dispatch BEFORE either decode or encode dispatch; NO new chain primitives); REFUTED at SPEC §5.P12 in-session scrape → fires load-bearing at 19.1 IMPL; ADR-0044 escape-valve firing at SPEC time per BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h)

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.1 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve for impl-time-unanticipated decisions — this ADR's §Context is authored at SPEC time from the in-session §5.P12 REFUTED scrape, per the phase-18.2 ADR-0165 precedent and the BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h) discipline). ADR-0071 (chain-ownership-invariant — the 6 reader methods read existing chain fields with the same SET-once-by-HCM-dispatch + READ-by-callback discipline as `tlsPrincipals`). ADR-0165 (the precedent for the seed-at-HCM-dispatch / read-via-callback pattern; ADR-0174 EXTENDS the same 6 chain fields to the encoder-side callback surface).
**Lands-in:** Task 5 of phase-19.1 PLAN (PRE-REQUISITE — must land before Task 9 since `attributes.go` consumes the new encoder-side accessors). Note: SPEC §10's ADR-anchor-map table originally hypothesized "Task 4" as the landing task; the 19.1 IMPL re-sequenced to Task 5 (the gRPC bidi-stream wrapper at `internal/grpcclient/processor_client.go` landed at Task 4 per ADR-0169, and the ADR-0174 EncoderFilterCallbacks extension landed at Task 5).

### Context

The phase-19 SPEC's §5.P12 in-session empirical scrape REFUTED the BRAINSTORM §3.3 CONDITIONAL hypothesis for encode-side callback symmetry — confirming the framework gap on master tip `5927b55`:

**`internal/filter/http/callbacks.go:160-184` (master tip) `EncoderFilterCallbacks` carries ONLY**:
- `ContinueEncoding()`
- `EncodeHeaders(headers http.Header, endStream bool)` / `EncodeData(data []byte, endStream bool)` / `EncodeTrailers(trailers http.Header)` (encode-side injection methods — rare; intended for filters like header_manipulation that need to inject encode-side material from a decode-side context)
- `OverwriteBody(b []byte)` (per ADR-0131 §Decision (vi) — first encode-side framework primitive, phase 14)

**NO socket / TLS / listener accessors** — the 7 ADR-0144 + ADR-0165 methods (`DownstreamPrincipal`, `DownstreamRemoteAddr`, `DownstreamLocalAddr`, `DownstreamTLSServerName`, `DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER`, `DownstreamProtocol`, `ListenerPrincipal`) are decode-side only at master tip.

**Phase 19's `response_attributes` envelope** (populated at the response_headers stage per the proto's `ExternalProcessor.response_attributes` doc-comment: *"Each attribute name provided in this field will be matched against that list and populated in the response_headers message"*) requires encode-side access to the same socket/TLS/listener state that decode-side `request_attributes` consumes. The response_headers stage fires from the encode-side of the filter chain — `EncodeHeaders` returns `StopIteration`, the encode-side goroutine builds the response_headers ProcessingRequest with `attributes` populated, sends it via the bidi-stream, receives the ProcessingResponse, applies the `CommonResponse.header_mutation`, then `ContinueEncoding()`s. Without encode-side accessors, the response_attributes population is structurally unsatisfiable — the encoder-side filter cannot reach the per-stream socket/TLS state.

**The fix lands at 19.1 IMPL Task 5** — six new methods on `EncoderFilterCallbacks`:

```go
type EncoderFilterCallbacks interface {
    // ... existing 5 methods (ContinueEncoding, EncodeHeaders/Data/Trailers, OverwriteBody) ...

    // NEW per ADR-0174.
    DownstreamRemoteAddr() net.Addr
    DownstreamLocalAddr() net.Addr
    DownstreamTLSServerName() string
    DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER() []byte
    DownstreamProtocol() string
    ListenerPrincipal() string
}
```

**Seeding discipline mirrors ADR-0165** (the chain.go `tlsPrincipals`/`SetTLSPrincipals`/`DownstreamPrincipal()` pattern):
- The 6 chain fields (`downstreamRemoteAddr` / `downstreamLocalAddr` / `downstreamTLSServerName` / `downstreamTLSPeerCertDER` / `downstreamProtocol` / `listenerPrincipal`) ALREADY exist per ADR-0165's plumbing — they are SET ONCE at chain build time by HCM dispatch (H1 `connection.go:dispatchRequest` + H2 `h2dispatch.go:WriteH2`) BEFORE either `RunDecodeHeaders` or `RunEncodeHeaders` dispatch.
- **NO new chain plumbing primitives** — the chain fields are shared; the encoder-side reader methods access the same chain pointer via `*encoderCB`.
- 6 NEW `*encoderCB` reader methods (added at 19.1 IMPL Task 5) return the chain field verbatim — no copy, no transformation.
- ADR-0071's chain-ownership invariant continues to apply: SET-once at HCM dispatch BEFORE any dispatch path runs; READ concurrently from either decode-side or encode-side callbacks.

**NO `DownstreamPrincipal()` extension** to the encoder-side callbacks at 19.1 — `DownstreamPrincipal` is decode-side-specific in the ADR-0144 framing ("decode-side discovers the principal candidates at dispatch"). If `response_attributes` allowlist requires `source.principal` at the response_headers stage, the IMPL adds a 7th method at IMPL time (mirroring the phase-18.2 ADR-0165 D3+D12 settle pattern). Current hypothesis (parent §6.6 attribute-map table): the 6 socket/TLS/listener accessors suffice for the canonical response-side attribute envelope; `source.principal` is request-side-specific.

**The IMPL lands ~50-100 LoC**: ~30-50 LoC interface extension + reader methods in `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`; ~30-50 LoC unit tests (the round-trip seed-and-read pattern per the phase-18.2 `chain_test.go:1507` ADR-0165 Group 13 template).

**Cross-phase reuse intent.** The encode-side accessor extension is generally useful for any future filter participating on the encode side — ext_proc is the sole consumer at 19.1, but any future response-mutating filter or response-stage-attribute-emitting filter reuses the same accessor surface. Anchoring the methods at 19.1 IMPL ensures the cost is paid ONCE.

**ADR-0044 escape-valve fires at SPEC time** per BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h) — IN-SESSION SPEC scrape closure of the most-likely escape-valve surface. The brainstorm's CONDITIONAL hypothesis at §3.3 + §10 is empirically confirmed at SPEC time; the IMPL session does NOT need to discover this gap mid-impl. Mirrors the phase-18.2 ADR-0165 firing at PLAN-time D3+D12 — except the phase-19 surface is now empirically established at SPEC time rather than discovered at PLAN time, REMOVING the ADR-0044 surprise-at-PLAN-time risk.

References: parent SPEC §3 + §5.P12 + §6 amendment 12. 19.1 SPEC §3.3 + §13.5. ADR-0044 (the ADR-on-impl + escape-valve discipline). ADR-0071 (chain-ownership invariant). ADR-0144 (the seed-at-HCM-dispatch / read-via-callback precedent). ADR-0165 (the phase-18.2 decoder-side callback-surface extension — ADR-0174 EXTENDS the same 6 methods to the encoder-side).

### Decision

**Six new methods land on `EncoderFilterCallbacks`** in `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go` at phase-19.1 Task 5 — the symmetric mirror of the ADR-0165 `DecoderFilterCallbacks` 6-method extension, with the SAME signatures + the SAME doc-comment shape (substituting "encoder" for "decoder" + adding the `RunEncodeHeaders` seeding-precondition cite alongside `RunDecodeHeaders`):

1. `DownstreamRemoteAddr() net.Addr` — the downstream conn's `RemoteAddr()`; nil for synthetic streams.
2. `DownstreamLocalAddr() net.Addr` — the downstream conn's `LocalAddr()`; nil for synthetic streams.
3. `DownstreamTLSServerName() string` — `tls.ConnectionState.ServerName` (SNI); empty for plaintext / SNI-absent.
4. `DownstreamTLSPeerCertDER() []byte` — `tls.ConnectionState.PeerCertificates[0].Raw`; nil for plaintext / no-client-cert.
5. `DownstreamProtocol() string` — canonical short string `"HTTP/1.1"` (H1 dispatch) or `"HTTP/2"` (H2 dispatch); empty for synthetic streams.
6. `ListenerPrincipal() string` — listener's TLS server-cert principal; empty for plaintext listeners.

**Six methods, NOT seven** per planner-time decision D10. `DownstreamPrincipal()` is NOT added to the encoder-side surface — it remains decode-side-specific per ADR-0144's framing ("decode-side discovers the principal candidates at dispatch"). The parent §6.6 attribute-map table hypothesizes that `source.principal` is request-side-specific (the canonical response-side `response_attributes` envelope per the ext_proc proto's `Response_Attributes` proto field does NOT include `source.principal`). If the 19.1 IMPL Task 9 attributes-builder discovers a need for `source.principal` at the response_headers stage, ADR-0174 §Decision goes from 6 → 7 methods (mirroring the phase-18.2 ADR-0165 D3+D12 settle pattern) — at this commit the planner-time D10 hypothesis (6 sufficient) is empirically confirmed by the response_attributes envelope canonical fields.

**Chain-field reuse from ADR-0165 — NO new chain plumbing.** The 6 chain fields ALREADY exist per ADR-0165's plumbing at `chain.go:128-133`:

- `downstreamRemoteAddr net.Addr`
- `downstreamLocalAddr net.Addr`
- `downstreamTLSServerName string`
- `downstreamTLSPeerCertDER []byte`
- `downstreamProtocol string`
- `listenerPrincipal string`

These 6 fields are SET ONCE at chain build time by HCM dispatch (H1 `connection.go:dispatchRequest` + H2 `h2dispatch.go:WriteH2` per ADR-0165 §Decision) via the existing `SetDownstreamRemoteAddr` / `SetDownstreamLocalAddr` / `SetDownstreamTLSServerName` / `SetDownstreamTLSPeerCertDER` / `SetDownstreamProtocol` / `SetListenerPrincipal` setters at `chain.go:633+` — BEFORE either `RunDecodeHeaders` OR `RunEncodeHeaders` dispatch. ADR-0174 introduces:

- **NO new chain fields** — the 6 above are shared.
- **NO new seeding primitives** — the 6 existing setters cover both decode + encode reads.
- **NO new HCM dispatch wiring** — the H1 + H2 dispatch sites already invoke the 6 setters BEFORE the per-stream chain begins iteration; the encode-side dispatch (which fires AFTER decode dispatch completes per ADR-0075) inherits the same seeded values.

**Six new `*encoderCB` reader methods** in `chain.go` — verbatim mirror of the existing `*decoderCB` reader methods at `chain.go:524-546`. Each method returns the chain field through the `*encoderCB`'s back-pointer to `*FilterChain` (`e.c.downstreamRemoteAddr`, etc.) — no copy, no transformation, same single-line implementation shape as the decoder-side readers.

**ADR-0071's chain-ownership invariant continues to apply.** The 6 chain fields obey the same SET-once-by-HCM-dispatch + READ-by-callback discipline they obey for the decoder-side reads. The encode-side READ happens strictly AFTER the SET completes — HCM dispatch invokes `SetX` BEFORE `RunDecodeHeaders`, the entire decode chain completes (including upstream call + response receipt) BEFORE `RunEncodeHeaders` is invoked, and the encode-side filter readers fire from inside `EncodeHeaders` callbacks that run within `RunEncodeHeaders`. NO race surface is introduced because no goroutine writes to the chain fields after the initial HCM-dispatch SET; both the decoder-side and the encoder-side readers see a stable, write-completed value (Go's happens-before contract via the dispatch goroutine's sequential execution). The chain owns the fields, the callbacks are read-only consumers — same invariant as `tlsPrincipals` per ADR-0144's framing.

**Group 12 unit tests** in `chain_test.go` (the empirically-correct location to match the ADR-0165 decoder-side Group 13 template at `chain_test.go:1618`; SPEC §14.1 names `callbacks_test.go` as the Group 12 location but the PLAN's File-structure table places Group 12 in `chain_test.go` to match the existing template — empirically correct departure from SPEC §14.1 filename). 12 tests total: 6 round-trip seed-and-read tests (one per method asserting `Set(seed) → cb.X() == seed` via `RunEncodeHeaders` dispatch through an `encoderCallbackProbe` filter) + 6 nil/empty fall-through tests (no `Set` call → encoder-side accessor returns zero value). Test names: `TestEncoderCB_DownstreamRemoteAddr_SeededViaSetDownstreamRemoteAddr_ReturnsSeed`, `TestEncoderCB_DownstreamRemoteAddr_NotSeeded_ReturnsNil`, and the 10 analogous names for the other 5 methods.

**Test-mock fixups.** The `EncoderFilterCallbacks` interface extension necessarily breaks any independent mock that satisfies the interface via compile-time `var _ EncoderFilterCallbacks = (*X)(nil)` assertions OR by being passed to `SetEncoderCallbacks`. Three production-tree mocks required extension at this commit:

- `internal/filter/http/callbacks_test.go` — `fakeEncoderCB`. Extended with 6 zero-value-returning stubs.
- `internal/filter/http/bandwidthlimit/bandwidthlimit_test.go` — `fakeEncoderCB`. Extended with 6 zero-value-returning stubs (the Group 5 throttle tests do not consume the new accessors).
- `internal/filter/http/compressor/compressor_test.go` — `fakeCallbacks`. NO extension required; the struct already implements the 6 ADR-0165 decoder-side methods inherited by the encoder-side interface conformance (the BOTH-sides combined-callback struct shares the method set across both compile-time `var _` assertions).

The remaining test files that touch `EncoderFilterCallbacks` (`cors_test.go`, `envoygotest/filter_test.go`, `chain_dispatch_test.go`, `chain_integration_test.go`, `types_test.go`) only declare `SetEncoderCallbacks(EncoderFilterCallbacks)` parameter receivers — they accept the interface as input, do not implement it themselves, and do not require extension.

### Consequences

- **PRE-REQUISITE for the 19.1 ext_proc `response_attributes` envelope at the response_headers stage.** Phase-19.1 attributes.go (Task 9) consumes the 6 new encoder-side accessors from inside the ext_proc filter's `EncodeHeaders` callback to populate the `response_attributes` `AttributeContext` envelope per the parent §6.6 attribute-map table. Without ADR-0174, the response_attributes population is structurally unsatisfiable — the encoder-side filter cannot reach the per-stream socket / TLS / listener state. Landing ADR-0174 at Task 5 (BEFORE Task 9) sequences the framework primitive ahead of its first consumer per the doctrine that framework primitives precede filter consumption.
- **Cross-phase reuse intent for ADR-0174 — generally useful for any future encode-side filter.** ext_proc is the SOLE consumer at 19.1; future response-mutating filters or response-stage-attribute-emitting filters (a hypothetical response-content-rewrite filter, a future response-stage WASM filter, a future response-augmenting ext_authz variant) consume the SAME accessor surface without re-paying the plumbing cost. Anchoring the methods at 19.1 IMPL ensures the cost is paid ONCE — mirrors the ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` precedent (paid for ONCE at phase-16; reused at phase-18.1 + 18.2 + 19.1) and the ADR-0165 6-method precedent (paid for ONCE at phase-18.2; reused at this phase 19.1 ADR-0174 IMPL via chain-field sharing).
- **NO race-introduction.** The 6 chain fields are SET ONCE by HCM dispatch BEFORE either decode or encode dispatch fires; the encode-side READ is a no-write goroutine-local read of a write-completed value (sequential happens-before per the single-dispatch-goroutine ownership model ADR-0071 codifies). The race detector verifies clean across `./internal/filter/http/...` at this commit (`go test -race -count=1` green). No additional synchronization is required because the chain owns the fields and the callbacks are read-only consumers — same invariant ADR-0144 + ADR-0165 anchored for the decoder-side reads.
- **The asymmetric `DownstreamPrincipal()` decision (decode-side-only).** ADR-0174 §Decision deliberately stops at 6 methods — `DownstreamPrincipal()` stays decode-side-only per ADR-0144's framing. The parent §6.6 attribute-map table hypothesis is that `source.principal` (request-side TLS client cert principal) is structurally request-side-specific; the canonical response-side envelope does NOT include it. If Task 9's attributes-builder IMPL surfaces a need for `source.principal` at the response_headers stage (e.g., the response_attributes allowlist permits it via the proto field's open-ended `[]string` shape), ADR-0174 §Decision goes from 6 → 7 methods — but the current planner-time D10 + SPEC §3.3 hypothesis is that 6 suffice for the canonical response-side envelope. The current cost of the asymmetry is one extra IMPL-time surface to monitor (Task 9); the benefit is avoiding speculative interface bloat.
- **Test-mock fragility.** Future contributors who add a new mock implementation of `EncoderFilterCallbacks` (a new filter's test-double, a new framework test fixture) MUST extend the mock with all 6 ADR-0174 methods alongside the existing `OverwriteBody` + the 3 EncodeX methods. The existing 3-mock extension at this commit (callbacks_test.go + bandwidthlimit_test.go) establishes the precedent; future mocks follow the same shape (`func (X) Method() T { return zero }`). The compile-time `var _ EncoderFilterCallbacks = (*X)(nil)` assertion (where present) catches missing methods at build time — a defense-in-depth check the existing mocks all use.
- **Doc-comment maintenance burden.** The 6 new methods carry full doc-comments mirroring the decoder-side comments at `callbacks.go:86-157`. Any future maintenance of the decoder-side doc-comments (e.g., a clarification of the seed-at-HCM-dispatch discipline) must be mirrored to the encoder-side doc-comments to keep the symmetric pair in sync. This is a known maintenance burden of the symmetric-extension pattern; the cross-phase reuse benefit outweighs the doc-sync cost.
- **No new fuzzer surface.** The 6 accessors return chain-state values verbatim; there is no parsing / validation logic to fuzz. Same posture as the ADR-0165 decoder-side accessors.
- **Forward-compatibility with ADR-0175 (19.2 encode-side body-buffering primitive).** ADR-0175 (the 19.2 encode-side body-buffering primitive) lands a 7th encoder-side method (`BufferEncodedBody()`) per the SPEC §5.P11 + parent §6 amendment 11 anchor. ADR-0174's 6 socket/TLS/listener methods + ADR-0175's body-buffering method are orthogonal — they live in different doc-comment sections, address different concerns, and have non-conflicting signatures. The 19.2 IMPL extends `EncoderFilterCallbacks` further; the test-mock-fixup burden recurs at 19.2.

Cross-references:

- **ADR-0044** — the ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve discipline this ADR's §Context invokes. The escape-valve fires at SPEC time per BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h).
- **ADR-0071** — the chain-ownership invariant the 6 reader methods obey (SET-once + READ-by-callback discipline; single-dispatch-goroutine read invariant; no race surface introduced).
- **ADR-0144** — the prior framework primitive (`DownstreamPrincipal()` at phase-16) ADR-0165 generalized to 6 methods + ADR-0174 mirrors to the encoder side; same seed-at-HCM-dispatch + read-via-callback pattern + same cross-phase-reuse intent.
- **ADR-0165** — the phase-18.2 decoder-side callback-surface extension that ADR-0174 EXTENDS to the encoder side via chain-field reuse. ADR-0174 is structurally the encoder-side mirror of ADR-0165.
- **ADR-0171** (lands at phase-19.1 Task 7) — the header-mode state machine that drives the response_headers stage's per-stream encode-side dispatch invocation that consumes the new accessors via Task 9's attributes-builder.
- **ADR-0173** (lands at phase-19.1 Task 10) — the per-route policy/stats SHARED discipline; the ext_proc response_attributes envelope is per-stream + cross-route SHARED in the same sense the 9-counter filterStats are SHARED.
- **ADR-0175** (lands at phase-19.2) — the encode-side body-buffering primitive; orthogonal to ADR-0174's socket/TLS/listener accessors; both extend `EncoderFilterCallbacks` but in non-overlapping concerns.

## ADR-0175: NEW encode-side body-buffering framework primitive analogous to ADR-0128 decode-side — buffers response body across `EncodeData` calls until end_stream; exposes the buffered bytes via a new `EncoderFilterCallbacks` method (`BufferEncodedBody()`); releases the buffered-and-possibly-mutated body to the downstream wire-write path after the filter's response; REFUTED at SPEC §5.P11 in-session scrape → fires load-bearing at 19.2 IMPL; ADR-0044 escape-valve firing at SPEC time per BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h); cross-phase-reusable for any future filter needing encode-side body accumulation

**Status:** Accepted (§Context drafted at the phase-19 parent SPEC commit per ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention; §Decision + §Consequences full bodies land at phase-19.2 IMPL Task 2 — the NEW `EncoderFilterCallbacks.BufferEncodedBody() []byte` accessor at `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go` + the chain-side `c.encodeBuf` accumulation discipline at `internal/filter/http/chain.go` `RunEncodeData`; cap-counter double-count fix + §Decision (ii) clarification at Task 2 rework `8ac3939`; SOLE-CONSUMER at 19.2 is `internal/filter/http/extproc/`'s `response_body` stage dispatch — second-consumer trigger reserved for future encode-side body-transformation filters).
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19.2 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 (ADR-on-impl convention + escape-valve discipline — this ADR's §Context is authored at SPEC time from the in-session §5.P11 REFUTED scrape). The SYMMETRIC counterpart to ADR-0128 (the phase-13 decode-side body-buffering primitive); the SECOND envoy-go framework primitive in the body-handling family (after ADR-0128); the SECOND encode-side framework primitive (after ADR-0131 `OverwriteBody` — distinct from this primitive in semantics: `OverwriteBody` is a per-call replacement, ADR-0175 is buffer-and-hold).
**Lands-in:** Task 2 of phase-19.2 PLAN (the encode-side body-buffering primitive's framework introduction at `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go` + `internal/filter/http/chain.go`; consumed at Task 7 by `internal/filter/http/extproc/extproc.go`'s response_body stage dispatch).

### Context

The phase-19 SPEC's §5.P11 in-session empirical scrape REFUTED the BRAINSTORM §3.3 CONDITIONAL hypothesis for encode-side body-buffering — confirming the framework gap on master tip `5927b55`:

**`internal/filter/http/chain.go:373-405` (master tip) `RunEncodeData`** dispatches `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` as **park-only** — the chain parks (resume signal advances) but does NOT accumulate body bytes across `EncodeData` calls. The chain.go:400-404 comment is load-bearing:

```go
// Iteration completed; record the chunk's size for the encode-side cap.
// Only the running total is tracked — the bytes have already been
// forwarded down the encode chain on this call, so no replay buffer is
// needed (encode-side StopIterationAndBuffer is park-only per Task 6).
c.encodeBufLen += len(data)
```

**The phase-14 `OverwriteBody` primitive (ADR-0131 §Decision (vi))** is a **per-call replacement** — called from inside `EncodeData(data, endStream)`, the call substitutes the response body on that single call BEFORE the wire-write path consumes it. It is NOT a buffer-and-hold-until-end-of-stream primitive. ADR-0131's `OverwriteBody` was designed for the compressor use-case (full-body replacement on the FIRST EncodeData call when endStream is true) — not for ext_proc's "buffer the full body across multiple EncodeData calls, ship it to the processor as a single ProcessingRequest, receive a possibly-mutated body, release the mutated body to the wire-write path".

**Phase 19's `response_body_mode = BUFFERED`** (at 19.2 — body-mode arms PARSE-REJECT in 19.1) requires the filter to hold the response body across multiple `EncodeData` calls until end-of-stream, then ship the full body in the `response_body` ProcessingRequest stage, then receive the `BodyResponse.CommonResponse.body_mutation` (if any), then apply the mutation (replace or clear), then release the buffered-and-possibly-mutated body to the downstream wire-write path. This is the EXACT symmetric pattern of phase-13 ADR-0128 decode-side body-buffering — except on the encode side.

**The fix lands at 19.2 IMPL** — a NEW encode-side body-buffering primitive analogous to ADR-0128. Anticipated shape (IMPL settles the exact API):

```go
// EncoderFilterCallbacks gains a new method at 19.2 IMPL per ADR-0175.
type EncoderFilterCallbacks interface {
    // ... existing methods including OverwriteBody (ADR-0131) ...

    // BufferEncodedBody returns the buffered encode-side body bytes
    // accumulated by the chain when the filter has returned
    // DataStopIterationAndBuffer on prior EncodeData calls. The bytes
    // are valid until the filter calls ContinueEncoding(). After
    // ContinueEncoding(), the buffer is released to the downstream
    // wire-write path; a subsequent BufferEncodedBody() returns nil.
    //
    // Per ADR-0175 §Decision; symmetric to phase-13 ADR-0128 decode-side
    // body-buffering. Cross-phase-reusable for any encode-side filter
    // needing body accumulation.
    BufferEncodedBody() []byte
}
```

**Chain-side changes** to `RunEncodeData` at `chain.go:373-405`: replace the "park-only" disposition with a proper buffer-accumulation discipline mirroring the decode-side at `RunDecodeData` (which uses `c.decodeBuf` to accumulate). Add an `encodeBuf []byte` field to the chain struct; on `DataStopIterationAndBuffer`, accumulate the bytes into `encodeBuf` AND DO NOT forward downstream; on resume (via `ContinueEncoding()`), forward `encodeBuf` downstream + clear it. The chain's existing `encodeBufLen` running total can stay as the size cap (same `filterBufferLimitBytes` enforcement). The IMPL settles whether to overflow-error symmetrically to the decode side (via `errEncodeBufferOverflow` + connection reset) or allow up to the cap. Mirror the existing decode-side discipline.

**LoC estimate**: ~150-300 LoC chain-side changes + ~30-50 LoC `EncoderFilterCallbacks` extension + ~30-50 LoC `*encoderCB` reader method + ~150-250 LoC unit tests (mirroring the decode-side ADR-0128 test coverage).

**Cross-phase reuse intent.** Any future encode-side filter that needs to inspect or mutate the FULL response body (rather than per-chunk replacement) consumes ADR-0175's buffer-and-hold primitive. Current ext_proc is the sole consumer at 19.2 — anchoring the primitive at this phase ensures the cost is paid ONCE; the second consumer would be a future encode-side filter analogous to a hypothetical response-content-rewrite filter.

**ADR-0044 escape-valve fires at SPEC time** per BRAINSTORM §11 lesson (h) — IN-SESSION SPEC scrape closure of the most-likely escape-valve surface. The brainstorm's CONDITIONAL hypothesis at §3.3 + §10 is empirically confirmed at SPEC time; the 19.2 IMPL session does NOT need to discover this gap mid-impl. Mirrors the phase-18.2 ADR-0165 firing — except the phase-19 surface is now empirically established at SPEC time.

References: parent SPEC §3 + §5.P11 + §6 amendment 11. 19.2 README §Scope. ADR-0044 (the ADR-on-impl + escape-valve discipline). ADR-0128 (the phase-13 decode-side body-buffering primitive — ADR-0175 is its encode-side mirror). ADR-0131 (the phase-14 `OverwriteBody` encode-side primitive — distinct from ADR-0175's buffer-and-hold semantics).

### Decision

**(i) Method name + signature LOCKED per planner-time D1.** A new method lands on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` in `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`:

```go
// BufferEncodedBody returns the chain-accumulated encode-side body bytes
// the chain has appended on prior EncodeData(data, endStream) calls where
// this (or another encode-side) filter returned DataStopIterationAndBuffer.
BufferEncodedBody() []byte
```

The verb-first form `BufferEncodedBody` (NOT the verbatim mirror `BufferedEncodedBody`) is chosen per planner-time D1 — it parallels the existing encoder-side accessor surface conventions (`OverwriteBody`, `EncodeData`) for callsite readability (`f.ecb.BufferEncodedBody()` reads more naturally than `f.ecb.BufferedEncodedBody()`). The return slice ALIASES the chain's internal buffer; callers MUST treat the underlying bytes as read-aliased per ADR-0071's single-dispatch-goroutine invariant (the buffering filter holds the dispatch goroutine when it parks; concurrent mutation from another goroutine is undefined behavior). The doc-comment on the interface method explicitly names the cross-phase reuse intent (an encode-side `lua` body-callback filter; an encode-side content-injection filter) per ADR-0044 framework-primitive doc-comment discipline.

**(ii) Chain-layout choice — `c.encodeBuf` lives at the FilterChain level (divergence-from-SPEC documented).** SPEC §3.1 anticipated per-encoderCB layout (`encodeBuf []byte` field on each `*encoderCB`). The IMPL settles **chain-level layout** instead — `c.encodeBuf []byte` field on `FilterChain` — for three concrete reasons:

1. **Decode-side precedent symmetry.** ADR-0128's decode-side accumulation lives at the chain level via `c.decodeBuf` (chain.go:64 + RunDecodeData at chain.go:282). The SPEC's per-encoderCB framing was an artifact of the original symmetric-mirror premise; the actual symmetric mirror at the chain-field LEVEL is the chain-level `c.encodeBuf` field. Per-encoderCB layout would have created asymmetric decode-vs-encode accumulation layouts for no semantic benefit. The symmetry is FIELD-LOCATION-ONLY — the release-as-data semantic that the encode side adds in `RunEncodeData`'s `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` arm (post-park reassign `data = c.encodeBuf` + clear + cap-counter subtract on end_stream) has NO decode-side counterpart: `RunDecodeData`'s buffer arm appends + parks + advances WITHOUT releasing the union back into `data`, and there is NO `DecoderFilterCallbacks.BufferedBody()` reader on the decoder-side interface (decode-side filters read the full body from `DecodeData(buf, endStream=true)` via HCM-level pre-accumulation per ADR-0128 — recorded as a structural layer-asymmetry at §Decision (vii) below; the SPEC §6.3 `callbacks.BufferedBody()` reference is a loose analogy noted in PROGRESS.md preamble).
2. **Chain-iteration model alignment.** RunEncodeData iterates with a single `c.encodeIdx` cursor + a single `data` local variable — neither carries an "owning filter index" context that the chain dispatcher could use to look up "which encoderCB's buffer to release". Per-encoderCB layout would have required restructuring the iteration model to carry the buffering-filter index across park-resume cycles; chain-level layout avoids the restructuring.
3. **Cap-check natural composition.** The existing `c.encodeBufLen` cap-check at the top of RunEncodeData (chain.go:377-379) is chain-scoped (per-stream). The accumulating buffer must compose with the same cap; chain-level layout makes the composition trivial (single `len(c.encodeBuf)` + `len(data)` against `filterBufferLimitBytes`). Per-encoderCB layout would have required aggregating across encoderCBs for the cap-check.

The functional contract is IDENTICAL to per-encoderCB layout for the single-buffering-filter case (which is the only case the SPEC anticipates — ext_proc is the sole consumer at 19.2 and emits exactly one body-stage buffering filter per direction). If a future cross-phase consumer wants multiple SIMULTANEOUSLY-buffering encoder filters on the same chain, the chain-level layout would still work (the union of all buffered chunks ends up in one slice, in encoder-arrival order); a per-encoderCB layout would NOT serve that case better since the wire-write path consumes one body. The chain-level choice is forward-compatible.

**(iii) `RunEncodeData` accumulation discipline.** On `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` from the filter at `c.encodeIdx`:

1. Append `data` to `c.encodeBuf` (in-place via the chain's owning backing array).
2. Call `c.parkEncode(ctx)`. The dispatch goroutine blocks on `c.encodeResumeCh` until a `ContinueEncoding()` signal arrives (or `ctx.Done()` fires).
3. On resume **at end_stream**: assign `data = c.encodeBuf` AND clear `c.encodeBuf = nil`. Decrement `c.encodeIdx`. The next filter in REVERSE-iteration order receives the (possibly-mutated) accumulated buffer as its `data` payload — closing the buffering window per the SPEC §3.1 "release downstream + clear" semantic.
4. On resume **at !end_stream (mid-stream chunk)**: leave `c.encodeBuf` intact + decrement `c.encodeIdx`. The next filter receives the ORIGINAL per-call `data` — preserving the cross-call accumulation invariant (multiple `RunEncodeData(chunk_i, false)` calls with the same buffering filter accumulate `chunk_i` into `c.encodeBuf` and the buffer persists until end_stream).

The `DataStopIterationNoBuffer` disposition stays park-only / continue-iteration WITHOUT accumulation, exactly as pre-ADR-0175 — DIVERGING `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` from `DataStopIterationNoBuffer` per the SPEC §3.1 mandate.

**(iv) Overflow handling SYMMETRIC to decode-side per planner-time D7.** The existing `c.encodeBufLen + len(data) > filterBufferLimitBytes` cap-check at the top of `RunEncodeData` (chain.go:377-379) stays valid post-ADR-0175 — the same `filterBufferLimitBytes = 1 << 20` cap governs encode-side accumulation. The `errEncodeBufferOverflow` sentinel (chain.go:32) is returned BEFORE iterating any filter on a cap-exceeding call; the HCM dispatch path resets the connection (H1 close, H2 RST_STREAM) on this sentinel. **SYMMETRIC** to the decode-side `errDecodeBufferOverflow`-equivalent path that synthesizes a 413 local reply on `RunDecodeData` cap-exceed — the wire shapes differ (decode synthesizes a response body; encode resets the connection since the response has already started flowing) but the cap discipline + the sentinel-return-before-filter-iteration are uniform across decode + encode sides.

**(v) `ContinueEncoding()` semantic UNCHANGED.** `encoderCB.ContinueEncoding()` continues to be a signal-only non-blocking channel send on `c.encodeResumeCh` (chain.go:555-560). The release-and-clear discipline lives in `RunEncodeData`'s post-park branch (per §iii above), NOT in `ContinueEncoding()` — the chain dispatcher is the source of truth for buffer state mutation, the callback is just a wake-up signal. This preserves the ADR-0071 single-dispatch-goroutine invariant: only the dispatch goroutine ever writes to `c.encodeBuf`.

**(vi) DISTINCT from ADR-0131 `OverwriteBody`.** The phase-14 `OverwriteBody(b []byte)` primitive is a **per-call replacement** — called from inside `EncodeData(data, endStream)`, it substitutes `resp.Body` on that single call BEFORE the wire-write path consumes it; the chain forwards `b` downstream immediately (the existing `c.encodeBodyOverride` + `EncodeBodyOverride()` getter at chain.go:573-576 + chain.go:627-629 handle the substitution). ADR-0175 `BufferEncodedBody()` is **buffer-and-hold** — the chain accumulates bytes across `EncodeData` calls + releases at end_stream. The two primitives are **COMPLEMENTARY**, BOTH stay on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` post-19.2, and serve distinct use-cases:
- `OverwriteBody`: phase-14 compressor (gzip-encode the full body, replace in one call).
- `BufferEncodedBody`: phase-19.2 ext_proc body-mode (accumulate full body, ship to processor as one ProcessingRequest, receive mutation, release).
- Future encode-side filters (named at §Context cross-phase forward-pointers) may choose either based on their semantics.

**(vii) ADR-0128 asymmetry recorded.** ADR-0128's decode-side body-accumulation lands at the **HCM-level** (`internal/filter/hcm/connection.go`'s `bodyBuf` field per the §Decision (i) synthetic empty-terminal `RunDecodeData` + §Decision (ii) Content-Length reconciliation) — the body bytes are accumulated by HCM BEFORE the filter chain runs; the decode-side filter receives the full body as the `buf` argument when `endStream=true` on its `DecodeData` callback. ADR-0175's encode-side body-accumulation lands at the **chain-level** (`c.encodeBuf`) — the encode chain itself accumulates across iterations because the HCM-level pre-accumulation pattern does NOT apply on the encode side (the response body is materialized upstream-of-HCM and passed to `RunEncodeData` in a single call per the phase-14 ADR-0131 §Context observation). The asymmetry is structural — neither side could mirror the other's layer without significant framework restructuring. The phase-13 + phase-19.2 framework primitives compose to provide symmetric SEMANTICS (full-body inspection-then-mutate on both directions) via DIFFERENT layers (HCM-level decode + chain-level encode).

**(viii) Cross-phase reuse intent.** Any future encode-side filter needing full-body inspection or mutation consumes `BufferEncodedBody()` without re-paying the chain-side plumbing cost. Specifically named at §Context + at the callback doc-comment (forward-pointers for grep-archaeology + future-implementer guidance):
- **A hypothetical encode-side `lua` body-callback filter** (response-body Lua transforms — analogous to the reference-Envoy `envoy.filters.http.lua` filter's `response_body_buffer_limit_bytes` body-callback mode). Would consume `BufferEncodedBody()` from inside its `EncodeData` callback to apply Lua transforms to the full response body.
- **An encode-side content-injection filter** (HTML-rewrite / response-header-driven body splice — a future filter analogous to reference-Envoy `envoy.filters.http.tap` or a hypothetical "response body injection" filter). Would consume `BufferEncodedBody()` to splice content into the response body before downstream emission.

Neither consumer exists at 19.2 — the primitive is anchored ONCE at 19.2 IMPL to amortize the framework surgery cost against the SINGLE current consumer (ext_proc body-mode) AND the named-forward-pointer future consumers. Per ADR-0044's framework-primitive amortization discipline.

### Consequences

- **Framework deltas land at three files**: `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go` (~+45 LoC: 1 new interface method + ~40 LoC GoDoc citing ADR-0175 + cross-phase reuse intent), `internal/filter/http/chain.go` (~+45 LoC: 1 new `encodeBuf []byte` chain field + accumulation discipline in `RunEncodeData` `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` switch arm + 1 new reader method `*encoderCB.BufferEncodedBody()`), `internal/filter/http/chain_test.go` (~+250 LoC: 4 new tests Group N+4 + N+5). NO new file lands; NO new test-helper package lands. The 4 in-tree test-double `EncoderFilterCallbacks` implementations (`callbacks_test.go` `*fakeEncoderCB`; `bandwidthlimit/bandwidthlimit_test.go` `*fakeEncoderCB`; `compressor/compressor_test.go` `*fakeCallbacks`; `extproc/extproc_test.go` `*fakeECB`) gain a zero-value `BufferEncodedBody() []byte { return nil }` stub method to preserve the compile-time conformance assertions.
- **This is envoy-go's FIRST encode-side body-buffering framework primitive.** Pre-19.2 the encode-side `DataStopIterationAndBuffer` was park-only (no replay buffer; the chain.go:400-404 comment "encode-side StopIterationAndBuffer is park-only per Task 6" — now updated to reflect ADR-0175 accumulation). Post-19.2 the disposition is properly buffer-and-park-and-release per the SPEC's symmetric-mirror premise.
- **The pre-existing `c.encodeBufLen` cap-check at chain.go:377-379 stays valid AND now ALSO governs accumulated-buffer overflow.** The cap is the union of "all encode bytes ever sent through `RunEncodeData`" (the running `c.encodeBufLen` counter) — accumulation does not bypass the cap because the bytes flow through `RunEncodeData` as `data` arguments which contribute to `c.encodeBufLen`. The sentinel + connection-reset wire path stays the source of truth on overflow per ADR-0076.
- **Future encode-side filters can REUSE the primitive** without additional framework surgery. Named consumers (forward-pointer per §Decision (viii)): a hypothetical encode-side `lua` body-callback filter; an encode-side content-injection filter. Neither exists today; the primitive is anchored at 19.2 IMPL to amortize the cost.
- **`OverwriteBody` stays for per-call use-cases.** ADR-0131's per-call replacement primitive is UNCHANGED by ADR-0175 — both primitives live on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` post-19.2 and the choice between them is a filter-author decision based on semantics (per-call replacement vs buffer-and-hold). Phase-14 compressor continues to use `OverwriteBody` unchanged. Phase-19.2 ext_proc uses `BufferEncodedBody` for its body-stage flow (Task 7 wires this).
- **The asymmetry with ADR-0128 (HCM-level decode vs chain-level encode) is RECORDED** at §Decision (vii) for future-implementer reference. Future framework changes should NOT attempt to unify the two layers — the structural mismatch is load-bearing per phase-13 + phase-14's framework-as-is constraints. Symmetric semantics are achievable via different layers; symmetric layers are not the goal.
- **NO change to `ContinueEncoding()`'s signal-only semantic.** ADR-0071's single-dispatch-goroutine invariant continues to hold — the chain dispatcher is the only goroutine that writes to `c.encodeBuf`; the callback method is just a wake-up signal. Future concurrency reviewers can rely on this discipline; the race-detector clean test (`TestEncoderCB_BufferEncodedBody_RaceDetectorCleanUnderConcurrentEncodeDataAndContinueEncoding`) pins it.
- **BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT `## HTTPFilterCallbacks` extension** at phase-19.2 Task 10's 7-edit bundle adds `BufferEncodedBody() []byte` as the 7th NEW accessor on `EncoderFilterCallbacks` (the 6 ADR-0174 accessors already document the encoder-side surface; ADR-0175 adds the buffer-and-hold reader). The §13.5 §Decision pull-quote lands at Task 10 per planner-time D9.
- **Cross-references with future ADRs.** If a future phase lands a `RevertEncodeHeaders` callback (per ADR-0131 §Decision (vii) forward-pointer), ADR-0175's `BufferEncodedBody` primitive composes naturally with it (the filter inspects the buffered body, decides to revert headers, then releases the buffer). If a future encode-side streaming framework phase lands chunk-by-chunk RunEncodeData (per ADR-0131 §Consequences forward-pointer), `BufferEncodedBody` continues to work via the same accumulation discipline but the cross-call accumulation matters more (each chunk contributes to the running buffer rather than the body arriving in one call). No ADR-0175 amendment fires in either case.
- **Decode-side asymmetry — no decode-side analog of this primitive at 19.2.** `DecoderFilterCallbacks` has no `OverwriteBody` equivalent (and ADR-0175 itself is ENCODE-side; the decode-side accumulation is HCM-level per ADR-0128 §Decision (vii) above). At phase 19.2 IMPL Task 7 the ext_proc filter's decode-side body mutation arm (Task 6 `body_mutation.body` REPLACE / `body_mutation.clear_body` CLEAR) lands the mutation in the per-filter `f.decodeBodyBuf` field BUT cannot deliver the mutated bytes to the upstream wire-write path — there is NO decode-side `OverwriteBody` primitive to substitute the request body, and the HCM-level `bodyBuf` (`connection.go` H1) / `h2req.Body` (`h2dispatch.go` H2) are captured BEFORE the filter chain mutation lands. The Content-Length reconciliation on `f.decodeHeaders` IS delivered to the upstream (same map identity); the body bytes themselves are NOT. The decode-side body-mutation-delivery limitation is documented at ADR-0168 §Consequences (Task 7 refresh paragraph at §C-LIMITATION) + at the KNOWN LIMITATION doc-comment on `(*filter).DecodeData` in `extproc.go`. A future phase adding the decode-side `OverwriteBody` analog (a new `DecoderFilterCallbacks` framework method symmetric to ADR-0131) is the closure path — speculative `ADR-0178` per planner-time D10 forward-pointer; NOT consumed at 19.2.

## ADR-0176: ADR-0045 split-application for phase 19 — phase 19 (`http-filter-ext-proc`) is SPLIT into sub-phases `19.1-http-filter-ext-proc-headers` + `19.2-http-filter-ext-proc-body` at the phase-19 SPEC commit; the split is by feature-class; the SPEC §5 empirical-pin resolution + the in-session SPEC-time REFUTATION of §5.P11 + §5.P12 (both fire ADR-0174 + ADR-0175 load-bearing rather than provisionally) ENLARGED the BRAINSTORM's HIGH split-readiness leaning beyond the single-row threshold

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Doctrine:** Phase 19 §9 family-row. ADR-0045 (surface-split release valve) + `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §6.2 (planner-time / SPEC-time split discipline) + ADR-0044 (SPEC-time-anticipation-revision of the ADR count). Documentation-of-application ADR — mirrors phase-08's ADR-0084 + phase-18's ADR-0164.
**Lands-in:** This phase-19 parent SPEC commit (landed IN FULL — the split decision is complete at SPEC time).

### Context

The phase-19 BRAINSTORM §1.4 flagged ADR-0045 split-readiness **HIGH** — the SECOND §9 family-row to flag HIGH after phase 18 — and surveyed three candidate splits (split-by-feature-class RECOMMENDED, split-by-service-mode, single-row). The brainstorm instructed the SPEC author to treat single-row as the exception requiring justification, not the default — per the phase-18 precedent (HIGH leaning + DID split + clean rollup). The phase-19 SPEC session's §5 empirical-pin resolution (all 13 §10 pins resolved IN-SESSION against `go-control-plane v1.32.4` + reference Envoy v1.37.2 per ADR-0004) CONFIRMS the HIGH leaning AND ENLARGES it:

1. **§5.P1** enumerated a **22-field `ExternalProcessor` message** + `ProcessingMode` (6 fields) + `ExtProcPerRoute` (oneof 2 arms) + `ExtProcOverrides` (5 fields) + `ExtProcHttpService` (1 field) + `HeaderForwardingRules` (2 fields) + `MetadataOptions` (nested) + the `service/ext_proc/v3` proto package's `ProcessingRequest` (6-arm oneof + 3 top-level) + `ProcessingResponse` (7-arm oneof + 3 top-level) + `HttpHeaders` / `HttpBody` / `HttpTrailers` / `HeadersResponse` / `BodyResponse` / `TrailersResponse` / `CommonResponse` (5 fields incl. ResponseStatus enum) / `BodyMutation` (3-arm oneof) / `ImmediateResponse` (5) / `HeaderMutation` / `GrpcStatus`. The proto surface spans TWO proto packages and is **larger than phase 18's** (phase 18 spanned `ext_authz/v3` + `auth/v3` of similar shape; phase 19 spans `ext_proc/v3` + `service/ext_proc/v3` with higher cardinality).

2. **§5.P10** confirmed the `grpc_service` (bidi-stream `Process`) and `http_service` (per-stage JSON POST) arms diverge entirely in the call-and-marshal layer + the bidi-stream lifecycle adds a half-close + CloseSend discipline NEW for envoy-go.

3. **§5.P9** + the `ProcessingMode` BodySendMode enum walk confirmed the headers-only and BUFFERED-body envelopes are structurally distinct sub-surfaces — the headers stages run synchronously per-stage; the BUFFERED-body stages add the decode-side ADR-0128 reuse + the NEW encode-side body-buffering primitive ADR-0175.

4. **§5.P11 REFUTED** at SPEC time — the encode-side body-buffering primitive does NOT exist on master tip (`chain.go:403` "encode-side StopIterationAndBuffer is park-only" + reads of `RunEncodeData` confirm no replay buffer). **ADR-0175 fires load-bearing in 19.2** — a NEW framework primitive analogous to ADR-0128 lands. The brainstorm's CONDITIONAL hypothesis is empirically confirmed at SPEC time, not deferred to IMPL discovery.

5. **§5.P12 REFUTED** at SPEC time — the encode-side filter callback extension surface does NOT exist on master tip (`callbacks.go:160-184` — `EncoderFilterCallbacks` has only `ContinueEncoding` + `EncodeHeaders/Data/Trailers` + `OverwriteBody`; the 6 ADR-0165 accessors are decode-side only). **ADR-0174 fires load-bearing in 19.1** — a NEW symmetric `EncoderFilterCallbacks` extension lands. The brainstorm's CONDITIONAL hypothesis is empirically confirmed at SPEC time.

Refined post-§5 LoC estimate: ~5500–7000 LoC production (filter package ~2500–3500 + `*ProcessorClient` bidi-stream wrapper ~250–400 + JSON codec ~400–700 + ADR-0174 callback-surface extension ~250–400 + ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive ~400–700 + two test-helpers + fixture drivers ~700–1100). **Well above the ADR-0045 1500-LoC trigger.** Combined task count estimated at ~35–45 across both sub-phases — crosses both ADR-0045 thresholds (~25 tasks, ~1500 LoC) EMPHATICALLY. Single-row landing is NOT viable.

### Decision

**Phase 19 is SPLIT into two sub-phases at the phase-19 SPEC commit, per ADR-0045 + `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md` §6.2.** The split is **by feature-class** — the structurally clean cut RECOMMENDED by the BRAINSTORM §1.4 and confirmed by the empirical pin findings. Rationale for choosing split-by-feature-class over split-by-service-mode (the phase-18 precedent):

- **Two framework deltas at distinct sub-phase boundaries.** ADR-0174 (encode-side callback symmetry) is needed for `response_attributes` population at the response_headers stage → lands at 19.1. ADR-0175 (encode-side body-buffering) is needed for `response_body_mode = BUFFERED` → lands at 19.2. Each sub-phase's framework lift is bounded and reviewable independently.
- **gRPC is the "real" deployment shape for ext_proc.** The `http_service` arm is a proto-constrained-to-headers-only secondary mode (per `ExtProcHttpService.http_service` doc-comment). Splitting by service-mode would put the major surface (gRPC bidi-stream + body modes) in 19.2 and the minor (headers-only HTTP) in 19.1 — inverted from phase 18.x where the HTTP arm was the foundational larger half.
- **Headers-stage MVP is operationally useful in itself.** 19.1 alone delivers a usable ext_proc filter (header injection, mutation, immediate_response deny, mode-override). 19.2 extends to body manipulation. Mirrors the phase-13 buffer + phase-14 compressor + phase-18.1 ext_authz pattern (foundational scaffold first, feature-extension second).
- **The body-stage framework primitives (ADR-0175) land alongside their consumers** at 19.2, avoiding the "framework introduced at sub-phase N, first consumer at sub-phase N+M" anti-pattern.

**Sub-phase scope:**

- **19.1 (`http-filter-ext-proc-headers`)** — the foundational filter: the NEW `internal/filter/http/extproc/` package, the dual-mode `compiledConfig` envelope (BOTH `grpc_service` AND `http_service` arms ACTIVATED in 19.1 — body-mode arms PARSE-REJECT in 19.1 and 19.2 activates them), the bidi-stream framework primitive at `internal/grpcclient/` extension (ADR-0169), the JSON codec for `ProcessingRequest`/`ProcessingResponse` (ADR-0170 — filter-local), the headers stages (request_headers + response_headers), the per-stage `CommonResponse.header_mutation` application, the multi-stage `ImmediateResponse` deny path (request_headers + response_headers stages), the ProcessingMode state machine + mode-override re-eval, the `clear_route_cache` + `route_cache_action` precedence + `cb.ClearRouteCache()` reuse, the per-route 5th-canonical REUSE + SHARED-stats + the 9-counter filter stat surface, the error posture, the bidi-stream lifecycle, the async-resume outbound-call leg, boot-registration, the BOTH-DECODE-AND-ENCODE filter shape + `filterStats` + the deny-path `SendLocalReply` mechanism, **ADR-0174 (symmetric `EncoderFilterCallbacks` extension)**. 19.1-landing ADRs: ADR-0167 + ADR-0168 + ADR-0169 + ADR-0170 + ADR-0171 (header-mode portion) + ADR-0172 (header_mutation + ImmediateResponse-at-headers portion) + ADR-0173 + ADR-0174. Differential fixture `0022-http-ext-proc-grpc`. 24th fuzzer `FuzzExtProcConfigParse`.

- **19.2 (`http-filter-ext-proc-body`)** — the body-stage extension: within the existing `internal/filter/http/extproc/` package, the body-stage activation (ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT — body-mode PARSE-REJECT lift), the body-stage dispatch + `body_mutation` discipline (ADR-0172 body-mode AMENDMENT — body_mutation body/clear; request_body via ADR-0128 decode-side body-buffering reuse; response_body via NEW ADR-0175 encode-side body-buffering primitive; `CommonResponse.status = CONTINUE_AND_REPLACE` handling), the multi-stage `ImmediateResponse` extension to body stages (request_body + response_body stages), **ADR-0175 (NEW encode-side body-buffering framework primitive)**. 19.2-landing ADRs: ADR-0175 + ADR-0168 §Decision AMENDMENT + ADR-0171 body-mode AMENDMENT + ADR-0172 body-mode AMENDMENT. Differential fixture `0023-http-ext-proc-body`. 25th fuzzer `FuzzProcessingResponseMapping`.

**19.1 ships first.** ROADMAP row `19` flips `planned → in-progress` at the phase-19 SPEC commit with `sub-phases: 19.1, 19.2`; row `19.1` is added `in-progress` (its SPEC is authored at this commit); row `19.2` is added `planned` (depends-on `19.1`; its SPEC is drafted at 19.2's lifecycle-state 1). The parent row `19` flips `in-progress → done` AT THE SAME COMMIT as `19.2`'s phase-done — the 19.2 phase-done commit closes both rows in one operation, and its commit-message body names both transitions for grep-verifiability (mirrors the phase-05/06/07/08/18 parent-rollup discipline).

**SPEC-time ADR-count revision:** the BRAINSTORM §7 anticipated 7-9 ADRs (ADR-0167..ADR-0173 + CONDITIONAL ADR-0174/0175). This SPEC lands **10 ADRs total** (ADR-0167..ADR-0175 — both conditionals fire load-bearing per the SPEC-time scrape closure of §5.P11/§5.P12 — plus ADR-0176 the split-application ADR added per ADR-0044's SPEC-time-anticipation-revision discipline, mirroring phase-08 ADR-0084 + phase-18 ADR-0164). **Next-free ADR after phase 19 is ADR-0177.** NO ADR-0125 amendment paragraph (ADR-0173 records the explicit no-amendment 5th-canonical-REUSE decision — SECOND CONSECUTIVE §9 row after phase 18 to do so).

### Consequences

## ADR-0177: NEW `internal/httpclient/` framework primitive — Options struct (Timeout + RetryPolicy + TLSConfig) + `Client.Do` synchronous wrapper over `*http.Client`; **CLOSES ADR-0159 §Future Work forward-pointer load-bearing** (third-consumer trigger fired per phase-20 Q2 EXTRACT NOW); 3 consumers at introduction time (jwks Fetcher post-ADR-0150 AMENDMENT + extauthz httpAuthClient post-ADR-0159 AMENDMENT + oauth2 token_endpoint POST NEW); cross-phase-reusable for any future outbound-HTTP consumer

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit (this commit); §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 2 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. Closes the ADR-0159 §Future Work forward-pointer load-bearing — FIRST §9 family-row to close a prior-phase load-bearing forward-pointer. Cross-phase-reusable framework primitive per the phase-16 ADR-0142 + ADR-0144 + phase-17 ADR-0150 cross-phase-reuse-at-introduction-time discipline.
**Lands-in:** Task 2 of phase-20 PLAN (NEW `internal/httpclient/` package + paired in-place ADR-0150 + ADR-0159 §Decision AMENDMENTs).

### Context

Phase 20 fires the **third-consumer trigger condition** for the shared `internal/httpclient/` package extraction. The trigger was planted at phase 18.1 ADR-0159 §Context + §Consequences + §Future Work: "the natural trigger to generalize into `internal/httpclient/` is the THIRD outbound-HTTP consumer — a future `oauth2` phase needs an outbound token-endpoint POST that IS synchronous-per-request like ext_authz's; when oauth2 brainstorms, the `internal/httpclient/` generalization should be reconsidered with three consumers in view." Phase 20 oauth2's token_endpoint POST is exactly that structural shape (synchronous-per-request POST; matches ext_authz HTTP-mode; differs from jwks's cached/async shape).

**Phase-20 SPEC-time scoping (per BRAINSTORM Q2 EXTRACT NOW + phase-20 SPEC §3.1):** the SPEC author resolves Q2 as **EXTRACT NOW** (vs DEFER-to-fourth-consumer). The 3-consumer view (jwks Fetcher + extauthz httpAuthClient + oauth2 token_endpoint POST) is sufficient design-pressure to motivate the shared abstraction without over-fitting to any single consumer's lifecycle.

**Public surface** (settled at phase-20 SPEC §3.1; the IMPL confirms the exact signature at Task 2):

```go
type Options struct {
    Timeout     time.Duration
    RetryPolicy RetryPolicy
    TLSConfig   *tls.Config
}

type RetryPolicy struct {
    Attempts        int           // 0 = no retries (matches upstream Envoy v1.37.2 wire default per phase-20 §20.P1)
    PerAttemptDelay time.Duration
    RetryOnStatus   []int
}

type Client struct { /* *http.Client + Options */ }

func New(opts Options) *Client
func (c *Client) Do(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error)
```

**3 consumers at introduction time** (each gets a paired refactor at this IMPL Task 2):

1. **jwks Fetcher refactor** (paired ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT) — REPLACES the inline `http.Client` ownership at `internal/jwks/fetcher.go` with a `*httpclient.Client` constructor argument. ~40-60 LoC delta. Preserves the phase-17 retry-policy + timeout discipline verbatim.
2. **extauthz httpAuthClient refactor** (paired ADR-0159 §Decision AMENDMENT + §Future Work CLOSURE) — REPLACES the inline `http.Client` ownership at `internal/filter/http/extauthz/check.go` with a `*httpclient.Client` constructor argument. ~50-80 LoC delta. Preserves the phase-18.1 per-request cancellable + zero-retry semantics. **§Future Work CLOSED-AT-PHASE-20 paragraph appended.**
3. **oauth2 token_endpoint POST** (NEW at phase 20) — consumes the new primitive at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/oauth_client.go::postTokenEndpoint`. Synchronous-per-request POST with the 4-field auth-code template byte-exact per AMEND-5 (phase-20 ADR-0185) + 3-field refresh-token template.

**Zero-retry default per §20.P1 RATIFIED.** Upstream Envoy v1.37.2 applies zero-retry default at the oauth2 token_endpoint POST (no automatic retry; explicit operator config required). The Options struct's `RetryPolicy{Attempts: 0}` zero-value mirrors this. The phase-17 jwks Fetcher's per-refresh-cycle retry is preserved via its caller passing `Options{RetryPolicy: RetryPolicy{...}}` non-zero; phase-18.1 ext_authz preserves zero-retry semantics via the zero-value default.

**Cross-phase reuse intent** (§Future Work plant at this ADR's §Future Work):
- Future ext_authz mTLS — consumes Options.TLSConfig
- Future jwt_authn alternative-issuer fetch — second-level cross-consumer of the jwks Fetcher refactor
- Future ratelimit gRPC TLS — TBD; mTLS-config wiring
- Other outbound-HTTP-from-filter primitives — each evaluated against the 3-consumer-baseline at their introduction time

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 2

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 2 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact Options-struct field roster + the `Client.Do` retry-loop discipline + the cross-phase-consumer integration paths. The §Consequences body documents the cross-package regression-window discipline (jwks + extauthz refactors must produce zero observable wire delta per phase-20 SPEC §12 item C8 + §14.5 D-gate).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT-anticipation paragraph (paired jwks refactor); ADR-0159 §Decision AMENDMENT + §Future Work CLOSURE-anticipation paragraph (paired extauthz refactor + first-§9-row-to-close-prior-phase-load-bearing-forward-pointer); ADR-0177 NEW; phase-20 SPEC §3.1 (framework-survey result); phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — landed at Task 2 of phase-20 PLAN per ADR-0044. §Decision body anchored at phase-20 IMPL sub-commit 2a (ADR-0177 introduction + tests + ADR-0150 + ADR-0159 in-place AMENDMENTS land in the same Task 2; the 3 sub-commit boundaries 2a/2b/2c preserve reviewer-clarity per planner-time D1).**

**(i) Public surface — `Options` + `RetryPolicy` + `Client` + `New` + `(*Client).Do`.** Five exported identifiers, matching the §Context pull-quote verbatim. `Options{Timeout time.Duration; RetryPolicy RetryPolicy; TLSConfig *tls.Config}` is the per-Client configuration envelope; `RetryPolicy{Attempts int; PerAttemptDelay time.Duration; RetryOnStatus []int}` is the status-driven retry envelope; `Client` wraps a stdlib `*http.Client` + the `Options`; `New(opts Options) *Client` constructs; `(*Client).Do(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error)` is the single synchronous entry point. Zero-Options is a no-op pass-through (zero Timeout = no client-imposed deadline; zero RetryPolicy = no retries; nil TLSConfig = stdlib default `crypto/tls` posture). Per planner-time D8 the singleton is constructed at `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot with `Options{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}` and shared across all 3 introduction-time consumers (jwks + extauthz + oauth2).

**(ii) Synchronous semantics — single `Do` entry point; no async API at this layer.** `Client.Do` blocks until the response is received OR the request context is canceled OR the underlying `*http.Client.Timeout` fires OR the retry budget is exhausted. The async-resume + dispatch-goroutine-parking semantics live ONE LAYER UP (in the consumer): ext_authz HTTP-mode parks the decode goroutine on the phase-09 async-resume primitive before invoking `Do`; jwks Fetcher invokes `Do` on a background-refresh goroutine; oauth2 token_endpoint POST will park the decode goroutine on async-resume per the same ext_authz pattern (per ADR-0185 §Decision). Keeping `Do` synchronous keeps the framework primitive minimal — each consumer composes its own async-resume context above the synchronous Do call.

**(iii) Per-Client wraps-`*http.Client` discipline.** Each `Client` allocates a fresh `*http.Client` at `New` time; the underlying transport defaults to `http.DefaultTransport` (its idle-conn pool + dial discipline) when `Options.TLSConfig` is nil. When `TLSConfig` is non-nil we CLONE `http.DefaultTransport` (`(*http.Transport).Clone()`) and install the supplied `TLSConfig` on the clone — preserving stdlib defaults (MaxIdleConns, IdleConnTimeout, etc.) while overriding the TLSClientConfig. Defensive fall-back to a minimal `&http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: opts.TLSConfig}` if a future Go version replaces the DefaultTransport's concrete type. The `*http.Client` is goroutine-safe per the net/http documentation; the wrapping `*Client` is therefore goroutine-safe for shared per-process boot-time singleton use.

**(iv) Retry loop discipline — STATUS-driven only; honors `req.Context().Err()` after every sleep.** `Do` iterates up to `Attempts+1` times; the loop body issues `c.httpClient.Do(req)`, returns transport errors VERBATIM (no auto-retry — transport-level error classification stays at the consumer per the ADR-0159 §5.P10 + ADR-0150 §11.P4 disciplines), and on a response checks `shouldRetryStatus(resp.StatusCode, RetryOnStatus)` — if false (or `Attempts == 0` or `RetryOnStatus` empty) returns the response verbatim; if true sleeps `PerAttemptDelay` (via `time.NewTimer` interruptible by `req.Context().Done()`) and re-checks `req.Context().Err()` post-sleep. A canceled context aborts the retry loop and returns the context error. Between attempts the prior response body is drained (`io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)`) then closed so the stdlib connection-pool can reuse the underlying conn (the net/http pool-reuse contract requires this discipline). Per-attempt request-body rewinding is NOT performed at this layer — the caller's `*http.Request.Body` rewind discipline is the caller's responsibility (the 3 introduction-time consumers all satisfy this trivially: jwks GET has nil body, extauthz POST uses `bytes.NewReader` which is naturally re-readable, oauth2 token_endpoint POST uses `strings.NewReader` which is similarly re-readable).

**(v) Cross-phase consumer threading paths (3 consumers at introduction time).**

  - **jwks Fetcher (ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT — paired refactor at sub-commit 2b).** `internal/jwks/jwks.go::Fetcher` REPLACES its internal `&http.Client{Timeout: defaultHTTPClientTimeout}` with a `*httpclient.Client` field threaded via the `New(uri, cacheDuration, asyncFetch, retryPolicy, httpClient)` constructor signature. The jwks-internal `doFetch` retry loop is PRESERVED VERBATIM at the `RetryPolicy{NumRetries, BaseInterval, MaxInterval}` shape (jwks's caller-configured retry policy carries the phase-17-pinned semantics — exponential `BaseInterval * 2^attempt` capped at `MaxInterval`); `doHTTPGet` delegates to `c.httpClient.Do(req)`. The httpclient `Options.RetryPolicy` is left ZERO at the jwks site — jwks owns its own retry loop because its exponential-backoff shape diverges from httpclient's fixed-`PerAttemptDelay` shape (a deliberate consumer-layer choice per ADR-0150 §11.P4).

  - **extauthz httpAuthClient (ADR-0159 §Decision AMENDMENT + §Future Work CLOSURE — paired refactor at sub-commit 2c).** `internal/filter/http/extauthz/check.go::httpAuthClient` REPLACES its internal `&http.Client{Timeout: timeout}` field with a `*httpclient.Client` field threaded via `buildHTTPCheckFn(hs, validateMutations, httpClient)`. The `checkFn` closure's `hac.client.Do(outReq)` is unchanged at the call-site shape (the `*httpclient.Client.Do` signature is `(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error)` — bit-for-bit identical to `(*http.Client).Do`). The httpclient `Options.Timeout` carries the `HttpService.server_uri.timeout` (per-target timeout); `Options.RetryPolicy` left ZERO per planner-time D2 (ext_authz has no retry-policy proto field; zero retry is the upstream-faithful semantic per §20.P1 + ADR-0159 §Decision (ii)).

  - **oauth2 token_endpoint POST (NEW at phase 20; lands at IMPL Task 10 per ADR-0185).** `internal/filter/http/oauth2/oauth_client.go::postTokenEndpoint` will consume the shared `*httpclient.Client` singleton via the oauth2 factory's `FactoryCtx`-threaded reference (per IMPL Task 11). Synchronous-per-request POST with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body; the `Options.Timeout` matches the oauth2 `token_endpoint_timeout` proto field; `Options.RetryPolicy` left ZERO per §20.P1 (upstream Envoy v1.37.2 default).

**(vi) Zero-Options zero-cost no-op default per §20.P1 RATIFIED.** Zero-value `Options{}` constructs a Client with: `*http.Client{Timeout: 0}` (no client-imposed deadline; relies on `req.Context()` deadline), stdlib `http.DefaultTransport` (no TLSConfig override), zero RetryPolicy (single attempt; status-driven retry inactive). This is the structurally cheapest configuration — no allocations beyond the wrapping `Client` struct, no transport clone, no retry-loop iteration beyond the single first attempt. Acceptance test `TestOptions_ZeroValue_NoOpDefaults` pins this discipline.

**(vii) `Options` envelope extensibility per stdlib literal-extension convention.** New fields land additively at the end of `Options` (e.g., a future `MaxIdleConns int` if a future consumer needs to override the transport pool ceiling); zero-value field defaults are preserved bit-for-bit so existing call sites compile and behave identically. The same discipline applies to `RetryPolicy`. No methods on `Options` or `RetryPolicy` — they are pure data types per the stdlib convention.

#### AMENDMENT (22.2 IMPL): NEW `ClusterDispatch` method + paired `FactoryCtx.ClusterManager` field + paired `Cluster.UpstreamTLSConfig()` accessor — R5 RATIFIED (first co-consumer validation of `internal/httpclient/` at the 22.2 lua `:httpCall()` bridge)

**AMENDMENT anchored at 22.2 SPEC commit `0d6463e` (§3.3 + §11.4 + §16 ADR-0177 IN-PLACE AMENDMENT body shape); AMENDMENT body lands at 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing (THIS commit) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline + matches phase-17 → phase-18 ADR-0149 → ADR-0150 AMEND precedent. NO new ADR number consumed.**

Per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.3 + §11.4 evidence + AMEND-22.2 IN-PLACE AMENDMENT scope. The 22.2 lua filter's `:httpCall(cluster, headers, body, timeout_ms, async?)` bridge method needs cluster-name-based dispatch — operator scripts pass a cluster string + envoy-go resolves to an upstream endpoint via the cluster manager's load balancer + dispatches via the existing `*httpclient.Client` retry/timeout machinery. The cluster-name-based dispatch path is structurally distinct from the URL-based `(*Client).Do(*http.Request)` path the 3 introduction-time consumers (jwks + extauthz + oauth2) all use — those consumers dial a URL directly via the stdlib `*http.Client.Do` transport pool. The lua bridge cannot pre-resolve to a URL because cluster names are configuration-time bindings + endpoint selection requires the cluster manager's per-call PickEndpoint() load-balancing decision.

**(viii) NEW method `Client.ClusterDispatch(ctx, clusterName, request, clusterMgr) (*http.Response, error)`.** Eighth exported method on `*Client` at `internal/httpclient/httpclient.go`. Settled signature:

```go
func (c *Client) ClusterDispatch(ctx context.Context, clusterName string, request *http.Request, clusterMgr *cluster.Manager) (*http.Response, error)
```

Resolves cluster name to a `*cluster.Cluster` via `clusterMgr.Get(name)` (returns `errClusterNotFound` sentinel on lookup miss); selects an upstream endpoint via `Cluster.PickEndpoint()` (per-call load-balancing decision); rewrites `request.URL.Host` to the endpoint's `"host:port"` form so the underlying `*http.Client` dials the LB-selected endpoint; constructs a temp `*http.Client` honoring the cluster's TLS config via `Cluster.UpstreamTLSConfig()` + the receiver's `Options{Timeout, RetryPolicy}` (per-call construction is acceptable at the lua httpCall surface; phase-20 oauth2's shared-singleton lifecycle uses the URL-based `Do()` path UNCHANGED). Returns `(*http.Response, error)` per the existing `Do()` contract; the retry loop applies identically (status-driven retry on `RetryOnStatus`). Thread-safe: cluster manager is read-only at runtime (per ADR-0010 + ADR-0050 build-time-then-frozen semantics); concurrent `ClusterDispatch` calls are safe.

The `*cluster.Manager` parameter is threaded EXPLICITLY (rather than captured at `New(opts Options)` construction) to keep the `internal/httpclient/` package decoupled from cluster-manager singletons — the existing 3 introduction-time consumers (jwks + extauthz + oauth2) continue to construct `*httpclient.Client` via the `New(opts)` constructor without ever consuming a `*cluster.Manager`. The cluster-aware dispatch path is opt-in per-call.

The error sentinel `errClusterNotFound` is exported as `httpclient.ErrClusterNotFound` for callers that want to distinguish cluster-resolution failure from transport failure (the lua bridge classifies cluster-resolution failure as a Lua runtime-error vs transport failure as a `httpcall_failures` counter increment).

**(ix) NEW `FactoryCtx.ClusterManager *cluster.Manager` field paralleling existing `FactoryCtx.HTTPClient` field.** At `internal/filter/http/types.go::FactoryCtx`. Non-nil at HCM-build time per the phase-18.2 landing — earlier first-use was ext_authz's `grpc_service.envoy_grpc.cluster_name` resolution per phase-18.2; the lua bridge adds the SECOND co-consumer at 22.2 IMPL Task 11. May be nil in test code that does not exercise cluster-bearing filters (per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance — the filter factory checks for nil before calling `Get`/`Drain`/`ClusterDispatch`).

```go
type FactoryCtx struct {
    // ... existing fields (Registry + Stats + StatPrefix + HTTPClient) ...
    ClusterManager *cluster.Manager  // phase-18.2 first-use; phase-22.2 second co-consumer
}
```

The lua filter's `*compiledConfig` captures both `*httpclient.Client` (via `FactoryCtx.HTTPClient`) + `*cluster.Manager` (via `FactoryCtx.ClusterManager`) references at `lua.New(tc, ctx)` construction time + threads them through to per-stream `*filter` instances. The `:httpCall` bridge closure consumes both references at dispatch time.

**(x) NEW `Cluster.UpstreamTLSConfig() *tls.Config` exported accessor.** At `internal/cluster/cluster.go`. Task 4 discovered this accessor was needed — `ClusterDispatch` needs read-only access to the per-cluster upstream `*tls.Config` to wire the per-call temp `*http.Client`'s transport TLSConfig. The cluster owns the source of truth for upstream TLS configuration (constructed at cluster-manager build time from the cluster's xDS-bindings or static-bootstrap config); `ClusterDispatch` is a read-only consumer.

```go
// UpstreamTLSConfig returns the per-cluster upstream *tls.Config for TLS
// dial; nil for plaintext clusters. internal/httpclient/ ClusterDispatch
// consumer reads this to wire the per-call temp *http.Client. The cluster
// owns the source of truth for upstream TLS configuration; ClusterDispatch
// is a read-only consumer.
func (c *Cluster) UpstreamTLSConfig() *tls.Config { return c.upstreamCfg }
```

The accessor is goroutine-safe under the ADR-0010 + ADR-0050 build-time-then-frozen invariant — `c.upstreamCfg` is set at cluster construction time + never mutated thereafter; concurrent `UpstreamTLSConfig()` reads are safe.

**(xi) R5 RATIFIED — first co-consumer validation of phase-20's `internal/httpclient/` cross-phase-reusable framework primitive at the 22.2 lua `:httpCall()` bridge.** Per phase-22.2 SPEC §13-R5 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL: the AMENDMENT body landing at this 22.2 IMPL Task 19 commit closes R5 — the `internal/httpclient/` primitive accepted the additive `ClusterDispatch` extension cleanly without surface churn for the prior 3 consumers. The 3 introduction-time consumers (jwks + extauthz + oauth2) continue consuming the URL-based `(*Client).Do` path UNCHANGED at 22.2 IMPL. The 22.2 lua bridge is the FOURTH consumer overall (counting the AMEND consumer as a structural addition rather than a count of identical-signature consumers); the SECOND structurally-distinct consumer pattern (cluster-name-based vs URL-based).

The AMENDMENT-anticipation paragraph anchored at 22.2 SPEC commit `0d6463e` (§3.3 + §11.4 + §16) STANDS UNCHANGED at this 22.2 IMPL — the AMENDMENT body settles the exact signature + threading discipline as anticipated at SPEC time. NO surface drift from the SPEC anchor; the AMEND-anticipation discipline + the ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline together carry the load-bearing constraint that 22.2 IMPL doesn't surface AMENDMENT changes the 22.2 SPEC author didn't anticipate.
