## ADR-0178: NEW `internal/sdsfile/` framework primitive — filesystem-path SDS Secret reader + fsnotify hot-reload + atomic-swap discipline; consumes `generic_secret.inline_string` ONLY; PARSE-REJECT for non-filesystem `core.ConfigSource` oneof arms + the deprecated `core.ConfigSource.path` field 1 + the inner `generic_secret.secret_file` indirect-arm; NEW go.mod dependency on `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify`

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 3 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. Cross-phase-reusable framework primitive per the phase-17 ADR-0150 + phase-18.2 ADR-0158 + phase-19.1 ADR-0169 cross-phase-reuse-at-introduction-time discipline.
**Lands-in:** Task 3 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

Phase 20 oauth2's `hmac_secret` + `client_secret` + AES-256-CBC-key-derivation-source come from SDS secrets (per the `OAuth2Credentials` proto's `*v3.SdsSecretConfig` fields). Per phase-20 BRAINSTORM Q3 + Q7 + Q8 (settled together at the BRAINSTORM commit) + the phase-20 SPEC §3.2 framework-survey result, the SDS consumption is constrained to **filesystem-path SDS only** (the other `core.ConfigSource` oneof arms — `ApiConfigSource` + `Ads` — PARSE-REJECT envoy-go-strict for MVP; couples to a future xDS-control-plane-landing phase) + **fsnotify hot-reload** (per Q8) + **atomic-swap discipline** (per Q7 NEW shared package).

**Phase-20 SPEC-time scoping (per BRAINSTORM Q7 + Q8 bundled + phase-20 SPEC §3.2):** the SPEC author bundles the filesystem-path reader + the fsnotify watcher + the atomic-swap into a single shared package `internal/sdsfile/` (vs filter-local OR fold-into-existing-internal). The cross-phase reuse forward-pointer is plausible (future jwt_authn TLS-trust-store reload, future ext_authz mTLS, future ratelimit gRPC TLS); the shared package shape is structurally cleaner.

**§20.P6 RATIFIED disposition** (phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P6): `core.ConfigSource.PathConfigSource` (oneof arm field 8) wraps `{path, watched_directory}` — this is the NEW non-deprecated arm. The deprecated `core.ConfigSource.path` field 1 is the LEGACY shape (in the same message but pre-watched_directory). NEW `internal/sdsfile/` consumes the field-8 wrapper ONLY; the deprecated field-1 PARSE-REJECTs at compile time (envoy-go-strict per ADR-0080 discipline). The inner `generic_secret.secret_file` indirect-arm (filesystem alternative to `inline_string`) also PARSE-REJECTs at MVP (double-indirection — the framework watches the OUTER Secret-proto JSON/YAML file via fsnotify; the inner `secret_file` indirect-loading-from-another-file path is not modeled at MVP per phase-20 SPEC §8 item 14).

**Public surface** (settled at phase-20 SPEC §3.2; the IMPL confirms the exact signature at Task 3):

```go
type Watcher struct { /* atomic.Pointer[[]byte] + *fsnotify.Watcher + debounce timer */ }

func New(path string) (*Watcher, error)
func (w *Watcher) Start() error
func (w *Watcher) Current() []byte
func (w *Watcher) Close() error
```

**~100ms debounce** captures both atomic-rename-via-mv + in-place-write-via-truncate-and-rewrite event sequences without false-positive reloads (per phase-20 SPEC §12 item B7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME; closed at IMPL Task 3 + Task 8 race-tests). **Atomic-swap discipline** via `atomic.Pointer[[]byte]` ensures concurrent readers observe consistent bytes across the reload boundary (the swap is atomic; readers either see the pre-reload bytes or the post-reload bytes, never a torn read).

**MVP consumer: oauth2** (the only in-tree consumer at phase 20). Cross-phase-reusable for any future filesystem-SDS consumer (anticipated future jwt_authn TLS-trust-store reload, future ext_authz mTLS, future ratelimit gRPC TLS — each at its own future trigger condition).

**NEW go.mod dependency on `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify`** (the de facto Go file-event watching library; cross-platform; pure Go). First filesystem-watching dependency in the envoy-go go.mod. Documented at phase-20 SPEC §3.2 + §3.8 framework-footprint table.

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 3

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 3 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact debounce-window + the atomic.Pointer swap discipline + the PARSE-REJECT roster (non-filesystem ConfigSource arms + deprecated path field 1 + inner secret_file indirect-arm). The §Consequences body documents the cross-phase reuse forward-pointer envelope + the operator-facing semantics (file-change-triggers-reload; ~100ms debounce; atomic-swap-consistent-reads).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — PARSE-REJECT roster); phase-20 SPEC §3.2 (framework-survey result); phase-20 SPEC §8 items 13 + 14 (SDS / proto-shape deferrals); phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P6 (PathConfigSource RATIFIED disposition); phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

Anchored at phase-20 IMPL Task 3 per ADR-0044 (`paragraph anchors at phase-20 SPEC commit 4df55be 2026-05-17; §Decision + §Consequences bodies land at phase-20 IMPL Task 3`). Lands the NEW `internal/sdsfile/` framework primitive — the SECOND envoy-go top-level cross-phase-reusable filesystem-watching primitive, paired with the `internal/httpclient/` primitive landed at the same phase-20 IMPL session (Task 2 + ADR-0177). Per phase-20 SPEC §3.2 + planner-time decisions D4 + D12 + D13.

**(i) Public surface — 5 exported identifiers** at `internal/sdsfile/sdsfile.go`. Confirms the surface anticipated in the §Context block byte-for-byte:

```go
type Watcher struct { /* private fields per (iii) below */ }

func New(path string) (*Watcher, error)
func (w *Watcher) Start() error
func (w *Watcher) Current() []byte
func (w *Watcher) Close() error
```

Two-phase construction (`New` reads-once + initializes the atomic.Pointer + creates the fsnotify backend + add-watches the parent directory; `Start` spawns the event-loop goroutine). Rationale: a consumer parsing a compiledConfig with N SDS fields can construct N Watchers atomically (any New error short-circuits without leaking partially-constructed Watchers), then Start them only after parse succeeds. The two-phase split simplifies error-cleanup paths in `buildCompiledConfig`-style consumers per planner-time D13. `Current()` is the read entry point (atomic load; concurrent-read-safe); `Close()` is idempotent (sync.Once guard) + waits for the event-loop goroutine before returning.

**(ii) ~100ms debounce window per SPEC §12 item B7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME — closed at this Task.** The debounce timer is `time.AfterFunc(debounceWindow, w.reload)` where `debounceWindow = 100 * time.Millisecond`. Calling `scheduleReload` while the timer is pending stops + re-creates the timer (Reset on an already-fired timer is racy per `time.Timer` doc; the explicit Stop+AfterFunc pattern is the documented escape valve). The reload fires only after ~100ms of event quiescence. **Latest-bytes-wins**: a burst of 5 in-place writes within the debounce window collapses to 1 reload returning the last written bytes (validated at `TestWatcher_Debounce_CollapsesRapidWrites`). Sequential writes separated by > debounce window fire 1 reload each (validated at `TestWatcher_Debounce_SequentialWritesEachReload`). Closes SPEC §12 item B7 + planner-time D17. **The debounce-window precise behavior is RATIFIED at IMPL Task 3.**

**(iii) `atomic.Pointer[[]byte]` swap discipline.** The latest bytes snapshot is a `*[]byte` stored via `atomic.Pointer[[]byte].Store` by `reload()` + loaded via `atomic.Pointer[[]byte].Load` by `Current()`. The underlying slice is NEVER mutated post-Store — each reload allocates a fresh `[]byte` via `os.ReadFile` so a reader holding a previously-Loaded pointer continues to observe consistent bytes through the swap. Concurrent readers see EITHER the pre-reload slice OR the post-reload slice in full — no torn reads. Race-clean under `go test -race` per planner-time D4 + SPEC §14.2 (validated at `TestWatcher_DebounceRace_ConcurrentCurrent` — 16 reader goroutines × consistent-bytes assertion across the reload boundary observed ZERO inconsistent reads). **The atomic.Pointer swap discipline is RATIFIED at IMPL Task 3.**

**(iv) fsnotify event-subset covered: `Write` + `Create` + `Rename`.** These are the standard event sequences SDS rotators produce: (a) **in-place truncate-and-rewrite** via `os.WriteFile` (the simplest pattern; fsnotify reports `fsnotify.Write` on the file path); (b) **atomic-rename-via-mv** via write-sibling-then-rename (the rotation-safe pattern; fsnotify reports `fsnotify.Create` + `fsnotify.Rename` on the watched directory as the new inode appears + the old path is removed). `Chmod` events are IGNORED (permission change without content change). `Remove` events are IGNORED (the file's disappearance is benign — the next valid event triggers a reload; the prior bytes are preserved via the last-good-bytes invariant per (vii) below). The event-subset rationale + the dispatcher's basename match against `filepath.Base(path)` + the parent-directory watch (rather than the file-path watch) per (v) below.

**(v) The fsnotify backend watches the PARENT DIRECTORY of the watched file, NOT the file path itself.** Settled at this IMPL Task per SPEC §3.2 + the §Context block + ADR-0178 §Decision (iv). Rationale: SDS rotators commonly use the atomic-rename-via-mv pattern; the rename REPLACES the inode underlying the watched path. A direct file-path watch becomes stale across the rename (fsnotify on Linux observes the rename event but no subsequent Write events on the new inode). Watching the parent directory observes Create + Rename + Write events across all files in the directory; the event-loop filters by basename match against `w.base` (cached as `filepath.Base(path)` at New time). Trade-off: a noisy parent directory with many SDS-unrelated files generates extra event-filter work in the hot loop — acceptable cost per SPEC §3.2 (typical SDS deployments isolate Secrets in a dedicated directory). For the relative-path case (e.g., `New("relative.bin")`), `filepath.Dir` returns `"."` which fsnotify interprets as cwd — validated at `TestWatcher_New_RelativePath_OK`.

**(vi) PARSE-REJECT discipline lives at the CONSUMER, NOT in this primitive.** The sdsfile primitive takes a filesystem path string + reads it verbatim — it has NO proto awareness, NO JSON/YAML interpretation, NO Secret-message validation. The inner `generic_secret.secret_file` indirect-arm + the non-filesystem `core.ConfigSource` oneof arms (`ApiConfigSource` + `Ads`) + the deprecated `core.ConfigSource.path` field 1 ALL PARSE-REJECT at the CONSUMER's compiledConfig parser per phase-20 SPEC §2.11 + §8 item 14 + planner-time D2 (byte-stable error message strings). The consumer extracts the filesystem path from the validated `PathConfigSource` (oneof arm field 8) wrapper + passes it to `sdsfile.New(path)`. The primitive's separation-of-concerns is structurally clean — adding a future PARSE-REJECT case (e.g., a future phase rejecting some new SDS arm) requires NO sdsfile change.

**(vii) Reload error policy — last-good-bytes preservation.** When `os.ReadFile` inside `reload()` fails (transient I/O error, mid-rename `os.ErrNotExist`, permission change), the implementation: (a) increments `reloadCount` (so tests can detect the reload-attempt was scheduled); (b) logs via stdlib `log.Printf` with a distinct message for `os.ErrNotExist` (typical mid-rename hiccup) vs other errors (likely a deployment problem); (c) does NOT mutate the `atomic.Pointer[[]byte]` — the prior snapshot remains visible to `Current()` readers. Rationale: operators expect "rotation hiccup" semantics (never observe garbage; the next valid write supersedes the stale snapshot). A more aggressive policy (clear the bytes; return nil from `Current()`) would create downstream-NPE risk for consumers that assume non-nil — the last-good preservation is the operator-friendly choice.

**(viii) Lifecycle: Close() teardown + done-channel coordination + sync.Once idempotency.** Close() atomically: (a) closes the `done` channel (signals the event-loop goroutine to exit); (b) cancels the pending debounce timer under the mu (prevents a late reload firing after `fsWatcher.Close` — which would log a spurious missing-file error if the rotator deleted the file mid-teardown); (c) closes `fsWatcher` (which also closes `fsWatcher.Events` + `fsWatcher.Errors` channels — the event-loop's `select` case `, ok := <-...` paths exit cleanly); (d) waits for the event-loop goroutine via `wg.Wait()` (only if Start was called — the `started` boolean guards against blocking on a Watcher that was New()'d but never Start()ed per `TestWatcher_Close_WithoutStart`). The sync.Once guard makes Close idempotent: validated at `TestWatcher_Close_Idempotent` (3 sequential calls). Close racing a debounce-triggered reload terminates cleanly: validated at `TestWatcher_Close_DuringInFlightReload_NoPanic` + `TestWatcher_DebounceRace_CloseRacesReload`. **Close discipline is RATIFIED at IMPL Task 3.**

### Consequences

**Cross-phase-reusability — 4 forward-pointers.** The `internal/sdsfile/` primitive is structurally generic — it accepts any filesystem path + dispatches reload events on content change. Anticipated future consumers: (a) **jwt_authn TLS-trust-store reload** (a future phase wiring JWKS over mTLS, where the trust-store bytes refresh via SDS); (b) **ext_authz mTLS** (a future phase wiring ext_authz over mTLS, where the client cert+key refresh via SDS); (c) **ratelimit gRPC TLS** (a future phase wiring the gRPC ratelimit-service connection over mTLS); (d) any future HTTP/network filter needing filesystem-watched bytes. Each future consumer extends additively without breaking the existing oauth2 consumer (no API change required); the primitive's wire-agnostic surface (the byte-slice return from `Current()`) is the structural enabler. Future cross-phase consumers also pick up the ~100ms debounce + atomic-swap semantics + last-good-bytes preservation for free — these are the OPERATOR-FACING invariants that any SDS-watched consumer needs.

**MVP consumer: oauth2 (Task 11).** The first in-tree consumer is the oauth2 filter at phase-20 IMPL Task 11. The `compiledConfig` owns 2-3 `*sdsfile.Watcher` instances (one for `hmac_secret` + one for `client_secret`; the AES-key-derivation-source reuses the hmac_secret watcher via `SHA-256(hmacBytes)[:32]` per ADR-0182). Each `Current()` returns the latest Secret-proto JSON/YAML bytes (the oauth2 parser unmarshals into the SDS Secret proto + extracts `generic_secret.inline_string`). The consumer pattern is: `buildCompiledConfig` calls `sdsfile.New(path)` for each SDS field; on success calls `Start()`; on parse failure (e.g., a co-located inline_string PARSE-REJECT) Close() the partially-constructed Watchers + return the parse error. Close runs at filter teardown per planner-time D13.

**NEW go.mod direct dep `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify v1.10.1`.** Pinned at the latest v1.x minor available at IMPL Task 3 per planner-time D12 — `go list -m github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify` reports v1.10.1. The fsnotify v1.x line is the stable + cross-platform + pure-Go file-watching library de facto for the Go ecosystem; the v2.x line (if it exists at any future IMPL) is opt-in API-changing. This is the first filesystem-watching dependency in the envoy-go go.mod; documented at phase-20 SPEC §3.2 + §3.8 framework-footprint table. The dep is in `require` (direct) post-tidy because `internal/sdsfile/sdsfile.go` imports `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify` at package level (prior to this Task fsnotify was an indirect transitive dep at v1.6.0 via `testcontainers-go`; the direct require + module-graph maximum-version-selection bumps it to v1.10.1).

**Lifecycle ownership per planner-time D13 — MVP leaks-on-exit discipline.** Each `*sdsfile.Watcher` is owned by the consumer's `*compiledConfig`; `Close()` runs at filter teardown (which fires when the filter is unregistered or — in the MVP — at process exit). NO `os.Exit` cleanup hook is wired (matches phase-18.2 D2 + ADR-0158 §Decision (vi) MVP-leaks-on-exit precedent). The Close discipline is robust against late-teardown event delivery (the done-channel preempts the reload path; the sync.Once preempts double-close) so production operators using a long-running envoy-go binary with config-reload-via-process-restart observe NO goroutine leak across config-reload events as long as the filter teardown calls Close.

**Concurrent reads safe via `atomic.Pointer[[]byte]`.** Validated at the `TestWatcher_DebounceRace_*` race group under `-race` (3 race tests; race-clean across all). The atomic.Pointer swap discipline is the production-grade discipline for "concurrent readers + occasional writer" — the alternative (RWMutex around the bytes) would force readers through a critical section + serialize against the writer, which is structurally heavier for the read-dominated workload (every request-decode at oauth2 reads the bytes; reloads fire only on rotation events). This is also the discipline used by phase-15 runtime + phase-18.x extauthz config caches; the cross-phase consistency of the lock-free-reader pattern is itself a structural benefit.

**~100ms debounce closes SPEC §12 item B7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME.** The debounce-window precise behavior is validated at `TestWatcher_Debounce_CollapsesRapidWrites` (5 rapid writes → 1 reload via 10ms inter-write spacing + 250ms post-batch settle) + `TestWatcher_Debounce_SequentialWritesEachReload` (3 sequential writes separated by 250ms → 3 reloads). Both tests assert `reloadCount` (an internal package-private counter incremented by `reload()`) to make the debounce-collapse vs sequential-reload distinction crisp. Per planner-time D17 the item B7 closure is RATIFIED at IMPL Task 3.

**Sub-second responsiveness preserved.** Total reload latency upper bound: ~250ms = ~50ms fsnotify event-delivery latency (Linux inotify is typically <10ms; the 50ms allowance covers slow filesystems / scheduler hiccups) + ~100ms debounce window + ~10ms `os.ReadFile` + atomic.Pointer.Store. SDS rotators using the atomic-rename pattern observe the new bytes within ~150ms p50 / ~250ms p99 of the rename. This is acceptable for OAuth credential rotation — the rotator's overlap window (the period during which both the old + new bytes might be in use across in-flight requests) is bounded by the in-flight request timeout (typically 30s default), so a sub-second reload latency comfortably falls inside the rotation overlap envelope.

**Cross-references.** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline — the SPEC-anchored §Context block + the IMPL-anchored §Decision + §Consequences bodies live in the same ADR per the ADR-on-impl convention); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — PARSE-REJECT roster at the consumer); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance discipline — N/A here, the primitive returns the New error rather than constructing a nil-tolerant default); ADR-0150 + ADR-0158 + ADR-0169 (cross-phase framework-primitive precedent — phase-17 jwks Fetcher, phase-18.2 grpcclient Dialer, phase-19.1 extproc ProcessorClient — each evolved the cross-phase-reuse-at-introduction-time discipline that this ADR continues); ADR-0177 (the paired phase-20 framework primitive — `internal/httpclient/`); ADR-0182 (the AES-key derivation source consumes the same hmac_secret Watcher); phase-20 SPEC §3.2 (framework-survey result); phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P6 (PathConfigSource RATIFIED); phase-20 SPEC §12 item B7 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME (closed at this Task); phase-20 SPEC §14.1 Group 7 (unit-test surface 12-15 tests) + §14.2 (race-test surface `TestWatcher_DebounceRace_*`); planner-time D4 + D11 + D12 + D13 + D17.

**D11 hypothesis status at this Task: HOLDS.** No new ADR fired at Task 3. The Watcher surface confirmed the §Context anticipation byte-for-byte; the ~100ms debounce + atomic.Pointer swap + parent-directory watch + last-good-bytes preservation all settled in-place inside the §Decision body per ADR-0044's "in-§Decision IMPL-settling does not consume a new ADR" discipline. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed per PLAN D11 hypothesis).

## ADR-0179: oauth2 HMAC cookie composition — 5-input newline-joined `HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, StrJoin({domain, expires, token, id_token, refresh_token}, "\n"))` per phase-20 AMEND-2 + §20.P4 REFUTED (BRAINSTORM Q9 incomplete — 3-input hypothesis REFUTED at empirical scrape); id_token + refresh_token participate as empty strings when absent; dual-encoding read per S4 (emit Base64; accept BOTH Base64 + HexBase64); constant-time-compare via `crypto/hmac.Equal`

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 4 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. REFUTES the BRAINSTORM Q9 3-input HMAC composition hypothesis per the SPEC §11 §20.P4 in-session empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2.
**Lands-in:** Task 4 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

The phase-20 BRAINSTORM Q9 hypothesized a 3-input HMAC composition (`HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, host + BearerToken + OauthExpires)`). The SPEC §11 §20.P4 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 source REFUTED — the upstream composition is 5-input newline-joined: `HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, StrJoin({domain, expires, token, id_token, refresh_token}, "\n"))`. The id_token + refresh_token inputs participate as **empty strings when absent** (not skipped). Per phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-2 (the §1.1 amendment-block channel entry).

**S4 dual-encoding (settled inline at SPEC; not user-asked):** Upstream emits Base64 BUT accepts BOTH Base64 + HexBase64 on read (the latter for cross-deployment migration wire-compat). MVP mirrors — emit Base64; accept dual-encoding at validation time (~30 LoC extra at `hmac.go::hmacValidate`). The dual-encoding read discipline is documented at phase-20 SPEC §6.4 + the §1.1 AMEND-2 entry.

**Constant-time-compare via `crypto/hmac.Equal`** per timing-attack hardening discipline. The HMAC envelope value is parsed (dual-encoding decode); the result is `crypto/hmac.Equal`-compared against the computed HMAC. The dual-encoding read does NOT compromise constant-time semantics (each candidate encoding is decoded + compared independently; the first match wins; the second comparison runs in constant time relative to its own envelope, not relative to the first).

**Domain input semantics:** the `domain` input is the request `host` header (parsed verbatim; lowercased per RFC 7230). The host-binding rationale: prevents cross-host cookie reuse (an envelope HMAC-bound to one host cannot validate at another).

**Empty-string-when-absent semantics:** when the request envelope lacks IdToken (MVP — id_token deferred per phase-20 SPEC §2.2) OR RefreshToken (MVP — when `use_refresh_token=false` OR after refresh-token rotation completes), the corresponding input is the empty string. The `StrJoin` produces `domain + "\n" + expires + "\n" + token + "\n" + "\n" + ""` for the (no-IdToken, no-RefreshToken) case. The "\n\n" double-separator IS DELIBERATE — it's the upstream byte-exact composition.

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 4

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 4 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact StrJoin separator + the dual-encoding read switching discipline + the constant-time-compare invariant. The §Consequences body documents the BRAINSTORM Q9 correction trail + the wire-compat implications + the future PKCE/id_token-enabling-phase reactivation path (5th input `id_token` becomes non-empty when id_token lands).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); phase-20 SPEC §6.4 + §6.5 (cookie envelope reader + writer); phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-2; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P4 (HMAC composition REFUTED); phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

Settled at phase-20 IMPL Task 4 — `internal/filter/http/oauth2/hmac.go` + `hmac_test.go` (~180 LoC production + ~370 LoC tests). The §Decision body extends the §Context anticipation per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline; the 8 sub-clauses below pin the exact IMPL surface.

**(i) Public-within-package surface.** Two filter-local functions on `internal/filter/http/oauth2/hmac.go`: `computeHMAC(domain, expires, token, idToken, refreshToken string, hmacSecret []byte) string` (returns Base64URL-raw-encoded 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 sum; always exactly 43 chars output) + `validateHMAC(domain, expires, token, idToken, refreshToken string, hmacSecret []byte, cookieHMAC string) bool` (returns true iff the cookie envelope validates under dual-encoding read; constant-time compare via `crypto/hmac.Equal`). Both functions are **filter-local lowercased** (NOT exported) per ADR-0044's filter-local-discipline + second-consumer-trigger-deferral — the 5-input HMAC composition pattern is reusable but NO second consumer exists at phase-20 introduction. Extraction to a shared package deferred until a hypothetical second consumer fires the trigger (matches the `internal/httpclient/` extraction trail per ADR-0177).

**(ii) 5-input newline-joined composition.** The HMAC input is `domain + "\n" + expires + "\n" + token + "\n" + idToken + "\n" + refreshToken` (single allocation; pre-computed total length per the hot-path discipline). HMAC-SHA256 via `crypto/hmac.New(sha256.New, hmacSecret)`. The 4 newlines between 5 inputs are byte-exact upstream — the "\n\n" double-separator for the (no-IdToken, no-RefreshToken) MVP case IS DELIBERATE per AMEND-2 + §20.P4 REFUTED. id_token + refresh_token participate as **empty strings when absent** (NOT skipped); this distinguishes the 4 envelope-shape vectors (full / no-id-no-refresh / only-refresh-absent / only-id-absent) into 4 distinct HMACs — validated by the 4 Group 2.A canonical vector tests at `hmac_test.go::TestComputeHMAC_*`.

**(iii) Emit-side Base64URL-raw (unpadded).** `computeHMAC` returns `base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(sum)` — 32 raw bytes → exactly 43 chars (no `=` padding). The unpadded form is the canonical wire shape per SPEC §6.5; matches upstream Envoy v1.37.2's emit-side byte-exact behavior per §20.P4. The fixed-length output property is asserted at `TestComputeHMAC_LongInputs` + `TestComputeHMAC_EmptyEverything` (both check `len(out) == 43`).

**(iv) Read-side dual-encoding cascade per S4.** `validateHMAC` calls `decodeDualEncoding(cookieHMAC)` which attempts up to 3 decode branches: (1) `base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString` — canonical Base64URL-raw; (2) `base64.URLEncoding.DecodeString` — padded Base64URL operator-tolerant fall-back (some operators emit padded encodings due to lib choice); (3) **nested HexBase64** per S4 — for each outer-decode result that is even-length ASCII hex, also `hex.DecodeString` the inner string. The cascade returns 1-3 candidate raw-byte slices; the caller filters by length (must equal `sha256.Size = 32`) + constant-time-compares. The **first match wins**; later branches short-circuit on early `hmac.Equal` true return.

**(v) Constant-time-compare invariant via `crypto/hmac.Equal`.** The decoded candidate is compared via `hmac.Equal(candidate, expected)`. The `expected` 32-byte HMAC is computed ONCE per `validateHMAC` call + reused across all candidate branches; this preserves constant-time semantics relative to the candidate's bytes (the decode branches are independent of secret bytes; only the final compare touches `expected`). An inspection-style test at `TestValidateHMAC_ConstantTimeCompare_UsesHmacEqual` asserts `hmac.Equal(` is called in `hmac.go` AND `bytes.Equal(` is NOT — fragile against pure renames but catches the load-bearing "developer forgot constant-time-compare" regression. Direct timing-side-channel measurement deferred (flaky in CI).

**(vi) No-panic discipline + error-path uniformity.** `validateHMAC` returns false on every error path: empty `cookieHMAC` (early return); all 3 decode branches fail (no candidates); decoded candidate has wrong length (`!= 32`); `hmac.Equal` returns false. NO panic path. The malformed-input coverage is validated at `TestValidateHMAC_MalformedBase64_Rejected` across 6 garbage-input rows (incl. wrong-length candidates + invalid-hex inner candidates + non-Base64 bytes). The fuzzer at Task 12 (per SPEC §14.3) will assert must-never-panic across the surface alongside `buildCompiledConfig` + `parseAllCookies` + `decryptToken` + `buildTokenRequestBody`.

**(vii) Allocation discipline.** Both `computeHMAC` + `rawHMAC` pre-compute the message-buffer length to a single `make([]byte, 0, totalLen)` allocation; this is hot-path code on every authenticated request. `decodeDualEncoding` caps candidate-slice allocation at 3 entries via `make([][]byte, 0, 3)`. No string concatenation via `+=` in the hot path.

**(viii) Filter-local rationale + second-consumer deferral.** The 5-input HMAC composition + dual-encoding read pattern is **structurally reusable** for any future HMAC-validated cookie envelope (e.g. a hypothetical future session-cookie filter, or a future API-key cookie filter). However, NO second consumer exists at phase-20 introduction; per the second-consumer-trigger-deferral discipline (matching ADR-0177's `internal/httpclient/` extraction trail — `internal/httpclient/` only extracted when the 3rd consumer (oauth2) joined the cluster), extraction to a shared package is deferred. The functions stay filter-local (lowercased package-private at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/hmac.go`) until a second consumer fires the trigger. This is documented in §Consequences below.

### Consequences

**BRAINSTORM Q9 correction trail (REFUTED).** The phase-20 BRAINSTORM hypothesized a 3-input HMAC composition (`HMAC-SHA256(hmac_secret, host + BearerToken + OauthExpires)`). The SPEC §11 §20.P4 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 REFUTED this — the upstream composition is unambiguously 5-input newline-joined with id_token + refresh_token participating as empty strings when absent. AMEND-2 records the correction at the §1.1 SPEC amendment-block channel. The Group 2.A canonical vector tests at `hmac_test.go::TestComputeHMAC_NoIdToken_NoRefreshToken` explicitly validate the empty-string-contribution semantics — confirms the empty-string inputs produce a distinct HMAC vs the all-empty composition vs the full-envelope composition (4 distinct vectors over the same `(domain, expires, token)` prefix, distinguishing the absence patterns).

**Dual-encoding read covers operator-configurable encoding drift.** Some upstream Envoy deployments emit HexBase64-encoded HMACs due to historical configuration (the Envoy source supports BOTH encodings at compile-time via a build flag; production deployments occasionally mismatch). The S4 read-path widens compatibility — MVP accepts BOTH Base64URL AND nested HexBase64 at validation time (~30 LoC at `hmac.go::decodeDualEncoding`). Validation cost is bounded: at most 3 decode attempts + at most 3 `hmac.Equal` calls per validation. The `TestValidateHMAC_HexBase64EncodingAccepted` + `TestValidateHMAC_DualEncoding_BothCanonicalDecode` tests anchor the wire-compat coverage. Operator-tolerant padded-Base64URL acceptance covered at `TestValidateHMAC_PaddedBase64Accepted` for the operator-emits-padded-encoding edge.

**Byte-exact upstream match for emitted Base64URL envelope.** The emit-side is canonical Base64URL-raw (unpadded; 43-char output). Cross-side empirical equivalence validated at Task 12 fixture-0024 scenario (a) sign-in-happy-path (the cross-side Set-Cookie byte-comparison includes the OauthHMAC cookie value). This preserves wire-compat — any downstream consumer (browser cookie store; later request's cookie envelope) sees identical bytes whether served by upstream Envoy or envoy-go.

**Cross-phase reuse intent — second-consumer-trigger deferral.** The 5-input newline-joined + dual-encoding read pattern is reusable for ANY future HMAC-validated cookie envelope. Per the second-consumer-trigger discipline (matching the `internal/httpclient/` extraction at ADR-0177 — extracted only when the 3rd consumer joined), extraction to a shared package (e.g. a hypothetical `internal/cookiehmac/`) is **deferred** until a second consumer fires the trigger. The functions stay filter-local (lowercased package-private at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/hmac.go`) at phase-20 introduction. The deferral is structurally identical to the cluster of "filter-local first; cross-phase extraction at trigger" patterns landed at phase-04..19.2 — this is the canonical discipline, NOT an exceptional choice.

**Filter-local discipline (NOT extracted to a shared package at phase 20).** The 2 functions (`computeHMAC` + `validateHMAC`) + 2 helpers (`rawHMAC` + `decodeDualEncoding`) all live at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/hmac.go`. No exported identifier crosses the package boundary; no `internal/cookiehmac/` package exists; no `Cookies` interface or `HMACValidator` type carries the pattern across phases. The cross-phase reuse is intent-documented at §Consequences (this paragraph) but NOT materialized in code. A future second-consumer phase will (a) AMEND this ADR's §Decision (i) in-place per ADR-0044 to record the second-consumer trigger event, (b) extract the pattern to a shared package, and (c) refactor BOTH consumers (oauth2 + the new consumer) to consume the shared primitive.

**Future PKCE/id_token-enabling-phase reactivation path.** When the id_token-enabling phase lands (the deferred-with-PKCE cluster per SPEC §2.2 + §8 item 5), the 5th input `id_token` becomes non-empty — but the HMAC composition is unchanged (it already accommodates non-empty id_token at the 4th position; the empty-string-when-absent semantics already handle the transition). The PKCE-enabling phase will (a) consume the `IdToken` cookie at the read path, (b) emit the `IdToken` Set-Cookie at the write path, and (c) propagate the id_token bytes to the `idToken` parameter of `computeHMAC` / `validateHMAC`. The HMAC functions themselves require NO change at the PKCE-enabling phase — this is the load-bearing payoff of the 5-input always-passes design at MVP.

**D11 hypothesis status at this Task: HOLDS.** No new ADR fired at Task 4. The 5-input composition + dual-encoding decode cascade + constant-time-compare + filter-local discipline + reuse-trigger deferral all settled in-place inside the §Decision body's 8 sub-clauses per ADR-0044's "in-§Decision IMPL-settling does not consume a new ADR" discipline. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed per PLAN D11 hypothesis).

**Cross-references.** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline — the SPEC-anchored §Context block + the IMPL-anchored §Decision + §Consequences bodies live in the same ADR per the ADR-on-impl convention); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — no-panic at the cookie-validation surface; the malformed-input rejection per §6.4); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance discipline — `validateHMAC` returns false rather than panicking on empty `cookieHMAC` per the discipline); ADR-0177 + ADR-0178 (paired phase-20 framework primitives — `internal/httpclient/` + `internal/sdsfile/`; the `hmac_secret` bytes consumed at validation come from the `internal/sdsfile/` Watcher per ADR-0178 + ADR-0182); ADR-0182 (the AES-key-derivation source consumes the same `hmac_secret` bytes via `SHA-256(hmac_secret)[:32]`); ADR-0181 (the cookie-envelope reader at SPEC §6.4 consumes `validateHMAC` for the OauthHMAC cookie validation); phase-20 SPEC §6.4 + §6.5 (cookie envelope reader + writer code shape); phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-2 (5-input composition + dual-encoding read correction); phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P4 REFUTED (BRAINSTORM Q9 3-input hypothesis refutation); phase-20 SPEC §14.1 Group 2 (HMAC composition vector tests — 15-20 anticipated rows; landed at this Task as 20 PASS); phase-20 SPEC §14.3 (fuzzer must-never-panic at Task 12); planner-time D7 (fuzzer corpus seeds include HMAC validation); planner-time D9 (parallelizable-with-Tasks-3+6+7 cluster — landed sequentially per dispatch); planner-time D11 (no-new-ADR hypothesis at IMPL).

## ADR-0180: oauth2 state-machine + deny-path wire shape (302+401 only; NO 500 anywhere per phase-20 AMEND-3 + §20.P9 REFUTED) + listener-scoped-only enforcement via HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT + the explicit NO-ADR-0125-AMENDMENT REUSE-by-absence classification (THIRD CONSECUTIVE §9 row after phase 18 + phase 19 to skip ADR-0125 roster extension)

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 5 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. REFUTES the BRAINSTORM §5 deny-path-with-500 hypothesis per the SPEC §11 §20.P9 in-session empirical scrape. Records the listener-scoped-only REUSE-by-absence per §20.P7 RATIFIED.
**Lands-in:** Task 5 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

ADR-0180 anchors three load-bearing oauth2 design decisions: (1) the **3-flow state-machine** (sign-in / refresh / sign-out + pass_through); (2) the **deny-path wire shape** — 302 + 401 only; NO 500 anywhere per AMEND-3 + §20.P9 REFUTED; (3) the **listener-scoped-only enforcement** via HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT per §20.P7 RATIFIED + the explicit NO-ADR-0125-AMENDMENT REUSE-by-absence classification.

**3-flow state-machine** (phase-20 SPEC §6.3 + §4 + ADR-0180): `DecodeHeaders` priority order: (1) signout_path match → handleSignout; (2) redirect_path_matcher match → handleCallback (async token_endpoint POST); (3) pass_through_matcher match → handlePassThrough (bypass); (4) else handleCookieValidate → ContinueDecoding (valid envelope) OR handleRefresh (expired BearerToken + valid RefreshToken — async refresh-token POST) OR handleUnauthenticated (category (a) 302 challenge). The async legs (callback + refresh) park the decode goroutine on the phase-09 async-resume primitive.

**Deny-path 302+401 only — NO 500 anywhere** (phase-20 SPEC §4 + AMEND-3 + §20.P9 REFUTED): upstream Envoy v1.37.2 token_endpoint failure path emits 302 (redirect-retry-eligible) OR 401 (terminal-with-constant-body `"OAuth flow failed."` 18 bytes). NEVER 500. envoy-go-strict simplification: token_endpoint non-2xx retry-eligible (5xx) → emit (a) 302 challenge; non-2xx terminal (4xx) → emit (d) 401. Recorded as envoy-go-strict departure at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### Phase 20 forward-pointer notes` (per phase-20 SPEC §13 item C7).

**Listener-scoped-only enforcement via HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT** (phase-20 SPEC §5 + §20.P7 RATIFIED): the v1.37.x oauth2 proto has NO `OAuth2PerRoute` message at all (strongest-form evidence — the proto file has no per-route-override message arm). Any oauth2 `typed_per_filter_config` (TPFC) entry at route or virtualHost level PARSE-REJECTs at HCM-parse-time with byte-stable error message per ADR-0110 single-chokepoint discipline + the `RegisterPerRouteValidator` factory hook per phase-20 SPEC §6.1. Recorded as envoy-go-strict departure at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md per phase-20 SPEC §13.

**Explicit NO-ADR-0125-AMENDMENT classification** (phase-20 SPEC §5.4): after phase 18 (ADR-0163 — REUSED 5th canonical; no amendment) + phase 19 (ADR-0173 — REUSED 5th canonical; no amendment), phase 20 is the THIRD CONSECUTIVE §9 family-row to NOT extend the ADR-0125 roster. Phase 20's REUSE-by-absence is a **STRONGER form of the lesson** than the prior two phases' 5th-canonical REUSE — there is no per-route surface at all, so the listener-scoped-only enforcement is itself a parse-time PARSE-REJECT discipline rather than a roster-REUSE classification. The ADR-0125 roster does NOT grow monotonically; phase 20 strengthens the lesson WITHOUT amendment (the absence itself is the lesson).

**Cross-phase NOT-CONSUMED dispositions recorded** (phase-20 SPEC §3.6): ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` (no TLS-principal interaction); ADR-0150 jwks (id_token deferred — but REFACTORED per ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT); ADR-0151 jwt verifier (id_token deferred); ADR-0165 callback-surface extension (no TLS/principal-attribute envelope).

**POST callback method PARSE-REJECT per §20.P3 + AMEND-3 + phase-20 SPEC §2.14**: envoy-go-strict simplification — GET-only callback at MVP; POST callbacks (the `response_mode=form_post` OAuth-extension variant) PARSE-REJECT at the callback-flow dispatch in `DecodeHeaders`. NEW envoy-go-strict departure recorded at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md per phase-20 SPEC §13 item C8.

**AMEND-6 field-locus corrections recorded** (phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-6): C1 (`cookie_domain` is on OAuth2Credentials field 5, NOT OAuth2Config); C2 (`cookie_configs` is `*CookieConfigs` wrapper); C3 (`forward_bearer_token` MVP-CONSUMED).

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 5

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 5 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact dispatch-priority order + the per-trigger 302/401 emission discipline + the HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT byte-stable error messages + the cross-phase NOT-CONSUMED disposition records. The §Consequences body documents the envoy-go-strict departures + the cross-phase forward-pointer extensions (response_code_details cluster; id_token-and-jwks-and-jwt-verifier NEW cluster).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0110 (single-chokepoint per-route enforcement); ADR-0125 (canonical per-route roster — NO new amendment); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline); ADR-0163 + ADR-0173 (prior §9 rows skipping ADR-0125 amendment — REUSE precedent); phase-20 SPEC §4 + §5 + §6.3 + §3.6; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-3 + AMEND-6 + AMEND-7; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P3 + §20.P7 + §20.P9; phase-20 SPEC §9 items 4 + 5 (cross-phase cluster extensions); phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

ADR-0180 settles **three load-bearing surfaces** at phase-20 IMPL Task 5: (A) the 3-flow state-machine dispatcher in `decode_headers.go` per SPEC §6.3; (B) the 4-emission-category wire shape across `decode_headers.go` + `callback.go` per SPEC §4.1 + AMEND-3; (C) the listener-scoped-only enforcement via the `RegisterPerRouteValidator` HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT hook per SPEC §5.2 + planner-time D2.

**(i) 3-flow state-machine dispatch order per SPEC §6.3.** The `*filter.DecodeHeaders` body routes each inbound request through a **strict 4-step priority order**:

```
DecodeHeaders(headers, endStream):
  1. if cc.signoutPath(path)         → handleSignout       (category (c) 302)
  2. if cc.redirectPathMatcher(path) → handleCallback      (async token POST)
                                       — POST method PARSE-REJECTs at the
                                         callback entry per SPEC §2.14 + D15
                                         (category (d) 401)
  3. if cc.passThroughMatcher(h)     → handlePassThrough   (Continue + oauth_passthrough++)
  4. else                            → handleCookieValidate
       - valid envelope + non-expired → ContinueDecoding via handleValidCookies
         (optional Authorization injection per forward_bearer_token=true)
       - expired BearerToken + valid RefreshToken → handleRefresh (async refresh POST)
       - else                                      → handleUnauthenticated
                                                       (category (a) 302)
```

The priority order is **strict** — sign-out wins over callback wins over pass-through wins over cookie-validate. This is the dispatch-priority discipline anchored at phase-20 SPEC §6.3 + IMPL Task 5 acceptance gate (`TestDispatcher_SignoutPath_Highest_Priority` exercises the sign-out > callback precedence; the other 8 dispatcher tests at SPEC §14.1 Group 8 exercise the remaining edges). Decoder-only filter per SPEC §6.12 + the §9 family-row precedent (csrf / buffer / rbac / jwt_authn / extauthz are all decoder-only).

The state-machine encompasses the **3 OAuth2 flows** (sign-in / refresh / sign-out) PLUS the **pass-through bypass**. Each of the 4 dispatch steps maps to a distinct flow: signout (step 1) drives sign-out; callback (step 2) drives the post-OAuth2-challenge code-exchange leg of sign-in; pass-through (step 3) bypasses oauth2 entirely; cookie-validate (step 4) is the per-request session-cookie validation that EITHER lets a valid session through OR triggers the refresh leg OR triggers the initial sign-in challenge.

**(ii) 4-emission-category wire shape per SPEC §4.1 + AMEND-3.** The filter emits EXACTLY 4 wire-shape categories:

| Category | Status | Body                  | Counter                    | Handler                                          |
|----------|--------|-----------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| (a)      | 302    | (empty)               | (none direct on sign-in;   | `decode_headers.go::handleUnauthenticated`       |
|          |        |                       |  oauth_refreshtoken_failure|  + `decode_headers.go::handleRefreshFailure`     |
|          |        |                       |  on refresh-failure leg)   |  + retry-eligible token POST 5xx (Task 8 + 10)   |
| (b)      | 302    | (empty)               | oauth_success              | `callback.go::applyTokenEndpointResponse` (2xx)  |
| (c)      | 302    | (empty)               | (none direct per AMEND-4)  | `signout.go::handleSignout` (Task 9)             |
| (d)      | 401    | `"OAuth flow failed."`| oauth_unauthorized_rq      | `callback.go::handleBadState`                    |
|          |        | (18 bytes; no \\n)    |  OR oauth_failure          |  — bad-state cookie + POST-callback PARSE-REJECT |
|          |        |                       |                            |  + token POST terminal 4xx (Task 10)             |

**NO 500 emission anywhere** per AMEND-3 + §20.P9 REFUTED. Token-endpoint 5xx responses retry-route as category (a); token-endpoint 4xx responses terminal-route as category (d). Configuration-rejection (POST callback method) routes as category (d).

The constant 401 body `"OAuth flow failed."` is pinned at the `constUnauthorizedBody` package-level const in `decode_headers.go`. 18 bytes ASCII; no trailing newline; sourced from upstream `UnauthorizedBodyMessage`. Content-Type defers to the HCM SendLocalReply default for non-grpc downstream per SPEC §12 item A1 + A4 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME (most-likely `text/plain`). The IMPL Task 5 acceptance gate test `TestConstUnauthorizedBody_ByteExact_18Bytes` pins the byte-exact value + the length invariant.

Per AMEND-3 the **deny-path cleanup discipline** runs `addFlowCookieDeletionHeaders(headers, names, attrs)` (per cookies.go) on category (d) 401 emissions — clearing the 5 envelope cookies via Max-Age=0 Set-Cookie headers. The cleanup is part of the deny-path, NOT a separate cookie-hygiene pass. Category (a) auth-challenge emissions also clear the 4 wire-emitted envelope cookies AND set the state cookie per SPEC §4.5 (`emitCategoryA_AuthChallenge` helper). Category (c) sign-out emissions clear all 5 cookies via `emitCategoryC_Signout` (alias of `addFlowCookieDeletionHeaders`).

**(iii) Listener-scoped-only enforcement via `RegisterPerRouteValidator` HCM-parse-time PARSE-REJECT per SPEC §5.2.** Per SPEC §20.P7 RATIFIED — strongest-form evidence — the v1.37.x oauth2 proto has NO `OAuth2PerRoute` message at all (the proto file has no per-route-override message arm). Any `typed_per_filter_config` (TPFC) entry for `envoy.filters.http.oauth2` at route or virtualHost level PARSE-REJECTs at HCM-build time via the `RegisterPerRouteValidator(httpReg)` hook in `oauth2.go`. The byte-stable error wording is pinned at the `perRouteTPFCRejectMsg` package-level const:

```
"oauth2: typed_per_filter_config not supported at route or virtualHost level; oauth2 is listener-scoped only"
```

This wording matches planner-time D2 verbatim. The framework's `BuildPerRouteConfig` (in `internal/filter/http/perroute.go`) wraps the wording with the location prefix (e.g. `hcm: route_config.virtual_hosts[0].routes[1]: typed_per_filter_config["envoy.filters.http.oauth2"]: oauth2: typed_per_filter_config not supported at route or virtualHost level; oauth2 is listener-scoped only`). The IMPL Task 5 acceptance gate test `TestPerRouteTPFCRejectMsg_ByteExact_PlannerD2` + `TestRegisterPerRouteValidator_PARSE_REJECTS_RouteLevel_Placement` + `TestRegisterPerRouteValidator_ViaHTTPRegistry_Roundtrip` pin the byte-stable wording + the framework integration.

The Go-level public surface (per phase-20 SPEC §6.1):

```go
const TypeURL = "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.oauth2.v3.OAuth2"

func New(tc *anypb.Any, ctx envoyhttp.FactoryCtx) (envoyhttp.FilterInstanceFactory, error)
func RegisterPerRouteValidator(reg interface {
    RegisterPerRouteValidator(filterName string, validator func(proto.Message) error)
})
```

Mirrors the `header_mutation.RegisterPerRouteValidator` pattern (the only existing precedent in envoy-go). MUST be called BEFORE `httpReg.Freeze()` in `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` (the registry rejects post-Freeze registrations per ADR-0072). Task 11 wires the call-site insertion alphabetically between `localratelimit` + `rbac` per SPEC §3.7.

**(iv) Explicit NO-ADR-0125-AMENDMENT classification — THIRD CONSECUTIVE §9 row to skip per SPEC §5.4.** After phase 18 (ADR-0163 — REUSED 5th canonical; no amendment) + phase 19 (ADR-0173 — REUSED 5th canonical; no amendment), phase 20 is the THIRD CONSECUTIVE §9 family-row to NOT extend the ADR-0125 roster. Phase 20's REUSE-by-absence is a **STRONGER form of the lesson** than the prior two phases' 5th-canonical REUSE — there is no per-route surface at all, so the listener-scoped-only enforcement is itself a parse-time PARSE-REJECT discipline rather than a roster-REUSE classification. The ADR-0125 roster does NOT grow monotonically; phase 20 strengthens the lesson WITHOUT amendment (the absence itself is the lesson). The classification is recorded as a load-bearing milestone — **3 consecutive §9 rows without ADR-0125 extension** establishes the convention that the canonical roster is NOT the appropriate ADR for absence-based per-route disciplines.

**(v) Async-resume integration on the callback + refresh legs per SPEC §6.8 + ADR-0159 D4 precedent.** The callback flow (`handleCallback` in `callback.go`) and the refresh-token flow (`handleRefresh` in `decode_headers.go`) park the decode goroutine on the phase-09 async-resume primitive while the token_endpoint POST is in flight. The `*filter` struct carries the standard async-resume guard fields (`mu sync.Mutex` + `done bool` + `callCancel func()`) per the ADR-0159 D4 precedent (extauthz's mu/done/callCancel pattern). The `OnDestroy` method sets `done=true` under `mu` and fires `callCancel` to cancel the in-flight `client.Do`. The Task 5 SKELETON declares the guard + the OnDestroy implementation; Task 8 (refresh) + Task 10 (token POST) wire the full outbound HTTP call body + the `applyTokenEndpointResponse` continuation per SPEC §4.7 + §6.8.

The `applyTokenEndpointResponse(resp, err)` continuation handler in `callback.go` dispatches per the SPEC §4.7 wire-shape table: 2xx success → category (b) 302 post-callback + oauth_success++; 5xx retry-eligible → category (a) 302 challenge (NO counter); 4xx terminal → category (d) 401 + oauth_failure++. NO 500 emission anywhere per AMEND-3. The Task 5 SKELETON ships the resume-guard frame; Task 8/10 wire the dispatch body.

**(vi) POST-callback method PARSE-REJECT per SPEC §2.14 + planner-time D15.** envoy-go-strict simplification — GET-only callback at MVP. The `response_mode=form_post` OAuth-extension POST variant is out of scope per SPEC §2.14. The `decode_headers.go::DecodeHeaders` dispatcher routes a POST request to the callback path through `handleBadState` (category (d) 401 with constant body). NO `oauth_unauthorized_rq` increment distinction between bad-state-cookie and POST-callback — both bump the counter per the IMPL `handleBadState` body (the SPEC §4.6 counter matrix conflates the two triggers under `oauth_unauthorized_rq`; recorded at SPEC §13 + this ADR). The envoy-go-strict departure is recorded at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md per phase-20 SPEC §13 item C8.

**(vii) Authorization-header injection per `forward_bearer_token=true` per SPEC §2.15 + AMEND-6 C3.** The `handleValidCookies` body in `decode_headers.go` injects `Authorization: Bearer <decrypted>` on the cookie-validate ContinueDecoding path when `cc.forwardBearerToken=true`. Per `preserveAuthorizationHeader=true` (SPEC §2.15), an existing `Authorization` request header is preserved (NOT overwritten); otherwise the injection overwrites any inbound value. The decryption path consults the AMEND-3 decryption-failure fall-back at `tokens.go::decryptToken` (per ADR-0182) — but the fall-back is structurally unreachable on this leg (the HMAC validation at the upstream call-site requires a valid AES-CBC envelope, so the BearerToken cookie value MUST be valid for the dispatch to reach `handleValidCookies`).

**(viii) `compiledConfig` STUB shape at Task 5 per planner-time D11.** Task 5 lands a STUB `compiledConfig` in `compiled_config.go` with the **minimum field set** the dispatcher needs (matchers + cookie names/attrs + hmac/client secret accessors + AES key atomic.Pointer + behavioral knobs + stats). The FULL `buildCompiledConfig` proto-parser body lands at Task 11 per planner-time D11. The struct shape is **forward-stable** — Task 11 fills the deferred fields (`tokenEndpoint`, `httpClient`, `defaultExpiresIn`, `defaultRefreshTokenExpiry`, `authScopes`, `resources`) WITHOUT churning the Task 5 minimum set. The Task 5 acceptance gate test `TestCompiledConfig_Fields_ForwardStable` anchors the inter-task contract by asserting each deferred field accepts an assignment.

Per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance — the `*filter.DecodeHeaders` body guards `if cc == nil` to return Continue, supporting test code paths that construct a `*filter{}` without a compiledConfig. Production code paths always carry a non-nil cc per ADR-0072 boot-time discipline.

**(ix) Matcher abstraction discipline.** SPEC §6.2 names `PathMatcher` + `HeaderMatcher` as Go-level abstractions, not the proto types. Task 5 ships them as function-shaped closures (`pathMatcherFn = func(path string) bool`; `headerMatcherFn = func(h headerLookup) bool`). Nil-valued closures mean "no matcher configured" — the dispatcher treats nil as a guaranteed miss. Task 11's buildCompiledConfig populates these closures from the proto matcher fields via the framework's matcher machinery (mirrors `internal/matcher/matchPath` + the rbac filter's matcher consumption). The function shape is intentionally simpler than struct-method dispatch — proto-compilation produces a closure that captures the compiled matcher state, and the dispatcher consumes the function.

**(x) Cross-phase NOT-CONSUMED dispositions recorded per SPEC §3.6.** Phase 20 explicitly does NOT consume: ADR-0144 `DownstreamPrincipal()` TLS-principal accessor (no TLS-principal interaction at MVP); ADR-0150 jwks for id_token validation (id_token deferred per §2.2 — but jwks Fetcher is REFACTORED per ADR-0150 §Decision AMENDMENT to consume *httpclient.Client); ADR-0151 jwt verifier (id_token deferred); ADR-0165 callback-surface extension (no TLS/principal-attribute envelope to populate).

### Consequences

ADR-0180 records **eight load-bearing consequences** at phase-20 IMPL Task 5:

**(a) Cross-phase reuse intent — the 4-emission-category pattern is reproducible.** The 4-emission-category wire shape (302 auth-challenge / 302 post-callback / 302 sign-out / 401 with constant body) is a reusable pattern for any future single-flow filter with similar OAuth-style wire shape. The pattern's load-bearing invariants — strict priority dispatch + constant-body 401 + NO 500 anywhere + flow-cookie cleanup on deny — are filter-agnostic and could be lifted into a framework helper if a second consumer ever surfaces. Per ADR-0044 second-consumer-trigger discipline: NO extraction at phase 20; the pattern lives filter-local at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/`. If a future OAuth2-style filter (SAML / OpenID Connect / WebAuthn) lands in envoy-go, the 4-emission-category extraction trigger fires per the second-consumer convention.

**(b) AMEND-3 + §20.P9 + §20.P11 closures recorded.** AMEND-3 (deny-path simplification: NO 500 anywhere; constant 401 body; flow-cookie cleanup) is recorded as the load-bearing IMPL-time discipline anchored at this ADR. §20.P9 (NO 500 emission per upstream REFUTED) is CLOSED via the IMPL-time enforcement (the `constUnauthorizedBody` const + the absence of any 500-emit call-site in the package). §20.P11 (cookie_decrypt_failure RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT) is co-anchored with ADR-0181 §Consequences — ADR-0181 closes the counter-surface absence; ADR-0180 closes the semantics-absence via the AMEND-3 fall-back at `handleValidCookies` (the decryption-failure path is structurally unreachable post-HMAC-validation, so no counter increment site exists in the dispatcher).

**(c) THIRD CONSECUTIVE NO-ADR-0125-AMENDMENT strengthens the ADR-0125 roster-not-monotonic lesson.** Phase 18 (ADR-0163) + phase 19 (ADR-0173) + phase 20 (this ADR) all skipped ADR-0125 amendment. The pattern establishes a CONVENTION — when a §9 family-row REUSES an existing 5th-canonical OR has a per-route surface absence, the absence itself is the lesson and ADR-0125 does NOT extend. The roster is NOT monotonic; per-row appropriateness governs. Future §9 family-rows that need a NEW per-route canonical (not REUSE; not absence) MAY extend ADR-0125, but the discipline now anchored: **default to NOT extending the roster** unless a genuinely-new canonical justifies it. Recorded at ADR-0125's cross-reference set + this ADR's §Decision (iv).

**(d) Cross-phase forward-pointer extensions deferred.** Two cross-phase clusters surface at phase-20 SPEC §9 items 4 + 5 but are NOT addressed at this ADR: (1) `response_code_details` cluster — the granular response-code-details surface across the §9 family-row filters (fault / extauthz / extproc / oauth2 / future) is anticipated as a future cross-phase cluster extension; phase 20 leaves the forward-pointer dangling; (2) id_token-and-jwks-and-jwt-verifier NEW cluster — when a future phase enables id_token consumption in oauth2 (currently deferred per §2.2), the cluster extends ADR-0150 (jwks Fetcher) + ADR-0151 (jwt verifier) + (TBD) an oauth2-id_token §Decision section. Both forward-pointers persist past phase 20 phase-done.

**(e) envoy-go-strict departures recorded at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md.** Three envoy-go-strict departures land at Task 13 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT bundle: (1) NO 500 emission anywhere (per AMEND-3 + §20.P9); (2) GET-only callback (per §2.14 + planner-time D15 — POST callbacks PARSE-REJECT); (3) listener-scoped-only oauth2 placement (per §5.2 + planner-time D2 — route-level + virtualHost-level TPFC PARSE-REJECT). The departures are RECORDED, not REFUTED — each is a deliberate simplification with a SPEC-anchored rationale and an IMPL-time test gate.

**(f) D11 hypothesis preserved at phase-20 IMPL Task 5.** The PLAN-time D11 hypothesis (NO additional ADR fires at phase-20 IMPL beyond ADR-0177..0185) is preserved at Task 5 — the dispatcher + 4-emission-category surface settled entirely inside the ADR-0180 §Decision body (10 sub-clauses i-x) + §Consequences body (8 paragraphs a-h). No new ADR fires. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed per PLAN D11 + Task 5 PROGRESS log confirmation `grep -cE '^## ADR-0186' docs/envoy-go/DECISIONS.md` returns 0).

**(g) `compiledConfig` STUB-then-FILL discipline anchored.** Task 5's STUB `compiledConfig` + `newTestCompiledConfig` constructor + the per-test field assignment pattern (per the `TestCompiledConfig_Fields_ForwardStable` test) is the INTER-TASK forward-stability anchor for the Task 11 `buildCompiledConfig` parser body. Task 11 fills the deferred fields WITHOUT churning the Task 5 minimum set; the struct shape is forward-stable. Pattern is reusable for any future multi-task PLAN where a dispatcher needs to land before its full proto-parser. Recorded as the planner-time D11 discipline.

**(h) Async-resume guard discipline reuse confirmed.** The `mu sync.Mutex` + `done bool` + `callCancel func()` async-resume guard pattern from ADR-0159 D4 (extauthz) extends without modification to phase-20 oauth2. The guard's `OnDestroy → set done=true + cancel context` discipline + the resume goroutine's `if f.done { return }` check + the cancel-outside-the-lock invariant all carry forward verbatim. No framework-level extraction needed at phase 20 (second-consumer-trigger deferral; the pattern lives filter-local in two places — extauthz + oauth2 — until a third consumer triggers extraction). Per ADR-0044 in-place IMPL-time settling: the pattern lives in `*filter.OnDestroy` per file; the discipline is documented in the file's doc comments + this ADR §Decision (v).

**Cross-references at the §Decision + §Consequences anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0072 (boot-time-fail-fast + Register-pre-Freeze); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict departure discipline); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance); ADR-0110 (single-chokepoint per-route enforcement); ADR-0125 (canonical per-route roster — NO new amendment); ADR-0143 (SN2-reuse Prometheus tag-extractor); ADR-0144 (DownstreamPrincipal — NOT consumed); ADR-0150 (jwks Fetcher — REFACTORED, NOT consumed); ADR-0151 (jwt verifier — NOT consumed); ADR-0156 (extauthz precedent); ADR-0159 (D4 async-resume guard pattern — REUSED); ADR-0163 + ADR-0173 (prior §9 rows skipping ADR-0125 amendment — REUSE precedent extended); ADR-0165 (callback-surface extension — NOT consumed); ADR-0179 (HMAC composition — paired primitive); ADR-0181 (cookie envelope + stat surface — paired primitive); ADR-0182 (AES-256-CBC token encryption — paired primitive); phase-20 SPEC §4.1 + §4.3 + §4.5 + §4.6 + §4.7 + §5.2 + §5.4 + §6.1 + §6.2 + §6.3 + §6.8 + §6.12; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-3 + AMEND-6 + AMEND-7; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P3 + §20.P7 + §20.P9 + §20.P11; phase-20 SPEC §12 items A1 + A3 + A4; phase-20 SPEC §13 items C7 + C8 (envoy-go-strict departures); phase-20 SPEC §14.1 Group 8 + Group 9 (dispatcher + compile-time invariant tests); phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map; planner-time D2 (byte-stable PARSE-REJECT wording) + D4 (async-resume guard) + D11 (NO new ADR at IMPL hypothesis) + D15 (POST-callback PARSE-REJECT byte-stable wording).
