## ADR-0181: oauth2 cookie envelope + stat surface — 5-of-7 `CookieNames` consumed at MVP (BearerToken / OauthHMAC / OauthExpires / IdToken-deferred / RefreshToken; oauth_nonce + code_verifier deferred-with-PKCE); Set-Cookie attribute discipline RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME (Secure / HttpOnly / SameSite=Lax / Path=/); stat surface 86 → 92 names per phase-20 AMEND-4 + S5 (6 counters wire-exact upstream — `oauth_unauthorized_rq` / `oauth_failure` / `oauth_passthrough` / `oauth_success` / `oauth_refreshtoken_success` / `oauth_refreshtoken_failure`); HCM-rooted SN2-reuse per ADR-0143; **CLOSES §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag as RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT** (no `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter); the `Partitioned` cookie attribute deferred per AMEND-7 + SPEC §8 item 15

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 6 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. REFUTES the BRAINSTORM 8-counter stat surface hypothesis (over-counted) per the SPEC §11 §20.P8 + §20.P11 in-session empirical scrape. Closes §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag as RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT.
**Lands-in:** Task 6 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

ADR-0181 anchors two load-bearing oauth2 envelope decisions: (1) the **5-cookie envelope** discipline (5-of-7 `CookieNames` consumed at MVP); (2) the **6-counter stat surface** (86 → 92 names; wire-exact upstream per AMEND-4 + §20.P8 REFUTED).

**5-of-7 `CookieNames` consumed at MVP** (phase-20 SPEC §6.4 + §6.5):
- **BearerToken** — AES-256-CBC-encrypted access_token (per ADR-0182 + AMEND-1)
- **OauthHMAC** — 5-input HMAC over the envelope per ADR-0179 + AMEND-2
- **OauthExpires** — epoch-seconds-as-decimal-string per §12 item A3 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME
- **IdToken** — deferred per SPEC §2.2 (id_token consumption deferred); parsed but neither emitted nor honored at MVP
- **RefreshToken** — AES-256-CBC-encrypted refresh_token; emitted when `use_refresh_token=true`

2-of-7 deferred-with-PKCE per SPEC §8 item 5: **oauth_nonce** + **code_verifier**.

**Set-Cookie attribute discipline RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME** (phase-20 SPEC §4.5 + §12 item A2): MVP-default Set-Cookie attributes are `Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`. The exact attribute ordering + the SameSite default (Lax vs Strict — BRAINSTORM Q1 hypothesized Strict; the empirical scrape needs to confirm v1.37.2 emits Lax — RFC 6265bis-default in modern browsers and reference Envoy mirrors this) settled at IMPL Task 13 fixture-0024 scenario (a) cross-side Set-Cookie byte-comparison. The `Partitioned` cookie attribute (CHIPS-style; per AMEND-7) deferred per SPEC §8 item 15 (depends on `cookie_configs`).

**6-counter stat surface wire-exact upstream** (phase-20 SPEC §4.6 + AMEND-4 + §20.P8 REFUTED — BRAINSTORM over-counted at 8):
- `oauth_unauthorized_rq` — per bad/missing state cookie at callback path → 401 (category d)
- `oauth_failure` — per token_endpoint POST terminal-failure → 401 (category d)
- `oauth_passthrough` — per `pass_through_matcher` hit (bypass)
- `oauth_success` — per successful sign-in completion (callback-flow + token_endpoint POST returns 2xx → category b 302)
- `oauth_refreshtoken_success` — per refresh-token rotation OK (CONTINUE with deferred Set-Cookie)
- `oauth_refreshtoken_failure` — per refresh-token rotation failed → 302 challenge (NOT also `oauth_failure` per phase-20 SPEC §4.6 + ADR-0183)

**ABSENT counters verified** (phase-20 SPEC §15 item C8 + §20.P11 + S5):
- `signout_completed` ABSENT — sign-out completion IS the 302 emission per AMEND-4; no separate counter
- `cookie_decrypt_failure` ABSENT — decryption-failure fall-back returns ciphertext-as-plaintext per AMEND-3 + §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT; downstream HMAC validation rejects naturally; no separate counter

**Stat surface 86 → 92 names** (NOT 94 per BRAINSTORM §5 hypothesis). HCM-rooted SN2-reuse per ADR-0143 (no new SN-flattening rule). Internal stat path: `http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.oauth2.<counter>`. SN2 stat-name compile-time guards per phase-20 SPEC §6.12 (each of the 6 counter names asserted at compile time via the package's stat-registration constructor pattern).

**CLOSES §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag as RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT** (phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P11): the BRAINSTORM §5 hypothesized a NEW envoy-go-strict `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter (departure from reference Envoy); the empirical scrape revealed upstream's decryption-failure fall-back semantics (return ciphertext-as-plaintext; no counter). envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSED — we do NOT add the counter. Mirrors upstream wire-compat fully.

**Field-locus corrections** (phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-6): `cookie_domain` is on `OAuth2Credentials` field 5 (NOT `OAuth2Config` per BRAINSTORM C1 correction); MVP defaults to empty (host-only cookies; no `Domain=` attribute per §20.P2 RATIFIED + SPEC §8 item 12).

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 6

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 6 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact 5-cookie envelope shape + the 6-counter stat-name byte-exact roster + the HCM-rooted SN2-reuse Prometheus tag-extractor + the compile-time SN2 stat-name guard pattern. The §Consequences body documents the BRAINSTORM 8-counter over-count correction trail + the §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT closure + the future operator-ergonomics-phase reactivation paths (per-cookie Set-Cookie attribute customization via `cookie_configs`; CHIPS via `Partitioned`).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0143 (SN2-reuse Prometheus tag-extractor); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — §20.P11 CLOSED); ADR-0182 (NEW AES-256-CBC token-encryption — paired primitive); ADR-0179 (HMAC composition — paired primitive); phase-20 SPEC §4.5 + §4.6 + §6.4 + §6.5 + §6.11 + §6.12; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-4 + AMEND-6 + AMEND-7; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P2 + §20.P8 + §20.P11; phase-20 SPEC §8 items 12 + 15; phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

ADR-0181 settles **two load-bearing surfaces** at phase-20 IMPL Task 6: (A) the 5-cookie envelope wire shape + Set-Cookie attribute discipline; (B) the 6-counter wire-exact stat surface with HCM-rooted SN2-reuse + compile-time stat-name guards.

**(i) 5-cookie envelope per SPEC §6.4 + §6.5.** The MVP envelope consumes 5-of-7 `CookieNames` per ADR-0181 §Context. The 5 wire-emitted cookie names (default; operator-configurable per the `cookie_names` proto field):

| Field         | Default name   | Wire role                                                                   |
|---------------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| BearerToken   | `BearerToken`  | AES-256-CBC-encrypted access_token bytes per ADR-0182 + AMEND-1             |
| OauthHMAC     | `OauthHMAC`    | 5-input HMAC over the envelope per ADR-0179 + AMEND-2 (Base64URL-raw emit) |
| OauthExpires  | `OauthExpires` | epoch-seconds-as-decimal-string per §12 A3                                  |
| IdToken       | `IdToken`      | id_token; DEFERRED per §2.2 (parsed for forward-compat; not consumed)       |
| RefreshToken  | `RefreshToken` | AES-256-CBC-encrypted refresh_token bytes (when `use_refresh_token=true`)   |

The 2-of-7 deferred-with-PKCE per SPEC §8 item 5 (`oauth_nonce` + `code_verifier`) are NOT part of the MVP envelope and NOT carried on the `CookieNames` struct at phase 20. The future PKCE phase extends `CookieNames` in-place per ADR-0044 in-§Decision-amendment discipline.

The Go-level surface lives at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/cookies.go`:

```go
type CookieEnvelope struct {
    BearerToken, OauthHMAC, OauthExpires, IdToken, RefreshToken string
}
type CookieNames struct {
    BearerToken, OauthHMAC, OauthExpires, IdToken, RefreshToken string
}
func DefaultCookieNames() CookieNames
func parseAllCookies(h http.Header, names CookieNames) CookieEnvelope
```

The parser is built on `(&http.Request{Header: h}).Cookies()` — the stdlib RFC-6265 cookie parser. It iterates ALL `Cookie:` header values per RFC 9113 §8.2.3 (HTTP/2 receivers may split the cookie set across multiple Cookie header fields), and collapses duplicate cookie names last-wins per the standard server-side cookie-handling convention. Absent cookies yield the empty string for the corresponding envelope field.

**(ii) Set-Cookie attribute discipline per SPEC §4.5 + §12 item A2.** MVP-default Set-Cookie attribute set (`DefaultSetCookieAttrs()`):

- `Path=/` — emitted unconditionally per the 4-attr base shape
- `Secure` — emitted (HTTPS-only cookie)
- `HttpOnly` — emitted (no JS access)
- `SameSite=Lax` — emitted (RFC 6265bis default; cross-site GET tolerated for top-level navigation)
- `Max-Age` — OPTIONAL; emitted only when `SetCookieAttrs.MaxAge != nil`. A zero-`Duration` value emits `Max-Age=0` (sign-out / cleanup clearing per §4.5 categories (c) + (d)).
- `Domain` — OPTIONAL; emitted only when `SetCookieAttrs.Domain != ""` (host-only cookie when empty per §20.P2 RATIFIED + SPEC §8 item 12).

Byte-exact emission order pinned: `name=value; Path=<path>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=<value>[; Max-Age=N][; Domain=...]`. The fixed order matches reference Envoy v1.37.2 wire emission; the IMPL Task 12 fixture-0024 scenario (a) cross-side byte-comparison confirms (closes SPEC §12 item A2 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME). Set-Cookie formatting is open-coded via a sized `[]byte` builder (NOT `net/http.SetCookie`) to preserve byte-exact upstream ordering — `net/http.SetCookie` emits attribute order driven by struct-field-introspection that does not match upstream's emission order.

**(iii) Per-category emission table per SPEC §4.1 + §4.5.** Four wire-emission categories drive the cookie payload:

| Category | Emission helper (per `cookies.go`) | Cookies emitted                                                                                    |
|----------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| (a) 302 auth-challenge | `emitCategoryA_AuthChallenge` | 4 cleared envelope cookies (Max-Age=0 each; NO IdToken — `(n/a)`); 1 state cookie SET to HMAC(state) |
| (b) 302 post-callback  | `emitCategoryB_PostCallback`  | BearerToken=enc-access-token; OauthHMAC=hmacValue; OauthExpires=epoch-seconds-decimal; RefreshToken=enc-refresh-token (when non-empty; OMITTED when `use_refresh_token=false`); NO IdToken |
| (c) 302 sign-out       | `emitCategoryC_Signout`       | Max-Age=0 for ALL 5 envelope cookies (full clearing — even deferred-write IdToken)                  |
| (d) 401 with body      | `addFlowCookieDeletionHeaders` | Max-Age=0 for ALL 5 envelope cookies per AMEND-3 (the 401-body emission is owned by callback.go SendLocalReply, NOT this helper) |

OauthExpires value format pinned at `strconv.FormatInt(epochSeconds, 10)` (epoch-seconds-as-decimal-string per SPEC §12 item A3 + planner-time D16 A3). NOT an RFC 3339 timestamp; NOT milliseconds. The format round-trips through `strconv.ParseInt`. A regression here would break the cross-side OauthExpires byte-comparison at IMPL Task 12 fixture-0024 scenario (a).

The 4 emission helpers + `addFlowCookieDeletionHeaders` accept an `http.Header` value and `Add("Set-Cookie", ...)` per emitted cookie — preserving the per-cookie insertion order for the downstream wire-write layer. Tasks 5 + 8 + 9 (decode_headers.go + callback.go + signout.go) call the helpers from their per-category emission sites.

**(iv) 6-counter wire-exact stat surface per AMEND-4 + S5 + §20.P8 REFUTED.** The 6 oauth2 counter names pinned upstream-byte-exact via per-counter `const statName*` declarations in `stats.go`:

| Const                              | Wire name                       | Trigger per SPEC §4.6                                           |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `statNameOauthUnauthorizedRq`     | `oauth_unauthorized_rq`         | bad state cookie at callback → category (d) 401                 |
| `statNameOauthFailure`            | `oauth_failure`                 | token_endpoint POST terminal-failure → category (d) 401         |
| `statNameOauthPassthrough`        | `oauth_passthrough`             | `pass_through_matcher` hit (bypass)                             |
| `statNameOauthSuccess`            | `oauth_success`                 | category (b) post-callback-success                              |
| `statNameOauthRefreshtokenSuccess`| `oauth_refreshtoken_success`    | silent refresh-token rotation success (per ADR-0183)            |
| `statNameOauthRefreshtokenFailure`| `oauth_refreshtoken_failure`    | silent refresh-token rotation failure → category (a) 302 (per ADR-0183) |

NOTE on the `refreshtoken` (no underscore) name shape: this is INTENTIONAL upstream byte-exact reuse, NOT a typo. The Go field name uses `Refreshtoken` (capital R, lowercase t) for parity. A `refresh_token_*` variant would diverge wire-compat.

**(v) HCM-rooted SN2-reuse per ADR-0143.** The stat-prefix shape mirrors the established §9 family-row convention (extauthz / extproc / jwt_authn precedent):

```
http.<HCM_stat_prefix>.oauth2.<counter>
```

Empty HCM stat_prefix (test code paths) folds to the bare `oauth2.<counter>` form to satisfy the Registry's nameRE (forbids leading dots / double dots). Mirrors `extauthz.baseStatPrefix` discipline per ADR-0156. NO new SN-flattening rule introduced; ADR-0143's Prometheus tag-extractor convention applies unchanged.

**(vi) Compile-time stat-name guards per planner-time D6 + SPEC §6.12.** Two-layer guard:

1. **Per-counter `const statName*` declarations** pin the byte-exact wire names at compile time. The `newFilterStats` constructor uses these constants — a regression on any wire name surfaces immediately at build time.
2. **`TestStatNames_Equal_*` Group-9 assertion tests** in `stats_test.go` pin each constant to its string literal — preventing a future refactor from silently renaming the constant alongside the string literal.

`newFilterStats` uses `stats.Registry.NewCounterIfAbsent` (NOT `NewCounter`) per the rbac Task 8 multi-listener-same-prefix lesson (recorded in ADR-0156). Idempotent registration is safe AND consistent with the §9 discipline. All 6 counters allocate unconditionally (predeclared empty counters for scrape stability per Prometheus best practice).

**(vii) ABSENT counters verified per §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT + S5.** Two counters that BRAINSTORM §5 over-counted into the surface:

- `signout_completed` ABSENT — sign-out completion IS the 302 emission per AMEND-4 + §6.9 + ADR-0184; no separate counter.
- `cookie_decrypt_failure` ABSENT — decryption-failure fall-back returns ciphertext-as-plaintext per AMEND-3 + §20.P11 + ADR-0182; downstream HMAC validation rejects naturally; no separate counter.

These two absences **CLOSE the §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag as RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT** — envoy-go does NOT add the BRAINSTORM-hypothesized `cookie_decrypt_failure` envoy-go-strict departure. Wire-compat with reference Envoy v1.37.2 stat surface preserved fully.

**(viii) Cross-file consumer wiring at Task 11.** `compiledConfig.stats *filterStats` (per SPEC §6.2) is allocated at `buildCompiledConfig` time (per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance gate: `if ctx.Stats != nil`). The 6-counter handles are read at the emission sites (Task 5 dispatcher + Task 8 callback + Task 9 signout); each emission site invokes `fs.<counter>.Inc()` on the appropriate handle per the counter-increment matrix per SPEC §4.6.

### Consequences

**(a) Stat surface 86 → 92 names per AMEND-4 (NOT 94 per BRAINSTORM §5 over-count).** The phase-20 IMPL extends the cross-phase stat surface by exactly 6 names. BRAINSTORM §5 anticipated 8 names (over-counted by 2: `signout_completed` + `cookie_decrypt_failure` both ABSENT per §20.P11); the empirical scrape at SPEC §11 §20.P8 + the in-place AMEND-4 correction settle the surface at 6. The BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md stat-mapping table at phase-20 phase-done (Task 13 — edit 2 per SPEC §13.B2) extends the existing 86-name → 92-name roster with the 6 new oauth2 counter rows.

**(b) §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSED-AS-ABSENT.** The BRAINSTORM §5 hypothesized a NEW envoy-go-strict `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter (departure from reference Envoy). The §11 empirical scrape revealed upstream's decryption-failure fall-back semantics (return ciphertext-as-plaintext; no counter). The envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSES — we do NOT add the counter. Mirrors upstream wire-compat fully. Recorded at SPEC §11 §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT + at this §Decision (vii).

**(c) `Partitioned` cookie attribute deferred per AMEND-7 + SPEC §8 item 15 (NEW deferral).** The CHIPS-style `Partitioned` attribute (per draft RFC `httpbis-rfc6265bis`) is a NEW deferral surfaced at phase-20 AMEND-7 (NOT anticipated by BRAINSTORM). The `SetCookieAttrs` carrier in `cookies.go` does NOT include a `Partitioned bool` field at MVP — the attribute lives behind the `cookie_configs` per-cookie attribute customization (also deferred per SPEC §2.5). A future operator-ergonomics phase MAY land BOTH `cookie_configs` AND `Partitioned` via a single in-place §Decision amendment per ADR-0044 — extending `SetCookieAttrs` with the new field + the corresponding `formatSetCookie` clause + a new `TestFormatSetCookie_Partitioned` test row. No new ADR fires at the extension.

**(d) `cookie_configs` per-cookie attribute customization deferred per SPEC §2.5.** Operators cannot override per-cookie Set-Cookie attributes at MVP — all 5 envelope cookies use the listener-default `SetCookieAttrs` value carried on `compiledConfig`. A future operator-ergonomics phase MAY extend `compiledConfig` with a per-cookie `map[CookieName]*SetCookieAttrs` override map; the existing `formatSetCookie` API supports the extension without breaking change. No new ADR fires at the extension.

**(e) Cross-phase reuse intent.** The 5-cookie envelope (`CookieEnvelope` + `CookieNames`) + 6-counter pattern (`filterStats`) are **filter-local** at phase 20 — NOT extracted to a shared package. Per ADR-0159 (b)-disposition rationale precedent: extraction is deferred until a second consumer materializes (anticipated: a hypothetical future cookie-validation evolution OR a downstream-OAuth2-variant filter; speculation only). The patterns ARE reusable for future Standard-OAuth2 evolution (PKCE envelope extension; id_token activation; cross-subdomain `cookie_domain` operator-config) — each future extension lands via in-place ADR-0181 §Decision amendment per ADR-0044.

**(f) Set-Cookie formatting open-coded vs `net/http.SetCookie`.** This §Decision deliberately open-codes Set-Cookie formatting in `formatSetCookie` rather than using `(*http.Cookie).String()`. The stdlib path emits attribute order driven by struct-field-introspection that does NOT match upstream's emission order (notably, the stdlib emits `Max-Age` before `Secure`; upstream emits `Secure` before `Max-Age`). The byte-exact upstream order matters for the IMPL Task 12 fixture-0024 cross-side byte-comparison at scenario (a). Trade-off recorded: open-coded `formatSetCookie` is ~30 LoC; sidesteps any future stdlib change to the cookie-attribute ordering.

**(g) `parseAllCookies` honors HTTP/2 multi-Cookie-header semantics per RFC 9113 §8.2.3.** The parser iterates `h.Values("Cookie")` rather than `h.Get("Cookie")` to cover the HTTP/2 cookie-set-splitting case. A regression here (e.g., a future "optimization" to `h.Get`) would silently drop cookies on HTTP/2 traffic — surfacing only at integration time with HTTP/2-emitting clients. Test `TestParseAllCookies_MultipleHeaders` pins the behavior at unit-test time.

**(h) Compile-time stat-name guards prevent wire-name drift.** The two-layer guard (per-counter `const` + assertion tests) protects against the most common regression class: a future refactor that renames the Go const without updating the wire-emitted name. Cross-phase consistency with the extauthz / extproc / jwt_authn `const statName*` patterns per ADR-0156 + ADR-0167.

**(i) `IdToken` cookie name configurable for forward-compat.** Although id_token consumption is deferred per SPEC §2.2, `CookieNames.IdToken` is configurable at MVP so operators carrying a non-default name can opt-in to the future id_token consumption phase without re-deploying config. The `IdToken` field is read by `parseAllCookies` (the value populates `CookieEnvelope.IdToken`) but is NOT emitted at categories (a) or (b) per §4.5; category (c) sign-out DOES emit Max-Age=0 for IdToken (full envelope clearing per §4.5 row C).

**(j) D11 hypothesis preserved.** This §Decision settles all surfaces in-place inside ADR-0181 (cookies + stats + per-category emission table + compile-time guards) per ADR-0044's in-§Decision IMPL-settling discipline. NO new ADR fires at Task 6 IMPL. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed; D11 hypothesis HOLDING per the planner-time D11 declaration).

**Cross-references at the IMPL anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0143 (SN2-reuse Prometheus tag-extractor); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — §20.P11 CLOSED-AS-ABSENT); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance gate); ADR-0156 + ADR-0167 (extauthz + extproc `const statName*` precedent); ADR-0159 (b)-disposition precedent (filter-local-vs-extracted rationale); ADR-0179 (HMAC composition — paired primitive); ADR-0182 (AES-256-CBC token-encryption — paired primitive); ADR-0183 (refresh-token rotation counter discipline — `oauth_refreshtoken_*`); ADR-0184 (sign-out flow — no separate `signout_completed` counter); phase-20 SPEC §4.1 + §4.5 + §4.6 + §6.4 + §6.5 + §6.11 + §6.12; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-4 + AMEND-6 + AMEND-7; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P2 + §20.P8 + §20.P11; phase-20 SPEC §8 items 12 + 15; phase-20 SPEC §12 items A2 + A3; phase-20 SPEC §14.1 Group 4 + Group 9; phase-20 PLAN planner-time decisions D6 + D11 + D16 A2 + D16 A3.

## ADR-0182: NEW filter-local AES-256-CBC token-encryption helper at `oauth2/tokens.go` per phase-20 AMEND-1 + §20.P5 REFUTED (algorithm swap from BRAINSTORM Q4-anticipated AES-GCM to upstream-byte-exact AES-256-CBC); SHA-256(hmac_secret)[:32] key derivation; random 16-byte IV per encryption (prepended); PKCS#7 padding; Base64URL(IV ‖ CT) envelope; `disable_token_encryption=true` skip-path (plaintext storage; explicit MVP-CONSUMED per S2 NO-runtime-gate decision); decryption-failure fall-back returns ciphertext-as-plaintext per AMEND-3 (no `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter per §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT)

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 7 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention. REFUTES the BRAINSTORM Q4 AES-GCM algorithm hypothesis per the SPEC §11 §20.P5 in-session empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2.
**Lands-in:** Task 7 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

The phase-20 BRAINSTORM Q4 hypothesized AES-256-GCM with random 12-byte nonce + integrated AEAD MAC. The SPEC §11 §20.P5 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 REFUTED — the upstream algorithm is **AES-256-CBC** (NOT GCM). The algorithm swap is recorded as phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-1.

**AES-256-CBC specifics** (phase-20 SPEC §3.3):
- **Key derivation**: `SHA-256(hmac_secret)[:32]` → 32-byte AES-256 key (single-pass SHA-256 hash; mirrors upstream `Encryptor::createKey`)
- **IV**: random 16 bytes per encryption (prepended to ciphertext; mirrors upstream `Encryptor::encrypt`)
- **Padding**: PKCS#7 (the standard block-mode padding; stdlib `crypto/cipher` does not provide it directly — phase-20 implements ~10-15 LoC helper at `tokens.go`)
- **Wire envelope**: `Base64URL(IV ‖ CT)` (standard URL-safe-base64; no padding chars; matches upstream wire emission)

**Public surface** (filter-local — NOT extracted to shared package at phase 20; second-consumer-trigger deferral):

```go
// encryptToken encrypts plaintext under AES-256-CBC with a random 16-byte IV.
// Returns Base64URL(IV ‖ CT) per upstream wire shape.
func encryptToken(plaintext, hmacSecret []byte) string

// decryptToken decrypts Base64URL(IV ‖ CT) back to plaintext.
// On failure: returns the original ciphertext bytes (NOT an error) per AMEND-3 fall-back.
// Downstream HMAC validation then rejects the cookie naturally. NO cookie_decrypt_failure counter.
func decryptToken(envelope string, hmacSecret []byte) []byte
```

**`disable_token_encryption=true` skip-path** (phase-20 SPEC §2.15 + S2): when the operator-config flag is true, the encrypt/decrypt path is bypassed entirely; cookies store + return plaintext values verbatim. Explicit MVP-CONSUMED per phase-20 SPEC §2 (the field is part of the MVP envelope; the runtime gate is dropped per S2 since envoy-go has no runtime-features layer — the proto field default `false` is the sole switch).

**Decryption-failure fall-back per AMEND-3** (phase-20 SPEC §3.3 + §6.4 + §11 §20.P11): on decryption failure (malformed envelope; bad padding; etc.), `decryptToken` returns the original ciphertext bytes (NOT an error). The downstream HMAC validation at `hmac.go::hmacValidate` then rejects the cookie naturally (the HMAC over the returned-as-plaintext ciphertext cannot match the expected HMAC). **NO `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter** per §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT + AMEND-4. Mirrors upstream wire behavior fully; envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSED.

**Filter-local — NOT extracted to shared package at phase 20** (phase-20 SPEC §3.3 + ADR-0159 (b)-disposition rationale precedent): no other in-tree filter needs AES-CBC at MVP. Future second-consumer trigger (anticipated: a hypothetical future cookie-encrypting filter; speculation only) would motivate extraction to `internal/aescbc/` or `internal/cookiecrypt/`; phase 20 holds at filter-local.

**Library-behavioral confirmation deferred to §12 item B6** (phase-20 SPEC §12 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME): the PKCS#7 padding behavior under decrypt-failure surfaces at IMPL Task 7 unit-tests + Task 13 fixture-0024 decrypt-failure path coverage. Most-likely outcome: Go's `crypto/cipher.NewCBCDecrypter` surfaces padding errors as garbage; the fall-back wrap at `tokens.go::decryptToken` catches the error and returns the original ciphertext bytes (mirrors upstream wire behavior).

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 7

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 7 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact KDF + IV-generation + PKCS#7-padding + Base64URL-encoding discipline + the decrypt-failure fall-back semantics + the `disable_token_encryption=true` skip-path branching. The §Consequences body documents the BRAINSTORM Q4 GCM-to-CBC correction trail + the §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT closure + the filter-local-vs-extracted disposition rationale + the future second-consumer-trigger forward-pointer.

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — §20.P11 CLOSED); ADR-0159 (b)-disposition precedent (filter-local-vs-shared-package rationale); ADR-0181 (cookie envelope + stat surface — paired primitive; the encrypted/decrypted bytes flow through the 5-cookie envelope); ADR-0179 (HMAC composition — paired primitive; the AES-derived key + the HMAC-secret share the `hmac_secret` source); phase-20 SPEC §3.3 + §6.4 + §6.5; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-1 + AMEND-3; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P5 + §20.P11; phase-20 SPEC §12 item B6; phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

ADR-0182 settles **one load-bearing surface** at phase-20 IMPL Task 7: the filter-local AES-256-CBC token-encryption helper at `internal/filter/http/oauth2/tokens.go` per AMEND-1 + §20.P5 REFUTED + AMEND-3 decrypt-failure fall-back. Eight sub-clauses settle the surface.

**(i) Filter-local Go-level surface per SPEC §3.3.** Two filter-local functions exposed within the `oauth2` package — NOT exported (lowercase initial letter; filter-local discipline per ADR-0182 §Context):

```go
// encryptToken encrypts plaintext under AES-256-CBC with a random 16-byte IV.
// Returns base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(IV ‖ CT) per upstream wire shape.
func encryptToken(plaintext, hmacSecret []byte) string

// decryptToken decrypts a base64.RawURLEncoding(IV ‖ CT) envelope under
// SHA-256(hmacSecret)[:32]. On ANY failure (malformed base64, truncated
// envelope, block-size mismatch, bad padding) returns []byte(envelope)
// verbatim per AMEND-3 fall-back. NO error returned.
func decryptToken(envelope string, hmacSecret []byte) []byte
```

Two internal helpers complete the surface: `deriveAESKey(hmacSecret) [32]byte` (the SHA-256-truncated-to-32 KDF) + `pkcs7Pad/pkcs7Unpad` (the PKCS#7 padding + constant-time-relative-to-padLen unpad). Both helpers are package-local (lowercase) — no cross-file consumer at MVP.

**(ii) AES-256-CBC algorithm per AMEND-1 + §20.P5 REFUTED.** The BRAINSTORM Q4 hypothesis of AES-256-GCM was REFUTED at SPEC §11 §20.P5 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 — upstream uses CBC, NOT GCM. The algorithm swap is recorded at AMEND-1 as load-bearing. Phase 20 lands upstream-byte-exact AES-256-CBC.

**(iii) SHA-256(hmacSecret)[:32] KDF.** Single-pass SHA-256 hash of the operator-supplied `hmac_secret`; the `[:32]` truncation is equivalent to the full sum (SHA-256 produces exactly 32 bytes) but pinned-as-such for spec-readability. The same `hmac_secret` source feeds BOTH the HMAC-SHA256 composition (per ADR-0179) AND the AES-256 KDF — operators who supply a strong secret get protection in both surfaces. The KDF is invariant to input length (nil/empty hmacSecret yields SHA-256([])[:32], a deterministic but PUBLIC AES key; operator-error-protected at HCM-parse-time by the SDS-secret-empty PARSE-REJECT discipline, NOT here in tokens.go).

**(iv) Random 16-byte IV per encryption (prepended).** IV is read via `crypto/rand.Read`; a failure to read from the OS RNG panics (unrecoverable — a broken OS RNG is not a recoverable condition at request time). The IV is prepended to the ciphertext: the envelope shape is `IV ‖ CT` raw, base64-encoded as a single string. This matches reference Envoy v1.37.2's `Encryptor::encrypt` envelope shape byte-exact.

**(v) PKCS#7 padding (RFC 5652 §6.3).** Plaintext padded to a multiple of `aes.BlockSize` (16 bytes); the padding byte value equals the padding length (1..16). An exact-block-multiple plaintext receives a FULL extra padding block of 0x10 bytes. The empty plaintext yields a single full padding block. `pkcs7Unpad` validates the padding byte is in [1, 16] AND the last padLen bytes are all equal to padLen; failure returns (nil, false) which routes to the AMEND-3 fall-back at decryptToken.

**(vi) Base64URL(IV ‖ CT) envelope (raw, no padding).** Output encoded via `base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString` — URL-safe alphabet (`-_` instead of `+/`), no `=` padding chars. Suitable for direct use as a cookie value (no quoting required per RFC 6265 cookie-octet alphabet). A regression that emitted standard Base64 (with `+/` chars or `=` padding) would break cookie wire-compat — the `+` char in a cookie value requires quoting per RFC 6265.

**(vii) AMEND-3 decryption-failure fall-back (no error, no counter).** `decryptToken` returns `[]byte(envelope)` verbatim on ANY error path:

| Failure mode | Detection |
|---|---|
| Malformed base64 | `base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString` error |
| Truncated envelope (< 16 bytes raw) | `len(raw) < aes.BlockSize` |
| Empty CT (no bytes after IV) | `ctLen == 0` |
| CT not a clean block multiple | `ctLen % aes.BlockSize != 0` |
| Bad PKCS#7 padding (length out of range OR bytes not all equal) | `pkcs7Unpad` returns `(nil, false)` |

NO error is returned. NO `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter is incremented (per §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT + AMEND-4). The downstream HMAC validation at `hmac.go::validateHMAC` rejects the fall-back bytes naturally — the recovered "plaintext" cannot produce a valid HMAC against the envelope tuple. This discipline keeps the wire response shape identical between "wrong key" and "tampered cookie" — both produce a downstream HMAC validation failure, NOT a distinguishable decrypt-error oracle.

**(viii) `disable_token_encryption=true` skip-path (consumer-level only).** When the operator-config flag is true (per SPEC §2.15), the consumer (the caller at callback.go / decode_headers.go landing at Tasks 5 + 8 + 11) does NOT invoke encryptToken/decryptToken — cookie values are stored + returned verbatim. tokens.go has NO awareness of the flag; the skip is exclusively at the caller. `TestDecryptToken_DisableEncryption_SkipPath_DocumentsConsumerBehavior` documents this contract (regression-canary against any future "convenience" refactor that moved the skip into tokens.go).

**(ix) `atomic.Pointer[[32]byte]` discipline (consumer-level, race-clean).** The cooperating consumer (`compiledConfig.aesKey` at Task 11) holds the AES key behind `atomic.Pointer[[32]byte]` for the sdsfile-driven reload path per ADR-0178. tokens.go's parameter shape (`hmacSecret []byte`) accepts any byte slice; the atomic discipline lives at the caller. The `TestAesKeySwap_Concurrent_*` race group (3 tests per planner-time D4) validates the atomic-pointer discipline at the unit-test level: 4 encryptor/decryptor goroutines + 1 swapper goroutine produce zero race-detector violations under `go test -race`. Task 11 re-validates the discipline at the integration level (compiledConfig wired end-to-end with the sdsfile-triggered reload path).

**(x) Constant-time-relative-to-padLen PKCS#7 unpad (defense-in-depth).** `pkcs7Unpad` iterates the entire last block, accumulating diffs in a single `byte` (XOR), then checks once at the end. This avoids early-exit on first-bad-padding-byte — a defense-in-depth against padding-oracle timing side-channels. The AMEND-3 fall-back at decryptToken is the load-bearing oracle-hardening (returning ciphertext-as-plaintext on failure eliminates the distinguishable error-path); the constant-time strip is the secondary defense.

**(xi) No-panic discipline (one documented exception).** encryptToken + decryptToken NEVER panic on input-driven paths. The single exception is encryptToken's `rand.Read` error — a broken OS RNG is unrecoverable; we let the panic propagate. `crypto/aes.NewCipher` cannot error for a 32-byte key (the SHA-256 KDF guarantees the size); we discard the error return per the documented stdlib contract. The fuzzer at Task 12 asserts the no-panic discipline across arbitrary inbound envelope bytes per SPEC §14.3.

**(xii) CLOSES SPEC §12 item B6 per planner-time D17.** SPEC §12 item B6 (AES-256-CBC PKCS#7 padding decrypt-failure semantics) was RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL-TIME at SPEC commit; the IMPL Task 7 unit-test coverage at `TestDecryptToken_BadPadding_ReturnsCiphertextAsPlaintext_NoError` + `TestDecryptToken_TruncatedEnvelope_ReturnsCiphertextAsPlaintext_NoError` + `TestDecryptToken_BlockSizeNotMultiple_ReturnsCiphertextAsPlaintext_NoError` + `TestDecryptToken_AmbiguousFallback_PlaintextLooksLikeEnvelope_StillFallsBack` settles each failure-mode branch byte-exact. Most-likely outcome confirmed: Go's `crypto/cipher.NewCBCDecrypter` produces garbage on key mismatch; the fall-back wrap at `tokens.go::decryptToken` catches the padding error (via `pkcs7Unpad` returning (nil, false)) and returns the original ciphertext bytes. SPEC §12 item B6 → CLOSED-AT-TASK-7.

### Consequences

**(a) AMEND-1 algorithm-swap-from-BRAINSTORM RECORDED as load-bearing.** The BRAINSTORM Q4 hypothesis of AES-256-GCM was REFUTED at SPEC §11 §20.P5 empirical scrape against reference Envoy v1.37.2 — upstream uses CBC, NOT GCM. This is the kind of empirical-scrape REFUTAL that the SPEC §11 12-pin block exists to catch; the AMEND-1 record at SPEC §1.1 + this ADR-0182 §Decision body together preserve the correction trail. A future code-archaeology session that finds "but BRAINSTORM Q4 said AES-GCM" can trace the swap rationale via AMEND-1 → §20.P5 → ADR-0182 (i)-(ii). No silent algorithm drift.

**(b) §20.P11 envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSED-AS-ABSENT.** The BRAINSTORM §5 hypothesized a NEW envoy-go-strict `cookie_decrypt_failure` counter (departure from reference Envoy). The §11 empirical scrape revealed upstream's decryption-failure fall-back semantics (return ciphertext-as-plaintext; no counter). The envoy-go-strict departure flag CLOSES — we do NOT add the counter. Mirrors upstream wire-compat fully. Recorded jointly at ADR-0181 §Consequences (b) + this §Consequences (b) + AMEND-3 + SPEC §11 §20.P11 RATIFIED-AS-ABSENT. The two ADRs (0181 + 0182) co-anchor the closure: ADR-0181 is the surface (the counter is ABSENT from the stat roster); ADR-0182 is the semantics (the decrypt path produces no observable failure that would warrant counting).

**(c) Filter-local discipline — NOT extracted to a shared package at phase 20.** Per ADR-0182 §Context + ADR-0159 (b)-disposition precedent: no other in-tree filter needs AES-CBC at MVP. Future second-consumer trigger (anticipated: a hypothetical future cookie-encrypting filter; speculation only) would motivate extraction to `internal/aescbc/` or `internal/cookiecrypt/`; phase 20 holds at filter-local. The 4 sub-pieces of the helper (AES-256-CBC encrypt + decrypt + SHA-256 KDF + PKCS#7 padding) ARE reusable as a unit. The extraction trail will mirror `internal/httpclient/` per ADR-0177 (extracted only when the 3rd consumer joined at phase 20). The "second consumer triggers extraction" forward-pointer is held implicitly at this §Decision; no §Future Work paragraph is authored because there is no concrete-second-consumer landscape at phase 20.

**(d) Cross-phase reuse intent.** The SHA-256-truncated-to-32 KDF + random-IV-prepended envelope + Base64URL(IV ‖ CT) envelope shape is a reusable pattern for future filter-local AES-CBC needs. The same pattern applies to any future cookie/header/body encryption surface where the operator already supplies an `hmac_secret` (or equivalent strong secret) — the KDF eliminates the need for a separate AES-key SDS surface. The pattern is recorded here as a forward-pointer for phase-20-successor filter designers.

**(e) AMEND-3 padding-oracle hardening — the fall-back IS the hardening.** Returning ciphertext-as-plaintext on decryption failure keeps the wire response shape identical between "wrong key" + "tampered cookie" + "malformed envelope" — all produce a downstream HMAC validation failure naturally. NO distinguishable error-path information leak. The constant-time-relative-to-padLen `pkcs7Unpad` is defense-in-depth (a regression in the fall-back wiring would still avoid timing leaks at the unpad layer). A regression that surfaced a distinguishable error (e.g., a future "convenience" refactor that returned `(nil, err)` from decryptToken) would re-introduce the padding-oracle distinguishability — the test `TestDecryptToken_BadPadding_ReturnsCiphertextAsPlaintext_NoError` is the unit-test-time canary against this regression.

**(f) `disable_token_encryption=true` skip-path is consumer-level only.** A future "convenience" refactor that moved the skip into tokens.go (e.g., `if disableEncryption { return string(plaintext) }`) would entangle the helper with operator-config awareness — tokens.go currently has ZERO operator-config dependencies. The contract is enforced by `TestDecryptToken_DisableEncryption_SkipPath_DocumentsConsumerBehavior` (regression-canary). The skip dispatch lives at the caller (Tasks 5 + 8 + 11) where it can branch on `compiledConfig.disableTokenEncryption` without polluting the helper's surface.

**(g) `atomic.Pointer[[32]byte]` discipline race-clean under `-race` at unit-test level.** The `TestAesKeySwap_Concurrent_*` race group (3 tests per planner-time D4) validates the atomic-pointer discipline that the compiledConfig.aesKey (Task 11) will use for the sdsfile-driven reload path. tokens.go itself takes `hmacSecret []byte` as a parameter (NOT an atomic.Pointer), so the atomic discipline lives at the caller. The race-test pattern simulates the caller — encrypt/decrypt goroutines `Load()` the current key, encrypt/decrypt with the snapshot, and the swapper concurrently `Store()` a new key. Zero race-detector violations across 800+ encrypt+decrypt iterations confirms the discipline holds.

**(h) D11 hypothesis preserved.** This §Decision settles all surfaces in-place inside ADR-0182 per ADR-0044's in-§Decision IMPL-settling discipline. NO new ADR fires at Task 7 IMPL. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed; D11 hypothesis HOLDING per the planner-time D11 declaration; confirmed via `grep -cE '^## ADR-0186' docs/envoy-go/DECISIONS.md` returns 0).

**Cross-references at the IMPL anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — §20.P11 CLOSED-AS-ABSENT); ADR-0159 (b)-disposition precedent (filter-local-vs-extracted rationale); ADR-0177 (httpclient extraction trail — second/third-consumer-trigger precedent); ADR-0178 (sdsfile + atomic.Pointer reload path — the cooperating consumer for the AES-key swap); ADR-0179 (HMAC composition — paired primitive; the HMAC-secret + AES-key share the `hmac_secret` source); ADR-0181 (cookie envelope + stat surface — paired primitive; the encrypted/decrypted bytes flow through the 5-cookie envelope; co-anchors §20.P11 CLOSED-AS-ABSENT); phase-20 SPEC §3.3 + §6.4 + §6.5; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-1 + AMEND-3 + AMEND-4; phase-20 SPEC §11 §20.P5 + §20.P11; phase-20 SPEC §12 item B6 (CLOSED-AT-TASK-7); phase-20 SPEC §14.1 Group 3 + §14.2 race detector; phase-20 PLAN planner-time decisions D4 + D11 + D17.

## ADR-0183: oauth2 refresh-token rotation timing + race-vs-rotation discipline — `default_refresh_token_expires_in` semantics + concurrent-request-with-same-expired-BearerToken-plus-valid-RefreshToken disposition (envoy-go-strict: no per-stream serialization; each in-flight request POSTs the refresh independently; the LATEST `Set-Cookie` envelope wins via the deferred Set-Cookie discipline); counter increment matrix (refresh-failure → 302 challenge, NOT also `oauth_failure` per AMEND-3 + phase-20 SPEC §4.6)

**Status:** §Context drafted at phase-20 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences anchor at phase-20 IMPL Task 8 per ADR-0044
**Date:** 2026-05-17 (§Context anchor)
**Doctrine:** Phase 20 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention.
**Lands-in:** Task 8 of phase-20 PLAN.

### Context

ADR-0183 anchors the refresh-token rotation behavioral discipline. When `DecodeHeaders` classifies an inbound request as "expired BearerToken + valid RefreshToken" (per phase-20 SPEC §6.3 dispatch step 4), the dispatcher invokes `handleRefresh` (per phase-20 SPEC §6.8) — a silent refresh-token POST to the configured `token_endpoint` using the 3-field refresh-token template byte-exact per AMEND-5 + ADR-0185.

**On success (2xx response)**: the dispatcher CONTINUES the request to the upstream + emits a deferred Set-Cookie envelope per phase-20 SPEC §6.8 (the cookies update on the eventual response). `oauth_refreshtoken_success` counter increments. Wire shape: the request flows through to the upstream with the (decrypted) NEW BearerToken Authorization-header injection per `forward_bearer_token=true` (per AMEND-6 C3); the response gets the NEW 5-cookie envelope via Set-Cookie response-side mutation.

**On failure (non-2xx response)**: the dispatcher falls through to handleUnauthenticated → emit (a) 302 challenge. `oauth_refreshtoken_failure` counter increments. **CRITICAL: `oauth_failure` does NOT also increment** per AMEND-3 + phase-20 SPEC §4.6 (refresh-failure path is distinct from token_endpoint-terminal-failure path; the counter discipline is one-counter-per-event, not stacked). The 302 challenge then proceeds via the normal sign-in flow (state-cookie + authorization_endpoint redirect).

**Race-vs-rotation discipline** (envoy-go-strict simplification): when MULTIPLE concurrent requests arrive with the same expired BearerToken + valid RefreshToken, each request independently invokes `handleRefresh` (no per-stream serialization; no token-endpoint POST deduplication). Each POST returns its own 2xx response with a (possibly identical, possibly newly-rotated) refresh_token; each request emits its own Set-Cookie envelope. The LATEST `Set-Cookie` envelope wins via the downstream HTTP cookie-handling semantics (later Set-Cookie headers in the same response stream override earlier ones; across multiple response streams the browser's per-request Set-Cookie absorption decides). This is OPERATIONALLY ACCEPTABLE — the worst-case is a few extra refresh-token POSTs in the concurrent-burst scenario; the authoritative cookie state converges within the response window. **NO mutex** at the filter level for refresh-token rotation per phase-20 SPEC §14.2 race-detector verification.

**`default_refresh_token_expires_in` semantics** (phase-20 SPEC §2 + §6.2): the proto field carries the operator-default refresh_token TTL (used when the token_endpoint POST response does not include an explicit `expires_in` for the refresh_token). MVP-CONSUMED per phase-20 SPEC §2.15. The OauthExpires cookie value (per phase-20 SPEC §6.4 + §6.5) records the BearerToken's expiry; the RefreshToken cookie has no separate expires-record (relies on the cookie's own Max-Age attribute set to `default_refresh_token_expires_in`).

**Counter increment matrix recap** (phase-20 SPEC §4.6):
- Refresh-success: `oauth_refreshtoken_success += 1`; NO other counters increment
- Refresh-failure: `oauth_refreshtoken_failure += 1`; NO other counters increment (NOT also `oauth_failure`)
- The 302 challenge fall-through after refresh-failure: NO category-(a)-level counter (the (a) 302 challenge is the deny-path emission; the only counter that increments on category-(a) emissions is the upstream `oauth_refreshtoken_failure` / `oauth_unauthorized_rq` per the trigger path)

**Concurrency-test surface at phase-20 SPEC §14.2**: `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_*` race-test group verifies zero data-race violations on the deferred-Set-Cookie path under `-race`.

### §Decision + §Consequences ANTICIPATED AT IMPL Task 8

Anchored at this SPEC commit; written in full at phase-20 IMPL Task 8 per ADR-0044. The §Decision body settles the exact refresh-trigger condition + the deferred-Set-Cookie emission discipline + the race-vs-rotation semantic + the counter-increment-once-per-event invariant. The §Consequences body documents the envoy-go-strict race-vs-rotation simplification + the operator-facing semantics (concurrent-burst tolerance; LATEST-wins cookie convergence).

**Cross-references at the SPEC commit anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0185 (refresh-token template byte-exact wire shape); ADR-0181 (cookie envelope — the deferred Set-Cookie emission flows through); ADR-0180 (state-machine — the handleRefresh dispatch step); phase-20 SPEC §6.3 + §6.8 + §4.6; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-3; phase-20 SPEC §2.15 (MVP-CONSUMED `default_refresh_token_expires_in` + `use_refresh_token`); phase-20 SPEC §14.2 race-detector tests; phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map.

### Decision

ADR-0183 settles **one load-bearing surface** at phase-20 IMPL Task 8: the refresh-token rotation continuation in `internal/filter/http/oauth2/callback.go` per planner-time D14 + AMEND-3 + SPEC §4.6 + §6.8 + ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline. Twelve sub-clauses settle the surface.

**(i) handleRefresh + applyRefreshTokenResponse live in callback.go.** Task 5 landed `handleRefresh` as a SKELETON in callback.go (returning StopIteration without firing the outbound POST). Task 8 finalizes the body: handleRefresh acquires f.mu, snapshots the (poster, clientID, clientSecret, refreshToken) tuple, arms f.callCancel for OnDestroy cancellation, allocates f.refreshDone for test-side synchronization, releases f.mu, and launches a goroutine that fires `poster(ctx, "refresh_token", refreshToken, clientID, clientSecret)` then dispatches the response via applyRefreshTokenResponse. The dispatcher (decode_headers.go::handleCookieValidate) already routes the expired-BearerToken + valid-RefreshToken envelope to handleRefresh per Task 5 + SPEC §6.3 step 4 — no dispatcher change at Task 8.

**(ii) `tokenEndpointPosterFn` function-shaped abstraction on compiledConfig.** Task 8 declares `tokenEndpointPosterFn = func(ctx, grantType, codeOrRefreshToken, clientID, clientSecret string) (*http.Response, error)` + the `tokenEndpointPoster tokenEndpointPosterFn` field on compiledConfig. Task 8 injects test implementations via newRefreshTestConfig in oauth_client_test.go; Task 10 wires the production implementation (oauth_client.go::postTokenEndpoint backed by *httpclient.Client per ADR-0185). The abstraction lets Task 8 land + test the rotation continuation without depending on the Task 10 outbound POST body. Per planner-time D11 forward-stability: Task 10's production poster fits the abstraction without churning the field set.

**(iii) Deferred Set-Cookie discipline.** The success-leg of applyRefreshTokenResponse builds the new 4-cookie envelope per SPEC §4.5 category (b) (BearerToken / OauthHMAC / OauthExpires / RefreshToken) via emitCategoryB_PostCallback (cookies.go), stores it on f.pendingSetCookies under f.mu, then calls dcb.ContinueDecoding() to resume the parked decode goroutine. The encode-side emission of pendingSetCookies onto the upstream response is Task 11 (full filter integration); Task 8 records the pending envelope. Task 12 fixture-0024 scenario (d) `refresh_token_rotation/` validates end-to-end byte-exact. Task 8 ships the envelope with empty cookie values (the byte-exact AES-CBC-encrypted access_token + refresh_token + epoch values land at Task 10/11 via the oauth_client.go JSON body parse — the Task 8 envelope SHAPE is the load-bearing invariant; the byte-exact VALUES are Task 10/11's concern).

**(iv) No per-stream serialization per planner-time D14.** Concurrent in-flight requests with the same expired BearerToken + valid RefreshToken EACH POST the refresh INDEPENDENTLY. No mutex on the token_endpoint POST; no request deduplication; no shared cache across concurrent rotations. The envoy-go-strict simplification accepts the worst-case "a few extra refresh-token POSTs in the concurrent-burst scenario" tradeoff in exchange for filter-side simplicity + race-detector cleanliness. The LATEST Set-Cookie envelope wins via the browser's standard cookie-overwrite semantic (the upstream's response stream's Set-Cookie absorbs the latest emission); no filter-side coordination required. `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_2RequestsSameCookies_BothPost` validates the no-dedup invariant (postCount == N for N concurrent rotations).

**(v) Counter increment matrix per SPEC §4.6 + AMEND-3 (one-per-event).** Success leg → `oauth_refreshtoken_success++` ONLY; failure leg → `oauth_refreshtoken_failure++` ONLY. Critically, the failure leg does NOT also increment `oauth_failure` — the refresh-failure path is distinct from the callback-leg's terminal-failure path; the counter discipline is one-per-event, not stacked. `TestHandleRefresh_FailedPost_5xx_Emits302ChallengeWithRefreshtokenFailureCounter` + `TestHandleRefresh_4xxFailure_Emits302ChallengeWithRefreshtokenFailureCounter` assert both counter rows (refreshtoken_failure == 1, failure == 0) per the AMEND-3 + §4.6 contract. The 5xx and 4xx classes BOTH route to handleRefreshFailure with the same counter increment — the dispatcher does NOT distinguish refresh-failure subtypes (mirrors SPEC §4.7 envoy-go-strict simplification for the callback leg).

**(vi) Failure leg wire shape: category (a) 302 challenge.** On non-2xx OR transport-level error, applyRefreshTokenResponse calls handleRefreshFailureLocked which (a) increments oauth_refreshtoken_failure, (b) emits the category (a) 302 wire shape (Location header → authorizationEndpoint + state cookie SET + 4 envelope cookies CLEARED) via SendLocalReply, then (c) calls dcb.ContinueDecoding() to unblock the parked decode goroutine. The handleRefreshFailureLocked variant is an f.mu-held helper (the unlocked decode_headers.go::handleRefreshFailure remains for direct call-sites that don't already hold the lock). The wire shape mirrors handleUnauthenticated byte-exact; only the counter call-site differs. Transport-level errors (timeout / connection-reset / context-canceled) also route to the failure leg (treated as non-2xx for counter + wire-shape purposes) per the failed-classification predicate `err != nil || resp == nil || resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300`.

**(vii) OnDestroy guard discipline per ADR-0159 D4.** applyRefreshTokenResponse acquires f.mu before touching any callback or stream state + short-circuits if f.done is set (mirrors extauthz applyDisposition pattern from Task 9 of phase 18.1). The OnDestroy guard fires at three sites: (1) handleRefresh's pre-goroutine check (don't launch the goroutine if OnDestroy already fired); (2) applyRefreshTokenResponse's done-check (don't touch dcb if OnDestroy fired during the in-flight POST); (3) the OnDestroy method itself (cancels f.callCancel outside the lock to avoid net/http cleanup running under f.mu). `TestApplyRefreshTokenResponse_OnDestroyGuard` + `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_OnDestroy_Mid_Refresh_NoPanic` validate the guard under both synchronous + concurrent OnDestroy races (the latter under `-race`).

**(viii) SendLocalReply + ContinueDecoding pattern per phase-09 fault precedent.** The async goroutine fires SendLocalReply from OUTSIDE the dispatch goroutine — SendLocalReply alone sets c.localReplyDone but does NOT unblock the park. ContinueDecoding() must follow to wake the parked goroutine so it can observe localReplyDone=true and return. Mirrors fault.go:321-324 + extauthz applyDisposition deny-leg pattern. Applies to BOTH the success-leg (ContinueDecoding for upstream propagation) AND the failure-leg (SendLocalReply for 302 emission + ContinueDecoding for park-unblock). The failure-leg's ContinueDecoding call is essential — without it the parked decode goroutine deadlocks on the resume channel.

**(ix) `pendingSetCookies` field + waitRefreshDone + snapshotPendingSetCookies test-only helpers.** Three additions to the filter struct at Task 8: (a) `pendingSetCookies envoyhttp.OrderedHeaders` for the deferred envelope under f.mu; (b) `refreshDone chan struct{}` for test-side synchronization (closed by the resume goroutine when applyRefreshTokenResponse returns); (c) test-only methods `waitRefreshDone()` + `snapshotPendingSetCookies()` for race-clean test inspection. Production code paths do NOT wait — the Envoy chain resumes via dcb.ContinueDecoding called from the resume goroutine. The `refreshDone` mechanism is a test-affordance, not a production primitive (it adds zero overhead to the production hot-path beyond an unused chan field).

**(x) Item B disposition — Task 5 reviewer flagged a perceived divergence between POST-callback counter conflation and D15; on Task 8 re-read, D15 literally states *"NO new counter (the standard `oauth_unauthorized_rq` increments per §4.6)"*, which means the standard counter SHOULD increment on both bad-state-cookie AND POST-callback paths.** Task 5's implementation was correct per literal D15. The Task 8 commit `df33e4b` introduced an erroneous call-site split (a transient `handleBadStateNoCounter` variant that emitted the identical (d) 401 wire shape WITHOUT the `oauth_unauthorized_rq` increment) which is REVERTED in the follow-up commit. The current dispatcher routes both PARSE-REJECT triggers (bad-state-cookie AND POST-callback) through `handleBadState` per literal D15; `handleBadState` increments `oauth_unauthorized_rq` once per PARSE-REJECT event. `emitCategoryD401` remains as the (d) 401 wire-shape emission helper called by `handleBadState`. The literal-D15 behavior is pinned by `TestHandleBadState_EmitsCategory_D_401_With_Constant_Body` (bad-state-cookie call-site asserts `oauth_unauthorized_rq == 1`) AND `TestDispatcher_CallbackPath_POST_ParseRejects` (POST-callback dispatcher path asserts `oauth_unauthorized_rq == 1` post-dispatch) — both assertions co-exist as the regression-pinning pair for the literal-D15 disposition.

**(xi) Item A disposition (`_ = env` in handleCallback) — comment-only clarification.** Task 5's handleCallback discarded the parsed cookie envelope (`_ = env`); the reviewer asked whether Task 8/10 would consume it. Task 8 disposition: keep `_ = env` with an expanded comment noting that the parsed envelope is retained for forward-compat with Task 10 (the auth-code token POST body builder needs the cookies for cookie-disambiguation in the multi-step OAuth dance). The handleRefresh leg already consumes the envelope via the dispatcher (handleCookieValidate parses the envelope, passes it to handleRefresh which extracts env.RefreshToken). The Item A divergence is resolved at the comment-clarification level — Task 10 will swap the `_ = env` for actual consumption.

**(xii) Item C deferred to Task 10 (URL-decode on extractCallbackParams).** Task 5's extractCallbackParams does NOT URL-decode the code + state query parameters. Per Item C of the Task 5 reviewer notes: URL-decoding is Task 10's concern (oauth_client.go owns the percent-encoding side via urlEncode per AMEND-5 + ADR-0185; the decoding side is symmetric and lives in the same file). Task 8 documents the deferral in the handleCallback body comment + this §Decision sub-clause; no code change at Task 8.

### Consequences

**(a) Envoy-go-strict race-vs-rotation simplification per D14.** The "no per-stream serialization; each request POSTs independently; latest Set-Cookie wins" pattern is the LOAD-BEARING simplification per planner-time D14 + ADR-0183. The alternative (per-stream serialization via a shared cache of in-flight refresh-token POSTs keyed by RefreshToken value) would require: (1) a package-level sync.Map of in-flight POSTs; (2) a request-coalescing mechanism that returns the same in-flight response to N concurrent requests; (3) a TTL-based cleanup of the cache. The complexity-cost is OUT OF PROPORTION to the worst-case "a few extra refresh-token POSTs in the concurrent-burst scenario" tradeoff — operators with a high-concurrency burst of expired-BearerToken requests see the worst case (N concurrent rotations triggering N concurrent refresh POSTs to the IdP), but the steady-state cookie convergence happens within the response window. The race-detector cleanliness at `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_*` (4 tests under `-race`) validates the no-mutex discipline.

**(b) Race-detector coverage at `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_*` per planner-time D4 + D14.** Four race-test rows landed at Task 8: (1) `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_2RequestsSameCookies_BothPost` (no-dedup invariant: postCount == N for N concurrent rotations); (2) `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_CounterIncrementOnePerEvent` (one-per-event invariant: oauth_refreshtoken_success == N for N concurrent successes); (3) `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_MixedSuccessAndFailure` (mixed-success counter partitioning: succ + fail == N; succ == N/2; fail == N/2); (4) `TestRefreshTokenRotation_Concurrent_OnDestroy_Mid_Refresh_NoPanic` (the OnDestroy + in-flight refresh race). All 4 GREEN under `go test -race -count=5` — zero data-race violations across 5 iterations + 60+ concurrent goroutines per row.

**(c) Cross-phase reuse intent — deferred Set-Cookie + no-per-stream-serialization pattern.** The pattern is reusable for any future cookie-refresh-on-success flow that wants race-free concurrent rotation without per-stream coordination. The 3-piece primitive (deferred envelope stored on filter state under mutex + async goroutine with done-guard + LATEST-wins browser semantic) generalizes to any hypothetical phase-20-successor filter that needs the same wire-shape — e.g., a future PKCE-with-stateful-refresh filter, or a future opaque-token-rotation filter. The pattern is recorded here as a forward-pointer for phase-20-successor filter designers (no concrete second-consumer landscape at phase 20; second-consumer trigger would re-evaluate extraction to a shared package per ADR-0177 trail).

**(d) Task 5 reviewer hand-off items A + B + C resolved.** Item A (`_ = env` clarification) resolved via comment-only update at handleCallback per §Decision (xi). Item B disposition (per re-read of literal D15 at the Task 8 follow-up): Task 5's implementation was correct per literal D15 — the standard `oauth_unauthorized_rq` counter SHOULD increment on BOTH the bad-state-cookie path AND the POST-callback PARSE-REJECT path. The Task 8 commit `df33e4b` introduced an erroneous call-site split (`handleBadStateNoCounter`) which was REVERTED in the Task 8 follow-up commit per §Decision (x). The current dispatcher routes both PARSE-REJECT triggers through `handleBadState` per literal D15. Item C (URL-decode in extractCallbackParams) deferred to Task 10 per §Decision (xii); the handleCallback body comment + this §Consequences paragraph record the deferral. All three items resolved or explicitly deferred; no pending Task 5 hand-off items at Task 8 close.

**(e) D11 hypothesis preserved.** This §Decision settles all surfaces in-place inside ADR-0183 per ADR-0044's in-§Decision IMPL-settling discipline. NO new ADR fires at Task 8 IMPL. Next-free ADR stays at `ADR-0186` (unconsumed; D11 hypothesis HOLDING per the planner-time D11 declaration; confirmed via `grep -cE '^## ADR-0186' docs/envoy-go/DECISIONS.md` returns 0 post-commit). The Task 8 surface — refresh-token rotation continuation + deferred Set-Cookie discipline + no-per-stream-serialization + counter increment matrix + OnDestroy guard discipline + tokenEndpointPosterFn abstraction + Task 5 hand-off items A+B+C — all settled in-place within ADR-0183 §Decision + §Consequences body. No surface emerged that warranted a separate ADR.

**(f) AMEND-3 deny-path discipline preserved at the refresh leg.** The refresh-failure wire shape (category (a) 302 challenge) is the SAME wire shape as the unauthenticated-from-scratch path (handleUnauthenticated). The only difference is the counter call-site (oauth_refreshtoken_failure vs. no counter on the (a) path proper). NO 500 anywhere — refresh-failure routes to (a) 302; transport errors route to (a) 302; the AMEND-3 + §20.P9 REFUTED "NO 500 anywhere" invariant holds at the refresh leg as it does at the callback leg + the dispatcher + the bad-state path. A regression that emitted 500 from the refresh failure leg would be caught at fixture-0024 (Task 12) — the wire-shape byte-comparison includes the status code.

**(g) `tokenEndpointPosterFn` forward-stability for Task 10.** The function-shaped abstraction is designed to fit Task 10's oauth_client.go::postTokenEndpoint implementation without churn. Task 10 wires the production implementation as: `func(ctx, grantType, codeOrRefreshToken, clientID, clientSecret string) (*http.Response, error) { body := buildTokenRequestBody(grantType, params) ; return cc.httpClient.Do(ctx, "POST", cc.tokenEndpoint.String(), body, jsonContentType) }` per AMEND-5 + ADR-0185. The Task 8 abstraction's 5-parameter signature accommodates both the auth-code template (4-field: grant_type=authorization_code&code={0}&client_id={1}&client_secret={2}&redirect_uri={3}) and the refresh-token template (3-field: grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token={0}&client_id={1}&client_secret={2}) — the redirect_uri parameter is sourced from cc.redirectURI on the auth-code leg (not passed through the abstraction), preserving the 5-parameter abstraction shape. Task 11's buildCompiledConfig populates the field from a closure capturing the Task 10 production poster + cc.httpClient + cc.tokenEndpoint.

**(h) Cross-phase forward-pointer for response-side Set-Cookie wiring at Task 11.** Task 8 stores the deferred Set-Cookie envelope on f.pendingSetCookies; Task 11's full filter integration wires the encode-side emission. The architectural choice (decoder-only filter per SPEC §6.12 + the §9 family-row precedent; deferred envelope flows through the response chain) preserves the decoder-only invariant — no encoder-side filter logic at MVP. A future phase that wants response-side observability of the rotation event (e.g., a Prometheus histogram of rotation latency) would add an encoder-side hook; Task 8's primitive accommodates the extension without rework.

**Cross-references at the IMPL anchor:** ADR-0044 (in-place edit discipline); ADR-0080 (envoy-go-strict discipline — AMEND-3 + §20.P9 + the no-500-anywhere invariant); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance for cc / dcb / stats / tokenEndpointPoster); ADR-0125 (canonical roster — NO amendment fires at Task 8; oauth2 strengthens the NO-extension lesson per §5.4); ADR-0143 (HCM-rooted SN2-reuse — the counter prefix shape oauth_refreshtoken_success / oauth_refreshtoken_failure; namespace continuity); ADR-0156 (extauthz precedent for the async-resume + applyDisposition pattern); ADR-0159 (extauthz async-resume + OnDestroy guard discipline — D4 reuse without modification); ADR-0177 (httpclient extraction precedent — Task 10's poster consumes *httpclient.Client; ADR-0183 declares the abstraction Task 10 implements); ADR-0178 (sdsfile + atomic.Pointer reload — Task 11's clientSecretFn closure captures the sdsfile.Watcher); ADR-0180 (state-machine — handleRefresh is dispatch step 4); ADR-0181 (cookie envelope — emitCategoryB_PostCallback is the Task 8 deferred Set-Cookie payload builder); ADR-0182 (AES-256-CBC — Task 10 will encrypt the new access_token + refresh_token before populating the envelope); ADR-0185 (Task 10's refresh-token POST body template byte-exact wire shape); phase-20 SPEC §3.6 + §4.1 + §4.5 + §4.6 + §4.7 + §6.3 + §6.8 + §6.12; phase-20 SPEC §1.1 AMEND-3 + AMEND-5; phase-20 SPEC §2.15 (MVP-CONSUMED `default_refresh_token_expires_in` + `use_refresh_token`); phase-20 SPEC §14.2 race-detector tests; phase-20 SPEC §10 ADR anchor map; phase-20 SPEC §13 items C7 + C8 (envoy-go-strict departures at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md); phase-20 PLAN planner-time decisions D4 + D11 + D14 + D15.
