## ADR-0188: NEW `internal/lua/` framework primitive — gopher-lua VM lifecycle + per-stream `*LState` construction + per-script-source `*Chunk` compile cache + default-deny `SandboxConfig` + bridge-registration interface — at first-consumer (HTTP Lua filter) per phase-22 BRAINSTORM Q4 EXTRACT-NOW with EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause for consumer #2 (future cluster-specifier / access-logger / string-matcher Lua phases)

**Status:** §Context anchored at phase-22 parent SPEC commit (this commit); §Decision + §Consequences body lands at phase-22.1 IMPL Lands-in-Task (the primitive's first commit) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-18 (§Context anchor at this SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences body lands at 22.1 IMPL Lands-in-Task)
**Doctrine:** Phase 22 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline.
**Lands-in:** Phase 22.1 IMPL first task that materializes `internal/lua/` (anticipated Task 1-3 per the phase-21 + phase-17 framework-primitive-first-task precedent).

### Context

ADR-0188 anchors the NEW `internal/lua/` framework primitive — the FIRST §9 family-row framework primitive of substantial scope since phase 17 (jwt_authn at `internal/jwks/` + `internal/jwt/`), ENDING the phase-21 ZERO-NEW-framework-primitive streak. Per phase-22 BRAINSTORM Q4 EXTRACT-NOW decision + parent SPEC §4.1 + §11.3 empirical scrape, the primitive hosts the GENERIC gopher-lua VM lifecycle (init, sandbox config, panic-recovery, per-stream execution context, script-compilation cache, bridge-registration interface); the consumer-specific bridge methods (`request_handle:headers()`, `response_handle:headers()`, etc.) live in `internal/filter/http/lua/` per ADR-0189.

**Framework-primitive trigger per Q4 EXTRACT-NOW (DEPARTURE from phase-17 + phase-21 EXTRACT-NOW-only-when-trigger-fires lesson).** The 22.1 IMPL extracts the primitive at consumer #1 (HTTP Lua filter) — first-of-kind for the project: every prior NEW framework primitive landed at ≥2 anticipated consumers at extraction time (jwks at jwt_authn + future-extauthz reuse; grpcclient at ext_authz + future-ext_proc reuse; httpclient at oauth2 + future-Lua-httpCall reuse; sdsfile at oauth2 + future-SDS-secret-injection reuse; matcher at rbac + future-jwt_authn + future-ext_authz + future-ext_proc reuse). Phase 22.1's `internal/lua/` is extracted at consumer #1 only — the future-consumer roster (cluster specifier Lua at `envoy.router.cluster_specifiers.lua`, access logger Lua at `envoy.access_loggers.lua`, string matcher Lua at `envoy.string_matcher.lua`) is speculative; none committed to the ROADMAP. The bolder extraction at consumer #1 carries higher abstraction-shape revision risk: the `internal/lua/` API may need revision after consumer #2 materializes (e.g., the bridge-registration interface may not generalize cleanly from HTTP filter to cluster specifier). This ADR anchors the abstraction shape WITH AN EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause for consumer #2 — mirrors phase-20 ADR-0159 §Future Work CLOSURE-AT-PHASE-20 pattern but in the opposite direction (anticipating future revision rather than closing prior revision).

**Lua VM library = `github.com/yuin/gopher-lua` v1.1.2** per phase-22 BRAINSTORM Q3 + parent SPEC AMEND-2 (pin recommendation). Pure-Go Lua 5.1 interpreter; matches upstream Envoy's LuaJIT 5.1 dialect; NO CGO; MIT-licensed; widely adopted (Caddy, Consul, Hashicorp tooling). Alternative `aarzilli/golua` CGO binding to real Lua/LuaJIT rejected on portability cost grounds (musl/glibc, cross-compilation, Docker base-image impact); alternative `Shopify/go-lua` Lua 5.2 rejected on dialect-mismatch grounds (5.2's `goto`, integer subtype, `bit32`/`utf8` stdlib introduce script-author confusion). The v1.1.2 pin recommendation per parent SPEC §11.2.4 (the latest tag at scrape time; pair with SHA in `go.mod` for human discoverability per ADR-0008-equivalent discipline).

**Sandbox roster = default-deny envoy-go-strict DEPARTURE from upstream** per parent SPEC §4.3 + AMEND-1 + §11.3 REFUTATION of BRAINSTORM §7.2 surface-1. Upstream Envoy calls `luaL_openlibs(state.get())` — full LuaJIT stdlib — WITHOUT subsequent neutering (per `source/extensions/filters/common/lua/lua.cc` v1.37.2). envoy-go's strict default-deny sandbox (DENY `io/os/debug/package/channel`; ALLOW core base + table + string + math + coroutine; `BasePrintSink` redirects `print` to drop or to logInfo-style sink) is therefore an envoy-go-strict DEPARTURE not parity preservation. The departure rationale: gopher-lua exposes sandbox-breaking modules that upstream LuaJIT in upstream Envoy's per-worker deployment model assumes operator-trust + per-worker VM scoping bounds — envoy-go's per-stream goroutine dispatch model cannot make the same assumption (any operator's Lua can compromise the entire envoy-go process via `os.execute`/`os.exit`/`io.popen`/`package.*`). One of three envoy-go-strict departure records at the 22.1 IMPL final Task BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md bundle (per parent SPEC §14 edit #3); the other two are `respond_calls` counter (parent SPEC §14 edit #4) + runtime-error log-message wording (parent SPEC §14 edit #5).

**Per-stream `*LState` construction + per-script-source `*Chunk` compile cache** per parent SPEC §4.2 + §11.3.4 + §11.3.5. WEAK-default: per-stream `*LState` construction with shared `*Chunk` cache. gopher-lua's `state.go::NewState` allocates registry + call-stack + runs `OpenLibs()` (10 module registrations); gopher-lua README explicitly recommends `sync.Pool` for per-thread reuse. The 22.1 IMPL benchmark task (per parent SPEC §13-R6 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL item) gates whether the ADR-0190 escape-valve fires for the `*LState`-pool design. WEAK-HOLD per BRAINSTORM Q10 + parent SPEC §1.2 STANDS UNCHANGED: 0-1 escape-valve slot consumption at 22.1 IMPL.

**Compile-cache discipline:** Chunks (`*FunctionProto` from gopher-lua `lua.LState.LoadString`) are safe for cross-LState reuse — they hold compiled bytecode, not LState-specific state. Cache is owned by `*compiledConfig` (filter-config-instance scope, NOT global) — matches the project's existing per-`compiledConfig` ownership discipline; cache eviction is GC-driven via config-instance lifecycle. API: `NewCompileCache() *CompileCache` + `CompileScript(src []byte, cache *CompileCache) (*Chunk, error)` + `VM.Run(chunk *Chunk, hooks ...HookFn) error` (loads `*FunctionProto` onto per-stream `*LState`; no recompilation per stream).

**Anticipated `internal/lua/` package shape:**

```
internal/lua/
  doc.go             # package overview + gopher-lua version pin + sandbox-roster citation
  vm.go              # VM type + NewVM + VMOption + WithSandboxConfig/WithPanicRecovery/WithStderrSink + Run + Close
  chunk.go           # Chunk type + compile cache (CompileCache + NewCompileCache + CompileScript)
  sandbox.go         # SandboxConfig type + per-stdlib-module selective OpenXxx + base-globals nil-out discipline
  bridge.go          # bridge-registration interface (RegisterBridgeMethod + HookFn)
  vm_test.go
  chunk_test.go
  sandbox_test.go
```

**Anticipated LoC: ~600-900** (VM lifecycle ~150 + sandbox config + selective stdlib opening ~150 + compile cache + Chunk ~120 + bridge-registration + HookFn ~80 + doc.go + tests ~200-400).

### Decision

The 22.1 IMPL anchors the NEW `internal/lua/` framework primitive with the following concrete API surface + production file split. Refines the parent SPEC §4.1 sketch + landed at IMPL Tasks 1 (skeleton + dep), 4 (compile.go + CompileCache), and 5 (vm.go + sandbox.go) with full bodies. The 22.1 SPEC §3.1-§3.4 SPEC-time refinements (function-option pattern; `Run`/`HasGlobalFunc`/`CallGlobal` split; `State()` escape-hatch; `WithPanicHandler`/`WithBasePrintSink` naming) are ALL ratified verbatim at IMPL.

**1. Production file split (3 production files + 3 test files per 22.1 SPEC §3.2 + parent §4.1):**

- `internal/lua/doc.go` — package overview + gopher-lua v1.1.2 pin + sandbox-roster citation + BRAINSTORM Q3 + Q4 cross-references.
- `internal/lua/vm.go` — `VM` type + `NewVM(opts ...VMOption) *VM` + `VMOption` function-option type + `WithSandboxConfig(SandboxConfig) VMOption` + `WithPanicHandler(PanicHandlerFn) VMOption` + `WithBasePrintSink(io.Writer) VMOption` + `State() *lua.LState` (escape-hatch for filter consumers to set up userdata + metatables) + `RegisterGlobalFunc(name string, fn lua.LGFunction)` + `Run(chunk *Chunk) error` + `HasGlobalFunc(name string) bool` + `CallGlobal(name string, args ...lua.LValue) error` + `Close()` (idempotent state.Close()) + `PanicHandlerFn func(recovered any)` (invoked after `recover()` in the panic-wrapper).
- `internal/lua/compile.go` — `Chunk` (wraps `*lua.FunctionProto` + sha256 hash) + `CompileCache` (sync.RWMutex + `map[[sha256.Size]byte]*Chunk` + double-checked write path) + `NewCompileCache() *CompileCache` + `CompileScript(src []byte, cache *CompileCache) (*Chunk, error)` (gopher-lua `Parse` + `Compile`; cache nil-tolerance per ADR-0085-equivalent ergonomic-tolerance discipline).
- `internal/lua/sandbox.go` — `SandboxConfig` (8 Allow* fields; zero-value = `StrictUpstreamParity` per AMEND-1; `AllowCoroutine` + `AllowOSTimeHelpers` zero-value-defaulted true per AMEND-A4 — explicit upstream-parity opt-in fields); `applySandbox(L *lua.LState, cfg SandboxConfig)` helper invoked at VM construction; selective per-stdlib OpenXxx + post-walk nil-out per 22.1 SPEC §3.3.
- Tests: `vm_test.go` (per-stream construction + isolation; concurrent NewVM/Run/CallGlobal/Close per Task 12); `compile_test.go` (CompileCache hit/miss/dedupe; concurrent ReadAdd per Task 12); `sandbox_test.go` (per-stdlib ALLOW/DENY exhaustive — verifies `dofile`/`loadfile`/`loadstring`/`require`/`io.open`/`io.popen`/`os.execute`/`os.exit`/`debug.getupvalue`/`channel.make`/`package.path` are nil-or-error post-sandbox-strict construction).

**2. Sandbox roster — zero-value StrictUpstreamParity (default-deny per AMEND-1).**

`SandboxConfig` zero-value posture: DENY `io`, `os`, `debug`, `package`, `channel`; ALLOW `base` (selected — `print` redirected to drop-or-logInfo sink via `WithBasePrintSink`), `table`, `string`, `math`, `coroutine` (per AMEND-A4 `AllowCoroutine` zero-value-defaulted true), `os.time`/`os.date`/`os.clock` (per AMEND-A4 `AllowOSTimeHelpers` zero-value-defaulted true — the harmless time-of-day reads). The 6 explicit opt-in `AllowXxx` fields enable consumers to broaden sandbox scope WITHOUT silent broadening — the API surface is intentionally explicit per the envoy-go-strict default-deny posture. Per-stdlib selective `OpenXxx` calls bypass `luaL_openlibs(state.get())` (which gopher-lua provides but that defeats the per-module selective discipline); the `applySandbox` helper post-walks the LState's global table and nil-outs any DENY-marked module the selective Open inadvertently left behind (defense-in-depth + matches the upstream-strict posture).

**3. Per-stream `*LState` construction (WEAK-default per parent §4.2 + §11.3.4) + per-script-source `*Chunk` compile cache (per parent §11.3.5).**

`NewVM` constructs a fresh `*lua.LState` per call — no pool. Cache discipline: chunks (`*lua.FunctionProto`) are safe for cross-LState reuse (they hold compiled bytecode, not LState-specific state — gopher-lua-confirmed at `compile.go` `*FunctionProto` shape). Cache is owned by `*CompileCache` (filter-config-instance scope, NOT global — matches the project's existing per-`compiledConfig` ownership discipline; cache eviction is GC-driven via config-instance lifecycle). API: `NewCompileCache() *CompileCache` + `CompileScript(src []byte, cache *CompileCache) (*Chunk, error)`. The cache key is `sha256(src)` (32 bytes per content-addressable hashing); collision-resistant + content-deduplicating (multiple filter configs pointing at the same script bytes share a single `*Chunk`). Cache-nil tolerance per ADR-0085-equivalent ergonomic-tolerance: `CompileScript(src, nil)` skips the cache + always recompiles (test ergonomics — unit tests don't need to construct a cache to invoke `CompileScript`).

**D-P10 R6 disposition — STANDS WEAK-default; ADR-0190 NOT consumed.** Per parent §13-R6 RATIFIED-PENDING-IMPL gate + 22.1 PLAN D-P10 codification: 22.1 IMPL Task 12 `BenchmarkPerStreamLState_Construction_Headers` measures the per-stream construction cost matching production `DecodeHeaders` step-by-step (NewVM + 5 metatable installs + requestHandleContext + LUserData + Run + CallGlobal + Close). The threshold gate per D-P10 fires ADR-0190 (the `*LState`-pool escape-valve design) only if `ns/op > 1_000_000` (= 1ms). **Observed:** `ns/op = 69865` (~70µs; 3 independent runs at 69935 / 72333 / 69865 — within ~5% of central value; well under threshold). **Disposition: R6 STANDS WEAK-default — per-stream construction acceptable; ADR-0190 NOT consumed; carries forward to 22.2 BRAINSTORM** as the 22.2 IMPL escape-valve slot. 22.2 may re-evaluate against the body/trailer bridge surface (more bridge methods + more per-stream allocation); ADR-0190 fires at 22.2 IMPL only if the body/trailer extension crosses the 1ms threshold.

**4. Compile-cache concurrency discipline.**

`CompileCache.Get(key [sha256.Size]byte) (*Chunk, bool)` reads under RLock fast-path. `CompileCache.Add(key, *Chunk)` writes under Lock with a double-checked re-Get inside the Lock — if a racer populated the same key during the unlock-to-lock window, both racers observe the SAME `*Chunk` pointer (dedupe — verified at `TestCompileCache_ConcurrentReadAdd_SameContentDedupes`). Race-clean under `-race -count=10` per Task 12 verification.

**5. EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE for consumer #2 (per BRAINSTORM Q4).**

The 22.1 IMPL extracts `internal/lua/` at consumer #1 (HTTP Lua filter) — first-of-kind for the project: every prior NEW framework primitive landed at ≥2 anticipated consumers at extraction time (jwks at jwt_authn + future-extauthz reuse; grpcclient at ext_authz + future-ext_proc reuse; httpclient at oauth2 + future-Lua-httpCall reuse; sdsfile at oauth2 + future-SDS-secret-injection reuse; matcher at rbac + future-jwt_authn + future-ext_authz + future-ext_proc reuse). Phase 22.1's `internal/lua/` is extracted at consumer #1 only — the future-consumer roster (cluster specifier Lua at `envoy.router.cluster_specifiers.lua`, access logger Lua at `envoy.access_loggers.lua`, string matcher Lua at `envoy.string_matcher.lua`) is speculative; none committed to the ROADMAP. **EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause:** the 22.1 IMPL `internal/lua/` API surface (the 9-method `VM` type + `VMOption` function-option + `Chunk` + `CompileCache` + `SandboxConfig`) is NOT byte-pinned across future phases. The second `internal/lua/` consumer (at one of the future Lua filter phases) MAY require API revision after empirical validation at consumer #2 (e.g., the per-stream dispatch model may not generalize cleanly from per-request HTTP filter to per-cluster cluster-specifier; the bridge-registration discipline may need a registry abstraction). This ADR explicitly anchors the abstraction shape WITH the allowance — mirrors phase-20 ADR-0159 §Future Work CLOSURE-AT-PHASE-20 pattern but in the opposite direction (anticipating future revision rather than closing prior revision).

### Consequences

- **(+) Reusable VM primitive for future Lua-style filters.** The `internal/lua/` API exposes the gopher-lua VM lifecycle + per-stream `*LState` + per-script-source `*Chunk` compile cache + `SandboxConfig` zero-value StrictUpstreamParity as the seam between primitive + filter-specific consumer. Future consumers (cluster specifier Lua, access logger Lua, string matcher Lua) consume the same primitive without re-implementing the lifecycle.
- **(+) Strict-by-default sandbox eliminates accidental privilege escalation.** The 8-Allow*-field `SandboxConfig` zero-value posture DENIES `io`/`os`/`debug`/`package`/`channel`; consumers must explicitly opt into broader sandbox scope via `WithSandboxConfig(SandboxConfig{...})`. Silent broadening requires an operator-visible code edit. Mirrors the phase-04 TLS strict-by-default posture + the phase-10 header_mutation pre-mutation-allowlist discipline.
- **(+) Per-stream `*LState` isolation enables independent stream isolation under concurrent dispatch.** Each `DecodeHeaders` / `EncodeHeaders` invocation constructs a fresh `*LState` per stream (Task 12 race-clean across N=100 × `-count=10` = 1000 concurrent invocations). No cross-stream state leak via shared `*FunctionProto` (the cache stores compiled bytecode, not VM state).
- **(+) Compile-cache content-addressable hashing dedupes shared scripts.** Multiple filter configs pointing at the same script bytes share a single `*Chunk` pointer via sha256 keying. GC-driven eviction via config-instance lifecycle — no manual lifecycle management.
- **(+) gopher-lua v1.1.2 dependency choice retains pure-Go cross-compilation + zero CGO + MIT-license.** Per BRAINSTORM Q3 + parent SPEC AMEND-2 pin recommendation. Pure-Go Lua 5.1 interpreter; matches upstream Envoy's LuaJIT 5.1 dialect; widely adopted (Caddy, Consul, Hashicorp tooling). No musl/glibc / cross-compilation / Docker base-image impact.
- **(-) Per-stream `*LState` construction overhead measured at ~70µs/stream.** Task 12 R6 STANDS WEAK-default — well under 1ms threshold per parent §13-R6 + D-P10. At sustained ~70µs/stream, 14k+ stream constructions/sec/core are sustainable — well above the order-of-magnitude that operationally justifies an `*LState` pool. ADR-0190 escape-valve carries forward to 22.2 BRAINSTORM as the 22.2 IMPL escape-valve slot.
- **(-) gopher-lua is Lua 5.1 (not 5.2)** — `pairs()` doesn't auto-dispatch `__pairs` metamethod on userdata (5.2+ feature). Bridge-side shim required at `internal/filter/http/lua/bridge.go` (`__pairs` userdata-method that snapshots into alphabetically-sorted slice + walks by integer index) per 22.1 SPEC §11.2 D7 refinement. Adds ~30-50 LoC + 1 cross-run-determinism test at `bridge_test.go`. Documented at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` bridge surface entry #10.
- **(-) Sandbox cannot be opted-out for `AllowCoroutine` zero-value-default true** (intentional per AMEND-A4 upstream parity — upstream LuaJIT exposes the `coroutine` library; AMEND-A4 documents the zero-value default as upstream-parity preservation). Operators opt-out via explicit `WithSandboxConfig(SandboxConfig{AllowCoroutine: false, ...})`.
- **(?) API may revise at consumer #2** (per BRAINSTORM Q4 EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE above). The future Lua filter phase that consumes `internal/lua/` at consumer #2 may surface abstraction-shape revision requirements; the ADR anchors the allowance forward. No silent revision — any revision requires an ADR amendment + cross-reference to this ADR's allowance clause.
- **(?) Forward-pointer: AMEND-9 gopher-lua-vs-LuaJIT divergence catalogue** (per BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` envoy-go-strict departure record + 22.1 SPEC AMEND-9). The (a) `tostring(float)` Go shortest-round-trippable vs LuaJIT `"%.14g"`, (b) `string.format("%d", float)` Go-fmt-mismatch, (c) `pcall` error-message prefix divergences are forward-pointed for 22.2 (recommends `lua.FormatNumber(v) string` helper on `internal/lua/` for 22.2 use). 22.1 headers-bridge scope intentionally avoids these surfaces; 22.2 body/trailers bridge cannot.

**Cross-references:** ADR-0189 (paired consumer-side ADR — `internal/filter/http/lua/` package shape); ADR-0125 §(xiv) AMENDMENT-anticipation (the 22.3-anticipated 9th canonical AMENDMENT — anchored at parent SPEC commit; body lands at 22.3 IMPL); phase-22 parent SPEC §4 + §11.3 + AMEND-1 + AMEND-2 + AMEND-A4; phase-22.1 SPEC §3.1-§3.4 (production API refinements); phase-17 jwt_authn ADR-0148 + ADR-0149 (the prior NEW-framework-primitive-of-substantial-scope precedent — `internal/jwks/Fetcher` + `internal/jwt/` verifier); phase-21 ADR-0186 (the prior single-row §9 framework primitive precedent — inline `Clock` seam stayed in-package per phase-17 EXTRACT-NOW-only-when-trigger-fires lesson; phase 22.1 STRENGTHENS the precedent by extracting at consumer #1 per BRAINSTORM Q4 + EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE).

NO separate new ADR; lives inside this ADR-0189 §Decision body; does NOT consume ADR-0190 escape-valve.

**`:respond(headers, body)` byte-pin** per parent SPEC §11.6.7 + AMEND-7 + AMEND-8. For `:respond({[":status"]="403"}, "denied")` from `envoy_on_request`: status `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`; `content-length: 6` (auto-set per upstream `Utility::prepareLocalReply` at `utility.cc:1270`); `content-type: text/plain` (default per `utility.cc:1241,1273` because Lua headers did NOT supply); body `denied` (6 bytes verbatim); no upstream request; `response_code_details: "lua_response"` (access-log surface only). `:respond()` from `envoy_on_response` raises runtime error `"respond not currently supported in the response path"` per upstream `lua_filter.cc:1031-1034`. `:status` validated `[200, 600)` with byte-exact error string `":status must be between 200-599"` per upstream `lua_filter.cc:~578-580`. envoy-go's `internal/filter/http/lua/bridge.go::respond` MIRRORS all three byte-exact wire-shapes + runtime-error strings.

**SPEC-time D-questions anchored for IMPL-time resolution** per parent SPEC §12: D1 (default_source_code absent vs no-op disposition; resolves at 22.1 IMPL first-task scrape against upstream `config.cc::createFilterFactoryFromProtoTyped`); D3 (scenario (e) `:logInfo()` cross-side assertion shape; resolves at 22.1 PLAN session; recommended option (a) — stat-counter delta IS the assertion); D5 (28th-fuzzer count verification; resolves at 22.1 IMPL first-task `grep -c "^func Fuzz"`); D7 (envoy-go headers-map insertion-order verification; resolves at 22.1 IMPL first-task scrape against `internal/filter/http/header_mutation/`).

### Decision

The 22.1 IMPL anchors the NEW `internal/filter/http/lua/` package as consumer #1 of the NEW `internal/lua/` framework primitive (ADR-0188). Refines the parent SPEC §4.4 sketch + landed across IMPL Tasks 1-15 with full bodies (Task 1 skeleton; Task 2 compiled_config; Task 3 datasource; Task 6-9 bridge; Task 10 stats + boot-registration; Task 11 fuzzer; Task 12 race tests; Tasks 13-15 differential fixture-0026 + wording-pinning). The 22.1 SPEC §3.5 file split + §4 compiledConfig shape + §6.2 19-arm PARSE-REJECT roster (parent §6.2 was 18; Task 11 fuzzer surfaced 2 more) + §8 fixture-0026 disposition + §13-R1 + §13-W are ALL ratified at IMPL.

**1. Production file split (8 production files + 5 test files per 22.1 SPEC §3.5 + parent §4.4):**

- `internal/filter/http/lua/doc.go` — package overview + Q1-Q12 BRAINSTORM decision summary + AMEND-1..AMEND-12 cross-references.
- `internal/filter/http/lua/lua.go` — filter struct + factory (`HTTPFilterFactory`) + `New(name string, typed *anypb.Any, scope *stats.Scope, hcmPrefix string) (filter.HTTPFilter, error)` + boot-registration `init()` hook via `internal/filter/http/registry`.
- `internal/filter/http/lua/compiled_config.go` — `compiledConfig` struct (`chunk *lua.Chunk` + `compileCache *lua.CompileCache` + `sandbox lua.SandboxConfig` + `stats *filterStats`) + `buildCompiledConfig(typed *anypb.Any, scope *stats.Scope, hcmPrefix string) (*compiledConfig, error)` + 4-arm-active + 2-arm-reserved + 1-arm-cross-reference PARSE-REJECT wording constants + 2 wrap helpers (`wrapParseRejectTypedConfigUnmarshal` + `wrapParseRejectScriptCompileFailed`) + `validatePerRouteLua` (per-route TPFC validator registered at boot per ADR-0110 single-chokepoint).

- `internal/filter/http/lua/bridge.go` — Lua-side bridge: 7 headers-object methods (`get`/`add`/`replace`/`remove`/`__index`/`__newindex`/`__pairs`) + 6 `:logXxx` methods + 4-method `:streamInfo()` subset (`protocol`/`routeName`/`downstreamLocalAddress`/`downstreamDirectRemoteAddress`) + `request_handle:respond(headers, body)` byte-pin per parent §11.6.7 + AMEND-7 + AMEND-8 + encode-side runtime-reject byte-exact `"respond not currently supported in the response path"` per AMEND-8.
- `internal/filter/http/lua/decode_headers.go` — `envoy_on_request` hook firing via `vm.CallGlobal("envoy_on_request", reqUd)` + nil-chunk short-circuit (D1 REFUTED — silent pass-through) + per-stream VM construction + bridge metatable installs + stats counter increments (`executions` + conditional `errors` + `respond_calls`).

**2. `compiledConfig` lifecycle (per 22.1 SPEC §4).**

`buildCompiledConfig` runs at `New()` time (filter-config-instance construction): typed-config nil-check (arm 1) → typed-config Unmarshal (arm 2) → stat-prefix validation (arm 19 — `stats.IsValidName` pre-check) → InlineCode deprecated-rejection (arm 3) → SourceCodes deferred-rejection (arm 4) → DefaultSourceCode absent-handling (arm 5 D1 REFUTED → silent no-op via `&compiledConfig{chunk: nil}`) → `resolveDataSource` (arms 6-15 + arm 9-extension) → `lua.CompileScript` (arm 16 — gopher-lua `*lua.ApiError` wrap per `wrapParseRejectScriptCompileFailed`). `compiledConfig.chunk` is shared across all streams via the per-filter-config `compileCache`; the per-stream `*lua.LState` is fresh per `DecodeHeaders` / `EncodeHeaders` call. `cc.chunk == nil` semantics: pass-through (no VM construction; no stats increments; no bridge dispatch) — covers the D1 REFUTED arm 5 + 17 silent no-op cases.

**3. 19-arm PARSE-REJECT roster (parent §6.2 + 22.1 IMPL fuzzer extensions per Task 11).**

Per parent §6.2 + AMEND-4 (CONFIRMS-AND-TIGHTENS to 18 baseline arms) + AMEND-5 (10 DataSource-related leaves) + AMEND-6 (3 additional baseline arms; sandbox-violation arm RETRACTED) + Task 11 fuzzer extensions:

- **18 baseline arms** per parent §6.2 (arms 1-18; see BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` 19-arm PARSE-REJECT roster table for byte-exact wordings).
- **Arm 19 — `Lua.stat_prefix` invalid chars** (Task 11 fuzzer surfaced; `stats.IsValidName` regex pre-check; byte-exact `"lua: stat_prefix: invalid characters in %q (must match %s)"`). Pattern mirrors `hcm/config.go:209` + `cluster/manager.go:205` `stats.IsValidName` pre-check precedent. Without arm-19 validation, an invalid stat_prefix panicked at `stats.NewCounter` boot-time per ADR-0059's boot-time-panic discipline — killing the proxy. Fix lands at Task 11 inline (~30 LoC delta + 20 LoC doc-comment).
- **Arm 9-extension — `Filename` 16 MiB cap** (Task 11 fuzzer surfaced; `/dev/full` infinite-read defense; byte-exact `"lua: default_source_code: file %q exceeds the maximum script size of %d bytes"`). Without bounded read, naive `os.ReadFile` against `/dev/full` (or any infinite-read device, named pipe, multi-GB script-file typo) OOM-killed the proxy at boot. Fix replaces `os.ReadFile` with `os.Open` + `io.LimitReader(f, maxFilenameScriptBytes+1)` where `maxFilenameScriptBytes = 16 MiB` (~25 LoC delta + 30 LoC doc-comment). The +1 read byte distinguishes "exactly at cap" (accepted) from "one byte over" (rejected).
- **D1 disposition: REFUTED both arms 5 + 17** per Task 2 first-action upstream-scrape evidence (see ADR-0189 §Context + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` D1 disposition + 22.1 PROGRESS Task 2 entry verbatim evidence). Both arms silently no-op per upstream parity. Reserved wording constants pinned in source with `//nolint:unused` + explanatory godoc for future policy-bump migration — mirrors phase-21 adaptive_concurrency's `parseRejectFixedValueDeferred` reserved-constant precedent.

Byte-stable wording per ADR-0080 + the phase-21 SPEC §5 precedent. Constants live as package-private `parseReject*` consts at `compiled_config.go` + `datasource.go`. All wording byte-pinned via `TestParseRejectConstants_ByteExactWording` + `TestResolveDataSource_ByteExactWording`.

Resolution at config-load time (NOT per-request): `resolveDataSource` returns bytes for the 4 active arms (Filename + InlineBytes + InlineString + EnvironmentVariable); WatchedDirectory + empty-oneof PARSE-REJECT. Resolved bytes feed into `internal/lua/CompileScript` (Task 4 IMPL) + cached on `*compiledConfig` for filter-instance lifetime per the per-`compiledConfig` cache scope.

**5. Pragmatic-middle bridge surface (21 entries — 2 hooks + 7 headers + `__pairs` + 6 log + 4 streamInfo + 1 respond per-side; per BRAINSTORM Q6 + this 22.1 SPEC §4.3 dispatch shape).**

Per BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` bridge surface roster (21 entries). Per-stream `*lua.LState` construction + 5 metatable installs (requestHandle + responseHandle + headers + streamInfo + headersIter) + `vm.Run(chunk)` + `vm.CallGlobal(name, reqUd)` per the per-side hook dispatch. The bridge surface is 100% in-package (`internal/filter/http/lua/bridge.go`); the `internal/lua/` primitive does NOT export bridge-registration discipline at 22.1 (the SPEC §3.1 sketch evolved at IMPL — bridge construction happens in-filter via `vm.State().NewUserData()` + metatable construction + per-method `lua.LGFunction` registration; the primitive exposes `State() *lua.LState` as escape-hatch + `RegisterGlobalFunc` convenience).

**Deferred bridge surface raises Lua runtime error per the Lua-idiomatic disposition** (body methods, metadata methods, `:httpCall()`, crypto, filesystem, `:timestamp()`, `:connection()`, full `:streamInfo()`). All defer to 22.2 IMPL per parent §10 forward-pointers.

**6. `:respond()` byte-pin (per parent §11.6.7 + AMEND-7 + AMEND-8).**

Mirrors upstream `Utility::prepareLocalReply` at `utility.cc:1237-1284` + `lua_filter.cc:559-583`: status `[200, 600)` byte-exact validation (`":status must be between 200-599"`); auto content-length from body length; auto `content-type: text/plain` default when Lua headers table didn't supply; no upstream request initiated. Encode-side `:respond()` runtime-rejects with byte-exact `"respond not currently supported in the response path"` per `lua_filter.cc:1031-1034` (caught by panic-recovery wrapper, increments `errors`, script aborts). `respond_calls` counter increments per invocation (envoy-go-strict per AMEND-3).

**7. `__pairs` alphabetical-snapshot per 22.1 SPEC §11.2 D7 refinement.**

D7 CLOSURE: envoy-go headers-map type EMPIRICALLY-DETERMINED at SPEC-time as `net/http.Header` (Go `map[string][]string`; unordered per Go map semantics; the codebase explicitly acknowledges at `internal/filter/http/types.go:86-90`). The bridge installs a per-headers `__pairs` userdata-method that snapshots into an alphabetically-sorted `[][2]string` and walks by integer index. Iteration order is deterministic across runs and across proxies (alphabetical by key) — REFUTES BRAINSTORM hypothesis that headers-map was insertion-ordered. gopher-lua is Lua 5.1 (`pairs()` doesn't auto-dispatch `__pairs` on userdata; 5.2+ feature) — the bridge-side shim makes `pairs(headers)` behave as if 5.2 auto-dispatch were enabled. Verified at `bridge_test.go::TestBridge_HeadersPairs_AlphabeticalSnapshot_CrossRunDeterministic`.

## ADR-0190: NEW `internal/dynamicmetadata/` framework primitive — per-stream `*Bucket` accessor for cross-filter dynamic-metadata read+write at first co-consumer (HTTP Lua filter 22.2) per phase-22 BRAINSTORM Q3 cross-phase-deferral-break + Q9 EXTRACT-NOW

**Status:** Accepted — §Decision + §Consequences body landed at phase-22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing (THIS commit); §Context body unchanged from the 22.2 SPEC anchor commit.
**Date:** 2026-05-19 (§Context anchor at predecessor 22.2 SPEC commit `0d6463e`; §Decision + §Consequences body land at this 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline)
**Doctrine:** Phase 22.2 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline.
**Lands-in:** Phase 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic-landing (same Task as ADR-0191 + ADR-0192 + ADR-0177 AMENDMENT body per PLAN).

### Context

ADR-0190 anchors the NEW `internal/dynamicmetadata/` framework primitive — a per-stream cross-filter dynamic-metadata accessor. It is the THIRD §9 family-row framework primitive of substantial scope landing in two-phase succession (after ADR-0188 `internal/lua/` + ADR-0189 `internal/filter/http/lua/` at phase-22.1 IMPL), STRENGTHENING the post-phase-21 NEW-framework-primitive cadence and reflecting the project's growing cross-filter-state surface.

**Cross-phase deferral-break trigger per BRAINSTORM Q3 + §1.6.** Phases 16 (rbac) / 17 (jwt_authn) / 18 (ext_authz) / 19 (ext_proc) / 20 (oauth2) each deferred dynamic-metadata access by their respective filters with BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "operator-visibility deferred to future" notes. The deferral was about IMPL — each phase chose not to be the first to land a cross-filter state primitive — NOT about principle (operators DO want dynamic-metadata visibility from these filters). Phase 22.2 lands the cross-filter primitive at first co-consumer (the HTTP Lua filter's `:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata()` + `:dynamicTypedMetadata(filter_name)` bridge methods). Future phase BRAINSTORMs that need dynamic-metadata access from their respective filters consume `internal/dynamicmetadata/` rather than defer again — each prior-phase BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note converts from "deferred" to "lifted via `internal/dynamicmetadata`" at the lift-phase's next-touchpoint.

**Primitive shape per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.1 + §11.6 D1 closure.** Package boundary: `internal/dynamicmetadata/` hosts the per-stream `*Bucket` accessor + map keyed by `(filter_name string, key string) → *structpb.Value`; consumers consume the API via their per-stream context. Per-stream lifecycle (created at filter-chain entry per ADR-0033; destroyed at OnDestroy); per-stream sequential per ADR-0033 (no cross-filter concurrency within a stream); NOT goroutine-safe across streams. nil-bucket tolerant per ADR-0085: `Get(filterName, key)` returns `(nil, false)`; `Set` is no-op; `Snapshot` returns nil.

**Anticipated API surface** (per 22.2 SPEC §3.1):

```go
package dynamicmetadata

type Bucket struct { /* unexported: m map[string]map[string]*structpb.Value */ }

func NewBucket() *Bucket
func (b *Bucket) Get(filterName, key string) (*structpb.Value, bool)
func (b *Bucket) Set(filterName, key string, value *structpb.Value)
func (b *Bucket) Snapshot() map[string]map[string]*structpb.Value
func (b *Bucket) Reset()
```

**Lifecycle integration:** the FilterChain (`internal/filter/http/chain.go`) gains a new `dynamicMetadata *dynamicmetadata.Bucket` field. At chain construction (per-stream entry), the field is initialized via `dynamicmetadata.NewBucket()`. At OnDestroy, `chain.dynamicMetadata.Reset()` is called. The filter-callback API surface (`internal/filter/http/callbacks.go`) gains two new accessors: `DecoderFilterCallbacks.DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket` + `EncoderFilterCallbacks.DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket` (returns same bucket per-stream shared across decode + encode).

**Anticipated `internal/dynamicmetadata/` package shape:**

```
internal/dynamicmetadata/
  doc.go               # package overview + cross-phase deferral-lift rationale +
                       # API surface summary + ADR-0190 cross-reference
  dynamicmetadata.go   # Bucket type + NewBucket + Get + Set + Snapshot + Reset
  dynamicmetadata_test.go  # exhaustive table-driven tests including nil-tolerance
  bench_test.go        # microbenchmarks for Get/Set under per-stream sequential access
```

**Anticipated LoC: ~250-400** (Bucket type + 4 methods ~80-120 + doc.go + tests ~150-250).

**Cross-phase deferral-lift expectation** documented in this ADR's §Consequences body at 22.2 IMPL: prior-phase BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "operator-visibility deferred to future" notes (phases 16-20) carry forward AS-IS until their respective lift-phase converts the note from "deferred" to "lifted via `internal/dynamicmetadata`". 22.2 lands the primitive + the FIRST consumer (HTTP Lua filter). The cross-phase reference paragraph at BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md's `### envoy.filters.http.lua` 22.2 sub-section + cross-phase note records the discipline.

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — landed at phase-22.2 IMPL Task 1 (NEW package skeleton + types + tests) + Task 5 (chain.go + callbacks.go wiring) + Task 6 (HCM H1/H2 seeding) + Task 9 (lua bridge consumer); §Decision body anchored at this 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing.** The §Decision codifies the final settled API signatures + lifecycle integration + nil-tolerance discipline as landed at the 22.2 IMPL tasks above. Per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.1 + §11.6 D1 closure + ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.

**(i) Public surface — `Bucket` type + 4 methods.** Five exported identifiers at `internal/dynamicmetadata/dynamicmetadata.go`. Confirms the surface anticipated in the §Context block byte-for-byte:

```go
package dynamicmetadata

import structpb "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/structpb"

// Bucket is a per-stream cross-filter dynamic-metadata accessor.
// Lifecycle: created at filter-chain entry; destroyed at OnDestroy.
// Per-stream sequential per ADR-0033 (no cross-filter concurrency within
// a stream); NOT goroutine-safe across streams.
type Bucket struct {
    m map[string]map[string]*structpb.Value
}

func NewBucket() *Bucket
func (b *Bucket) Get(filterName, key string) (*structpb.Value, bool)
func (b *Bucket) Set(filterName, key string, value *structpb.Value)
func (b *Bucket) Snapshot() map[string]map[string]*structpb.Value
func (b *Bucket) Reset()
```

`NewBucket` constructs an empty per-stream metadata bucket (lazily allocates the inner map on the first `Set` call — zero-allocation under read-only-access workloads). `Get` returns `(value, ok=true)` on lookup-hit + `(nil, false)` on lookup-miss + `(nil, false)` for a nil receiver (per ADR-0085 nil-tolerance). `Set` overwrites at the `(filterName, key)` coordinate + no-ops for a nil receiver. `Snapshot` returns a SHALLOW COPY of the bucket's contents for read-only iteration — the outer + inner map references are fresh; the `*structpb.Value` pointers are shared (callers must NOT mutate the value structs). `Reset` clears all entries (called at `OnDestroy`).

**(ii) Per-stream lifecycle integration per ADR-0033.** `internal/filter/http/chain.go::FilterChain` carries a new `dynamicMetadata *dynamicmetadata.Bucket` field. The field is lazily initialized via `c.DynamicMetadata()` accessor (the first read constructs via `dynamicmetadata.NewBucket()`; subsequent reads return the same per-chain bucket). Per-stream lifecycle: the chain is created at filter-chain entry (per ADR-0033 + ADR-0100); destroyed at `OnDestroy` where `chain.dynamicMetadata.Reset()` is called. Cross-filter visibility per-stream: all filters within the same chain see the same bucket — `DecoderFilterCallbacks.DynamicMetadata()` + `EncoderFilterCallbacks.DynamicMetadata()` BOTH return the same per-stream `*Bucket` pointer (the encoder-side accessor exists for symmetry with the decoder-side; both surface the same backing storage).

**(iii) Nil-tolerance discipline per ADR-0085.** All 4 `Bucket` methods accept a nil receiver. `Get` returns `(nil, false)`; `Set` is a no-op; `Snapshot` returns nil; `Reset` is a no-op. Rationale: callers (lua bridge at 22.2; future consumers) may invoke the accessor unconditionally without per-call nil checks; the nil-receiver path is the safe degenerate case for test scaffolding + fuzzer inputs that don't allocate the chain-level field. The `Get` nil-receiver path is the most-exercised at 22.2 (the lua bridge's `:dynamicMetadata():get(filter_name, key)` accessor invokes `Bucket.Get` regardless of whether any filter has written; absence of any writes returns `(nil, false)` cleanly via either the nil-receiver path or the empty-map path).

**(iv) Per-stream sequential access discipline per ADR-0033.** The `Bucket` is NOT goroutine-safe for concurrent access across streams (each stream has its own `*Bucket`); the `Bucket` is NOT goroutine-safe for concurrent access WITHIN a stream (per-stream sequential filter dispatch per ADR-0033 means at any moment at most one filter touches the bucket). No internal mutex; no atomic operations; the map+nested-map storage is pure-Go-runtime with no synchronization. This is the deliberate design choice per ADR-0033 § sequential filter dispatch discipline — adding internal synchronization would (a) waste cycles on the steady state (single-goroutine per stream), (b) mask design errors (any cross-stream sharing of a `*Bucket` is a bug — the per-stream lifecycle is the contract), and (c) misalign with the project's broader ADR-0033 single-goroutine-per-stream invariant.

**(v) Cross-phase deferral-break disposition per phase-22 BRAINSTORM Q3 + §1.6.** Phases 16 (rbac) / 17 (jwt_authn) / 18 (ext_authz) / 19 (ext_proc) / 20 (oauth2) each deferred dynamic-metadata access by their respective filters with BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "operator-visibility deferred to future" notes — the deferral was about IMPL (each phase chose not to be the first to land a cross-filter state primitive) NOT about principle (operators DO want dynamic-metadata visibility from these filters). Phase 22.2 lands the cross-filter primitive at first co-consumer (the HTTP Lua filter's `:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata()` + `:dynamicTypedMetadata(filter_name)` bridge methods per ADR-0192 §Decision). Future phase BRAINSTORMs that need dynamic-metadata access from their respective filters consume `internal/dynamicmetadata/` rather than defer again — each prior-phase BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT note converts from "deferred" to "lifted via `internal/dynamicmetadata`" at the lift-phase's next-touchpoint (the future phase that next edits the prior-phase filter's deferral note).

**(vi) Settled file split** (per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.1 + Task 1 landing):

```
internal/dynamicmetadata/
  doc.go               # package overview + cross-phase deferral-lift rationale +
                       # API surface summary + ADR-0190 cross-reference
  dynamicmetadata.go   # Bucket type + NewBucket + Get + Set + Snapshot + Reset
  dynamicmetadata_test.go  # exhaustive table-driven tests including nil-tolerance
  bench_test.go        # microbenchmarks for Get/Set under per-stream sequential
                       # access
```

LoC landed: ~280 production (doc.go ~70; dynamicmetadata.go ~95; dynamicmetadata_test.go ~95 + bench_test.go ~20). Within the §Context anticipated envelope of ~250-400.

**(vii) Cross-filter callbacks API surface (per ADR-0192 §Decision body + phase-22.2 SPEC §3.1 + Task 5 IMPL).** `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go::DecoderFilterCallbacks` + `EncoderFilterCallbacks` gain TWO new accessors:

```go
DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket  // both decoder-side + encoder-side
```

Both accessors return the SAME per-stream `*Bucket` pointer threaded from the chain. The asymmetry between decode-side and encode-side does NOT exist at the bucket level — both sides see the same backing storage; the encoder-side accessor exists for symmetry with the decode-side + to honor the per-side cross-cutting filter-callbacks API surface convention from prior §9 family rows (ADR-0144 TLS-principals; ADR-0168 ext_proc dynamic-metadata-bridge anticipation).

### Consequences

**THIRD §9 framework primitive in two-phase succession** (after ADR-0188 `internal/lua/` + ADR-0189 `internal/filter/http/lua/` at phase-22.1 IMPL). STRENGTHENS the post-phase-21 NEW-framework-primitive cadence + reflects the project's growing cross-filter-state surface. The phase-22 BRAINSTORM-time 3-way pre-split (22.1 + 22.2 + 22.3) deliberately schedules the framework-primitive landings across the sub-phases — 22.1 = `internal/lua/` + `internal/filter/http/lua/`; 22.2 = `internal/dynamicmetadata/` + `internal/lua/` API extensions; 22.3 = (anticipated) per-route 9th canonical extension. The cadence is sustainable + each landing is tightly bound to a specific consumer-driven trigger.

**Consumers at this commit (single co-consumer at 22.2 IMPL):**

- **HTTP Lua filter 22.2** (`internal/filter/http/lua/`) — consumes `*Bucket.Get` + `*Bucket.Set` via the `:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():get(filter_name, key)` + `:set(filter_name, key, value)` + `:streamInfo():dynamicTypedMetadata(filter_name)` bridge methods. The lua bridge's metadata.go IMPL (Task 9) consumes the bucket via the per-stream `*filter.chain.dynamicMetadata` field threaded through the filter callbacks.

**Cross-phase deferral-lift expectation (FUTURE consumers).** Phases 16/17/18/19/20 deferred dynamic-metadata access by their respective filters. Future phase BRAINSTORMs that need dynamic-metadata access reuse `internal/dynamicmetadata/`. Each prior-phase BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md "operator-visibility deferred to future" note converts from "deferred" to "lifted via `internal/dynamicmetadata`" at the lift-phase's next-touchpoint. NO automatic mass-update at this 22.2 IMPL — the deferral notes carry forward AS-IS until each prior-phase filter is next touched. The deferral-lift discipline is documented at the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `### envoy.filters.http.lua` 22.2 sub-section's cross-phase reference paragraph + the per-prior-phase ADR cross-references above.

**(+) Cross-filter state visibility without per-filter ad-hoc primitive extraction.** Each future filter that needs dynamic-metadata access reuses the SAME primitive — no per-filter ad-hoc cross-filter-state primitive (which would duplicate code + fragment the cross-filter state surface). Per the phase-17 ADR-0150 + phase-18.1 ADR-0159 + phase-20 ADR-0177 + phase-20 ADR-0178 cross-phase-reuse-at-introduction-time discipline.

**(+) Per-stream lifecycle aligns with ADR-0033 sequential filter dispatch.** No cross-stream caching; no global state; no boot-time singleton — each per-stream bucket is fresh + GC-collected at stream-end via `Reset` + chain-end via Go's runtime GC. The lifecycle integration is bug-free by construction (the only path that allocates is `Set`; the only path that deallocates is `Reset`; no `Close` failure mode + no leak surface).

**(+) Nil-tolerance per ADR-0085 + simple test scaffolding.** Callers can pass nil chain (test code; fuzzer inputs); accessors degrade to the safe degenerate case. The lua bridge's `metadata.go` IMPL exercises this for its unit tests via the `nilCallbacks` fixture path.

**(-) Per-stream sequential access constraint is implicit, not enforced.** A future bug that shares a `*Bucket` across streams (e.g., cross-stream caching mistake) would silently race the map+nested-map storage without crashing under happy-path concurrency (Go map writes are not atomic but the race-detector would flag under `-race`). The constraint relies on the ADR-0033 single-goroutine-per-stream invariant — if a future ADR relaxes that invariant, this ADR's design needs revisiting. Documented at the package's `doc.go` + `dynamicmetadata.go::Bucket` doc-comment for future maintainers.

**(-) `Snapshot` shallow-copy can be misused.** Callers MUST NOT mutate the returned `*structpb.Value` pointers (mutation would corrupt the bucket's view of the value). The constraint is documented at the `Snapshot` method doc-comment; the test suite does NOT exercise the misuse path (the bucket's storage is private; misuse would require explicit type assertion + unsafe mutation). Acceptable trade-off vs deep-copy cost (`structpb.Value` is a proto type with potentially deep recursive structure — deep-copying on every `Snapshot` call would defeat the read-only-iteration use case).

**(?) Future framework-primitive extraction for cross-stream caching.** The current scope is per-stream only. A hypothetical future use case (e.g., a cross-stream metadata-aggregation surface — "what's the rate of `envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn::issuer == X` across the last 1000 streams?") would need a different primitive (likely `internal/dynamicmetadatacache/` with TTL + eviction + atomic snapshots). Not in scope at 22.2.

**Per-stream test coverage at this Task 1 landing** (`dynamicmetadata_test.go`):
- `TestBucket_NewBucket_Empty` — verifies fresh bucket returns `(nil, false)` for all `Get` calls.
- `TestBucket_SetGet_RoundTrip` — verifies value round-trips through `Set(...)` + `Get(...)`.
- `TestBucket_Set_Overwrite` — verifies repeat `Set` at the same coordinate overwrites the prior value.
- `TestBucket_GetMissing` — verifies `Get` at absent `(filterName, key)` returns `(nil, false)`.
- `TestBucket_Snapshot_NonEmpty` — verifies `Snapshot` returns a copy of the contents.
- `TestBucket_Snapshot_NilReceiver` — nil-tolerance: nil receiver returns nil snapshot.
- `TestBucket_Reset_Clears` — verifies `Reset` empties the bucket; subsequent `Get` returns `(nil, false)`.
- `TestBucket_NilReceiver_GetSetReset_NoOp` — nil-tolerance: nil receiver handles all 4 methods without panic.
- `BenchmarkBucket_Get_Hit` + `BenchmarkBucket_Set_NewKey` — microbenchmark coverage; per-call cost ~30-50 ns/op (map lookup + value-pointer assignment).

The 22.2 IMPL benchmark surface (Task 15 `BenchmarkPerStream_FullBridge_LState_Construction`) confirms the Bucket's amortized per-stream overhead is invisible at the FULL bridge surface (ns/op = 98157 ~98µs; the bucket allocation contributes ~50ns of that envelope).

**Cross-references:** ADR-0188 (paired prior §9 framework primitive — `internal/lua/`); ADR-0189 (paired prior §9 package — `internal/filter/http/lua/`); ADR-0191 (sibling NEW ADR at predecessor 22.2 SPEC commit — `internal/lua/` 22.2 API extensions); ADR-0192 (sibling NEW ADR at predecessor 22.2 SPEC commit — `internal/filter/http/lua/` 22.2 package shape extensions; consumer-#1 of `internal/dynamicmetadata/` at this 22.2 IMPL); ADR-0085 (nil-tolerance discipline); ADR-0033 (per-stream sequential filter dispatch); ADR-0044 (ADR §Decision + §Consequences in-place body landing discipline); ADR-0052 (atomic landing); phase-16 ADR-0143 (rbac dynamic-metadata deferral); phase-17 ADR-0148/0149/0150/0154 (jwt_authn dynamic-metadata deferral); phase-18 (ext_authz dynamic-metadata deferral); phase-19 (ext_proc dynamic-metadata deferral); phase-20 (oauth2 dynamic-metadata deferral); phase-22 parent SPEC §1.6 cross-phase deferral discipline; phase-22.2 BRAINSTORM Q3 + Q9 + §1.6; phase-22.2 SPEC §1.6 + §3.1 + §9 + §11 + §16.1; phase-22.2 PLAN Task 1 + Task 5 + Task 6 + Task 9.

## ADR-0191: `internal/lua/` 22.2 API extensions for coroutine yield/resume + body-bridge buffer seam at HTTP filter Lua consumer-#1 scope-expansion — NEW ADR per BRAINSTORM Q10 strict scope (ADR-0188 EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE stays scoped to consumer-#2)

**Status:** Accepted — §Decision + §Consequences body landed at phase-22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing (THIS commit); §Context body unchanged from the 22.2 SPEC anchor commit.
**Date:** 2026-05-19 (§Context anchor at predecessor 22.2 SPEC commit `0d6463e`; §Decision + §Consequences body land at this 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline)
**Doctrine:** Phase 22.2 §9 family-row. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. NEW ADR (NOT in-place AMEND on ADR-0188 per Q10 strict scope).
**Lands-in:** Phase 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic-landing (same Task as ADR-0190 + ADR-0192 + ADR-0177 AMENDMENT body per PLAN).

### Context

ADR-0191 anchors the NEW `internal/lua/` API extensions at 22.2 — coroutine yield/resume support + body-bridge buffer seam interface. Per BRAINSTORM Q10 strict scope: NEW ADR (NOT in-place AMEND on ADR-0188). ADR-0188's EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause STAYS scoped to consumer-#2 (future cluster-specifier / access-logger / string-matcher Lua phases per ADR-0188 §Decision §5). 22.2 is consumer-#1-scope-expanded (still HTTP filter Lua); the scope-expansion API revisions land under NEW ADR-0191 instead of in-place AMEND on ADR-0188.

**Lineage-separation rationale (per BRAINSTORM Q10).** Apply-allowance-to-scope-expansion + in-place-AMEND was REJECTED on lineage-separation grounds: over-loading ADR-0188 with consumer-#1-expansion AMENDMENTs would dilute the consumer-#2 ALLOWANCE's empirical-validation rationale (ADR-0188's allowance is a FUTURE-USE allowance triggered by a different consumer's empirical validation; mixing it with same-consumer scope-expansion confuses the lineage). NO-API-revisions was REJECTED on duplication grounds: building coroutine + body-bridge surfaces outside `internal/lua/` would duplicate primitive-like code at the lua filter; the second `internal/lua/` consumer at the future consumer-#2 phase would then face TWO API surfaces to validate.

The strict-scope decision is the load-bearing ADR-lineage decision: each ADR's scope tightly bound to a single semantic event (ADR-0188 = primitive landing at consumer-#1; ADR-0191 = primitive extensions at consumer-#1-scope-expansion; future ADR for consumer-#2 = primitive extensions per the ADR-0188 ALLOWANCE).

**Coroutine API per §11.1 D2 closure** — gopher-lua native via `(*LState).NewThread() (*LState, context.CancelFunc)` (`state.go:1614`) + `(*LState).Resume(th, fn, args...) (ResumeState, error, []LValue)` (`state.go:2157`) + `(*LState).Yield(values...) int` (`state.go:2217` — returns sentinel `-1`). The yield mechanism: a Go-side LGFunction yields by returning a negative value — exactly what `LState.Yield()` returns. The bridge implements `:body()` (and similar async-suspended methods) by stashing the `*LState` in a per-stream pending-map; returning `L.Yield(lua.LNil)` from the LGFunction. The matching resume happens from the Envoy data callback via `parent.Resume(th, nil, lua.LString(bodyBytes))`. Per-stream lifecycle: 1 parent `*LState` per stream (compiled-bytecode owner; lives for filter lifetime) + 1 child `*LState` per phase invocation (the coroutine; cheap to construct — shares `G`+`Env`). Both released on stream destroy; child's `context.CancelFunc` from `NewThread()` MUST be invoked to cancel the child's ctx-derived loop.

**Body-buffer seam interface** — `BodyBuffer interface { Bytes() []byte; Chunks() [][]byte; EndStream() bool }`. Consumed by the lua bridge's `:body()` + `:bodyChunks()` LGFunction methods. Implemented by the per-stream body-bridge wrapper at `internal/filter/http/lua/body.go` (consuming ADR-0128's HCM-level decode-side `bodyBuf` accumulation; defensive copy at endStream per §11.3 D3 recommendation; matching ext_authz `f.body` + ext_proc `f.decodeBodyBuf` per-filter accumulation patterns).

**Anticipated API surface** (per 22.2 SPEC §3.2):

```go
package lua  // EXTENDS the 22.1 internal/lua/ package

// In vm.go (appended):
func (vm *VM) NewThread() (*lua.LState, context.CancelFunc)
func (vm *VM) Resume(child *lua.LState, fn *lua.LFunction, args ...lua.LValue) (lua.ResumeState, error, []lua.LValue)
func YieldFromBridge(L *lua.LState, args ...lua.LValue) int

// In body_buffer.go (NEW):
type BodyBuffer interface {
    Bytes() []byte
    Chunks() [][]byte
    EndStream() bool
}
```

`YieldFromBridge` codifies the gopher-lua VM unwinding discipline per §11.1 D2 closure — bridge LGFunctions that need to suspend the script call `YieldFromBridge(L, lua.LNil)` and return its result; the gopher-lua VM's `callGFunction` (`vm.go:200-210`) sees the `-1` sentinel and calls `switchToParentThread`. The bridge then stashes the suspended `*LState` in a per-stream pending-map.

**File split** (~150-300 LoC additions to existing `internal/lua/`):
- `vm.go` — APPEND: `NewThread` + `Resume` methods on `*VM` + the panic-wrapper integration for child LState.
- `body_buffer.go` — NEW: `BodyBuffer` interface + helper functions if needed.
- `bridge_helpers.go` (or appended to `vm.go`) — NEW: `YieldFromBridge` helper.
- Tests: `coroutine_test.go` (NEW: NewThread + Resume + YieldFromBridge integration tests; race-clean under -race -count=10) + `body_buffer_test.go` (NEW: BodyBuffer interface conformance tests).

**Anticipated LoC: ~300-500** (vm.go append + body_buffer.go + bridge_helpers.go + 2-3 NEW test files).

### Decision

**Status: Accepted — landed at phase-22.2 IMPL Task 2 (NEW `internal/lua/coroutine.go` + tests) + Task 3 (NEW `internal/lua/body_buffer.go` + tests) + Task 7 (lua bridge body consumer) + Task 11 (lua bridge sync httpCall yield consumer) + Task 19a (production HCM coroutine orchestration); §Decision body anchored at this 22.2 IMPL Task 19 atomic landing.** The §Decision codifies the final settled API signatures + body-buffer seam interface + integration with ADR-0188 primitive + lineage-separation rationale + future-consumer-#2 ALLOWANCE clause discipline as landed at the 22.2 IMPL tasks above. Per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.2 + §11.1 D2 closure + §11.3 D3 RECOMMENDED + ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.

**(i) D-P5 LOCK: NEW FILES (NOT in-place APPEND to vm.go).** Per phase-22.2 PLAN D-P5 closure: the coroutine + body-buffer API extensions land as NEW `internal/lua/coroutine.go` + `internal/lua/body_buffer.go` files — NOT as in-place APPEND to the 22.1 `vm.go`. Rationale: preserves the ADR-0188 vs ADR-0191 lineage separation per Q10 strict scope (the consumer-#1 22.1 surface lives in `vm.go`; the consumer-#1-scope-expansion 22.2 surface lives in `coroutine.go` + `body_buffer.go`; the future consumer-#2 surface — per ADR-0188's EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause — will land in further-segregated files when that future phase fires). Test files paired: `coroutine_test.go` + `body_buffer_test.go`.

**(ii) Coroutine API surface — 3 exported identifiers at `internal/lua/coroutine.go`.** Confirms the surface anticipated in the §Context block byte-for-byte per the §11.1 D2 closure:

```go
package lua

// NewThread constructs a child *lua.LState as a coroutine state, sharing
// globals with the parent. Per §11.1 D2 closure: gopher-lua native
// LState.NewThread() is the underlying mechanism. The returned *LState is
// the coroutine state; callers Resume it via the parent's Resume method.
// The returned CancelFunc from gopher-lua's NewThread MUST be invoked at
// coroutine cleanup (typically at filter OnDestroy).
func (vm *VM) NewThread() (*lua.LState, context.CancelFunc)

// Resume invokes parent.Resume(child, fn, args...) per gopher-lua semantics.
// Per §11.1 D2 closure: the parent *LState drives the child; on ResumeYield
// returns with the yield args, on ResumeError returns the API error, on
// ResumeOK returns the script's return values.
func (vm *VM) Resume(child *lua.LState, fn *lua.LFunction, args ...lua.LValue) (lua.ResumeState, error, []lua.LValue)

// YieldFromBridge is a Go-side helper for bridge LGFunction implementations.
// Pushes args onto the bridge LState and returns the gopher-lua yield
// sentinel (-1). The caller (an LGFunction) MUST return the result
// directly to gopher-lua per vm.go:200-210 switchToParentThread discipline
// (callGFunction sees gfnret<0 and unwinds to the parent thread).
func YieldFromBridge(L *lua.LState, args ...lua.LValue) int
```

`NewThread` delegates to `gopher-lua.(*LState).NewThread()` (`state.go:1614`) which mints a child `*lua.LState` sharing the parent's `G` (global state) + `Env` (registry) but with its own per-stack execution context + its own `context.CancelFunc` derived from the parent's context (the cancel func MUST be invoked at coroutine cleanup to release the per-child resources — the cancellation discipline lives in the consumer at Task 19a's `decode_headers.go` + `encode_headers.go` `decodeChildCancel` / `encodeChildCancel` fields on `*filter`).

`Resume` delegates to `parent.Resume(child, fn, args...)` (`state.go:2157`). The return type triple `(lua.ResumeState, error, []lua.LValue)` carries the yield/return values on `ResumeYield` (so the bridge can inspect what the script wants — body? httpCall? — by inspecting the per-filter pending fields) + the API error on `ResumeError` + the script's return values on `ResumeOK`. The caller (HCM dispatch wrapper at `decode_headers.go` + `encode_headers.go`) drives the dispatch loop: on `ResumeYield` re-invokes `vm.Resume(child, nil, /*args from the satisfying source*/...)` when the awaited resource (body bytes + httpCall response) is available.

`YieldFromBridge` codifies the gopher-lua VM unwinding discipline per §11.1 D2 closure. A Go-side LGFunction that needs to suspend the script calls `YieldFromBridge(L, lua.LNil)` (or `YieldFromBridge(L, ...args)` with the values to surface to the resume caller) and returns its result (the `-1` sentinel) directly to gopher-lua. The gopher-lua VM's `callGFunction` (`vm.go:200-210`) sees the negative return value + calls `switchToParentThread`, unwinding the call stack to the parent `*LState`. The bridge then stashes the suspended `*LState` in a per-stream pending-map (e.g., `f.pendingBodyResume` for body yields; `f.pendingHTTPCallResume` for sync httpCall yields). The matching `vm.Resume(child, nil, ...satisfyingArgs)` is invoked from the Envoy decode-data callback when the awaited resource becomes available — for body, from `accumulateRequestBody` / `accumulateResponseBody` at endStream; for sync httpCall, from the dispatch goroutine after `ClusterDispatch` returns.

**(iii) BodyBuffer seam interface at `internal/lua/body_buffer.go`.** ONE exported identifier confirms the §Context anticipation byte-for-byte:

```go
package lua

// BodyBuffer is the seam interface consumed by the lua bridge's :body() +
// :bodyChunks() methods. Implemented by the per-stream body-bridge wrapper
// at internal/filter/http/lua/body.go that consumes ADR-0128's decode-side
// buffer (HCM-level bodyBuf accumulation; defensive copy at endStream per
// §11.3 D3 recommendation).
type BodyBuffer interface {
    // Bytes returns the full accumulated body as one byte slice. Returns
    // nil if body not yet available; the slice MUST NOT be mutated by
    // consumers (treat as read-only).
    Bytes() []byte

    // Chunks returns the body as a sequence of per-DecodeData chunks.
    // Returns nil if body not yet available. Each inner slice is
    // read-only.
    Chunks() [][]byte

    // EndStream reports whether the terminal endStream=true signal has
    // fired. Returns false until the body is fully accumulated.
    EndStream() bool
}
```

The `BodyBuffer` interface is the integration point between `internal/lua/` API + ADR-0128's HCM-level decode-side buffer accumulation. The lua bridge (at `internal/filter/http/lua/body.go`) constructs concrete `*decodedBodyBuffer` + `*encodedBodyBuffer` structs implementing `BodyBuffer` that wrap per-filter accumulated chunks (paralleling ext_authz's `f.body` + ext_proc's `f.decodeBodyBuf` patterns per §11.3 evidence). At endStream, the bridge's `:body()` method makes a defensive copy of the accumulated bytes into a Go string via `lua.LString(string(f.decodedBodyBytes))` — Lua owns the resulting Go string (immutable; safe across coroutine yield/resume per §11.3 D3 RECOMMENDED disposition).

**(iv) Per-stream child-LState lifecycle integration per §11.1 D2 closure.** The per-stream lifecycle: ONE parent `*LState` per stream (compiled-bytecode owner; constructed at filter `OnStream` per ADR-0188 §Decision §3) + ONE child `*LState` per phase invocation (decode side + encode side each get a fresh child at their respective hook entry — `envoy_on_request` runs in `decodeChild`; `envoy_on_response` runs in `encodeChild`). Both released on filter `OnDestroy`. The child's `context.CancelFunc` from `NewThread()` MUST be invoked to cancel the child's ctx-derived loop (production wiring at `*filter.OnDestroy()` in `lua.go` invokes both `decodeChildCancel` + `encodeChildCancel` per Task 19a's lifecycle gate).

**(v) Resume semantics + error propagation per §11.1 D2 closure.** `Resume` returns `(ResumeState, error, []lua.LValue)`. The three states + semantics:

- `lua.ResumeOK` → script completed normally; `[]LValue` carries the script's return values; `error` is nil.
- `lua.ResumeYield` → script called `YieldFromBridge` or `coroutine.yield`; `[]LValue` carries the yield args; `error` is nil; the caller (HCM dispatch wrapper) inspects per-filter pending fields to decide which kind of yield this is (`pendingBodyResume != nil` → body yield; `pendingHTTPCallResume != nil` → sync httpCall yield).
- `lua.ResumeError` → script panicked / Lua runtime error / `pcall`-uncaught error; `error` carries the `*lua.ApiError`; `[]LValue` is empty. Per `threadRun` (`vm.go:272-293`), gopher-lua installs `defer recover()` so the panic surfaces as `ResumeError` rather than crashing the host goroutine — the bridge MUST always pair every `Resume` call with parent-side error handling.

**(vi) D2 closure rationale — Option A (gopher-lua native) over Option B (Go-side channel wrapper).** Per §11.1 D2 evidence: Option B was REJECTED on goroutine-blocking grounds. gopher-lua's VM is single-threaded over each `*LState`; blocking a Go bridge LGFunction on a channel would block the OS goroutine driving `threadRun` (the OS goroutine is one of the worker pool's goroutines — blocking it would consume the worker for the duration of the script's wait). Wasted complexity when `Yield(-1)`/`Resume` is built-in: the gopher-lua VM unwinds the call stack via the `-1` sentinel without consuming a worker goroutine for the duration of the wait. Option A's mechanical simplicity (the unwinding discipline is documented in gopher-lua source at `vm.go:200-210`) carries forward to envoy-go's bridge without behavioral surprises.

**(vii) Task 2 panic-wrapper integration at the coroutine seam (per Task 2 IMPL).** The 22.1 ADR-0188 §Decision 2 introduced a panic-wrapper discipline at the LState dispatch seam — `vm.CallGlobal` wraps `parent.PCall` in a defer-recover that converts `*lua.ApiError` panics to the `errors` stat counter increment. Task 2 extended this discipline to the coroutine seam: `vm.Resume` (the parent's Resume call) similarly wraps in a defer-recover so that a script panic in a child thread is converted to `ResumeError` (with the `*lua.ApiError` carried in the error return) rather than propagating to the host goroutine. The wrapper helper `coroutineDispatchPanic` lives in `internal/lua/coroutine.go` + is invoked by `vm.Resume` directly before delegating to `parent.Resume`. The Task 2 helper extension to ADR-0188 §Decision 2 panic-wrapper discipline is BROADER ApiError scope than the 22.1 `ApiErrorPanic`-only scope (the coroutine seam handles `ApiErrorRun` + `ApiErrorPanic` + `ApiErrorOther` uniformly — any *lua.ApiError shape that surfaces during Resume is captured).

**(viii) Q10 strict scope — NEW ADR (NOT in-place AMEND on ADR-0188).** Per BRAINSTORM Q10 strict-scope decision: 22.2's consumer-#1-scope-expansion lands under THIS NEW ADR rather than in-place AMEND on ADR-0188. ADR-0188's EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause STAYS scoped to consumer-#2 (future cluster-specifier / access-logger / string-matcher Lua phases). The lineage-separation rationale per BRAINSTORM Q10:

- **Apply-allowance-to-scope-expansion + in-place-AMEND was REJECTED** on lineage-separation grounds: over-loading ADR-0188 with consumer-#1-expansion AMENDMENTs would dilute the consumer-#2 ALLOWANCE's empirical-validation rationale (ADR-0188's allowance is a FUTURE-USE allowance triggered by a different consumer's empirical validation; mixing it with same-consumer scope-expansion confuses the lineage).
- **NO-API-revisions was REJECTED** on duplication grounds: building coroutine + body-bridge surfaces outside `internal/lua/` would duplicate primitive-like code at the lua filter; the second `internal/lua/` consumer at the future consumer-#2 phase would then face TWO API surfaces to validate.

Each ADR's scope is now tightly bound to a single semantic event: ADR-0188 = primitive landing at consumer-#1; ADR-0191 = primitive extensions at consumer-#1-scope-expansion; future ADR for consumer-#2 = primitive extensions per the ADR-0188 ALLOWANCE.

**(ix) Production HCM coroutine orchestration landed at Task 19a (PRE-ATOMIC-LANDING).** `internal/filter/http/lua/decode_headers.go` + `encode_headers.go` invoke `envoy_on_request` + `envoy_on_response` via `vm.NewThread()` + `vm.Resume(child, fn, reqUd / respUd)` per the API surface above. The orchestration:

1. At `DecodeHeaders` entry: `child, cancel := vm.NewThread()`; stash `cancel` in `*filter.decodeChildCancel`; `vm.Resume(child, envoyOnRequest, reqUd)`.
2. On `lua.ResumeYield`: inspect `*filter.pendingHTTPCallResume` vs `*filter.pendingBodyResume`. If `pendingHTTPCallResume != nil` → close `httpCallReady` channel + wait on `httpCallDone` channel so the dispatch goroutine drives the resume to script completion synchronously inside DecodeHeaders. If `pendingBodyResume != nil` → return `Continue` so the chain's `RunDecodeData` fires; `accumulateRequestBody` at endStream invokes `vm.Resume(child, nil, lua.LString(string(f.decodedBodyBytes)))` to resume the suspended coroutine.
3. On `lua.ResumeOK`: `*filter.respondCaptured` is the source of truth for whether to short-circuit; if non-nil return the captured local-reply via the standard HCM short-circuit path; if nil return `Continue`.
4. On `lua.ResumeError`: increment `errors` stat counter; log the error via the panic-recovery wrapper; return `Continue` (degraded pass-through).

The "Continue on body-yield" trade-off is the deliberate production decision documented at the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `#### Phase 22.2 full bridge surface delta` subsection. Multi-decoder-filter topologies that depend on body-after-yield header-mutation visibility ARE a known limitation flagged for REVIEW.md + future framework work (deferred to 22.3 or a separate framework phase per §1.2 + parent §10).

### Consequences

**(+) ADR-0188's API-REVISION ALLOWANCE STAYS scoped to consumer-#2.** The strict-scope decision per Q10 preserves the ALLOWANCE's empirical-validation rationale + the per-ADR single-semantic-event discipline. Future consumer-#2 BRAINSTORM (cluster-specifier / access-logger / string-matcher Lua) consumes the ALLOWANCE cleanly without lineage entanglement against this consumer-#1-scope-expansion. The Q10 strict-scope decision is the load-bearing ADR-lineage decision for the 22.2 phase.

**(+) Coroutine yield/resume orchestration enables non-blocking body bridge + sync httpCall bridge.** Bridge methods that need to suspend the script (await body bytes + await sync httpCall response) yield via `YieldFromBridge` without consuming a worker goroutine for the duration of the wait. The HCM dispatch wrapper drives the resume from the appropriate satisfying source (decode-data callback at endStream for body; dispatch goroutine post-`ClusterDispatch` for sync httpCall). The per-stream child-LState lifecycle integration aligns with ADR-0033 sequential filter dispatch.

**(+) Future framework phases that extend `internal/lua/` per consumer-#2 scope can edit `vm.go` without touching `coroutine.go` / `body_buffer.go`.** Per D-P5 LOCK NEW FILES discipline: the consumer-#1-scope-expansion files are independently maintainable from the consumer-#1 base files. Future consumer-#2 phase that extends `vm.go` for cluster-specifier / access-logger / string-matcher Lua needs (e.g., a NEW `RegisterStringMatcher` API) does NOT touch this 22.2 commit's `coroutine.go` / `body_buffer.go` files — preserves the file-level lineage separation.

**(+) D2 closure: gopher-lua native vs Go-side channel wrapper.** The Option-A choice is mechanically simple + leverages built-in gopher-lua machinery. The bridge implementation surface at this consumer-#1-scope-expansion is straightforward (Task 2 + Task 7 + Task 11 IMPLs total ~120 LoC across `coroutine.go` + `body_buffer.go` + bridge consumer; the production HCM orchestration at Task 19a is ~100 LoC across `decode_headers.go` + `encode_headers.go`).

**(+) Defensive-copy at endStream per §11.3 D3 RECOMMENDED is GC-safe.** The `BodyBuffer` interface contract specifies that `Bytes()` returns a read-only slice; the bridge consumer copies once at endStream (`lua.LString(string(f.decodedBodyBytes))`) — Lua owns the immutable Go string from that point forward. Coroutine yield/resume + HCM dispatch goroutine lifetimes are all safe under this discipline. Task 15 `BenchmarkBodyBridge_DefensiveCopy_PerStream` confirms the perf threshold gates: sub-MB body at ~103µs (gate ≤ 1ms; 9.7× under) + 16-MiB-saturated at ~9.3ms (gate ≤ 100ms; 10.7× under).

**(-) The "Continue on body-yield" trade-off is a known limitation for multi-decoder-filter topologies.** Returning Continue (vs StopIteration) on body yield is required because envoy-go's HCM serializes Headers→Data — returning StopIteration would deadlock the chain. The trade-off: subsequent decode-side filters see request headers BEFORE Lua's post-:body() mutations. For 22.2's single-lua-decoder topology (fixture-0027) this is benign because router runs AFTER the chain's RunDecodeData. Multi-lua-chain or lua→<header-reading-filter> topologies that depend on body-after-yield header-mutation visibility silently lose those mutations. Deferred to phase-22.3 or a separate framework phase that introduces a "park-headers-iteration-pending-body" cooperative discipline.

**(-) Per-stream child-LState construction adds modest overhead vs the 22.1 baseline.** Task 15 `BenchmarkPerStream_FullBridge_LState_Construction` reports `ns/op = 98157` (~98µs) at the FULL 22.2 bridge surface — 1.4× the 22.1 headers-only baseline of `ns/op = 69865` (~70µs). The child-LState mint via `NewThread` contributes a small fraction of that delta; the bulk is from the 7 NEW metatable installs at the FULL bridge surface. The cost is well under the 1ms threshold (10.2× under) — conditional ADR-0193 *LState-pool escape-valve NOT consumed; carries forward to 22.3 BRAINSTORM unconsumed.

**(-) `coroutineDispatchPanic` helper wraps `vm.Resume` with broader scope than ADR-0188's `ApiErrorPanic`-only wrapper.** The broader scope (handles `ApiErrorRun` + `ApiErrorPanic` + `ApiErrorOther`) is necessary because the coroutine seam's error surface is broader (Lua-runtime errors during a yielded-then-resumed script can surface as `ApiErrorRun`); the broader scope adds ~5 LoC of defer-recover plumbing at the `vm.Resume` callsite. Documented at the Task 2 PROGRESS entry.

**(?) Future consumer-#2 phase may revisit the API surface per ADR-0188 EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE.** That future phase's BRAINSTORM may surface API revisions (e.g., a different `Resume` signature that returns yield-args via a callback rather than the return triple; a NEW `WithCoroutineQuota` option to bound per-thread CPU consumption). Per the ALLOWANCE clause, that future phase's revisions land under a NEW ADR (or in-place AMEND on ADR-0188 — settled per the Q10-equivalent dialogue at that future BRAINSTORM); the consumer-#1 22.2 surface STAYS at this ADR-0191's settled signatures.

**(?) Body-buffer GC safety in pathological adversarial scenarios.** The defensive-copy at endStream is GC-safe because Go strings are immutable + length-prefixed; the underlying byte slice may be freed by the runtime GC after the copy. Pathological scenarios — operator scripts that retain references to the `:body()` result across very long-lived coroutines (e.g., a coroutine that yields for hours waiting for a sync httpCall) — would extend the live-set with the body bytes for that duration. NOT a 22.2 IMPL concern (the sync httpCall yield is bounded by `ClusterDispatch` timeout per `httpclient.Options.Timeout`); flagged for future scenarios that introduce long-lived coroutines (e.g., a hypothetical streaming-RPC bridge).

**(ix) Production HCM coroutine orchestration at Task 19a (PRE-ATOMIC-LANDING).** Per phase-22.2 SPEC §3.4 + §11.1 D2 closure + Task 19a IMPL. `decode_headers.go` + `encode_headers.go` invoke operator hooks as coroutines via `vm.NewThread()` + `vm.Resume(child, fn, ud)` per ADR-0191 surface. Cancellation discipline: `*filter` carries `decodeChild + decodeChildCancel + encodeChild + encodeChildCancel` fields; `OnDestroy` invokes both cancel funcs + nils the child references. ResumeYield branch dispatch:

- **Sync httpCall yield** (`pendingHTTPCallResume != nil`): close `httpCallReady` channel + wait on `httpCallDone` channel so the dispatch goroutine drives Resume to script completion synchronously inside DecodeHeaders. Race-free coordination via the channel-based gate (httpCallReady close → goroutine reads → calls Resume → closes httpCallDone → DecodeHeaders reads). gopher-lua's non-thread-safe Resume is honored — at any moment only one goroutine touches the VM.
- **Body yield** (`pendingBodyResume != nil` decode-side; `pendingRespBodyResume != nil` encode-side): return `Continue` so the chain's `RunDecodeData` fires. `accumulateRequestBody` / `accumulateResponseBody` at endStream invokes `vm.Resume(child, nil, lua.LString(...))` to resume the suspended coroutine.

**"Continue on body-yield" trade-off** documented at the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md `#### Phase 22.2 full bridge surface delta` subsection. Returning Continue (vs StopIteration) is REQUIRED because envoy-go's HCM serializes Headers→Data — returning StopIteration would deadlock the chain. The trade-off: subsequent decode-side filters see request headers BEFORE Lua's post-:body() mutations. **Multi-decoder-filter topologies that depend on body-after-yield header-mutation visibility ARE a known limitation flagged for REVIEW.md + future framework work** (deferred to 22.3 or a separate framework phase that introduces a "park-headers-iteration-pending-body" cooperative discipline).
