## ADR-0207: NEW `internal/filterstate/` framework primitive at 25.2 second-consumer scope — generic per-stream filter-state Bucket + FilterStateObject interface + StateType discriminator (read-only vs mutable) + sync semantics; consumer #1 = phase-22.2 `internal/filter/http/lua/filterstate.go` MIGRATES non-breaking; consumer #2 = phase-25.2 wasm `proxy_get_property "filter_state.*"` + `"upstream_filter_state.*"` paths per AMEND-B4; ADR-0188 API-revision allowance NOT consumed (the `internal/lua/` primitive itself is untouched); EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause for consumer #3+ (rbac filter-state read; ext_authz filter-state inject; ext_proc filter-state pass-through; new filter families)

**Status:** Accepted; §Context anchored at phase-25.2 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences body landed at phase-25.2 IMPL Tasks 9 + 10 + ratified at IMPL Task 22 atomic landing per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-25 (§Context anchor); 2026-05-26 (§Decision + §Consequences body landed at 25.2 IMPL Task 22).

**Status:** §Context anchored at phase-25.2 SPEC commit (this commit); §Decision + §Consequences body lands at phase-25.2 IMPL Lands-in-Task (the task that materializes `internal/filterstate/` + the follow-up migration task in `internal/filter/http/lua/`) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-25
**Doctrine:** Phase 25.2 §9 family-row sub-phase. ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline + EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer discipline per phase-22.1 ADR-0188 (the cross-phase precedent for `internal/lua/` at the symmetric scope).
**Lands-in:** Phase 25.2 IMPL Tasks that materialize `internal/filterstate/` + the phase-22.2 lua MIGRATION (anticipated Tasks NN + NN+1 per the framework-primitive-pair-with-migration discipline).

### Context

ADR-0207 anchors the **NEW `internal/filterstate/` framework primitive** per phase-25.2 BRAINSTORM Q7 + 25.2 SPEC §3.2 + AMEND-B4. Phase 22.2 lua landed `:filterState()` IN-PACKAGE at `internal/filter/http/lua/filterstate.go` per phase-22.2 BRAINSTORM Q9 EXTRACT-NOW-only-when-trigger-fires posture — at the time the project had no cross-filter state primitive and no committed second consumer. The IN-PACKAGE landing was the conservative posture. Phase 25.2 wasm's `proxy_get_property "filter_state.*"` + `"upstream_filter_state.*"` paths per AMEND-B4 require the same primitive surface — **this is the second consumer; the EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer trigger fires** per the discipline ADR-0188 established at phase-22.1 for `internal/lua/`.

**Framework-primitive trigger per Q7 + EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer.** The 25.2 IMPL extracts the primitive at consumer #2 (HTTP WASM filter; specifically the `proxy_get_property` host dispatcher's `filter_state.*` + `upstream_filter_state.*` branches per AMEND-B4) AND migrates consumer #1 (phase-22.2 lua's `:filterState()` Lua bridge) to consume the new primitive. The migration is **non-breaking** — the `:filterState()` Lua surface stays UNCHANGED byte-identical to phase-22.2 IMPL (the 2 envoy-go-strict divergences from upstream lua per phase-22.2 AMEND-22.2-4 — mutation exposure + typed Lua-value marshaling — carry forward UNCHANGED).

**Why now (vs deferring to consumer #3).** Three reasons: (a) **upstream_filter_state distinct root** per AMEND-B4 — the property roster scrape against `envoyproxy/envoy@v1.37.2:source/extensions/filters/common/expr/context.h:87` revealed that `upstream_filter_state` is a DISTINCT root co-equal to `filter_state` (BRAINSTORM Q7 OMITTED this; 25.2 SPEC §11.4 added it). The primitive must handle BOTH roots — this surface complexity is non-trivial vs the phase-22.2 in-package single-`map[string]any` shape and warrants the primitive extraction. (b) **Cross-filter visibility** — wasm's `filter_state.*` property paths expose values that may have been set by lua OR by future cross-filter primitives; a shared primitive ensures cross-filter state visibility (matches upstream Envoy v1.37.2's per-stream FilterState shape where ANY filter can Set/Get under a string key + the visibility is automatic). (c) **Future-consumer roster is high-confidence** — rbac filter-state read (phase-16 + future amendments); ext_authz filter-state inject (phase-18 + future); ext_proc filter-state pass-through (phase-19 + future); plus new filter families (network-filter family; cluster-specifier family) — the cross-filter primitive extraction is high-value vs the cost of carrying it in-package for additional sub-phases.

**Primitive API shape** (provisional at this 25.2 SPEC commit; production signatures land at 25.2 IMPL Task NN; see phase-25.2 SPEC §3.2 for the full signatures):

```go
// internal/filterstate/filterstate.go
package filterstate

type FilterStateObject interface {
    Marshal() ([]byte, error)
    Unmarshal([]byte) error
    HasData() bool
    StateType() StateType
}

type StateType int
const (
    StateTypeReadOnly StateType = iota  // = 0
    StateTypeMutable                    // = 1
)

type Bucket struct { /* unexported; per §3.2 */ }
func NewBucket() *Bucket
func (b *Bucket) Set(key string, obj FilterStateObject) error
func (b *Bucket) Get(key string) (FilterStateObject, bool)
func (b *Bucket) Keys() []string
```

**Read-only-vs-mutable conflict semantic:** Mutable-state-type entries OVERRIDE existing entries; read-only-state-type entries with the same key as a Mutable entry are REJECTED (Set returns error). This mirrors upstream Envoy v1.37.2 `FilterState::setData(key, obj, state_type, life_span)` semantics (a read-only Set against a key with a Mutable existing value is rejected). The Bucket is NOT goroutine-safe at the per-stream level (access path is single-goroutine per envoy-go's filter dispatch model); the internal `sync.RWMutex` is defensive (covers the rare concurrent-access cases that may surface at future cross-filter primitives).

**Package boundary:** `internal/filterstate/` hosts the GENERIC per-stream filter-state primitive (cross-filter-reusable; no HTTP-filter-specific knowledge). Consumer #1 = `internal/filter/http/lua/filterstate.go` (REWRITES to consume the primitive via a thin adapter; the `:filterState()` Lua surface stays UNCHANGED). Consumer #2 = `internal/filter/http/wasm/property.go` (or wherever the `proxy_get_property` host dispatcher's `filter_state.*` + `upstream_filter_state.*` branches live; consumes the primitive via two parallel `*Bucket` instances per per-stream context — one for `filter_state` + one for `upstream_filter_state`).

**MIGRATION discipline at 25.2 IMPL.** Phase-22.2's `internal/filter/http/lua/filterstate.go` REWRITES to delegate to `internal/filterstate/*Bucket`:
- The existing in-package `map[string]any` storage layer flips to the `*Bucket.Set/Get` accessors.
- The Lua bridge's `:filterState():get(name)` accessor calls `bucket.Get(name)` → unwraps the `FilterStateObject` to the underlying typed value via the existing typed-Lua-value marshaler.
- The Lua bridge's `:filterState():set(name, value)` accessor wraps the value in a `mutableFilterStateObject{value: value}` (an in-lua-package FilterStateObject impl) + calls `bucket.Set(name, obj)`.
- Migration delta: ~50-100 LoC inside `internal/filter/http/lua/`. The 22.2 lua test file expectations stay byte-identical (non-breaking migration; 25.2 IMPL Task NN+1 runs the existing phase-22.2 lua filterstate tests AFTER the migration to verify no test breakage).

The 2 envoy-go-strict divergences from upstream lua per phase-22.2 AMEND-22.2-4 carry forward UNCHANGED:
- `:filterState():set()` mutation exposed (upstream lua is read-only; envoy-go-strict envoy-go-only extension because C++ filters mutate FilterState directly; Go has no analog at 22.2 — the divergence remains at 25.2 because the primitive supports mutation natively).
- Typed Lua-value marshaling at `:get()` (upstream lua returns `serializeAsString` strings; envoy-go returns native Lua values via the typed-value marshaler). The primitive returns `FilterStateObject` (typed); the lua adapter unwraps.

**ADR-0188 API-revision allowance NOT consumed.** ADR-0188 anchors `internal/lua/` (the VM-class primitive). The `internal/filterstate/` extraction is a DISTINCT primitive at a DIFFERENT scope (filter-state vs lua-runtime). The `internal/lua/` framework primitive itself is untouched at 25.2 — only the in-package `filterstate.go` file inside `internal/filter/http/lua/` migrates. ADR-0188's API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause stays available for future `internal/lua/` evolutions at the consumer-#2 scope (i.e., a future second `internal/lua/` consumer — likely a future `lua_cluster_specifier` filter — may revise the `*LState` API per ADR-0188 §Decision body's allowance).

**EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause for consumer #3+** (anchored at ADR-0207 §Decision body at 25.2 IMPL Lands-in-Task): the primitive's API shape is provisional at consumer #2 (25.2 wasm); future consumers MAY require API revision after empirical validation. Mirrors phase-22.1 ADR-0188 + phase-22.2 ADR-0190 + phase-25.1 ADR-0202 allowance pattern at the symmetric scope. Anticipated consumer #3+ surfaces (from BRAINSTORM §3.2 + this 25.2 SPEC §3.2 commitment):
- rbac filter-state read (phase-16 + future amendments) — consumer #3 if RBAC SPEC adds filter-state-keyed rule support.
- ext_authz filter-state inject (phase-18 + future) — consumer #3 if ext_authz SPEC adds filter-state pass-through from authz check response.
- ext_proc filter-state pass-through (phase-19 + future) — consumer #3 if ext_proc SPEC adds filter-state read/write in the gRPC stream protocol.
- New filter families: network-filter framework's filter-state (out-of-row); cluster-specifier framework's filter-state (out-of-row); WASM host family's network-filter-wasm + access-logger-wasm + cluster-specifier-wasm consumers (all of which would re-consume `internal/filterstate/` at the corresponding cross-row scope).

The future-consumer roster is **structurally MORE committed than phase-22.1 lua's speculative future-consumer roster** because the EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer trigger has ALREADY fired (the primitive is NOT speculative — consumer #1 + consumer #2 are landing in this same 25.2 IMPL session); future consumers consume the same primitive without re-litigating the abstraction shape. The API revision risk envelope at consumer #3+ is LOWER vs phase-22.1's first-consumer extraction.

**Anticipated `internal/filterstate/` package shape** (per 25.2 SPEC §3.2 + future test-file extensions per §14.3):

```
internal/filterstate/
  doc.go                       # package overview + ADR-0207 cross-ref + consumer roster

  filterstate_test.go          # Set/Get/Keys round-trip + read-only-vs-mutable conflict + nil-handling
  bucket_concurrency_test.go   # RWMutex discipline + concurrent-read concurrent-add tests

```

**Anticipated LoC:** ~150-250 LIVE + ~250-400 TEST at 25.2 IMPL per BRAINSTORM §3.2 envelope. Plus ~50-100 LoC migration delta inside `internal/filter/http/lua/` at the consumer #1 MIGRATION task.

**Cross-references:** ADR-0188 (`internal/lua/` precedent for the cross-phase EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer discipline — but ADR-0188's API-revision allowance is NOT consumed here per above); ADR-0190 (phase-22.2 `internal/dynamicmetadata/` precedent for the cross-filter primitive extraction shape — sibling cross-filter primitive at the symmetric scope); ADR-0202 (phase-25.1 `internal/wasm/`); ADR-0205 (root VM lifecycle); ADR-0206 (25.2 ABI extensions including the `proxy_get_property` host dispatcher that consumes this primitive at filter_state.* + upstream_filter_state.* branches); ADR-0208 (paired filter-package extension ADR — co-anchors the consumer #2 integration at `internal/filter/http/wasm/property.go`); phase-25.2 SPEC §3.2 + §11.4 AMEND-B4 (upstream_filter_state addition + property roster).

### Decision

At 25.2 IMPL the NEW `internal/filterstate/` framework primitive lands at second-consumer scope per the §Context above:

1. **NEW `internal/filterstate/filterstate.go` + `bucket.go` + `object.go`** at Task 9 — materializes the framework primitive:
   - `type Bucket struct { ... }` — per-stream filter-state container; `Set(key string, obj FilterStateObject) error` + `Get(key string) (FilterStateObject, bool)` + `Keys() []string` + read-only-vs-mutable conflict semantics + `sync.RWMutex` for concurrent-read concurrent-add isolation.
   - `type FilterStateObject interface { Serialize() ([]byte, error); StateType() StateType }` — minimal interface; consumers implement to participate.
   - `type StateType int` enum — `ReadOnly = 0` / `Mutable = 1` discriminator; read-only objects reject `Set` overwrites; mutable objects accept overwrites.
   - Test coverage at `filterstate_test.go` + `bucket_concurrency_test.go` + `filterstateobject_test.go`.

2. **Consumer #1: phase-22.2 lua MIGRATES non-breaking** at Task 10. `internal/filter/http/lua/filterstate.go` REWRITES to delegate to `internal/filterstate/*Bucket` via an ephemeral `bucketFromMap`/`materializeBucketIntoMap` pattern that preserves the existing test file's `cb.filterState as map[string]any` shape (forced by the §14.5 non-breaking discipline — the test wording cannot change). The Lua surface (`:filterState():get/:set`) is byte-identical to 25.1 + 22.2; all existing phase-22.2 lua filterstate tests PASS without modification.

3. **Consumer #2: phase-25.2 wasm at `proxy_get_property` `filter_state.*` + `upstream_filter_state.*` branches** at Task 13. The per-stream property resolver (`internal/wasm/property.go` + `internal/filter/http/wasm/property.go`) dispatches the `filter_state.<key>` + `upstream_filter_state.<key>` path families against the `*filterstate.Bucket` via the consumer-side adapter; results are Serialize()'d to wire bytes for `proxy_get_property`. The two roots are DISTINCT per AMEND-B4 SUBSTANTIVE REFINEMENT (vs. BRAINSTORM Q7's hypothesized single root) — `upstream_filter_state` is byte-faithful to upstream Envoy v1.37.2 `source/extensions/filters/common/expr/context.h::upstreamFilterState`.

4. **ADR-0188 API-revision allowance NOT consumed.** The phase-22.2 `internal/lua/` framework primitive itself (the LState pool + the lifecycle discipline + the sandbox) is UNTOUCHED at this migration; only the in-package `filterstate.go` file delegates to the NEW `internal/filterstate/` primitive. The phase-22.2 ADR-0188 EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE for consumer #2 (deferred to phase-25 WASM consumer) is preserved as not-yet-consumed at consumer #1 (lua); when consumer #2 (wasm) consumes `internal/lua/` directly at some future phase (e.g., if a Wasm-script-via-Lua bridge surfaces), the allowance is available.

5. **EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE for consumer #3+** anchored in this §Decision body. Future consumers (rbac filter-state read at phase 16+ revisit; ext_authz filter-state inject at phase 18+ revisit; ext_proc filter-state pass-through at phase 19+ revisit; new filter families that surface filter-state coupling) may require API revision after empirical validation at consumer #2 (wasm). The minimal interface (`FilterStateObject` with `Serialize()` + `StateType()`) is anticipated to generalize cleanly — but the revision allowance is preserved for the canonical cross-consumer API-stability concern.

### Consequences

**Positive:**

- **SECOND occurrence of EXTRACT-NOW-on-second-consumer discipline** after phase-22.1+22.2's `internal/lua/` + `internal/dynamicmetadata/`. The pattern HOLDS — primitives extracted at the second-consumer scope (rather than first) get their API shape empirically validated at extraction time rather than retrofit-validated later.
- **Phase-22.2 lua MIGRATION non-breaking** preserves operator-visible API at the `:filterState()` Lua surface. Existing operators have no migration burden.
- **Consumer #2 (wasm) integration confirms the API shape generalizes.** The `*Bucket` API surface that emerged from phase-22.2's needs maps cleanly onto wasm's `proxy_get_property "filter_state.*"` dispatch without revision.
- **EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE for consumer #3+** preserves the flexibility to revise the `*Bucket` API when empirical evidence from rbac / ext_authz / ext_proc surfaces friction. The minimal interface is anticipated to generalize; the allowance is a defensive option, not a commitment.
- **Distinct `filter_state` + `upstream_filter_state` roots per AMEND-B4** match upstream Envoy v1.37.2 byte-faithfully; operators familiar with upstream see structurally-equivalent path semantics.

**Negative / Trade-offs:**

- **Phase-22.2 lua filterstate ephemeral Bucket pattern** (consumer #1 migration) preserves the `cb.filterState as map[string]any` test-shape via ephemeral `bucketFromMap`/`materializeBucketIntoMap` adapter calls. The deeper migration (storing as `*Bucket` directly + updating all test wordings to match) was OUT OF 25.2 scope; documented as a 25.2-follow-up architectural debt in REVIEW.md. The API-level migration IS complete; storage migration is the remaining work.
- **Consumer-side adapter complexity at `internal/filter/http/wasm/property.go`** for the `filter_state.*` + `upstream_filter_state.*` dispatch. The dispatch must (a) project the `<key>` from the `filter_state.<key>` path; (b) look up via `*Bucket.Get(key)`; (c) Serialize() the result; (d) handle the read-only-vs-mutable distinction for `proxy_set_property` (the set path is not yet wired at 25.2 — read-only at consumer #2; lifts at 25.3 IF SPEC settles a mutable set path).

**Forward-pointers:**

- Consumer #3+ may require API revision; allowance preserved.
- 25.3 SPEC may settle the `proxy_set_property` mutable set path for wasm consumer #2.
- The phase-22.2 lua storage migration (away from `cb.filterState as map[string]any`) is a 25.2-follow-up phase candidate.

**Per-stream body-buffer accumulation per Q1 + Q2.** Per 25.2 SPEC §4.3 + §3.6 body.go. Each `DecodeData(data, endStream)` invocation accumulates `data` into `f.decodeBody`; the per-`*StreamContext` body buffer grows per chunk. If `len(f.decodeBody) > cfg.bodyBufferCapBytes` (default 16 MiB) and not already cap-exceeded, set sticky `f.decodeBodyCapExceeded = true` + increment `cfg.stats.bodyBufferCapExceeded` + increment `cfg.stats.envoyGoFailures` (per 25.2 SPEC §2.25 scope extension) + return `StopAllIteration` + `decoderCb.SendLocalReply(413, "Payload Too Large", ...)`. If the guest has not opted into body callbacks (`HasGlobalFunc("proxy_on_request_body") == false`), the body data passes through without buffering (NO accumulation; NO cap enforcement at the filter layer). The encode side mirrors decode for `proxy_on_response_body` + response termination.

- **fixture-0036 deliberate-break liveness verification cycle** (per `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`) addresses the dead-vacuous-assertion risk at extraction time rather than retrofit (mirrors 25.1 Task 15+17 follow-up which surfaced the same risk).

**Negative / Trade-offs:**

- **fixture-0036 cross-side arms a-j skipped on Envoy v1.37.2 503 upstream-buffering parity gap** (Concern 1 deferral). The reference Envoy v1.37.2 wasm filter returns 503 on body PAUSE-then-CONTINUE patterns that envoy-go handles correctly; the cross-side `CompareBytes` assertion would fail on the divergent wire shape. Production fix: wire envoy-go upstream-buffering to match Envoy's `Action::Pause + buffer-then-forward` byte-faithfully. Documented as a 25.2-follow-up architectural debt in REVIEW.md.
- **scenario (j) `std::env::vars()` RefCell** — per AMEND-A6 env_vars deferred to 25.3; the scenario still fails on response_headers callback. Workaround in fixture-0036 (scenario skipped pending 25.3 activation).
- **fixture-0034 cap-set widening at Task 22 fix-up** (gate-at-registration regression). The 25.1 fixture's cap-set didn't include the 14 NEW 25.2 hostcall caps; the gate-at-registration discipline broke module instantiation. Cap-set widened at this Task 22; the 25.2 IMPL fixture is now consistent with the AMEND-B5 discipline.
- **9 envoy-go-strict counters expand the stat surface 119 → 128** — operators integrating with envoy-go's stats sink see the new namespace at upgrade time; documented in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md.

**Forward-pointers:**

- 25.3 IMPL extends the BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md bundle with per-route + multi-plugin + conformance harness detail.

## ADR-0210: Per-route Wasm 5th-canonical REUSE-by-absence — EXPLICIT-NO-NEW-CANONICAL classification per AMEND-A3 ABSENCE-DEFINITIVE + 25.3 AMEND-C1 (no `WasmPerRoute` message; wholesale `Wasm` TPFC override; "dangling vm_id" MOOT — referential VM configs unimplemented upstream); ADR-0125 STAYS at 10 canonicals (NO §(xvi) amendment); per-route override resolves through the existing phase-13/14/15 3-tier resolver (REUSE-1)

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at phase-25.3 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at phase-25.3 IMPL Task 15 atomic landing (this commit) — `internal/filter/http/wasm/perroute.go` materialized at Task 6.
**Date:** 2026-05-28 (§Context); 2026-05-29 (§Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at 25.3 IMPL Task 15)
**Doctrine:** Phase 25.3 §9 family-row sub-phase (third-and-final). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. EXPLICIT-NO-NEW-CANONICAL classification ADR shape per ADR-0173 (phase-23) / ADR-0180 (phase-20) / ADR-0197 (phase-24).
**Lands-in:** Phase 25.3 IMPL task that materializes `internal/filter/http/wasm/perroute.go` (Task 6; dispatch wiring Task 9).

### Context

ADR-0210 anchors the **per-route Wasm 5th-canonical REUSE-by-absence** classification per parent SPEC AMEND-A3 ABSENCE-DEFINITIVE + 25.3 SPEC §4 + §11.1 D-25.3-1 re-CONFIRMATION. The v1.37.2 IDL + go-control-plane v1.32.4 binding define exactly ONE message in the `envoy.extensions.filters.http.wasm.v3` namespace — `message Wasm { envoy.extensions.wasm.v3.PluginConfig config = 1; }` (`api/envoy/extensions/filters/http/wasm/v3/wasm.proto:19-22`) — and the wasm filter factory `WasmFilterConfig` (`source/extensions/filters/http/wasm/config.h:20-66`) overrides ONLY `createFilterFactoryFromProto*`, NOT `createRouteSpecificFilterConfig`. There is NO dedicated `WasmPerRoute` proto. Per-route override is therefore a wholesale `Wasm`-message replacement carried in a route's `typed_per_filter_config` + resolved by the existing 3-tier per-route resolver from phase 13/14/15 (per-route → listener-level → no-op) — REUSE-1 at 25.3 SPEC §3.4. ADR-0125's canonical-per-route roster STAYS at 10 entries; NO §(xvi) amendment (the BRAINSTORM-era escape-valve "ADR-0125 amendment 10 → 11" is RETIRED at parent SPEC commit + INHERITED through 25.1/25.2/25.3).

**AMEND-C1: "dangling vm_id" is MOOT.** The BRAINSTORM §6.1 / §10 D-25.3-1 anticipated a fixture-0039 boot-reject arm for "dangling vm_id reference" (a per-route override referencing a vm_id with no matching listener-level PluginConfig), mirroring phase-17 jwt_authn 8th-canonical dangling-name discipline. The §11.1 empirical scrape REFUTES the premise: `vm_id` (`api/envoy/extensions/wasm/v3/wasm.proto:76-81`) is a pure VM-sharing key, and the `vm` oneof (`:165-168`) carries an inline `VmConfig vm_config = 3;` with a `// TODO: add referential VM configurations.` comment — referential (named cross-reference) VM configs are UNIMPLEMENTED upstream. Every `PluginConfig` self-contains its `VmConfig`; there is no cross-reference for a dangling `vm_id` to dangle against. The fixture-0039 arm shifts to env_vars cap-exceeded OR env_vars key-collision (final at 25.3 IMPL per D-25.3-P1).

### Decision

Per-route `envoy.filters.http.wasm` override is classified **EXPLICIT-NO-NEW-CANONICAL** per AMEND-A3 ABSENCE-DEFINITIVE + AMEND-C1. There is NO `WasmPerRoute` Go type and NO new canonical per-route shape: a route's `typed_per_filter_config` carries a **wholesale `envoy.extensions.filters.http.wasm.v3.Wasm` message** (the SAME message type as the listener-level filter config), and per-route resolution is a wholesale REPLACEMENT of the listener-level config — not a field-merge or a disabled-flag override. `ADR-0125` STAYS at **10 canonicals** (NO §(xvi) amendment).

Materialized at `internal/filter/http/wasm/perroute.go`:

1. **`parsePerRouteWasm(m proto.Message, factoryCtx)` (perroute.go:70)** type-asserts the per-route TPFC to `*wasmv3.Wasm`, round-trips through `anypb.New`, and builds a per-route `*compiledConfig` through the SAME `buildCompiledConfig` single-source-of-truth path as the listener-level config (so EVERY PARSE-REJECT arm + the registry `AcquireFor` VM-sharing path applies identically to a per-route override). A validate-only mode (`validateWasmConfigShape` → `buildCompiledConfigImpl(..., validateOnly=true)`) runs the full reject roster at HCM-build time WITHOUT claiming the process-wide plugin-config name (arm 26) or constructing/refcounting a `*RootVM` — so a route's `RegisterPerRouteValidator` hook validates the shape pre-freeze without leaking a name claim or a VM refcount.
2. **`resolvePerRoute(routeCfg, listenerCfg) *compiledConfig` (perroute.go:105)** is the 3-tier selection: per-route override (if present) → listener-level → no-op. This REUSES the phase-13/14/15 3-tier per-route resolver pattern (REUSE-1); it is a pure pointer-select with negligible per-request cost (`BenchmarkPerRouteResolve` = 0.2 ns/op at Task 15).

**Empirical finding (reference v1.37.2 has NO per-route wasm support).** The differential exercise at fixture 0038 (Task 11) empirically confirmed that reference Envoy v1.37.2 **boot-rejects** any per-route config for `envoy.filters.http.wasm`: *"The filter envoy.filters.http.wasm doesn't support virtual host or route specific configurations"* (`WasmFilterConfig` overrides only `createFilterFactoryFromProto*`, NOT `createRouteSpecificFilterConfig`). Per-route wasm override is therefore intrinsically an **envoy-go capability surfaced subject-only** in the differential — fixture 0038's `perroute_override_applies` arm asserts it SUBJECT-ONLY via `wasm.plugin_perroute_override.executions` (the reference bootstrap carries no per-route TPFC). This is a strict superset of upstream behavior, not a divergence from a supported upstream surface.

### Consequences

- **No new canonical; ADR-0125 unchanged at 10.** The per-route override is carried in the existing canonical `typed_per_filter_config` slot as a wholesale `Wasm` message; no `WasmPerRoute` type, no 11th canonical, no ADR-0125 §(xvi) amendment.
- **"Dangling vm_id" is MOOT** (AMEND-C1): referential VM configs are unimplemented upstream (`// TODO: add referential VM configurations.`), so there is no cross-reference for a per-route `vm_id` to dangle against. The fixture-0039 boot-reject arm shifted to env_vars cap-exceeded (D-25.3-P1, Task 12).
- **BUG-1 (frozen-registry per-route stats), surfaced by fixture 0038.** The Task-9 lazy per-route build originally called `reg.NewCounter` POST-BOOT, panicking against the boot-frozen stats registry. FIXED by routing per-route `newFilterStats` through `NewCounterIfAbsent` (post-freeze-tolerant). The unit test passed only because it used a non-frozen test registry; the differential against the frozen production registry caught it. (See REVIEW.md §the-4-bugs.)
- The per-route override is subject-only in the differential; the 0038 arm proves it LIVE via a deliberate-break cycle on `wasm.plugin_perroute_override.executions`.

## ADR-0211: Multi-plugin VM-sharing process-global registry (`Sha256(vm_id‖vm_configuration‖code)` key; runtime-not-in-key; raw-vm_id shared-data scope; two-layer-collapse) + `failure_policy = FAIL_RELOAD` reload state machine (`FailurePolicy` enum + RuntimeError-gating + `FAIL_CLOSED` default + base_interval-only backoff + envoy-go-strict 100ms floor + Group-C `vm_reload_*` triplet + `fail_open`⊕`failure_policy` mutual-exclusivity reject) + `VmConfig.environment_variables` activation (collision-REJECT not override + WASI environ feed + envoy-go-strict 64-entry/4-KiB cap) — BUNDLED per D-25.3-2; REFINES ADR-0205 anchor `*RootVM per *compiledConfig` → per-`(vm_id, vm_configuration, code)` shared `*RootVM`

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at phase-25.3 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at phase-25.3 IMPL Task 15 atomic landing (this commit). `internal/wasm/registry.go` (Task 1) + `internal/wasm/reload.go` (Task 3) + `internal/wasm/env_vars.go` (Task 4) materialized. BUNDLE disposition (Q1+Q2+Q3 under one ADR) settled at SPEC commit per D-25.3-2.
**Date:** 2026-05-28 (§Context); 2026-05-29 (§Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at 25.3 IMPL Task 15)
**Doctrine:** Phase 25.3 §9 family-row sub-phase (third-and-final). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline + Q10 strict-scope precedent (consumer-#1-internal evolution lands under a NEW ADR; ADR-0202 API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause STAYS scoped to consumer #2). REFINES ADR-0205 via in-place §Consequences acknowledgment at IMPL (no new ADR number for the acknowledgment).
**Lands-in:** Phase 25.3 IMPL tasks that materialize `internal/wasm/registry.go` (Task 1) + the per-`*RootVM` reload state machine `internal/wasm/reload.go` (Task 3) + env_vars assembly `internal/wasm/env_vars.go` (Task 4) + dispatch wiring (Task 9).

### Context

ADR-0211 anchors the THREE BUNDLED 25.3 VM-lifecycle surfaces per BRAINSTORM Q1+Q2+Q3 + 25.3 SPEC §3.1-§3.3 + the §11.2 + §11.3 + §11.4 empirical pins. The BUNDLE (vs split) disposition is settled at this SPEC commit per D-25.3-2: the surfaces are operationally cohesive (reload of a shared `*RootVM` invalidates ALL plugin contexts under its key; env_vars is a small VM-lifecycle surface) + the combined §Decision body is within the ADR-body envelope + ADR-economy precedent (25.2 ADR-0206 bundled body+buffer+trailer). Conformance harness STAYS at ADR-0212; ADR-0213 STAYS a reserve.

**Multi-plugin VM-sharing process-global registry (Q1 + AMEND-C2).** NEW `internal/wasm/registry.go` materializes a process-global `*Registry` keyed by `Sha256(vm_id ‖ "||" ‖ vm_configuration ‖ "||" ‖ code)`, mirroring cpp-host `makeVmKey` (`proxy-wasm-cpp-host@da3ce05d:src/wasm.cc:90-92`). The key folds in `vm_configuration` AND the full `code` bytes (not a precomputed code-hash); **runtime is NOT in the key** (envoy-go is wazero-single-runtime; the cpp-host engine arrives via the `WasmHandleFactory`, not the key). On `compiledConfig.New` the registry looks up an existing `*RootVM` by the composite key; on hit reuses + bumps refcount; on miss constructs fresh + inserts at refcount 1 (cpp-host `createWasm` `:546-589` `.lock()`-on-match pattern; envoy-go holds strong references with explicit refcount rather than cpp-host's `weak_ptr` + `shared_ptr`-ownership model). At `compiledConfig.Close` the registry decrements; at zero it removes the entry + `rootVM.Close()`. Each `PluginConfig` sharing a key gets a distinct `*PluginContext` child (own `root_id` + configuration bytes + capabilities; cpp-host plugin identity `Sha256(root_id‖plugin_configuration‖key)` per `src/context.cc:92-94`). **Cross-plugin shared-data is SHARED at raw-`vm_id` scope** (broader than the composite VM-instance key — cpp-host `SharedData::data_` is outer-keyed by the raw user `vm_id` per `src/shared_data.cc:44-79`, NOT the vm_key): distinct `*RootVM` instances under the same `vm_id` (differing only in vm_configuration/code) observe ONE shared-data namespace via a per-process `sharedDataByVmID` store looked up at `*RootVM` construction. envoy-go COLLAPSES cpp-host's two-layer (process-global `base_wasms` weak_ptr map + thread-local `local_wasms` clone layer, `src/wasm.cc:35-40`) into ONE process-global registry because Go's goroutine concurrency model has no Envoy per-worker thread-local equivalent (the wazero Runtime+Module is shared with the per-RootVM serialization discipline from ADR-0205). REFINES ADR-0205's anchor `*RootVM per *compiledConfig` → `*RootVM per (vm_id, vm_configuration, code)` shared across `*compiledConfig` instances with matching identity (in-place §Consequences acknowledgment to ADR-0205 at IMPL; no new ADR number).

**`failure_policy = FAIL_RELOAD` reload state machine (Q2 + AMEND-C3).** `FailurePolicy` enum `{UNSPECIFIED=0, FAIL_RELOAD=1, FAIL_CLOSED=2, FAIL_OPEN=3}` (`api/envoy/extensions/wasm/v3/wasm.proto:24-42`); UNSPECIFIED (default) resolves to `FAIL_CLOSED` (HTTP 503) — NOT bypass. `FAIL_RELOAD` is gated to guest `FailState::RuntimeError` (=7) ONLY; all other fail-states (StartFailed, ConfigureFailed, UnableToInitializeCode, …) fall back to `FAIL_CLOSED` (`wasm.proto:33` + `source/extensions/common/wasm/wasm.cc:482-536`). State machine `{Running, Reloading, Failed}` per-`*RootVM`; reload is request-driven + backoff-rate-limited (NOT a background respawn). Backoff honors `ReloadConfig.backoff` = `config.core.v3.BackoffStrategy` (`wasm.proto:44-48`, PluginConfig field 8; "only applied when failure_policy is FAIL_RELOAD"); upstream consumes ONLY `backoff.base_interval` (default 1000ms when unspecified; PGV `gte 1ms`) feeding a `JitteredLowerBoundBackOffStrategy` (`wasm.cc:603-606`) — `max_interval` is in the proto but DEAD in the wasm path. envoy-go honors `base_interval` with an envoy-go-strict floor `max(operator_value, 100ms)` (departure record; rationale: prevent reload-storm) + mirrors upstream's base_interval-only backoff + RETIRES the BRAINSTORM Q2 `max_interval` 1s floor as MOOT. `fail_open: bool` (PluginConfig field 5, deprecated-at-3.0) and `failure_policy` (field 7) are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — both-set is PARSE-REJECT (`wasm.cc:573-574` "only one of fail_open or failure_policy can be set"); `fail_open=true → FAIL_OPEN`; unset → UNSPECIFIED → `FAIL_CLOSED`. Group-C `vm_reload_success` + `vm_reload_runtime_failure` + `vm_reload_backoff` triplet activates (mirrors upstream `VmReloadSuccess`/`VmReloadFailure`/`VmReloadBackoff`; project stat 128 → 131). The reload state machine consumes `internal/clock.Clock` (THIRD co-consumer of ADR-0186, after phase-21 + 25.2 tick goroutine) — RATIFIES the Clock-seam extraction at multi-consumer-real-scope.

**`VmConfig.environment_variables` activation (Q3 + AMEND-C4).** `EnvironmentVariables { repeated string host_env_keys=1; map<string,string> key_values=2; }` on `VmConfig` field 7 (`wasm.proto:131-149`). **Collisions across the two fields PARSE-REJECT at config-load** byte-faithful to upstream (`source/extensions/common/wasm/plugin.cc:30-42` builds a key-set + throws `EnvoyException("All the keys must be unique")` BEFORE merging) — there is NO override semantic (REFUTES the BRAINSTORM Q3 "key_values overrides" hypothesis). `key_values` is additionally rejected for the null runtime (`plugin.cc:25-28`; subsumed by envoy-go's wazero-only-runtime PARSE-REJECT). Host-env-keys absent from the host process env are silently skipped (`plugin.cc:49-51`). The assembled map feeds the wazero WASI `environ_get` + `environ_sizes_get` shims as `KEY=VALUE\0` entries (`src/exports.cc:802-846`; the shims returned zeros at 25.2 per AMEND-A6 deferral — 25.3 populates them). envoy-go-strict cap (64 total entries + per-value 4 KiB; hardcoded NOT operator-tunable; upstream has NO cap) → PARSE-REJECT + `env_vars_cap_exceeded` envoy-go-strict counter (project stat 131 → 132) + departure record. Resolves the fixture-0036 scenario-(j) `std::env::vars()` RefCell panic (25.2 REVIEW §7 debt #4) by populating env from config.

**0 NEW ABI surface (D-25.3-4 / AMEND §11.6).** All three surfaces are HOST-SIDE: multi-plugin sharing is mediated by the registry (the guest replays existing `proxy_on_vm_start`/`proxy_on_configure`/`proxy_on_context_create`); reload re-instantiates + replays existing lifecycle callbacks (no `proxy_on_reload`); env_vars feeds the existing WASI shims. `ABICallbacks` STAYS at 25 methods; capability roster STAYS at 58 keys.

### Decision

The three BUNDLED VM-lifecycle surfaces materialize as follows.

**(1) Multi-plugin VM-sharing registry (`internal/wasm/registry.go`, Task 1+2).** A process-global `*Registry` (exported `DefaultRegistry`) holds `map[string]*registryEntry` keyed by `makeVMKey = Sha256(vm_id ‖ "||" ‖ vm_configuration ‖ "||" ‖ code)` (runtime NOT in key — envoy-go is wazero-single-runtime). The filter package acquires via `Registry.AcquireFor(vmID, vmConfig, code, factory) (*RootVM, key, error)`: on a key HIT the existing `*RootVM` is reused + refcount++; on MISS the factory constructs a fresh `*RootVM` at refcount 1. `compiledConfig.Close()` calls `Registry.Release(key)` (refcount--); at refcount 0 the entry is removed + `rootVM.Close()` fires. Each sharing `PluginConfig` gets a distinct per-stream `*StreamContext` child against the shared instance; the shared `rootABICallbacks` multiplexer is retrieved on a HIT via `(*RootVM).RegisteredABICallbacks()` so configs sharing one VM share one per-stream routing table. **Cross-plugin shared-data is SHARED at raw-`vm_id` scope** — a separate `sharedDataByVmID` store keyed by the RAW user `vm_id` (broader than the composite VM-instance key), mirroring cpp-host `SharedData::data_`. envoy-go COLLAPSES cpp-host's two-layer (process-global `base_wasms` + thread-local `local_wasms`) into ONE process-global registry (Go has no per-worker thread-local equivalent; the wazero Runtime+Module is shared under the per-RootVM `dispatchMu` serialization from ADR-0205). REFINES ADR-0205's anchor `*RootVM per *compiledConfig` → `*RootVM per (vm_id, vm_configuration, code)` shared across matching `*compiledConfig` instances.

**(2) `failure_policy = FAIL_RELOAD` reload state machine (`internal/wasm/reload.go`, Task 3+9).** `FailurePolicy` enum `{UNSPECIFIED=0, FAIL_RELOAD=1, FAIL_CLOSED=2, FAIL_OPEN=3}`; UNSPECIFIED resolves to `FAIL_CLOSED` (HTTP 503), NOT bypass. A per-`*RootVM` `{Running, Reloading, Failed}` state machine, request-driven + backoff-rate-limited (NOT a background respawn). `FAIL_RELOAD` is gated to guest `FailState::RuntimeError` ONLY (`NoteReloadRuntimeError`); all other fail-states fall back to `FAIL_CLOSED`. Backoff honors `ReloadConfig.backoff.base_interval` ONLY (`max_interval` is DEAD in the wasm path upstream) with an envoy-go-strict floor `base_interval = max(operator, 100ms)` (departure record — prevents reload-storm). Group-C `vm_reload_success` / `vm_reload_runtime_failure` / `vm_reload_backoff` triplet activates (project stat 128 → 131). **Critical ordering (the BUG-4 fix, Task 9):** `ReloadDispatch` runs BEFORE `initStreamContext` in `decode_headers.go`, so a Failed FAIL_RELOAD VM is reinstantiated into a fresh un-poisoned instance BEFORE `proxy_on_context_create` is attempted — the only sequence under which a guest-trap-poisoned instance can recover. The whole dispatch (reload-then-context-create) is serialized under the existing `*RootVM.dispatchMu` per D-25.3-P3. `fail_open` (deprecated field 5) and `failure_policy` (field 7) are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — both-set is PARSE-REJECT; `fail_open=true → FAIL_OPEN`. The reload machine consumes `internal/clock.Clock` (the THIRD co-consumer of ADR-0186).

**(3) `VmConfig.environment_variables` activation (`internal/wasm/env_vars.go`, Task 4).** `AssembleEnvVars` merges `host_env_keys` (looked up from host process env; silently skipped if absent) + `key_values`. **Collisions across the two fields PARSE-REJECT at config-load** (byte-faithful to upstream — NO override semantic, refuting the BRAINSTORM Q3 hypothesis). The assembled map feeds the wazero WASI `environ_get` + `environ_sizes_get` shims as `KEY=VALUE\0` entries (the shims returned zeros at 25.2 per AMEND-A6; 25.3 populates them via `WithRootEnv`). An envoy-go-strict cap (64 total entries + 4096 bytes per value; hardcoded, not operator-tunable; upstream has no cap) → PARSE-REJECT + the `env_vars_cap_exceeded` envoy-go-strict counter on the stat surface (project stat 131 → 132). This resolves the fixture-0036 scenario-(j) `std::env::vars()` RefCell panic (25.2 REVIEW §7 debt #4) by populating env from config.

**0 NEW ABI surface (D-25.3-4).** All three surfaces are HOST-SIDE: sharing is mediated by the registry; reload re-instantiates + replays existing lifecycle callbacks (no `proxy_on_reload`); env_vars feeds the existing WASI shims. `ABICallbacks` STAYS at 25 methods; the capability roster STAYS at 58 keys.

### Consequences

- **ADR-0205 is REFINED in place** (see ADR-0205 §Consequences AMEND): `*RootVM per *compiledConfig` → `*RootVM per (vm_id, vm_configuration, code)` shared via the registry. No new ADR number for the acknowledgment.
- **ADR-0186 is RATIFIED at multi-consumer-real scope** (see ADR-0186 §Consequences RATIFIES clause): the reload machine is the consumer that, together with the Task-5 phase-21 migration, validates the unified `internal/clock` superset.
- **3 production bugs surfaced by the differential (fixture 0038) + fixed** (the reload/sharing surface is what the differential stresses; unit tests masked all three because they used synthetic guests + non-frozen registries):
  - **BUG-3 (guest-trap Close cascade):** a Rust `panic!`/trap in `proxy_on_request_headers` leaves the SDK dispatcher's `RefCell` poisoned; envoy-go then dispatched the SAME poisoned instance for `proxy_on_response_headers`/`proxy_on_done`, cascading `panic_already_borrowed`. FIXED with a `StreamContext.trapped` guard that abandons further callbacks on a trapped instance.
  - **BUG-4 (ReloadDispatch-before-context-create reorder):** as originally ordered (`initStreamContext` before `ReloadDispatch`), a poisoned FAIL_RELOAD instance could never reinstantiate — every post-trap request fail-OPENed at `proxy_on_context_create` before the reload machine was consulted. FIXED by reordering `ReloadDispatch` before `initStreamContext`.
  - **BUG-2 (reload triplet does not engage)** was the symptom-level read of BUG-3/BUG-4; resolved as a consequence of those fixes. Post-fix the triplet engages live: req2 within the ~1s window → `vm_reload_backoff=1`; req3 past the window → `vm_reload_success=1` (proven via deliberate-break at fixture 0038).
- **`env_vars_cap_exceeded` is allocate-only at boot-PARSE-REJECT.** The cap fires at config-load (`parseEnvVars`) where there is no running per-plugin stats scope to increment a counter; the counter is ALLOCATED on the stat surface (so the surface is 132) but is consistent with the other 25.2 cap counters being runtime-only — it exists for future runtime use. Documented as a precise behavioral note in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md.
- **2 NEW envoy-go-strict departures:** (a) reload-floor `base_interval = max(operator, 100ms)`; (b) env_vars-cap 64 entries / 4096 bytes-per-value → PARSE-REJECT.

## ADR-0212: `test/conformance/proxy-wasm/` conformance harness seed per Q7 + AMEND-A8 + 25.3 AMEND-C5 — `go test`-driven harness (mirrors phase-05 h2spec at `test/conformance/h2spec/`); pin SHA `proxy-wasm-cpp-host@da3ce05d`; the 16 cpp-host `test/*_test.cc` UNIT-test families re-expressed as Go-test sub-tests; 10 ported / 6 deferred per host-capability alignment; 62.5% (10/16) numeric threshold; 100%-of-10 phase-done gate; deliberate-break liveness per family; 6-deferred-family forward-pointer roster

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at phase-25.3 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at phase-25.3 IMPL Task 15 atomic landing (this commit). `test/conformance/proxy-wasm/` materialized at Tasks 13+14 (10/10 families GREEN).
**Date:** 2026-05-28 (§Context); 2026-05-29 (§Decision + §Consequences body LANDED at 25.3 IMPL Task 15)
**Doctrine:** Phase 25.3 §9 family-row sub-phase (third-and-final). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. Conformance-harness-INDEPENDENT-of-differential discipline per phase-05 h2spec + grpc-conformance precedent. Deliberate-break liveness MANDATORY per `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`.
**Lands-in:** Phase 25.3 IMPL tasks that materialize `test/conformance/proxy-wasm/` (harness scaffold Task 13; 10 family ports Task 14).

### Context

ADR-0212 anchors the **`test/conformance/proxy-wasm/` conformance harness seed** per BRAINSTORM Q7 + parent SPEC AMEND-A8 + `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md §7.3` + 25.3 SPEC §8.4 + the §11.5 D-25.3-3 empirical pin. The harness is a NEW Go-test package + driver, SEPARATE from `test/fixtures/` + `test/differential/`, mirroring the phase-05 h2spec discipline at `test/conformance/h2spec/`. Runs in CI per-commit via `go test ./test/conformance/proxy-wasm/...` (6-gate phase-done Gate F posture). INDEPENDENT of the differential harness (subject-only; proxy-wasm conformance runs against envoy-go ONLY; no reference-Envoy cross-side comparison).

**AMEND-C5: the family roster is the 16 cpp-host UNIT-test files, NOT an ABI-conformance corpus.** The §11.5 scrape of `proxy-wasm-cpp-host@da3ce05d:test/` found 16 `*_test.cc` files (bytecode_util, endianness, exports, logging, null_vm, pairs_util, runtime, security, shared_data, shared_queue, signature_util, stop_iteration, vm_id_handle, wasm, wasm_vm + `fuzz/`) — the suite is engine/runtime UNIT tests, NOT a hostcall-by-hostcall ABI-conformance corpus. There is NO dedicated `http_call`/`metric`/`property`/`foreign_function`/`grpc`/`tick` test file at this pin (those surfaces ride along inside the `logging`/`runtime` drivers + the `test_data` plugin fixtures: abi_export.rs, callback.rs, clock.rs, env.rs, http_logging.cc, random.rs, stop_iteration.cc, trap.rs). This REFINES the BRAINSTORM Q7 / parent AMEND-A8 "10-of-16 hostcall families" framing to "10-of-16 cpp-host unit-test families re-expressed as Go-test sub-tests."

**10 PORT** (host-capability-aligned per 25.3 SPEC §8.4): logging, stop_iteration (header maps + continue/stop-iteration), shared_data (CAS), endianness (ABI value/buffer marshalling), exports (env/clock/random WASI), security (hostcall restriction), runtime (traps + mem-limit + host↔VM callback), wasm_vm (VM init/clone/memory), bytecode_util (custom-section + ABI-version parse), pairs_util (header-map pairs wire format). **6 DEFER** (with rationale): shared_queue (WasmService cross-VM queues + `proxy_on_queue_ready` — not implemented); signature_util (Ed25519 signed/remote code fetch — not implemented); wasm (thread-local WasmHandle cache + canary presupposes WasmService singleton model); vm_id_handle (cross-VM scoping substrate — defer with shared_queue/WasmService); null_vm (compiled-in NullVM — N/A for a Go host with no NullVM engine); fuzz (libFuzzer harnesses, not gtest). The 62.5% (10/16) numeric threshold HOLDS. Vendored bytecode/`test_data` fixtures ported to Go-test scaffolding under `families/<family_name>/` (driver shape settled at PLAN per D-25.3-P4). Phase-done gate = ALL 10 ported families PASS. Each family's subject-side assertion (counter increment, response code, body shape, log emission) proven LIVE via an explicit deliberate-break cycle per `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch` (the memo bit phase-23 fixture-0030 dead-vacuous assertions). The 6 deferred families' absence documented as forward-pointers in `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md §7.5` + `ENVOY_TARGET.md` + the 25.3 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT bundle.

### Decision

The `test/conformance/proxy-wasm/` conformance harness is a NEW Go-test package, materialized as an **in-process `go test` harness over vendored prebuilt `.wasm` blobs** — NO Docker, NO Rust-in-CI (D-25.3-P4). Each conformance guest is a vendored Rust crate (`sources/<crate>/` → `bytecode/<crate>.wasm`, built offline `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1 --offline`, SDK proxy-wasm-rust-sdk =0.2.4, exporting `proxy_abi_version_0_2_1`); the harness drives the guest through the existing exported `internal/wasm` RootVM / StreamContext / ABICallbacks / CompileModule surface and asserts host-observable behavior. The harness is INDEPENDENT of the differential harness (subject-only; no reference-Envoy cross-side comparison). It runs in CI per-commit via `go test ./test/conformance/proxy-wasm/...` (Gate F posture).

**10-of-16 cpp-host family port** (pin `proxy-wasm-cpp-host@da3ce05d`), per AMEND-C5 (the family roster is the 16 cpp-host UNIT-test files, NOT a hostcall-by-hostcall ABI corpus). PORTED (10): logging, stop_iteration, shared_data, endianness, exports, security, runtime, wasm_vm, bytecode_util, pairs_util. Each family registers a `run` func into `conformanceFamilies` via a test-scope `init()` (the production global stays an empty literal). Phase-done gate = ALL 10 families PASS; each family's host-observable assertion was proven LIVE via an explicit deliberate-break → FAIL → restore → PASS cycle per `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch` (all 10 cycles run + confirmed at Task 14). The 62.5% (10/16) numeric threshold HOLDS.

**6 DEFERRED families** (recorded as forward-pointers in `BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT.md §7.5` + `ENVOY_TARGET.md` + the 25.3 BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT bundle): **shared_queue** (WasmService cross-VM queues + `proxy_on_queue_ready` — not implemented), **signature_util** (Ed25519 signed/remote code fetch — not implemented), **wasm** (thread-local WasmHandle TLS-cache + canary presupposes the WasmService singleton model), **vm_id_handle** (cross-VM scoping substrate — defer with shared_queue/WasmService), **null_vm** (compiled-in NullVM — N/A for a Go host with no NullVM engine), **fuzz** (libFuzzer harnesses, not gtest).

### Consequences

- **Gate F is widened:** the 6-gate phase-done evidence now requires `go test ./test/conformance/proxy-wasm/...` → 10/10 GREEN in ADDITION to h2spec 53/53. Both are conformance gates under Gate F.
- **No production code modified by the conformance harness** (Task 14) — every family's host-observable behavior was assertable through the existing exported surface; no production bug surfaced from conformance (the 4 production bugs all came from the differential, not conformance).
- **Finding (NOT a bug):** the proxy-wasm-rust-sdk =0.2.4 `hostcalls::get_current_time()` PANICS (no graceful `Err` path) on a non-`Ok` host result, so a DENIED active hostcall surfaces to the guest as a wasm TRAP. The `security` family asserts the capability gate via the trap; this is SDK behavior, not an envoy-go defect (the host correctly returned the deny sentinel + correctly surfaced the resulting guest trap).
- **The 6 deferred families** are the §9-WASM-host-family forward-pointer roster; their absence is documented, not a regression. Re-evaluated when the WasmService singleton / cross-VM-queue substrate lands in a future §9 WASM-host phase.

## ADR-0213: NEW `internal/filter/network/` read-filter chain framework — L4 read-filter iteration-status protocol (`OnNewConnection`/`OnData` → `Continue`/`StopIteration`, two-value enum) + `ReadFilterCallbacks` (connection accessor + `ContinueReading()` + `DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket`) + connection-level read buffering on `StopIteration` + per-connection runtime context + single-goroutine-per-connection concurrency + read-filter-ONLY scope (write-filter deferred) + EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause for a future write-filter / connection-metadata-storage addition

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at phase-26 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LANDED at phase-26.1 IMPL Task 17 (this commit) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-30 (§Context anchor at the parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies landed at 26.1 IMPL Task 17, 2026-05-30, this commit).
**Doctrine:** Phase 26 §9 Network-filters-family row (FIRST). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline.
**Lands-in:** Phase 26.1 IMPL — `internal/filter/network/` materialized across IMPL Tasks 2-6 (skeleton + `Buffer` + `ReadFilterCallbacks`/`Connection`/`CloseType` + `Registry` + chain runner); echo/direct_response first consumers at Tasks 7-9; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies landed at the Task-17 atomic-docs commit.

### Context

ADR-0213 anchors the NEW `internal/filter/network/` read-filter chain framework — the L4 analogue of the phase-07.1 `internal/filter/http/` HTTP filter framework, and the FIRST new filter-category framework primitive since phase-07.1. At master tip the only network filters (`tcp_proxy` + HCM) are terminal-only, selected one-per-chain via a hardcoded `map[string]filterConstructor` in `internal/listener/manager.go:102` with a private `filterHandler { Handle(ctx, conn) }` interface (`manager.go:44-46`) — no iteration, no callbacks, no read/write-filter protocol, no extensible registration. ADR-0213 establishes the missing chain framework; ADR-0214 establishes its registry.

**Iteration-status protocol mirrors ADR-0038 at L4.** The `ReadFilter` interface is `OnNewConnection() Status` + `OnData(buf []byte, endStream bool) Status` returning a TWO-value `Status` enum (`Continue` / `StopIteration`). Per the §11.5 D5 empirical scrape against Envoy v1.37.2 `envoy/network/filter.h` + `source/common/network/filter_manager_impl.cc`, the network filter manager's `FilterStatus` enum has exactly two values (no `StopIterationAndBuffer`/`StopAllIteration` variants — unlike the HTTP chain's `FilterDataStatus`) because L4 buffering is CONNECTION-level, not filter-level. `OnNewConnection` is called eagerly per filter at connection accept (before any data), in registration order, stopping on `StopIteration` (upstream `initializeReadFilters()`); `OnData` is called with the connection read buffer when `length>0 || endStream`. On `StopIteration` the chain runner stops at the current filter and leaves undrained bytes in the connection read buffer; `ContinueReading()` resumes at the NEXT filter with the currently-available buffered bytes (upstream `onContinueReading(this, connection_)` resuming at `std::next(filter->entry())`). This is the byte-faithful iteration contract the runner mirrors.

**`ReadFilterCallbacks` shaped at 26.1 to need NO 26.3 revision (per parent SPEC §11.4 D4 SPEC-BLOCKING resolution + AMEND-A5).** The callbacks expose: a `Connection()` accessor (`Write([]byte, endStream)`, `Close(closeType)`, `LocalAddr()/RemoteAddr() net.Addr`, `RequestedServerName() string`, `DownstreamPrincipals() []string` — the L4 inputs the §11.3 D3 RBAC matcher subset needs), `ContinueReading()`, and `DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket`. The `DynamicMetadata()` accessor is shaped at 26.1 (returning the per-connection runtime context's `*dynamicmetadata.Bucket`, constructed via `dynamicmetadata.NewBucket()` at connection entry) even though only `rbac_network` (26.3) writes to it — this is exactly why D4 was SPEC-blocking: shaping the accessor now avoids a post-hoc 26.1 callbacks-API revision when 26.3 lands the storage. Mirrors the HTTP decoder/encoder callbacks' `DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket` at `internal/filter/http/callbacks.go:285,476`.

**Per-connection runtime context = the genuinely-NEW primitive (the L4 analogue of the HTTP chain's per-stream `FilterChain` state).** It owns the `*dynamicmetadata.Bucket` (lifetime = connection; `Reset()`+nil at close, mirroring `internal/filter/http/chain.go:314,676`) and is threaded into each filter's `ReadFilterCallbacks`. Unused by echo/direct_response at 26.1; consumed by rbac_network at 26.3.

**Read-filter-ONLY scope + write-filter deferral (per BRAINSTORM Q4).** Every near-term Network-family filter (`echo`, `direct_response`, `tcp_proxy`, `rbac`, `sni_cluster`) is a read filter; write filters (`onWrite` / `WriteFilter`) appear only in deferred protocol proxies. Building unexercised write-filter plumbing would violate the deliberate-break / every-surface-exercised discipline. ADR-0213 carries an EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE clause (mirrors phase-22.1 ADR-0188 + phase-25.1 ADR-0202) for a future write-filter addition.

**Single-goroutine-per-connection concurrency (ADR-0071 spirit).** The chain runner dispatches synchronously on the connection goroutine (`internal/listener/manager.go` `serveConnection`), consistent with the existing `Handle(ctx, conn)` model. Cross-goroutine async read-filter resume is deferred (parent SPEC §2.1).

**First consumers echo + direct_response (per §11.7 D7).** `echo` (`envoy.filters.network.echo.v3.Echo`, empty config) — `OnData` writes bytes back via `Connection().Write(buf, endStream)`, drains the buffer, returns `StopIteration`. `direct_response` (`envoy.extensions.filters.network.direct_response.v3.Config`, field `response` DataSource) — logic in `OnNewConnection` (not `OnData`): write the configured response with `endStream=true`, set response-code-details `DirectResponse`, close with `FlushWrite`, return `StopIteration`; no configurable delay in v1.37.2.

### Decision

The NEW `internal/filter/network/` read-filter chain framework lands at 26.1 with the following pinned shape (materialized + unit-tested across IMPL Tasks 2-6; first consumers echo/direct_response at Tasks 7-9):

1. **Two-value `Status` protocol.** `Status` is a TWO-value enum — `Continue` / `StopIteration` — and NOTHING ELSE. The HTTP-style per-filter buffer variant (`StopIterationAndBuffer` / `StopAllIteration`) is DELIBERATELY ABSENT because L4 buffering is CONNECTION-level (the read buffer is owned by the connection runtime, not per filter), confirmed by the §11.5 D5 scrape of Envoy v1.37.2 `envoy/network/filter.h` (the network `FilterStatus` enum has exactly two values vs the HTTP `FilterDataStatus`'s four).
2. **`ReadFilter` interface** = `OnNewConnection() Status` + `OnData(buf []byte, endStream bool) Status` + `SetReadFilterCallbacks(cb ReadFilterCallbacks)` + `OnDestroy()`. `OnNewConnection` is dispatched eagerly per filter at connection accept (registration order, stopping on `StopIteration`); `OnData` is dispatched when `length > 0 || endStream`.
3. **`ReadFilterCallbacks`** = `Connection() Connection` (the L4 accessor — `Write([]byte, endStream)`, `Close(CloseType)`, `LocalAddr()/RemoteAddr() net.Addr`, `RequestedServerName() string`, `DownstreamPrincipals() []string`) + `ContinueReading()` + `DynamicMetadata() *dynamicmetadata.Bucket`. The FULL Connection accessor surface (the §11.3 D3 RBAC matcher subset) + `DynamicMetadata()` are shaped at 26.1 so 26.3 `rbac_network` needs NO callbacks-API revision (this is exactly why D4 was SPEC-blocking). `CloseType` carries `FlushWrite` / `NoFlush` ONLY at 26.1 (the first consumers need no other variant).
4. **Connection-level buffering on `StopIteration`, with per-socket-read re-iteration semantics.** On `StopIteration` the runner stops at the current filter and leaves the undrained bytes in the connection read buffer. CRITICALLY there are TWO distinct halt behaviors: a terminal `OnData`-`StopIteration` stops the CURRENT pass only (it is NOT a sticky halt — the runner records the resume index and the NEXT socket read re-runs the data pass from the stopping filter, re-delivering the accumulated buffer, mirroring upstream `onRead` re-iteration); ONLY an `OnNewConnection`-`StopIteration` persists across reads (the sole cross-read-persistent halt, cleared by `ContinueReading()`). `ContinueReading()` resumes at the NEXT filter (`std::next(filter->entry())`). This split is load-bearing — `echo` returns `StopIteration` from EVERY `OnData` without ever `ContinueReading`, yet must echo every subsequent read (a single sticky-halt flag was a real bug found + fixed at IMPL Task 11).
5. **Single-goroutine-per-connection.** The runner dispatches synchronously on the connection goroutine (`internal/listener/manager.go serveNetworkChain` — renamed from `serveReadFilterChain` at the 26.2 dispatch unification, ADR-0215); no per-filter goroutine, no cross-goroutine async resume (ADR-0071 spirit at L4).
6. **Per-connection runtime context** owns the REUSED `*dynamicmetadata.Bucket` (`internal/dynamicmetadata/`; `NewBucket()` at connection entry, `Reset()`+nil at `OnDestroy` — mirroring the HTTP chain's per-stream lifecycle), threaded into each filter's callbacks. It also holds the `closeRequested` flag (driving the read-loop exit) and the response-code-details sink (below).
7. **Drainable `Buffer`** (`Append`/`Bytes`/`Len`/`Drain`, over-drain clamped) faithfully models upstream's `Buffer::Instance` drain semantics that `echo`'s write-back-then-drain depends on (D-P26.1-1 resolved in favor of the drainable buffer over a `[]byte`-with-consumed-count model).
8. **Read-filter-ONLY scope; write-filter DEFERRED with an EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE.** The `WriteFilter` / `onWrite` surface is NOT built at 26.1 (every near-term Network-family filter is a read filter; building unexercised write-filter plumbing violates the every-surface-exercised discipline). ADR-0213 carries an explicit API-revision allowance (mirrors phase-22.1 ADR-0188 + phase-25.1 ADR-0202) for a future write-filter addition AND a future connection-metadata-storage addition: `CloseType` may gain variants beyond `FlushWrite`/`NoFlush`, and the response-code-details sink (set-but-unread at 26.1) may gain a real reader.

### Consequences

- **The L4 read-filter framework exists** as the network-layer analogue of phase 07.1's HTTP framework — the first new filter-category primitive since 07.1. echo + direct_response are its first two consumers (Tasks 7-9); `tcp_proxy`/HCM migrate onto it at 26.2; `rbac_network` consumes `DynamicMetadata()` at 26.3.
- **The two-value `Status` + connection-level buffering** keep the L4 runner SIMPLER than the HTTP chain (no per-filter buffer state machine) at the cost of the non-obvious per-read re-iteration semantics (item 4) — which were the source of the one IMPL bug (the sticky-halt flag) and are now pinned + regression-tested (`TestChainEchoStyleMultipleReads`, the multi-write `0040` fixture).
- **The DynamicMetadata accessor is shaped-but-unwritten at 26.1** (set-but-unread Bucket; R5). This is the deliberate D4-resolution cost: a per-connection `*dynamicmetadata.Bucket` is constructed + threaded + Reset on every connection even though no 26.1 filter writes it — paying a small allocation now to avoid a 26.1→26.3 callbacks-API revision.
- **The response-code-details sink is set-but-unread (D-P26.1-5b).** direct_response sets `DirectResponse` on the per-connection runtime context's RCD sink for upstream parity + forward-consumer readiness; there is NO operator-visible surface at master tip (no L4 `streamInfo` equivalent), no fixture assertion. The API-revision allowance covers a future real reader.
- **Write-filter absence is an envoy-go-strict departure** recorded in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT `## Network filters` (joint divergence-window with the prior §9 rows); the API-revision allowance bounds the forward cost.
- **`FactoryCtx` was refined to carry `BaseDir`** (D-P26.1-2) — the parent SPEC §3.1 specified an empty struct, but direct_response's `filename` DataSource arm needs the boot-time base dir for byte-stable boot-reject parity; the `BaseDir string` field threads from `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` through the manager.

**Cross-references:** ADR-0214 (paired registry + boot-wiring ADR); ADR-0038 (HTTP iteration-status protocol — the L4 model); ADR-0071 (single-goroutine-per-stream concurrency — the per-connection spirit); ADR-0072 + ADR-0079 (freeze-after-boot registry discipline — mirrored by ADR-0214); ADR-0207 (per-stream `internal/filterstate/` — the per-stream sibling of the per-connection runtime context); ADR-0188 + ADR-0202 (the EXPLICIT API-REVISION ALLOWANCE precedent); phase-07.1 (the HTTP filter framework this mirrors); phase-26 parent SPEC §4.1 + §4.2 + §11.5 D5 + §11.7 D7 + AMEND-A5; provisional ADR-0217 (the connection-metadata sink whose storage the `DynamicMetadata()` accessor anticipates).

## ADR-0214: extensible freeze-after-boot threaded-constructor network-filter registry `*network.Registry` (mirrors ADR-0072 HTTPRegistry + ADR-0079 listener-filter registry; no package-global `init()`; late-`Register` panics; lock-free post-Freeze lookup; two-step factory) + `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot-wiring + 26.1 dual-dispatch (new read-filter chain path alongside the untouched terminal-filter path) + planned 26.2 hardcoded-registry retirement

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at phase-26 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LANDED at phase-26.1 IMPL Task 17 (this commit) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-30 (§Context anchor at the parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies landed at 26.1 IMPL Task 17, 2026-05-30, this commit).
**Doctrine:** Phase 26 §9 Network-filters-family row (FIRST). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. ADR-0059 stats-registry LBP-1 root.
**Lands-in:** Phase 26.1 IMPL — `internal/filter/network/registry.go` at Task 5; the `manager.go` dual-dispatch at Tasks 10-11; the `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` boot-wiring at Task 12; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies at the Task-17 atomic-docs commit.

### Context

ADR-0214 anchors the extensible network-filter registry that the ADR-0213 chain consumes, plus its boot-wiring and the 26.1 dual-dispatch strategy. It mirrors the project's established freeze-after-boot threaded-constructor registry discipline byte-for-byte.

**Registry shape = byte-identical discipline to `internal/listener/listenerfilter/registry.go:19-58` + `internal/filter/http/registry.go:17-110` (ADR-0072/0079).** `*network.Registry` carries `sync.RWMutex` + `byTypeURL map[string]NetworkFilterFactory` + `frozen atomic.Bool`. `Register(typeURL, factory)` panics if `frozen.Load()` ("registry frozen: cannot register %q post-boot") or on duplicate registration; `Lookup(typeURL)` takes `RLock` (lock-free in practice post-Freeze); `Freeze()` is idempotent (`frozen.Store(true)`); `KnownTypeURLs()` supplies error-message context. NO package-global `init()` — registration is explicit at boot. The two-step factory pattern (parse `typed_config` once at boot → per-connection instance factory) mirrors `listenerfilter/types.go:91-96`: `NetworkFilterFactory func(tc *anypb.Any, ctx FactoryCtx) (FilterInstanceFactory, error)` + `FilterInstanceFactory func() ReadFilter`.

**Boot-wiring in `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` (mirrors the HTTP + listener-filter registry wiring at `main.go:129-183,198-200`).** Construct `*network.Registry` → `Register(echo.TypeURL, echo.New)` + `Register(directresponse.TypeURL, directresponse.New)` → `Freeze()` BEFORE manager construction → thread as a NEW argument into `listener.NewManagerWithBaseDirAndAllowH2C(...)` (alongside the existing `httpReg` + `lfReg` arguments).

**26.1 dual-dispatch confines blast radius to NEW code (per BRAINSTORM §1.1.1(d) + parent SPEC §3.2 + D-P2).** At 26.1 the new read-filter chain dispatch is wired into `manager.go` as a NEW path ALONGSIDE the existing terminal-filter path: a filter chain whose `filters[0]` type_url resolves in the frozen `*network.Registry` dispatches via the new read-filter chain runner; a chain whose terminal filter is `tcp_proxy`/HCM keeps the EXISTING `buildTerminalFilter` (`manager.go:569`) + `Handle` (`manager.go:1005`) path UNTOUCHED. This keeps 26.1's blast radius confined to new code (`tcp_proxy`/HCM are not yet on the read-filter interface — that is 26.2's job). The hardcoded `filterRegistry`/`filterHandler`/`filterConstructor`/`buildTerminalFilter` are RETIRED at 26.2 (ADR-0215), when `tcp_proxy`/HCM migrate onto the read-filter interface and the dispatch unifies; back-compat is proven by the EXISTING `0000-tcp-echo` + TLS-TCP + HCM differential fixtures staying byte-exact green.

### Decision

The extensible network-filter registry + its boot-wiring + the 26.1 dual-dispatch land at 26.1 with the following pinned shape (registry at IMPL Task 5; dual-dispatch at Tasks 10-11; boot-wiring at Task 12):

1. **`*network.Registry` mirrors ADR-0072 HTTPRegistry + ADR-0079 listener-filter registry byte-for-byte.** It carries `sync.RWMutex` + `byTypeURL map[string]NetworkFilterFactory` + `frozen atomic.Bool`. `Register(typeURL, factory)` PANICS if frozen (`network: registry frozen: cannot register %q post-boot`) or on duplicate registration (`network: duplicate factory for %q`); `Lookup(typeURL)` takes `RLock` (lock-free in practice post-Freeze); `Freeze()` is idempotent (`frozen.Store(true)`); `KnownTypeURLs()` (insertion-sorted, mirroring `http/registry.go`) supplies error-message context. NO package-global `init()` — registration is explicit at boot. The TWO-STEP factory mirrors `listenerfilter/types.go`: `NetworkFilterFactory func(tc *anypb.Any, ctx FactoryCtx) (FilterInstanceFactory, error)` (parse `typed_config` ONCE at boot) + `FilterInstanceFactory func() ReadFilter` (allocate a fresh `ReadFilter` per connection).
2. **The new `netReg *network.Registry` ctor arg is threaded through the manager.** `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` constructs `netReg`, `Register`s `echo.TypeURL`/`directresponse.TypeURL`, `Freeze()`s it (after the `lfReg` block, before manager construction), and passes it as the NEW (11th) argument to `listener.NewManagerWithBaseDirAndAllowH2C(...)` (alongside the existing `httpReg` + `lfReg`). The thinner ctor variants + all admin/manager_test callers pass `nil` (which makes the dual-dispatch inert — see item 3).
3. **Build-time dual-dispatch.** At chain-build time (`manager.go buildTerminalFilter` call sites), a pre-check: the NEW read-filter chain path is taken IFF `netReg != nil` AND `filters[0]`'s type_url resolves in `netReg` (and EVERY filter in the chain resolves at boot); otherwise the EXISTING `tcp_proxy`/HCM terminal path runs UNTOUCHED. The chain's `chainInfo.netChainFactory func() []network.ReadFilter` produces fresh filter instances per connection; `serveConnection`'s step-7 has a dual branch (new `serveReadFilterChain` read loop vs the existing `Handle`). When `netReg == nil` the pre-check is fully skipped — R4 back-compat is intrinsic + byte-identical, proven by the existing `0000-tcp-echo` + `0002-tls-tcp` + HCM differential fixtures staying byte-exact green.
4. **`network-filter-mixed-chain-unsupported` boot-reject for partial resolution.** A chain whose `filters[0]` resolves in `netReg` but whose `filters[1..]` do NOT all resolve (a new-path chain mixing echo/direct_response with `tcp_proxy`/HCM) is REJECTED at boot. This is an envoy-go-strict 26.1-only transitional reject (upstream supports mixed chains), unit-test-only (no cross-side fixture), LIFTED at 26.2.
5. **Planned 26.2 hardcoded-registry retirement.** The hardcoded `filterRegistry` map + `filterHandler`/`filterConstructor` types + `buildTerminalFilter` in `manager.go` are RETIRED at 26.2 (provisional ADR-0215), when `tcp_proxy`/HCM migrate onto the read-filter interface and the dispatch unifies through `*network.Registry` (the mixed-chain reject is lifted then).

### Consequences

- **The registry discipline is now established at L4** — the THIRD freeze-after-boot threaded-constructor registry (after ADR-0072 HTTPRegistry + ADR-0079 listener-filter registry), with zero new structural invention (faithful mirror; verified by `registry_test.go` mirroring `listenerfilter/registry_test.go`: freeze / late-Register-panic / duplicate-panic / lock-free-lookup).
- **26.1's blast radius is confined to NEW code.** The dual-dispatch leaves the load-bearing `tcp_proxy`/HCM path byte-identical; the new path only activates for chains leading with a registered network filter (echo/direct_response). The `nil`-`netReg` thinner variants keep the dispatch inert outside the real binary until Task 12 wires it.
- **`FactoryCtx.BaseDir` refinement (D-P26.1-2).** The parent SPEC §3.1 `FactoryCtx` was an empty struct; the registry's `NetworkFilterFactory` signature carries `FactoryCtx` so direct_response's `filename` DataSource arm resolves relative to the bootstrap base dir at boot (threaded `main.go` → manager → factory). Recorded here as the registry-surface consequence of the ADR-0213 framework refinement.
- **echo TypeURL `extensions.` correction (empirical, 26.1 IMPL).** The boot-wiring `netReg.Register(echo.TypeURL, ...)` surfaced that the SPEC/PLAN-pinned echo type URL `type.googleapis.com/envoy.filters.network.echo.v3.Echo` is WRONG — the actual go-control-plane v1.32.4 proto full-name is `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.echo.v3.Echo` (WITH `extensions.`; verified via `proto.MessageName`, the boot smoke, and fixture 0040 against upstream v1.37.2 — without it the binary cannot boot an echo config). `echo.TypeURL` was corrected; the SPEC §3.6/§4.1 + BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT echo subsection were corrected in-place at Task 17. direct_response's URL already carried `extensions.` and was correct. The echo + direct_response extension protos were also added to `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`'s blank-import block (per the cors precedent) to guarantee `@type` resolution.
- **The 26.2 unification is set up but not done.** The dual-dispatch is deliberately transitional; ADR-0215 (26.2) retires the hardcoded path. Until then the two dispatch paths coexist with the mixed-chain reject as the explicit boundary.

**Cross-references:** ADR-0213 (paired framework ADR — the chain the registry feeds); ADR-0072 (HTTPRegistry freeze-after-boot — the direct model); ADR-0079 (listener-filter registry + two-step factory — the closest structural analogue); ADR-0059 (stats-registry LBP-1 freeze-after-boot root); provisional ADR-0215 (the 26.2 hardcoded-registry retirement + dispatch unification this dual-dispatch plans for); phase-26 parent SPEC §4.1 + §3.2 + §11.8 D8 + D-P2.
