## ADR-0219: the connection-scoped upstream-cluster-override seam — a NARROW typed per-connection override on the `chainRuntime` (the envoy-go stand-in for Envoy's `PerConnectionCluster` filter-state key `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster`) written via a `SetUpstreamCluster` accessor ON `ReadFilterCallbacks` + threaded to the terminal filter via the call `ctx` + `tcp_proxy` made per-connection-cluster-resolving (retain `*cluster.Manager` + boot-resolved default; override-then-fallback at `Handle`; unknown-cluster→downstream-close) — at byte-exact back-compat (the existing `tcp_proxy` fixtures stay green) + NO general connection-scoped filter-state primitive (Q2/YAGNI; API-revision allowance)

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at the phase-27 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LAND at phase-27 IMPL per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-31 (§Context anchor at the 27 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies at the 27 IMPL atomic-docs commit).
**Doctrine:** Phase 27 §9 Network-filters-family row (the SECOND, flat row — ADR-0106). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. ADR-0004 empirical-pin-against-reference-Envoy (v1.37.2). ADR-0045 split-gate (single phase). ADR-0052 atomic-landing + six-gate. ADR-0072 registration-order-neutral. ADR-0213 (the read-filter chain framework + the API-revision-allowance lineage). ADR-0215 (the `TerminalFilter` seam + `prefixConn` mixed-chain handover). Project memory `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` (the OnNewConnection-Continue constraint) + `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`.
**Lands-in:** Phase 27 IMPL — `internal/filter/network/chain.go` (the `upstreamClusterOverride` field + `handleTerminal` ctx-threading + the concrete `SetUpstreamCluster`), `internal/filter/network/callbacks.go` (the `SetUpstreamCluster` interface method), `internal/filter/network/` (the `UpstreamClusterOverride` context accessor), `internal/filter/tcpproxy/filter.go` (retain manager + default; per-connection resolution at `Handle`; unknown→close); the §Decision/§Consequences bodies at the 27 IMPL atomic-docs commit.

### Context

ADR-0219 anchors the Network-filters family's first **routing-control** primitive: a connection-scoped channel by which a read filter publishes the upstream cluster the terminal `tcp_proxy` should dispatch to. It is the seam the phase-26 BRAINSTORM §8 named as `sni_cluster`'s blocker ("a connection-level cluster-override seam that rbac does not need"), now built. It is the BRAINSTORM Q2 ("narrow typed per-connection override") decision and the SPEC §3 anchor. The empirical mechanism it mirrors (ADR-0004, v1.37.2): Envoy's `sni_cluster` writes a `TcpProxy::PerConnectionCluster` object into `connection().streamInfo().filterState()` under the key `"envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster"` (`StateType::Mutable`, `LifeSpan::Connection`), and `tcp_proxy`'s `Config::getRegularRouteFromEntries` reads that key FIRST — overriding the configured `cluster:`/`default_route_` when present, falling through to the configured cluster when absent (SPEC §11 D27-2/D27-5).

**The narrow typed shape (Q2 — NOT a general filter-state primitive).** The `chainRuntime` (`chain.go:127`) gains ONE field `upstreamClusterOverride string` (zero value `""` = no override). This is the deliberate extract-at-Nth-consumer / YAGNI shape the project entrenched (the `internal/rbac/` engine extracted only at its SECOND consumer in 26.3; `internal/dynamicmetadata/` storage landed only at its first writer): a single typed value for the one consumer (`sni_cluster`), NOT a general string-keyed connection-scoped filter-state map. It generalizes to a real filter-state primitive if/when a SECOND override-publishing consumer appears (API-revision allowance — the ADR-0213/0215 lineage). Reusing the ADR-0217 dynamic-metadata bucket was REJECTED: Envoy uses filter-state (control) NOT dynamic-metadata (observability) for this override; conflating them diverges from upstream semantics while still needing the same terminal-threading work.

**The writer accessor — ON the `ReadFilterCallbacks` interface (not the `SetResponseCodeDetails` type-assert).** `SetUpstreamCluster(name string)` is added to the `ReadFilterCallbacks` interface (`callbacks.go:16`), implemented by the concrete `*callbacks`. This contrasts the `rcd` sink (`chain.go:351`, deliberately OFF the interface, type-assert-reached, because it has "no operator-visible surface") and follows the `DynamicMetadata()` precedent (`callbacks.go:25`, ON the interface as an essential per-connection channel). Rationale: the override is the ESSENTIAL function of `sni_cluster` (not a best-effort detail), so it earns compile-time safety (a drifting impl is a build error, not a silent runtime no-op) and forces every test double to implement it (a type-assert sink would silently no-op against a mock that omits it — a footgun for the filter whose entire job is the write). The rejected type-assert alternative is recorded here for the IMPL-body completion.

**The terminal-reader threading — via the call `ctx` (not a signature change, not a terminal-side accessor).** The `TerminalFilter.Handle(ctx, net.Conn)` signature (`terminal.go:42`) is FIXED and SHARED by HCM — it must not change for a `tcp_proxy`-only feature. `handleTerminal` (`chain.go:209`) wraps the call `ctx` with an unexported context key carrying the override ONLY when one is set, and `tcp_proxy.Handle` reads it via an exported `network.UpstreamClusterOverride(ctx) (string, bool)`. Rationale: (a) no HCM/interface ripple; (b) `tcp_proxy`'s terminal `*Filter` is a SHARED boot instance (`NewNetworkFactory`, `filter.go:81`) with no per-connection handle, so `ctx`+`conn` are its only per-connection inputs; (c) `context.Value` is Go's idiomatic per-call out-of-band channel, naturally connection-scoped here. HCM ignores the override (an `sni_cluster`→HCM chain is not a meaningful upstream combination) — harmless.

**`tcp_proxy` per-connection resolution + the unknown-cluster close.** `tcp_proxy`'s `Filter` retains `*cluster.Manager` + the boot-resolved `defaultCluster` (today it stores only the resolved cluster); `NewFilter`'s boot-time parse + configured-cluster resolution + the byte-stable `tcpproxy: cluster %q not found` / `weighted_clusters` rejects are UNCHANGED. At `Handle`: `override present & non-empty → cm.Get(override)` (miss → close the downstream conn, zero bytes) `else → defaultCluster`. The unknown-cluster close mirrors Envoy's `downstream_cx_no_route` + `NoFlush` close behaviorally (downstream sees a zero-byte close); the `tcp.<stat_prefix>.downstream_cx_no_route` counter is NOT mirrored (envoy-go's `tcp_proxy` emits no `downstream_cx_*` family — a pre-existing coverage boundary, SPEC §7.2). `weighted_clusters` is moot — envoy-go rejects it at parse, keeping it on the single-cluster path where Envoy honors the override (SPEC §1.1 F-WEIGHTED). Back-compat: no override → `defaultCluster` → byte-exact with master tip (the existing `tcp_proxy` fixtures are the regression gate — deliberate-break discipline).

### Decision

The connection-scoped upstream-cluster-override seam lands at phase 27 IMPL as built across Tasks 2-4. The as-built shape:

1. **The narrow typed override field (Q2 — NOT a general filter-state primitive).** `chainRuntime` (`internal/filter/network/chain.go`) gains ONE field `upstreamClusterOverride string` (zero value `""` = no override). This is the deliberate extract-at-Nth-consumer / YAGNI shape: a single typed value for the one consumer (`sni_cluster`), NOT a general string-keyed connection-scoped filter-state map. `OnDestroy` need not reset it (the runtime is per-connection, discarded after dispatch). It generalizes to a real filter-state primitive if/when a SECOND override-publishing consumer appears (API-revision allowance — the ADR-0213/0215 lineage). Reusing the ADR-0217 dynamic-metadata bucket was REJECTED: Envoy uses filter-state (control) NOT dynamic-metadata (observability) for this override; conflating them diverges from upstream semantics while still needing the same terminal-threading work.
2. **The writer accessor — ON the `ReadFilterCallbacks` interface (not the `SetResponseCodeDetails` type-assert).** `SetUpstreamCluster(name string)` is added to the `ReadFilterCallbacks` interface (`callbacks.go`), implemented by the concrete `*callbacks` (`func (c *callbacks) SetUpstreamCluster(name string) { c.rt.upstreamClusterOverride = name }`). This contrasts the `rcd` sink (deliberately OFF the interface, type-assert-reached, because it has "no operator-visible surface") and follows the `DynamicMetadata()` precedent (ON the interface as an essential per-connection channel). Rationale: the override is the ESSENTIAL function of `sni_cluster` (not a best-effort detail), so it earns compile-time safety (a drifting impl is a build error, not a silent runtime no-op) and forces every test double to implement it (a type-assert sink would silently no-op against a mock that omits it — a footgun for the filter whose entire job is the write). The REJECTED type-assert alternative: an `interface{ SetUpstreamCluster(string) }` type-assertion in `handleTerminal` against the concrete callbacks — rejected for the silent-no-op footgun above. At IMPL the three out-of-package `fakeCallbacks` doubles (`rbac`/`directresponse`/`echo` tests) each gained a no-op `SetUpstreamCluster` (compile-forced — exactly the safety the on-interface placement buys).
3. **The terminal-reader threading — via the call `ctx` (not a signature change, not a terminal-side accessor).** A NEW `internal/filter/network/upstreamcluster.go` carries an unexported `upstreamClusterKey struct{}` ctx key, an unexported `withUpstreamClusterOverride(ctx, override) context.Context` (framework-internal — only `handleTerminal` calls it), and an exported `UpstreamClusterOverride(ctx) (string, bool)` (the cross-package `tcp_proxy` reader). `handleTerminal` (`chain.go`) wraps the call `ctx` with the key carrying the override ONLY when one is set, before `rt.terminal.Handle(ctx, conn)`. The `TerminalFilter.Handle(ctx, net.Conn)` signature (`terminal.go`) is UNCHANGED. The REJECTED alternatives: (a) a signature change on `Handle` — ripples to HCM + the `TerminalFilter` interface for a `tcp_proxy`-only feature; (b) a terminal-side callbacks accessor — `tcp_proxy`'s terminal `*Filter` is a SHARED boot instance (`NewNetworkFactory` yields one `*Filter` per chain) with no per-connection handle, so `ctx`+`conn` are its only per-connection inputs. `context.Value` is Go's idiomatic per-call out-of-band channel, naturally connection-scoped here. HCM ignores the override (an `sni_cluster`→HCM chain is not a meaningful upstream combination) — harmless.
4. **`tcp_proxy` per-connection resolution (retain manager + default; unknown→close).** The `Filter` struct's `cluster *cluster.Cluster` is replaced by `cm *cluster.Manager` + `defaultCluster *cluster.Cluster` (`statPrefix`/`dm` unchanged); `NewFilter`'s boot-time parse + the configured-cluster resolution (stored as `defaultCluster`) + the byte-stable `tcpproxy: cluster %q not found` / `weighted_clusters` rejects are UNCHANGED. At `Handle` (before the Dial): `eff := f.defaultCluster`; if `network.UpstreamClusterOverride(ctx)` returns `(override, true)` with `override != ""`, then `c, found := f.cm.Get(override)` — found → `eff = c`; MISS → `log.Printf("tcpproxy: per-connection override cluster %q not found", override)` + `return` (the deferred `downstream.Close()` yields a zero-byte close). The two `f.cluster` references in `Handle` (`Dial` + `Name()`) became `eff.Dial`/`eff.Name()`. Precedence: override present & non-empty → override cluster (override==configured resolves identically — no special case); absent/empty → `defaultCluster`. The `OnNewConnection` `sni != ""` guard and the `Handle` `override != ""` guard are redundant-by-design (defense-in-depth — both kept deliberately).
5. **The `downstream_cx_no_route`-unmirrored decision (D27-4 / §7.2).** Envoy increments `tcp.<stat_prefix>.downstream_cx_no_route` on the unknown-override path; envoy-go's `tcp_proxy` emits NO `downstream_cx_*` counters at all (a pre-existing gap). Adding a single `downstream_cx_no_route` only on the override-miss path would be an inconsistent partial of an absent family — DEFERRED (the whole family; +0). `downstream_cx_no_route` is recorded as a known-unmirrored upstream counter (a coverage boundary NOT introduced by phase 27). The unknown-override behavior IS proven cross-side byte-exact (fixture `0045-sni-cluster` arm 3); the stat absence is invisible to a response-body differential. Project stat surface stays **136** (+0).
6. **Back-compat-via-existing-fixtures discipline (the regression gate).** No override → `defaultCluster` → byte-exact with master tip. Proven by: a `tcpproxy/filter_test.go` back-compat sentinel (`TestHandle_NoOverrideUsesDefaultCluster` — a two-cluster manager, `Handle` with `context.Background()` / no override, asserts the configured cluster's sentinel) AND the existing `tcp_proxy` differential fixtures (`0000`/`0001`/`0002` + the 26.x network fixtures) staying byte-exact green (8/8 re-verified at Task 8). These are the strongest regression proof of the per-connection-resolution change (deliberate-break discipline).
7. **No general primitive / API-revision allowance.** The narrow typed override is the envoy-go stand-in for Envoy's `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster` filter-state key; there is NO general connection-scoped filter-state primitive at phase 27 (Q2/YAGNI). It generalizes if/when a SECOND override-publishing consumer appears (the ADR-0213/0215 API-revision-allowance lineage).

### Consequences

- **The Network-filters family has its first routing-control primitive.** A read filter can now publish the upstream cluster the terminal `tcp_proxy` dispatches to — the seam the phase-26 BRAINSTORM §8 named as `sni_cluster`'s blocker is built (ADR-0220 is its first consumer). The §9 Network-filters family STAYS OPEN at 27 phase-done (5 candidates remain: redis/mongo/kafka_broker/thrift/zookeeper).
- **`tcp_proxy` is now per-connection-cluster-resolving.** Cluster selection moved from boot-once to per-`Handle`; the no-override path is byte-exact with master tip (proven by the back-compat sentinel + the existing fixtures), so the change is non-regressive. `tcp_proxy` now retains its `*cluster.Manager` for the lifetime of the chain (a slightly larger per-`Filter` footprint than the single boot-resolved cluster — negligible; the manager is a shared boot singleton).
- **The on-interface `SetUpstreamCluster` is compile-enforced across all callbacks consumers.** A drifting concrete impl or a test double that omits it is a build error, not a silent runtime no-op — the safety the on-interface placement was chosen for (it forced no-op stubs into the three existing out-of-package `fakeCallbacks` doubles at IMPL).
- **The override is threaded out-of-band on the call `ctx`** — `TerminalFilter.Handle`'s signature (shared with HCM) is untouched, so HCM and any future terminal filter are unaffected. HCM ignores the override (harmless). A future terminal filter that wants to honor the override reads `network.UpstreamClusterOverride(ctx)` — the same path `tcp_proxy` uses.
- **`downstream_cx_no_route` (and the wider `downstream_cx_*` family) is a known-unmirrored upstream counter.** Recorded in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT (the `tcp_proxy per-connection cluster resolution — 27 amendment` block) + here. A future phase that mirrors the `downstream_cx_*` family would close this boundary and add the counter on the override-miss path in lockstep.
- **Counts at 27 phase-done:** stat surface stays **136** (+0); fixtures 46 → 47 (the `0045-sni-cluster` cross-side dir); fuzzers stay **36** (+0). DECISIONS.md tail STAYS ADR-0220 (next-free ADR-0221 — no new number; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies landed in place per ADR-0044).

**Cross-references:** ADR-0220 (the `sni_cluster` filter — the first and only consumer of this seam); ADR-0213 (the read-filter chain framework + the `ReadFilterCallbacks`/`DynamicMetadata()`/`SetResponseCodeDetails` sinks + the API-revision-allowance lineage); ADR-0215 (the `network.TerminalFilter` `Handle(ctx, conn)` seam this threads the override through + the shared-boot-instance constraint); ADR-0217 (the dynamic-metadata bucket whose REUSE for this override was rejected — control vs observability); ADR-0080 (byte-stable PARSE-REJECT — the `tcpproxy:` rejects stay byte-stable); ADR-0072 (registration-order-neutral); ADR-0004 (the empirical pin against Envoy v1.37.2 — `PerConnectionCluster` key `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster`, `getRegularRouteFromEntries` reads-first, `downstream_cx_no_route` + `NoFlush` close); ADR-0044 (§Context-at-SPEC / §Decision+§Consequences-at-IMPL); project memory `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` + `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`; SPEC §3 / §7.2 / §11 (D27-2/D27-3/D27-4/D27-5) + the PLAN Tasks 2-4.

## ADR-0220: NEW `sni_cluster` filter (`envoy.extensions.filters.network.sni_cluster.v3.SniCluster`, an EMPTY proto) — a config-less L4 read-filter that in `OnNewConnection` reads the TLS SNI (`Connection.RequestedServerName()`) and publishes it VERBATIM as the per-connection upstream-cluster-override (ADR-0219) then returns `Continue` (no sticky halt); no-op `OnData`/`OnDestroy`; the 6th `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` registration; empty/absent-SNI→configured-cluster fallback + unknown-cluster→connection-close parity; the SECOND production mixed read→terminal chain

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at the phase-27 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LAND at phase-27 IMPL per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-05-31 (§Context anchor at the 27 SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies at the 27 IMPL atomic-docs commit).
**Doctrine:** Phase 27 §9 Network-filters-family row (the SECOND, flat row — ADR-0106). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. ADR-0004 empirical-pin (v1.37.2). ADR-0079 two-step factory. ADR-0080 byte-stable wording. ADR-0052 atomic-landing + six-gate. ADR-0072 registration-order-neutral. Project memory `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` (the OnNewConnection-Continue constraint) + `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions` (the `proto.MessageName` TypeURL verification) + `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint` + `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`.
**Lands-in:** Phase 27 IMPL — NEW `internal/filter/network/snicluster/` package (config-less parse + `OnNewConnection` SNI→override + no-op `OnData`/`OnDestroy`); the 6th `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` registration; the `0045-sni-cluster` 3-arm cross-side fixture; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies at the 27 IMPL atomic-docs commit.

### Context

ADR-0220 anchors `sni_cluster` — the Network-filters family's fourth concrete filter and its first routing-steering read-filter — at full upstream parity. It is the BRAINSTORM Q1 ("full upstream parity, single phase") + Q3 ("all three arms cross-side") decision and the SPEC §4 anchor. The empirical pins (ADR-0004, v1.37.2; SPEC §11): `sni_cluster.cc::onNewConnection()` reads `requestedServerName()`, and when the SNI is non-empty `setData`s the `PerConnectionCluster` (key `envoy.tcp_proxy.cluster`) with the SNI **verbatim** (`Mutable`/`Connection`), returning `FilterStatus::Continue` (always); `onData()` is a no-op `Continue` (D27-2/D27-6). The `SniCluster` proto is field-less; its `@type` is `type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.sni_cluster.v3.SniCluster` (verified via `proto.MessageName`, the `extensions.` segment — D27-1).

**The filter (config-less; the `echo` template).** NEW `internal/filter/network/snicluster/` (single-token sub-package, the `echo`/`directresponse` precedent). `TypeURL` via `proto.MessageName(&snicluster.SniCluster{})` (NOT hand-typed — `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`). `New` accepts an empty/absent `typed_config` (mirrors `echo.New`; a malformed `Any` surfaces `sni_cluster: invalid typed_config: %w`). In `OnNewConnection`: `if sni := cb.Connection().RequestedServerName(); sni != "" { cb.SetUpstreamCluster(sni) }; return Continue`. The verbatim SNI is the override (no transform — D27-2). It MUST return `Continue`, not `StopIteration` — an `OnNewConnection` `StopIteration` sets the sticky `connHalted` flag that blocks ALL `OnData` (`reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts`; `chain.go:233`); Envoy's filter also returns `Continue`, so parity and the framework constraint coincide. `OnData` returns `Continue` (pass-through — does NOT drain), making `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]` a mixed read→terminal chain. Registered as the 6th built-in (`builtins.RegisterBuiltins`; config-less → no `Deps`).

**The three behavior arms (Q3; the `0045-sni-cluster` cross-side fixture).** (1) SNI naming an existing cluster → routed to that backend (distinct sentinel); (2) empty/absent SNI → no override → `tcp_proxy`'s configured fallback cluster (F-RESOLVE); (3) SNI naming an unknown cluster → override miss → downstream close, zero bytes (F-NOROUTE). All three cross-side byte-exact via the differential runner's body comparison (one cross-side dir — no boot-reject arm, config-less; `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint`). TLS required (SNI is populated by the TLS handshake / tls_inspector — the `ConnFacts.ServerName` path).

**The SECOND production mixed read→terminal chain (R-MIXED-2).** `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]`: `sni_cluster` `Continue`s from `OnNewConnection`, the 26.2 chain runner's `TerminalReady()` fires, `HandleTerminal` threads the override via ctx (ADR-0219) to `tcp_proxy.Handle`. It is the first config-less read filter that `Continue`s to a terminal (26.3 `rbac_network` was the first mixed chain, but it decides in `OnData`; `sni_cluster` publishes in `OnNewConnection`). No stats (upstream parity — SPEC §7.1); no per-route surface (D27-7); no boot-reject (config-less — §6.1); fuzzer DEFERRED (echo-parity — SPEC §10).

### Decision

`sni_cluster` (`internal/filter/network/snicluster/`) lands config-less at full upstream parity as the sole consumer of the ADR-0219 override seam. The as-built shape (Tasks 5-7):

1. **TypeURL via `proto.MessageName` (NOT hand-typed).** `const TypeURL = "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.sni_cluster.v3.SniCluster"`, pinned by a test against `"type.googleapis.com/" + proto.MessageName(&snicluster.SniCluster{})` (the network-filter type URLs carry the `extensions.` segment — `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`; deriving from the descriptor is the only safe source). The `SniCluster` proto is field-less (D27-1).
2. **Config-less parse (the `echo` template).** `New(tc *anypb.Any, _ network.FactoryCtx) (network.FilterInstanceFactory, error)` accepts an empty/absent `typed_config`; if `len(tc.GetValue()) > 0` it `UnmarshalTo(&snicluster.SniCluster{})` (an empty message — any bytes that unmarshal are accepted; a malformed `Any` surfaces `sni_cluster: invalid typed_config: %w`, the `echo.New` shape). Returns `func() network.NetworkFilter { return &filter{} }`. The filter struct embeds `network.Marker` + holds `cb network.ReadFilterCallbacks`.
3. **`OnNewConnection` SNI-verbatim→override + `Continue`.** `if sni := f.cb.Connection().RequestedServerName(); sni != "" { f.cb.SetUpstreamCluster(sni) }; return network.Continue`. The verbatim SNI is the override (no transform — D27-2). It MUST return `Continue`, not `StopIteration` — an `OnNewConnection` `StopIteration` sets the sticky `connHalted` flag that blocks ALL `OnData` (`reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts`); Envoy's filter also returns `Continue`, so parity and the framework constraint coincide. Empty/absent SNI → no override set → `tcp_proxy` uses its configured cluster (fallback).
4. **No-op `OnData`/`OnDestroy`.** `OnData(*network.Buffer, bool) network.Status { return network.Continue }` — pass-through (NOT a drain, NOT a halt), so the inspected bytes flow to the terminal (`echo` halts/drains; `sni_cluster` does not). `SetReadFilterCallbacks(cb)` stores cb; `OnDestroy()` is a no-op. This makes `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]` a mixed read→terminal chain.
5. **6th built-in registration.** `reg.Register(snicluster.TypeURL, snicluster.New)` is the 6th `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` entry (no `Deps` — config-less, no boot singletons, like `echo`/`direct_response`). D27-S2 RESOLVED: `cmd/envoy-go/main.go` delegates wholly to `RegisterBuiltins` (single insertion point — no parallel edit; registration order is behavior-neutral per ADR-0072). The package doc + `RegisterBuiltins` doc were updated 5→6 built-ins.
6. **The bootstrap blank-import (the `echo` precedent).** `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go` gained `_ "github.com/envoyproxy/go-control-plane/envoy/extensions/filters/network/sni_cluster/v3"` so protojson round-trips a bootstrap carrying a `sni_cluster` `typed_config` (the `bootstrap.Load` path does NOT import `builtins`, so the transitively-registered path via the filter package does not protect bootstrap parsing). Mirrors the echo/direct_response pattern; documented in PROGRESS (ADR-0016 amendment policy — not a new ADR).
7. **The three behavior arms + the differential fixture (Q3; `0045-sni-cluster`).** ONE cross-side TLS dir (no boot-reject arm — config-less; `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint`): (1) SNI `foo.example.com` → routed to cluster `foo.example.com` (distinct backend sentinel); (2) empty/absent SNI → `tcp_proxy`'s configured `c_fallback` cluster (F-RESOLVE); (3) SNI `unknown.example.com` (no such cluster) → override miss → downstream close, zero bytes (F-NOROUTE). Single TLS listener, one `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]` filter chain, a single multi-SAN server cert. The route/fallback arms are made NON-VACUOUS by a `fixture.DistributionAsserter` on the driver: per-backend accept counts `[1, 1]` (FOO backend + FALLBACK backend; the unknown-close arm dials neither). A broken `SetUpstreamCluster` (everything routed to `c_fallback`) gives `[0, 2]` and the asserter FIRES — proven by a liveness-break at IMPL (commenting out `SetUpstreamCluster` failed both the byte-stream comparison AND the distribution assertion, then restored).
8. **The `closeOK` close-parity normalization (D27-S3).** On the unknown-cluster arm, reference Envoy closes PRE-TLS-handshake (tls_inspector peeks the SNI and the proxy aborts before the ServerHello), whereas envoy-go extracts the SNI from the COMPLETED `*tls.Conn` handshake (`ConnFacts.ServerName`), then closes POST-`tcp_proxy.Handle`. Both produce ZERO application bytes. The driver's `tlsDial` accepts a `closeOK` flag that treats a TLS-handshake-failure (EOF) as zero application bytes — both sides normalize to `closed_no_bytes`. The RST-vs-FIN distinction is out of scope (the body differential does not observe it).
9. **The SECOND production mixed read→terminal chain (R-MIXED-2).** `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]`: `sni_cluster` `Continue`s from `OnNewConnection`, the 26.2 chain runner's `TerminalReady()` fires, `HandleTerminal` threads the override via ctx (ADR-0219) to `tcp_proxy.Handle`. The first config-less read filter that `Continue`s to a terminal (26.3 `rbac_network` was the first mixed chain, but it decides in `OnData`; `sni_cluster` publishes in `OnNewConnection`). The end-to-end override-routes / unknown-close integration tests are HOMED in the `builtins` package test — the only place that imports BOTH `network` + `tcpproxy` without an import cycle, driving the full seam via `NewChainRuntime`→`OnNewConnection`→`OnData`→`HandleTerminal`.

### Consequences

- **The Network-filters family has its first routing-steering read-filter at full upstream parity.** SNI→cluster steering, the empty-SNI fallback, and the unknown-cluster close are all byte-faithful to upstream — proven cross-side by the three `0045-sni-cluster` arms. The §9 Network-filters family STAYS OPEN at 27 phase-done (5 candidates remain: redis/mongo/kafka_broker/thrift/zookeeper).
- **The ADR-0219 override seam is now production-proven.** ADR-0219's `SetUpstreamCluster`/ctx-threaded override was shaped for exactly this consumer; `sni_cluster` is that consumer (R-OVERRIDE + R-SNI ratified). The seam stays narrow (one typed value) until a SECOND override-publishing consumer appears (API-revision allowance).
- **`sni_cluster` adds NO stats and NO per-route surface (upstream parity).** Project stat surface stays **136** (+0). No `typed_per_filter_config` (network filters have none — D27-7).
- **The route/fallback arms are protected against silent vacuity by the `DistributionAsserter`.** Identical echo backends would otherwise make both arms produce `echo_ok` regardless of which cluster was dialed; the per-backend accept-count distribution `[1, 1]` makes a broken override FIRE — a known differential-vacuity trap (`reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`) closed at IMPL with a recorded liveness-break.
- **A known close-lifecycle divergence is normalized, not hidden (D27-S3).** Reference closes pre-handshake; envoy-go post-handshake. Both yield zero application bytes; the `closeOK` normalization is documented in the driver godoc + here. A test needing the RST-vs-FIN distinction is out of scope (the body differential does not observe it).
- **Counts at 27 phase-done:** fixtures 46 → 47 (`0045-sni-cluster`); stat surface stays **136** (+0); fuzzers stay **36** (+0 — DEFERRED per D27-S4: `sni_cluster`'s parse is byte-identical to `echo`, which carries no dedicated fuzzer). DECISIONS.md tail STAYS ADR-0220 (next-free ADR-0221 — no new number; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies landed in place per ADR-0044).

**Cross-references:** ADR-0219 (the connection-scoped upstream-cluster-override seam `sni_cluster` is the sole consumer of — the `SetUpstreamCluster` writer + the ctx-threaded reader + `tcp_proxy` per-connection resolution); ADR-0213 (the read-filter chain framework + the `ReadFilterCallbacks`/`Connection().RequestedServerName()` accessors + the `Marker` embed); ADR-0214 (the freeze-after-boot `*network.Registry` + `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` this is the 6th entry of); ADR-0215 (the `network.TerminalFilter` seam + the `prefixConn` mixed-chain handover); ADR-0079 (the two-step factory `New` shape); ADR-0080 (byte-stable `sni_cluster:`/`tcpproxy:` wording); ADR-0072 (registration-order-neutral — D27-S2); ADR-0016 (the bootstrap blank-import amendment policy); ADR-0004 (the empirical pin against Envoy v1.37.2 — `onNewConnection` sets `PerConnectionCluster` verbatim + `Continue`, `onData` no-op); ADR-0044 (§Context-at-SPEC / §Decision+§Consequences-at-IMPL); project memory `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` + `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions` + `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint` + `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch`; SPEC §4 / §8 / §11 (D27-1/D27-2/D27-6/D27-7) + the PLAN Tasks 5-7.

## ADR-0221: the `network.WriteFilter` seam — the write-direction (upstream→downstream) dispatch half of the `internal/filter/network/` chain framework: a `WriteFilter` interface (`OnWrite(buf *Buffer, endStream bool) Status`) + `WriteFilterCallbacks` + chain classification extended to read / write / both / terminal + REVERSE-chain-order write dispatch (upstream LIFO parity) + delivery via a `writeChainConn` wrapping the downstream `net.Conn` handed to `handleTerminal` (zero-write-filter chains UNWRAPPED → byte-identical back-compat; `TerminalFilter.Handle` signature UNCHANGED; `tcp_proxy`/HCM untouched) + StopIteration-on-write = the-write-does-not-proceed (upstream parity) documented-unsupported-by-consumers + the terminal-originated-writes-only boundary — CONSUMING the ADR-0213 API-revision allowance (consumer #1 `zookeeper_proxy`; anticipated #2 `mongo_proxy`)

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at the phase-28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LANDED at phase-28.1b IMPL (2026-06-02) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-06-01 (§Context anchor at the 28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies at the 28.1b IMPL atomic-docs commit, 2026-06-02).
**Doctrine:** Phase 28 §9 Network-filters-family row (the THIRD; a parent pre-split row — ADR-0106). ADR-0044 ADR-on-impl convention + §Context-draft discipline. ADR-0004 empirical-pin-against-reference-Envoy (v1.37.2). ADR-0045 split-gate (2-way pre-split; the 28.1 D-P1 caveat). ADR-0052 atomic-landing + six-gate. ADR-0213 (the read-filter chain framework whose API-revision allowance this CONSUMES). ADR-0215 (the `TerminalFilter` seam + `prefixConn` — the conn-wrap precedent). ADR-0219 (the no-ripple seam-addition precedent — thread state via wrappers/ctx, never signature churn).
**Lands-in:** Phase 28.1 IMPL — `internal/filter/network/types.go` (the `WriteFilter` + `WriteFilterCallbacks` interfaces), `internal/filter/network/chain.go` (classification + reverse-order write dispatch), a NEW `internal/filter/network/writeconn.go` (the `writeChainConn`); the §Decision/§Consequences bodies at the 28.1b IMPL atomic-docs commit (both halves: 28.1a write side + 28.1b read side).

**AMEND acknowledgment (one-line in-place AMEND at 2026-06-02 per the phase-28.1b SPEC; no new ADR number consumed; per the ADR-0045 §AMEND / 25.2 IMPL Task 22 one-line in-place AMEND-acknowledgment precedent):** *This ADR's scope is EXTENDED from "the write-direction dispatch half" to **the terminal-handoff conn-wrap seam, BOTH directions**. The phase-28.1 IMPL Task-16 `0046` fixture proved the chain runtime exits its read loop permanently at terminal handoff, so a request-decoding read filter sees only the FIRST socket read per connection (vs reference Envoy's forever-re-iteration) — the gap that forced the user-approved ADR-0045 28.1a/28.1b split. The symmetric READ-direction half (a `readChainConn` re-feeding post-handoff reads through the read chain via `chainRuntime.replayRead`, the `Buffer.TotalAppended` decoder-feed re-base, the shared ≥1-write-filter wrap predicate [R1], the observational post-handoff boundaries, and the goroutine-placement concurrency pins incl. the 28.2 synchronization forward-pointer) is designed at the **28.1b SPEC §3** (`docs/envoy-go/phases/28.1b-network-filter-read-seam-and-zookeeper-requests-proof/SPEC.md`) and lands at the 28.1b IMPL. The §Decision + §Consequences bodies (landing at the 28.1b IMPL completion task, re-scoped from "28.1 IMPL" by the split) cover BOTH halves. The write-side facts in §Context below are unchanged.*

### Context

At master tip the `internal/filter/network/` framework is read-direction-only: `ReadFilter.OnNewConnection`/`OnData` see downstream→upstream bytes, and `TerminalFilter.Handle` owns the conn — but upstream→downstream bytes (the terminal's writes back to the client) are INVISIBLE to chain filters. This was a deliberate 26 BRAINSTORM Q4 scope cut ("read-filter only; write deferred until a consumer needs it"), recorded in ADR-0213 §Decision item 8 with an EXPLICIT API-revision allowance for "a future write-filter addition". `zookeeper_proxy` (phase 28) is that consumer: a both-direction protocol sniffer that must decode server responses (upstream→downstream) to emit `*_resp` counters and latency signals. This ADR consumes the allowance — the project's first deferred-with-allowance framework surface consumed by the consumer it was deferred for.

**The upstream model (empirically pinned at the parent SPEC §11.8 against Envoy v1.37.2).** Upstream `Network::WriteFilter` carries `onWrite(Buffer&, bool end_stream)`; a combined `Network::Filter` is both read and write (one instance, both directions — zookeeper_proxy registers via `addFilter`). Write filters dispatch in REVERSE config order (LIFO: `addWriteFilter` front-inserts into `downstream_filters_`; `onWrite` iterates front→back; doc: "Filters are invoked in LIFO order"). Writes ENTER the chain at `ConnectionImpl::write` → `filter_manager_.onWrite()` BEFORE any data reaches the write buffer / transport socket — i.e. the producer of upstream→downstream bytes is the terminal filter's own `connection.write()` call, and the write chain intercepts it. `StopIteration` on the write path means the write does not proceed (the data is left in the caller's buffer, never reaches the transport); upstream has NO `continueWriting()` ("we don't support restart/continue on the write path" — `connection_impl.cc` source comment).

**The envoy-go delivery mechanism: `writeChainConn` (per BRAINSTORM Q2; the `prefixConn` precedent).** envoy-go's terminal filters write upstream→downstream bytes by calling `Write` on the `net.Conn` that `handleTerminal` hands them (`chain.go:215-227`). Wrapping that conn in a `writeChainConn` — whose `Write(p)` runs the write chain (reverse order) over a `*Buffer` view of `p`, then forwards to the wrapped conn — is the exact structural mirror of upstream's `ConnectionImpl::write` → `onWrite()` → transport pipeline. The wrap composes with the existing `prefixConn` (the terminal sees `writeChainConn(prefixConn(conn))` for a mixed chain with buffered prefix). A chain with ZERO write filters gets NO wrap — `handleTerminal` stays byte-identical to today, which is the seam's back-compat invariant (ratified by all 47 existing fixtures staying green). `TerminalFilter.Handle`'s signature is UNCHANGED — no HCM ripple, no fake-double churn (the ADR-0219 no-ripple discipline).

**Two pinned boundaries (both under the API-revision allowance).** (i) StopIteration-on-write: envoy-go mirrors the upstream no-forward semantic (the bytes are not forwarded to the wrapped conn) but documents it as UNSUPPORTED-BY-CONSUMERS — no production filter may return it at 28.x (zookeeper always Continues, exactly as upstream's zookeeper does); the no-resume/inject machinery is deferred until a consumer (mongo fault-delay) needs it. (ii) Terminal-originated-writes-only: a ReadFilter writing via `Connection().Write` (echo, direct_response) does NOT pass through the write chain at 28.1 — the write chain observes the terminal's writes only. This is sufficient for zookeeper (whose chain `[zookeeper_proxy, tcp_proxy]` has all upstream→downstream bytes produced by tcp_proxy) and is recorded in BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT as a framework boundary.

### Decision

The terminal-handoff conn-wrap seam lands as the symmetric write + read extension of the `internal/filter/network/` chain framework, with the pinned shape below. The write half landed at 28.1a; the read half landed at 28.1b (28.1b SPEC §3); the two halves share ONE wrap predicate and one conn-composition.

**The write half (28.1a-landed; `internal/filter/network/types.go` + `chain.go` + `writeconn.go`).**

1. **The `WriteFilter` / `WriteFilterCallbacks` interfaces.** `WriteFilter` carries `OnWrite(buf *Buffer, endStream bool) Status` + `SetWriteFilterCallbacks(cb WriteFilterCallbacks)` + `OnDestroy()` (the same OnDestroy a both-directions filter satisfies once — `types.go:57-71`). `WriteFilterCallbacks` is MINIMAL at 28.1 (D-P2): `Connection() Connection` only, returning the SAME per-connection accessor the read callbacks expose (`types.go:81-84` + `chain.go:469-471`). Upstream's `WriteFilterCallbacks` carries more (`injectWriteDataToFilterChain`); zookeeper needs only the connection accessor, so the surface stays minimal until a consumer needs more (the API-revision allowance).
2. **Independent-type-assert classification (NOT a type-switch).** `NewChainRuntime` (`chain.go:60-102`) classifies each `NetworkFilter` by INDEPENDENT type-asserts into a read set, a write set, and an optional trailing terminal: a filter implementing BOTH `ReadFilter` and `WriteFilter` lands in BOTH sets as the SAME instance (`zookeeperproxy` is the first — a type-switch's first-match-wins cannot express this). Each write filter receives `SetWriteFilterCallbacks` exactly once at construction (`chain.go:98-100`); a both-directions filter therefore receives BOTH a read-callbacks injection (in `newChainRuntime`) and a write-callbacks injection (D-P2 dual injection). `OnDestroy` is deduped once-per-instance via an interface-identity map across both sets (`chain.go:405-419`) so a both-directions filter's `OnDestroy` runs exactly once.
3. **REVERSE-chain-order write dispatch (AMEND-A11 LIFO).** `handleTerminal` hands the `writeChainConn` a REVERSED COPY of the chain-order `writeFilters` slice (`chain.go:274-279`): config `[A, B, C]` ⇒ write dispatch `C → B → A`, mirroring upstream `addWriteFilter`'s front-insert into `downstream_filters_` (LIFO).
4. **`writeChainConn` + D-P7 return semantics (`writeconn.go`).** The terminal writes upstream→downstream bytes by calling `Write` on the conn `handleTerminal` hands it; `writeChainConn.Write(p)` allocates a fresh per-Write `*Buffer`, runs the dispatch-order chain over it, then forwards the POST-CHAIN buffer to the wrapped conn. Return semantics (D-P7): chain-stopped (StopIteration) → `(len(p), nil)` — the terminal cannot distinguish a stopped write from a delivered one (exactly as upstream `ConnectionImpl::write` returns void; a dropped write surfaces as downstream silence); underlying-write error → `(0, err)`; success → `(len(p), nil)`.
5. **The write-only-filter boot boundary (manager.go untouched).** `internal/listener/manager.go` is UNTOUCHED by the seam — its `[read*, terminal?]` chain classification is unchanged, so a write-ONLY filter (no `ReadFilter` half) leading a chain still fails boot exactly as before. Every 28.x both-directions filter (zookeeper, the planned mongo) carries a `ReadFilter` half, so this boundary constrains nothing real; it is recorded as a framework boundary, lifted under the API-revision allowance if a write-only consumer appears.
6. **The terminal-originated-writes-only boundary.** A `ReadFilter` writing via `Connection().Write` (echo, direct_response) does NOT pass through the write chain — the `writeChainConn` wraps only the conn handed to the TERMINAL, so the write chain observes terminal-originated writes only. Sufficient for `[zookeeper_proxy, tcp_proxy]` (all upstream→downstream bytes are produced by tcp_proxy).

**The read half (28.1b-landed; 28.1b SPEC §3 — `readconn.go` + `chain.go` + `buffer.go` + the zookeeperproxy feed).**

7. **`readChainConn` (`readconn.go`, NEW; innermost wrap).** A conn wrapping the RAW downstream conn; `Read(b)` reads the live socket, replays any received bytes through the read-filter chain (`rt.replayRead(b[:n], false)`) BEFORE returning them to the terminal, and on `io.EOF` delivers a final endStream replay (`rt.replayRead(nil, true)` — pre-handoff read-loop symmetry, `manager.go:1073-1077`). Replay-before-return makes stat increments visible before the bytes are forwarded upstream (deterministic ordering for the 0046 scrape). It restores upstream `FilterManagerImpl::onRead` re-iteration parity (`readconn.go:34-43`), which envoy-go otherwise loses: the chain runtime exits its read loop permanently at terminal handoff, so without this wrap a request-decoding read filter sees only the FIRST socket read per connection (the Task-16 `0046` divergence that forced the 28.1a/28.1b split).
8. **`chainRuntime.replayRead` (`chain.go:389-395`).** Appends `p` to the per-connection `rt.buf`, calls EVERY read filter's `OnData` in chain order (Status IGNORED — observational, §3.5), then DRAINS `rt.buf` fully after the pass (bounded memory — the bytes' forward path is the terminal's conn, not the chain buffer). It reuses the same `rt.buf` the pre-handoff path used, so `Buffer.TotalAppended()` is continuous across the handoff boundary. R3 is preserved: filters still never drain — the RUNTIME drains, mirroring upstream's terminal-most-filter buffer consumption.
9. **The `Buffer.TotalAppended` (int64) decoder-feed re-base (§3.3; redesigns 28.1 SPEC §4.5's mark basis).** `Buffer` gains a monotonic `total int64` incremented on every `Append`, exposed via `TotalAppended() int64` (`buffer.go:18,24,29` — int64 per D-S28.1b-1: a long-lived connection can exceed 2^31 bytes). The zookeeperproxy decoder's high-water mark (`requestDecoder.chainConsumed int64`) is kept against `TotalAppended()`, NOT the physical chain-buffer length: `decodeOnData(chainBytes, totalAppended)` feeds the trailing `(totalAppended − chainConsumed)` bytes of `chainBytes` (`decoder.go:75-79`), correct regardless of WHO drains the buffer and WHEN. This is the ONLY 28.1a-landed code the read seam modified. Equivalence: on any never-drained execution `TotalAppended() == Len()`, so the re-based feed selects byte-for-byte the same slice the 28.1a feed selected — the equivalence keeps every pre-existing decoder unit-test assertion valid unchanged. The **soundness invariant** (pinned + unit-tested): the re-base is sound iff the runtime never drains bytes a filter has not yet been shown — both drain sites satisfy it by construction (the handoff drain `chain.go:258-263` happens only after the final pre-handoff pass; the replay drain happens after the pass delivered the buffer to every read filter).
10. **The SHARED `len(rt.writeFilters) > 0` wrap predicate (R1 — LOAD-BEARING).** Both conn-wraps install under the EXACT SAME predicate (`chain.go:255` for the read wrap, `:274` for the write wrap): a chain gets BOTH wraps or NEITHER. Every existing production chain (`tcp_proxy`-only, HCM, `[echo]`, `[direct_response]`, `[rbac_network, tcp_proxy]`, `[sni_cluster, tcp_proxy]`, and all 47 pre-existing fixture dirs) has zero write filters → gets neither wrap → `handleTerminal` stays byte-identical to 28.1a (which was byte-identical to 26.2/27). The predicate is equivalent at 28.1 to "≥1 read-decoding filter" (every planned request-decoding network filter is a both-directions WriteFilter).
11. **The conn composition** (`handleTerminal`, `chain.go:246-285`): innermost → outermost = `readChainConn` (the raw conn), then `prefixConn` (iff undrained buffered prefix), then `writeChainConn` (outermost). The terminal sees `writeChainConn(prefixConn(readChainConn(conn)))` for a mixed chain with buffered prefix. Innermost-readChainConn is load-bearing: `prefixConn.Read` serves its buffered prefix (the pre-handoff bytes the read filters already saw) WITHOUT delegating inward, so prefix bytes bypass the replay — only LIVE post-handoff socket reads pass through `readChainConn.Read`.

### Consequences

- **The seam CONSUMES the ADR-0213 §Decision item-8 API-revision allowance** — the project's first deferred-with-allowance framework surface consumed by the consumer it was deferred for. Consumer #1 is `zookeeper_proxy` (the both-directions request/response sniffer); the anticipated consumer #2 is `mongo_proxy` (the natural next §9 family candidate). The allowance bounds the forward cost: the minimal `WriteFilterCallbacks`, the StopIteration-no-resume boundary, and the observational read boundaries below all generalize under it when a consumer needs more.
- **Three observational post-handoff read boundaries (§3.5), each deferred under the same allowance to the first consumer needing it.** Post-handoff: (i) an `OnData` `StopIteration` is IGNORED (the bytes are already committed to the terminal by `readChainConn.Read`'s return — an upstream divergence; honoring it would require the seam to suppress the terminal's read, a flow-control surface no consumer needs); (ii) `Connection().Close(...)` is NOT ACTED ON (the terminal owns the conn lifecycle post-handoff); (iii) `ContinueReading()` is MEANINGLESS (no parked state exists post-handoff). No production consumer needs any of these — zookeeperproxy always Continues, never closes, never drains (R3). These are documented framework boundaries, not silent gaps.
- **The §3.4 future-generalization note.** A hypothetical read-decoding filter that is NOT a write filter (a one-direction protocol sniffer) would need post-handoff reads but miss the `len(writeFilters) > 0` predicate. No such filter exists or is planned; the next consumer `mongo_proxy` is a request/response decoder and must implement `WriteFilter` (even as a no-op `OnWrite`, exactly as zookeeper does at 28.1) to get the read seam. When a one-direction read-decoder appears, the predicate generalizes via an opt-in marker interface under the API-revision allowance (the rejected-as-premature D-28.1b-2 alternative).
- **Hot-path cost is wrapped-chains-only; the R1 population pays ZERO.** A wrapped chain pays one extra interface indirection per `Read` + one `Buffer.Append` copy + one read-chain pass + one `Drain` per socket read — accepted for protocol-decoding chains (the decode work dominates). Every unwrapped chain (all existing production chains + all 47 pre-existing fixtures) is byte-identical to pre-28.1, ratified by the 47-dir back-compat gate staying byte-exact green.
- **The §3.6 concurrency pins + THE 28.2 FORWARD-POINTER.** Post-handoff, two pump goroutines run: goroutine A (downstream→upstream) calls `readChainConn.Read → replayRead →` the request decoder; goroutine B (upstream→downstream) calls `writeChainConn.Write →` the write filters' `OnWrite`. At 28.1b the two share NO mutable state — B's `OnWrite` is a pure no-op and `writeChainConn.Write` allocates a fresh per-Write `Buffer` — so **the 28.1b race surface is EMPTY** (verified by `go test -race` + a dedicated concurrent-pumps unit test over `net.Pipe`). `OnDestroy` runs strictly after both pumps join (race-free). **THE 28.2 FORWARD-POINTER (must be carried into ADR-0223 / the 28.2 SPEC):** when 28.2's response decoder lands in `OnWrite`, goroutine B will READ + ERASE the correlation structures (the data map + the control FIFO queues) that goroutine A WRITES — a data race under the as-built lock-free design. **The 28.2 SPEC MUST add synchronization** — the anticipated shape: a per-connection `sync.Mutex` on the decoder guarding the correlation maps (+ any shared latency state); the per-direction reassembly buffers stay unshared/lock-free. Upstream has no such race only because libevent serializes both directions onto one dispatcher thread. This is a direct consequence of the read seam's goroutine placement, pinned HERE so 28.2 cannot miss it.
- **Counts at 28.1 close:** `handleTerminal` byte-identical for all zero-write-filter chains (R1); the seam adds 0 stats of its own; the read half modified exactly two 28.1a-landed lines (the decoder feed + `OnData`'s `TotalAppended()` pass) plus the additive `Buffer.total`. DECISIONS.md tail STAYS ADR-0223 (no new ADR number is minted; the §Decision/§Consequences body landed in place per ADR-0044, with the §AMEND scope-extension recorded at the 28.1b SPEC commit).

**Cross-references:** ADR-0213 (the read-filter chain framework whose §Decision-item-8 API-revision allowance this seam consumes — consumer #1 zookeeper, anticipated #2 mongo); ADR-0222 (the `zookeeper_proxy` filter that is this seam's first + only 28.1 consumer); ADR-0223 (the 28.2 response side that lands in `OnWrite` and MUST add the per-connection decoder mutex this §Consequences forward-points); ADR-0215 (the `TerminalFilter` seam + `prefixConn` — the conn-wrap precedent the read/write wraps compose with); ADR-0219 (the no-ripple seam-addition discipline — state via wrappers/ctx, `TerminalFilter.Handle` signature UNCHANGED); ADR-0044 (§Context-at-SPEC / §Decision+§Consequences-at-IMPL, with the §AMEND scope-extension in place); ADR-0045 (the 28.1a/28.1b split this read half forced); the 28.1 SPEC §3 (the write seam) + the 28.1b SPEC §3 (the read seam: §3.1 readChainConn, §3.2 replayRead, §3.3 TotalAppended re-base + soundness invariant, §3.4 wrap predicate, §3.5 observational boundaries, §3.6 concurrency + the 28.2 forward-pointer); project memory `reference_network_chain_terminal_handoff_ends_ondata` (the root-cause memory the read seam closes).

## ADR-0222: NEW `zookeeper_proxy` filter (`envoy.extensions.filters.network.zookeeper_proxy.v3.ZooKeeperProxy`), request side — the family's first stats-PRIMARY filter and the first both-direction (`ReadFilter` + `WriteFilter`) consumer: 9-field config parse (`stat_prefix` PGV-required → boot-reject; `max_packet_bytes` default 1 MiB; the three `enable_per_opcode_*` increment-gating flags; latency fields parsed at 28.1 / consumed at 28.2; `access_log` parse-accept-ignore) + the 201-counter EAGER roster under scope `<stat_prefix>.zookeeper.` (creation parity — response-side counters exist-at-zero until 28.2) + the SHALLOW request decoder (BE length-prefix framing + xid sniffing + special xids 0/−1/−2/−4/−8 + the 26-value gapped wire-opcode enum + per-opcode min-length validation + decoder-internal partial-packet reassembly + unconditional passthrough) + the TWO xid→opcode correlation structures (data map + control FIFO queues, written at 28.1 / consumed at 28.2) + dynamic per-scheme `auth.<scheme>_rq` counters + the `.zookeeper.` Prometheus INLINE-PREFIX arm (ADR-0138 shape — NO tag extraction, upstream parity) + dynamic-metadata DEFERRAL (coverage boundary) + fixtures `0046-zookeeper-requests`/`0047-zookeeper-boot-reject` + the 37th fuzzer — the 7th `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` built-in

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at the phase-28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LANDED at phase-28.1b IMPL (2026-06-02) per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-06-01 (§Context anchor at the 28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies at the 28.1b IMPL atomic-docs commit, 2026-06-02).
**Doctrine:** Phase 28 §9 Network-filters-family row (the THIRD — ADR-0106). ADR-0044 + ADR-0004 + ADR-0045 + ADR-0052 + ADR-0080 (byte-stable rejects). ADR-0213/0214 (the chain framework + registry). ADR-0221 (the WriteFilter seam this filter is consumer #1 of). ADR-0060 (histogram deferral). ADR-0138 (the inline-prefix Prometheus-arm precedent). ADR-0072/0079 (registry + two-step factory). Project memories `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions` + `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` + `reference_differential_fixture_dispatch_constraint` + `reference_differential_asserter_dispatch` + `reference_proto_roster_extraction_digits`.
**Lands-in:** Phase 28.1 IMPL — NEW `internal/filter/network/zookeeperproxy/` (config.go / stats.go / decoder.go / filter.go / zookeeperproxy.go), `internal/filter/network/builtins/builtins.go` (7th registration), `internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go` (blank-import), `internal/stats/name.go` (the `.zookeeper.` arm), `test/fixtures/0046-zookeeper-requests/` + `0047-zookeeper-boot-reject/`; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies at the 28.1b IMPL atomic-docs commit (both halves: 28.1a write side + 28.1b read side).

### Context

`zookeeper_proxy` is a passive observability sniffer: it decodes the ZooKeeper client protocol (jute framing) flowing through a `[zookeeper_proxy, tcp_proxy]` chain in both directions and emits per-opcode counters. It never mutates bytes, never halts iteration, never closes the connection — its entire operator-visible surface IS its stats. This makes it the §9 family's first stats-PRIMARY filter (echo/direct_response/sni_cluster: 0 stats; rbac_network: 4) and makes the cross-side `StatsAsserter` differential the load-bearing proof (a body differential is intrinsically vacuous — bytes pass through unchanged on both sides).

**The stat surface is much larger than brainstorm-anticipated (parent SPEC AMEND-A2).** Upstream's `ALL_ZOOKEEPER_PROXY_STATS(COUNTER)` macro declares **201 counters**, ALL created eagerly at config load under scope `<stat_prefix>.zookeeper.` (parent SPEC AMEND-A1 — the prefix order is `<stat_prefix>` first, refuting the BRAINSTORM's `zookeeper.<stat_prefix>` hypothesis; confirmed live against the booted reference image). The four `enable_*` flags gate INCREMENTS, never creation — flag-false counters exist at 0 forever. The roster carries asymmetries the IMPL must mirror exactly (parent SPEC AMEND-A3): `connect_readonly_rq`/`connect_readonly_rq_bytes` exist (rq-side only); there is NO `auth_rq` (auth requests are counted via LAZY dynamic per-scheme counters `auth.<scheme>_rq`); `auth_resp*` ARE in the macro. Project stat surface goes 136 → 337 — the largest single-filter addition in the project.

**The decoder is SHALLOW; metadata is DEFERRED (parent SPEC AMEND-A8/A9).** Upstream's decoder fully parses every opcode's payload (paths, versions, ACLs, multi-transactions — ~1100 lines) primarily to emit per-message dynamic metadata. envoy-go's Q1 scope is COUNTER parity; the metadata has zero observable surface in envoy-go (no consumer of connection-level dynamic metadata; invisible to the differential; cleared per-message upstream). The 28.1 decoder therefore does framing + xid sniffing + opcode dispatch + per-opcode min-length validation + the `max_packet_bytes` check, with partial packets reassembled in decoder-internal buffers (mirroring upstream's `zk_filter_read_buffer_` model — the chain `Buffer` is read, never drained: passthrough is unconditional). Consequence (recorded as an envoy-go-LENIENT departure): a packet with a valid header but malformed payload counts as `<op>_rq` on envoy-go vs `decoder_error` upstream; the fixture corpus contains no such packets.

**Prometheus exposition is flat (parent SPEC AMEND-A4).** Reference Envoy applies NO tag extraction to zookeeper stats — `/stats/prometheus` emits `envoy_<stat_prefix>_zookeeper_<counter>{}` (empty label set; probed live with two prefixes). envoy-go's `name.go` default branch errors on unrecognized prefixes, so 28.1 adds a `.zookeeper.` INLINE-PREFIX arm (the ADR-0138 bandwidth_limit shape: dot→underscore + `envoy_` prefix, NO label promotion) — NOT a `.rbac.`-style tag-extractor.

### Decision

`zookeeper_proxy` lands as the request-side filter with the pinned shape below (the package is `internal/filter/network/zookeeperproxy/`; the 7th `builtins.RegisterBuiltins` built-in). 28.1b modified exactly the §3.3 feed re-base (item 7); everything else is the as-built 28.1a request package.

1. **TypeURL via `proto.MessageName`; `NewFactory(reg)` closure-capture.** `TypeURL` is derived as `"type.googleapis.com/" + proto.MessageName(&zookeeper_proxyv3.ZooKeeperProxy{})` (NEVER a hand-typed docs string — `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions`; the `extensions.` segment is intrinsic; `zookeeperproxy.go:17`). `NewFactory(reg *stats.Registry)` returns the `NetworkFilterFactory` with the stats Registry CLOSURE-CAPTURED (the rbac `NewFactory(reg)` / D-26.3-3 precedent — `network.FactoryCtx` carries no stats registry). The factory parses + validates ONCE at boot (ADR-0079 two-step) and EAGERLY creates the roster per distinct stat_prefix; the returned `FilterInstanceFactory` allocates a fresh per-connection `*filter` sharing the boot-parsed `*compiledConfig` (counter increments are atomic).
2. **The 9-field parse + PGV-mirror PARSE-REJECT arms + proto→wire opcode mapping (`config.go`).** `parseConfig` validates the 9-field proto: `stat_prefix` PGV-required → boot-reject (`zookeeper_proxy: stat_prefix is required`, the load-bearing 0047 arm); `max_packet_bytes` default 1 MiB; the three increment-gating `enable_per_opcode_*` flags; the latency fields (`enable_latency_threshold_metrics`, `default_latency_threshold` PGV gte-1ms, `latency_threshold_overrides` keyed by WIRE opcode via `protoToWireOpcode`, duplicate-override → reject) parsed at 28.1 / consumed at 28.2; `access_log` parse-accept-IGNORED (upstream parity — completely unread). The PARSE-REJECT strings are byte-stable from the 28.1a commit (ADR-0080; `config.go:148-155`). The proto enum (27 contiguous values 0..26) maps to the GAPPED wire opcode enum (negative `opClose = -11`, gaps, `>100` values) via `protoToWireOpcode` (`config.go:47-75`; AMEND-A6 — the two enums differ).
3. **The 201-counter EAGER roster + creation parity (D-P5) + the dynamic `auth.<scheme>_rq` counters (`stats.go`).** `rosterSuffixes()` returns the exact 201 upstream-macro suffixes: 4 plain (`decoder_error`, `request_bytes`, `response_bytes`, `watch_event`) + 28 `_rq` + 29 `_rq_bytes` + 28 `_decoder_error` + 28×4 (`_resp`/`_resp_bytes`/`_resp_fast`/`_resp_slow`) = 201 (R2; verified against `stats.go` at this task). `newRosterStats` creates ALL 201 eagerly under scope `<stat_prefix>.zookeeper.` via `NewCounterIfAbsent` (post-Freeze-permitted + idempotent across listeners sharing a prefix; D-P5 creation parity — response-side counters exist-at-zero until 28.2). The roster carries the AMEND-A3 asymmetries exactly: `connect_readonly_rq`/`connect_readonly_rq_bytes` are rq-side-only (no `connect_readonly_resp`); there is NO static `auth_rq` (auth requests increment LAZY dynamic per-scheme counters `auth.<scheme>_rq` via `authSchemeCounter`, gated through the upstream builtin-scheme set — a non-builtin scheme collapses to `auth.unknown_scheme_rq`); `auth_resp*` ARE in the macro. The dynamic counters use `NewCounterIfAbsent` (decode time is post-Freeze runtime).
4. **The SHALLOW request decoder (framing + xid sniffing + min-length table + AMEND-A8 no-resync) + the 28.1b §3.3 TotalAppended feed re-base (`decoder.go`).** The decoder does BE 4-byte length-prefix framing + xid sniffing (special xids `connect=0`/`ping=-2`/`auth=-4`/`setWatches=-8`; `watch=-1` is response-side, 28.2) + opcode dispatch + per-opcode min-length validation (the D-S28.1-1 `dataRequestMinLength` table, transcribed from upstream `decoder.cc` ensureMinLength calls) + the `max_packet_bytes` check, with partial frames reassembled in the decoder-internal `readBuf` (AMEND-A8: a decode failure ABANDONS the buffer — NO resync; the connection is never closed; passthrough is unconditional). The high-water mark `chainConsumed` is kept against the monotonic `Buffer.TotalAppended()` counter, NOT the physical buffer length (the 28.1b §3.3 re-base; D-S28.1-3 mark OWNERSHIP unchanged — the re-base changes its basis, not its owner), so the feed is correct under the read seam's runtime drains (handoff + after every replay pass). The chain buffer is READ, never drained by the filter (R3).
5. **The TWO xid→opcode correlation structures (written 28.1, consumed 28.2 — R5).** `requestsByXid` (the data map; xid > 0; insert overwrites) + `controlRequestsByXid` (per-xid FIFO queues for connect/ping/auth/setwatches; AMEND-A7). Both are written on every successful request decode at 28.1 and NEVER read until the 28.2 response decoder consumes them. KNOWN 28.1 boundary: the control queues grow unbounded for the connection's lifetime at 28.1 (nothing drains them until 28.2) — accepted hand-off, documented in PROGRESS. These are exactly the structures the ADR-0221 §3.6 forward-pointer flags for the 28.2 cross-goroutine race.
6. **The `.zookeeper.` `name.go` arm (AMEND-A4 flat Prometheus).** A `.zookeeper.` INLINE-PREFIX detection arm at `internal/stats/name.go:243-255` flattens `<stat_prefix>.zookeeper.<counter>` (counter MAY contain dots — the dynamic `auth.<scheme>_rq` family) to `envoy_<stat_prefix>_zookeeper_<counter>` (dot→underscore + `envoy_` prefix, NO label promotion — the ADR-0138 bandwidth_limit shape, NOT a `.rbac.`-style tag-extractor). KEEP-IN-SYNC with the roster.
7. **The both-directions filter glue + pure no-op `OnWrite` (`zookeeperproxy.go`).** `*filter` implements BOTH `ReadFilter` and `WriteFilter` (one instance, both directions — the first consumer of the ADR-0221 seam; upstream `addFilter` parity). `OnNewConnection` is a no-op `Continue` (an OnNewConnection StopIteration would set the sticky `connHalted` — `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts`); `OnData` feeds the decoder `buf.Bytes()` + `buf.TotalAppended()` (the §3.3 re-based feed) and ALWAYS returns `Continue`; `OnWrite` is a PURE no-op `Continue` at 28.1 (it does NOT buffer write-direction bytes — with no response decoder to drain it, a write-side buffer would grow unboundedly; the write-side buffer lands WITH the 28.2 response decoder). The no-op `OnWrite` exists so the filter satisfies `WriteFilter` (hence gets the shared wrap predicate → the read seam) AND so the 0046 traffic exercises the `writeChainConn → OnWrite` seam end-to-end. `OnDestroy` drops the per-connection decoder (the §3.3 once-per-instance dedupe).
8. **The fixtures + the TCPSink pin + the 37th fuzzer.** `0046-zookeeper-requests` is the cross-side proof (7 arms via a `fixture.StatsAsserter` on the now-green re-enabled driver; the body differential is intrinsically vacuous — bytes pass through unchanged, so the StatsAsserter is the load-bearing proof; the `TCPSink` BackendKind feeds deterministic ZooKeeper request frames). `0047-zookeeper-boot-reject` is the differential proof of the `stat_prefix`-required PARSE-REJECT (`differential.BootRejectFixture`, symmetric, `ExpectedBootErrorSubstring() = "stat_prefix"`). The 37th fuzzer (`FuzzZookeeperRequestDecode`) covers the shallow decoder. (Counts at 28.1 close: 49 active fixture dirs; 37 fuzzers.)
9. **The AMEND-A9 dynamic-metadata deferral + the shallow-decode leniency departure.** Upstream's decoder fully parses every opcode's payload (~1100 lines) primarily to emit per-message dynamic metadata; envoy-go's Q1 scope is COUNTER parity and the metadata has ZERO observable surface in envoy-go (no consumer; invisible to the differential; cleared per-message upstream) — DEFERRED (AMEND-A9), a documented coverage boundary. The shallow decode is an envoy-go-LENIENT departure: a packet with a valid header but malformed payload counts as `<op>_rq` on envoy-go vs `decoder_error` upstream (the fixture corpus contains no such packets).

### Consequences

- **`zookeeper_proxy` is the §9 Network-filters family's first stats-PRIMARY filter** (echo/direct_response/sni_cluster: 0 stats; rbac_network: 4) — its entire operator-visible surface IS its stats, which is why the cross-side `StatsAsserter` differential is the load-bearing proof (0046 GREEN on all 7 arms; R4 deliberate-break recorded).
- **Project stat surface goes 136 → 337** (+201) — the largest single-filter addition in the project. The BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT stat-table roll lands at 28.1b (not 28.1a) because the contract records cross-side-PROVEN surface and the proof is the now-green 0046 (the deliberate 28.1a deferral). Per-row enumeration of 201 rows is NOT required — the roster is normatively defined by `stats.go` `rosterSuffixes()` + the R2 golden-list unit test (the 25.x large-roster precedent).
- **The request package is consumer #1 of the ADR-0221 seam** (the both-directions classification, the no-op `OnWrite`, the shared wrap predicate that gives it the read seam). The §3.3 feed re-base is the ONLY package code the 28.1b read seam modified; the equivalence argument keeps the pre-handoff path byte-identical.
- **The correlation structures (R5) are written-but-unread at 28.1** — they exist solely for the 28.2 response decoder, and they are the cross-goroutine race surface ADR-0221 §3.6 forward-points (the 28.2 SPEC MUST add the per-connection decoder mutex). The latency fields are likewise parsed-not-consumed at 28.1 (28.2 / ADR-0223).
- **Counts at 28.1 close:** fixtures 47 → 49 (`0046` re-enabled + `0047`); stat surface 136 → 337; fuzzers stay 37 (no new fuzzer at 28.1b — the 37th already covers the replay-fed decoder (added at 28.1a)). DECISIONS.md tail STAYS ADR-0223 (no new ADR number is minted; the §Decision/§Consequences body landed in place per ADR-0044).

**Cross-references:** ADR-0221 (the WriteFilter + read-seam terminal-handoff conn-wrap seam this filter is consumer #1 of — the both-directions classification, the no-op OnWrite, the shared wrap predicate, the §3.6 race forward-pointer the correlation structures create); ADR-0223 (the 28.2 response side that consumes the R5 correlation structures + the latency fields parsed here); ADR-0213/0214 (the chain framework + registry); ADR-0080 (the byte-stable PARSE-REJECT wording); ADR-0138 (the inline-prefix Prometheus-arm precedent the `.zookeeper.` arm follows); ADR-0079 (the two-step factory + closure-capture); ADR-0060 (the histogram deferral 28.2 records against); ADR-0044 (§Context-at-SPEC / §Decision+§Consequences-at-IMPL); the parent SPEC §5/§7/§11 (AMEND-A1..A11) + the 28.1 SPEC §4 (the as-built request package) + the 28.1b SPEC §3.3 (the feed re-base); project memories `reference_network_filter_typeurl_extensions` + `reference_network_read_filter_onnewconnection_halts` + `reference_proto_roster_extraction_digits`.

## ADR-0223: `zookeeper_proxy` response side + latency-threshold counters (phase 28.2) — the response decoder in `OnWrite` (response framing xid+zxid+error; connect-response special framing; watch-event handling xid −1 → `watch_event`, never correlated; unknown response xid → `decoder_error`) + xid correlation consuming the 28.1 structures (data map erase-on-lookup; control FIFO queues) + per-opcode `*_resp`/`response_bytes`/flag-gated `*_resp_bytes` increments + latency measurement with the `enable_latency_threshold_metrics` fast/slow counter surface (`latency <= threshold` → fast; `default_latency_threshold` 100 ms default, PGV gte-1ms; `latency_threshold_overrides` keyed by WIRE opcode via the proto→wire mapping; duplicate-override → boot-reject) + the DETERMINISTIC-threshold differential discipline (extreme thresholds → all-fast / all-slow arms) + fixture `0048-zookeeper-responses` + the 38th fuzzer + the latency-HISTOGRAM coverage boundary (ADR-0060) + the parent-row-28 ROLLUP

**Status:** ACCEPTED. §Context anchored at the phase-28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies LAND at phase-28.2 IMPL per ADR-0044 in-place edit discipline.
**Date:** 2026-06-01 (§Context anchor at the 28 parent SPEC commit; §Decision + §Consequences bodies at the 28.2 IMPL atomic-docs commit).
**Doctrine:** Phase 28 §9 Network-filters-family row (the THIRD — ADR-0106). ADR-0044 + ADR-0004 + ADR-0045 + ADR-0052. ADR-0221/0222 (the seam + the request side this completes). ADR-0060 (the histogram deferral this records a coverage boundary against). The 18/19/22/24/25/26 parent-ROLLUP precedent.
**Lands-in:** Phase 28.2 IMPL — `internal/filter/network/zookeeperproxy/` (decoder.go response path + latency), `test/fixtures/0048-zookeeper-responses/`; the §Decision/§Consequences bodies + the parent-row-28 ROLLUP at the 28.2 IMPL atomic-docs commit.

### Context

Phase 28.2 completes zookeeper_proxy's round-trip observability: the response decoder runs in `OnWrite` (the ADR-0221 write chain), correlates responses to the requests 28.1 recorded, and emits the response-side + latency-threshold counter families. This is what the WriteFilter seam exists for — without 28.2, the seam's only consumer would be a write-direction no-op.

**Response framing + correlation (parent SPEC §11.4).** Standard responses carry xid(4) + zxid(8) + error(4); connect responses are special (protocol_version + timeout + session_id + password — no zxid/error); watch events (xid −1) are server-initiated pushes with no corresponding request (counted as `watch_event`, never correlated). Correlation consumes the two 28.1 structures: the data map (xid > 0; erased on lookup — a second response with the same xid is a `decoder_error`) and the control FIFO queues (connect/ping/auth/setwatches xids repeat; FIFO-matched). A response whose xid has no pending request → `decoder_error` (upstream parity).

**Latency-threshold counters are the deterministic stand-in for the deferred histograms (BRAINSTORM Q1 + parent SPEC AMEND-A10).** Upstream emits both latency HISTOGRAMS (deferred per ADR-0060 — the project-wide histogram deferral; recorded as a coverage boundary at 28.2) and threshold-based fast/slow COUNTERS (`<opname>_resp_fast`/`<opname>_resp_slow`, gated by `enable_latency_threshold_metrics`). The counters use only existing counter machinery and are differentially provable under DETERMINISTIC extreme thresholds: a `default_latency_threshold: 3600s` arm makes every response fast on both sides; a 1 ms threshold + a fixture backend that delays ≥ 10 ms makes every response slow on both sides — eliminating cross-side timing nondeterminism. The comparison is INCLUSIVE (`latency <= threshold` → fast); overrides are keyed by WIRE opcode int (via the proto-enum → wire-enum mapping — the two enums differ, parent SPEC AMEND-A6); a duplicate opcode override is an upstream config-load exception → a 28.2 boot-reject parity arm.

**The parent ROLLUP.** Phase 28.2's IMPL final task flips ROADMAP sub-row 28.2 `in-progress → done` AND parent row 28 `in-progress → done` ATOMICALLY (the 18/19/22/24/25/26 precedent), closing the THIRD §9 Network-filters-family row. After phase 28, 4 family candidates remain (`redis`/`mongo`/`kafka_broker`/`thrift`); `mongo_proxy` is the natural next (consumer #2 of the WriteFilter seam).
